5.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Scratch Notes]] METADATA:{"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/04 21:35:07"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ## [[01 - Main Event Shadows]]
When the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] brings its blood-soaked spectacle to [[Steeltown]], tensions explode as undefeated champion **[[Bobby Cutman|Bobby “The Iron Bull” Cutman]]** disrespects the crowd, the city, and the **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**. As security duty turns personal, **[[Abel May Jr.]]** steps up and steals the spotlight, triggering a ferocious standoff that nearly ignites a riot. But while the world watches [[Bobby Cutman]] rage, a shadowy offer is made. And behind the scenes, something far more dangerous is watching everything from the dark. --- ## [[02 - Ghosts On The Waves]]
When [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and the [[Rustwater Raiders]] are summoned to [[The Silo]] in [[Ashmoor]] for a secret job, they’re ordered to smuggle a high-value prisoner to [[Steeltown]] — but the “prisoner” turns out to be something else entirely. As tensions rise aboard [[The Black Marauder]], Lyla must decide whether to complete the job or risk everything by defying [[The Duke]]. Meanwhile, a chilling vision haunts the [[Unseen Widows]]: a glimpse of the horrors still to come. --- ## [[03 - The Devil In The Row]]
When two off-duty [[Loyalist Guard]]s in [[Gutter Row]] take their drunken power trip too far behind [[Hollow House]], they come face to face with a shadow the city guard pretends doesn’t exist. As [[Shana]] fights for survival, a chain rings through the alley, and with it, [[The Grim Man]] delivers his silent judgment. Blood hits brick, legend becomes real, and a quiet pact is sealed in the dark. And somewhere else in [[Steeltown]], a message is delivered. Not everyone welcomes it. --- ## [[04 - Glowing Darkness]]
[[Lash Hawkins]] breaks from the [[Murray Boys]], revealing his own potent [[Luxyn]] supply and igniting a dangerous feud with [[Nico Murray]]. After publicly humiliating Nico in the streets of [[Gutter Row]], Nico returns home and informs his family, [[Marco Murray]] and [[Rosa Murray]] of Lash's decisions. Meanwhile, Lash sets out to expand his empire—but a quiet street and a pale stranger bring his rise in the [[Luxyn]] game to a sudden, chilling stop. Elsewhere in [[Ashmoor]], private meetings are held and plans are discussed. --- ## [[05 - Sight Unseen]]
In the fog-choked wilds of [[The Drownlands]], twin hunters [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] and [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] complete the sacred rite to become Unseen, pledging their lives to the goddess [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]. With [[Riley Thorne]] guiding them, they embark on their quest to become Widows and find an unlikely first kill. Meanwhile, far from the mire, [[Ava Victoria]] searches the chaos of [[Gutter Row]] for the vanished [[Lash Hawkins]], forcing an uneasy alliance with [[Nico Murray]] as shadows gather and secrets deepen. --- # Chronos Cheatsheet After installing the Chronos Timeline plugin for Obsidian, copy and paste this whole markdown file into a file in your vault to play around and learn the syntax. Hover on a timeline and click the Edit button in the upper right to play with the data. ## Date formats Chronos can visualize dates from the year down to the second level, using the syntax `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss`. The only required component of a date is the year (`YYYY`). Beyond that, you can specify additional time granularity as needed for your use case. If not explicitly provided: - The month and day default to `01` (January and the 1st) - The hour, minute, and second default to `00` (top of the hour or minute) ### Examples ```chronos - [2020] A year - [2020-02] A month - [2020-02-28] A day - [2020-02-28T12] An hour - [2020-02-28T12:30] A minute - [2020-02-28T12:30:09] A second ``` ## Events **Full Syntax** ``` - [Date~Date] #Color {Group Name} Event Name | Description ``` - The second Date, Color, Group Name, Event Name, and Description are optional - Description appears when you hover on an event in the timeline ### Examples #### Single Date **Syntax** ``` - [Date] Event Name ``` ```chronos - [1879-03-14] Einstein born ``` #### Date range **Syntax** ``` - [Date~Date] Event Name ``` ```chronos - [1991~2001] Time I believed in Santa ``` #### Date range with description **Syntax** ``` - [Date~Date] Event Name| Description ``` ```chronos - [1991~2001] Time I believed in Santa | ended when my brother tried to videotape Santa with a hidden camera ``` #### With color See available [Colors](#colors) **Syntax** ``` - [Date~Date] #Color Event Name| Description ``` ```chronos - [2001~2009] #red Bush - [2009~2017] #blue Obama - [2017~2021] #red Trump - [2021~2025] #blue Biden ``` #### With groups **Syntax** ``` - [Date(~Date)] {Group Name} Event Name| Description ``` ```chronos @ [1892-10-08~1941-08-31] {Marina Tsvetaeva} 1892-1941 - [1916] {Marina Tsvetaeva} "Подруга" - [1928] {Marina Tsvetaeva} "Поэма концов" - [1941] {Marina Tsvetaeva} "Записки о поэзии" @ [1899-08-24~1986-06-14] {Jorge Luis Borges} 1899-1986 - [1944] {Jorge Luis Borges} "Ficciones" - [1949] {Jorge Luis Borges} "El Aleph" - [1962] {Jorge Luis Borges} "Labyrinths" ```

METADATA:{"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/04 21:35:07"}

(cont'd) ## Periods

**Full Syntax**

```
@ [Date~Date] #Color {Group Name} Period Name
```

- Color, Group Name, and Period Name are optional

### Examples

#### Basic

```chronos
@ [-300~250] Yayoi Period
- [-100] Introduction of rice cultivation
- [-57] Japan’s first recorded contact with China
```

#### With color

See available [Colors](#colors)

```chronos
@ [-300~250] #red Yayoi Period
- [-100] Introduction of rice cultivation
- [-57] Japan’s first recorded contact with China

@ [250~538] Kofun Period
- [250] Construction of keyhole-shaped kofun burial mounds begins
- [369] Yamato state sends envoys to Korea
```


## Points

**Syntax**

```
* [Date] Point Name | Description
```

```chronos
- [2024-02-26~2024-03-10] Tournament
* [2024-02-26] Game 1 | Austin
* [2024-02-28] Game 2 | Los Angeles
* [2024-03-06] Game 3 | Tokyo
* [2024-03-10] Game 4 | Jakarta
```

## Markers

**Syntax**

```
= [Date] Marker Name
```

### Examples

```chronos
= [1440] Invention of the Gutenberg Press

- [1455] Gutenberg Bible Printed
@ [1501~1600] The Spread of Printing
- [1517] Martin Luther's 95 Theses
```

## Advanced example

```chronos
- [1945-07-17] {Europe} Potsdam Conference | where post-WWII Europe is divided
- [1947-03-12] {USA} Truman Doctrine | committing the U.S. to containing communism
- [1948-06-24~1949-05-12] {Europe} Berlin Blockade | and Airlift in response to Soviet actions in Berlin
- [1949-04-04] {Europe} Formation of NATO

# Early Cold War

@ [1957~1969] #cyan {USSR} Space Race
@ [1957~1969] #cyan {USA} Space Race
- [1950-06-25~1953-07-27] {Asia} Korean War | between North and South Korea
- [1955-05-14] {USSR} Warsaw Pact | in response to NATO
- [1957-10-04] #cyan {USSR} Sputnik launched | initiating the Space Race
- [1961-04-17] {Cuba} Bay of Pigs Invasion | in Cuba

# Height of Tensions

- [1962-10-16] {Cuba} Cuban Missile Crisis | a peak confrontation between the U.S. and USSR
- [1963-08-05] {Global} Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty signed
- [1969-07-20] #cyan {USA} Apollo 11 Moon landing | U.S. wins the Space Race
- [1972-05-26] {Global} SALT I signed | first Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty

# Détente Period

- [1979-12-24~1989-02-15] {USSR} Soviet-Afghan War | straining Soviet resources
- [1983-03-23] {USA} Reagan announces the Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI)
- [1986-04-26] {USSR} Chernobyl nuclear disaster
- [1987-12-08] {Global} INF Treaty | signed, eliminating intermediate-range nuclear missiles

# Late Cold War

- [1989-11-09] {Europe} Fall of the Berlin Wall | symbolizing the end of Cold War tensions
- [1991-07-31] {Global} START I Treaty signed | further arms reduction
- [1991-12-26] {USSR} Dissolution of the Soviet Union | officially ending the Cold War

= [1991-12-26] End of the Cold War

```

## Ordering

**Order by start date**

```chronos
> ORDERBY start

- [2026~2028] Event D
- [2024~2028] Event B
- [2025~2030] #red Event C
- [2020~2030] #red  Event A
```

**Order by start (descending)**

```chronos
> ORDERBY -start

- [2026~2028] Event D
- [2024~2028] Event B
- [2025~2030] #red Event C
- [2020~2030] #red  Event A
```

**Order by color and start**

```chronos
> ORDERBY color|start

- [2026~2028] Event D
- [2024~2028] Event B
- [2025~2030] #red Event C
- [2020~2030] #red  Event A
```

## Default view dates

Use the `> DEFAULTVIEW start|end` flag to specify default start and end dates for your timeline's initial load

```chronos
> DEFAULTVIEW  -3000|3000

- [2024] AGI
```

## Colors

- `#red`
- `#orange`
- `#yellow`
- `#green`
- `#blue`
- `#purple`
- `#pink`
- `#cyan`

#### Overall Outline
- Political turmoil spreads across Disgraceland as [[The Duke]] raises already high taxes on basic necessities like fuel and food. The Duke and his wealthy, elite circle get richer as the people struggle and get poorer. Deals start to be made behind [[The Duke]]s back and when he finds out, [[The Duke]] cracks down hard. Causing a rebellion in [[Charspire]] that spreads to [[Gutter Row]]. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] and the [[Rustwater Raiders]] make an uneasy alliance to stop The Duke's [[Loyalist Guard]] and protect the people. Civil War breaks out in [[Charspire]] and [[Gutter Row]] officially.

- [[Rachel Gold]] will discover secret documents claiming [[The Duke]] will sign an act declaring any undesirables as slaves from henceforth.

- [[Salem Quinn]] and [[Prophet Veerah]] will have the same vision of the A.I. Frankensteins. Quinn believes it's a warning and is trying to warn [[The Duke]]. Veerah believes it's a prophecy and she is being instructed to kill men to bring the return of [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]].

- [[Bobby Cutman]] kills [[Bastian Redd]] in their rematch. [[Abel May Jr.]] signs with [[World Lucha Libre]] and agrees to fight Cutman. May Jr. is also challenged by Raider [[Blacktide Cray]]. [[Bastian Redd]]'s body disappears after the fight.

- [[Morris Gable]] is assassinated on live tv by [[Hella]] or [[The Grim Man]], maybe?

- [[The Grim Man]] assassinates [[Gorren Brile]]

- Someone, maybe [[Emily Burton]] will assassinate [[The Duke]] and claim power for themselves. 

- In the finale, [[Ora Razchek]] will release his army of A.I-Frankensteins that include a dead [[Bastian Redd]] to unleash hell on a warring nation. Indiscriminately killing everyone. Ora and [[Hella]] will arrive at [[The Silo]] and murder whoever The Duke/Duchess is at the time. Claiming [[TRIBUCIA MAP]] as their dark world.

---

## Chapter 3 - The Devil In The Row
  
  - ### **Part 1**: 
    Shana, the owner of Hollow House takes a break from managing her girls and steps out back for a cigarette in the night air. Two clearly drunk loyalist guards appear acting like assholes and ask her for a smoke and start harrassing Shana, but Shana is cool and confident and does what she can to try and calm things. Eventually one of them grabs Shana and she slaps him. The other guard grabs her and starts threatening her. Both guards drag Shana down deeper into the alley, covering her mouth as she tries to scream. 
  - ### **Part 2**: 
  Behind a dumpster the guards toss Shana, who immediately stands up and attacks but is quickly overpowered. The guards laugh and mock her as they rip at her clothes and grab at her body. They discuss what they're going to do to her and pretend to play a game as to who will take her first. Suddenly a loud CLANG is heard. The guards quickly turn their heads and see The Grim Man, standing motionless about 20 feet away in the alley holding his chain, the long spike of it resting on the ground. The guards are nervous but try to mock Grim Man, who just stands there. Finally the guards let go of Shana and stand up to face the Grim Man. They run their mouths at him and pump themselves up before slowly taking steps towards Grim Man. Grim Man just watches them advance. 
  - ### **Part 3**: 
In a flash Grim Man launches his chain spike at one of the guards, instantly impaling through his eye. The other guard freezes in shock for a moment but quickly draws his gun and fires at Grim Man. Grim Man jumps behind another dumpster as the Guard yells at him. The guard slowly advances with his gun drawn to the dumpster, finally he looks behind it but Grim Man isn't there. The guard turns around quickly but Shana is there and kicks him square in the nuts. The guard falls. Grim Man appears behind Shana and Shana gasps in fright but Grim Man just grabs the other guard, takes the guards own cuffs and cuffs the guard before throwing him into the dumpster. 
  - ### **Part 4**: 
  Shana watches the Grim Man for a moment. Finally Grim Man looks over at Shana and stops. Shana slowly steps towards him and thanks him for saving her. Grim Man nods. Shana says she has heard about him but didn't think he was real. Says people in Gutter Row call him the Grim Man. She says he's something this hell hole needs. - a person doing whats right. Shana tells him she owes him now and if he ever needs a favor to come find her. Grim Man nods again and disappears into the shadows as Shana watches him go.
  
  ---

9.title: OUTLINES
9.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[OUTLINES]]

METADATA:{"cover":"zz_media/002.png","tags":["title"],"created":"2025/05/13 20:12:44","modified":"2025/06/09 09:39:55"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ## Chapter 4 - White Gold
  
  - ### **Part 1**: 
    Lash Hawkins waits, cool and calm near the Three Nail Market in Gutter Row for Nico Murray to show. Eventually Nico walks up with two girls on his arms. Lash and Nico exchange phony pleasantries before Nico asks why Lash called him out here. Lash tells Nico he's out. He's not going to be selling for the Murray Boys anymore. Lash tells Nico he's learned over the years how to manufacture his own, and recent batches are testing even more pure than Murray Luxyn. Nico is furious, telling Lash he's making a huge fuckin mistake. Does Lash realize that puts him in direct competition on the streets with The Murray Boys? Lash just grins at him, infuriating Nico even more. Nico swings at Lash but Lash is too quick and ducks, quickly slapping Nico hard in the face, telling him to smarten up, embarrassing him in front of the girls. Nico, incensed, leaves.
  - ### **Part 2**:
  Nico arrives back at the Murray House and tells Rosa and Marco, his parents, what has happened. Rosa says she never trusted that boy and Marco says he'll send word to Francis to let him know. Marco tells Nico scum like Lash will be dealt with. Marco patienly pulls on a cigar and tells Nico to settle down and remember nobody wins against the Murrays. Marco tells Nico to make contact with the leader of the Third Row gang, Samson Knight, see about brokering a meeting. Maybe having the Third Row sell Luxyn for them right out of the Three Nail Market.
- ### **Part 3**:
  Inside an unassuming shack somewhere inside Gutter Row, Lash works in his homemade lab, Night Time with Morris Gable is on the small television as Lash cooks up a fresh batch of Luxyn. Lash turns and watches Morris Gable deliver some monologue jokes as he lights up a cigarette and chuckles at the tv. There is a *ding* and Lash opens a small glass container, omitting a steam and looks at his latest batch of Luxyn, smiling widely at it. He holds it up and studies the faint glowing properties for a moment before commenting "This about to me my town now." Lash looks around for another baggy to stash it but realizes he is out. He puts things down, throws on his jacket and walks out into the cool night, locking his homemade lab shut behind him as he ventures out to the shops open at this time in the Three Nail Market.
- ### **Part 4**:
Lash walks alone down the quiet cobblestone streets in disrepair, lighting up another cigarette and plotting how best to build his empire. He passes a group of people he knows and smiles, slapping hands with them and hugging one of the girls. Lash says he'll catch them on his way back, he's just running to the shop. Lash walks on and turns down some more streets, finally he comes to a quiet corner and turns the corner. Hella is standing there about 10 feet in front of him, smiling. Lash looks at her and freezes. Lash tries to play it cool but Hella just stares at him and grins. Lash starts to get freaked out a bit and takes a step forward to get around Hella, but Hella steps in front of him. Lash warns Hella one more time but suddenly Hella spits a mist of green liquid from her mouth into Lash's face. Lash yells but falls over, unconscious. Hella looks down at Lash as she pulls out a rope.

---

10.content:

(cont'd) ## Chapter 5 - Sight Unseen
  
  - ### **Part 1**: 
Deep in the marshes of The Drownlands, the Unseen Widow twins, Raina & Risa quietly hunt a boar foraging in the thick bush. They communicate just with their eyes and hand signals as they move to surround the boar. The boar is unaware of their presence. Slowly, Risa pulls a bow from her back and hooks an arrow up to it, launching the arrow directly into the boar. The Boar wails and runs but Raina pounces on it quickly, slicing her blade across it's throat in one quick motion. The twins are pleased as they pack the animal up. Talking about how it will be good to honor the god Mirella with a boar feast. 
They walk through the bush and return to where Riley Thorne is waiting, Riley tells the twins they did great and they are almost ready. The twins are pleased.

- ### **Part 2**:
Raina, Risa and Riley all return to the compound and are greeted by Len Vyne. Len tells the other girls to come quickly as Prophet Veerah has had another vision and has gathered the sisters. All four make their way to the sermon stand where Prophet Veerah stands looking out at about a dozen girls. Veerah sees Riley and the twins and smiles, asking them to come in. They enter and Veerah begins a monologue on the vision she had in her sleep. The vision was of a point in the near future where Ora Razchek's AI Frankenstein monsters are attacking an unknown part of Tribucia, killing indiscriminately. All Veerah sees are the monsters attacking but she has no context as she is unaware of the existence of Ora or the monsters. Because of that, she attributes her vision to the goddess Mirella and interprets it as Mirella telling Veerah that war will come to destroy everything unless Veerah and the widows stop it. 

- ### **Part 3**
After Veerah's sermon, she is in her cabin as Riley and Raina & Risa enter. Veerah asks them to sit and they do. Veerah asks Riley if the twins are ready and Riley says she believes they are. Veerah asks the twins directly if they are ready. Raina and Risa say yes. Veerah says good. Veerah stands and tells the twins to follow her. They exit the cabin with Riley following and wander down a small path until they reach a clearing on a small cliff overlooking The Drownlands. Veerah walks to a small cauldron and adds mud, grass, tree bark, bits of earth. She mixes it as she speaks. Telling them that this is the body of Mirella, that the godess Mirella is one with the land and air and sea and is everything and everywhere. Veerah asks the twins if they pledge their lives to Mirella. The twins say yes and Veerah fills two small cups with the contents of the cauldron and hands the twins a cup each. She tells them to consume the body of Mirella and once complete they will become Unseen. The twins do. Veerah and Riley are pleased. Veerah says they are now Unseen. Veerah then tells them that to become a Widow, they must first each kill one man.

- ### **Part 4**
A short time later, Raina, Risa and Riley Thorne are coming out of a clearing on the edge of The Drownlands. To their east is Grave Bay. They notice the Black Marauder sailing out in the bay in the direction of Steeltown. To their west is the Loyalist Guard Base. The group make their way along the edge of the Loyalist Base they hide and watch General Colt command a squad through multiple intense drills. They see Colt grab a whip and start beating a recruit who failed the drill apparently. The group watches him and Raina and Rise decide he will be their first kill.

11.title: OUTLINES
11.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[OUTLINES]]

METADATA:{"cover":"zz_media/002.png","tags":["title"],"created":"2025/05/13 20:12:44","modified":"2025/06/09 09:39:55"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ## Chapter 6 - Showdown In Gage Park
  
  - ### **Part 1**
A fisherman at the docks in Gage Park, Steeltown is packing up for the day, saying goodnight to friends, etc, when he notices the Black Marauder pirate ship in the Rustwater Bay. He watches it nervously for a time and realizes it is headed for the docks. He yells and people begin to notice the approaching vessel. Women grab up children and hurry them off, fishermen scurry to get out of the water and away from the docks. The first fisherman begins to run, passing by people, one of his friends from earlier bumps into him and he tells his friend he's going to inform the Wrecking Crew of the impending appearance of the Rustwater Raiders.
  
  - ### **Part 2**
On the Black Marauder, Blacktide Cray, Lyla Bonetooth and Silas Vayne stood watching the shores of Gage Park, watching the people panicking and fleeing. Blacktide says this may have been a bad idea. Silas is sure that the Wrecking Crew are going to attack them. Blacktide agrees with Silas and says we need to prepare for a fight. Salt-Eye Marloow enters and Lyla asks him how the slaves are doing. Salt-Eye says they're hangin' on, but the girl, the little one has a right bad fever. This news hits Lyla like a gutpunch, as she does not want to be moving slaves at all. Lyla orders Salt-Eye to bring the girl anything she needs. Zadie Adeyemi enters and asks Captain Bonetooth what her orders are. Lyla looks at her crew and watches the shore some more. Lyla sighs. Finally Lyla says that her and Blacktide Cray will take a dingy into shore alone, with a white flag raised and speak to the Wrecking Crew themselves. Silas is not happy about this and says the Crew will kill them, Zadie agrees with Silas, saying it's a suicide run. Lyla asks Blacktide what he thinks and Blacktide tells her that where she goes, he goes. Lyla says it's settled and to prepare the dingy.

  - ### **Part 3**
  Inside the Wrecking Crew clubhouse, Jimmy Douglass, Mark Jeffrey and Selena Matissao are sitting and watching a trashflick film comedy. Jimmy thinks it's dumb but Mark is laughing his ass off at the movie and Selena is just enjoying Mark's reactions. Behind them Abel May Jr and Rodney Blythe are playing a tense game of Sliver when there is a frantic banging on the front doors. The crew look at each other before Rodney Blythe, the large red head bodyguard of the Crew walks to the door and answers. The fisherman is standing there panting breathlessly, desperately trying to communicate. Rodney watches the man and gets annoyed and assumes he's high on Luxyn or something until Katie Kowalski, the doctor of the Crew comes over and calmly introduces herself to the fisherman. The fisherman composes himself enough and explains to Rodney and Katie that the Black Marauder is pulling into the Rustwater Bay. Katie looks shocked, Rodney turns back inside and motions for Jimmy & Mark. Jimmy comes over and Rodney repeats what the fisherman said. Mark & Jimmy look at each other. Mark gets up and rings the big bell, signaling for the crew to assemble. The other members, Joe Ameen comes in from the garages, Lincoln Jones from his room and the rest. Jimmy stands in front of them, with Mark at his side. Jimmy tells them what the Fisherman said. Jimmy says the pirates are crossing boundries they know they shouldn't be crossing. Jimmy says if the Raiders want a war, we'll give them one. Mark tells the group to keep their heads and don't fire until word from either him or Jimmy. Mark tells the Crew it's time to ride out. Outside Jimmy, Mark, Abel, Selena, Rodney, Lincoln, Joe & Katie all get on and warm up their bikes before riding off to the Gage Park docks.

  - ### **Part 4**
The Wrecking Crew arrive on their motorcycles at the crest overlooking the docks as people part to let them pass and watch their protectors get to work. - Mark tells Selena Matissao to deal with the crowd. Selena gets the attention of the people and tells them for their safety they should leave the area. Selena's good with crowd control. - Jimmy Douglass and Lincoln Jones stand at the crest watching the Black Marauder out in the water. They're discussing the purpose of the unannounced visit when Jimmy notices something in the water. They look closer and see it's the dingy carrying Lyla and Blacktide. A white flag flying off of it. Jimmy calls Mark over. - Jimmy and Mark and Lincoln stand there watching the dingy get closer. They wonder if this is a trap or a set up of some kind. Finally Jimmy turns back and gathers the Crew. - The crew gather around Jimmy. Jimmy tells them that it looks like a dingy with two people are headed towards us. A white flag flying. Abel says it could be a trap. Everybody agrees. - The dingy is near the beach now so Jimmy, Mark and Abel May Jr. head down. As they're walking Abel mentions to them that Flint Garritt has invited Abel to the Final Reckoning fight as Flint's personal guest. Mark and Jimmy are shocked. Abel tells them Flint came to him the night of the confrontation between Abel and Bobby and offered him a contract. Abel tells them he hasn't signed it, but hasn't thrown it away either. Abel says he's thinking of going. Jimmy says it's not safe for him to go alone. Mark agrees, says the Wrecking Crew rides together. - The dingy pulls into the beach and Lyla and Blacktide step out about 100 yards away from Mark, Jimmy & Abel. For a time, both sides just glare at each other. Finally Lyla and Blacktide begin walking forward. Jimmy looks up and signals to the other crew members watching from the top of the crest and Jimmy, Mark & Abel begin walking too.

12.title: OUTLINES
12.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[OUTLINES]]

METADATA:{"cover":"zz_media/002.png","tags":["title"],"created":"2025/05/13 20:12:44","modified":"2025/06/09 09:39:55"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) - ### **Part 5**
The two sides move closer towards each other across the open beach. - Finally once eveybody is close, Mark stops about 20 paces behind and Jimmy and Abel walk to Lyla and Blacktide. - Jimmy says "You must be Lyla Bonetooth." Lyla corrects him and says it's Captain Lyla Bonetooth. Lyla says it's a pleasure to finally meet the legend Jimmy Douglass himself face to face. - Abel and Blacktide have stared at each other the whole time. - Jimmy tells Lyla her reputation preceeds her but it's an honor. Lyla commends Jimmy on leading Steeltown towards independence against The Duke. - Jimmy asks Lyla what she's doing here. Lyla eyes Jimmy for a moment, but tells him she is there for a favor. And since the Wrecking Crew didn't attack the moment The Raiders pulled into the bay, you might as well hear us out. - Abel and Blacktide continue to stare at each other. - Jimmy is surprised that the Rustwater Raiders need help from anybody. Lyla tells him it isn't help for them. It's help for the slaves on their ship. - Jimmy gets serious and asks what she means. - Lyla tells Jimmy that The Duke summoned the Raiders to The Silo in order for the Raiders to secretely deliver a group of slaves to Steeltown. - Jimmy is shocked. Jimmy says Slavery is outlawed in Steeltown. Lyla says she knows. - Jimmy demands to know who bought the slaves but Lyla says The Duke didn't tell her. - Abel and Blacktide continue to glare at each other. - Lyla tells Jimmy she feels the same way about slaves. She tells him that they came in here this way, making a grand entrance, so the Crew would know that we're not here for a fight. We're here to talk. - Jimmy asks Lyla what she wants him to do. Lyla says she wants the Crew to take the slaves from them. - Jimmy says if he takes them he's going to free them. Lyla says she knows. Jimmy says this will put a target on her back. Lyla says she knows that too. - Abel and Blacktide continue to glare at each other. - Jimmy turns from Lyla and calls over Mark Jeffrey. Jimmy introduces Mark to Lyla. Mark says it's an honor to meet Lyla Bonetooth. Lyla corrects him and says it's Captain Lyla Bonetooth. Mark smiles and apologizes. Lyla smiles back at Mark. - Jimmy tells Mark that the Raiders are here with slaves. Mark suddenly gets serious and says slavery ain't legal here. Jimmy fills Mark in and says they're going to take them and free them. - Abel and Blacktide stare. - Jimmy tells Mark to get the rest of the Crew. Mark notices Abel and Blacktide staring at each other and asks them what the hell is going on. - Abel says Blacktide is staring at him. Blacktide says Abel is staring at him! - Jimmy, Lyla and Mark watch as the big men argue about who is staring at who. - Finally Mark says he'll go get the others and leaves. - Lyla turns to Blacktide and tells him to settle down. - Jimmy looks Abel, who also backs off a bit. - Lyla tells Jimmy that Mark is amusing. Jimmy rolls his eyes and tells her if she only knew... - Lyla signals to the Black Marauder. After a time another dingy appears with a group of discheveled looking slaves on it. - The Wrecking Crew roll up and watch the slaves approaching. Jimmy introduces the Crew to Lyla. Katie especially is a fan of Lyla. Telling her that Lyla is an inspiration for women in Disgraceland. Lyla tells Katie that she is too. Katie is flattered Lyla even knows who she is. Lyla tells Katie that the Wrecking Crew is known in every corner of Disgraceland. - The slave dingy lands on the beach and Katie, Selena and Lincoln race over and help them. Katie being the doctor gets right to work. - The Crew members work on getting the slaves looked after. - Lyla walks over to Mark and says it was an honor to meet him and thank him for his help today. Mark smiles at Lyla and says she's welcome. Mark tells her that if she ever comes across slaves, she can bring them here and the Wrecking Crew will protect them. And Lyla, if needed. Lyla looks at Mark and knows he means it. - Lyla then moves to Jimmy and thanks him for his help. Jimmy nods and wishes her luck and they shake hands. - Lyla and Blacktide board the dingy. They watch the Wrecking Crew ride off. - Blacktide asks Lyla what she thought of the Crew. Lyla says they weren't what she expected. Blacktide says he wants to beat the fuck out of the "big one."

13.content:

METADATA:{"cover":"zz_media/002.png","tags":["title"],"created":"2025/05/13 20:12:44","modified":"2025/06/09 09:39:55"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ## Chapter 7
  
  - ### **Part 1**
At TTV Studios in Gravenwild, Charspire Morris Gable is preparing for that nights taping of Night Time with Morris Gable. He's at his desk on the main stage going over the notes. Morris is upset over a specific piece the station manager Owen McCready handed him. Owen tells Morris that it's a directive straight from The Duke's office. Morris is annoyed at The Duke's constant interference in his program but also knows where his bread is buttered, so goes along with everything. On the other end of the stage, the house band, The Wanderer's are tuning up. Their lead singer, Jaden Kade is watching Morris yelling at Owen. Jaden notices that Morris kept looking in his direction as Morris and Owen were talking. Owen tells Morris to do a dry-run on the new script pages and steps back. Morris turns on his stage persona and begins to read the new page The Duke insists be added. The page is detailing the upcoming Ashmoor Festival. Listing games, prizes, festivities, entertainment and so on, and ends noting there will be a special performance by The Wanderers. Jaden Kade and The Wanderers are shocked, being very anti-establishment they had no intention of attending. "Are you fucking kidding me?!" Jaden yells across the stage.
 
  - ### **Part 2**
Immediately Jaden Kade is pissed. He starts yelling at Owen McCready who pleads with Jaden that the directive came right from The Duke. Jaden tells Owen that he doesn't play music for fascists. Owen tells him he does every night. What, Jaden doesn't think fascists watch Night Time too? Jaden tells Owen The Wanderer's won't be at the Ashmoor Festival. Jaden says he thought the agreement was he'd play music for the show only. If he knew he'd be outsourced to propaganda parties he never would have taken the job. Owen tells him to take it up with The Duke because there is nothing he can do and he's sorry. He knows this goes against Jaden's principals. Owen tells Jaden to take some advice and just perform at the festival and make The Duke happy. No need to cause trouble. Jaden just shakes his head. Morris Gable was sitting at his desk watching Jaden yelling at Owen as he smoked on his cigar. He rubbed his temples and complained that he's getting too old for this shit. The Wanderer's did their job well as the house band but Jaden Kade was a bit too wild for the easy viewing program Morris strived to cultivate. Finally Morris yelled over that Owen was right and Jaden should just play the festival and move on. Jaden tells Morris to fuck off and that he's the biggest fucking sell-out in this building. Morris gets up and starts yelling back about how he's kept peace between the citizens and The Duke for almost a decade! What he does here at Night Time is important to the people! And if Jaden could pull his head out of his fucking ass for 5 seconds and think of something other than himself maybe he'd see that! Jaden yells back that Morris does his best to keep this whole nation subdued and under the thumb of the oppressive Duke. Jaden says Morris is a talking head for fascism and nothing more. Morris says the citizens deserve one hour of their day where they don't have to think about how awful their life is! Jaden sighs as he knows Morris has a point.

  - ### **Part 3**
  The door to the studios open and Warren Scottyard, the anchor for TTV Evening News walks onto the stage and says they can hear the yelling from the studio next door and if everything is alright over here? Morris tells his friend Warren that everything is good. They just received some "surprising" news is all. Warren leans closer to his friend Morris and asks if he needs any help dealing with "that one", motioning to Jaden. Morris sighs and tells Warren that Jaden reminds him of himself when he was that age. An idealistic entertainer, just trying to do right by people. Warren tells Morris people watch his show not out of obedience but because people genuinely love Morris. Morris thanks Warren and tells him sometimes he forgets that. Morris asks Warren what is on tap for the TTV Evening News tonight. Warren tells Morris "Loyalist guard and some whore dead in Gutter Row. Looks like some ritualistic killing or some such. And some dead-beat Luxyn dealer's gone missin' apparently." Morris sighs and smiles at Warren, they shake hands, Morris and Warren agree to have dinner soon and Warren leaves. Owen returns and asks Morris if he's ready for the full rehearsal. Morris says fine but both of them notice Jaden is gone. Owen says "Ember fuckin' damnit. This fuckin' kid." Morris asks how they're going to do the show with no music. Owen says he'll go talk to the rest of The Wanderers and see if they know where Jaden is. Morris goes back to his desk, smoking his cigar and reading over script notes when Owen returns saying Jaden isn't with the rest of the band and they don't know where he is. Morris is pissed off and says someone find Jaden's girlfriend, Cassidy LaRue.

14.title: OUTLINES
14.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[OUTLINES]]

METADATA:{"cover":"zz_media/002.png","tags":["title"],"created":"2025/05/13 20:12:44","modified":"2025/06/09 09:39:55"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) - ### **Part 4**
  High up on the rooftop of TTV Studios, Jaden Kade and his girlfriend Cassidy LaRue are in sitting in a spot that overlooks Gravenwild. A spot they've come to before. Cassidy pulls out the little baggy of Luxyn and tells Jaden that it's new stuff called "Lash's Glow" and is the strongest shit she has ever had. Jaden takes the baggy and bumps out a little line across Cassidy's mirror. He runs his nose across the fine white powder and throws his head back as the Luxyn hits his brain. He feels good. He feels better than good. He feels invincible. His eyeballs start to glow white. Cassidy smiles at him and says he looks cute when he glows. Cassidy sets up her own line and runs her nose across it, laughing as she does. Jaden and Cassidy sit there watching the city, eyes glowing high. Jaden tells Cassidy that The Duke is forcing him to perform at the Ashmoor Festival. Cassidy says fuck that and to ditch it and come be with her. Jaden says he just might do that. Jaden calls Owen and Morris two old, out of touch fuck-faces. Cassidy says if he hates it maybe he should leave the show. Jaden says he thinks that everyday, but then every Restday his slugs (money) come in and he tells himself just one more week. Cassidy tells Jaden he doesn't need the slugs, that they'd get by just fine. Maybe The Wanderer's could go on tour. Jaden and Cassidy do another bump of Luxyn. Eyes glowing even brighter. Jaden wonders if he keeps performing on Night Time, will he eventually become an old, out of touch fuck-face like Morris Gable. Cassidy laughs and kisses him. She tells him that she won't let that happen. The two laugh and make out, high on luxyn, eyes glowing. Suddenly there's a voice. "Well now. Isn't that a sweet tune." Cassidy and Jaden quickly look up and see Scumbag (Scumbag is a murderous psychopath, like The Joker.).

  - ### **Part 5**
Immediately at the sight of Scumbag, Jaden Kade stands upright, blocking the path between Cassidy and Scumbag. Jaden, eyes still glowing white, tells Scumbag he needs to get the fuck outta here. Scumbag laughs at him. He mentions how he doesn't usually find other people on the rooftops. Scumbag likes to think of the rooftops as his domain. Jaden asks him what the fuck he's talking about. Scumbag makes a joke about how he's babbling on again. Scumbag watches Jaden for a moment and it finally dawns on Scumbag that Jaden Kade is the lead singer of The Wanderers! Scumbag mock fan-girls out for meeting Jaden Kade. Scumbag says it's such a shame the beautiful music of The Wanderer's has to end tonight. Cassidy asks what that means. Scumbag says well since they've seen him, he can't let them leave, just like that. Cassidy starts to panic. Scumbag says to not blame him, he's just a product of the environment he grew up in, or so he's been told. Jaden tries to reassure Cassidy and says Scumbag has to get through him first. Scumbag suddenly goes serious and asks if Jaden is challenging him. Jaden looks at Scumbag, defiant, and says 'Take it any way you want, freak-show.' Scumbag says he chooses to take it as a challenge then. Scumbag raises his machete and steps at Jaden, but Jaden, holding the baggy of Lash's Glow, throws the powder into Scumbag's face. Scumbag is blinded by the Luxyn and Jaden throws his whole body into the larger Scumbag, sending Scumbag sprawling to the ground. Jaden quickly turns to Cassidy and grabs her, telling her to run. Cassidy runs past the downed Scumbag and to the door, as Jaden follows, Scumbag grabs his ankle. Jaden tries to fight him off but Scumbag gets back to his feet and begins hammering at Jaden with powerful fists. Jaden stunned, but tough in his own right, fights back. Blocking blows and throwing his own shots. Scumbag is laughing the whole time. Scumbag lunges for his machete and grabs it before Jaden can. Scumbag mocks Jaden and says "songs over." Scumbag gets serious and holds the machete high before a gunshot rings out over the rooftop. Scumbag and Jaden turn quickly and see Morris Gable standing there with Cassidy holding a smoking gun, pointed at Scumbag. Cassidy runs over to Jaden and Scumbag quickly darts into the shadows. Morris yells for him to stop but Scumbag has seemingly jumped off the roof and disappeared. 

  - ### **Part 6**
Minutes before showtime, people are busy backstage getting last minute details sorted before Night Time goes on the air at midnight. Jaden Kade is sitting in a small chair as a woman applies make-up to his wounds from the fight with Scumbag. Morris Gable comes over and asks Jaden how he is. Jaden says he's okay. Jaden stands up and extends his hand to Morris and thanks him for saving his ass tonight. Morris nods and shakes Jaden's hand. Morris tells Jaden the camera's won't cut to him too much tonight but the make-up looks great anyway, so he'll be okay on air. Morris asks Jaden if he knew who that guy (meaning Scumbag) was. Jaden says No. Jaden says if he ever sees him again he's going to kill him.

In a small room somewhere, lit up only by a television a man in the shadows stares at the television. The voiceover is announcing that nights show and guests before Morris Gable is introduced. Morris announces The Wanderers and Scumbag steps from the shadow glaring menacingly at the television as Jaden Kade is shown playing guitar. Scumbag looks incensed and mutters, "Oh I'm comin' for you now, boy."

(cont'd) ### Current Threads

- The Ashmoor Festival is coming up.
- The Final Reckoning fight is coming up.
- The Unseen Widows, Raina & Risa are hunting General Colt
- The Rustwater Raiders chose to not deliver the slaves. The Duke will be pissed.
- Mark & Lyla Bonetooth maybe flirted a bit.
- Lash Hawkins has been taken by Hella and Ora Razchek and Ava Victoria is trying to find him.
- Salem Quinn had his prophecy and is on his way to warn The Duke
- Veerah had the same prophecy but interpreted it as she needs to kill men.

### Notes:


- Nico goes to the Third Row for help moving Luxyn. Samson and the Row tell Nico that they are loyal to Lash Hawkins and suspect the Murray's to be involved. They won't help them.
- Raina & Risa assassinate General Colt. The Duke is furious and demands a full investigation
- Expand POUNDBALL more
- Raiders in Steeltown
- Ashmoor Festival
- Final Reckoning

- [[Bastian Redd]] will return as one of [[Ora Razchek]]'s A.I monsters.

- [[Hella]] is [[The Grim Man]]'s long lost sister. 

- Electricity is controlled by [[The Duke]].  
  
- Slavery is legal in Disgraceland, but loathed by the citizens. Slavery isn’t race-centric. Anybody can be a slave if born into it, sentenced to it, agreed to be purchased (which people would do for money for their families.), etc.

- Fuel is sold by The Duke only, though theft is a problem for him. The Duke recently began a large tax on the fuel he sells to his citizens. Hurting an already poor populace.  
  
- Most of Disgraceland is dirty and poor. With families living in make-shift homes or moving into old ruins.  
  
- Over the years construction and rebuilding has occurred, but The Duke focused most of the funds on Ashmoor and his home territory.  
  
- The Duke has insisted every residence have one Duke issued standard crt television that only broadcasts messages from The Duke. When the broadcast isn’t live, It’s showing images of The Duke.  

- The Duke’s Loyalist Guards have begun cracking down on dissenters and protestors more lately. People have gone missing and things are getting tense.

- There is a daily newspaper handled by a small printshop in Gutter Row. The Duke allows it because the owner has agreed to not speak poorly of The Duke. It’s called the Tribucia Tribute.

- Food is rationed to each family, or single person, twice a week at local markets sponsored by The Duke. It is illegal to grow your own food. Food is forcibly purchased at huge discounts from the Rancher Collective.
  
- CRT TV’s get hi-jacked by rebels at some point. Maybe Wrecking Crew? Not sure yet.

- CRT TV’s maybe sometimes flash random images of something?

- There’s a location somewhere with mysterious qualities.

21.title: TIMELINE
21.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[TIMELINE]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"lore","NoteStatus":"New","status":null,"tags":"home","cover":"zz_media/t1.png","created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/05/27 14:55:42"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ```
2109
The Water Wars Begin
Global freshwater sources collapse. Climate change and privatization spark brutal conflict. AI drones, high-tech weapons debut.
2113
The Northwest Sieges
Militias bombard northwest aquifers. Civilians suffer mass casualties.
2119
Collapse of Central Authority
Governments fall or become corporate shells. Borders dissolve. Cities become faction zones.
2121
The Tetra Bomb is Deployed
The war ends not in victory, but decimation. Cities vanish. Ash falls. Over 8 billion living organisms are eviscerated immediately.
2123–24
The Long Winter Ends
After the bomb, sun disappears. Crops die. Temperatures plummet. Survivors crawl back into daylight as the sky clears.
2124–44
The Dead Years
Two decades of warlords, scavengers, and failed rebuilds. Civilization collapses further. Technology lost. Chaos reigns.
2144
The Rise of the Duke
A 25-year-old future Duke begins rebuilding on the north-east banks of the Dead Waters. He calls the settlement Ashmoor and gathers followers with law, protection, and trade.
2145–70
The Founding of Tribucia
The Duke expands his reach. Some regions fall, others are bought. He names it United Tribucia. Locals mockingly call it Disgraceland.
2151
Steel Rises Again
Darrell Douglass restarts the first steelmill in Steeltown. The first fire since the war.
2153
Threshton Harvest
Harp Langston yields the first post-war harvest in Threshton. Food security starts to return.
2158
Duke Seizes Steeltown Industry
The Duke forces Darrell Douglass to produce steel for him under military pressure.
2164
Loyalist Guard Formed
The Duke and General Colt establish the Loyalist Guard to enforce order, crush rebellion, and protect the regime.
2165
Tribucia Takes Shape
Ashmoor, the Drownlands, Steeltown, and Threshton are officially unified as the founding territories of United Tribucia.
2169
Gutter Row Incorporated
Gutter Row is brought into Tribucia following purges and backdoor deals.
2167
Darrell Douglass Assassinated
Darrell is hanged for acts against the regime.
2171
Charspire Enters
Charspire joins Tribucia. Mayor Gorran Brile is appointed. Industrial slavery begins.
2177
The Steeltown Wrecking Crew Forms
Former allies of Darrell unite under his eldest son, forming a biker gang banner to protect the people. The Steeltown Wrecking Crew is born.
2180
Steeltown Declares Autonomy
After clashes and one-upping The Duke's Loyalist Guard repeatedly, the Steeltown Wrecking Crew secures Steeltown and declares it a free territory. The Duke is forced to accept, for now. An uneasy truce is born.
2186
Present Day
The Duke is 67. Slavery and corruption thrive. Prophets speak of the Reckoning Coil and The Second Birth. Something dark stirs underground.

22.title: WATER
22.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[WATER]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["water"],"cover":"zz_media/chars.png","Alignment":"Lawful Good","created":"2025/06/02 10:20:47","modified":"2025/06/02 16:45:25"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - water cover: zz_media/chars.png Alignment: Lawful Good --- # BODIES OF WATER IN TRIBUCIA

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎CHARSPIRE > ![[chars.png|400]] Water is both a source of survival and sorrow in Disgraceland. What little remains is poisoned, patrolled, or pulsing with death. These are the major bodies of water that shape the land, carve borders, and drown hope.

Bodies of Water


#### Sinners' Sea - South-West edge of Tribucia - If the [[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]] are cold and silent, the **Sinner’s Sea** is loud, lawless, and cursed by name. This roiling western ocean crashes against the black cliffs of [[Steeltown#The Hammer|The Hammer]] and seeps into [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] and the shanty wharfs of [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]]. Its waves smell like salt and rust, and its tides carry in wreckage, bones, and broken cargo from lands no longer listed on maps. Old sailors swear the sea shifts. That islands once charted vanish overnight, and strange lights flicker beneath the waves. It’s said that the worst criminals — the ones even [[The Duke]] won’t keep — are exiled into its current. No records, no trials, just pushed into the surf and forgotten. Despite the danger, this sea is not empty. Smugglers, pirates, and ghost-traders sail its chop. Some say they dock on hidden coves along the western cliffs. Others claim there’s a floating market far out past where compasses spin, where you can buy anything — if you’re willing to pay in memory or blood. - They call it the **Sinner’s Sea** because only the damned survive it. --- #### Rustwater Bay - Between [[Steeltown]] and [[Gutter Row]] - A polluted bay of orange-brown runoff from the broken mills and machine-yards of [[Steeltown]]. Thick with sludge and sharp with rust stink, the bay is technically navigable — but good luck finding a boat that’ll survive more than an hour. Gulls feed on ironfish here, and even the pirates give it a wide berth. --- #### Rustwater River - Runs inland from [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] - The toxic artery that cuts through [[Steeltown]] and spills into the gutters of [[Gutter Row]]. Locals sometimes use it for travel, and desperate scavengers paddle homemade rafts down it. Children born near it often have breathing issues. Some swear the river “talks” at night — whispering curses or laughter beneath the current. --- #### Grave Bay - Dead center of [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]] - A stagnant inland sea that once connected various trade routes. Now it sits thick and unmoving — a brackish grave for lost ferries, traitors, and political prisoners. The name isn’t poetic. Bodies float here, face-down or face-up, bloated and forgotten. On calm nights, people say the surface glows faintly red. Nobody knows why. --- #### The Dead Waters - The eastern coast of Tribucia. - The **Dead Waters** stretch endlessly east of [[Charspire]] and [[Gutter Row]], swallowing the coastlines of Burnt Coast, Broken Bones Bay, and the jagged Four Tombs Islands. It is the last known ocean in this ruined world — vast, lifeless, and unnavigable by ordinary means. No merchant ships cross it. No trade lanes exist. It’s said that even the storms avoid this water. The salt here tastes bitter, wrong. Fog banks roll in without warning, and massive skeletal fish sometimes wash up on the jagged shorelines, long dead and unidentifiable. The [[Unseen Widows]] believe the sea remembers the end of the old world — that it’s where the gods once drowned themselves after the [[Tetra Bomb]]. [[The Duke]] has declared it off-limits to all but official Loyalist craft, though even they rarely venture far from the coast. - Many say it’s not the sea that’s dead — it’s everything that enters it. --- #### Faded Lake - Far north, bordering [[Threshton]], [[The Drownlands]] & [[Ashmoor]] - A frigid inland lake shrouded in pale mist most of the year. Its waters are dark, and nothing reflects on its surface. [[Coffin Island]] Prison sits like a broken tooth in the center. Rumor claims the bottom of the lake is littered with chains, bones, and drowned inmates — and that the lake itself “remembers.” Some locals refer to it as _The Eye That Never Shuts._ --- #### Broken Bones Bay Named for what it gives, not what it takes. Broken Bones Bay is a jagged stretch of beach and black water, where rusted ship remains rot beside sun-bleached shanties. Kids fish with wire. Old folks drink sea-moonshine and stare out past the surf, muttering about shapes that move under the water. It’s a place for the unwanted, the forgotten, and those too stubborn to die inland. You don’t vacation here. You vanish here. ---

23.title: THRESHTON
23.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[THRESHTON]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","threshton","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/df.png","Alignment":"Lawful Good","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"working class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Marla Rusk"]],"region":["North-West Tribucia"],"size":"Small Farming Community","population":"13,000","religion":["Word of the Stillborn Star"],"exports":["Literally all of the food"],"imports":[null],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/05 14:35:12"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - threshton - territory cover: zz_media/df.png Alignment: Lawful Good Government: Mayor reputation: working class politics: Mayor leader: [[Marla Rusk]] region: - North-West Tribucia size: Small Farming Community population: 13,000 religion: - Word of the Stillborn Star exports: - Literally all of the food imports: - --- # THRESHTON

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎THRESHTON > ![[df.png|400]] Threshton is the dusty breadbasket of Disgraceland — a land of cracked soil, stubborn cattle, and long grudges. Stretching wide across the southern edge of the map, it’s where the grain grows, the livestock breeds, and the backbones break. The region feeds the rest of United [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]], but barely feeds itself. Every harvest is taxed by [[The Duke]]'s regime, skimmed off by crooked ledgers and escorted out by [[Loyalist Guard#**Amberforce**|Amberforce]], the brown-shirted enforcers who watch the silos closer than they watch the streets. At the heart of Threshton is the [[Rancher Collective]] — a loose and uneasy alliance of ranch owners who were once competitors, now forced to work together under pressure. Their ranches are sprawling compounds with weather-beaten fences and names that sound like threats: [[THRESHTON#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Bonebreak Ranch|Bonebreak Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Snake Kiss Ranch|Snake Kiss Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Red Night Ranch|Red Night Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Hangman's Ranch|Hangman’s Ranch]]. They meet under candlelight and spit into the same whiskey bottle when the deals are done. Officially, they only trade with the Duke. Unofficially, a good portion of their grain and meat finds its way into the hands of the hungry in [[Steeltown]] and [[Gutter Row]]. The region’s largest settlement is Farmington — not much more than a loose web of barns, bunkhouses, and crop mills, but it’s where the deals are struck and the rumors fly. Out here, the land is everything, and trust is rare. Outsiders aren't welcomed without purpose. Even the [[Loyalist Guard#**Amberforce**|Amberforce]] treads lightly. Threshton’s mayor, [[Marla Rusk]], is a wiry, sun-wrinkled woman who’s survived more droughts and shootouts than most men in Disgraceland. She’s not part of the Collective, but she knows how to play them against each other when she needs to. The Duke appointed her to keep the food flowing and the workers in line — but whether she truly answers to him, or to the people of Threshton, is an open question. She smiles like a rattlesnake. Keeps a shotgun in the room during every meeting. And no one — not even the ranchers — wants to be alone with her for too long.

Districts

#### Double Cross Ranch Westernmost and best run, **Double Cross Ranch** is [[Turner Anderson]]'s empire of dirt and precision. The docks hum with activity day and night, moving food across Tribucia like lifeblood through veins. Anderson’s operation is smooth, strict, and respected. Workers here know their roles, the land stays clean, and the books are balanced. If something fails, it gets fixed. If someone fails, they’re gone. --- #### Red Night Ranch [[Harp Langston]]'s legacy is carved into the soil of **Red Night Ranch**, the oldest in Tribucia. It’s where the first post-bomb harvest grew, a turning point etched into every Tribucian textbook — but here, it's religion. Named for the crimson sky the night Harp and his wife staked their claim, the ranch is sacred to some, mythic to others. The land remembers, and Harp walks it like a man guarding memory with a shotgun. --- #### Hangman's Ranch Won in a game of [[Sliver]] and managed like a tavern with cattle, **Hangman’s Ranch** belongs to [[Beau DuNoir]]. It hugs the border of Steeltown’s [[Steeltown#West Mountain|West Mountain]], and if the ranch itself runs well, that’s thanks to the actual ranchers. Beau's often too busy drinking, gambling, or charming someone he shouldn't. Parties at Hangman’s are legendary. So are the debts. But the cattle still come fat and the grain gets weighed — somehow. --- #### Bonebreak Ranch If you hear a whip crack in Threshton, it’s probably coming from **Bonebreak Ranch**. [[Freddy Blanchard]] runs it hard, runs it clean, and works the land like he's still proving something. It’s the most productive of the ranches, known across Disgraceland for its meat — thick, red, and tough like the men who raise it. Blanchard doesn’t smile much. His ranch speaks for him. --- #### Snake Kiss Ranch The runt of the land. **Snake Kiss Ranch** used to be a thriving estate until [[Danny Dandelion]] talked the elderly widow Greta Harp into signing it over. Since then, the place has slipped into disrepair, with fences falling and workers walking. Danny talks big, dresses louder, and pretends he’s one of the boys. He isn’t. The other ranchers know it. Snake Kiss is a joke — and Danny’s the punchline nobody laughs at. --- #### Split Rest Far north, where Threshton touches the Wildlands and Gravebay, sits **Split Rest** — a trading outpost turned district. Supplies, tools, weapons, smokes — it’s all here, alongside the mayor’s home and a few dusty bars that stay open too late. The winds from the bay carry secrets, and locals say the Wildlands howl at night. Split Rest is where civilization ends and something stranger begins. ---

25.title: THE DROWNLANDS
25.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[THE DROWNLANDS]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","drownlands","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/drown.png","Alignment":"Lawful Neutral","Government":"None","reputation":"feared","politics":"None","leader":"None","region":["North Tribucia"],"size":"Large wooded area","population":"Unknown","religion":["Faith of Mirella"],"exports":["None"],"imports":["None"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/05/28 11:15:50"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - drownlands - territory cover: zz_media/drown.png Alignment: Lawful Neutral Government: None reputation: feared politics: None leader: None region: - North Tribucia size: Large wooded area population: Unknown religion: - Faith of Mirella exports: - None imports: - None --- # THE DROWNLANDS

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎A SWAMP IN THE DROWNLANDS > ![[drown.png|400]] A place older than the fall. The Drownlands slither in the lowlands east of Ashmoor, a haunted quilt of drowned trees, rotted boardwalks, and fog that never lifts. Some call it a swamp, but that word doesn't do it justice. It's a breathing thing — a tangled forest of gnarled cypress and ash, their roots strangled in black water, their limbs hung with funeral moss. The air smells of wet bark, fungal rot, and something sweet underneath, like the perfume of something long dead still clinging to its bones. Sunlight barely filters through the canopy here. Instead, the world is lit in pale greens and grays, reflections of half-light on slick water. Frogs croak like old engines. Insects hum in strange rhythms. Every so often, you might hear the slap of something large slipping beneath the surface — and if you're smart, you don't go looking. The Unseen Widows rule these parts. Women clad in black, silent and swift, they watch from the shadows, veiled faces peeking between the moss. Most folks believe they’re witches, or ghosts, or both. But the Widows follow one woman only — **Veerah**, their Prophet. They say she sees the future in her sleep. They say her dreams come true. They say no man who walks into the heart of the Drownlands returns unchanged… if he returns at all. People steer clear, and for good reason. The land doesn’t welcome strangers. Paths vanish. Trees move. Your voice doesn’t echo here, it sinks. The Drownlands aren’t just a place. They’re a warning. And they remember you.

26.title: GUTTER ROW
26.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[GUTTER ROW]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","gutter row","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/gutt1.png","Alignment":"Unlawful Evil","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"trash class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Cricket Granger"]],"region":["South Tribucia"],"size":"Township","population":"88,000","religion":["Church of the Ember Saint"],"exports":["Power, Authority"],"imports":["Everything"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/05 17:07:55"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - gutter row - territory cover: zz_media/gutt1.png Alignment: Unlawful Evil Government: Mayor reputation: trash class politics: Mayor leader: [[Cricket Granger]] region: - South Tribucia size: Township population: 88,000 religion: - Church of the Ember Saint exports: - Power, Authority imports: - Everything --- # GUTTER ROW

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎GUTTER ROW > ![[gutt1.png|400]] Gutter Row is the choking heart of Disgraceland — a lawless sprawl of rusted rooftops, splintered alleyways, and desperate humanity. It's where the black market thrives, the weak vanish, and the rules don’t apply. Smoke curls from every rooftop. The streets reek of sweat, piss, rot, and fried rat. You don’t come here unless you have to — and if you do, you don’t linger. By far the most overpopulated zone in all of United Tribucia, Gutter Row stretches endlessly in every direction, packed shoulder-to-shoulder with shanties, scrap-built towers, and narrow corridors crawling with barterers, thieves, and worse. The economy runs on favors, smuggling, and the unspoken understanding that everything — and everyone — has a price. The slave trade operates in plain sight, tucked just behind the street food vendors and stolen tech booths. Locals carve their lives out in the districts of [[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]], [[GUTTER ROW#Nailstooth|Nailstooth]], [[GUTTER ROW#Pisstown|Pisstown]], [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]], [[GUTTER ROW#Reapton|Reapton]], Garbage Bay, and [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]] — each one worse than the last, each with its own twisted rhythm. There's no safety, only familiarity. People grow up fast here. Or they don’t grow up at all. The so-called police force is a unit known as [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]], though most call them _Black Shirts_. Dressed in matte black armor with emotionless masks and reinforced batons, they patrol sporadically — more interested in keeping tribute flowing to [[The Duke]] than protecting anyone. When they do show up, it’s usually to silence someone who said too much. Gutter Row isn’t just where the forgotten live. It’s where power hides. Where secrets are bought in whispers. And where a match, dropped in the right place, could burn the whole rotten thing down.

Districts

#### Vileby The black heart of Gutter Row. **Vileby** is where the Three Nail Market churns night and day, pumping illicit deals into every vein of Tribucia. [[Third Row]] gang runs things from the shadows — and sometimes not-so-shadowy rooftops. Vileby Hills rises just north, where the [[Murray Boys]] hold court in their fortified mansion. It’s the only place in Gutter Row where guards wear suits, and deals end with champagne instead of switchblades. --- #### Nailstooth A place even Gutter Row winces at. **Nailstooth** is where you land when you’ve got nothing left — not even the decency to die in a proper alley. It’s all rusted iron, tar-paper roofs, and barking dogs with ribs showing. The ground smells like rot. The people don't flinch when guns go off. You don’t walk into Nailstooth. You get dragged there. --- #### The Docks Southernmost point in all of Tribucia, **The Docks** is a salt-bitten maze of boats, rusted cranes, and rat-infested boardwalks. Fishermen haul in whatever the Dead Waters will spare, and families scrape by in tide-worn homes. When the fog rolls in, it feels like the world ends here — and maybe it should. --- #### Crossyork If Gutter Row has a postcard, it's **Crossyork** — and even that’s water-stained and half-torched. The mayor lives here behind iron bars and blackout curtains, trying to pretend the rest of the Row doesn’t exist. But the Rustwater Raiders haven’t forgotten. They hit often, sailing in from the Four Tombs Islands just off the coast. Crossyork smells like brine, smoke, and fresh betrayal. --- #### Pisstown No place bleeds like **Pisstown**. It’s where dreams die screaming and legends are born twisted. [[Dusty Dillon]] grew up singing in the alleys here. [[Ora Razchek]] built his death house above it all. And somewhere in the fog, [[The Grim Man]] stalks like a goddamn ghost with a grudge. Pisstown’s streets eat souls and spit bones. If you’re here, you’ve already lost something. --- #### Reapton They call it the working spine of Gutter Row — bent, cracked, and somehow still upright. **Reapton** is where the [[Tribucia Tribute]] gets printed, and where proud folks grind out survival without a safety net. It's paperboys dodging knives. It's ink-stained hands and busted typewriters. If Gutter Row has a conscience, it’s buried somewhere beneath Reapton’s mud. --- #### Savage Hill Everything’s louder in **Savage Hill**. The wind off Garbage Coast blows sour through these streets, but laughter still rises above it — the kind that hides pain. The **Ha Ha Hole** comedy club lights up the block, defiant and alive. Outside, trash fires burn, rats riot, and broken TVs scream static. But inside, jokes land harder than fists. --- #### South Point Close to Ashmoor, far from the madness. **South Point** is a sleepy stretch where a few local farmers till what land they can. The soil’s no good, the water’s worse, but the air isn’t poison and the nights are quiet. Folks here keep their heads down and their fences mended. It ain’t paradise — but it ain’t Pisstown either. --- #### Red Light District Vice without apology. **The Red Light District** is Gutter Row's fever dream, lit by flickering neon and fueled by broken morals. The **Hollow House**, run by [[Shana]], is the beating heart — a brothel, a fortress, a sanctuary of sin. Luxyn dealers, synth clubs, fight dens. You want it, it’s here. Just remember, payment comes due — one way or another. ---

27.title: STEELTOWN
27.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[STEELTOWN]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","steeltown","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/s5t.png","Alignment":"Lawful Good","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"working class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Ellis Westmount"]],"region":["South-west Tribucia"],"size":"Small City","population":"54,000","religion":["Word of the Stillborn Star"],"exports":["Steel, Auto"],"imports":["Everything they need"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/05/31 19:35:27"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - steeltown - territory cover: zz_media/s5t.png Alignment: Lawful Good Government: Mayor reputation: working class politics: Mayor leader: [[Ellis Westmount]] region: - South-west Tribucia size: Small City population: 54,000 religion: - Word of the Stillborn Star exports: - Steel, Auto imports: - Everything they need --- # STEELTOWN

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎STEELTOWN > ![[s5t.png|400]] Steeltown is a rustbucket miracle. A defiant patchwork of soot-streaked buildings and stubborn souls holding tight to dignity with oil-stained hands. Once the fire-belching pride of pre-Tetra industry, this was where steel was born and rails were fed across the continent. Now? It's a smoldering husk of its former self… and still somehow, impossibly, alive. The chimneys still cough black smoke like dying lungs. Oil drums burn on every corner just to beat back the frost, and market stalls burst out between rusted scaffolds and slag piles like weeds through concrete. What little industry survives does so through spit, weld, and willpower, jury-rigged machines, local scrapworks, and makeshift furnaces that forge just enough parts, just enough weapons, just enough hope to keep the fires lit. It's a town that shouldn't work anymore. But it does. Districts like [[STEELTOWN#Mohawk Valley|Mohawk Valley]] and [[STEELTOWN#Cannon|Cannon]] house most of the laborers, rough-and-tumble families living stacked in old brick tenements or boxcar shanties. [[STEELTOWN#Gage Park|Gage Park]] is where the kids play and the river cuts through. [[STEELTOWN#Barton|Barton]] is home to the Mayor and other more affluent citizens of [[Steeltown]]. [[STEELTOWN#The Hammer|The Hammer]] is where the hard fishermen make their living. The southern most point of [[Steeltown]], bordering the Sinner's Sea. Officially, **[[BLUEFORCE]]** patrols these streets — [[The Duke]]’s sanctioned peacekeepers, dressed in crisp blue uniforms and stiff regulation. But the people call them **Blue Shirts**, mostly with a sneer, and they don’t hold the reins here. Not really. The real law is written in exhaust fumes and tire tracks by the **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**, a biker gang turned protectorate. Their clubhouse flies the colors over an old foundry, and their presence alone keeps most slavers, thieves, and Loyalist enforcers from pushing too hard. There’s a balance here, but it’s a bloody one. **Mayor [[Ellis Westmount]]**, a former union-buster from [[Ashmoor]], rules like a boot on the throat, pushing The Duke’s taxes, cracking down on trade. But the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] doesn't take orders from city hall. Not really. They raid Loyalist convoys when the shipments get too fat, free slaves smuggled in from **Charspire**, and sometimes, if the mood's right, torch a Blue Shirt patrol car just to remind everyone who really owns these streets. Steeltown’s people live hard, die young, and laugh anyway. They drink strong, love rough, and wear their scars like medals. They’re not waiting for liberation. They _are_ liberation, a quiet resistance of grease-stained hands and midnight deals. And if rebellion ever truly sparks across Disgraceland, it won’t begin in a palace or a chapel. It’ll start here. In [[STEELTOWN#Gage Park|Gage Park]]. With steel, smoke, and a war cry carried on the wind. ---

Districts

#### Gage Park Closest to the poisoned banks of the Rustwater River, Gage Park is where [[Steeltown]] breathes in the smoke and spits back grit. Cranes creak above rusted docks, unloading shipments by day and bodies by night. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] keep their clubhouse here, casting a long shadow over the bay. South of Gage Park, the Rustwater Bay churns with sludge and secrets, a dark vein feeding the territory's lifeblood. --- #### Barton They call Barton the crown of Steeltown, but that crown’s cracked and copper green. It’s where Mayor [[Ellis Westmount]] lives behind reinforced glass, and the streetlamps actually work. The folk here aren't rich by [[Ashmoor]] standards, but they’ve got roofs, clean shirts, and enough distance from the riots to sleep easy. Barton pretends the rest of Steeltown doesn’t exist, and most days, it succeeds. --- #### Mohawk Valley The beating, bleeding heart of Steeltown. Mohawk Valley is a labyrinth of flame-belching stacks, collapsing row houses, and workers who haven’t taken a full breath in years. It’s the biggest district, packed with families who eat steel dust and shit rust. You don’t move to Mohawk. You survive it. Factory whistles mark the hours, and fists mark everything else. --- #### Cannon Up near Knuckles Lake, Cannon sprawls like a bad idea that never stopped growing. Steelworkers who couldn’t squeeze into [[STEELTOWN#Mohawk Valley|Mohawk Valley]] built shacks between half-finished homes and forgotten projects. Cannon’s a maze of contradictions, where kids play ball beside men with lung burns, and every decent street's got a burned-out twin. It’s loud, proud, and on the edge of boiling over. --- #### The Hammer Way down south, where [[Steeltown]] kisses the sea, lies The Hammer. Don’t let the pretty beaches fool you—this place works. Fishermen drag nets at dawn, while smugglers move food from [[Threshton]] under tarps and half-truths. The Hammer’s where meals are made, fish are gutted, and sea-worn families cling to the only honest trade left. It smells like salt, diesel, and fried eel. --- #### East Mountain Rising above the smoke and grind, East Mountain is forested, quiet, and strange. A far cry from the steel districts below, this is sacred land to followers of the [[El Santo]] faith. At its peak sits the Cathedral of [[the Grand Mascara]], white-stone and gold, visible for miles on a clear day. Pilgrims hike wooded trails while old-timers claim to see spirits in the trees. You don’t go to East Mountain to make noise. You go to listen. ---

29.title: CHARSPIRE
29.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[CHARSPIRE]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","charspire","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/chars.png","Alignment":"Lawful Good","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"working class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Gorren Brile"]],"region":["East Tribucia"],"size":"Small City","population":"74,000","religion":["Word of the Stillborn Star"],"exports":["Textiles, rubber, ore, minerals, etc."],"imports":["Barely anything"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/05/31 19:34:02"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - charspire - territory cover: zz_media/chars.png Alignment: Lawful Good Government: Mayor reputation: working class politics: Mayor leader: [[Gorren Brile]] region: - East Tribucia size: Small City population: 74,000 religion: - Word of the Stillborn Star exports: - Textiles, rubber, ore, minerals, etc. imports: - Barely anything --- # CHARSPIRE

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎CHARSPIRE > ![[chars.png|400]] Charspire is a choking wound in the heart of Disgraceland — a sprawling industrial hellscape belching smoke into the sky day and night. The air is thick with soot, the ground slick with oil, and the people look half-dead before they even finish their morning shift. This is where machines come to feed and men come to die. Massive factories grind endlessly through the days, pulling ore from the black guts of [[CHARSPIRE#Smashstock|Smashstock]] The city is ruled by Mayor [[Gorren Brile]], a bloated rat of a man whose appointment came directly from **[[The Duke]]** himself. Short, round, and always sweating, **Brile** lords over the region like he’s royalty — perched high in his rust-stained tower, surrounded by sycophants and paid women. He wears a cracked monocle like it gives him class, but everyone knows he’s filth. He’s not just corrupt, he _is_ corruption. A man with no loyalty, no shame, and no bottom. If selling his own mother would buy him another month in power, he’d ask for a discount on the rope. The streets of [[CHARSPIRE#Dog City|Dog City]] and [[CHARSPIRE#Burnt Coast|Burnt Coast]] are a mess of flickering red lights, chainlink fences, and hunger. Workers drag their boots through blood-slick alleys to get to illegal bunkhouses, while gangs patrol the districts with homemade blades and black market guns. Brile’s enforcers, the **[[Redforce]]** — or _Red Shirts_, as the people bitterly call them — stomp through neighborhoods like gods in cheap uniforms. They don’t solve problems. They cause them. If you’re poor and bleeding, you stay that way. If you complain, you disappear. There’s one district where the lights never go out — [[CHARSPIRE#Fistfront|Fistfront]]. Part brothel, part trap, it’s where Brile indulges most of his appetites. Drugs, girls, men, slaves, whatever. Nobody keeps count anymore. It’s a festering playground for the worst kind of men, and the only ones who rise here are the ones who’ve already given up their souls. But even here, the fires of revolt still flicker in shadow. Whispers in the alleys. Weapons stashed beneath bunkbeds. Maps hidden under floorboards. One day, Charspire will burn — and not from the furnaces this time.

Districts

#### Gravenwild A little less choked, a little more forgotten — Gravenwild sits on the western edge of Charspire like a cigarette burn on a silk sheet. It's rural by Charspire standards, but it hosts [[TTV Studios]], the black heart of propaganda where [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] and the [[TTV Evening News]] drip-feed the public their nightly lullabies. The fields are dry, the roads cracked, but the broadcast towers shine like teeth. Gravenwild keeps smiling, even when nobody’s watching. --- #### Dog City Stacked metal and spit. Dog City’s a tangled shantytown built from shipping crates, scrap, and hope that never arrived. It houses the miners and laborers of [[CHARSPIRE#Smashstock|Smashstock]], packed in shoulder-to-shoulder and drunk off fumes. Kids play in soot, women barter for water, and every fourth face’s got a scar worth hearing about. Call it what it is — a kennel for broken workers waiting to be put down. --- #### Burnt Coast As clean as Charspire ever gets. The Burnt Coast stretches along the Dead Waters’ edge, lined with weary trees and soot-washed skies. Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] lives here, tucked in his polished estate, away from the stink of his city. The district’s name comes from the fires that used to rage here after the [[Tetra Bomb]] fallout, but these days, it’s calm. Quiet. Dangerous in a different way. --- #### Smashstock This is where the air chews back. Smashstock is a sprawling industrial hell where [[Clay Industries]] runs the mines and furnaces without pause. Smoke chokes the sky, the ground trembles with drills, and the people — if you can call them that — are worked like mules. Slaves, mostly. It’s also where the [[Blackshift Massacre]] happened, when a protest was met with fire and steel. Nobody speaks of it out loud. But everyone remembers. --- #### The Molten Zone Northern Charspire is home to something worse than just smoke and ash. The Molten Zone is a cordoned-off wasteland, where slag fields glow under cracked earth and old structures hum with buried power. [[The Duke]]’s signs call it “Restricted.” Locals call it cursed. Rumor has it something was unearthed during a deep-core dig — not a resource, but a structure. Now RedForce patrols the perimeter in shifts, and anyone caught inside gets vaporized or vanishes. Maybe both. --- #### Fistfront Where [[Gutter Row]] spills into Charspire like a cut that won’t clot. Fistfront’s got the shops, food stalls, and scavenger markets that [[CHARSPIRE#Dog City|Dog City]] doesn’t. It’s where desperate folks go to trade stories for bullets, or meat for meds. The guards patrol here more often, but not out of kindness — this is the corridor where loyalty is bought, sold, and lost. Nobody smiles in Fistfront unless they’re selling something or about to steal it. ---
