31.title: ASHMOOR
31.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[ASHMOOR]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","ashmoor","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/ashmoor.png","Alignment":"Unlawful Evil","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"elite class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Soria Langston-Clay"]],"region":["North-East Tribucia"],"size":"Township","population":"22,000","religion":["Church of the Ember Saint"],"exports":["Power, Authority"],"imports":["Everything"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/04 11:11:38"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - ashmoor - territory cover: zz_media/ashmoor.png Alignment: Unlawful Evil Government: Mayor reputation: elite class politics: Mayor leader: [[Soria Langston-Clay]] region: - North-East Tribucia size: Township population: 22,000 religion: - Church of the Ember Saint exports: - Power, Authority imports: - Everything --- # ASHMOOR

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎SOUTH OF DIAMOND VALLEY, ASHMOOR > ![[ashmoor.png|400]] Ashmoor is the glittering jewel of the ruined world. The polished lie at the heart of Disgraceland. This is where [[The Duke]] sits on his rusted throne in [[The Silo]], surrounded by towers of steel and glass rising like teeth from the carcass of the old world. In the years following the [[Tetra Bomb]], Ashmoor was the first region rebuilt, and it shows. Roads are paved. Lights stay on. The air smells of expensive oil and perfumed sewage. While the rest of Tribucia struggles and rots, Ashmoor gleams with a fresh coat of power. At the center of Ashmoor is [[The Silo]], a towering spire of metal and surveillance that houses The Duke’s command center, archives, and inner sanctum. Surrounding it are sprawling districts like [[ASHMOOR#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]], known for its manmade lake and private boat clubs, and [[ASHMOOR#Knifedale|Knifedale]], home of the Loyalist Guard. [[ASHMOOR#Hush Town|Hush Town]], a walled off fortress of doomsday cottages the elite of Tribucia plan to escape to in case of revolt. Law enforcement in Ashmoor is handled by the [[Greenforce]], a brutal, heavily equipped police unit known as the _Green Shirts_ by locals. Their armor is olive-dipped and their tactics are blunt. They do not ask questions. They do not negotiate. They are loyal to the Duke alone, and every citizen knows it. In Ashmoor, smiling wrong gets you watched. Speaking wrong gets you disappeared. This is not a place for dreamers. It’s a city of deals, debt, and double-crosses—where power is currency and silence is survival.

Districts

#### The Silo A gleaming rot at the heart of Ashmoor. The Silo isn’t just the name of the white-stone palace where [[The Duke]] resides, it's the name of the district built around it — a carefully manicured 11-mile zone carved out of privilege and paranoia. Security checkpoints dot the streets, and visitors walk with straight backs and quiet mouths. Grave Bay laps softly at the Silo’s edge, but the real danger is inside, where whispered orders reshape Disgraceland by the hour. --- #### Diamond Valley Polished to a shine no one asked for, Diamond Valley is where the power sleeps. Renovated plantation homes line the hills, each more obscene than the last. [[Jacoban Clay]] & [[Soria Langston-Clay]]. [[Flint Garritt]]. [[Warren Scottyard]]. These are the names carved into the gates, each estate fenced and flanked by private guards. The streets are smooth, the lawns trimmed, and the silence enforced. Diamond Valley doesn’t just house the elite — it hides them. --- #### Amber Valley Just a little further out from the rotunda glamour of Diamond Valley lies Amber, the quieter cousin with a matching bloodline. The properties here are still large, still clean, but the fences are lower and the names on the mailboxes carry a little less weight. Rising stars, minor Loyalist officials, and ambitious merchants make their homes here, hoping one day to be invited uphill. It’s all glass, stucco, and ambition. --- #### Homa Point Named for Homa Bahram, the explorer who never made it back, Homa Point juts out over rocky cliffs and stares down the Wildlands with stubborn defiance. The district carries a kind of haunted reverence, more memorial than neighborhood. There are some settlements here — modest cabins, weather posts, and ranger stations — but most folks avoid it. The wind screams at night, and some say it carries Homa’s last breath. --- #### Greencove Greencove is a rare pocket of quiet in Ashmoor — a northern stretch of forest bordering the eerie Faded Lake. It’s mostly used by wealthy hunters, off-duty officers, and those who need to disappear for a few days. Old wood lodges creak beside still waters, and mist curls through the trees like it’s listening. Locals say the lake whispers at dawn. Nobody’s tried to prove it. --- #### Hush Town A fortress disguised as a retreat. Hush Town is a walled district pressed up against Faded Lake and brushing the edge of [[The Drownlands]]. Behind its reinforced gates lie massive doomsday cottages — panic mansions, really — built for the elite in case Ashmoor burns. Bunkers, satellite dishes, emergency stores. It’s where the powerful plan to wait out the end of the world. The place is armed to the teeth, but they still call it a “getaway.” --- #### Knifedale Knifedale cuts through the territory like its name implies. Home to the main Loyalist Guard training compound and the largest base in Ashmoor, it’s a district of barracks, kill-houses, and saluting. New recruits bleed on the gravel here while high-ranking officers bark from polished steps. Most civilians aren’t allowed in, but the ones who live nearby have learned to sleep through gunfire and marching boots. ---

# 🜨 Word of the Stillborn Star

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of El Santo
> ![[ss.png|400]]  

> **"The silence between the stars is not emptiness. It is Galliah, watching, waiting, and remembering us all."**


**Word of the Stillborn Star** is the oldest organized religion in the world of Disgraceland. Its roots stretch back to the age of ancient cities and lost empires—when astronomers gazed up and wrote of a silent, failed sun named **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**.  The faith is cold, patient, and relentless. Believers see all things as cycles, destined to fade and restart when **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** finally awakens. Rituals are stark and quiet. Theirs is a god that speaks only through absence.

## Core Beliefs

- **Galliah, the Stillborn Star:**  
  A celestial body that never ignited—trapped between birth and death. **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** is both god and warning, a promise that everything ends and begins again.
- **The Echo of Silence:**  
  Silence is holy. The world is full of lies and noise, but truth is found in what is *not* said. Temples and homes of the faithful are austere and eerily quiet.
- **The Great Reset:**  
  One day, when corruption overtakes the world, **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** will “ignite,” burning everything to ash and starting the cycle anew.
- **Prophecy of Return:**  
  When omens align, the First Stillborn (the living prophet) will lead the faithful to “witness the Dawnless Light”—the sign of Galliah’s return.

---

## History

- **Founded by Mesh'den:**  
  Once a lonely astronomer-priest, Mesh'den claimed to hear **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s voice in the silence. His followers, called **Stillborns**, swept through ancient cities and unified warring tribes with their chilling faith.
- **First Religion of the Old World:**  
  For centuries, it was the dominant faith. Many early texts, city laws, and holidays are rooted in Stillborn doctrine.
- **Decline and Survival:**  
  Overtaken in influence by the Ember Church and others, Stillborns are now a minority, but remain respected (and sometimes feared) for their age and mystery.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Silence Hour:**  
  At dusk, followers meditate in silence, facing the eastern sky.
- **Ash Oath:**  
  Vows are sworn over cold ashes—a reminder that all things fade.
- **Star Vigil:**  
  On the first new moon of each year, all Stillborns gather for a night-long silent vigil, watching the sky for Galliah’s sign.
- **Names of the Faithful:**  
  Most adherents take a second name in old tongue (“-ah” or “-en” suffix) after completing the Rite of Stillness.

---

## Symbols

- **The Unlit Star:**  
  A black circle with a faint lavender halo—**[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s mark.
- **Chains of Renewal:**  
  Interlocking rings, symbolizing endless cycles.

---

## Structure

- **First Stillborn:**  
  The living prophet, said to channel **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s will. The First Stillborn leads all major rites and appoints regional Speakers.
- **Speakers:**  
  Local religious heads, guardians of doctrine and silent keepers of the faith.
- **Lay Stillborns:**  
  Everyday followers; expected to maintain silence, charity, and ritual observance.

---

## Influence

- **Law & Time:**  
  The Disgraceland calendar was originally structured by Stillborn priests. Many laws about contracts, death, and inheritance come from their traditions.
- **Temples:**  
  Ancient, spartan buildings—many now ruined or repurposed by newer faiths.

---

## Holy Days

- **Day of Quiet (last day of the year):**  
  All work stops at dusk. The world is meant to fall silent—no music, no fire, no words—until dawn.
- **Vigil of Ashes (midyear):**  
  The faithful gather, burn old regrets and tokens, and let the ashes scatter at sunrise.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "We are the dust that dreams of fire."
- "When Galliah wakes, so too shall the world sleep."
- "Truth lives where sound dies."

---

## Notable Figures

- **Mesh'den:**  
  Founder and “First Stillborn.”  
- **Current First Stillborn:**  
  (Name open for your input—can flesh out if you want.)

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Bitter rivals in the old world—Ember preaches action, Stillborns preach patience.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Little direct conflict; both are considered “old faiths.”  
- **El Santo:**  
  Not directly opposed—Stillborns view El Santo as a regional offshoot or heresy.

---

> *“All things end in silence, but Galliah’s silence is never empty.”*

---

# Overview of Religions in Disgraceland:



### **[[Church of the Ember Saint]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** This is the **wealthiest and most widespread faith** in Disgraceland. It reveres the **Ember Saint**, a legendary figure who braved fire to save hundreds during the Burning of Prattia, an ancient city. Followers believe that **suffering is a forge**, through which the faithful emerge stronger, and that fire purifies without destroying. **Service to others is sacred**, while hoarding wealth or power is considered heresy.
- **Practices & Traditions:** They follow the **Ember Book** of parables and conduct **Rites of Passing** where the dead are cremated and a single ember is given to the family. Monthly, they light communal fires on **Ember Day** for storytelling and sharing food, and hold a **Saint’s March** with lanterns on the anniversary of the Great Fire.
- **Symbols:** The **Burning Halo** (a golden ring of flame) and the **Unburned Hand** (a palm surrounded by stylized fire).
- **Structure:** Before the Water Wards they were led by the **High Flame (Pontiff)**, chosen from the **Council of Embers** (senior clergy), with **Redrobes** serving as priests/priestesses, and **Lay Faithful** as everyday followers. Today it's an unorganized religion.
- **Influence:** Their cathedrals, even if ruined, remain **symbols of hope**. Ember celebrations unite people, including non-believers. Figures like [[Bobby Cutman]], [[Dusty Dillon]], and the Murray family members (Marco, Rosa, Francis, Nico) are listed as followers.
- **Relationships:** They are **bitter rivals** with the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] and **somewhat opposed** to the [[Faith of Mirella]] due to differing elemental outlooks (fire vs. earth). They have **strong mutual respect** with the Faith of [[El Santo]].

### **[[Faith of Mirella]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** This is an **ancient, secretive, and feared** faith tied to swamps, bogs, and shadowed waters. Followers believe the world itself recoiled from mankind's violence, and the sleeping goddess **Mirella (the Sleeping Mother)** waits for women to reclaim what was lost. **Men are considered dangerous, expendable, or cursed** by birth. The faith emphasizes **prophecy, visions, and blood rites**, believing Mirella’s dreams shape fate and her will is revealed through them.
- **Practices & Traditions:** Initiates wear **black veils** as a symbol of mourning, secrecy, and solidarity. They conduct **Dream Rites** involving herbs, chanting, and bloodletting, and perform an **Offering** on each new moon by letting blood fall into the swamp. The dead are returned to the earth in **unmarked graves** near water or roots.
- **Symbols:** The **Gold Bird** (a stylized golden bird on a black background) and **Tangled Roots** (marked in chalk or blood).
- **Structure:** Led by a **Prophet (currently [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]])**, who is believed to channel Mirella’s will. Elite followers are the **Unseen Widows** (assassins, spies, ritual law keepers), with **Sisters** as ordinary faithful. Men are rarely trusted and never included in inner circles.
- **Influence:** Their influence spreads quietly, often among the desperate and wronged. **The Drownlands** is their largest and most sacred sanctuary. Even [[The Duke]]’s men avoid crossing the Widows. [[Prophet Veerah]] had a vision of "creatures of metal and flesh" that she interprets as a war Mirella wants the Widows to stop.
- **Relationships:** They **distrust** the Word of the Stillborn Star. They are **openly opposed** to the [[Church of the Ember Saint]]. They mostly **ignore** [[El Santo]]'s followers.

### **Faith of [[El Santo]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** More than a religion, it's the **pulse of Disgraceland’s working class, fighters, and survivors**. It honors grit, resilience, and justice earned with blood. **El Santo**, the Masked Saint, is believed to battle darkness in the underworld, with his spirit rising in every act of courage. **Justice is personal**, found in action, loyalty, and honor, rather than corrupt law. **Pain, bruises, scars, and broken bones are sacred marks** of survival.
- **Practices & Traditions:** Every follower owns a **mask**. After fights, combatants participate in the **Brotherhood of Bruises** to share drinks and bless wounds. They hold **Vigil Matches** where a champion fights for truth, and an annual **Day of the Last Bell** for remembrance and sparring. The **Noche de Lucha** tournament, held every four years, is the heart of their culture.
- **Symbols:** The **Mask** (white, silver, or gold) and **Bruised Knuckles**.
- **Structure:** The spiritual head is the **[[Grand Mascara]]**, with the **Grand Luchador** ([[Noche de Lucha]] champion) as a spiritual icon. The **Senior Enmascarados** are a secretive council who remain powerful figures in the religion.
- **Influence:** This faith is the **"glue" in [[Steeltown]]** and a beacon across Disgraceland, with even rivals showing up for Noche de Lucha. All training grounds and gyms are considered sacred. Many members of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] follow this faith.
- **Relationships:** They are sometimes rivals, sometimes allies with the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]], and have **strong mutual respect** with the [[Church of the Ember Saint]]. They have little direct overlap with the Faith of Mirella.

# 🜃 Faith of Mirella


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Faith of Mirella
> ![[fm.png|400]]  

> **"Beneath the mud, beneath the root, her dreams tangle through our veins."**

**Faith of Mirella** is ancient, secretive, and feared. It is the faith of swamps, bogs, and shadowed waters. Followers believe the world itself recoiled from the violence of mankind, and the sleeping goddess **Mirella** lies beneath the earth, waiting for women to reclaim what was lost.  
The faith is almost exclusively female—men are considered dangerous, expendable, or cursed by their birth. The Unseen Widows are its most visible hand in Disgraceland, but Mirella’s whisper travels farther and deeper than anyone admits.

## Overview



---

## Core Beliefs

- **Mirella, the Sleeping Mother:**  
  An ancient earth-goddess who slumbers beneath the swamps and roots. Her dreams shape fate, her will is revealed in blood and vine.
- **The Land Remembers:**  
  All wounds inflicted by men upon the earth and upon women are remembered. Mirella’s memory is long, and her vengeance slow but certain.
- **Prophecy of Reclamation:**  
  When the time is right, Mirella will rise and reclaim the world for women. Until then, her followers must act in secret, sowing chaos for the old order.
- **The Power of Blood and Dream:**  
  Prophecy, visions, and the rites of blood are central. Dreams are messages; omens are sought in birth, death, and the movement of animals.

---

## History

- **Old as Soil:**  
  The faith predates organized religion. Its rites and symbols are carved into the oldest stones, whispered in forgotten languages.
- **Persecuted and Hidden:**  
  Always feared, sometimes hunted, the faith went underground. Secret covens and hidden sanctuaries kept the old ways alive.
- **The Unseen Widows:**  
  In Disgraceland, the Widows are the faith’s enforcers, assassins, and prophets. Every action serves the dream of reclamation.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Veil:**  
  Initiates wear black veils over the lower half of their faces. Only the Prophet may go unveiled. The veil is a symbol of mourning, secrecy, and solidarity.
- **Dream Rites:**  
  All major decisions and rituals begin with shared dreams—herbs, chanting, and bloodletting are common tools.
- **The Offering:**  
  On each new moon, followers cut their palms and let their blood fall into the swamp, feeding Mirella’s dreams.
- **Burial Rites:**  
  The dead are returned to the earth in unmarked graves, always near water or thick roots.

---

## Symbols

- **The Gold Bird:**  
  A stylized golden bird on a black background, worn over the heart—symbolizes Mirella’s watchful spirit and the freedom to come.
- **Tangled Roots:**  
  Marked in chalk or blood at gathering places, representing connection and secrecy.

---

## Structure

- **The Prophet (currently Veerah):**  
  The unquestioned leader, believed to channel Mirella’s will through prophetic dreams.
- **The Unseen Widows:**  
  Elite followers—assassins, spies, and keepers of ritual law.
- **Sisters:**  
  Ordinary faithful, responsible for raising daughters, spreading lore, and acting as Mirella’s eyes and hands.
- **Outsiders (Men):**  
  Rarely trusted; sometimes used, never included in inner circles.

---

## Influence

- **Whispers and Shadows:**  
  The faith is small but dangerous. Its influence spreads quietly, mostly among the desperate, wounded, and wronged.
- **The Drownlands:**  
  The largest, most sacred sanctuary in Disgraceland; the White Mansion sits hidden in the marsh, always guarded.
- **Fear and Respect:**  
  Even The Duke’s men avoid crossing the Widows if they can help it.

---

## Holy Days

- **Night of the White Veil (first full moon of spring):**  
  All faithful gather by water to renew their vows and honor the fallen.
- **Bloodwake (last new moon of the year):**  
  A secret ritual—each woman dreams alone, seeking Mirella’s guidance for the year ahead.
- **Reclamation’s Eve:**  
  A rare, dangerous night. Assassins strike targets chosen in prophecy.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "The swamp forgets nothing."
- "Dreams speak when tongues are cut."
- "Her vengeance rises through our daughters."

---

## Notable Figures

- **Veerah:**  
  Current Prophet; her visions are law.
- **The First Widow:**  
  Mythic founder; may never have existed.

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Distrusted. Too cold, too distant, too bound by old men’s words.
- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Openly opposed—fire seeks to burn the swamp, but the swamp always returns.
- **El Santo:**  
  Mostly ignored; his followers are rarely women.

---

> *“In the silence of the roots, she remembers every sin.”*

---

36.title: El Santo

# 🥊 Faith of El Santo


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of El Santo
> ![[els.png|400]]  

> **"A bruise is a prayer the world can see."**


The **Faith of El Santo** is more than a religion—it’s the pulse of Disgraceland’s working class, fighters, and survivors. Inspired by the masked champion who became legend, El Santo’s followers honor grit, resilience, and justice earned with blood.  
Their faith lives in every gym, street fight, and act of stubborn courage. The beating heart of their culture is **[[Noche de Lucha]]**—the most celebrated event in Disgraceland.


## Core Beliefs

- **El Santo Lives:**  
  The Masked Saint never died—he battles darkness in the underworld, and his spirit rises in every act of courage.
- **Strength is Sacred:**  
  True strength is the power to lift others, not to dominate them.
- **Justice is Personal:**  
  The corrupt law is nothing. Justice is found in personal action, loyalty, and honor.
- **Pain is Proof:**  
  Bruises, scars, and broken bones are sacred marks—signs of survival and the soul’s resilience.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Mask:**  
  Every follower owns a mask. Most are simple, but each is personal. Losing your mask is the greatest shame.
- **Brotherhood of Bruises:**  
  After fights, combatants gather to share drinks, bless wounds, and trade stories—scars are a badge of honor.
- **The Vigil Match:**  
  When justice demands, a champion is chosen to fight for truth in the ring. Winner decides the verdict.
- **Day of the Last Bell:**  
  An annual day of remembrance—bells ring for every soul lost, and all are invited to spar in their honor.

---

## Symbols

- **The Mask:**  
  White, silver, or gold, each mask is a symbol of identity, struggle, and hope.
- **Bruised Knuckles:**  
  Devotees often wrap their hands or tattoo their knuckles as a sign of their faith.

---

## Structure

- **Grand Luchador:**  
  The reigning champion of [[Noche de Lucha]]; spiritual head and icon for the next four years.
- **The Grand Mascara:**  
  The head of the faith. The spiritual leader of the El Santo religion. Upon death, a new Grand Mascara is chosen by the Senior Enmascarados.
- **The Senior Enmascarados:**  
  The secretive council who selects the tournament’s fighters and guides the faith’s traditions.
- **Ring Elders:**  
  Local leaders, keepers of custom, and mediators in disputes.
- **Santos (Saints):**  
  Ordinary faithful—anyone who stands up, fights on, and helps the fallen.

---

## Influence

- **Everywhere, for Everyone:**  
  El Santo’s faith is the glue in Steeltown and a beacon across Disgraceland. Even rivals show up for Noche de Lucha.
- **Gyms & Rings:**  
  All training grounds are sacred. Every gym is part sanctuary, part school, part court.
- **Justice in the Streets:**  
  Santo’s justice is swift and personal—handled in the ring, never left to corrupt officials.

---

## Holy Days

- **Noche de Lucha (every four years):**  
  The greatest tournament and festival in Disgraceland.
- **Day of the Last Bell (annually):**  
  Sparring and blessings for the departed.
- **Founding Match (spring equinox):**  
  Young faithful compete for the right to wear their first mask.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "Bruises fade. Honor stays."
- "If you can stand, you can fight."
- "The mask never leaves you, even when you take it off."
- "In the ring, truth can’t hide."

---

## Notable Figures

- **El Santo:**  
  The masked founder—legend says he fights evil beneath the world, waiting to rise again.
- **The Last Stillborn Champion:**  
  The only non-believer to win Noche de Lucha—now a folk hero and symbol of changing times.
- **The Senior Enmascarados:**  
  The faith’s shadowy council. Their names are known only to each other and the Grand Luchador.

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Sometimes rivals, sometimes allies—recent openness has bridged old divides.
- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Strong mutual respect—fire and iron both endure, even when they clash.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Little direct overlap, but women have fought and won in the ring—widows and sisters have left their mark.

---

> *“If you’ve never stood in the ring, you’ve never really lived.”*

---

# 🔥 Church of the Ember Saint


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of the Ember Saint
> ![[es.png|400]]  

> **"Through the flames, we rise. Through the ashes, we endure."**

The **Church of the Ember Saint** is the wealthiest and most widespread faith in Disgraceland’s modern era. Born in the ashes of an ancient city, the church reveres the legendary figure who braved the flames to save all he could—known simply as the **Ember Saint**.  
Wherever there is fire, there is hope. Followers believe suffering is a forge, and the faithful emerge stronger for it. In public, Ember Saints are grand and generous. In private, they are hard as iron.


## Core Beliefs

- **The Ember Saint:**  
  The first and greatest of the faithful, the Ember Saint walked through fire untouched, saving hundreds during the great blaze of Prattia. His deeds are both myth and moral code.
- **The Flame Endures:**  
  Fire purifies, but it does not destroy. Each trial faced is a test, a chance to be reforged.
- **Service is Salvation:**  
  To help others is sacred. To hoard wealth or power is heresy.
- **Ashes Remember:**  
  The past is not forgotten. Every ember is a spark of memory, kept alive through story and ritual.

---

## History

- **The Burning of Prattia:**  
  Legends tell of a fire that nearly destroyed the greatest city of the old world. The Ember Saint emerged, saving lives, guiding the lost, and inspiring a movement.
- **Rise to Power:**  
  The faith spread through charity and spectacle. Ornate cathedrals rose, and the faith’s leaders became rich and influential.
- **Survival and Renewal:**  
  The Church survived wars, disasters, and purges. Even now, after so much has been lost, their temples (ruined or not) remain symbols of hope.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Ember Book:**  
  Holy scripture containing parables of the Ember Saint’s deeds and teachings. Each tale ends with a question or lesson for the reader.
- **Rites of Passing:**  
  The dead are cremated, and a single ember is given to their family. The flame symbolizes the spirit’s endurance.
- **Day of Ember:**  
  Once a month, believers light a communal fire at dusk, sharing stories and food with neighbors and strangers alike.
- **Saint’s March:**  
  On the anniversary of the Great Fire, followers parade through the city with lanterns, chanting and singing hymns until sunrise.

---

## Symbols

- **The Burning Halo:**  
  A golden ring of flame, often painted above doors or tattooed on the chest.
- **The Unburned Hand:**  
  A palm surrounded by stylized fire, representing protection and sacrifice.

---

## Structure

- **High Flame (Pontiff):**  
  The supreme leader of the church, chosen from the Council of Embers.
- **Council of Embers:**  
  Senior clergy who oversee regions, temples, and doctrine.
- **Redrobes:**  
  Priests and priestesses who serve the faith, recognized by their long, hooded ember-red robes.
- **Lay Faithful:**  
  Everyday followers, often organized into charitable guilds and work crews.

---

## Influence

- **Wealth:**  
  The church controls enormous wealth, much of it redistributed through charity—but some suspect greed and corruption at the top.
- **Architecture:**  
  Their cathedrals are renowned for marble, glass, and gold—most now ruined or gutted, but a few remain standing as beacons.
- **Festivals:**  
  Ember celebrations bring people together, even nonbelievers.

---

## Holy Days

- **Ember Day (monthly):**  
  A night of communal fire, feasting, and storytelling.
- **Saint’s Vigil (anniversary of the Great Fire):**  
  All-night procession, ending at dawn with the lighting of the Grand Flame.
- **The Forging:**  
  Every five years, followers gather for a mass ritual of renewal and oaths—new Redrobes are anointed here.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "No one is alone in the fire."
- "Flames do not ask who is worthy—they burn, and we endure."
- "The ember you carry lights the way for others."

---

## Notable Figures

- **The Ember Saint:**  
  Legendary founder, both a man and a myth.
- **High Flame Parvelius:**  
  (Placeholder for current leader—customize or name as needed.)

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Ancient rivals—Ember faith believes in action, Stillborns in patient waiting.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Somewhat opposed—fire and earth rarely mix, and their outlooks clash.
- **El Santo:**  
  Mutual respect, especially among Steeltown’s poor, though their doctrines rarely overlap.

---

> *“In every ash is the story of survival.”*

---

# World Lucha Libre

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description:
> In Disgraceland, **Lucha Libre** is king.  
> It’s not choreographed wrestling—it’s brutal, high-stakes MMA, the truest test of will and skill. The sport kept its ancient name from the legendary [[Noche de Lucha]], but here, the fights are real.  
> Spectacle is everything: dramatic entrances, wild personalities, and fierce rivalries light up every show. But in the cage, nothing is fake—victory and pain are both earned.
> 
>> [!rustwater] World Lucha Libre
>> ![[wll1.png|250]]

> **"No script, no mercy—just blood, grit, and glory."**

## History

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[wll.png|260]]

- **Origins:**  
  Lucha Libre grew from the old [[Noche de Lucha]] tournaments—an ancient tradition of combat, now evolved into a spectator sport for a broken world.
- **Golden Age:**  
  Before the [[Tetra Bomb]], the **WLL (World Lucha Libre)** was a global phenomenon. Champions toured the world, and the best fighters became household names.
- **The Fall:**  
  After the [[Tetra Bomb]], the sport vanished. Only small, dangerous underground matches survived in the chaos.
- **Revival:**  
  In the last 15 years, as Disgraceland clawed back to stability, a wealthy industrialist (a bitter rival to [[Jacoban Clay]]) resurrected the WLL—building a new arena in [[Gutter Row]] and sparing no expense on belts, hype, and spectacle.  
  Anyone with fists, dreams, or something to prove can enter—win, and you might become a legend.

---

## Culture & Masks

- **Masks:**  
  In modern Lucha Libre, masks are *not* required. The mask remains a sacred symbol for the clergy and the most faithful of [[El Santo]], but the sport itself is about the fighter’s reputation, skill, and swagger.
- **The Show:**  
  Theatrics, promos, and hype are a must. Fighters adopt bold personas, enter the arena like legends, and stir the crowd before a punch is even thrown.
- **The Fights:**  
  All-out MMA—no scripts, no predetermined winners, no mercy.  
  Fighters are judged by toughness, technique, and the ability to thrill a crowd.

---

## The Modern WLL

- **Arena:**  
  The new WLL arena in [[Gutter Row]] is part fortress, part theater—a beacon of light (and vice) in the chaos.
- **Fighter Recruitment:**  
  Open call. The desperate, the daring, and the washed-up all get a shot. The best rise fast; the weak go home broken or worse.
- **Titles:**  
  Real belts, real champions. Winning one means respect, money, and all the trouble that comes with fame in Disgraceland.
- **Promoters:**  
  The WLL’s owner is a kingmaker—pitting would-be legends against each other and using the league to grow his own influence.
- **Entertainment:**  
  Beyond the fights, every show is an event: music, fireworks, dancing, wild costumes. It’s part bloodsport, part circus, all survival.

---

## Impact on Society

- **Unity & Escape:**  
  For a few hours, faith, faction, and class mean nothing. People come together to watch the fights, forget their troubles, and gamble their last coins.
- **Fame & Fortune:**  
  Fighters can become folk heroes—or cautionary tales.  
  Some win riches, others disappear after a brutal loss.
- **Rivalries:**  
  The WLL is a pressure valve for Disgraceland. Old grudges and street feuds often play out in the cage, with the crowd roaring for blood.

---

## Famous Champions (Examples)

- **“The Sand Viper”** – undefeated, merciless, beloved by the crowd, but feared in the locker room.
- **Freya “The Iron Widow”** – former Unseen Widow who shocked the world with her fighting spirit.
- **Marcus “Steeljaw” Torres** – a Steeltown legend known for never tapping out.

---

## Notable Moments

- **The Arena Riot (Year 2182):**  
  When a match ended in a disputed stoppage, fans stormed the cage. The promoter doubled security after.
- **The First Open Challenge:**  
  The owner’s “anyone can fight” policy led to a month where a farmer, a priest, and a disgraced Loyalist all stepped into the ring—none won, but the city still talks about it.

---

## Connections to Faith

- **El Santo’s Influence:**  
  The faith’s values—endurance, honor, and justice—live on in the sport’s code, even if most fighters now go unmasked.
- **Noche de Lucha:**  
  Once every four years, the line between faith and sport blurs as champions from the WLL are invited to compete in the greatest tournament of all.

---

# [[The Water Wars]]

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Global Conflict
> **Conflict Name:** The Water Wars  
> **Duration:** 2109 – 2121  
> **Catalyst:** Privatization of global freshwater supplies  
> **Final Event:** Detonation of the [[Tetra Bomb]]  
> **Casualties:** Estimated 5.6 billion lives (direct and secondary effects)
> 
>> [!rustwater] Water Wars
>> ![[w.png|400]]

> *"They didn’t fight for territory. They fought for the last cup of clean water."*  
> – Recovered transmission, Year 2109

## 🌊 Background

The planet was already dying.  
The oceans were poisoned, the skies were cracked, and the aquifers had run dry.

In the final decades of civilization, most remaining freshwater sources were sold off under what was known as the **Global Hydration Accord** — a desperate treaty that handed control of water to corporate conglomerates in exchange for infrastructure repair.

The people revolted. The governments panicked.  
The corporations fortified.  
And war began.

---

## 🏴 Phase One: The Corporate Front

Private security forces armed with bleeding-edge tech enforced strict water zones. The world was carved into zones of control.

- **The North Reach**: First major flashpoint. Riots led to the collapse of three citystates.  
- **The Coil Rim**: Tech hubs where AI combat drones were first deployed.  
- **Flood Zones**: Heavily bombed river territories. Access denied to civilians.  
- **The Salt Wastes**: Deserts soaked in blood and broken desalination rigs.

---

## 🤖 Phase Two: The Machine Years

| Technology             | Role in the War |
|------------------------|-----------------|
| **Combat Drones**      | Controlled key rivers and dam zones  
| **Skimmer Raiders**    | Stole mobile reserves mid-transit  
| **Neural Infantry**    | Failed attempt at mind-linked soldiers  
| **Orbital Pulse Cannons** | Used to vaporize contested reservoirs

Most of this tech died with the cities that built them.

---

## 🧍 Phase Three: The Return to Blood

By 2118, the machines were gone — broken, turned rogue, or unpowered.  
And the world returned to the old ways.  
Boots. Guns. Trenches. Mass graves.

Water shipments were hijacked by the gallon. Whole battalions slaughtered to take a single well. And in the end, everyone was thirsty.

---

## 💥 Final Phase: The Tetra Ignition

When the **[[Tetra Bomb]]** was deployed across the **Midcontinent Line**, nothing survived.

Not the corporations.  
Not the governments.  
Not the war.

The world froze.  
And then it waited to be reborn.

---

## 📅 Major Events Timeline

| Year | Event Title | Description |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| **2109** | **Global Hydration Accord** | Governments privatize all freshwater to survive infrastructure collapse. |
| **2111** | **The Severance Riots** | Dozens of megacities fall to internal unrest after water bans. |
| **2113** | **Corporate Armies Mobilize** | Security forces backed by hydro-conglomerates take control of rivers, dams, lakes. |
| **2114** | **Battle for the North Reach** | First massive conflict. Water convoys intercepted. Dams destroyed. |
| **2115** | **Orbital Strikes on the Coil Rim** | Entire tech cities erased to stop rebel AI control. |
| **2116** | **Neural Infantry Collapse** | Linked soldiers begin disappearing or going berserk. Project abandoned. |
| **2118** | **The Low-Tech Turn** | Countries resort to infantry, tanks, and desperation warfare. |
| **2121** | **Tetra Ignition** | The [[Tetra Bomb]] is dropped. The war ends. So does civilization.

---

## 🔗 Legacy

- No government has ever reformed.
- Fresh water remains the rarest commodity in [[DISGRACELAND]].
- Children are taught to fear thirst before fire.
- No one speaks of the Accord anymore — only the aftermath.

---

# TTV Evening News

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎TTV EVENING NEWS
> ![[en.png|400]]  

> “United we stand, informed we thrive.”  
> — Warren Scottyard, opening line to every broadcast

## Overview  
The **TTV Evening News** is the primary nightly news broadcast aired across all of United Tribucia, streaming directly into every home via the mandatory CRT television sets issued by The Duke. Airing five nights a week at **18:00 sharp**, the program recaps daily events across the six major regions, delivers weather updates, and highlights notable achievements of Loyalist programs.

While the show claims impartiality, it's heavily censored and curated by the **Tribucian Communication Bureau**, ensuring all content either supports Loyalist rule or tactfully avoids criticizing it. Citizens see the show as either a dependable news source or subtle propaganda, depending on who you ask — and where you live.

The broadcast originates from **Studio 3B at TTV Headquarters in Gravenwild, Charspire**, the same complex where [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] is filmed.

---

## 🧑‍💼 Anchors

### [[Warren Scottyard]]
**Role:** Lead Anchor  
**Background:** Once a decorated field journalist during the reconstruction years, [[Warren Scottyard]] earned his reputation covering The Duke’s rise in Ashmoor. With a deep, authoritative voice and icy composure, Warren is both respected and distrusted depending on who's watching. He's seen as the "face of facts" by Loyalists and the "voice of polished lies" by skeptics.  
**Style:** Calm, unwavering, textbook Loyalist professional. Tends to pause dramatically before stating statistics or issuing official statements.

> “The Duke reminds us tonight — stability is not free. It is earned.”

---

### [[Layla Hawk]]
**Role:** Co-Anchor & Field Correspondent  
**Background:** A younger, sharper contrast to Warren, [[Layla Hawk]] was handpicked from a pool of regional broadcasters in Threshton for her charisma and on-camera presence. Rumors suggest she’s the niece of a former Loyalist commander, but nothing's confirmed. Layla covers softer segments, like weather, daily spotlights, and public health alerts, but occasionally handles field reports in more dangerous regions like Gutter Row or Steeltown.  
**Style:** Relatable, conversational, often smirking beneath the surface. A few viewers suspect she’s not quite as Loyalist-aligned as she lets on.

> “Sun’s rising early in Threshton tomorrow — but not as early as the ranchers hope. Grain quotas remain unmet for the fourth week running.”

---

## 🎥 Segments

- **The State Rundown:** Quick summaries from each region. Loyalist-approved only.  
- **Weather from the Watchtower:** Regional weather provided via airship telemetry and ground scouts.  
- **Public Safety Alerts:** Official bulletins from the Guard Forces. Often vague or cryptic.  
- **Faces of Tribucia:** Human-interest pieces focused on "model citizens" and Loyalist success stories.  
- **Field Reports:** Pre-recorded dispatches from reporters embedded across the regions.

---

## 🕯️ Cultural Impact

The TTV Evening News remains required viewing for many Loyalist families and a tolerated background noise in poorer households where it doubles as a light source. In black markets and backrooms, recordings are often edited into parody broadcasts known as "False Flags" — spliced with unflattering cuts, subversive commentary, or ghosted transmissions that include forbidden footage.

Layla Hawk has a secret following in Steeltown zines, where her smirks and unscripted side comments are interpreted as signs of quiet resistance.

---

# TRASHFLICKS

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ TRASHFLICK
> ![[trash.png|450]]

> "Luck’s a lie. In *Sliver*, you either *bleed for your win* or you lose with style." — [[Ninepack]]

## 🩸 Overview

Trashflicks are low-budget, underground films passed around Disgraceland on scavenged tapes, discs, or crude cartridges. Screened on battered CRTs in basements, alley clubs, or projected onto ruined walls, Trashflicks are the desperate artform of a starving culture. Content ranges wildly — from salvaged pre-Tetra movies, to outlaw documentaries, raunchy comedies, staged propaganda parodies, and even whispered rumors of snuff or prophetic reels.

---

# 🎞️ Trashflick Genres

> _“The Duke’s afraid of guns in the streets, but not half as afraid as he is of a tape in the right hands.”_

Trashflicks are the chaotic, street-level soul of Disgraceland cinema. Shot, edited, and distributed by desperate hands using salvaged tech, they reflect the raw emotional nerve of a society struggling to breathe.

---

#### 🕰️ Pre-Fall Relics

**Description:**  
Ultra-rare original pre-Tetra cassettes — action movies, romantic dramas, cartoons, even sitcoms — usually warped, static-laced, or dubbed over.

**Value:**  
Extremely scarce. Most believe only **[[The Duke]]**, **[[Jacoban Clay]]**, and a few elite collectors possess intact originals.

**Popular With:**  
Wealthy traders, rebel archivists, artists hunting for forgotten truth.

**Subculture:**  
“**Tape Purists**” believe the soul of the old world lives on in its flicks.

---

#### 📽️ Disgraceland Docs

**Description:**  
Raw handheld footage and stitched-together edits exposing corruption, starvation, rebel activity, secret experiments, and executions. Sometimes staged, sometimes all too real.

**Notable Flicks:**  
- *Grain Chain* — exposes famine tactics in **[[Threshton]]**  
- *White Tiger* — rumored footage of a beast in **[[The Drownlands]]**  
- *Red Tape* — alleges **[[The Duke]]** uses doubles  

**Popular With:**  
Steeltown crews, underground educators, Widows, and rebel youth.

**Danger Level:**  
High. Possession is a crime punishable by imprisonment or worse.

---

#### 🎭 Blacktown Comedies

**Description:**  
Crude sketch reels, sarcastic puppet shows, or street acts captured during **[[Backburn]]** gatherings. Some are brilliant. Some are borderline nonsense.

**Subgenres:**  
- *Ha Ha Holes* — joke reels mocking regions or public figures  
- *Ratstick & Friends* — a filthy puppet show parodying Loyalist propaganda

**Popular With:**  
Everyone who needs to laugh to keep from crying — especially in **[[Gutter Row]]**.

**Slang:**  
**“Bloopers”** — prank reels or slapstick failures turned viral.

---

#### 🔥 Loverunners (Sextapes)

**Description:**  
The best-selling Trashflicks. Shot in secret, passed around under fake names. Sometimes consensual, sometimes questionable, always watched.

**Why They’re Big:**  
In a world starved of intimacy and driven by paranoia, voyeurism becomes currency.

**Notable Rumors:**  
- *The Widow’s Mouth* — said to feature a disguised Unseen Widow  
- *Ashmoor After Dark* — suspected Loyalist bait series  

**Trade Lore:**  
A seller in **[[Charspire]]** allegedly produced over 200 tapes under 17 pseudonyms before vanishing.

---

## 🦆 Duke-Flips & Propaganda Spools

**Description:**  
Two opposing categories — one mocking, the other glorifying **[[The Duke]]**.

- **Duke-Flips:** Overdubbed, cut-up broadcasts turned into satire or horror.  
- **Propaganda Spools:** Clean, well-produced Loyalist reels glamorizing regime victories.

**Secret Culture:**  
Some flicks are **“True Forks”** — tapes spliced to contain both a propaganda reel *and* its mockery, depending on how they're played.

**Suspected Creators:**  
Rumors point to the **Blueforce Media Division** for the propaganda, and rogue editors from **[[Ha Ha Hole]]** or the **[[Tribucia Tribute]]** for the flips.

---

## ⚙️ The Charspire Machines

**Origin:**  
A seller named **Harrel Kint** in East Gravenwild began repairing old cassette players and handheld recorders in 2175, selling them from a junk stall.

**The Decline:**  
By 2181, Kint had vanished. Official reports cite a “licensing issue.” His workshop burned one week later.

**Legacy:**  
Kint’s refurbished devices, now called **“Kint Boxes”**, are valuable collector’s items. Some say they contain hidden features or preloaded banned flicks.

---

(cont'd) ## 🔟 Top 10 Most In-Demand Trashflicks in Disgraceland

These are the flicks people lie, steal, and bleed for. Some are traded like holy relics. Others are whispered about like cursed myths. Most are illegal. All are unforgettable.

---

### 1. 🎥 *Ashmoor After Dark*  
**Genre:** Loverunner / Suspected Propaganda  
**Rumors:** Said to be produced by Loyalists as bait. Features a masked man resembling **[[The Duke]]** in multiple graphic scenes. Some swear it's real. Others claim it's a test.  
**Status:** Extremely dangerous. Possession can result in disappearance.

---

### 2. 🎥 *Grain Chain*  
**Genre:** Docu-tape  
**Summary:** Documents famine enforcement in **[[Threshton]]**, including Loyalist dumping sites, corrupt crop seizures, and interviews with starving families. Credited with sparking three food riots.  
**Status:** High-priority contraband. Blueforce raids any known screening site.

---

### 3. 🎥 *The Widow’s Mask*  
**Genre:** Loverunner / Hoax Flick  
**Rumors:** A heavily stylized tape featuring a veiled woman in black performing ritualistic dances and whispering cryptic lines. Promoted as a “Widow reveal,” but almost certainly staged.  
**Truth:** No verified connection to the **[[Unseen Widows]]**. Likely a tasteless imitation or Loyalist psy-op.  
**Status:** Controversial, widely condemned in **[[The Drownlands]]**, but still sold under the table.

---

### 4. 🎥 *The Feral Tape*  
**Genre:** Found Footage / Horror  
**Summary:** Footage from a destroyed Redforce outpost. Flashes of something inhuman. Ends with a whisper over static: *“We’re not dead. We’re waiting.”*  
**Status:** Dozens of bootlegs exist. No one knows who shot it.

---

### 5. 🎥 *Duke’s Doodles*  
**Genre:** Parody  
**Summary:** A surreal animated satire of **[[The Duke]]** as a deranged children’s show host, co-starring a talking goose and haunted sink. Borderline genius.  
**Status:** Spread mostly via Ha Ha Hole patrons. Creators remain anonymous.

---

### 6. 🎥 *The Nine-Hour Kiss*  
**Genre:** Loverunner  
**Summary:** A continuous shot of two lovers in hiding — possibly ex-Wrecking Crew. Shows intimacy, desperation, and confession. Not pornographic — emotional, raw, and real.  
**Status:** Treasured and worn thin. Original tape believed lost.

---

### 7. 🎥 *Static Eden*  
**Genre:** Art Film / Prophetic Vision  
**Summary:** A disturbing montage of decaying cities, broken statues, biomech corpses, and stormlight flickers — all set to a droning hum.  
**Rumors:** Some believe it's based on a real dream. Others call it a hoax.  
**Status:** Treated with reverence by some cult circles. Illegal in Ashmoor.

---

### 8. 🎥 *Stitched Up*  
**Genre:** Docu-tape / Horror  
**Summary:** Smuggled footage allegedly from **[[Ora Razchek]]'s** mansion. Shows flickering images of reanimated bodies, mechanical organs, and stitched skin.  
**Status:** “Too fake to be true” — unless you’ve seen one of his monsters.

---

### 9. 🎥 *Red Velvet Goldmine*  
**Genre:** Loverunner  
**Rumors:** Shot in a high-rise suite in **[[Ashmoor]]**. The masked woman resembles a high-ranking official. Some say **[[Soria Langston-Clay]]**, though it's never confirmed.  
**Status:** Blacklisted by name. Copies fetch entire livestock trades.

---

### 10. 🎥 *The Day the Sky Forgot*  
**Genre:** Spoken Word / Documentary  
**Summary:** A former steelworker narrates his life before, during, and after the Tetra Bomb, over footage of the cratered ruins. Beautiful and heartbreaking.  
**Status:** Played quietly in backrooms. Always gets passed on.

---

> _“You can burn books. You can hang preachers. But a flick? That shit crawls.”_  
> — **[[Reel Rat Jules]]**, legendary tape-runner


---

> _“Every tape tells a truth. Doesn’t matter if it’s a lie.”_ — **[[Reel Rat Jules]]**, black market legend



## 🎬 Glossary & Slang

- **Tape Purist** – someone who believes pre-Fall cinema holds historical truth
- **Reel Rat** – slang for Trashflick traders and bootleggers
- **Tape Burn** – the distortion caused by overwriting old tapes (also slang for watching too much in one sitting)
- **Static Run** – a long night of flicks watched through haze and fuzz
- **Veed** – short for "viewer", usually used mockingly
- **True Fork** – a tape spliced to contain both propaganda and parody

---

Let me know if you want a **Trashflick Hall of Fame** with famous tapes and who starred in them — or even a **Reel Rat** NPC page for a black market tape lord.

# 🎸 The Wanderers  

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Details
> **Type:** Musical Group  
> **Founded:** Approx. 2178  
> **Current Lineup:**  
> [[Jaden Kade]] – Lead vocals, guitar

> **Reggie Vaughan** – Bass  
> **Base of Operations:** Roaming; currently housed within TTV Studios, [[Gravenwild]], [[Charspire]]  
> **Affiliation:** Featured nightly on [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]
> **Status:** Active  
> **Public Image:** Popular, charismatic, government-sanctioned — with a growing cult following
> 
>> [!rustwater] The Wanderers
>> ![[wand.png|500]]

> *“Play the song. Just don’t let ‘em know what it’s really about.”* — [[Jaden Kade]]

## 🎤 Overview  
**The Wanderers** are a post-collapse rock group formed in the streets of Charspire, now known across [[DISGRACELAND]] as the nightly house band on *Night Time with Morris Gable*. While the regime promotes them as “a symbol of restored culture,” many citizens — especially the young and restless — feel something deeper pulsing beneath the music.

Led by [[Jaden Kade]], a wiry frontman with a scorched voice and rebel heart, The Wanderers walk a dangerous line between performance and resistance. Their lyrics ride the edge of censorship, and every show feels like a gamble — how much truth can be hidden in a song before someone notices?

---

## 🎶 Style & Themes  
Their sound is a fusion of post-industrial blues, rustrock, and stripped-down synthwave.  
- Instruments are salvaged, wired by hand, often shorting out mid-performance.  
- Lyrics often reference roads, fire, static, chains, and lost memory — metaphors for rebellion, surveillance, and grief.

**Notable Songs:**  
- *“Last Light Left”* — Believed to be about the failed uprising in [[Steeltown]]  
- *“Cracked Signal”* — Features a reversed vocal loop that some claim is a coded message  
- *“Rustwater Hymn”* — Banned from public radio three weeks after debut  
- *“King of Glass”* — Thought to be a veiled insult toward [[The Duke]]  
- *“Deadman Waltz”* — A fan favorite known to stir emotion in live crowds

---

## 🎤 Relationship with Morris Gable  
Their inclusion on *Night Time with Morris Gable* is widely seen as strategic — both for the regime, which uses their popularity to retain viewer interest, and for Jaden Kade, who uses the airtime to echo unrest through rhythm.

**Publicly:**  
- Morris praises them weekly as “the soul of the nation.”  
- The band appears polite and cooperative — but never speaks much during interviews.

**Privately:**  
- Jaden Kade despises Morris but respects the opportunity.  
- It’s a cold truce: ratings in exchange for silence.

---

## 🔥 Rebellion Rumors  
- Multiple resistance cells have reportedly used The Wanderers’ lyrics as code phrases.  
- Bootlegged live recordings circulate in outlaw zones.  
- It’s believed the band helps fund small acts of sabotage using their TTV stipend.  
- Some fans claim to have received blank tapes from the group containing anti-regime broadcasts when played backward.

---

## 🧠 Trivia  
- The band refuses to play pre-Duke cover songs — all material is original.  
- Their instruments have names: Jaden’s guitar is “**Crowtooth**,” Silas’s snare is “**July**

# [[Transportation in Disgraceland]]

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Specific Vehicles
> **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**: Every member rides a functioning motorcycle — mostly retrofitted cruisers or choppers. Their loud engines are a warning and a promise.
> **Sgt. Rottwyler**: Drives a reinforced military Hummer painted bone-white, covered in decals and Loyalist Guard iconography.
> **[[The Duke]]**: Travels in a fully restored white limousine — old-world luxury, spotless, custom-armored. It’s said he has never once driven it himself.
> **Mayors**: Each appointed mayor is provided a standard black sedan and a full-time government driver. The vehicles are symbolic of power, even if they require regular patchwork repairs.
> There are official buses that travel into [[Charspire]] each day for work.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Transportation
>> ![[car.png|400]]

## Overview

Transportation in Disgraceland is a brutal mix of scarcity, improvisation, and control. With fuel tightly rationed and roads barely maintained, only the powerful ride in comfort — while the rest walk, limp, or saddle up.

---

## Fuel Economy

All known fuel reserves and refining operations are controlled by [[The Duke]], with refining centralized in [[Charspire]] under the iron grip of Mayor [[Gorren Brile]]

Fuel is distributed exclusively through state-run depots in each major territory, sold at severe markups. This keeps everyday citizens dependent, while also rewarding loyalty and punishing dissent.

Smuggling fuel is punishable by death — and still happens daily.

---

## Common Transportation Methods

- **Walking**: The most common way to get around. Simple. Free. Slow. Dangerous.
- **Pack Animals**: Horses, mules, and even oxen are making a slow return. Ranchers in [[Threshton]] have started quietly breeding stock again. Carts, carriages, and sleds are now a common sight in rural regions.
- **Scavenged Bikes & Carts**: Children, merchants, and drifters often use homemade wheelbarrow carts or two-wheeled junkbikes made from scrap.
- **Automobiles**: Rare. Frankenstein rigs built from old-world parts and scrap. Think Mad Max — armored panels, engine smoke, and heavy welds. Loud. Unpredictable. Respected.

---

## Notable Vehicles



---

## Road Conditions

Most highways are fractured, overgrown, or outright collapsed. Bridges are rare and fiercely protected. Those that remain are either toll-controlled or watched by [[Loyalist Guard]].

Travel outside safe zones is extremely risky — requiring guards, fuel, water, and luck.

---

## Black Market Travel

If you know the right people, you can:

- Rent a hidden fuel stash.
- Buy a seat on a roaming trader’s armored bus.
- Hire a stealth wagon convoy to smuggle you through enemy regions.

Just don’t ask questions. And always pay in advance.

# [[The Silo]]


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎The Silo, Ashmoor
> ![[silo.png|500]]  

## Overview
**[[The Silo]]** is the towering, marble-and-steel heart of [[Ashmoor]] — a brutalist palace-turned-government fortress that serves as the official residence and command center of [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland. Rising from the highest point in the city like a monument to dominion, it casts a long shadow over the rebuilt districts below.

Once an abandoned military weapons facility from the Water Wars, The Silo was repurposed by [[The Duke]] during his rise in 2144. It is both a symbol of order and a shrine to his narcissism, wrapped in banners, statues, and surveillance.

---

## Description
- **Architecture**: Cold, brutalist structure reinforced with blastproof plating and reinforced glass. Marble columns line the entrance, stained from rain and smoke. Twin Loyalist banners hang from the central tower.
- **Interior**: Lavish, polished floors contrast with bare steel walls. Giant screens line every corridor, looping messages of "unity through strength." Secret passageways and panic rooms are built into the walls. Most who work here know only fragments of its layout.
- **Security**: Operated by [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] and elite [[Loyalist Guard]], with surveillance drones in constant rotation. Unauthorized entry is a death sentence.

---

## Key Areas
- **The Throne Room**: Where [[The Duke]] delivers speeches and performs his weekly *[[State of Tribucia]]* broadcasts. It features a golden throne forged from melted artillery.
- **The Chapel of Continuity**: A strange, candlelit room filled with relics from the pre-Tetra era — propaganda photos, tattered flags, and the original blueprints of [[TRIBUCIA MAP]].
- **The Glass Office**: [[Soria Langston-Clay]]'s elevated, fully transparent work chamber. She can see everyone. They cannot see her.
- **The Underlevels**: Heavily restricted subfloors rumored to house interrogation cells, vaults of pre-war tech, and black project labs. Only a few living people know its full contents.

---

## Lore & Significance
- **Foundation**: Converted in 2144 by [[The Duke]] after uniting the [[Ashmoor]] factions. Became a seat of power by 2150.
- **Public Perception**: Seen as both sacred and terrifying. Citizens of [[Ashmoor]] call it "The Eye." Rumors say it broadcasts sonic signals at night.
- **Propaganda Hub**: He hosts his weekly address, the  [[State of Tribucia]] live every [[CALENDAR|Alphaday]] on the [[TTV Studios|TTV Network]].

---

## Notable Events
- **2157**: The assassination attempt by the Ashmoor Scholars — ended in the mass public execution of 43 citizens on the Silo’s steps.
- **2169**: [[Soria Langston-Clay]] appointed Mayor of Ashmoor from within The Silo after a "gas leak" killed the previous mayor.
- **2182**: Alleged quake under The Silo revealed a sealed chamber. Access denied. [[Salem Quinn]] called it "a voice buried in the steel."

---

## Secrets & Theories
- **Silo Core**: Conspiracy theorists claim the entire building is powered by a pre-Tetra AI core known as “Motherglass.”
- **Ghost Broadcasts**: Late-night static often cuts across other channels with snippets of [[The Duke]] speaking... when he isn’t on air.
- **Unseen Access**: Some believe the [[Unseen Widows]] infiltrated the Silo once. Only [[Veerah]] would know if that’s true.

---

## Quote
> “This isn’t a building, it’s a mirror. And it shows us all just how small we are.”  
> — [[Royce Sincayd]], in an unpublished editorial draft

# [[Tetra Bomb]]

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[tbomb.png|cover hmed]]

> [!warning]+ Classification: EXTINCTION-LEVEL DEVICE  
> **Code Name:** TETRA  
> **Type:** Multi-element fusion warhead  
> **Era:** Final Phase of the [[Water Wars]]  
> **Blast Radius:** Unmeasured – total ecosystem-level detonation  
> **Casualties:** Estimated 7.2 billion (direct and chain-reaction effects)  
> **Known Surviving Cities:** Zero

> *"It wasn't built to save anyone. It was built to end the argument."*  
> – Unknown scientist, post-incident interview

## ☣️ Design & Composition

The **Tetra Bomb** was the result of a last-ditch black project from the Unified Continental Defense Pact during the height of the **[[Water Wars]]** — a conflict already choking the planet’s final resources.

The bomb’s name refers to its four core components:

1. **Helionite Plasma** – A synthetic isotope that destabilized upon impact with moisture  
2. **Black Crysilin Dust** – A nano-powder that fed on electrical currents and atmospheric pressure  
3. **Red Virex** – A biochemical ignition gel that reacted violently with oxygenated blood  
4. **Human Nervous Tissue** – Taken from dying test subjects. No explanation ever declassified.

The fourth element was added late. It worked.

---

## 💀 Deployment

The bomb was **not tested**. No simulation was conclusive. The scientists and strategists that signed off on its use assumed a localized continental sterilization effect — a final scare tactic.

What happened instead was **a cascade of chain reactions** across the stratosphere. Weather patterns collapsed. Power grids melted. Any nearby biome — human, animal, or machine — stopped functioning.

And then, silence.

---

## 🌎 Aftermath

Surprisingly… nature survived.

| Element             | Status After Detonation |
|---------------------|-------------------------|
| **Fresh Water**     | Largely unaffected      |
| **Plant Life**      | Regrew within months    |
| **Human Civilization** | Functionally erased |
| **Digital Infrastructure** | Obliterated |
| **Nuclear Fallout** | None – Tetra had no uranium, no fusion ring. |

The only immediate result:  
**One long, endless winter.**  
Cold enough to kill the desperate. Quiet enough to bury the loud.  
A thousand unmarked graves frozen in the open.

---

## 🧬 Legacy

- Tetra was only detonated once.  
- The schematics were **never recovered**.  
- The name “Tetra” is now used in **curses, prayers, and warnings**.  
- Some say remnants of the fourth element — the **nervous tissue core** — are still out there, buried beneath Dead Waters.  
- Others claim the **Reckoning Coil** is its second birth.

# SWILLPOTS

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ SWILLPOT in CHARSPIRE
> ![[swill.png|450]]

# 🥃 Swillpots of Disgraceland

Swillpots are the lifeblood of the broken people of Disgraceland — rough, loud, chaotic watering holes where drinks flow, fists fly, and secrets slip like spilled liquor on a crooked counter. While technically unsanctioned, they’ve become so culturally ingrained that even [[The Duke]] dares not outlaw them, despite his well-known hatred for alcohol. He’s called it “the rust in the gears of rebuilding,” but even his most Loyalist advisors know that banning swill would spark instant riots.

### 📜 History

The first Swillpot was nothing more than a hole-in-the-wall lean-to near the original strip mine in [[Charspire]], almost 50 years ago. Miners needed somewhere to forget how close they were to death every day, and a one-eyed ex-barkeep named [[Renny Slub]] gave them that place. His original shack, **The First Spill**, still stands — though it’s mostly a museum piece now, kept up by locals out of spite and pride.

From there, Swillpots spread across Tribucia, becoming a sacred refuge for the overworked, the outcast, the outlaw, and the brokenhearted.

---

## 🧃 Standard Fare

**Popular Drinks:**
- Lager
- Ale
- Whiskey
- Rum
- Wine

Most Swillpots also serve greasy food: meats, stews, thick breads, or salt-fried root vegetables. The rare ones offer fancier mixed drinks or imports — but expect to pay heavy in **slugs**.

---

## 🍻 Notable Swillpots by Region

### **STEELTOWN – The Furnace Gullet**
A loud, sweat-soaked pit of hammered steel and busted stools. Locals say fights here settle quicker than court disputes. Always hot inside, no matter the season. Home turf for a few off-duty Wrecking Crew bruisers.

### **ASHMOOR – The Amber Touch**
A 'high-class' Swillpot by Disgraceland standards. Velvet seats, expensive wines, and waitstaff that’ll rob you blind with a smile. Frequented by minor bureaucrats, spies, and smugglers in nice coats.

### **GUTTER ROW – The Slick Room**
Run out of the bottom floor of a collapsing tenement in Vileby. Walls drip from busted pipes, and rats are considered regulars. Nobody knows who actually owns it, but everyone pays the same: don’t cause trouble, or you disappear.

### **CHARSPIRE – The Spill House**
The original. Old, blackened stone walls with rusted beams overhead. Hasn’t cleaned its tankards in years. RedForce guards have an unspoken rule to leave it alone — even they need to forget sometimes.

### **THRESHTON – The Broken Bale**
A rancher-run hideaway where cowboys drink their fill and trade secrets over sour mash and molasses bread. Anyone badmouthing the [[Rancher Collective]] gets their boots nailed to the porch.

---

## 🧨 Notes

- The Duke would outlaw alcohol entirely if he believed he could get away with it.
- Instead, he taxes it heavily in Ashmoor, ignores it in Steeltown, and pretends it doesn't exist in Gutter Row.
- Despite his hatred, it’s common knowledge that some of his most loyal guards drink off-duty.

# State of Tribucia

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎The Silo, Ashmoor

# 📡 [[State of Tribucia]]
> “*Your land. My vision. Our duty.*” — *[[The Duke]]*

## 🗓 Schedule
- **Every [[CALENDAR|Alphaday]]** at **20:00hrs**  
- **Broadcast live from** [[The Silo]] on **[[TTV Studios]]**  
- **Mandatory viewing** across [[TRIBUCIA MAP]], though enforcement is unofficial and widely ignored outside of [[Ashmoor]].

---

## 🎙 Overview
The **State of Tribucia** is a weekly broadcast led by **[[The Duke]]**, designed to **project authority, maintain illusionary order, and reinforce loyalty** across the fractured zones of Disgraceland. Though framed as a patriotic update, each address is carefully crafted propaganda — blending truth with distortion, veiled threats with hollow optimism.

Each episode opens with a militaristic version of the *Hymn of Unity*, followed by a wide shot of **[[The Duke]]** standing beneath a giant eagle-and-scythe emblem in a cold metal chamber deep inside [[The Silo]]. He speaks alone — no advisors, no questions, just the voice of a ruler to his subjects.

The broadcasts vary in length from **20 minutes to an hour**, depending on current events, [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] movements, political unrest, or how much ego-stroking **[[The Duke]]** needs that week.

---

## 🗝 Purpose
- Reaffirm **The Duke’s control and divine right** to rule.  
- Announce **policies**, **fuel quotas**, **slave relocations**, or **raids**.  
- Issue **warnings**, call out **traitors**, or deliver personal messages to mayors like [[Soria Langston-Clay]] or [[Gorran Brile]].  
- Respond to incidents (e.g., rebel attacks, blackouts, shortages) with **blame-shifting** and **ominous rhetoric**.

---

## 🗣 Tone & Delivery
**[[The Duke]]** speaks with calm theatrical flair — part dictator, part televangelist. His voice is confident, sonorous, and condescending, often addressing viewers as “*my children*” or “*my debtors in paradise-to-be*.”

He often ends each address with a ritualistic phrase:  
> *“May the fires of unity burn ever upward. May your loyalty be as constant as my gaze.”*

---

## 📺 Reception & Impact
- In **[[Ashmoor]]**, residents typically watch out of fear or ambition.  
- In **[[Steeltown]]**, many **refuse to watch**, though some relay summaries via pirate radio.  
- **[[Gutter Row]]** treats it as a drinking game.  
- In **[[The Drownlands]]**, it is considered an ill omen to even speak during the broadcast.  
- **[[Threshton]] ranchers** often *intentionally work late* to miss it, calling it "**the Bull’s Sermon**."  
- **[[Charspire]] factories** pipe it in through loudspeakers, though most workers wear earplugs.

---

## 🧠 Notable Lore Hooks
- [[Rachel Gold]] once tried to fact-check a broadcast. She was *"reassigned to cultural desk duties."*  
- The phrase **“Two Harvests, One Hope”** was first coined in a 2179 address — later used to justify doubling [[Threshton]] grain quotas.  
- A malfunction in 2183 caused [[The Duke]]’s face to **freeze mid-grin** for 11 minutes — the clip was later turned into a banned [[Steeltown]] sticker.

---

#  Sliver

> "Luck’s a lie. In *Sliver*, you either *bleed for your win* or you lose with style." — [[Ninepack]]

## 🩸 Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ game of sliver
> ![[sliver.png|450]]

**Sliver** is a rogue-deckbuilder card game born in the underbelly of [[Gutter Row]] and [[Steeltown]]. Inspired by old-world poker but twisted by post-collapse desperation, it's part strategy, part madness.

Some say the game was first played with bones and blood in the [[Three Nail Market]]

---

## 🕹 How to Play

### 🎯 Objective
Build hands to score **Influence** each round. First to **100 Influence** wins. In outlaw variants, the winner takes all—coin, secrets, or lives.

### 👥 Players
2–4 players (standard); up to 6 in high-stakes variants.

### 🃏 Deck Composition

#### Standard Deck (64 cards):
- Suits:
  - **Bones** (Spades)
  - **Ashes** (Clubs)
  - **Blood** (Hearts)
  - **Coin** (Diamonds)
- Ranks: 1–10 per suit
- 4 "Wild" Sliver-backed cards (draw from **Sliver Deck**)

#### Sliver Deck (20 cards):
Unique power cards that warp reality and strategy. Drawn through combos or faction effects.

#### Modifier Deck (30 cards):
Cards that grant permanent or round-limited buffs/debuffs. Includes:
- **Scar Cards** (persistent effects)
- **Rust Cards** (negative mutations)
- **Favor Cards** (faction or character boosts)
- **Dust Cards** (instant plays, volatile)

---

## 🔄 Game Loop

1. **Draw Phase**
   - Each player draws **7 base cards**.
   - If a card or effect allows, draw from the **Sliver Deck** or **Modifier Deck**.

2. **Build Hands**
   - Players arrange their 7 cards into a single **poker-style hand**.
   - Traditional hands apply (Pair, Three-of-a-Kind, Straight, Flush, etc.).
   - Some Sliver or Modifier cards allow players to split into **multiple hands**.

3. **Play Phase**
   - Play up to 2 Sliver or Modifier cards before revealing.
   - Cards may enhance hand strength, add multipliers, or sabotage others.

4. **Reveal Phase**
   - Players reveal hands simultaneously.
   - Hands are scored based on tier + any effects.
   - Highest hand wins the **Influence Pool** for the round.
   - Second-highest earns **1 Influence**, others get nothing.

5. **Burn Phase**
   - All played cards go to discard except Scar and Rust (they persist).
   - Draw back to 7. Repeat.

---

## 🧠 Hand Scoring Example

| Hand Type        | Influence Gain | Notes                                |
|------------------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| Pair             | +2             | Basic combo                          |
| Two Pair         | +4             | Common early-game score              |
| Three-of-a-Kind  | +6             | Moderate score, combo friendly       |
| Straight         | +8             | Sequential, hard to block            |
| Flush            | +10            | Same suit                            |
| Full House       | +13            | Rare, strong                         |
| Four-of-a-Kind   | +16            | Unlocks special Sliver draw          |
| Straight Flush   | +20            | May trigger **Vision** effects       |
| Bone Royal (10-9-8-7-6, Bones) | +30 | Legendary, rare as sin              |

---

## 💀 Sliver Cards (Drawn Separately)

| Name                        | Effect                                                                 |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **[[The Grim Man]]**        | Destroy lowest scoring card on all other players' hands                |
| **[[Dusty Dillon]]'s Echo** | If you make a Straight, score 1.5x and draw one Modifier next round    |
| **Gable’s Signal**          | Cancel one opponent’s Modifier this round                             |
| **Widow’s Mercy**           | If you lose this round, deal 3 damage to a chosen player’s deck        |
| **Steeltown Switch**        | Swap hands (at random) with one player before reveal                   |
| **Double Duke**             | Your hand score is doubled, but you draw 1 less card next round        |

---

## ☠ Modifier Cards

### Scar Cards (Persistent)

| Name           | Effect                                                            |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Burnt Nerve    | Lowest scoring hand is doubled each round                        |
| Hollow Crown   | Start each game with one Sliver draw                             |
| Bone Tattoo    | Flushes of Bones grant +4 extra Influence                        |

### Rust Cards (Negative)

| Name         | Effect                                                      |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Brittle Deck | Max hand size is reduced by 1                              |
| Flickering Eye | You must reveal your hand early each round               |
| Cracked Memory | You cannot use the same Modifier more than once per game |

---

## 🔥 Culture & Setting

- **Backburn rules** apply in underground games. All modifiers allowed. Real-world stakes often replace Influence.
- Winners may demand weapons, favors, secrets, or blood.
- Famous tables:
  - **The Red Table** in [[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]
  - **The Runglow Cart** (a mobile Sliver game hidden inside a food vendor)
  - **Dust Alley Den** behind the [[Rustwater Raiders]]' tavern

---

## 🗨 Quote
> “*Sliver* don’t care about fairness. Just who’s got the guts to stay in.” — [[Dusty Dillon]]

---

# 🏴 [[Poundball]]

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ POUNDBALL
> ![[pound.png|450]]  

**Poundball** is a brutal, fast-paced sport played throughout Disgraceland in abandoned lots, broken parking decks, and dusty fields. It’s a game of speed, force, and survival — where glory is earned through blood and bruises. Banned in [[Ashmoor]] but beloved everywhere else, Poundball is more than a game — it’s a warzone with rules.

---

## 🧱 Basic Rules

- **Teams of 6:**
  - **3 Runners** – Only players allowed to carry or pass the Poundball.
  - **2 Pounders** – Defense. Smash and stop opposing runners by any means.
  - **1 Anchor** – A grounded goalie. Cannot leave the goal zone.

- **The Ball:**
  A 25-pound leather-wrapped sand-and-scrap core called the *Poundball*.

- **Field:**
  Played on any wide-open space. Each end has a marked **scoring zone** — sometimes spray-painted, sometimes built from junk.

- **Scoring:**
  A runner scores by:
  - Crossing into the scoring zone while holding the ball (3 points), or
  - Underhand-lobbing it into the "zone", usually a trashcan, from outside (1 point).

- **Turnovers:**
  If a runner is tackled and drops the ball before scoring or passing, possession flips to the other team after three hits if the Runner still holds the ball.

- **Passing:**
  Lateral or underhand only. No overhand forward throws.

- **Winning:**
  First team to 13 points or the most points in 45 minutes.

---

## 🚫 Fouls & Penalties

- **Illegal moves:** Eye-gouging, biting, groin shots.
- **Grifter Drops:** Faking a drop to bait a hit. Results in a **Grime Stop**.
- **Scrap Box:** Players penalized for dirty play serve 3 minutes in a caged side zone.

---

## 🥊 Positions & Strategy

| Role       | Description                        |
|------------|------------------------------------|
| **Runner** | Agile, strategic, good hands       |
| **Pounder**| Massive, mean, relentless hitters  |
| **Anchor** | Stationary juggernaut, goal guard  |

**Tactics:**
- **"Bleeding the Field"** – Luring defenders to one side for a clean run.
- **"Gravel Grind"** – A low crawl burst to sneak past defenders.
- **"Fleshing the Anchor"** – Forcing the goalie to commit so another runner can score.

---

## 🎭 Poundball Attire

Players wear scavenged, makeshift gear for protection and intimidation:

- **Runners:**
  - Stripped-down outfits for speed.
  - Gloves, elbow wraps, light pads.
  - Often shirtless or in cut tanks.

- **Pounders:**
  - **Makeshift shoulder pads** fashioned from metal scraps, car seat foam, or layered rubber.
  - Reinforced boots, padded forearms, chain wraps.

- **Anchors:**
  - Heavy torso padding.
  - **Leather helmets**, some with horn-like additions or personal paintjobs.
  - Thick gloves for bone-breaking tackles.

Many paint their faces or bodies with ash, rust, or blood before matches. Team symbols are often carved or stitched into their gear.

---

## 🔥 Notable Teams

- **[[Steeltown Wreckers]]** – Tough, brawling veterans. Never back down.
- **[[Threshton Cattle Dogs]]** – Fast, deceptive, and full of dirty tricks.
- **[[Gutter Row Shockrats]]** – Street kids turned legends. Aggressive and wild.
- **[[Charspire Heavy Bolts]]** – Built like mining rigs. Known for crushing hits.
- **[[Ashmoor Gildsmen]]** – Rich-sponsored killers. Well-trained and ruthless.
- **[[Coffin Island Lockjaws]]** – Inmates. Silent. Scary. Undefeated in brawls.

---

## 🏆 Poundball Culture

Poundball is more than entertainment — it’s a release. A way for citizens to forget about Loyalists, rations, or chains. Betting is rampant. Fans chant in the stands made of shipping crates, and riots often break out when a ref call goes wrong.

Kids play it with bricks and trashballs in alleys. Adults die playing it for glory. Legends are born in the dust and blood of the Poundball pit.

---

> “You don’t *win* Poundball. You *survive it longer than the other bastard.*”
