# NOCHE DE LUCHA

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Backburn Show
> ![[ancientnl.png|450]]  

## Overview
**Noche de Lucha (“Night of the Fight”) is a one night, 16 person single elimination tournament that takes place every four years.** 
**Open to All:**   Traditionally reserved for faithful of [[El Santo]], the tournament is now open to all, regardless of faith, in recognition of the world’s upheaval and the need for unity. Even an Ember Saint won the last Noche de Lucha. An event talked about in every corner of Disgraceland.
 **Selection:**  The Senior Enmascarados—the highest council of the faith—select 16 fighters based on merit, reputation, and sometimes, rumor or legend or popular support.
**The Arena:**  Held in the Arena Mascarada in [[STEELTOWN#East Mountain|East Mountain]], [[Steeltown]].
**The Celebration:**  Noche de Lucha is a festival as much as a tournament—food, music, street games, and weeks of communal joy and rivalry.
**The Prize:**  The winner is crowned Grand Luchador, head of the faith and symbol of the era’s spirit for the next four years.
**Enduring Tradition:**  War, bombs, famine—nothing has stopped Noche de Lucha. It is the one promise the world has kept.

## ANCIENT ORIGINS

Since time immemorial, every four years on the 15th–20th of [[Calendar|Rainsun]], Noche de Lucha has been held.

- **Sacred Combat:** The earliest Nights took place at the center of ancient villages, on stone platforms beneath torchlight. Masked warriors fought not for sport, but to resolve disputes, seek the blessing of their gods, or determine leaders.
- **The Masked Champion:** Legends tell of a figure known only as **[[El Santo]]**, the first to don a sacred mask and win the Night—not through brute strength, but through heart, cunning, and mercy.
- **The Eternal Ring:** These battles happened in rings drawn in dirt, carved in stone, or built from woven ropes—always as a circle, representing eternity and unity.
- **Rituals & Myths:** Every Noche began with offerings, music, and storytelling. Winners were believed to carry the favor of the divine, and sometimes, to become living saints.

## EVOLUTION

The tradition endured. As civilizations rose and fell, the Night was passed down through generations, its true origins lost but its rituals surviving.  
Later cultures reshaped it—sometimes as gladiator games, sometimes as wrestling, sometimes as rebellion against tyrants.  
But always:  
- Masks, to honor the unknown gods and spirits  
- A ring, to contain the struggle  
- The winner’s right to challenge fate and change their life

## LEGACY IN DISGRACELAND

In the world of Disgraceland, **Noche de Lucha** is the oldest surviving ritual. It is the **heartbeat of the Faith of El Santo** and the unbroken thread connecting the present to a forgotten age.

Even after the fall, the bombs, and the end of empires, the Night remains.  
Each four-year cycle is not just a contest—but a reenactment of a myth older than memory.

## CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE

**Noche de Lucha** is:
- The living memory of ancient peoples
- Proof that unity, struggle, and hope endure
- A bridge between mortals and the divine

# 📺 Night Time with Morris Gable

**Air Time:** Weeknights at midnight  
**Location:** [[TTV Studios]] (Tribucia TeleVision), [[Gravenwild]], [[Charspire]]

**Mandatory Broadcast:** No — marketed as entertainment, but loaded with regime-approved content  
**Host:** [[Morris Gable]]  
**House Band:** [[The Wanderers]]
>
>> [!rustwater] Night Time w/ Morris Gable
>> ![[nt.png|500]]

> *“If the world’s still turnin’ — then I’ll still be talkin’. Welcome to Night Time, friends.”*  
> — [[Morris Gable]]

## 🕰 Overview
*Night Time with Morris Gable* is the flagship late-night broadcast of [[TTV Studios]], aimed at soothing the nerves of a fractured nation while subtly reinforcing loyalty to the regime. Airing five nights a week across all of [[DISGRACELAND]], it delivers charm, distraction, and just enough optimism to keep people passive.

The show is not mandatory, but it might as well be. CRT sets gifted by [[The Duke]] ensure everyone has access. In many homes, Morris is the only voice still speaking when the world goes quiet.

---

## 📋 Format
### 🗣 Opening Monologue
Delivered from his desk with a glowing microphone and practiced smile. Warm, vaguely hopeful, always safe. Opens every night with:  
*“If the world’s still turnin’ — then I’ll still be talkin’. Welcome to Night Time, friends.”*

### ✨ Bright Spots
Footage of regime achievements across the territories. New rail lines, ration increases, community events — all curated, staged, or exaggerated for effect.

### 🎤 Guest Appearances
Carefully vetted guests — factory workers, local “heroes,” regime-approved performers — share cheerful stories that reinforce the illusion of progress and unity.

### 🎸 Live Music by *The Wanderers*
Every episode features a live musical performance by [[The Wanderers]], a beloved Disgraceland band. Their presence has boosted the show’s popularity across even the more rebellious territories.  
Morris personally recruited them, recognizing their influence. They rarely speak on air, but always close with a subtle nod to the camera.

### 🌒 Final Thoughts
Morris ends the show with a quiet monologue and a reassuring smile, sending viewers to sleep with soft words and measured calm.

---

## 📺 Cultural Impact
- **Charspire & Gutter Row:** The show is embraced as soothing late-night comfort.
- **Steeltown & Threshton:** Viewed with skepticism or irony, but still widely watched.
- Children mimic Morris’s voice. Fan art and black-market merchandise exist.
- Some claim hearing Morris’s voice helps them sleep. Others say it’s the only reason they haven’t screamed in years.

---

## 🏢 TTV Studios & Broadcast Details
Filmed live from **[[TTV Studios]]** in the heart of industrial **Gravenwild**. The building is one of the last fully functional towers from the pre-Tetra era, retrofitted with massive signal boosters and armed [[Redforce]] patrols.

The studio set is bright on screen but surrounded by soot-streaked scaffolding and smoke beyond the cameras. Power is often inconsistent, but the signal rarely fails.

---

## 🧠 Trivia
- Morris wears the same style of burgundy suit every night — he owns over 40 identical versions.
- [[The Wanderers]] are rumored to slip hidden anti-Duke messages into their instrumentals.
- A leaked memo once described the show as *“the regime’s velvet rope — not to bind, just to lull.”*
- [[The Duke]] has never appeared on the program.

---

# Luxyn ("White Delight")

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ LUXYN PROPAGANDA POSTER
> ![[luxyn.png|500]]  

## Overview
**Type:** Synthetic euphoric drug  
**Street Names:** White Delight, Blank, Ghostrocks, Snowdrop, Glow  
**Produced in:** [[Charspire]] (from mined elements in [[Gutter Row]])  
**Main Markets:** [[Gutter Row]], [[Charspire]]  
**Overseen by:** Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] & Mayor [[Cricket Granger]] (secretly)  
**Distributed by:** [[Murray Boys]]


---

## Description

**Luxyn** is a white, faintly glowing powder—almost looks illuminated in the dark. The main ingredient is extracted from deep mines in Gutter Row, then shipped to Charspire, where it’s refined and cut for the streets.

Most users snort Luxyn for the fastest hit. Desperate addicts will eat it straight, chasing even a hint of euphoria. It has a faintly sweet, chemical taste, and leaves a cold, tingling numbness in the mouth and throat.

---

## Effects

**Upsides:**
- Instant, powerful euphoria: All pain, fear, hunger, sadness, and regret vanish.
- The world feels “soft and beautiful.”  
- Lasts 3–6 hours.

**Downsides:**
- Highly addictive. Chasing the first high becomes all-consuming.
- Overdose is common, especially with street-cut Luxyn. Signs: violent shaking, vomiting, then cardiac arrest.
- **“White Eyes”:** Prolonged or heavy use turns the user’s eyes milk-white and eventually blinds them. Addicts with this look are called **Blanks**.
- Withdrawal: Debilitating pain, hallucinations, severe depression. Some die from the process.

---

## Culture & Trade

- **Main Hubs:** Gutter Row (mining, distribution), Charspire (processing, cutting, packaging).
- **Power Structure:** Overseen by mayors Brile (Charspire) and Granger (Gutter Row) in a secret alliance. The two split profits and keep supply flowing, all while avoiding Loyalist Guard raids and the Duke’s notice.
- **Street Dealers:** Sell openly in alleys, clubs, and “pain clinics.” The [NAME MAFIA GROUP] enforces turf and quality.
- **Duke’s Stance:** The Duke is strictly anti-drug. If he discovers Brile and Granger’s involvement, both are dead men walking.

---

## Slang & Lore

- **White Delight:** Most popular street name.
- **Blanks:** Heavy users with fully white, blind eyes.
- **Glow:** The faint shine of pure Lumin.
- **“Going Blank”:** Losing yourself to addiction.
- **“Taste the Light”:** Dealer slang for dosing up.

---

## Visuals

- Luxyn is packaged in small waxed paper envelopes, each stamped with a crude symbol (different for each dealer or mafia crew).
- Blanks are a common sight in Gutter Row and Charspire—shuffling, blind, lost in their heads.

---

## Story Hooks

- A poisoned batch hits [[Steeltown]]—dozens dead, sparking a crackdown.
- [[Abel May Jr.]]s family was destroyed by Luxyn—he hates it with a passion.
- [[Unseen Widows]] exile anyone caught “Going Blank”—they consider it a curse.

---

**Related:** [[Cricket Granger]] • [[Gorren Brile]] • [[Gutter Row]] • [[Charspire]] • [[The Duke of Disgraceland]] • [[NAME MAFIA GROUP]]

# Galliah, the Stillborn Star

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
Galliah is the ancient dead sun, the stillborn star that slumbers beyond mortal sight. To the faithful of the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]], Galliah is not simply a celestial body — it is a god, a grave, and a prophecy.
Once a star that sought to burn but failed, Galliah cracked under its own sorrow, bleeding faint silver light into the abyss. In the shattered legends of pre-Tetra times, it is said Galliah **"tried to awaken but was denied the flame"** — an eternal symbol of futility, cycles, and the inevitable rebirth of worlds from ruin.
Its broken corpse now drifts at the edge of all things, encased in tendrils of ghostly mist, orbited by debris from civilizations long forgotten.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Galliah, the stillborn star
>> ![[gall.png|400]]
>> 

> "We are the ash of its dreams. We are the silence of its breath."

## Appearance

- **Shape**: A vast, blackened sphere, like volcanic glass shattered by unseen hands.
    
- **Surface**: Crisscrossed by deep fractures; faint, ghostly silver light leaks from the cracks.
    
- **Atmosphere**: Ashen mist swirls around it, remnants of ancient failed solar flares.
    
- **Orbit**: A graveyard of broken asteroids, ruins of shattered worlds, drifting slowly around it.
    

---

## Beliefs Surrounding Galliah

- **The Silent Cycle**: Followers believe all things exist in a cycle of creation, collapse, and rebirth — Galliah’s failure is not an end, but a silent waiting.
    
- **The Awakening**: One day, Galliah will stir, not with light, but with **perfect silence**, heralding the final collapse of the broken world.
    
- **The Stillborn Gospel**: Ancient priests like Mesh'den recorded visions of Galliah's dreams — barren worlds, forgotten empires, and endless night — and taught that humanity must embrace futility to achieve true peace.
    
- **Ash Children**: Some extremist sects of Stillborns mutilate their bodies with brands and ash to "mark themselves for Galliah" and welcome the collapse early.
    

---

## Influence on Disgraceland

- **The [[Word of the Stillborn Star]]** is the oldest faith in the world.
    
- Symbols of Galliah — a cracked black circle leaking silver threads — are still found carved into ruins, graveyards, and hidden shrines across United Tribucia.
    
- People praise Galliah when things go right, and curse the star god when things go wrong.

---

## Rumors and Legends

- **The Shard of Galliah**: Whispers tell of a fragment of Galliah that fell to Earth before recorded history. Some claim it slumbers deep in [[the Drownlands]], poisoning the swamps and feeding ancient gods.
    
- **The Dead Choir**: Some travelers claim to hear ghostly singing when staring into the night sky near the Dead Waters — a cosmic lament attributed to Galliah’s ancient dreamers.
    
- **The Hollow Crown**: According to old tales, a king once forged a crown from a piece of Galliah’s fallen ash. He ruled a silent kingdom where nobody spoke and all eventually vanished without a trace.
    

---

# FINAL FORCE a.k.a The F.F

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
> **Type:** Elite Special Forces Military Unit, Loyalist Guard Special Division
> **Nicknames:** FF, The Iron Dogs, [[The Duke]]’s Hammers
> **Commander:** [[Sgt. Rottwyler]]
> **Headquarters:** Loyalist Base [[Ashmoor]], with mobile deployment units stationed in armories across Disgraceland.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Final Force
>> ![[ff.png|400]]


## Uniform & Gear  
- Armored “Iron” Suits—bulky, steel-gray, inspired by early Iron Man Model-1 design.
- Features:  
    - Heavy, riveted plating  
    - Grated faceplates (slitted eyes, grated mouth)  
    - Short-burst flight (rocket-leap or glide)  
    - Built-in arm cannons: concussive blasts, incendiaries, slug launchers  
    - Shoulder/back mini-missile racks (some units)  
    - Power: experimental fusion cells or chemical batteries (dangerous, unreliable)
- **[[Sgt. Rottwyler]]s suit:** Larger, custom-forged, extra weapons, scarred plating, dog tags welded into the chest.

## Selection  
- Only the toughest, most loyal, or most feared [[Loyalist Guard]]s get “volunteered.”
- Suits are bio-locked to each trooper.

## Reputation  
- Feared by civilians and rebels; even Loyalist Guards keep their distance.
- The FF is deployed only for major threats or to “make an example.”
- Their arrival is announced by the roar of jets and the thunder of armored boots.
- Rumors: Some suits malfunction and cook the pilot alive.  
- Some believe the suits can run on “ghost mode,” piloting themselves after the wearer dies.

## Tactics  
- Shock & Awe: Enter loud, crush resistance fast.
- No mercy. Rottwyler kills his own for cowardice or failure.
- Heavy support by engineers/mechanics; suits require constant upkeep.

## Infamous Event: The Blackshift Massacre

> “No one forgets the day the Iron Dogs marched into the mines. The smoke still hangs over [[Charspire]].”

In 2178, the Duke deployed the Final Force to [[Charspire]] after miners at the Blackshift Pit staged a mass walkout over starvation rations and lethal conditions. What started as a tense standoff turned to horror when the FF, led by [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], breached the mine gates and unleashed their arsenal. Now known as the [[Blackshift Massacre]].

The massacre was swift and total. Workers—men, women, even children hiding in supply rooms—were slaughtered without warning.  
The event might have faded into rumor, but a reporter from the **[[Tribucia Tribute]]** was present, snapping photos from a hidden alcove as the carnage unfolded. Those photos, smuggled out and copied in secret, became symbols of resistance across Disgraceland.

To this day, “Blackshift” is a curse in Charspire. It’s a name whispered when the Duke’s iron hand comes down. Even Loyalist Guards remember it as a black scar on the regime—a day the world saw the true face of the Final Force.


## Members  
- [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] (Commander)
- [Other FF troopers – add names as needed]

---

## In Lore  
- The FF is the Duke’s final word. When diplomacy fails or terror is required, he sends the Iron Dogs.
- Rottwyler’s legend grows with every mission—unmatched brutality, zero hesitation.

---

# Darrell Douglass

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Details
>> **Titles:** Father of [[Jimmy Douglass]] & [[Mark Jeffrey]]
>> **Alias/Nickname:**  El Ders - The People's Champion
>> **Home Location:** [[Mohawk]], [[Steeltown]]
>> **Public Reputation:** Loved, good, helpful, leader, strong
>> **Gender:** Male
>> **Spouse:** None
>> **Age:** 54
>> **Height:** 6'1"
>> **Weight:** 241 lbs.
>> **Date of Birth:** 12th of Greensun, 2111
>> **Occupation:** Steelworker
>> **Status:** Deceased
>> **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]
>> **Known Associates:** [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]]
>> **Faith:**  [[El Santo]]
> 
>> [!rustwater] Darrell Douglass
>> ![[darrell.png|300]]


## Overview  
**Darrell Douglass** was the father of [[Jimmy Douglass]] and [[Mark Jeffrey]], and one of the founding members of the original [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]. A former steelworker turned revolutionary, Darrell was a symbol of defiance in the early days of Disgraceland’s formation — known for his booming voice, unbreakable work ethic, and fierce loyalty to the people of [[Steeltown]].

He was executed on the direct orders of [[The Duke]] nearly two decades ago, after refusing to cooperate with [[Ashmoor]]’s new food and fuel directives. His death marked a turning point in [[Steeltown]]’s relationship with the regime — a martyrdom that galvanized the rise of the modern [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]].

In the early years of the reconstruction, Darrell Douglass formed a quiet but powerful alliance with [[Harp Langston]], the hard-edged rancher from [[Threshton]]. Though they came from different worlds — one a union man of steel and soot, the other a farmer forged from soil and sweat — they saw eye to eye on the most important thing: the people had been forgotten. When Darrell restarted the first mill in [[Steeltown]] in 2151, Harp rode north to see it with his own eyes. That meeting sparked the start of an unspoken brotherhood. Harp sent food. Darrell sent tools. Together, they created the Black Route — a secret lifeline of grain and supplies flowing between Steeltown and the southern fields.

But like all quiet revolutions, it didn’t stay hidden. In 2158, The Duke’s men cracked down. Darrell was captured and forced into steel production. Harp wanted to act — to fight, to break him out — but the newly forming Rancher Collective refused. The risk to Threshton was too great. Darrell and Harp argued for the last time, and their bond fractured. For the next decade, Darrell was a ghost — kept alive only to fuel the machine he once tried to stop. When he was finally hanged in 2167, Harp didn’t attend. But word spread that a grain silo burned that night in Threshton, ash scorched into the dirt in the shape of a hammer and sickle. The message was clear. Their friendship may have ended in silence, but the respect never died.

---

## Known For  
- Organizing the first major work strikes after the [[Water Wars]]  
- Personally leading the blockade of [[Steeltown]]’s railyards  
- Declaring [[The Duke]] a “parasite in a crown” in a broadcasted protest  
- Being publicly hanged under [[Loyalist guard]] surveillance outside the old steel gates  

---

## Legacy  
- His sons, [[Jimmy Douglass]] and [[Mark Jeffrey]], both inherited his drive but took different paths.  
  - Jimmy became  the hammer — carrying his father’s fire and fury forward.  
  - Mark became the heart — trying to keep the Wrecking Crew honorable.
- Steeltown still marks the anniversary of his death with a midnight vigil known as *The Burn Mark*, where torches are lit along the old railyard fences.  
- A faded mural of Darrell still stands on a warehouse wall — chipped, bullet-riddled, but never painted over.

---

## Quotes  
> “You can’t build a nation on the backs of dead men and call it justice.”  
> – Darrell, minutes before his execution

> “He didn’t just raise us. He raised hell.”  
> – [[Mark Jeffrey]]

---

## Affiliation  
- Former steel foreman, union leader  
- Founding member of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]  
- Enemy of the [[Loyalist Guard]] and [[The Duke]]

---

## Status  
**Deceased** – Executed by hanging on The Duke’s order, c. 18th of Dusktide, 2167

#  Dark Night


## Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎DARK NIGHT
> ![[dn.png|400]]  

**Date:** 30th of Hollowtide  
**Type:** Forced Observance / Day of Lawlessness
- Dark Night is a relatively new event in Disgraceland’s troubled history.  
- It began after a massive but failed uprising against **The Duke** — an event that shook his regime but ultimately ended in brutal suppression.
- Rather than simply erase the memory, The Duke twisted it into an annual reminder of his absolute power.  
- Every year since the uprising, on the 30th of [[CALENDAR|Hollowtide]], **The Duke orders all Loyalist Guard forces to stand down** for exactly 24 hours across all territories.
- **Only the Final Force remains active**, stationed around **The Silo** in Ashmoor to protect the wealthy and the ruling elite.

## Modern Observance

- **No Guard patrols** exist during Dark Night across [[Steeltown]], [[Charspire]], [[Gutter Row]], [[Threshton]], and [[the Drownlands]].
- **Ashmoor**, by contrast, becomes a fortress — [[Final Force]] soldiers patrol heavily around [[The Silo]] and its surrounding elite districts.
- **Crime explodes** across the unprotected regions: murders, robberies, fires, uprisings, and revenge killings surge.
- Some gangs and factions **plan entire operations** around Dark Night, knowing there will be no government interference.
- Many ordinary citizens **barricade their homes** and pray to survive until sunrise.

Meanwhile, within [[Ashmoor]], the night takes on a disturbingly festive tone.  
At **The Silo**, the wealthy and politically connected hold **grand parties** — drinking, dancing, and celebrating their untouchable status while the world outside burns.

---

## Cultural Significance

- **The Duke's Message:**  
  > "You are beasts without my rule. You will tear yourselves apart without my leash."
- **Psychological Warfare:**  
  Dark Night reinforces fear, dependency, and hopelessness. The chaos keeps citizens divided and desperate.
- **Resistance Symbol:**  
  For rebels and radicals, Dark Night is a solemn reminder of the original uprising — and a yearly call to remember those who fought and died for freedom.

> "In Ashmoor, they toast. In Steeltown, they bleed."


# 🧠 Notes

- Some underground movements now see Dark Night not as a defeat, but as an opportunity for resistance operations and assassinations.
- Religious cults tied to the **[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]** or **[[Faith of Mirella]]** hold secret rites during Dark Night, believing the veil between worlds is thinnest on this night.

---

# 📺 CRT Televisions

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Ashmoor Festival
> ![[crt.png|500]]  

Issued by decree of [[The Duke]], every family in Tribucia receives **one government-supplied CRT television** — whether they want it or not. These bulky, crackling boxes are considered “essential technology” by the regime, intended to connect the people with **[[TTV Studios|TTV]]**, the official state broadcast network.

---

## 📡 Broadcast Content

The only available channel on every set is **TTV**. There are no remotes, no buttons to change the channel. The airwaves are strictly monitored and centrally controlled from [[TTV Studios]] in [[Charspire]].

**TTV Programming Includes:**
- 🛑 **The [[State of Tribucia]]** – Weekly broadcast from [[The Duke]] himself.
- 🌙 **[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]** – Late-night propaganda and entertainment, Mon–Thurs.
- 🥊 **[[WLL: Fight Night on TTV]]** – Broadcast live every Restday (Friday), sponsored by [[Flint Garritt]].
- 📰 **TTV Nightly News** – A state-run news program (anchor TBD).

**When no scheduled programming is on-air, the screen defaults to eerie static.** There is no off switch — only unplugging the device or smashing it, the latter of which is strictly prohibited by law.

---

## 🏚️ Use Among the Poor

In the decaying slums of [[Gutter Row]], the smokestacks of [[Charspire]], and the shantytowns of [[Steeltown]], the glowing CRT screens serve a second purpose: **light source**. Residents often cluster around the flickering blue-white static in otherwise pitch-black homes. Some even time their evenings by the hum of the screen.

The televisions are seen as both a curse and a convenience — constant propaganda machines that also keep the shadows at bay.

---

## 🕵️‍♂️ Rumors & Urban Myths

Despite the controlled nature of TTV, whispers circulate that **some televisions have displayed... something else**. Unknown images. Strange figures. Messages not approved by The Duke.

No one has ever officially confirmed these sightings, but:
- A boy in [[Steeltown]] claimed he saw **a woman in a mask whispering names**.
- A miner in [[Charspire]] swears the screen turned blood red for six straight minutes.
- A vendor in [[Gutter Row]] insists he saw **[[Ora Razchek]]’s death house** appear in the static for a brief moment.

The Loyalist Guard has dismissed all such claims as "hallucinations caused by fatigue or substance abuse."

---

## 🧠 Trivia

- Most units are decades old, scavenged and rebuilt by [[Clay Millwrights]].
- Tampering with the TV is punishable by **20 lashes or 5 years of labor**, per Duke Mandate #47.
- A hidden chip inside each unit logs viewing duration and reports it back to TTV HQ.

# THE BLACKSHIFT MASSACRE

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
> **Date:** **2165** (21 years ago)
> **Location:** Blackshift Pit Mine, [[Charspire]]
> **Summary:** The **Blackshift Massacre** marks the most infamous atrocity committed by the [[Final Force]]. What began as a workers’ rebellion over deadly conditions and starvation rations in the Blackshift Pit ended in blood and infamy.  
[[The Duke]] ordered the FF to the site, seeking to end the standoff. He never gave a direct kill order, but the FF’s then-commander (now deceased) chose brute force.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Final Force
>> ![[bs.png|400]]

## The Massacre  
- **FF troopers**—including a young [[Sgt. Rottwyler]]—stormed the mine.
- All workers—men, women, and children—were massacred.  
- Survivors and witnesses claim the FF unleashed their arsenal without warning or mercy.
- The ground ran red and the smoke from burning equipment choked [[Charspire]] for days.

## Aftermath  
- [[The Duke]]’s silence and slow public response fueled outrage across Disgraceland.
- Only after mounting public fury did the regime admit the “grave mistake.” The families were all paid to keep quiet.
- The original FF commander died mysteriously within months; some say as penance, others say as a cover-up.

## The Reporter  
- A young, unnamed reporter for the **Tribucia Tribute** was on-site—hidden, taking photos.
- Their images, smuggled out and widely copied, became iconic symbols of state brutality.
- The reporter’s work fueled dissent and memorialized the massacre for future generations.

## Raynar Ventura’s Role  
- [[Raynar Ventura]] entered the Duke’s orbit soon after the Blackshift Massacre, seizing the opportunity to ingratiate himself during the Duke’s lowest moment.
- Ventura used his political cunning to help reshape the Duke’s public image, controlling the narrative and managing fallout in the aftermath.

## Legacy  
- “Blackshift” is now a curse in [[Charspire]] and across Disgraceland.
- Annual vigils and underground art keep the memory alive.
- The massacre’s infamy permanently stained the Duke’s rule; whispers about what happened that day still spread.
- Many see this as the moment the public learned the true cost of the Duke’s iron rule—and the birth of widespread dissent.

# Backburn Shows

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Backburn Show
> ![[bbshow.png|450]]  

## Overview  
**Backburn Shows** or Backburners are informal, often spontaneous music gatherings that erupt across Disgraceland — in alleyways, ruins, scrapyards, and fields. Named for the way they *"burn backward"* through neighborhoods like wildfire, these gatherings start as small jams and quickly swell into full-blown, pulse-throbbing performances under rusted scaffolding or broken moonlight.  

Though technically illegal under United Tribucian law for *“encouraging non-sanctioned assembly and the performance of subversive lyrics,”* Backburns are sacred to the common folk. Here, no stage, no tickets, no rules — just sound and sweat and something that almost feels like freedom.

---

## Origins  
The term *Backburn* was first coined by early street poets in [[Steeltown]] who described the way word of a jam would spread backward through the districts, lighting up ears long before boots hit gravel. These fires of rhythm couldn’t be contained.  

Legends say both [[Dusty Dillon]] and [[Jaden Kade]] first turned heads during midnight Backburns — one behind a collapsed factory furnace, the other in the shell of a bombed-out theater in [[Charspire]]. Their sounds — gritty, defiant, unfiltered — became the anthems of the ignored.

---

## Common Locations
- **[[Steeltown]]**: Often in rusted-out loading bays, rooftops, or inside gutted rail cars.  
- **[[Gutter Row]]**: Hidden courtyards off the [[Three Nail Market]], where drums and synths echo through poison-lit alleys.  
- **[[Charspire]]**: In old mine shafts, scorched lots, or beneath scaffolds during [[Loyalist Guard#Redforce|Redforce]] shift changes.  
- **[[The Drownlands]]**: Rare, but when they happen — eerie, swamp-lit, and whispered about for months.  
- **[[Threshton]]**: Usually tied to secret Rancher celebrations, shielded by crops and prairie silence.

---

## Enforcement & Rebellion  
[[TTV Studios]] and the [[Loyalist Guard]] officially denounce Backburn Shows as breeding grounds for *“anti-Tribucian messaging and sedition.”* Patrols are dispatched to break them up, but the gatherings shift fast — and locals protect them like sacred rites.  

Whispers claim even some lower-ranking Loyalists attend in secret, pulling caps low and mouthing lyrics with fire in their throats.

---

## Cultural Role  
Backburns aren’t just about music. They’re grief rituals. Love letters. Acts of war. Here, banned instruments wail, forbidden words fly, and hope lives for three chords longer than it should.  

Some say if you listen hard enough, you’ll hear the future humming through the static.

##  **[[Ashmoor Festival of Unity]]**

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Ashmoor Festival
> ![[unity.png|500]]  

**Date:** 14th of **[[CALENDAR|BLOOMSUN]]**  
**Type:** Propaganda Celebration  
**District Held:** [[Ashmoor#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]], [[Ashmoor]]
**Established by:** [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland

The **Ashmoor Festival of Unity**, often shortened to *Unity Day* or mockingly called *Duke’s Day*, is an annual celebration held on the 14th of **[[CALENDAR|BLOOMSUN]]** — commemorating the official founding and “rebuilding” of [[Ashmoor]] by [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland. It marks the beginning of the modern era in [[Ashmoor]] and serves as a symbol of Loyalist control, prosperity (for some), and enforced gratitude.

---

### 🎉 **Common Practices**

- **Parades** featuring Loyalist military units, schoolchildren waving banners, and mechanized floats sponsored by Clay Industries and other regime-aligned entities.
- **Concerts** held in the [[Ashmoor]] Central Plaza, showcasing government-approved artists and propaganda anthems.
- **The Grand Address**, a live broadcast from [[The Silo]], where The Duke speaks directly to the people of United Tribucia.
- **“Unity Tokens”** — ration boosters, entertainment passes, or temporary curfew lifts handed out in richer districts, sparking envy in the poor sectors.

---

### 🏙️ **Cultural Notes**

- The festival is **lavishly celebrated by the wealthy and loyal** in [[Ashmoor]], complete with masquerade balls and private rooftop galas.
- For citizens in regions like [[Steeltown]] or [[The Drownlands]], the day is **seen as a cruel farce** — a reminder of their suffering and exclusion from the so-called prosperity.
- Despite the cynicism, **many across Disgraceland still look forward to it** as a day of relief: no work, lighter patrols, and a chance to gather, drink, and complain in peace.

---

### 💬 **Quotes**

> “Every BLOOMSUN, he stands there in white and tells us we should be thankful. I stand there in grease and wonder how the fuck he sleeps at night.”  
> — [[Dusty Dillon]], overheard in [[Steeltown]]

> “It’s not a holiday. It’s a mirror. And some folks just don’t like what they see in it.”  
> — [[Morris Gable]], *Night Time with Morris Gable* (Episode #742)

# TTV Studios


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Hollow House
> ![[ttv.png|500]] 

> “Broadcasting Unity to All of Disgraceland — Like It or Not.”

## Details
**Location:** Gravenwild, [[Charspire]]  
**Type:** Post-apocalyptic Broadcast Station  
**Owner:** [[The Duke]] (through loyalist proxies)  
**Station Manager:** [[Owen McCready]] (see below)

---

### Overview

TTV Studios is the only functioning television and radio station in Disgraceland. Housed in a crumbling, retrofitted broadcast building topped by a patched-together transmission tower, it’s become the lone source of “official” news, propaganda, and nightly entertainment for the people of Tribucia. The original tower dates back to pre-Tetra times; the current crew scrounged, rewired, and extended it until the signal finally reached every region again.

**TTV** (“Tribucia TeleVision”) schedule:

| Program           | Date                              | Time              |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| [[TTV Evening News]]  | Every Weeknight                        | 18:00hrs       |
| [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]      | Every Weeknight          | 23:00hrs    |
| [[WLL Fight Night]]      | Weekly Every Restday   | 22:00hrs         |
| [[The Duke]]'s [[State Of Tribucia]] Address    | Weekly Every Alphaday| 20:00hrs           |

The building is a hodgepodge of old tech, scavenged gear, jury-rigged generators, and blacked-out windows. On-air sets are painted to look more impressive on screen than in person — think flickering stage lights, patched curtains, and “live” audiences comprised mostly of the same few extras in different hats.

---

### Staff & Security

- **Manager:** [[Owen McCready]] — A burned-out, deeply private old technician, brought in by The Duke’s people for his uncanny knack for keeping ancient tech alive. Just wants to clock out, drink himself to sleep, and avoid getting dragged into the region’s politics.
- **Security:** A mix of bored Loyalist Guards and failed actors doubling as “security” on camera.
- **Production Crew:** Whoever can still operate a camera, solder a wire, or read a script.

---

### Station Manager: [[Owen McCready]]

**Bio:**  
Gruff, hunched, maybe late 50s, always in a sweat-stained broadcast cap, haunted eyes. Used to run pirate radio back in the Water Wars. Knows how to get a picture up on a broken screen with nothing but a coat hanger and a prayer. Trusts nobody, drinks nightly, and keeps a sawed-off shotgun hidden behind the filing cabinet “just in case.” Hates The Duke, but hates the alternative (unpaid work, or worse) more.

> “I just keep the lights on. What you do in front of the cameras is your problem.”

---

### Lore Notes

- **The tower** is visible from anywhere in Gravenwild — tall, ugly, patched with sheet metal and wire, always buzzing with static and the occasional power arc.
- Most citizens tune in, even if they don’t admit it. Half for news, half for a laugh at how desperate the government is to control the story.
- Occasional “signal interruptions” happen when someone sabotages the lines or when storms hit, but Switch usually gets it running again.

---

# Tribucia Tribute

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[paper.png|300]]

## Overview  
The *Tribucia Tribute* is the largest and most widely read newspaper in [[TRIBUCIA MAP|Disgraceland]]. Though not officially mandatory, it’s printed overnight and delivered to homes and businesses every morning — making it a daily presence in nearly every region.

Originally founded as a beacon of free journalism, the paper has since become a tool of subtle propaganda under the watchful eye of [[The Duke]]. Direct criticism of the regime is forbidden, though occasional subversive truths still slip through — especially when reported by the paper’s most famous journalist.

---

## Ownership  
The paper is owned by [[Royce Sincayd]], a once-principled journalist turned political opportunist. Royce started the *Tribucia Tribute* out of a genuine love for storytelling, public truth, and accountability. Over time, he succumbed to political pressure and now cooperates directly with Loyalist Forces to ensure all Duke-facing articles are filtered or adjusted to maintain “order.”

Royce is not hated by the public — but nobody really trusts him either.

---

## Key Staff  

- **[[Rachel Gold]]** — The paper’s uncontested star reporter. She’s known across Tribucia as a folk hero. Brilliant, fearless, and relentless in her pursuit of truth. Her stories always find the beating heart of a crisis, even if she has to dig it out with her bare hands.  
  Despite the risk, [[Royce Sincayd]] is often forced to run her stories front and center, knowing the public demands it. Rachel constantly tests the paper’s boundaries and frequently butts heads with Royce over censorship.

- **[[Marlon Lambert]]** — A capable, methodical journalist who lives in [[Rachel Gold]]’s shadow. Marlon lacks her charisma but is quietly respected. He often cleans up after her, does follow-ups on her investigations, and keeps her safe when things get risky. He won’t say it, but he’s protective of her — maybe too much.

---

## Recent Controversy  
A recent front-page piece by [[Rachel Gold]] broke down the new fuel tax imposed by [[The Duke]], detailing how it disproportionately hurts working citizens while funneling wealth into Ashmoor. Though the article never directly attacked The Duke, the numbers spoke for themselves.  

The fallout was immediate: protests, ration hoarding, and quiet investigations into Rachel’s past sources. [[Royce Sincayd]] nearly fired her, but public backlash forced him to keep her in place — for now.

---

## Public Reputation  
The *Tribucia Tribute* is both trusted and distrusted. Most people read it because there’s no real alternative. But many know to read between the lines, especially in [[Rachel Gold]]’s stories.  

Her byline signals something worth reading.  
Royce’s editorials usually signal something worth ignoring.  
Nobody talks about Marlon’s stories — but everybody reads them.

---

## Possible Future Threads  
- An underground press begins circulating, inspired by [[Rachel Gold]]’s bravery.  
- [[Royce Sincayd]] receives a direct order from [[The Duke]] to muzzle her permanently.  
- [[Marlon Lambert]] begins investigating Rachel’s enemies... without telling her.

# 📍 Three Nail Market — Vileby, Gutter Row


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait
> ![[tnm.png|500]]  

## Overview

The **Three Nail Market** is the blackened heart of commerce in [[Gutter Row#Vileby|Vileby]], a festering urban sprawl within [[Gutter Row]]. Named after the three rusted nails still embedded in the wall of the first slave-post in the region, the market operates as a brutal bazaar of flesh, chemicals, and desperation. It's a place where danger is the currency, and survival is the only reward.

---

## Structure

### 🔹 The Top Layer – *"The Facade"*
- A chaotic mix of legitimate and not-so-legitimate vendors.
- Stalls sell scavenged tech, canned goods, reworked clothing, and "imported" wares.
- Some stores are fronts for brothels, gambling rings, or backroom clinics.
- Lanterns of specific colors above doorways serve as coded signals — red for sex, green for meds, blue for weapons.

### 🔸 The Mid Layer – *"The Run"*
- Reached through alleys, basements, or coded stairwells.
- Location of most drug deals, Luxyn exchanges, illegal surgeries, and smuggling transactions.
- Slave pens are wheeled in and out under cover of tarps.
- Frequented by gangs, mercs, and rogue surgeons.

### ⚫ The Deep Layer – *"The Roots"*
- Hidden tunnels and ruins beneath the city used during the Water Wars.
- Secretive auction halls, holding cells, execution rooms, and biochemical labs.
- Ghostly quiet, except when it’s not — screams are common and ignored.
- Whispers of blood rites, body modification dens, and worse.

---

## Notable Elements

- **[[Luxyn]] Trade**  
  A rare and potent hallucinogenic stimulant, Luxyn is difficult to manufacture.  
  - Main suppliers:  
    - **The [[Murray Boys]]** – a local crime family with blood-soaked hands.  
    - **[[Lash Hawkins]]** – a gutsy young street dealer with a growing rep.  
  - Both do their selling in Three Nail Market, often guarded and always watched.

- **Slave Auctions**  
  Weekly events held in the mid and deep layers. Children, workers, and “custom orders” available. Desperate men and women can "sell themselves" into slavery. This system is often abused.

- **Flesh Parlors**  
  Gruesome medical dens where "doctors" perform on the desperate.

- **Merc Boards**  
  Physical message boards listing contracts: hits, deliveries, abductions, or organ bounties.

---

## Power & Protection

- **The Nail Lords** *(Details TBD)*  
  A shadow council of market overlords who maintain order, enforce the rules, and extract tribute.

- **Mayor: [[Cricket Granger]]**  
  Corrupt and cunning. Publicly dismisses the market, privately benefits from it.

- **Official Force: [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]]**  
  Gutter Row's designated security unit. Known for brutality but rarely step foot inside Three Nail.

# [[The Ha Ha Hole]]

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Ha Ha Hole Comedy Club
> ![[haha.png|450]]  

**Location:** [[Savage Hill]], [[Gutter Row]]
**Founded:** 2140s  
**Founder:** [[Tyren Will]]

---

## Overview

Deep in the twisted alleys of [[Savage Hill]], where broken signs hang like nooses and laughter usually means someone’s about to get hurt, sits one of the most unlikely cultural landmarks in all of Disgraceland — **The Ha Ha Hole**.

Opened in the 2140s by a wild-eyed maniac named [[Tyren Will]], this underground comedy club has grown from a dive for drunks to a nightly pilgrimage site for anyone desperate to laugh — or drink — their way through the horror show of modern life. With a rotting neon grin over the door and the famous slogan **“First drink is on us”**, The Ha Ha Hole is packed nearly every night.

The club draws crowds from every region — even a few brave souls from [[Ashmoor]] and [[Threshton]] — all crammed into a basement of sweaty seats, leaning in for the next punchline, heckle, or blackout.

---

## The Founder – [[Tyren Will]]

A former traveling magician, failed preacher, and once-suspected poisoner, [[Tyren Will]] is a living myth. Nobody’s entirely sure how old he is or how he managed to keep The Ha Ha Hole open during some of the darkest years after the Tetra Bomb, but he’s always been there — top hat, cane, silver tongue and all. 

Now well into his eighties, he still takes the stage unannounced on occasion to deliver bizarre rants, surreal monologues, or what he calls “anti-jokes” — strange, unsettling stories that sometimes end with a single word: *“Think.”* The audience still cheers him every time.

---

## Atmosphere

- **Stage:** A cracked wooden platform with a dented mic that sparks when tapped.
- **Decor:** Candlelight, red velvet curtains stained with gods-know-what, and every wall covered in graffiti and signatures from past performers.
- **Drinks:** The first one's free, everything after that gets progressively stronger (and less legal).
- **Security:** None. The crowd polices itself, usually with laughter or bottles.

---

## Signature Acts

- **Joley Punch** – Queen of the deadpan roast. She once told a joke so mean a Redforce officer walked out in tears.
- **Little Duke** – A parody act mocking The Duke in crown and cape. Somehow still alive.
- **Shivvy** – Combines burlesque with satire. Leaves the crowd dazed, confused, and howling.
- **Riggs Mahoney** – An ex-Loyalist turned loudmouth stage beast.
- **The Masked Heckler** – A recurring mystery comic who destroys hecklers with surgical precision. No one knows who it is.

---

## Cultural Impact

Despite being a cesspool of rebellion, filth, and unlicensed liquor, **The Ha Ha Hole** has become a cultural staple. Even citizens loyal to The Duke secretly tune into bootleg recordings of sets from the club. Its influence on slang, satire, and protest culture across Disgraceland is undeniable.

[[The Duke]] publicly despises the place and has tried to shut it down twice — once via regulation, once with a full Loyalist raid. Both attempts failed. The crowd turned violent. The club only got more popular.

---

## Rumors & Lore

- **Red Room in the Back:** Some say a private room exists where Tyren meets with outlaws, prophets, and ghosts.
- **The Laugh That Kills:** Urban myth claims one joke told in '62 made a man laugh so hard he seized and died. The tape was burned.
- **Secret Resistance:** Some believe The Ha Ha Hole is more than a club — it’s a safehouse, a spy ring, a gathering place for the loud and dangerous.

---

## Quote

> *“We don’t do hope here. We do laughter — it stings less.”*  
> — [[Tyren Will]]

#  [[Geo Huxley|Geo]]'s P.I.


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait
> ![[gpi.png|500]]  

## Overview

Geo’s P.I. started as a favor — one missing girl, no one else looking. Word spread. Now it’s **the** place you go in [[Gutter Row]] when you need someone to find the truth, retrieve the lost, or deliver justice without waiting for permission.

Geo works alone. No receptionist, no backup. Just his reputation and whatever’s in his coat. He’s turned down bribes from the [[Loyalist Guard#Redforce|Redforce]], pissed off three regional mayors, and solved cases that [[Loyalist Guard]] "couldn’t."

---

### 📍 Location

**Crossyork, [[Gutter Row]]**  
A decaying district wedged between dead factories and rail lines. Rats run thicker than rainwater, and Blackforce rarely patrols here unless they’re dragging a body out.

Geo’s P.I. is located above **Jasko’s Pawn & Gun**, a crooked little corner shop run by a mute ex-smuggler who owes [[Geo Huxley]] his life. The office itself is a creaking second-floor unit with a cracked glass door that reads:

**GEO’S P.I. — Discreet. Determined. Dangerous.**

### 💰 Payment & Policy

- **Price:** Hefty. [[Geo Huxley]] doesn’t work cheap — not because he’s greedy, but because what he does costs. Time. Blood. Silence.
    
- **Currency:** Slugs preferred. Barter possible. Payment plans accepted if your story gets under his skin.
    
- **No Refunds.** If you lie to him, he walks. If you come clean, he’ll crawl through hell for you.
    

---

### 🕵️ Services Offered

- **Missing Persons** — the living, the dead, or the unsure
    
- **Murder Investigations** — especially the kind everyone else ruled “accidental”
    
- **Blackmail & Secrets** — identifying leaks, ghosting threats
    
- **Surveillance** — targets, buildings, caravans
    
- **Off-the-Book Justice** — if you know, you know
    

---

### 🧩 Notable Cases

- _The Thornburn Widow_ – Found her son buried beneath a Redforce scrapyard
    
- _The Weeping Mask_ – Unmasked a killer posing as a traveling preacher
    
- _Station Ghosts_ – Uncovered a Loyalist interrogation chamber beneath the Crossyork rail yard
    
- _MUTE FILES_ – Rumored job involving a missing Unseen Widow… never confirmed
    

---

### 🧃 Street Reputation

People in Gutter Row say Geo’s P.I. gets results even the Loyalists read about after. He's not beloved, but he’s respected. The desperate know his door. The dangerous know his eyes.

> “It ain’t cheap. But if Geo takes your case, you’ll get an answer. Just hope you’re ready to hear it.”

# Four Tombs Islands


> *"A place of the dead, ruled by the damned."*  
> —Common saying in [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]]

## Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Four Tombs Islands
> ![[4t.png|400]] 

The **Four Tombs Islands** are a small chain of four landmasses located off the southeast coast of [[Gutter Row]], nestled in the shadowy swell of the [[WATER#The Dead Waters|Dead Waters]]. Though seemingly tranquil from the mainland, the islands have a deadly reputation—thanks to their only residents, the [[Rustwater Raiders]].

Each of the islands is named for the enormous, ancient tomb it houses. These monolithic structures, shaped like thin obelisks or long pillars, pierce the sky like grave markers for forgotten kings. No known historical record explains who built them or who lies within. Locals claim the tombs are ancient rulers from time immemorial.

## Inhabitants

The **[[Rustwater Raiders]]** have completely taken over the largest of the four islands. They've fortified the ruins of an old coastal **fort** and converted the still-standing **lighthouse** into a watchtower. Any ships foolish enough to drift too close are warned off—or sunk. The Raiders operate out of this isolated stronghold, launching occasional raids on the coastlines of [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]] and [[Charspire]].

No one lands on the Four Tombs Islands without permission. No one.

## Geography & Wildlife

While the islands are soaked in dread, they are reportedly lush with overgrowth and teeming with wild game. Deer, wild boar, seabirds, and freshwater springs make the land viable for long-term survival, though only the Raiders benefit from the abundance.

Many hunters and desperate fishermen have tried sneaking ashore over the years. None are known to have returned.

## Legends & Lore

- Some claim the tombs are cursed, and that the Raiders have made blood pacts with whatever lies buried inside.
- Others whisper that strange blue lights glow around the monuments during storms, and that voices can be heard humming beneath the soil.
- Old [[Gutter Row]] tales say one of the tombs isn't a grave at all—but a sealed gate.

## Strategic Significance

The Four Tombs Islands sit in an important position along the southern shipping lines between [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]] and [[CHARSPIRE#Broken Bones Bay|Broken Bones Bay]]. The presence of the Raiders has made this route perilous, forcing most trade vessels to reroute far north through [[WATER#Grave Bay|Grave Bay]] or risk brutal ambush.

## Known Structures

- **The Lighthouse** – Converted to a sniper post and signal tower.
- **The Old Fort** – Now the heavily guarded headquarters of the Rustwater Raiders.
- **The Four Tombs** – One on each island, made of ancient stone and towering high above the treetops.

---

> **WARNING:**  
> The [[Rustwater Raiders]] have been designated *Hostile Non-Recognized Sovereign Entities* by [[Loyalist Guard]] Command. Civilian approach is strictly prohibited. Survivors will not be recovered.

# [[Coffin Island]] 🩸  
*Also known as: The Coffin*  
**Location:** Largest island in [[Bone Lake]]  
**Type:** Offshore Supermax Prison  
**Territorial Affiliation:** Neutral (Supplied by [[Ashmoor]], governed by [[The Duke]])  


---

## 📜 Overview  
[[Coffin Island]] is the most feared prison in all of [[TRIBUCIA MAP]]. Surrounded by the icy black waters of [[Bone Lake]], it serves as a final destination for traitors, dissidents, escapees, and anyone [[The Duke]] wants erased from history. No trial. No paperwork. Just a number, a cell, and silence.

The prison is built atop a decaying [[Water Wars]]-era military research complex, repurposed into a fortress of misery. Locals call it *The Coffin* because once you're sealed inside, you're already dead.

---

## 🔒 Structure & Design  
- **Triple perimeter walls**: Electrified, rusting, always manned  
- **Blackspire Tower**: Central watchtower and signal relay — visible from [[Burton Point]]  
- **Underground chambers**: Pre-War bunkers turned solitary tombs and "processing" rooms  
- **Open-yard punishments**: Inmates are subjected to freezing winds as discipline  
- **Single-point dock access**: One weekly barge brings food, medicine, and rotating guards

---

## 🌫 Conditions  
- Constant cold, high winds, and bone-deep dampness  
- Prisoners are **not named**, only numbered  
- **Disappearance without record** is standard protocol  
- Brutal guards, spoiled rations, no medical care unless it’s experimental  
- Prisoners fight, scream, or go mad. Sometimes all three

---

## 🧍 Leadership & Staff  
- **[[Katarina Volkoff]]** – A cold, precise woman in her late 30s. Daughter of a decorated soldier. Runs the prison like a forward operating base. Took over after the last warden was murdered in his sleep — some say by guards, others by prisoners. Rimshaw personally petitioned [[The Duke]] for the job. Rumors swirl that her loyalty came with favors, but no one dares say that to her face.  
- Most guards are dishonorably discharged [[Greenforce]] members, bitter and cruel  
- Whispers persist that [[Ora Razchek]] still pulls strings in the tunnels below

---

## 🩸 Myths & Rumors  
- **"No one escapes."** The waters are deadly, the island worse  
- The **Dead Choir**, a cult of prisoners, holds nightly rituals in the tunnels below  
- It’s said a **former Duke family member** is locked away under a false identity  
- Common saying in [[Ashmoor]]: *"Coffin’s got no door. Only a lid."*

---

## ⛓ Notable Mentions  
- **Prisoner #1412 – "Moorjaw"**: A large, quiet inmate held in the deepest cellblock. He’s survived 12 winters, multiple assaults, and even an execution order that was mysteriously rescinded. Some say he’s [[The Duke]]’s hidden bastard son, locked away after a failed uprising. Others claim he knows the truth about what’s buried under Coffin Island  
- The **Dead Choir** — cult-like inmate group living in the forgotten sublevels. They chant, bleed, and speak in riddles. Rimshaw tolerates them… barely  
- Ferry traffic to [[Coffin Island]] is managed through [[Burton Point]], with supply runs approved only by the Warden herself

---

## 🗺 Related Locations  
- [[Bone Lake]] – The frigid lake surrounding the island  
- [[Burton Point]] – Nearest mainland ferry site  
- [[The Drownlands]] – Visible shore if you ever made it across… not that you would

77.title: Unseen Widows
77.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Unseen Widows]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"faction","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/UnseenWidows.png","leader":[["Prophet Veerah"]],"status":"Active","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","tags":["faction","widow"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/09 10:23:32"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: faction NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/UnseenWidows.png leader: [[Prophet Veerah]] status: Active location: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" tags: - faction - widow --- # UNSEEN WIDOWS ```datacards TABLE thumbnail, location, status FROM #widow SORT name ASC // Settings preset: compact columns: 8 imageProperty: thumbnail showImageOnHover: true cardSpacing: 4 ``` > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎UNSEEN WIDOWS > ![[UnseenWidows.png|400]] ## Overview **Group:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Founder:** [[Prophet Veerah]] **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Whispers in the wind **Current Leader:** [[Prophet Veerah]] **2nd in Command:** [[Riley Thorne]] **Status:** Active **Controlled Territory:** [[The Drownlands]] **Members:** [[Prophet Veerah]], [[Nita Blackbird]], [[Riley Thorne]], [[Raina & Risa]], [[Len Vyne]] ---
History of the Unseen Widows
>

“Veerah will lead us all to the everlasting light.”

The Unseen Widows are a shadow that lingers over Disgraceland — silent, patient, and deadly. They are not a mere faction or band of raiders; they are a force born from sorrow and vengeance. Composed solely of women who have endured the worst of the world’s cruelty, the Widows move unseen through the ruins, striking without mercy and disappearing before the blood dries. Their name is both a warning and a promise. Many who cross them will not live to see their assassins. The Widows trace their origin to Veerah, a self-proclaimed prophet who rose from the ashes of despair. After her vivid dreams of the future began to come true, she was declared a living oracle by those desperate to believe in something greater. But the Widows were not built on faith alone. Many of the women who now call her leader were once victims of the Duke’s brutality — slaves, prisoners, and survivors of unimaginable torment. When they had no one else, Veerah offered them purpose. In her name, they found strength. Operating under a strict code of silence and loyalty, the Unseen Widows are masters of assassination, espionage, and psychological warfare. Veerah teaches them the art of moving without sound, of vanishing into shadows, and of striking down their enemies before they are even aware of the threat. Each Widow wears black, their faces partially veiled to mask their identities. Only Veerah remains unveiled, her golden hair and striking presence a symbol of the divine force they believe guides them. A gold bird emblem — the mark of the Widows — gleams on the chest of every member, a symbol of rebirth from the ashes of their past. But it is not only steel that makes the Widows formidable. Veerah instructs her followers to use their femininity as a weapon. Beauty, charm, and seduction are as deadly as any blade in a world where desire blinds even the most powerful. The Widows infiltrate, manipulate, and dismantle their enemies from within, leaving ruin in their wake. While most of the women are trained assassins, others specialize in gathering intelligence, sowing fear, and undermining the Duke’s strongholds. Their devotion to Veerah is absolute. Many see her as a living conduit of divine will, believing that her visions are proof of a higher power’s guidance. Dissent is rare, but those who question her prophecies are met with suspicion. Even the most trusted Widows, like Riley Thorne, Raina, and Risa, carry unspoken doubts about the true nature of Veerah’s visions — but to speak them aloud would risk exile or worse. While their methods are brutal, the Widows justify their violence as necessary in their fight against the Duke’s tyranny. But the longer they operate from the shadows, the more the line between justice and vengeance blurs. For now, they remain a whispered legend, feared by the powerful and revered by the oppressed. In Disgraceland, mothers tell their children that the Widows only come for the wicked. But in truth, the Widows come for anyone standing in their way.

Details

>> **Group:** [[Third Row]] >> **Founder:** [[Shad Rengal]] >> **Home Location:** [[Gutter Row]] >> **Public Reputation:** Feared >> **Current Leader:** [[Samson Knight]] >> **2nd in Command:** >> **Status:** Active >> **Primary Headquarters:** Reapton, Gutter Row >> **Controlled Territory:** Gutter Row, Three Nail Market --- ## Overview A ruthless, street-born gang operating out of [[Reapton]] in [[Gutter Row]], **The Third Row** rose from desperation and grit to become the undisputed rulers of the [[Three Nail Market]]. Once just a clique of kids from Row Three, they now control trade, fear, and punishment throughout the district. --- ## 🔰 Symbols & Identity - **Colors:** Purple and black Members wear a **purple bandana** somewhere visible when in public — a sign of pride and warning. - **Tattoo:** A large **"III"** (three vertical scars or lines), with the word **"ROW"** carved or inked across it. Common placements include forearms, necks, and knuckles. - **Taglines / Street Sayings:** - *“Third Row rides deep.”* - *“Cross the Row, dig a hole.”* - *“Three nails, no mercy.”* --- ## 🧠 Leadership ### **Samson Knight** (a.k.a. **Mr. Knight**) A towering, sharp-minded Black man with a reputation for calm brutality. Street-raised and steel-spined, **Mr. Knight** unified the fractured remains of The Third Row in the 2170s after years of decline. Now, he oversees the entire [[Three Nail Market]] from the shadows — or from a barstool, depending on the day. His word is law. --- ## 📜 Origins & History - **Founded:** Circa 2140s By **Shad Rengal** and **Eddie Furlong**, two poor Charspire miners who worked night shifts and ran rackets by day. Originally just a way to make extra coin, the gang evolved into a powerful syndicate. - **Eddie’s Death:** Died in the 2160s under mysterious circumstances — rumored hit job over Luxyn territory. - **The Blackshift Massacre:** Shad Rengal was killed during this tragic and pivotal event. His death left the Row rudderless and vulnerable. - **Reformation:** In the 2170s, **Samson Knight** rose from the lower ranks and crushed rival cliques, uniting the remnants under a new code and strict hierarchy. --- ## 🎯 Influence - The Third Row is the *de facto* authority inside the [[Three Nail Market]]. - Loyalist guards and even [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] units avoid direct conflict with them. - They control the movement of Luxyn (through unofficial deals with **The Murray Boys** and **Lash Hawkins**) and take a cut from every transaction in the market — legal or otherwise. --- Want to build out Mr. Knight’s inner circle? Maybe a few named enforcers, chemists, or lieutenants from different eras of the Row? Could also give them a home base — like a burned-out rec center turned war room.

80.title: Steeltown Wrecking Crew
80.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"faction","NoteStatus":"New","religion":"Non-Believer","leader":[["Jimmy Douglass"]],"location":"[[Steeltown]]","faction":"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","tags":["steeltown","faction","wrecking_crew"],"thumbnail":"zz_media/SWC.png","created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/04 19:05:04"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ## Overview **Group:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Founder** [[Jimmy Douglass]] **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Beloved by the people **Current Leader:** [[Jimmy Douglass]] **2nd in Command:** [[Mark Jeffrey]] **Status:** Active **Primary Headquarters:** [[Wrecking Crew Clubhouse]] **Controlled Territory:** [[STEELTOWN]] **Members:** [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]], [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen]], [[Selena Matissao]], [[Rodney Blythe]], [[Abel May Jr.]], [[Lincoln Jones]] ---
History of the Steeltown Wrecking Crew
>

“Pray to El Santo, the Wrecking Crew is coming.”

The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] wasn’t born from ambition — it was born from grief. Long before [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland claimed his iron throne, [[Steeltown]] was a place of industry and resilience. Steel mills once roared, their fires lighting the sky as men like [[Darrell Douglass]] worked tirelessly to provide for their families. The people of Steeltown didn’t have much, but they had each other — a bond forged in sweat and smoke. But when the [[Tetra bomb]] fell and the water wars erupted, everything changed. The mills shut down, and the city crumbled. Fuel became scarce, and clean water even scarcer. The Duke, sensing opportunity, seized control of what little remained, imposing brutal taxes and using his enforcers to crush any resistance. When the people of Steeltown dared to stand up, the Duke made an example of them. Among those victims was Darrell Douglass, a man who refused to bow. He led a strike against the Duke’s fuel rationing, calling for fair treatment. His courage inspired others, but the Duke had no tolerance for defiance. Darrell was beaten and left to die in the streets — a message to anyone who dared to challenge the regime. But the Duke underestimated the spirit of Steeltown. Darrell’s sons, Jimmy and [[Mark Jeffrey]], didn’t weep. They didn’t beg. They rose. Fueled by anger and the need for justice, Jimmy vowed to tear down the system that took their father. He gathered a handful of like-minded souls — fighters, mechanics, survivors — and together they formed the Steeltown Wrecking Crew. At first, they were nothing more than a band of rebels on patched-together bikes, striking back where they could and vanishing before the Duke’s forces could respond. But word spread. Stories of the Crew's defiance reached every corner of Disgraceland. People whispered of the brothers in black, of roaring engines and fires in the night. For the forgotten, the Wrecking Crew became a symbol of resistance. Jimmy, with his relentless fire, led the charge. Mark, ever the tactician, made sure they stayed one step ahead. They struck supply chains, liberated prisoners, and rerouted stolen resources to the people. And as their legend grew, so did their numbers. The Steeltown Wrecking Crew welcomed outcasts and survivors — anyone willing to fight for something greater. Among the first to join was [[Abel May Jr.]], a towering force who had been left for dead by the Duke’s men. Jimmy and Mark saved his life, and from that day, Abel swore to stand by them. He became the Crew’s enforcer, a wall of muscle and loyalty. Then came [[Joe Ameen]], the mechanical genius who kept the Crew’s bikes and rigs running. Joe hated the Duke’s control over the fuel supply, and his skills became invaluable in their war. The Crew rode faster and hit harder with Joe’s ingenuity fueling their machines. [[Katie Kowalski]] was another pillar of the Crew. A self-taught doctor, she grew up alongside Mark and Joe. When the violence of the wasteland left its mark, it was Katie’s steady hands that patched the wounds. Her kindness tempered the Crew’s brutality, a reminder that not all battles are fought with steel. Even as the Crew grew, their bonds remained unbreakable. Every patch earned was a promise — to fight, to protect, and to stand together. The Crew wasn’t just a rebellion. It was family. But the Duke wasn’t blind. As the Wrecking Crew’s reputation spread, so did the Duke’s wrath. He sent his enforcers to burn their hideouts, slaughter their allies, and sow fear wherever the Crew’s name was spoken. Brady and Brody May, twisted remnants of the Duke’s experiments, were unleashed as his monstrous enforcers. The fact that they were Abel’s own cousins made the betrayal even more bitter. Yet, no matter how much blood the Duke spilled, the Crew endured. Jimmy’s calls for full rebellion grew louder. He believed the people of Disgraceland were ready to rise. But Mark, ever the cautious one, knew the price of war. Tension simmered between the brothers, though their love for each other kept it from boiling over. In the face of hardship, the Crew’s spirit only strengthened. [[Selena Matissao]] joined the fight, a fierce warrior who had lost her husband to the Duke’s cruelty. Known as The Phoenix in the streets, she brought her tracking skills and ruthless efficiency to the Crew’s cause. When [[Lincoln Jones]] arrived, his quick thinking and fierce loyalty earned him a place among them — as well as the role of the Crew’s most celebrated cook. Now, the Steeltown Wrecking Crew is more than a rebellion. They are a symbol of what Disgraceland could be — free from tyranny, united by the bonds of survival. They still ride the twisted highways, their engines roaring defiance against the Duke’s rule. For Jimmy, the war is far from over. He dreams of the day the Duke falls, of a world where children no longer grow up in fear. Mark watches the horizon, knowing the hardest battles are yet to come. Abel, Joe, Katie, Selena, Lincoln, and every patched-in member stand ready — because to wear the Steeltown Wrecking Crew patch means to fight for something worth dying for. And so, they ride. ---

[[Lyla Bonetooth]] **Home Location:** [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] / [[WATER#Sinners' Sea|Sinner's Sea]] / [[WATER#The Dead Waters|Dead Waters]] **Public Reputation:** Feared across the water **Current Leader:** Capt. [[Lyla Bonetooth]] **2nd in Command:** [[Blacktide Cray]] **Status:** Active **Primary Headquarters:** Aboard *[[The Black Marauder]]* **Controlled Territory:** The open waters of Rustwater Bay, Sinner's Sea & Dead Waters **Members:** [[Lyla Bonetooth]], [[Blacktide Cray]], [[Clinton Firebay]], [[Silas Vayne]], [[Zadie Adeyemi]], [[Darius Adeyemi]], [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] ---
History of the Rustwater Raiders
>

“Stormborn. Steel-fed. No graves on water.”

The [[Rustwater Raiders]] are Disgraceland’s most infamous aquatic marauders, their black sails a harbinger of violence and smoke. Born from betrayal and bound by blood, they sail where no one else dares, feeding on fear and salt. Captain [[Lyla Bonetooth]] forged the Raiders from chaos. Her mutiny aboard a government patrol ship lit the first fire — when she seized the vessel and rechristened it [[The Black Marauder]], the era of the Raiders began. What followed was a campaign of calculated terror: raiding settlements, destroying convoys, and rewriting the rules of power in the bay. Beside her sails the stone-faced [[Blacktide Cray]], a man said to have drowned once and clawed his way back. And behind the captain’s smile is [[Silas Vayne]], the crew’s voice in foreign waters and their dagger in the dark. [[Zadie Adeyemi]] and [[Darius Adeyemi]], siblings with secrets, fuel the Raiders' dominance through invention, sabotage, and strategy. [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] — once a killer-for-hire, now a killer-by-oath — ensures discipline through violence. Their reach spans far past the deck of the Marauder. They rule invisible harbors and hidden ports, unmarked on any map but whispered of in terror. No fortress is safe, no merchant unwatched. Even the [[The Duke]] treads lightly when the Raiders loom. Their code is brutal: freedom at all costs, and loyalty unto death. Mutiny is met with blades. Weakness is thrown to the sea. But loyalty? Loyalty is treasure — and Captain Bonetooth rewards it with spoils and survival. The Raiders live without chains. No kings. No borders. Just the wind, the blade, and the endless blue. And still they sail — through mist and myth, leaving legends in their wake. ---

82.title: Rancher Collective
82.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Rancher Collective]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"faction","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/rcl.png","leader":[["Turner Anderson"]],"status":"Active","location":"[[Threshton]]","faction":"[[Rancher Collective]]","tags":["faction","protagonist","rancher"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/06 15:07:37"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: faction NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/rcl.png leader: [[Turner Anderson]] status: Active location: "[[Threshton]]" faction: "[[Rancher Collective]]" tags: - faction - protagonist - rancher --- # RANCHER COLLECTIVE ```datacards TABLE thumbnail, location, status FROM #rancher SORT name ASC // Settings preset: compact columns: 8 imageProperty: thumbnail showImageOnHover: true cardSpacing: 4 ``` > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[rcl.png|400]] ## Overview **Group:** [[Rancher Collective]] **Founder:** [[Harp Langston]] **Home Location:** [[Threshton]] **Public Reputation:** Mostly loved by the people **Current Leader:** [[Turner Anderson]] **2nd in Command:** [[Freddy Blanchard]] **Status:** Active **Primary Headquarters:** [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] **Controlled Territory:** [[Threshton]]'s ranches **Members:** [[Turner Anderson]], [[Freddy Blanchard]], [[Harp Langston]], [[Danny Dandelion]], [[Beau DuNoir]] ---
History of the Rancher Collective
>

“Our mission is survival.”

Long before [[The Duke]] cemented his rule with rations and rifle barrels, [[Threshton]] was just dust, starvation, and wild cattle. After the [[Tetra Bomb]], most of the area fell silent — fields went fallow, families scattered, and the old supply chains turned to rust. What remained was fought over, stolen, or hoarded by those with the might to defend it. But in the ruins of that scorched earth, after decades had healed what time could of the land, a man named [[Harp Langston]] planted a seed — literally and otherwise. He built [[Threshton#Red Night Ranch|Red Night Ranch]] with scarred hands and the kind of fury only true survival breeds. While others traded bullets for bread, Harp raised cattle and coaxed wheat out of poisoned soil. His methods were brutal, his land cursed with sweat and bone, but somehow, it worked. He fed himself, then a few neighbors, then word started spreading: “There’s food in [[Threshton]].” Soon, other ranches sprouted like weeds around Red Night — desperate men trying to mimic Harp’s stubborn miracle. A few succeeded. Most failed. But the ones who made it? Harp brought them to his table. Not out of charity. Out of strategy. “We got two choices,” he’d said, leaning over a cracked map and a bottle of rotgut whiskey. “Fight each other ‘til we all starve… or link arms and deal from strength.” Thus, the [[Rancher Collective]] was born — five ranches banding together, agreeing to share resources, protect their convoys, and negotiate food distribution as one voice. And it worked. [[The Duke]], still consolidating power in [[Ashmoor]], needed a reliable food source — and the Collective had it. So a deal was struck: 30% for the ranchers. 70% for the Duke. Harsh, but better than bullets. Over time, ranches rose and fell, and with them, membership shifted. Only Harp remained constant — the scarred sentinel of Red Night Ranch. Others came and went. Turner Anderson, now the largest landowner in Threshton, brought size and steady leadership. Freddy Blanchard brought heart and muscle. Beau DuNoir brought silver-tongued deals and backroom charm. And then, like a bad smell in a locked room, came Danny Dandelion, who conned his way into Snake Kiss Ranch and a seat at the table. The Collective operates under simple but ironclad rules: - Majority vote rules. Always. - No one acts alone in major trade matters. - All members must contribute to the food output. - And every meeting ends with a shot of whiskey — no matter how heated the vote. They are not friends. They are not brothers. They are a working alliance, forged by fire and held together by the brittle string of necessity. Without them, Disgraceland starves. With them, it teeters on the edge of rebellion. And everyone knows — the day the [[Rancher Collective]] falls apart… the whole damn region goes with it.

83.title: Loyalist Guard
83.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Loyalist Guard]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"faction","NoteStatus":"New","leader":[["The Duke"]],"status":"Active","location":"[[ASHMOOR]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","tags":["antagonist","military","faction","loyalist"],"thumbnail":[["zz_media/lgg.png"]],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/04 18:40:55"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: faction NoteStatus: New leader: [[The Duke]] status: Active location: "[[ASHMOOR]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" tags: - antagonist - military - faction - loyalist thumbnail: [[zz_media/lgg.png]] --- # LOYALIST GUARD ```datacards TABLE thumbnail, location, status FROM #loyalist SORT name ASC // Settings preset: grid columns: 6 imageProperty: thumbnail imageHeight: 30px showImageOnHover: true cardSpacing: 4 ``` > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Loyalist Guard > ![[lgg.png|400]] **Group:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Founder:** [[The Duke]] & [[General Colt]] **Home Location:** [[Ashmoor]] **Public Reputation:** Feared and Resented **Current Leader:** [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland **2nd in Command:** [[General Colt]] **Status:** Active **Primary Headquarters:** [[The Silo]] **Controlled Territory:** Across all of [[TRIBUCIA MAP]] ---
History of the Loyalist Guard
>

“Obedience is order. Order is survival.”

In the scorched days following the [[Tetra Bomb]], [[The Duke]] knew he needed more than fear to hold what he’d seized. He needed *control*. He found it in a man named [[General Colt]], a former military tactician with a broken moral compass and a talent for discipline. Together, they created the Loyalist Guard — not a militia, but a machine. The Guard began as a personal protection unit for the Duke, drawn from the dregs of old-world armies, ex-mercenaries, and psychopaths. Colt molded them into an elite force: brutal, obedient, and unquestioning. Every recruit underwent reconditioning. Every mission ended in silence. Over time, the Guard grew into a nation-spanning power — a symbol of fear etched into the fabric of every region in Disgraceland. To enforce the Duke’s rule more effectively, specialized subgroups were deployed into each territory: #### **Blueforce** – Stationed in [[Steeltown]]; used for riot control and Wrecking Crew suppression. #### **Greenforce** – Based in [[Ashmoor]]; guards the elite, runs checkpoints, and oversees Silo operations. #### **Blackforce** – Active in [[GUTTER ROW]]; works with informants, black markets, and slave transports. #### **Redforce** – Brutal enforcers in [[Charspire]]; protects Mayor Brile and ensures factory compliance. #### **Amberforce** – Operating in [[Threshton]]; watches ranchers and tracks illegal food supplies. At the Guard’s head remains General Colt, a man feared even by the Duke’s inner circle. His enforcer, **[[Sgt. Rottwyler]]**, handles discipline internally with savage precision. Beneath them operate a growing roster of loyal agents: [[Raynar Ventura]], silent but surgical; [[Jacoban Clay]], a political insider and family to the feared Clays of [[GUTTER ROW]]; and [[Emily Burton]], the cold, calculating logistics coordinator who ensures the Duke’s will moves like clockwork. More terrifying still are the Duke’s “fail-safes” — experimental soldiers twisted by science and desperation. [[Brady]] and [[Brody May]], former men turned monsters, unleashed only when terror alone won’t do. For many, the Loyalist Guard *is* the law. For others, it’s the boot that never lifts. They are feared, hated, and unrelenting. But above all else — they are loyal. --- ## Regional Forces - **Blueforce** – Steeltown - **Greenforce** – Ashmoor - **Blackforce** – Gutter Row - **Redforce** – Charspire - **Amberforce** – Threshton ## Enemies - [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] - [[Unseen Widows]] ## Allies - [[Soria Langston-Clay]] - [[Jacoban Clay]] ## Rumors & Secrets > - “There’s something beneath [[The Silo]]… and the Guard protects it at all costs.” > - “The Redforce boys in Charspire aren’t just guards. They run the whole damn factory floor.” > - “Some say Brody May doesn’t sleep. Or blink.”
