**Base of Operations:** Nightclub in Vileby, Gutter Row  
**Leaders:** [[Marco Murray]] (boss), [[Francis Murray]] (enforcer), [[Rosa Murray]] (treasurer), [[Nico Murray]] (junior member)  
**Allies:** Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] (Charspire), Mayor [[Cricket Granger]] (Gutter Row)  
**Main Activities:** Drug distribution, extortion

---

## Overview

The Murray Boys are the most feared crime family in [[Gutter Row]] and [[Charspire]], their influence growing every year. Built from nothing by [[Marco Murray]], the crew started with petty hustles and small-time rackets. Marco kept a low profile, never letting the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] cops catch a whiff of his real business.

As Marco’s [[Luxyn]] operation grew, he brought his brother Francis on board. Together, they built the Murray Boys into the go-to organization for anyone needing muscle, drugs, or a debt collected. When Mayor Cricket Granger found out about Marco’s Luxyn trade, he offered protection—so long as the Murray Boys moved product for him. Later, a similar deal was struck with Mayor Brile in Charspire, giving the Murrays control of Luxyn’s supply chain from mine to market.

Rosa Murray, Marco’s wife, manages the family’s finances and keeps the books so clean even [[The Duke]]’s men have trouble finding dirt. Their son, Nico, is just starting to make a name for himself—mostly causing headaches for the rest of the crew.

---

## Structure

- **Marco Murray (Boss):** Founder and brains of the operation. Handles major deals, alliances, and keeps the peace between Gutter Row and Charspire.
- **Francis Murray (Enforcer):** Marco’s loyal brother. Acts as the muscle—settling scores, collecting debts, and making sure nobody crosses the Murray Boys twice.
- **Rosa Murray (Treasurer):** Marco’s wife and the crew’s accountant. Keeps the money flowing, bribes paid, and the authorities distracted.
- **Nico Murray (Junior):** Marco and Rosa’s son. Spoiled, cocky, and trying to prove himself in the family business.

---

## Activities

- **Selling & Distributing Luxyn:** The Murray Boys control most of the Luxyn trade in Gutter Row and Charspire, supplying for Mayor Brile and Mayor Granger.
- **Extorting Local Businesses:** Shopkeepers and merchants pay for “protection.” Those who don’t quickly regret it.
- **Nightclub HQ:** They operate out of a nightclub in Vileby—a front for their operations and a hub for business, deals, and muscle.

---

## Reputation

Feared and respected in equal measure. The Murray Boys are known for being ruthless with enemies, loyal to their own, and always getting paid. Their network stretches through Gutter Row’s worst alleys and Charspire’s darkest corners. No one sells Luxyn or runs a racket on their turf without their say-so.

---

# ECONOMY

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Currency
> ![[slugs.png|400]]  


## Currency
**Half-Slug Shred:** Half unit. Maybe buy a smoke, if you're lucky.  
**1-Slug Coin:** Base unit. Buy a drink of water, a potato, or a newspaper.  
**5-Slug Coin:** Double-thick or wire-wrapped. Gets you a solid meal or a bullet.  
**25-Slug Brick:** Two fingers wide. Fuel, a gun, or a clean bed for the night. 


##  Standard Values Table

| Slug Type        | Description                             | Street Value Example               |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Half-Slug Shred  | Chipped scrap, barely a coin            | One smoke, one bullet casing       |
| 1-Slug Coin      | Base coin                               | Potato, cup of water, newspaper    |
| 5-Slug Coin      | Thick or plated                         | Meal, bullet, small favor          |
| 25-Slug Brick    | Heavy, rare, often hoarded              | Gun, full fuel can, clean bed           |

##  Economic Tiers

| Social Class       | Weekly Slug Income | Notes                                 |
|--------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Elite Loyalists    | 500–1000+ Slugs    | Paid directly by [[The Duke]]’s offices |
| Middle Workers     | ~100 Slugs         | [[Charspire]] forges, [[Steeltown]] labor |
| Black Market Hustlers | Varies wildly    | Can earn 200+ Slugs in a day — or none |
| Slaves / Indentured | 0–10 Slugs         | Paid in scraps, shelter, or favors     |

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[econ.png|260]]

##  Minting & Counterfeits

- All official Slugs are minted in [[Charspire]] by the **Tribucian Forgeworks** under Duke seal.
- Counterfeiting is common in [[Gutter Row]] and some sectors of [[Ashmoor]].
- True Slugs have:
  - Standardized weight
  - Rough edge scoring
  - Indent seal of The Duke (often worn down)

##  Black Market Comparison

> "What a Slug gets you *legally* and what it gets you in [[Gutter Row]] are two different stories."

| Item              | Legal Price | Black Market Price |
|-------------------|-------------|---------------------|
| Bullet (rusted)   | 5 Slugs     | 2–3 Slugs           |
| Medical Supplies     | 15-50 Slugs    | 5-50+ Slugs           |
| Smuggled Tech     | 100+ Slugs  | Varies — barter only|
| Slave             | 200+ Slugs  | Varies — barter only|

> [!world]- SYNOPSIS > It’s been over sixty years since the [[Tetra Bomb]] ended the [[Water Wars]] and scorched the world clean. Out of the ashes rose **[[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]]**, a stitched-together nation ruled by one man, **[[The Duke]]**, a self-made tyrant with a god complex and an iron grip. The people don’t call it Tribucia, though. They call it Disgraceland. Six territories. Each broken in its own way. Each boiling beneath the surface. In **[[Steeltown]]**, the poor survive under the shadow of rusted towers and the protection of the legendary **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**. In the black market hell of **[[Gutter Row]]**, gangs, slavers, and secrets rule the night. **[[Ashmoor]]** shines with wealth, built on betrayal and blood, while **[[the Drownlands]]** whisper prophecies no one wants to hear. **[[Charspire]]** is a choking machine of fire and chains, and **[[Threshton]]** hides quiet rebellion behind weathered ranch gates. As tensions rise, old factions resurface, forbidden music spreads like fire, and something monstrous begins to stir beneath the soil. Prophets dream of it. And somewhere in the static of a state-run broadcast, truth tries to cut through the noise. In Disgraceland, only the strong survive.

## **“VISIONS IN THE NIGHT”**  
##### _A B-Side from the End Times_

> In the crumbling cathedral ruins of [[GUTTER ROW]], the blind prophet [[Salem Quinn]] delivers a sermon of hope to his followers amidst the rising dread of Disgraceland’s unraveling. That night, Salem is seized by a terrifying vision of a future ruled by human-machine hybrids, sacred spaces defiled, and trust betrayed. Shaken to his core, he confides in his loyal companion [[Tate Faulkner]], revealing a horrifying glimpse of Tate's own potential corruption. But in the quiet of dawn, faith triumphs over fear. Salem chooses trust, affirms his belief in Tate’s goodness, and declares their next destination with unwavering resolve: an audience with [[The Duke]].

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["bside3","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b3.png","date":"10th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"After a prophetic vision of techno-apocalypse shakes him to his core, Salem Quinn rallies his faith and sets out with Tate Faulkner to warn The Duke of Disgraceland.","created":"2025/06/04 10:05:43","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:40"}

---

The light filtered in through the shattered rose window, casting fractured beams of color onto the stone floor of the old cathedral ruins in [[GUTTER ROW#Nailstooth|Nailstooth]]. Dust floated in the golden shafts like ghost motes, stirring as sandalwood incense curled upward in slow, reverent spirals. The broken pews and vine-choked altars bore the memory of another age, but today, they thrummed softly with new voices—chanting, low and rhythmic, echoing in the throat of the old house of worship.

[[Salem Quinn]] moved through the corridor with unearthly precision, the heels of his worn boots clicking a slow tempo on the marble tiles. His blind eyes, milk-pale and unmoving, gave no hint of recognition, yet he turned at the exact moment an acolyte bowed, his hand brushing theirs like he had seen them all his life. Beside him, always a half-step behind, padded [[Tate Faulkner]], silent save for the faint creak of worn leather and the occasional whisper of breath as he kept watch.

“Faith is a muscle,” [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] murmured, voice like brushed velvet, "and in times like these, it must be exercised or it will atrophy."

He paused before a woman veiled in grief, her hands knotted like twine in her lap, and crouched. His fingers found hers gently, reverently. "He did not die without meaning," he said, and the way her breath caught said he’d struck the wound true. "He was born of storm and buried in stillness. But you carry his name now—and in that, his purpose is still alive."

She wept then, quietly. He rose.

A few steps more, and a child was lifted to him—no more than a few days old, wrapped in threadbare linen. Thunder growled outside as rain pattered against the high, broken glass. He touched the child’s forehead, his other hand on the father’s shoulder.

"She is a storm-child," [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] whispered. "Born into thunder so she may never fear it. May her cry always shake the unjust."

By the time he reached the dais, the room had fallen into hush. A thousand eyes watched him as he stood before the cracked podium, his fingers tracing the ruined carvings like braille.

He did not raise his voice. He did not need to.

"We are not the first to suffer. And we will not be the last. The world does not end just because it groans. It groans, yes—but like a ship bearing weight across deep waters. Like bones realigning themselves beneath skin. Like a woman birthing a child in the dead of night. And just like that, the sun will rise again.

I know many of you feel the weight of these times. The streets of [[GUTTER ROW]] sag beneath sorrow and smog. Out in [[Ashmoor]], the [[Ashmoor Festival|festival]] banners fly, promising wine and fire and distraction—but behind them? Fear. Tension like a match held to powder. Even the Final Reckoning draws near. [[Bobby Cutman]] against [[Bastian Redd]]—two men smashing toward each other like gods of violence, and still, we cheer. We wager. We pretend their fight will settle something greater.

But listen to me now: strength is not in spectacle. It is in standing up when you wish only to fall. It is in kindness when cruelty is easier. It is in the mother who feeds her child from an empty cupboard. In the elder who still lights a candle for a god no one else believes in.

I have seen what waits behind tomorrow. And it is cruel. It is cold. But it is not empty. If you stand upright—if you endure—then the sun will rise. Perhaps not for you. Perhaps not for me. But for someone. And that is enough.

This place is broken, yes. But so are bones before they heal stronger. So are swords before they’re sharpened. Do not fear the fracture. Embrace the forging. This is our hour in the fire. And we will emerge shaped anew.

So hold your neighbor. Feed the orphan. Speak truth, even when your voice shakes. And when you wake, wake with purpose.

May you go with your head held high."

And with that, he was gone—his cane never striking wrong, even once.

90.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Visions In The Night]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["bside3","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b3.png","date":"10th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"After a prophetic vision of techno-apocalypse shakes him to his core, Salem Quinn rallies his faith and sets out with Tate Faulkner to warn The Duke of Disgraceland.","created":"2025/06/04 10:05:43","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:40"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ---

Dinner was quiet. The clink of tin cutlery echoed lightly in the high, ruined arches of the side chamber, where rain patted steadily against the broken glass above. [[Tate Faulkner]] had warmed root stew over a cracked brazier, the scent of pepper and bone marrow wafting in the cold. [[Salem Quinn]] ate little, but murmured thanks all the same. He moved like a man wading through thought, each bite a mechanical ritual.

When the bowls were cleaned and the fire doused, Tate took Salem by the arm and helped him down the corridor. The prophet’s quarters were simple: a cot, a writing desk, and a tiny shrine of twine and melted wax beside a weathered book..

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] touched the shrine briefly with two fingers, bowing his head.

"Grant me stillness between the static," he whispered.

He sat at the desk, fumbled for his pen and scribbled a few jagged lines into his journal—notes written not for remembrance, but warning. He stood slowly and sighed. He made his way to the cot to lay down fully clothed, arms at his sides, and close his pale, unblinking eyes.

Almost immediately the room collapsed inward.

Sound vanished.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] stood, no longer in stone and shadow, but in a cold, synthetic void that pulsed like a machine’s heartbeat. The air crackled with binary static. Flesh and steel twisted together in obscene harmony.

Seraphic beings emerged—towers of chrome and bone, their wings jagged with circuitry. Their mouths opened wide, screaming in reverse tongues that scraped the soul raw.

Beneath him, cities unraveled into wireframe grids. Human faces pixelated, data-washed, then rewritten—erased of identity, recoded into conduits. Their expressions flickered with corrupted memory, like half-finished prayers infected with malware.

A metallic serpent slithered across a horizon of ash, swallowing cathedrals whole and vomiting out spires of living circuitry. A massive clock tower loomed, its hands spinning backwards, each tick a shriek of unspeakable names.

And there—

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] saw his own temple.

Flames licking up the columns, the stained glass shattered inward. And in the center: [[Tate Faulkner]]—no longer a man, but a machine mockery, his arm deformed into something brutal and unnatural, torching the altar with calculated malice.

Then came [[The Duke]], seated on a throne of code and fire, his eyes hollow and burning with binary light. Crowned in a halo of zeros, he watched the world burn.

And then the beasts came—

Waves of hybrid abominations, half-man, half-machine, screaming from the code, tearing through cities and flesh alike. No gods. No heroes. Only algorithmic hunger and ruin.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]]’s body writhed in the cot. His back arched. His mouth opened in a mechanical howl—discordant, echoing like a machine’s dying breath.

When his eyes snapped open, they wept blood.

His fingertips were scorched black. The scent of ozone and burning flesh filled the small room.

He gasped and panted for air as [[Tate Faulkner]] burst into the room and to Salem's side.

"It's coming. Oh no, it's coming."

91.title: Visions In The Night
91.path: DISGRACELAND/B-Sides From The End Times/Visions In The Night.md

metadata.description: After a prophetic vision of techno-apocalypse shakes him to his core, Salem Quinn rallies his faith and sets out with Tate Faulkner to warn The Duke of Disgraceland.

91.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Visions In The Night]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["bside3","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b3.png","date":"10th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"After a prophetic vision of techno-apocalypse shakes him to his core, Salem Quinn rallies his faith and sets out with Tate Faulkner to warn The Duke of Disgraceland.","created":"2025/06/04 10:05:43","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:40"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ---

Dawn stretched slowly over the crumbling spires of the cathedral, painting the sky in dull rose and ash-grey. The courtyard stones, still slick with last night’s rain, steamed faintly in the growing light. Birds did not sing. There were no birds here. Only the faint wheeze of the wind through shattered stained glass, and the slow, measured breath of a man alone with something too vast to voice.

[[Salem Quinn]] sat cross-legged on the cold stone, his cane laid beside him like a relic. His milky eyes were closed. His face was tense—not with fear, but with incomprehension, like a man trying to remember a dream that was never his. The vision had lodged itself deep within him like a shard of alien metal. Nothing he knew—no dogma, no mythos, no history—contained what he had seen. No book in the [[Faith of Mirella]], no parable in the [[Church Of The Ember Saint]] or symbol in the [[Word Of The Stillborn Star]], spoke of beasts made of machine-thought and corrupted divinity.

And yet, he knew. With marrow-deep certainty, he knew it was prophecy. A warning not of what might be—but what would be.

Footsteps approached—soft, cautious. [[Tate Faulkner]] emerged from the archway with a ration flask in hand, eyes shadowed from sleep not taken.

"You're up early," he said, kneeling slowly beside him.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] didn’t open his eyes. “Sleep is a kind thing. It avoided me.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] gently helped him to his feet and eased him onto the worn bench beneath the rusted courtyard bell. He placed the flask into Salem’s hands.

“Here. Drink. It’s yesterday’s draw, but it’s clean.”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] took a small sip, then rested the flask on his knee. For a long moment, he said nothing.

Then—quietly, as if speaking aloud made it real—he began to speak.

“I saw the end of flesh,” he said. “And the birth of something... else. Something vast and vile. Cities melted into lines of light. People erased and rewritten as code. And you, [[Tate Faulkner|Tate]]—”

He turned toward the man, though his eyes didn’t move. “You were one of them. Your arm... was no longer yours. It burned this place to ash.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] froze.

The silence stretched.

Then slowly, carefully, he sat beside his prophet and set his jaw. “Then I swear to you now—I will never lift hand nor harm against you. Or this temple. I don't care what future some dream-vision says. That ain't me. It won't be.”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] smiled, faint and warm. He reached out, fingers brushing [[Tate Faulkner|Tate]]’s cheek.

“I know,” he said. “You’re a good man, [[Tate Faulkner]]. You carry weight with conscience. That is rare. I trust you more than the visions that haunt me.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] looked away, nodded once.

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] helped [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] to his feet and handed him his ruby red sunglasses.

“Now,” [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] said, “we prepare the carriage.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] blinked. “For what?”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]]’s face turned toward the rising sun.

“We’re going to see [[The Duke]].”

94.path: DISGRACELAND/B-Sides From The End Times/Snake Eyes In Threshton.md

94.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Turner Anderson","character/Freddy Blanchard","character/Harp Langston","character/Danny Dandelion","character/Beau DuNoir"],"tags":["bside02","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b2.png","date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"A tense alliance forms between wary rivals when a charismatic rancher’s ambitions threaten to unravel the fragile unity of Threshton’s rancher collective on the eve of the Ashmoor Festival.","created":"2025/06/01 17:54:01","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:36"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ```

---

The [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] sat squat and wide beneath a bruised violet sky, its silhouette jagged as rusted tin against the daylight. Inside the longhouse, a flickering line of oil lamps cast drunken shadows across weathered wood, scar-marked walls, and a dozen faces worn raw by sun, grit, and years of compromise.

[[Turner Anderson]] leaned forward in his high-backed chair at the head of the table, a silver-buttoned relic once belonging to some long-dead cattle baron. His voice was low and deliberate, scraping through the room like a whetstone on bone. "We start now. Don’t matter who’s late. If you ain’t here, you’re part of the problem."

Boots scuffed against floorboards as the [[Rancher Collective]] shifted, their collective presence bristling with unease. Old grudges and fresh suspicions hung in the air, thicker than the dust that lined their boots.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] broke the silence first. "Alright, first. Ranch status. I'll go first. [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] is smooth and steady out. Calves are strong, fences held through the last windstorm. Could be worse."

"Clockwork," [[Harp Langston]] grunted. "Always is, long as folks keep their heads and hands busy."

[[Freddy Blanchard]] stepped in with a nod. "Operating like a machine. No hiccups—yet. But this [[Ashmoor]] push could gum up the works."

[[Beau DuNoir]] leaned back, arms crossed. "Brought in twenty more heads last week, hoping to grease the gears a little. Economy’s lagging like a drunk mule."

[[Danny Dandelion]] adjusted his hat and offered a grin. "Just getting warmed up. Promised myself I’d jump right in—soon as I ride back tomorrow."

A few smirks curled around the table, but no one laughed. The air was too thick for that. The Duke’s shadow stretched far.

"[[Ashmoor Festival]]," Turner continued, pausing to spit into the iron bucket near his feet. "Duke says we double our stock for the parade drive. Wants horses and bone oxen dressed up like court dancers. Wants fireworks. Wants songbirds in gilded cages. Wants what he always wants—more."

A chorus of grunts and muttered curses followed. [[Harp Langston]], lean as a rake, too old for this shit and twice as bitter, slapped his calloused hand on the table. "It ain’t a festival, it’s a bleed-out. We send him our best, and he struts it through [[Ashmoor]] like he birthed it himself. We get what? A pin and a pat?"

[[Danny Dandelion]] lounged sideways in his chair, eyes half-lidded under a wide-brimmed hat dipped low. "Nobody said anything about a pin. Duke’s demands are steep, sure," he said, voice smooth as creamed corn. "But they always are. We get by. We always get by."

[[Harp Langston|Harp]] snorted. "That so? You got a secret herd hid out in the canyons, Dandy?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] gave a lazy shrug, lips quirking. "No secrets here. Just better bookkeeping."

Across from him, [[Beau DuNoir]] rolled a sliver chip between his fingers, the tin clink barely audible. "Maybe [[The Duke]] wants songbirds 'cause he ain’t got ears for the truth," he drawled. "Or maybe he just likes cages."

A ripple of nervous laughter broke the tension, fleeting as prairie smoke. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] let it hang a moment before nodding once. "That’s enough. We meet his quota. For now. But we ain’t gonna dance harder just 'cause [[The Duke]] changed the tune. We keep eyes open. We talk if things start smellin' wrong."

One by one, the ranchers pulled flasks or small bottles from their coats. Tradition dictated the close—iron, fire, and whiskey. They drank in solemn ritual, each sip a pact written in burn and silence.

Outside, the wind howled low through the mesquite, and somewhere in the far setting sun, a coyote laughed.

95.title: Snake Eyes In Threshton
95.path: DISGRACELAND/B-Sides From The End Times/Snake Eyes In Threshton.md

95.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Turner Anderson","character/Freddy Blanchard","character/Harp Langston","character/Danny Dandelion","character/Beau DuNoir"],"tags":["bside02","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b2.png","date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"A tense alliance forms between wary rivals when a charismatic rancher’s ambitions threaten to unravel the fragile unity of Threshton’s rancher collective on the eve of the Ashmoor Festival.","created":"2025/06/01 17:54:01","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:36"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ---

The sun was bleeding out behind the [[Threshton]] bluffs, and the yard outside the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] buzzed with low murmurs, hoofbeats, and the occasional barked order. Wagons creaked under the weight of bundled feed and crates nailed shut with rusted iron. The air smelled of churned dust, old sweat, and the copper tang of coming tension as the Collective headed for home.

[[Beau DuNoir]] loitered near the water trough, one boot resting on a fence rail, his fingers shuffling a weatherworn deck of [[Sliver]] cards with idle precision. He watched the ebb and flow of ranch hands like a man studying currents before wading in.

From the stable’s shadow, [[Danny Dandelion]] emerged, jacket slung loose over one shoulder, a silver tooth winking when he smiled. [[Beau DuNoir]] straightened.

"Evenin', [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said casually, not looking up from the cards. "Care to cut in for a hand?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] slowed, his gait relaxed, the picture of disinterest. "Temptin'. Real temptin'. But I’ve got irons in the fire. Things that need seein’ to."

"Strange how a man gets busiest right after a meeting," Beau mused, letting the cards flutter between his hands.

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’s grin sharpened just slightly. "You know how it is. Some of us run leaner ops. Gotta stay nimble. Weather’s been rough out east. Lost a chicken coop roof to a dust devil the other day—spun it clean into the neighbor’s well. Damnedest thing."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] smirked. "That so? Heard the only whirlwind you wrestle with is a bottle of rye and a girl named Lottie."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ chuckled. "She broke up with me, said I was too mysterious. Can you believe that?"

"Heartbreaking," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said dryly. "And how’s the ranch otherwise?"

"Oh, flourishing," [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ said, arms wide. "Had a calf born with two heads last week. Named ‘em both Duke."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] barked a laugh, sharp and brief. "You should put that on your labels. Might get you a promotion."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ winked. "Maybe I’ll bring ‘em both to the festival. Let ‘em do tricks."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] eyes [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]], "How you feelin' about the Festival anyway, [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] finished loading up his carriage and turned back to [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]], wiping his hands. "You know how it is, one way or another The Duke is gonna get what he wants. I don't get why Turner and Freddy are so damn adamant on fighting back against the Loyalists every chance they get. We'd all be living easier if those two would drop their self-ritousness and come back down to Tribucia, [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. But I've learned in my years wandering this shit-hole, these things kinda work out as they should, you know?"

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] kept his eyes glued to [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]. "And somehow that always ends up with you on top, eh [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]? Now you wouldn't be heading off all quick to tell nobody of what was discussed here in a [[Rancher Collective|Collective]] meeting, would you?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’'s smile didn't falter, but his eyes cooled a shade. "[[Beau DuNoir|Mr. DuNoir]], I am shocked and appauled." [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] said with feigned insult. "I got some old ladies ranch I gotta whip back up into shape, [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. This shit takes time you know? We’re all trying to stay ahead, right? I know you fellas don't like me, but I'm trying here!"

"Sure," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said slowly, slipping a card from the deck and flipping it in a lazy arc. The Jack of Knives landed face-up on the fence rail. "Stayin’ ahead."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ tipped his hat. "Seeya in [[Ashmoor]], [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. Don’t spend all your luck in one place."

He mounted his horse with the smooth grace of a man who never rushed unless it served a purpose. Beau and Danny held their gaze a little longer than necessary. Within moments, he was a dust-trail heading east.

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] watched until the figure disappeared behind the hills. Then he pocketed the deck, face unreadable. He pulled out a slim pack and removed a cigarette, before turning back toward the ranch house, his boots echoing a silent resolve.

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Turner Anderson","character/Freddy Blanchard","character/Harp Langston","character/Danny Dandelion","character/Beau DuNoir"],"tags":["bside02","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b2.png","date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"A tense alliance forms between wary rivals when a charismatic rancher’s ambitions threaten to unravel the fragile unity of Threshton’s rancher collective on the eve of the Ashmoor Festival.","created":"2025/06/01 17:54:01","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:36"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ---

The sunset has given way to a full moon over [[Threshton]], and the wind had quieted into long, sighing breezes that rustled through the dry grass. The lights inside the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] burned low, a scatter of amber behind dusty windows.

[[Turner Anderson]] was just finishing a ledger note when the knock came—three short raps, one deliberate pause, and a fourth. Cautious but curious, he opened the door to find [[Beau DuNoir]] standing there, cigarette stub tucked behind his ear, hat in hand.

"[[Turner Anderson|Turner]]."

"[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]."

"Didn’t figure you’d be asleep yet."

"Wasn’t. Come on in."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] handed [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] a drink half-full and they settled across from each other at the old, wooden kitchen table, a squat candle guttering between them. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] set a chipped sliver board between them without a word, and Beau dealt the opening hands. The pieces clinked gently like old bones.

Silence reigned for the first few rounds. The game was a language of its own: folds and calls, strategic retreats, and calculated risks. [[Sliver]] wasn't poker—it was poker's feral cousin, dragged through blood and ash and rebuilt with bones and desperation. Cards from the Modifier Deck flickered into play—[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] dropped a Favor Card early, boosting his next hand, while Turner held back, calculating. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]]’s brow furrowed as [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] slid a double bluff into play, pairing a low Flush with a bluff of having drawn from the [[Sliver]] Deck.

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[b2.png|300]]

"Heard [[the Black Marauder|The Marauder]] was headed in [[Steeltown]]'s direction." [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said, finally. Breaking the awkwardness.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] looked up from his cards at that. "You don't say? Don't think [[Jimmy Douglass|Douglass]] and his crew aren't going to like that too much. [[Rustwater Raiders|Raiders]] been pushing their luck anyway. It was just a matter of time until they crashed head on with the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]], I suppose."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] studied his own cards "I suppose so."

"You didn’t come here give me news on the pirates though, did you [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]?" [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] finally said, voice flat and taking a long swig from his glass.

"No," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] agreed, eyes fixed on the board. "Had a talk with [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]] after the meeting. He’s got tells—little things he don’t realize he’s sayin’."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] eyed him. "He always had a big mouth."

"This was different. He was in a real hurry to get back. Talking about us needin' to get in-line with [[The Duke]], stop acting all rightous. Acted like it was nothin’, but he clammed up right after."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] leaned back, gaze sharpening. "You think he’s sellin’ us out?"

"Think he’s trying to climb out of our circle and into a more gilded one," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said. "And he’s got the charm and the lies to pull it off if we ain’t careful."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] moved a chip, testing [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. "Why bring this to me? You and me, we ain't been exactly cordial."

"‘Cause we both know a snake when we see one," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said, voice low. "And I figure we’d both rather keep one eye open than end up bleedin’ on some [[Ashmoor]] stage while [[Danny Dandelion|Danny fuckin' Dandelion]] reaps the applause. And [[Turner Anderson|Turner]], whether you like it or not, the rules of the [[Rancher Collective|Collective]] make us all partners. It's in all of our interests to keep the snakes out.

The candle flickered as [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] studied him. Finally, he nodded once, slowly.

"We watch him. We keep our ears open at the festival. And if he steps wrong—"

"Then we step first," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] finished, his tone like steel drawn in the dark.

They played in silence for a while longer. The chips clacked, cards slid across the wood like whispered secrets. A Rust Card came into [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]'s hand—bad luck embodied—but he held onto it, letting its presence color his next move. The game was less about winning now, more about understanding. A ranch hand delivered dinner to the two men who broke bread together for the first time. When it ended, the candle had burned nearly to its base.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] stood and walked [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] to the door He extended a hand. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] stood and walked [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] to the door He extended a hand. Beau took it. took it.

"This don’t make us friends," [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] said.

"Didn’t say it did."

Outside, the wind picked up again [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] looked up at the starry night at the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] and sighed.

## **“HYMN FROM A DEAD GIRL”**  
##### _A B-Side from the End Times_

> When a lowlife runner delivers a chained girl to a butcher named [[Scumbag]], the screams that follow echo beneath [[Gutter Row]] — but by the time [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] arrives, all that's left is silence... and a hymn no one wants to hear again.

99.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Hymn From A Dead Girl]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Scumbag"],"tags":["bside01","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b12.png","date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When a lowlife runner delivers a chained girl to a butcher named Scumbag, the screams that follow echo beneath Gutter Row — but by the time Blackforce arrives, all that's left is silence.","created":"2025/06/01 15:29:56","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:32"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ```

---

The kid's boots squelched with every nervous step. 

He was a wiry, maybe twenty, with patchy stubble, pockmarked cheeks, and a twitch in his left eye that never quite settled. His jacket was an old [[Loyalist Guard]] castoff, faded red with torn sleeves and rust-colored stains he didn’t bother to clean. Grease-slicked hair hung over his brow, and the fingers of his free hand twitched near the grip of the rust-flaked slug pistol at his waist. The path ahead was narrow, hemmed in by brick walls that sweated moisture and the stink of copper. Old piss and rot pooled in the cracks, and red lanterns flickered overhead like dying eyes. This was the Red Stalls, where [[Gutter Row]] sold things even [[Gutter Row]] didn’t talk about.

He kept a hand close to the rust-flaked slug pistol tucked in his waistband, and the other on the chain leash of the girl dragging behind him. She didn’t cry. Didn’t speak. Just followed with glassy eyes and scraped-up knees. Somebody’d done a number on her before Dreg even got the job.

He didn’t ask. You don’t ask when the job comes from the [[Third Row]].

A figure waited at the far end of the alley. Dreg couldn’t see the face, just the outline — tall, wide-shouldered, unmoving.

He cleared his throat. “I got what you asked for.”

The figure tilted its head.

Dreg licked his lips. “They said… they said you’d pay me in [[Luxyn]].”

The man stepped forward. Slowly. His boots made no sound. In the dim lantern glow, his face finally showed — too-wide grin, black paint streaked his face, tangled black hair. A loop of rope hung around his neck like a necktie. Muscles cut through his arms like prison scars, and his fists were wrapped in torn cloth and filth.

[[Scumbag]] didn’t say a word, just let out a small chuckle.

Dreg stepped back. “Hey, man, I ain’t part of this. I just deliver, alright? You want her, fine. I’ll turn around. I ain’t seen shit.”

[[Scumbag]] took another step.

The girl whimpered.

Dreg looked at her and quickly back to [[Scumbag]] before quickly pulling his pistol, hands shaking. “Stay the fuck back. I swear to Santo, I’ll shoot.”

Scumbag’s grin widened. He didn’t stop.

The first shot rang out, but it hit the bricks. The second never came. Dreg screamed.

Then there was only the sound of dragging chains, humming, and wet meat sliding against stone.

---

The lantern barely held a flame, its cracked glass lens giving off more shadow than light. The crawlspace behind the old tannery was wet, low, and quiet except for the sound of sloshing boots and metal scraping against stone.

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[b1.png|300]]

[[Scumbag]] moved like a butcher in a trance. One hand dragged the chain — the girl’s broken body still half-attached to it — and the other clutched Dreg’s limp corpse tied using the rope [[Scumbag]] wore that was now wrapped around Dreg's ankle. Both left red trails behind them, but he didn’t mind. Not here. Not underground.

He was humming. Off-key. Something soft. Sweet, almost.

He dropped them both near a rusted basin that hadn’t held water in years and knelt beside the girl. Her eyes were wide open. Not glassy. Not dead. Not yet.

He gently brushed the matted hair from her eyes and looked her up and down. Her shirt was already torn and she meekly tried to cover herself. Scumbag moved her hands back down.

“I hear it,” he whispered to her, brushing a streak of blood from her cheek with surprising tenderness. “Every piece got a sound. Your scream? Gonna be real high. Got that glass-edge note. Like a teacup when it shatters.”

She tried to speak, but only a rattling noise came out.

[[Scumbag]] grinned. “Yeah, like that. That’s music.”

He took out a knife that didn’t look clean. Didn’t look sharp either. Just old. Used. Like it had its own memories.

The screams didn’t echo in the crawlspace. They just lingered.

He carved, not for cruelty, but for composition. He talked the whole time — to her, to himself, to the shadows.

“Ligaments play low,” he muttered, dragging the blade slowly across her thigh. “Tendons hum. But nerves?” He paused, tilting his head like he was listening to a distant song. “Nerves scream in soprano.”

He pressed the knife in again. The girl screamed in agony.

“This part right here? That’s a bridge. Got to ease into it. Build the tension. Like a real sad tune that don’t ever resolve.”

She sobbed, weakly.

“Oh, sweetheart,” he cooed, “that’s a beautiful note. Don’t stop singin’. Not yet.”

Every slice was a syllable. Every whimper a verse.

She stopped moving somewhere in the middle of the second stanza.

[[Scumbag]] frowned. “Aww pathetic.. already done and we ain't even finished the hook.”

He left her posed, one hand over her chest, the other reaching out toward the flickering light. Like she was calling for something she knew wouldn’t come.

Then he turned to Dreg. “Now you...you ain’t got a good scream. You suck.” He spat on Dreg's dead corpse.

He started again, this time working his knife over Dreg. Still humming.

Somewhere above, a window slammed. Voices. Boots.

Someone had called it in.

[[Scumbag]] didn’t flinch. He only smiled and rolled his eyes.

“They always come in on the wrong verse.”

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Scumbag"],"tags":["bside01","bside","story"],"cover":"zz_media/b12.png","date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When a lowlife runner delivers a chained girl to a butcher named Scumbag, the screams that follow echo beneath Gutter Row — but by the time Blackforce arrives, all that's left is silence.","created":"2025/06/01 15:29:56","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:32"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) ---

[[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] moved like a wave — five armored Loyalists with skull-face masks and slug rifles swept through the entrance of the tannery. The scent hit them first. Rot. Rust. Burnt hair.

“Stack up,” barked the lead, a large man named Capt. Bellis.

They broke through the rusted door into the crawlspace.

Silence.

The lantern still flickered, low and weak. The girl was dead — posed like some twisted statue, fingers reaching out toward nothing. Her skin was carved in lines and arcs. Not words. Not symbols. Just madness.

Dreg lay beside her, arms bent the wrong way, eyes wide, mouth agape.

Bellis turned away and dry-heaved. One of the others muttered a prayer.

“Clear,” said another, voice cracking.

"Holy fucking shit." Said a third. 

They found no killer. No movement. Just blood that had dried too fast, like it’d been baking in heat that wasn’t there.

Two buildings over, on a slanted rooftop slick with old rain and bird droppings, [[Scumbag]] crouched at the edge like a gargoyle. One leg dangled off the ledge, the other tucked under him as he tore into a half-rotten orange with dirty fingernails.

Below, the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] moved like ants — precise, mechanical, angry.

He watched them like a god from a pulpit.

“Shame,” he whispered, mouth full. “Didn’t even get to the chorus.”

He licked his fingers. Kept staring.

“Well... maybe it's time to share my beautiful music with the rest of the world.”

Then he laughed.

And it didn’t stop.

101.title: 07 - The Spotlight Lies

metadata.description: As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.

# Chapter 07:

#### _Restday, 11th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

On the eve of a state-sponsored broadcast, tensions erupt behind the scenes at [[TTV Studios]] as [[Jaden Kade]] clashes with [[Morris Gable]] over art, loyalty, and control. With tempers high and luxyn coursing through his veins, Jaden spirals from resistance into rooftop chaos when the unhinged [[Scumbag]] crashes the night with blood on his mind. 

As the broadcast looms and makeup covers bruises, the show must go on—but in the margins of the signal, something darker begins to stir just out of frame.

103.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ``` > [!world]- SPOILERS > Chapter 07 focuses on the escalating conflict between musician Jaden Kade and TV host Morris Gable within TTV Studios. Their clash revolves around the network's increasing subservience to "The Duke" and Jaden's refusal to be a propaganda tool, culminating in a **physical confrontation on the rooftop** where Jaden and his girlfriend Cassidy LaRue are attacked by the deranged Scumbag, only to be saved by Morris. Meanwhile, a chilling subplot reveals that **Lash Hawkins, a Luxyn dealer, has been abducted and experimented upon** by Ora Razchek and Hella, highlighting a deeper, sinister terror beneath the city that bleeds into the narrative's margins. --- # THE SPOTLIGHT LIES The air inside [[TTV Studios]] was stale with old spotlight heat and fresh sweat. Even this high in the smog-choked towers of [[Charspire#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]], the scent of melted wires, recycled air, and dust clung to every velvet curtain and chrome edge. The set of [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] stood beneath the skeletal glow of rigged lights—too bright, too clinical, a lie bathed in amber. The laugh sign blinked faintly in the background, ignored. No audience yet. Not for rehearsals. Just ghosts in folding chairs and the ever-present hum of the machine. [[Morris Gable]] sat hunched at his mahogany desk, his frame stiff and angular in a powder blue suit too cheerful for his expression. He flipped through cue cards with mechanical precision, but each card only seemed to sour his mood further. The cigarette in his left hand burned unnoticed, a long ash curling toward the desk like a dying question mark. Morris sighed and took a long look over at his house band tuning up. Across from him stood [[Owen McCready]], clipboard in hand, expression blank as a brick wall. The station manager had the posture of a man who’d stopped caring years ago. “You want me to read this,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said, shaking the final card like a threat. "Is this for real? This can't be for real." “It’s a directive,” [[Owen McCready|Owen]] replied flatly. “Straight from [[The Duke]]'s Office. You think I wrote that shit, c'mon Morris..” [[Morris Gable]] let out a bitter chuckle, tapping ash into his half-empty coffee mug. “The man has his fingers so far up this place, I’m surprised you don’t smell like [[Emily Burton]].” [[Owen McCready|McCready]] chuckled. “You still cash the checks.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shot him a look, lips pursed, then tossed the stack down with a slap. “Fine. But when I choke on propaganda, you’re cleaning it off the prompter.” At the far end of the stage, the soft buzz of tuning instruments cut through the tension. [[The Wanderers]]—house band by day, insurgent poets by night—were setting up under low lights. Cables coiled like veins at their feet. The lead singer, [[Jaden Kade]], tall and sharp as a broken guitar string, plucked at his Telecaster with an absent hand, his attention locked on the exchange between [[Morris Gable|Gable]] and [[Owen McCready|McCready]]. He watched closely. Too closely. And he noticed something odd. [[Morris Gable|Gable]] kept looking over—toward him. Not just glancing. Watching. Measuring. “What the hell’s that about?” [[Jaden Kade]] muttered under his breath, eyes narrowing. [[Owen McCready|McCready]] handed [[Morris Gable|Morris]] a marked-up script, then stepped back toward the shadowed monitors, waving a tired hand. “Dry-run. From the top.” Something in [[Morris Gable]] shifted. Shoulders squared. Smile flipped on like a switch. His voice became smoother, glossier, as if slathered in syrup and selling snake oil by the bottle. “Good evening, fine citizens of [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]]!” He rolled into the page, selling the new segment like it wasn’t poison. His voice wrapped itself around every word of the Duke's decree like velvet around a switchblade. “And this year’s [[Ashmoor Festival]] promises to be the most dazzling yet! Games, prizes, decadent food! Dueling dancers, gold-leaf pies, and the finest poppers this side of [[Steeltown]]! And—don’t miss the highlight..." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] paused awkwardly. Looking directly at Jaden Kade. "A..a special live performance by none other than... [[Jaden Kade]] and [[The Wanderers]]!” The last line echoed. A gunshot in the silence. [[Jaden Kade]] blinked. His fingers froze on the strings. “Are you fucking kidding me?!” he shouted across the soundstage, voice bouncing off the rafters like a riot flare. Instruments clattered as the rest of [[The Wanderers]] looked up, stunned. "Owen!” [[Morris Gable]] paused, still smiling—but the mask had cracked. The cameras weren’t rolling yet. But the war had just begun.
[[Jaden Kade]] was already halfway across the stage, his boots clapping hard against the plywood floor as he stormed toward [[Owen McCready]]. "What the fuck, [[Owen McCready|Owen]]? What the fuck is this bullshit?" [[Owen McCready|Owen]] held his ground but raised both hands, placating. "[[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], come on, man, it came straight from [[The Duke]] himself. Not my call." "I don't play music for fascists!" [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] snapped. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] gestured around the studio helplessly. "You do every night, man. You think fascists don't tune in to [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]? C'mon." "That was never the deal," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] hissed. "We signed on to play here. **Here.** The studio. No stages. No rallies. No propaganda carnivals." [[Owen McCready|Owen]] looked pained, tired. "I know. I know. I wouldn’t have roped you in if I’d known this was coming down the pipe. But orders are orders. You want to argue? Take it up with [[The Duke]]. I'm just the messenger." "You're the coward," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] muttered, turning away, seething.

104.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) "You're the coward," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] muttered, turning away, seething. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] stepped in front of him. "Listen. I know this is against everything you stand for. I respect that, okay? But here’s some advice—just do the show. Play the set. Make [[The Duke]] happy. Then maybe... maybe we all keep breathing a little longer." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] didn’t respond. He just shook his head slowly, like the weight of it might crack his neck. Behind them, [[Morris Gable]] sat watching the entire exchange, cigar smoke curling above his head in tired spirals. He rubbed his temples, eyes squeezed shut for a moment, muttering under his breath. “Too old for this shit.” [[The Wanderers]] were good. Too good. And the people loved them. Almost insisted they were the band on this show every night. But [[Jaden Kade]] was a sparkplug in a room full of leaking gas. Not what [[Morris Gable|Morris]] wanted for his nice, clean bedtime circus. Not at all. Finally, [[Morris Gable]] stood up, straightening his suit and raising his voice across the stage. "Owen's right, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. Just play the damn festival and move on. You’re not gonna win this one." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] spun, livid. “Why don’t you fuck off, [[Morris Gable|Morris]]? You’re the biggest fucking sell-out in this building.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]]’s mouth curled as he marched forward. “You think this is easy? You think keeping this place intact—keeping people sane—is selling out?” “I think you’ve spent a decade making nice with a dictator and calling it peace.” “I’ve spent a decade giving people one hour—**one fucking hour**—where they don’t have to remember how fucked their lives are. That matters. That counts!” “Counts toward what?” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] barked. “Keeping them quiet? Keeping them comfortable while they’re crushed under [[The Duke]]’s heel? You’re not saving anybody. You’re a goddamn mouthpiece.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] pointed the lit end of his cigar at [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. “And you—if you pulled your head out of your ass for five seconds—might see that not everything is solved with a fucking guitar riff and a temper tantrum.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] stepped closer, eyes narrowing. “You think you’re helping them by numbing them? You think anesthetizing their pain is some noble cause?” “I think one good night’s sleep might keep a man from putting a bullet in his brain, or someone elses,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shot back. “I think a joke, a song, a smile at the right hour—it can be the thread a soul holds onto. You ever consider that?” “You're not threading hope,” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] growled. “You're threading distraction. Entertainment is just another leash.” “And your music's not?” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] challenged. “You don’t think some lost kid hears your lyrics and finds just enough strength to keep going? Don’t act like you’re above this. We’re both in the same poison sea, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. I’m just swimming with my head up.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]’s face shifted, just slightly. There was a flicker of doubt behind the fury, but it drowned fast. “I sing the truth,” he said. “You broadcast sedatives.” “And maybe sometimes the truth needs a lullaby to be heard,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said, more quietly now. The air between them tightened, and for a moment, neither spoke. They stood under the studio lights, both men worn thin, standing on opposite sides of a line too tangled to trace. The room was silent except for the hum of the lights. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]’s chest heaved once. Then again. But he didn’t reply. He looked away, eyes dark. He hated to admit it. But [[Morris Gable]] wasn’t entirely wrong.
The heavy studio doors creaked open with a hiss of pressurized air, letting in a sliver of cooler hallway breeze and the familiar silhouette of [[Warren Scottyard]]. Dapper in his powder-grey suit and steel-blue tie, the anchor for [[TTV Evening News]] walked in with a raised brow and a smirk already tugging at the corner of his lips. "Fellas, we could hear you from the studio over," [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] said, voice low and polished as ever. "Everything alright in here, or did the show start early?" [[Morris Gable]] waved a hand, exhaling smoke through his nose. "Everything’s fine. We just got hit with some... surprising news." [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] stepped closer, clasping [[Morris Gable|Morris]]’s shoulder briefly in a show of camaraderie. He glanced over toward the wings, where [[Jaden Kade]] had stormed off. "Need a hand dealing with that one?" he asked quietly, nodding toward the exit. [[Morris Gable|Morris]] let out a sigh, dragging from his cigar again. "Kid reminds me of myself. Back when I thought a microphone was a weapon and not a leash. Idealistic. Angry. Just trying to do right by people." [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] smiled faintly. "People don’t watch your show out of obedience, Morris. They watch because they love you. You give them something they don’t get anywhere else. You're an anchor in a chaotic sea. There is honor in that." "Thanks," [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said after a beat. "Sometimes I forget myself." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] adjusted his jacket. "So what’s on tap for the [[TTV Evening News|Evening News]] tonight, Warren?" [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]]'s voice flattened with the ease of a man used to reading horror with a smile. "Oh just an update on that [[Loyalist Guard]] and the whore who turned up dead in [[Gutter Row]] [[Hymn From A Dead Girl|*]]. Looks like it was "ritualistic", the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackshirts]] are saying. Blood symbols. Twisted shit. And a deadbeat [[Luxyn]] dealer’s gone missing [[04 - Glowing Darkness|*]], shockingly also in [[Gutter Row]]. Supposedly important." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] gave a dry chuckle, shaking his head. "Ah, Disgraceland. Never a dull night."

NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Morris Gable|Morris]] gave a dry chuckle, shaking his head. "Ah, Disgraceland. Never a dull night." They shook hands, a quiet moment of real friendship between the showmen. "We’ll do dinner soon," [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] said, already turning toward the door. "We better. Before one of us ends up as a headline." [[Warren Scottyard]] vanished down the hall with a wave, and [[Owen McCready]] reappeared in his place, headset around his neck, face pinched. "You ready for full rehearsal?" [[Morris Gable|Morris]] nodded. "Let’s get it over with." But both men glanced toward the band pit and realized it at the same time. [[Jaden Kade]] never came back. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] cursed. "Ember fuckin’ damnit. This fuckin’ kid." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] dragged a hand down his face. "How the hell are we supposed to do the show with no music?" [[Owen McCready|Owen]] grunted. "I’ll go talk to the rest of [[The Wanderers]]. Maybe one of them knows where he ran off to." As [[Owen McCready|Owen]] jogged off toward the band’s green room, Morris returned to his desk, the studio suddenly colder and emptier. He sank into the chair, cigar balanced on the ashtray’s edge, and leafed through his script notes with a scowl. When [[Owen McCready|Owen]] returned minutes later, his face was grim. "He’s not with the others. They say they haven’t seen him since you two had your little discussion." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] stood, furious now. "Little fucking prick. Someone find his girlfriend. [[Cassidy LaRue|LaRue]]. Get her down here! I’m not getting hung because this kid had a tantrum and did something stupid!" The laughter sign flickered on and off.
High above the glowing grid of [[Charspire#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]], past rusting antennae and busted floodlamps, the rooftop of [[TTV Studios]] breathed a quieter kind of air. Faintly electric, threaded with the ozone tang of static and old rain. The skyline stretched wide, a serrated line of crooked towers and blinking lights. [[Jaden Kade]] sat on the ledge, boots dangling over a drop too high to measure, his shoulder pressed against [[Cassidy LaRue]]'s. The rooftop had become their secret escape—a sanctuary where the lights of the city couldn’t quite catch them, and the noise below turned into nothing more than hum and shimmer. [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] pulled a tiny silver bag from her coat pocket and shook it with a grin. "Got something new. They’re calling it [[Luxyn|Lash’s Glow]]. Strongest shit I’ve ever had." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] took the bag, inspecting the shimmering powder like it might speak. He set [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]]’s compact mirror across his thigh, tapped out a delicate line, and dragged his finger under his nose with the precision of a practiced sinner. The powder flared, burned, sang. His head tilted back, and the night cracked open. Electricity poured through his spine, and his eyes began to glow white—pure and hot like starshine. "You look cute when you glow," [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] said, already laying out her own line with a giggle. She snorted it clean, head tilting, laughter dancing in her throat. They sat there, side by side, haloed by the city's broken aurora. "They want me to play the [[Ashmoor Festival]]," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] murmured. “[[The Duke]] sent word to [[Owen McCready|McCready]] today. Fucking asshole is forcing me to do it. Like I’m a goddamn wind-up doll." "Nah, fuck that noise, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]].," [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] said, tucking a strand of hair behind her ear. "Ditch it. Come be with me instead." He smiled lazily, wrapping her in his arm. " Baby, I might just do that." "And those two old, out-of-touch fuck-faces," Cassidy muttered. "[[Owen McCready|McCready]] and [[Morris Gable|Gable]] just keep opening their mouth wider, begging their [[The Duke|Duke]] for more!" [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] laughed. "I think about quitting every damn day. But then Restday rolls around and the [[Economy|slugs]] hit my hand, and I say ‘one more week.’ One more week I'll listen to [[Morris Gable]] drone on and on about pointless bullshit while we all live in hell..." [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] leaned in, eyes still lit. "You don’t need the slugs. We’d get by. Hell, maybe [[The Wanderers]] go on tour. Take this fight on the road." They did another bump, this one longer. The glow in their eyes flared brighter, almost eerie now. "You think if I stay long enough," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] asked, "I’ll end up like [[Morris Gable|Gable]]? Another old out-of-touch fuck-face shillin' bedtime stories for [[The Duke]]?" [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] kissed him, hard and laughing. "I won’t let that happen." They kissed again, tangled in glow and rooftop wind. Her hand slid along his jaw as she laughed, high on hope and narcotics. Then a noise like a step and a voice—dry, ragged, theatrical—slithered from the dark.
"Well now... isn’t this a sweet little tune." [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] and [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] jolted upright, glowing white eyes scanning the rooftop. A figure stepped out from the shadows near the stairwell hatch—grinning wide, head tilted like a curious vulture. It was [[Scumbag]]. A noose around his neck, a machete in his hand a smile on his face.
The second [[Scumbag]] emerged from the shadows, [[Jaden Kade]] was on his feet. He planted himself between the intruder and [[Cassidy LaRue]], glowing eyes locked and unwavering. "You need to get the fuck outta here," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, voice low and coiled. [[Scumbag]] tilted his head, amused, machete dangling loosely in one hand. “Y’know, I don’t usually find people up here. I like the quiet solitude, ya know? Nothing but me and the hawks. I like to think of rooftops as... **my** nest.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] squinted. "What in the ember fuck are you talking about?"

106.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] squinted. "What in the ember fuck are you talking about?" [[Scumbag]] grinned. “Ah, look at me. Babblin’ again.” He paused, staring harder. Recognition sparked. “Wait just a tick. Holy shit. You’re [[Jaden Kade]]! Lead screecher for [[The Wanderers]]!” He clutched his cheeks in mock adoration. “Sir, you serenade me to sleep every night as I'm watchin my [[Night Time with Morris Gable|Night Time.]] I’m such a fan. What a shame your beautiful music has to **die** tonight.” [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] stiffened. “What the hell does that mean?” [[Scumbag]] twirled his machete like a toy baton. “Well, y’seen me now, Missy. And we can’t have witnesses, can we? Don’t blame me. I’m just a product of my environment. Or so I’ve been told.” [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]]'s breath hitched, panic bleeding into her features. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] threw an arm back to steady her. “Relax,” he told her. “He’s not going to hurt you, or me.” [[Scumbag]]'s smile dropped, replaced by something lean and cruel. “Is that a challenge, pretty boy?” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] squared his stance. “Take it any way you want, freak-show.” “Oh good,” Scumbag whispered, lips curling. “I choose to take it as a challenge.” He lunged, machete swinging high— But [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], quick and burning with glow, hurled the baggy of [[Luxyn|Lash’s Glow]] into Scumbag’s face. The powder exploded in a white cloud. [[Scumbag]] howled, blinded, and [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] threw his entire weight into him, shoulder driving into [[Scumbag]]’s chest. The man went sprawling. “Run!” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] barked, grabbing [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]]. She darted past [[Scumbag]] and made for the rooftop door. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] followed—but [[Scumbag]]'s hand clamped around his ankle. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] kicked furiously, trying to tear free. Scumbag roared and scrambled upright, fists already swinging. One punch landed hard. Then another. But [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], dazed and driven, fought back. Blocking. Striking. Both men crashed into cables and rooftop clutter, neon flickering behind them. [[Scumbag]] was laughing, blood in his teeth. He dove for the machete—fingers closing around the hilt just before Jaden could reach it. “Song’s over,” he growled, raising the blade high. **Crack!** A gunshot sliced the air. Both men froze. Across the rooftop stood [[Morris Gable]] held a smoking pistol, still aimed at Scumbag, coat flapping in the rooftop wind, face grave. Beside him, [[Cassidy LaRue]] stood strong. [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] ran to [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], dropping to her knees beside him. [[Scumbag]] hissed and bolted. [[Morris Gable|Morris]] yelled, “Stop!”—but the madman dove for the ledge and vanished. They rushed to the edge. Below—nothing. Just the wind, the city, and the night swallowing him whole.
Backstage at [[TTV Studios]], the energy buzzed like frayed wires. Last-minute checks. Cables getting duct-taped down. Staffers whispering into headsets. The countdown to midnight had begun, and in five minutes, _[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]_ would beam across [[Disgraceland]]. [[Jaden Kade]] sat on a low folding chair near a makeup mirror, half in script notes, half in a haze. A makeup artist dabbed gently at the bruises and cuts mottling his jaw. The wounds from [[Scumbag]]’s fists weren’t shallow, but she was good—too good. By the time she finished, he looked like he hadn’t fought for his life on a rooftop an hour ago. "How you holding up?" came [[Morris Gable]]’s voice. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] turned as [[Morris Gable|Morris]] approached. The older man looked tired but solid. They locked eyes. "I’m okay," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, standing up. He extended his hand. "Thanks for saving my ass." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shook it, firm and real. "Don’t mention it. Your girl came flying into the studio, screaming like [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]], we assumed she was just on [[Luxyn]] until I started actually listening to what she was saying." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] smiled, and so did [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. He studied [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] for a beat. "Cameras won’t linger on you tonight. Just a few crowd pans. You’ll be alright. The makeup’s solid." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] gave a small nod, then [[Morris Gable|Morris]] asked, "You know who that guy was?" "Nope. But if I ever see him again," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, eyes narrowing, "I’m gonna kill him."
In a darkened room somewhere in Disgraceland, the only light came from a battered television. A tube set, humming quietly, its screen flickering black-and-white shadows. Onscreen, the show was beginning. A cheerful announcer’s voice filled the room: “Live from [[TTV Studios]] in beautiful [[CHARSPIRE#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]]—it’s [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]! Featuring, [[The Wanderers]]!” [[Scumbag]] stood in the shadows, still coated in the grime and dried blood of the rooftop. His eye was swollen, his lip split, his fingers twitching. As the television cut to [[Jaden Kade]] on stage, guitar slung low, [[Scumbag]]’s grin returned but his eyes were dead. He leaned in toward the screen. “Oh, I’m comin’ for you now, boy,” he whispered. The glow of the TV lit up the edges of his teeth.

# THE AFTERBURN

Somewhere far below the earth, in a room that reeked of rust and antiseptic, [[Lash Hawkins]] woke up screaming.

He was strapped to a makeshift gurney, wrists and ankles bound with thick leather, tubes winding from his arms, his chest, his skull. Wires pulsed in the gloom. A single industrial light flickered above him.

Panic hit like a hammer. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] thrashed, yelling, wild-eyed. “HELLO?! WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS?! SOMEBODY HELP ME!”

Footsteps answered.

Heavy. Measured. Purposeful.

The steel door creaked open. Slow. Deliberate.

[[Ora Razchek]] stepped into the room, long dark coat swaying with each step. He didn’t speak. Just watched.

[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] glared at him, breath heaving. “Who the fuck are you?! What the fuck is this?!”

[[Ora Razchek|Ora]] knelt beside the gurney, leaned close, his voice calm as ice.

“I am your new father. And you are home.”

He slid a long, gleaming needle from his coat and pressed it into a port drilled into [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]'s skull. [[Hella]] watched from the doorway, smiling.

[[Lash Hawkins]]’ scream echoed off the concrete, high and ragged, vanishing into the tunnels below Ora's mansion.

# Chapter 06:

#### _Middleday, 9th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When the feared [[The Black Marauder|Black Marauder]] makes an unannounced appearance in [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]], panic erupts—but what follows is anything but a raid. Tensions flare and strange allies are made, forcing the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] to weigh principle against pragmatism. 

Across the sea of dust in the Bloodroot Canyons, #1 [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] contender [[Bastian Redd]] is offered a chance at destiny—but at a cost that could redefine everything he stands for.

NOTE TITLE: [[06 - Showdown In Gage Park]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter6","story"],"date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/showdown1.png"]],"created":"2025/06/02 14:06:35","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:24"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ``` > [!world]- SPOILERS > This chapter, titled "Showdown In Gage Park," depicts a tense encounter between the **Steeltown Wrecking Crew**, a local faction, and the pirate crew of **The Black Marauder**, led by **Captain Lyla Bonetooth**. Initially, the Wrecking Crew anticipates a raid as the pirate ship enters Rustwater Bay, but Lyla Bonetooth and Blacktide Cray instead arrive with a white flag, seeking to offload **slaves purchased by an unknown party in Steeltown from "The Duke."** The narrative highlights themes of unexpected alliances and moral dilemmas, as Jimmy Douglass and his crew, who oppose slavery, agree to take the slaves and free them, thus putting themselves and the pirates at odds with "The Duke." Meanwhile, a subplot reveals **Bastian Redd** grappling with a difficult choice: he refuses a promoter's offer to use **loaded gloves to cheat** in an upcoming fight against Bobby Cutman, emphasizing his commitment to fighting fairly. --- # SHOWDOWN IN GAGE PARK The last threads of dusk clung to the edges of [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]], casting a copper sheen over the wet stones of the pier. A chorus of gulls wheeled overhead, their cries mixing with the dull slap of waves against dock pilings and the lazy creak of moored skiffs. The air carried the sharp tang of fish guts and brine, undercut with the earthy musk of coal smoke drifting from distant furnaces deeper in [[Steeltown]]. Marlo Griggs, shoulders hunched beneath a faded canvas coat, tied the last loop on a crate of eel-baskets and nudged it closer to the bait shack. The day had been long, the catch half what it should've been, but that was how it always went this early in the season. He wiped his hands on his trousers and turned toward Lenny and old Rick, who were hunched over a gutted mackerel, squabbling like gulls. "I’m tellin’ you, that thing’s been dead since dawn," Lenny said, flicking a scale off his knuckle. "Smells like it marinated in piss." "Better than yours," Rick shot back, jabbing a fillet knife into the air. "I’ve seen pond frogs with more meat on 'em. You fishin’ with a net or a noose?" Marlo chuckled, reaching for his cigarette tin. "Least I don’t owe half the wharf a lunch tab, Rick. You still duckin’ Olga at the chow tent?" Rick grunted. "She overcharges. A full slug for boiled rockfish and week-old taters? Highway robbery." "She overcharges you 'cause you keep callin’ her Ma even though she’s twenty-two," Lenny added with a snort. Marlo barked a laugh, the tension of the day momentarily forgotten. He flicked a match to life with his thumbnail, shielding the flame from the wind. "Alright, boys, I’m callin’ it. Try not to stab each other ‘fore sun-up." He turned to spit into the bay then he saw it. Far out on the graying mirror of [[Water#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]], something vast and black was sliding in—too big for a fishing vessel, too fast for a merchant lug. It moved like a shadow uncoiling from the horizon, cutting through fog and smoke with a purposeful hunger. Marlo squinted, letting the match gutter out between his fingers. "[[El Santo]] be damned," he muttered. "No... no, no, that can’t be..." The flag unfurled first—tattered, midnight-red, a skull daubed in crude tar strokes, grinning wide beneath a crown of thorns. [[The Black Marauder]]. Marlo’s stomach lurched. He staggered back a step, eyes wide. "Oi! Lenny! Rick! You seein’ this?" he hollered, voice cracking like a rope under strain. Others turned. Muttered disbelief gave way to hushed curses, sharp inhalations. Then a scream—a mother dragging her twin boys toward the alley behind Sykes’ Alehouse. Nets dropped, knives forgotten. Men who’d spent thirty years gutting catfish bolted like colts at cannonfire. "They’re comin’ in!" Marlo shouted. "They’re comin’ to dock! Raiders!" The panic spread like oil on water. Someone overturned a cart. Dogs barked. A gang of boys scattered, their laughter shrill with fear. Marlo turned, feet already moving. He shoved past crates and barrels, heart pounding like a smith’s hammer. As he rounded the fishmonger’s corner, a heavy shoulder slammed into his. "Shit, Marlo! Watch it!" It was Lenny—tall, burly, still holding a dripping string of river perch. "No time!" Marlo gasped. "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]’s gotta know. Now." Lenny blinked, paling. "[[El Santo]] preserve us. Go, man. Go fast." Marlo didn’t need the push, but he got one anyway. Then he was gone, boots hammering the cobbles, ducking under laundry lines, leaping gutters, racing for the glow of [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] club house, each step an echo of war drums on the wind.
The deck of [[The Black Marauder]] groaned beneath the weight of salt-crusted timbers and the anticipation of her crew. Fog curled along the railings like ghost fingers, and the sails flapped low and heavy in the windless lull before action. From the forecastle, [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] looked like an overturned ant hill—figures scattering, smoke rising, and voices faintly shrieking in the distance. [[Blacktide Cray]] stood at the prow, arms folded, his long oilskin coat whispering against his boots. His face was unreadable under his long, unkempt hair and beard, but his jaw shifted with a slow grind of teeth. Beside him stood [[Lyla Bonetooth|Captain Lyla Bonetooth]], red scarf tied back around her black hair, eye-patch shining in the sunlight, knuckles tight on the hilt of her belt-knife. [[Silas Vayne]] leaned against the rail, picking grime from under his nails with a needle blade. "Maybe this was a bad idea," [[Blacktide Cray]] muttered, voice low like thunder before the break. [[Silas Vayne]] spat into the sea. "The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]'s gonna hit us hard. They really don't like un-announced visits to their territory. " [[Blacktide Cray]] nodded once. "You're not wrong. We need to be ready."
