NOTE TITLE: [[06 - Showdown In Gage Park]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter6","story"],"date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/showdown1.png"]],"created":"2025/06/02 14:06:35","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:24"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Blacktide Cray]] nodded once. "You're not wrong. We need to be ready." The door to the lower decks creaked open. [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] emerged, his face slick with sweat and sea grime, shirt clinging to his wiry frame. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] turned to him immediately. "How are they? The slaves?" [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] scratched his neck. "Holdin’ on, Cap’n. Most of ‘em, anyway. But the girl—the little one—she's runnin’ hot. Fever’s real bad." The words hit [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] like a lash. Her breath caught. She looked away, jaw tightening. "Damn it. Fucking [[The Duke|Duke]], asshole piece of shit mother fuck....." "Aye Lyla, aye," [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] said softly. "But we’re already knee-deep in it now, no sense in lettin' it all get away from ya." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] turned back, eyes flaring. "[[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]], Bring her anything she needs. I don’t care what. You find someone with herbs, boil rags, steal Ember Saint-blood if you have to. You hear me?" "Aye, [[Lyla Bonetooth|Cap’n]]. I'm on it. I'll get that lil' one up and goin' in no time." [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] disappeared below deck again, boots thudding dully on wood. Moments later, [[Zadie Adeyemi]] stepped onto the deck, arms folded tight across her chest, brows drawn low like stormclouds. "[[Lyla Bonetooth|Captain]]. What’s the call?" [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] didn't answer at first. Her eyes were locked on the shore, watching the movement of townsfolk scrambling like mice from a flood. "They’re afraid," she said finally. "There's no way to signal to them that we're not here to hurt them but it's probably best if less people are around for this." [[Zadie Adeyemi]] nodded and stepped closer. "And the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]? We wait for them to come to us, or do we draw the line?" [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] sighed, long and heavy, as if trying to expel the burden of command from her lungs. She looked to [[Blacktide Cray]]. "We go ashore," she said, turning back to the small desk. [[Blacktide Cray]] arched a brow. "You sure?" "We go ashore," she repeated. "You and me. Just us. We raise a white flag, speak to the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] face to face. Everybody else stays here, cannons ready, on alert. If you see us give the signal, start blasting." [[Silas Vayne]] barked a laugh, sharp and bitter. "You're mad. They'll gut you on sight." [[Zadie Adeyemi]] nodded. "It’s a suicide run. You know what they do to pirates who show up unarmed." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] looked to [[Blacktide Cray]]. "You trust me?" He didn’t hesitate. "Where you go, I go." "[[Jimmy Douglass]] isn't a stupid man. In fact, his problem might be he's too smart. He would know not to attack us. Especially if we ride in on a dingy, waving a white flag. At least, I hope..."  [[Silas Vayne|Silas]] crossed his arms and looked to [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] and [[Blacktide Cray]]. "It ain't [[Jimmy Douglass]] that concerns me. You seen the [[TTV Evening News|news]]? You read the [[Tribucia Tribute|Tribute]] this week? [[Abel May Jr.|Abel May]] went face to face with [[Bobby Cutman|Bobby fuckin' Cutman]] and lived to tell the tale. If that man decides we have a problem, then we have a problem. [[Blacktide Cray]] stood up, looking menacing. "And that's where I come in." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] gave a firm nod, the decision sealing like iron in her chest. "Then it’s settled. Ready the dingy." The crew dispersed with wary glances and hurried hands. Overhead, the gulls had gone silent.
The low flicker of a junky projector played against the smoke-stained wall of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] clubhouse. A [[Trashflicks|trashflick]] comedy blared tinnily through the room—overacted pratfalls, exaggerated fart noises, and cartoonish synth stabs doing their best to rouse laughter. [[Jimmy Douglass]] sat at the center of the worn-out couch, arms crossed and brow furrowed. "This might be the absolute worst flick I have ever seen," he muttered. Beside him, [[Mark Jeffrey]] was doubled over, howling with laughter. "What?! He pissed on the robot dog, man! You saw that?!" On [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]’s other side, [[Selena Matissao]] had her feet up, cradling a warm beer and smiling—not at the screen, but at [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]'s reactions. "You’re such a dumbass," she said softly, grinning. Behind them, [[Abel May Jr.]] and [[Rodney Blythe]] were locked in a dead-silent game of [[Sliver]], the cards spread like glass shards between them. Abel’s brow was beaded with sweat, one hand hovering mid-air, deciding. Then— BANG. BANG. BANG. Everyone froze. The pounding on the front door was frantic, urgent. [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]], all six-and-a-half feet of muscle and temper, stood slowly. "Someone better be dyin’ out there." He lumbered to the door and yanked it open. A man stood on the threshold, panting like he’d outrun a firestorm. It was Marlo Griggs, the fisherman, face blotched red and eyes wide. "Black... Black Marauder... Bay—" [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]] watched the man. "What?" Marlo gasped and held his ribs. [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]] raised a hand and rolled his eyes. "Breathe, dammit. You high on [[Luxyn]] or somethin’?" Behind him, [[Katie Kowalski]] appeared, resting a gentle hand on [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]]'s shoulder. Her lab coat half-buttoned, blonde hair tied back. Her voice was calm and even. "Hi, I’m [[Katie Kowalski|Doctor Kowalski]]. Just slow down, you're alright. What’s happening?" Marlo gulped, drew in a rattling breath. "[[The Black Marauder]]. It's in [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]]. Heading for [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] docks. Raiders. I saw it myself." [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]]’s eyes widened. "Oh shit." [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]] turned on his heel and strode back into the clubhouse. "[[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]! [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]!" he barked.

NOTE TITLE: [[06 - Showdown In Gage Park]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter6","story"],"date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/showdown1.png"]],"created":"2025/06/02 14:06:35","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:24"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]]’s eyes widened. "Oh shit." [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]] turned on his heel and strode back into the clubhouse. "[[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]! [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]!" he barked. [[Jimmy Douglass]] stood, rubbing his jaw, and [[Mark Jeffrey]] hit pause on the projector remote. [[Rodney Blythe|Rodney]] gestured with a thumb. "Fisherman says [[the Black Marauder]] just pulled into bay." The brothers, [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] and [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] locked eyes. [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] stood. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] already knew. "Bell." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] strode to the corner and yanked the thick rope hanging from the iron bell. Its brassy bellow echoed through the compound. Within moments, the rest of the Crew appeared: [[Joe Ameen]] wiping oil from his hands as he stepped in from the garages, [[Lincoln Jones]] blinking sleep from his eyes, the others filtering in, alert now, tense. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] stepped forward, arms folded across his chest. Mark stood at his right. "So it seems the Raiders are at the dock," [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] said. "[[The Black Marauder]] came into bay like they own the place. They know the rules. They know where they ain’t supposed to go. If they’re lookin’ for a war, we’ll give them one." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] raised a hand. "But we do this smart. No shots fired unless you hear it from me or [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]. Clear? Everybody just be cool until we figure out what is going on. [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]], don't get too close. If you see any of us go down, you know what to do." A chorus of nods and quiet affirmations. [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] cracked his neck. "Time to ride." Outside, engines growled to life. [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]], [[Abel May Jr.]], [[Selena Matissao]], [[Rodney Blythe]], [[Lincoln Jones]], [[Joe Ameen]], and [[Katie Kowalski]] swung onto bikes—machines painted in black and blood-orange, polished chrome flashing in the overhead lights. One by one, they rolled out of the garage and roared into the city, heading for the docks. [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] was about to get loud.
> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎ > ![[showdown1.png|400]] The roar of engines faded into a heavy silence as the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] rolled up to the crest above the [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] docks. Their black and gold bikes lined the overlook like sentinels, idling in unison, chrome catching the gray light. Below, the crowd of townsfolk began to part, murmurs rising as their guardians took their place. [[Mark Jeffrey]] lifted his visor and scanned the scene below. "Selena," he said, nodding toward the throng. "Deal with them. Get 'em clear." [[Selena Matissao]] swung off her bike, calm and commanding. She strode to the edge and cupped her hands around her mouth. "Everyone! For your safety, I need you to move back. Away from the docks. Go home or head toward the east ward! No one wants kids caught in any crossfire." Her voice was practiced, confident. People listened. They always did when [[Selena Matissao|Selena]] spoke like that. Back at the crest, [[Jimmy Douglass]] stood beside [[Lincoln Jones]], arms folded, eyes fixed on [[the Black Marauder]] still looming in the bay. "What the hell do they think they’re doin’?" [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]] muttered. "No message, no signal. Just roll in like this?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] exhaled through his nose. "Either they’re bold or desperate. Maybe both." [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]] squinted out toward the bay. "You think they’re here for a deal? Or just lookin’ to provoke us?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] shrugged, his jaw tight. "Like...it doesn’t feel like a raid. Not with the ship sittin’ that still. But I don’t like guessin’ when Raiders are involved." [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]] nodded, then leaned forward, eyes narrowing. "Wait... you see that? In the water. Just off the port side." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] leaned with him. "Dingy. Two bodies. Is that a white flag?" [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]] crossed his arms. "Well shit. Now what the fuck are we supposed to make of this?" "[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]!" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] called. [[Mark Jeffrey]] walked over, flicking away a cigarette. "They’re sendin’ a pair in. Look there. That’s a white flag." The three stood in a row, watching the little boat bob its way toward the shore. Wind tugged at the pale cloth fluttering atop a splintered oar mast. "Huh. I did not see that one coming...could be a setup," [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] muttered. "Trap, ambush, distraction—any of it," [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]] added. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] didn’t blink. "Either way, we don’t wait." He turned back to the bikes. "Crew, on me." The others gathered, circling him. [[Rodney Blythe]], [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen]], [[Abel May Jr.]], [[Selena Matissao]], and Lincoln. "Two comin’ in on a dingy, not sure who yet," [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] said. "They're flyin' a white flag. We don’t assume nothin’." [[Abel May Jr.]] shifted uneasily. "The fuck is that? Flags don’t mean shit to Raiders." Murmurs of agreement passed through the group. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] pointed down the slope. "[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]], [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]]—you’re with me. Let’s meet ‘em." As he walks by, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] slaps [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]]'s chest and grins at him. "You ready for your first war, big man?" [[Lincoln Jones|Lincoln]], the newest member of the Crew grins back. "Oh hell yeah." "Everybody get in positions around the crest. [[Rodney Blythe|Rod]], keep an eye on [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]]." As the three began descending, [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] spoke up. "Hey, I didn’t say nothin' yet—but [[Flint Garritt]] invited me to Final Reckoning. Personally. Wants me to come as his guest." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]’s head turned. "The hell you say?"

113.title: 06 - Showdown In Gage Park

metadata.description: Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.

113.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[06 - Showdown In Gage Park]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter6","story"],"date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/showdown1.png"]],"created":"2025/06/02 14:06:35","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:24"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]’s head turned. "The hell you say?" "Came to me after the thing with [[Bobby Cutman|Bobby]]," [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] said. "Offered me a contract. I haven’t signed it... [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] glances sideways at his partners, "...but I didn’t tear it up either." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] frowned. "Well shit. You serious about goin’?" [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] nodded slowly. "Thinkin’ about it." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] exhaled through his nose. "[[Abel May Jr.|Big Main]] is gonna be [[World Lucha Libre|World Champion]]! Holy shit!" "I don't want you going alone." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] said, more serious. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] nodded again, eyes distant. "Yeah. I know." They stopped at the edge of the beach. The dingy scraped into the shallows, oars tossed aside. [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and [[Blacktide Cray]] stepped out, boots crunching wet stone. They stood maybe a hundred yards away, still as statues. For a moment, nothing happened. Just two sides, staring across the open beach. Then [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] took a step and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] followed. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] looked up, raised a hand to the crew atop the ridge. "Well, let’s go meet our guests, then, shall we?" The three men started forward across the sand.
The beach stretched wide and bare between the two groups, damp sand crunching underfoot, the wind tugging at coats and loose strands of hair. On one side, [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]], and [[Abel May Jr.]] moved down from the crest. On the other, [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and [[Blacktide Cray]] strode forward with deliberate steps, the surf whispering around their boots. As they drew closer, tension hung like fog. Finally, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] stopped about twenty paces back, arms crossed and eyes narrowed, lit a cigarette. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] and [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] continued forward alone. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] came to a halt a few feet from the pirate captain. "You must be [[Lyla Bonetooth]]." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] lifted her chin. "That’s **Captain** [[Lyla Bonetooth]]. It’s a pleasure to finally meet the legend [[Jimmy Douglass]]. Face to face." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] had not spoken a word, nor broken their hard, unwavering stares. "Your reputation precedes you, Captain." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] gave a half-smile. "I gotta say you got balls just pulling up here like that." He motions towards the Marauder out in the bay. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] returned the nod. "Yeah well, I bet on you being able to read the situation accordingly, and considering [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] and myself have made it to shore alive I'd say I made the right bet." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]’s smile faded slightly. "And what is it that made you pull up to our shores, Captain?" [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] glanced at [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]], then back to [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]. She studied him for a breath. "We have something. Some...cargo, on the Marauder. Something [[The Duke]] has us moving for him. Said he wanted it done quietly." "What is it you're running for [[The Duke]]?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] asked. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] took a moment then just blurted out, "Slaves." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] still hadn’t looked away from each other. Their silence was its own conversation. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]’s whole body tensed. The forced politeness left his voice. "Slaves? What are you talkin’ about?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] raised a brow as he noticed [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] still staring holes through each other. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]]’s voice was even, but there was a heaviness to it. "[[The Duke]] summoned us to [[The Silo]] a few days back. He paid us a lot of [[Economy|slugs]] to run some slaves. Told us to deliver them to [[Steeltown]], quietly." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] looked stunned. "Slavery’s outlawed here." "I know," [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said. "Believe me, I know." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] took a step closer. "Who? Who in [[Steeltown]] bought them?" [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] shook her head. "He didn’t tell me. Just said to be here on the 10th at midnight, someone would be here to collect them." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] hadn’t moved. Their eyes were locked like they were reading each other’s sins. "I don’t believe in slavery either," [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said firmly. "We came in like this, all grand and loud, because I wanted you to see it wasn’t a raid. It’s not a trap. We’re here to talk." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] studied her, quiet for a long moment, before taking a confused glance back at [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]]. Then: "So, what is it you want from me?" "I want you to take them." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] straightened. "Take the slaves from us. I can't just give them to whoever bought them. They're people. A little girl in there has a fever, if she doesn't get help soon she ain't gonna make it." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]’s jaw clenched. "If I take them, I’m gonna free them. You know that." "I do." "Whoever bought them ain't gonna get what they paid for. [[The Duke]]'s gonna know you didn't deliver. Giving me those people puts a target on your back." "I know that too." Still, [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] said nothing—eyes locked, breaths shallow. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] turned from [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] and called over his shoulder. "[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]! Come here." [[Mark Jeffrey]] strode forward, flicking his smoke into the sand. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] gestured between them. "[[Lyla Bonetooth]]—this is my brother, [[Mark Jeffrey]]." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] nodded with a warm grin. "It is an honor to meet you, [[Lyla Bonetooth]]."

114.title: 06 - Showdown In Gage Park

metadata.description: Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.

114.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[06 - Showdown In Gage Park]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter6","story"],"date":"9th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Pirates come face to face with Bikers as uneasy truces and dangerous choices test the loyalties of warriors on land, sea, and in the ring. The winds of change sweep through Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/showdown1.png"]],"created":"2025/06/02 14:06:35","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:24"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] nodded with a warm grin. "It is an honor to meet you, [[Lyla Bonetooth]]." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] corrected smoothly, "**Captain** [[Lyla Bonetooth]]. And likewise, [[Mark Jeffrey]]. Your fortification of [[Steeltown#Barton|Barton]] during the Loyalist crackdown is the stuff of legend." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] chuckled, raising both hands. "Apologies, Captain. And yeah, it was a good night." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] smiled faintly up at him. "Forgiven." For a moment, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] and [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] eyed each other. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]'s expression turned serious again. "[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]—the [[Rustwater Raiders|Raiders]] came in here with slaves." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]’s eyes sharpened instantly. "Well... That's an odd gift to bring to someone's home on your first visit, Cap. Slavery ain’t legal here. Not in [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] land." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] nodded. "She knows. Someone in [[Steeltown]] bought them from [[The Duke]]. We’re gonna take 'em. We're gonna free 'em. Then we're gonna find out who bought them." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] nodded. "They should've known better." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] still hadn’t blinked. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] nudged [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]. "Go get the rest of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Crew]]." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] looked between the two silent men. "What the hell is goin’ on with them?" [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] crossed his arms. "He’s starin’ at me." [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]]’s lip curled. "You’re starin’ at **me**!" [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stepped forward slightly. "If I was starin’, it’s ‘cause I’m tryin’ to figure out what grown ass man walks around with a fuckin' parrot on his shoulder." [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] grinned wide. "That so? I was just wonderin’ what kind of dumbass wears shades when the sun ain't out." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] pointed a thick finger. "These are prescription." "Yeah? Well maybe I should prescribe my boot in your ass." "You're going to prescribe a boot in my ass? Are you an idiot?" "Says the man who get's in the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] champs face." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]], [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], and [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] all stared at the two goliaths, dumbfounded. "This is what we’re doin’ now?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] muttered. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] folded her arms. "I swear to every Saint on the sea, if they start swinging, I’m lettin’ ‘em knock each other out." [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] chuckled. "Oh I got five slugs on the big guy with the long beard!" Finally he shook his head and turned back toward the crest. "Alright. I’ll get the others." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] turned to [[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]]. "Settle down." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] shot a look at [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]], who took a step back and unclenched his fists. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] watched [[Mark Jeffrey]] ascend the crest to inform his fellow members. She leaned toward [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]. "Your brother [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] is... amusing. Does he take anything seriously?" [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] rolled his eyes. "Oh if you only knew..."
From her coat, [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] pulled a thick patch of straw wrapped in string. She lit one end, sending a thick white smoke into the air. Moments later, another dingy began its slow crawl across the water. Onboard: a half-dozen people, thin and ragged, eyes hollow. "[[El Santo|El fuckin' Santo]]...." [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] whispered as he noticed the decrepit looking people on the dingy. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] rolled up as the boat neared shore. [[Jimmy Douglass]] stepped forward. "Crew—this is Captain [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and [[Blacktide Cray]]." [[Katie Kowalski]] stepped out first, nearly tripping over her own boots in her excitement. "You’re **the** [[Lyla Bonetooth]]? Oh my god. I’ve read about you in **every** [[Tribucia Tribute|Tribute]] report and article. The Dagger of the Delta? The [[Rachel Gold]] piece, The Queen of Salt? You’re a legend! An absolute legend!" [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] raised an eyebrow, amused. "I haven’t heard Queen of Salt in years." [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]] practically squealed. "I used to keep a picture of you I cut from the newspaper in my medbag. When I was stuck in the Underslums hospital, I told myself, ‘If [[Lyla Bonetooth]] can carve her way through the Iron Strait with nothing but a harpoon and spite, then I can survive a week of infected bite wounds and stolen antibiotics.’" Lyla smiled, visibly touched. "That might be the most colorful praise I’ve ever gotten. Thank you, [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]]." [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]]’s eyes widened again. "Wait, do **you** know who **I** am?" "Of course I do," [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said. "The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] is known in every corner of Disgraceland. And the doctor who stabilized twenty-two wounded during the Siege of the Foundry? Yeah, I know who you are." [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]] covered her face with her hands. "The is the coolest moment of my life." [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] gave her a wink. "I’m glad we finally met, [[Katie Kowalski|Doctor Kowalski]]." [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]] turned to [[Selena Matissao|Selena]], who was watching and smiling and mouthed silently, **She winked at me**! The dingy scraped against the beach. [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Selena Matissao]], and [[Lincoln Jones]] rushed forward. [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]] immediately crouched to examine a girl whose lips were cracked and skin blotched with fever. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] worked quickly, offering coats, water, food. Moving with purpose. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stepped beside [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] extending her hand. "It was nice finally meeting you, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]. Thank you for your help."

(cont'd) [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stepped beside [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] extending her hand. "It was nice finally meeting you, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]. Thank you for your help."

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] nodded. "You’re welcome. If you ever come into possession of more...human cargo... bring ‘em here and we’ll protect them. And you."

[[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] studied him for a moment, seeing nothing but sincerity. Finally she looked away and released her hand and nodded.

Then she moved to [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]].

"Thank you, [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]. For hearing us out. I heard you're a man of honor and I'm pleased to find out that is the case."

[[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] nodded. "Good luck out there, Captain."

They shook hands, firm and fast.

[[Lyla Bonetooth]] and [[Blacktide Cray]] stepped back into the dingy. As it was rowed away, they watched the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Crew]] ride off into the dusk.

[[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] muttered, "So. What’d you think of 'em?"

[[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] smirked faintly. "They were...not what I expected."

[[Blacktide Cray|Blacktide]] grunted. "I want to beat the fuck outta the big one."

[[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] just laughed.

# THE AFTERBURN

In the wind-carved hollows of the Bloodroot Canyons of [[Threshton]], the air smelled of red dust and pine smoke. The sun had begun its slow descent behind the fractured stone spires, casting long, jagged shadows across the camp. Tents stitched from hide and nylon stood in a loose circle, smoke rising from a central fire where a few of [[Bastian Redd]]’s kin prepared dried meat and strong tea.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stood shirtless beneath a bone-hung awning, his braided hair damp with sweat, muscles slick and coiled as he pounded into a weathered heavy bag that swung from a tree limb. Each hit echoed through the canyon like distant thunder. His knuckles were taped raw. His breath came in controlled bursts.

From the ridge above, a slow clap sounded.

[[Flint Garritt]] descended the slope with that same lopsided grin he wore on every promotion poster in [[Disgraceland]]. Impeccable boots crunched red gravel, and a leather bag swung at his side.

"You look ready, [[Bastian Redd|Redd]]."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] didn’t stop punching. "[[Flint Garritt]]. What are you doing on my land? I didn't think you made house calls."

"I don’t, usually." [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] said, stepping under the awning. "But this ain’t just any usual fight, is it? You're 0 and 2 against [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]], [[Bastian Redd|Redd]]. It's now or never."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] finally stopped, wiping his brow with the back of his arm. He gave [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] a long, measuring look. "So what’s this?"

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] pulled a chair close with his foot. "To be blunt, I’m sick of [[Bobby Cutman]] holdin’ that belt. He’s stale. The company needs fresh blood. A new direction. I want **you** to be the new face of the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]]."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]’s eyes narrowed, then drifted back to the bag. "Yeah, that’s the plan."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] smiled. "Of course it is, of course it is. And I have every confidence in you, [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]. Just...maybe I could offer a little help."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] threw a quick jab. "Don’t need help training."

"Not that kind of help."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] unzipped the leather bag and laid out two sleek, gleaming fight gloves. Heavy. Slightly too heavy. They thudded against the table like iron weights.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] walked over, picked one up. His brow furrowed at the heft.

"You want me to cheat?" he asked, voice low. "These gloves are loaded. I’d kill [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] wearin’ these."

"If the [[Church Of The Ember Saint|Ember Saint]] decides that then...," [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] shrugs. "It’s time the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] evolved. I’m just trying to help it along. You win, and the world’s yours. Fame, sponsors, the belt... Everything."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stared at the gloves.

The sun dipped lower, a wolf’s howl curling through the canyons.

He shook his head. "Nah."

He tossed the gloves at [[Flint Garritt|Flint]]’s feet. "I’m gonna beat him clean. Or I’m not gonna beat him at all."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] crouched, picked them up with a smirk. "Suit yourself. Hope you’ve got what it takes. Because there ain’t gonna be any rematches."

Without another word, [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] turned and strode out of camp, his silhouette shrinking against the bleeding sunset.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stood there alone, fists clenched, the wind tugging at the edge of the heavy bag.

# Chapter 05:

#### _Temperday, 8th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

In the fog-choked wilds of [[The Drownlands]], twin hunters [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] and [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] complete the sacred rite to become Unseen, pledging their lives to the goddess Mirella. With [[Riley Thorne]] guiding them, they embark on their quest to become Widows and find an unlikely first kill.

Meanwhile, far from the mire, [[Ava Victoria]] searches the chaos of [[Gutter Row]] for the vanished [[Lash Hawkins]], forcing an uneasy alliance with [[Nico Murray]] as shadows gather and secrets deepen.

119.title: 05 - Sight Unseen

metadata.description: As twins Raina and Risa embrace the deadly path of the Unseen in the misty Drownlands, Ava Victoria searches Gutter Row for the missing Lash Hawkins, forging a fragile alliance with Nico Murray as fate tightens its grip and darkness closes in from all sides.

119.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[05 - Sight Unseen]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Prophet Veerah","character/Raina & Risa","character/Riley Thorne","character/Len Vyne","character/General Colt"],"tags":["chapter","chapter05","story"],"date":"8th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As twins Raina and Risa embrace the deadly path of the Unseen in the misty Drownlands, Ava Victoria searches Gutter Row for the missing Lash Hawkins, forging a fragile alliance with Nico Murray as fate tightens its grip and darkness closes in from all sides.","cover":[["zz_media/05.png"]],"created":"2025/05/26 09:40:25","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:20"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ``` > [!world]- SPOILERS > This chapter primarily follows two intertwining plotlines: the **initiation of twin hunters Raina and Risa** into the mystical order of the Unseen, devoted to the goddess Mirella, and **Ava Victoria's desperate search for the missing Lash Hawkins** in the chaotic district of Gutter Row, forcing an uneasy alliance with Nico Murray. The most important ideas revolve around the **sisters' transformation into "Widows" by pledging allegiance and consuming a symbolic "body of the goddess,"** which culminates in a ritualistic requirement to kill a male target, and Prophet Veerah's **prophetic vision of a coming war against "creatures of metal and flesh,"** urging the Widows to act. The narrative highlights the harsh realities of their world, from brutal military training under General Colt, chosen by the twins as their first target, to the cutthroat environment of Gutter Row. --- # SIGHT UNSEEN The marsh whispered. Thick fog draped over twisted reeds and drowned cypress roots. Every step sank with a quiet suck into the muck, and somewhere beyond the gray haze, a fat boar grunted and rooted through the brush. Oblivious. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] crouched low, still as bone. A flick of her fingers. A tilt of her head. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] moved in tandem, ghostlike through the slush. No words. Just the silent code they had shared since birth—eyes, hands, breath. The boar shuffled forward, snorting at a patch of damp ferns. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] pulled the bow from her back in a single slow motion. Drew. Held. Let the arrow loose. The boar screamed and charged three feet before [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] exploded from the scrub. Her blade kissed the throat in one swift arc, spraying steam and blood into the cold air. The marsh went silent again. They knelt by the corpse, hands blood-wet, grinning. "[[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] will feast well," [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] said. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] nodded. "It's good meat. We honor her with this." The sisters worked in rhythm, stringing the boar with braided vine and slinging it between them on a rough pole. As they moved through the mist, their shapes blurred into the wild. At the edge of the bush, [[Riley Thorne]] waited. Cloak damp, one hand on the hilt of her curved blade, the other flipping a carved bone token over and over. "Well done. That was clean and silent, you were Unseen" Riley said, eyes flicking from the boar to the twins. "You're almost ready." [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] smirked. "Almost?" "You want the rite," Riley said, stepping aside to let them pass. "You need more than blood. You need fire." [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] grinned, teeth sharp in the gloom. "Then let's burn." The fog swallowed them whole as they made their way back to the compound.
They stepped from the wild into the compound’s tangled clearing, a wide sprawl of land nestled deep in the mire. Earthen huts rose from the muck like fungi, their walls packed with clay and root, thatched with swampgrass and reeds. Raised walkways of scavenged planks and knotted vines connected the homes, elevated just enough to stay dry above the constant wet. Smoke drifted up from clay chimneys, and voices carried through the mist—low songs, soft prayers, the sound of knives being sharpened. Lanterns swung from skeletal tree limbs, casting flickers across pools of stagnant water and mud-slick trails. Totems made of bone, wood, and twisted iron lined the perimeter, watching in silence. Animal skulls, carved with runes and hung with swamp lilies, marked thresholds. The air was thick with the scents of wet moss, rendered fat, and incense smoke. [[Len Vyne]] waited at the threshold, arms crossed, hood thrown back to show her dark cropped hair. "You're back just in time," she said. "Come. [[Prophet Veerah]] has seen something. She's gathered the sisters." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] exchanged a glance with the twins, then nodded. They followed Len through the winding paths between huts, past hanging charms and smoldering braziers, until they reached the sermon stand—a moss-slick platform built beneath the roots of a fallen oaktree, its bark etched with symbols of Mirella's many faces. [[Prophet Veerah]] stood tall above a semicircle of gathered sisters, no less than a dozen in all. Her black robe was wet from the knees down, her eyes bright with vision-madness. She held a staff capped with a hollowed horn, which she tapped thrice on the wood. When she saw [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] and the twins approach, she smiled. "And how did they do?," she called. The group walked forward. "Excellent, Sister." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] began. "The twins made sure we have an offering to [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] tonight." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] looked at the twins pleased as they bowed slightly to her. They joined the crowd. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] raised her arms, voice ringing like thunder through the still fog. "I was graced last night, sisters. I was graced by the beloved [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] in my dreams. And as thankful as I am that [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] has chosen me to speak with, what she has shown me fills me with pain." She turned slowly, letting her gaze fall on each face. "She showed me fire," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said, her voice high and trembling. "A war not yet born, but near. I saw creatures of metal and flesh, things with half human, half mechanical bodies but endless, unsatiating hunger. They tore through the land like rot through fruit, killing all. I saw no banners, no flags, no names. Only blood. Only screaming." The crowd stirred. Some crossed themselves. Others reached for blades. "I do not know these beasts," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said. "Where they come from or what they want. But the vision was true. And [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]'s hand guided it." She stepped forward, eyes gleaming.

NOTE TITLE: [[05 - Sight Unseen]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Prophet Veerah","character/Raina & Risa","character/Riley Thorne","character/Len Vyne","character/General Colt"],"tags":["chapter","chapter05","story"],"date":"8th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As twins Raina and Risa embrace the deadly path of the Unseen in the misty Drownlands, Ava Victoria searches Gutter Row for the missing Lash Hawkins, forging a fragile alliance with Nico Murray as fate tightens its grip and darkness closes in from all sides.","cover":[["zz_media/05.png"]],"created":"2025/05/26 09:40:25","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:20"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) She stepped forward, eyes gleaming. "This is her warning. If we do not act, they will come. They will raze the land. They will burn our goddess from root to bloom. We, the Widows, must stop it before it begins." A murmur of fear and fire spread through the gathered sisters. Some knelt. Others muttered prayers. A few whispered doubts. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] met the twins’ eyes again. No words. Just understanding.
The door to [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]]’s cabin creaked open under Riley’s hand. Inside, the space was dim and warm, thick with the scent of moss, sage smoke, and damp wood. Clay effigies of Mirella lined the walls, their many eyes carved deep and unblinking. Bundles of dried herbs hung from the ceiling, swaying gently with each breath of the wind. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] sat cross-legged near the hearth, the flicker of the fire painting her face in amber and shadow. She looked up as the trio entered. "Come. Sit." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]], [[Raina & Risa|Risa]], and [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] did as she asked, settling onto low cushions across from her. The warmth from the fire crackled between them. "[[Riley Thorne|Riley]]," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said, her voice soft but steady. "Are they ready?" [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] didn’t hesitate. "I believe they are. They hunt like shadows. Move like breath. Think as one." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]]’s eyes moved to the twins. "And you? Are you ready to leave behind the seen world and walk among the unseen?" [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] and [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] nodded in perfect sync. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] spoke first. "We are." [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] followed. "Yes, sister." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] studied them for a long moment, her expression unreadable. Then she rose. "Very well. Follow me." She led them out of the cabin into the chill evening air, the fog curling around their feet like curious spirits. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] trailed behind, silent, watchful. They followed a narrow trail that wound through ferns and roots slick with dew until it opened into a wide clearing perched on a small cliff. Below, [[The Drownlands]] sprawled into forever—a tapestry of water and green and gray, with ghostlights flickering in the far marsh. At the center of the clearing sat a blackened cauldron on a ring of carved stone. Strange sigils had been etched into the earth around it, faintly glowing with swamplight. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] approached the cauldron and knelt. She scooped mud from the base of a tree, added crushed bark, moss, strands of vine, and flecks of lichen from a stone. As she stirred the dark mixture with a wooden rod carved like a spine, she spoke. "This is her body," she said. "The land, the water, the sky. All that grows and rots. [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] is not above us. She is not distant. She is everything." The twins stood still, watching the motion of her hand, the rhythm of her words. "To walk with her, to speak her name in truth, you must consume her. Let her roots take hold in your blood. Let her breath mix with your own." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] pulled two small clay cups from a pouch at her waist and filled them with the viscous, earthy brew. She rose and held them out. "Do you pledge your lives to [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]?" "We do," the twins said together. "Then drink. Become Unseen." The twins took the cups. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] drank first. The taste was bitter and alive, like wet leaves and iron. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] followed, her throat working as she swallowed the body of a goddess. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] watched, eyes dark and full of fire. When they finished, she smiled. "You are now Unseen to man. Only [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] watches you now." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] gave a quiet nod of approval, the corner of her mouth twitching in pride. But [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] wasn’t finished. "But to fulfill your pledge, to become a Widow," she said, stepping closer, her tone sharpening like a blade drawn from its sheath, "you must each offer one life to the earth. One man each. Killed by your hand. Not for sport. Not for anger. To remove the male influence over your life and return their blood to their rightful mother, [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]." The wind shifted, carrying the scent of rain. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] and [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] did not flinch. "We understand," said [[Raina & Risa|Risa]]. "We’re ready," said [[Raina & Risa|Raina]]. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] closed her eyes and raised her head to the sky. "Then [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] guide your blades. And may the Drownlands drink deep." The clearing held its breath, and the sisters did not speak again.
A short time later, the trio emerged from the mire's tangle at the edge of [[The Drownlands]]. The air was heavy with brine and rot, the boundary between swamp and sea soft and shifting. To the east, Grave Bay opened wide and gray, waters choppy beneath a veiled sky. Out on the horizon, [[The Black Marauder]] moves fast through the waters, outlines cut a dark silhouette against the surf, its sails fat with wind, headed toward distant [[Steeltown]]. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] shaded her eyes. "That’s the [[The Black Marauder|Marauder]]. They’re moving fast." "Oh wow, I've never seen it in person! [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] quipped. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] nodded. "They're an impressive group. Loyal to nobody. They've attacked Loyalist, Wrecking Crew, Rancher's and everybody in between. They're led by a woman named [[Lyla Bonetooth|Bonetooth]]" "A woman leads the Raiders?" "Yes. A formidable one by all accounts too." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] responded. To the west rose the jagged edges of the [[Loyalist Guard]] Base—stone and steel set into the dry rock like a knife in the mire. Watchtowers dotted the perimeter, and the sharp clang of drills echoed off the mudflats.

(cont'd) The group crouched low along a rise overlooking the compound, careful not to rustle the reeds. From their vantage, they could see a unit of recruits being put through brutal exercises—mud runs, combat drills, formation shifts.

At the center, barking commands like a man possessed, stood [[General Colt]]. Slim, bald and grim, his armor gleamed beneath the gray sun. His voice cracked through the air like breaking bones.

"Again! Again! That’s not a charge, that’s a piss-soaked stumble!"

When one recruit faltered, knees buckling in the mud, [[General Colt|Colt]] marched over like a stormfront. He didn’t hesitate. Grabbed the coiled whip from the rack and lashed it hard. Once. Twice. A third time that ripped cloth and drew blood.

"Useless! Fucking disgraceful! You shame the Guard!"

He kept going. Four. Five. Six. The recruit cried out, but [[General Colt|Colt]] didn’t stop. Not until the boy was curled into himself, trembling, the back of his tunic in tatters.

"On your feet!" [[General Colt|Colt]] roared, spittle flying. "Or I’ll break every bone you’ve got and send your mother the teeth!"

The recruit weakly tried to get up but [[General Colt|Colt]] planted his boot hard into his ribs. Even the other recruits had frozen, unmoving, their faces pale.

[[General Colt|Colt]]’s chest heaved as he dropped the whip and turned away like nothing had happened.

[[Raina & Risa|Risa]]’s jaw clenched.

[[Raina & Risa|Raina]] whispered, "He’ll do."

[[Riley Thorne|Riley]] glanced between them, eyes narrowing slightly. "You’re sure?"

The twins answered in unison, staring at [[General Colt]]. "He’s the one."

Below, [[General Colt]] bellowed more orders, his face a thundercloud.

And above, hidden by brush and shadow, the Unseen began to plan.

# THE AFTERBURN 


Three Nail Market swelled with steam, smoke, and shouting.

[[Ava Victoria]] shouldered her way through the crowd, desperation souring her sweat. She darted past fishmongers and pipe-hawkers, past screaming kids and drunk old women pissing in the gutter. Her eyes scanned every stall, every alley, every scrap of shadow.

"[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]?!" she shouted at a knot of gamblers. "You seen [[Lash Hawkins]]?!"

No one answered. One man laughed in her face. Another turned his back.

She cursed under her breath, spun around, and nearly collided with [[Nico Murray]].

"You! You motherfucker!"

[[Nico Murray|Nico]] raised his hands, startled. "Whoa, [[Ava Victoria|Ava]], easy—"

"Don’t ‘easy’ me! Where the fuck is he?!"

"Who? [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]? What’re you talking about?"

"Don’t play dumb with me, [[Nico Murray|Nico]]!" she hissed. "He’s gone! I’ve been looking for him since last night and no one knows shit!"

[[Nico Murray|Nico]] frowned. "I haven’t seen him. Not since last evening..."

He paused.

"He slapped me outside the market. I left after that."

[[Ava Victoria|Ava]] stared at him, jaw tight, eyes full of fire and confusion.

"That’s it?"

"That’s it," Nico said. "I swear."

A long silence. [[Ava Victoria|Ava]]’s breathing slowed. Her shoulders dropped, just a little.

"Fuck," she muttered. "Sorry. I just—something’s wrong."

"Yeah," [[Nico Murray|Nico]] said. "It seems that way."

For reasons he couldn’t name, something twisted in his gut. A feeling like guilt—or maybe dread.

"I’ll help you look," he said.

[[Ava Victoria|Ava]] narrowed her eyes. "If your family—if the [[Murray Boys|Murrays]] had anything to do with this..."

"They didn’t," [[Nico Murray|Nico]] said, sharper now. "We didn’t. I promise."

He held her gaze.

She held it back.

For now, it was enough.

125.title: 04 - Glowing Darkness

metadata.description: Lash Hawkins breaks from the Murray Boys and sparks a fierce feud with Nico Murray, but just as his solo Luxyn empire begins to rise, a quiet street and a pale stranger bring it all to a sudden and deadly halt.

125.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[04 - Glowing Darkness]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/04.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lash Hawkins","character/Nico Murray","character/Marco Murray","character/Rosa Murray","character/Ava Victoria","character/Hella",{"cover":"04.png"}],"tags":["chapter","chapter4","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Lash Hawkins breaks from the Murray Boys and sparks a fierce feud with Nico Murray, but just as his solo Luxyn empire begins to rise, a quiet street and a pale stranger bring it all to a sudden and deadly halt.","created":"2025/05/24 17:32:29","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:15"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ``` > [!world]- SPOILERS > This chapter introduces a significant turning point as **Lash Hawkins declares independence from the powerful Murray Boys**, asserting his own superior Luxyn supply and sparking an immediate, dangerous feud with Nico Murray. His attempt to build a solo empire is dramatically cut short when a **mysterious, pale stranger named Hella violently incapacitates him**. Concurrently, a meeting reveals **the Duke's oppressive plan to implement a severe 70% tax increase** on essential goods across Tribucia, a decision that his wife, Emily, fears will lead to widespread rebellion and bloodshed among the already struggling populace. # Glowing Darkness The stink of grease-fried rat, spoiled fruit, and sour wine hung thick over [[Three Nail Market]]. Neon signs buzzed overhead, casting sickly pink and green light across the wet cobblestones. Hawkers barked over each other from metal stalls, selling everything from fake teeth to real nightmares. It was later and dark but it was Gutter Row in full bloom—ugly, loud, alive. [[Lash Hawkins]] leaned against a rust-pocked pillar, afro perfect, sunglasses shining off neon, smoking a thin roll with one hand tucked deep in his coat. He looked like he always did—half-asleep, half-smiling, like the city’s poison didn’t quite reach him. He watched the crowd move like a clogged artery, not really looking for anyone. Until he saw [[Nico Murray]]. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] came swaggering through the mess like he owned it. Black jacket. Gold chains. Girls on both arms—one blonde in a mesh skirt, the other with a buzzcut and fresh claw marks on her neck. They laughed too loud, clung too close. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] grinned like a man who thought the world should kiss his rings. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] didn’t move. Just waited. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] spotted him and peeled off from the flow, stepping up like they were old friends. “[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]], baby. Hope you haven't been waiting long, I was just..uh.. getting aquainted with my new friends here.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] grins and the girls laugh. “Just waiting on you,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said, flicking ash at his feet. “Didn’t want to interrupt your strut.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] chuckled, flashing teeth. “So, what you doing calling me down here to this shithole for, [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]? In case you forget, we call you. Remember?” “I’m out,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said. The smile on [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s face froze. “Out of what?” “Out of your game,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said. “I’m done pushing Murray dust. I’ve been working my own cook the last couple years. Quiet. Careful. The last batch? Cleaner than your Charspire cut. Stronger, too. Glow’s perfect.” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] looked calmly at [[Nico Murray|Nico]]. For a long second, [[Nico Murray|Nico]] didn’t say anything. Then the laugh came—forced and brittle. “You’re telling me you’re making your own Luxyn now? Like some bootleg piece of trash?” “I’m telling you I don’t need your family’s supply. I’ve got my own line. People like it. They’re talking.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] stepped forward, close enough for his breath to sour the air between them. “You know what you’re doing? You realize this ain’t ‘fuckin DIY Drug Week,’ right? You start pushing your shit in our streets, you ain’t just quitting. You’re competing. You’re coming at the Murray Boys.” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] smiled. Not wide. Just enough. “I know exactly what the fuck I'm doing, [[Nico Murray|Nico]]. Now run on home and tell Daddy for me.” “You dumb piece of shit.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s face went red. The girls looked nervous now, backing up a step. “You think Marco’s gonna let you live?” “I think I’m not scared of you,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] snapped—swung wild, fast. But [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] moved faster, ducking the punch like he’d seen it in a dream. Then his hand whipped out—crack—a slap across [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s face that turned heads. Not a brawl. Not a beatdown. Just enough to humiliate. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] staggered, blinking, the left side of his face going bright red. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stepped closer, voice low. “You wanna be your old man so bad, [[Nico Murray|Nico]], but you ain’t got the brains or the balls. You’re just a boy playin’ gangster. Oh, and tell your mom I said hello.” The blonde’s jaw dropped. The buzzcut girl laughed once, sharp and loud before covering her mouth. [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s breath hissed through his teeth. His fists clenched. Then he turned and walked. Fast. The girls hesitated—then followed. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stayed a while longer, finishing his smoke. The market didn’t care. It moved on like always. But something had just shifted under its skin.
[[Nico Murray|Nico]] stomped up the stone path to the Murray House, boots loud against the wet cobbles. The home was an old mansion in the old days that had been renovated over the years into a large, two story townhome. The walk from Three Nail Market hadn’t cooled his blood—if anything, it had stoked the fire. The slap still burned. Inside, the house was all shadows and golden trim—Tribucian wealth soaked in old violence. He found [[Rosa Murray]], his mother, in the sitting room, ledger open, pen tapping in rhythm. [[Marco Murray|Marco]]]] sat nearby, slow-burning a cigar, watching smoke curl toward the chandelier, reading over that day's edition of the [[Tribucia Tribute]]. “What happened?” [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]] asked without looking up. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] pulled off his coat and tossed it at a chair. “Lash fuckin' [[Lash Hawkins|Hawkins]] happened. He’s out. Says he’s not pushing [[Luxyn]] for us anymore.” That got their attention. [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]]’s pen stopped. [[Marco Murray|Marco]] exhaled a long stream of smoke. "The boy is out?" [[Marco Murray|Marco]] inquired.

NOTE TITLE: [[04 - Glowing Darkness]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/04.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lash Hawkins","character/Nico Murray","character/Marco Murray","character/Rosa Murray","character/Ava Victoria","character/Hella",{"cover":"04.png"}],"tags":["chapter","chapter4","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Lash Hawkins breaks from the Murray Boys and sparks a fierce feud with Nico Murray, but just as his solo Luxyn empire begins to rise, a quiet street and a pale stranger bring it all to a sudden and deadly halt.","created":"2025/05/24 17:32:29","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:15"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) That got their attention. [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]]’s pen stopped. [[Marco Murray|Marco]] exhaled a long stream of smoke. "The boy is out?" [[Marco Murray|Marco]] inquired. “Says he’s been cooking his own,” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] went on, pacing now. “And it’s good. Real good. Better than our Charspire batches, he says. He’s selling it already.” [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]] closed the ledger and exhaled. “I never trusted that boy.” [[Marco Murray|Marco]] took another pull on his cigar, eyes steady. “I’ll send word to Francis. Let him know what’s happened. If Mr. [[Lash Hawkins|Hawkins]] wants to run against us, that's his choice to make. We will make our own choices accordingly as well.” “He slapped me,” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] blurted, the words bitter on his tongue. That earned a pause. [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]] raised her eyebrows. [[Marco Murray|Marco]] didn’t blink. “Gutter trash like [[Lash Hawkins|Hawkins]] will be dealt with,” [[Marco Murray|Marco]] said calmly. “But not with tantrums.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] flushed. “You think I'm gonna just let that motherfuc—” “I think you need to settle down. Emotions don't win wars, my boy.” [[Marco Murray|Marco]] cut in. “And remember something. Nobody wins against the Murrays. Nobody.” He stood slowly, smoothing his shirt with one hand, cigar in the other. “I want you to make contact with [[Samson Knight]],” he said. "[[Third Row]] owes us a favor for looking the other way on that fuel shipment they stole. See if we can broker a meeting. Might be time to get them selling our powder right out of [[Three Nail Market|Three Nail]].” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] nodded, still seething. But the fire in his chest was cooling. His father had that effect—an icewater voice behind the fire. “Go clean yourself up, Nico” [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]] said, standing, resting a hand on her son's shoulder. He left without a word, the slap still stinging deeper than skin.
Inside a battered shack tucked deep in Gutter Row, [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] moved through his homemade lab with quiet precision. Rusty shelves sagged under the weight of glass beakers, jars of powdered chemicals, and tangled tubing. A dusty TV flickered in the corner, barely holding signal, but the familiar voice of [[Morris Gable]] carried clear enough. "[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]," the host's voice echoed, followed by canned laughter and a rimshot. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] glanced over his shoulder at the screen, lips tugging into a grin as Morris launched into jokes about Loyalist curfews, bad street meat and the upcoming [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] vs. [[Bastian Redd|Redd]] fight. He struck a match and lit a cigarette, watching the tv and laughing under his breath. Onscreen, [[Morris Gable|Morris]] paused, stood grinning in front of a large blue curtain as he delivered that evenings monologue. “And how about that [[Luxyn]] bust in [[Charspire]], huh? Six arrested, two plants locked down, and the [[Loyalist Guard]] says it’s just the beginning. Yeah officials at the two plants apparently finally noticed when everybody leaving the plant for the day had glowing white eyes!” The audience laughed. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] didn’t. His face twitched. For just a second, his smile cracked. He took a drag from the cigarette, turned back to his station, and muttered, “Shit.” He sat still, listening to the laughter echoing from the TV. The sound made his skin itch. He forced a breath out through his nose, slow and even, then flicked the ash into a nearby tray. No one knew about his place—no one he didn’t trust. Still. The walls felt thinner all of a sudden. A high-pitched ding pulled his attention. He moved to the sealed glass container sitting at the center of his setup. Steam curled out as he cracked the seal, revealing a pile of faintly glowing white powder. [[Luxyn]]. His [[Luxyn]]. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] grinned wide, grabbing a thin scoop and lifting a pinch to eye level. The powder shimmered faintly in the lab's low light, like it knew it was something special. “Oh yeah baby. This about to be my town now,” he murmured. He looked around for an empty container for his new batch but everything was already packed to the brim. He cursed softly, set the scoop down, stood up and pulled on his jacket. The shack door creaked as he stepped out and locked it behind him, double-checking the padlock. The night was cool, the air sharp with rain-soaked rust and charcoal smoke. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stepped onto the broken path and headed toward the Three Nail Market, boots crunching on grit, thinking of the empire he was about to build—one glowing grain at a time.
[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] lit another cigarette as he walked, trailing smoke through the broken veins of Gutter Row. The city was quieter now. Most of the stalls had shuttered, but a few still flickered under dull neon. He passed a cluster of familiar faces near a boarded-up music shop—old friends, loose ties standing around smoking and drinking. A small stereo blasting out the tunes of [[Dusty Dillon]] played at their feet. “Ah that's my homie right there!” one called out. "What's good, my peoples?" [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] grinned. He slapped hands and pulling one of the girls into a quick hug. "[[Ava Victoria|Ava]], sugar. How you doin', girl?" "[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]], baby you coming to the [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] fight with us?" The pretty girl with long jet black hair asked, inquiring about the Cutman vs. Redd fight. “I don't know yet, [[Ava Victoria|Ava]], I might need to work that night, you know? "Hawkins you work too much. Fuck the Murray's." [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] said. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] laughed. "Actually I just told the [[Murray Boys|Murray's]] to fuck off just tonight. I work for me now." [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] looked impressed. "Is that right? I bet little Nico took that well. So, you make your own hours and stuff now, huh?" She looked up at Lash.

NOTE TITLE: [[04 - Glowing Darkness]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/04.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lash Hawkins","character/Nico Murray","character/Marco Murray","character/Rosa Murray","character/Ava Victoria","character/Hella",{"cover":"04.png"}],"tags":["chapter","chapter4","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Lash Hawkins breaks from the Murray Boys and sparks a fierce feud with Nico Murray, but just as his solo Luxyn empire begins to rise, a quiet street and a pale stranger bring it all to a sudden and deadly halt.","created":"2025/05/24 17:32:29","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:15"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] looked impressed. "Is that right? I bet little Nico took that well. So, you make your own hours and stuff now, huh?" She looked up at Lash. "Well, yeah I guess I do. Why? You want me to... pencil you in sometime?" [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] grinned at her. [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] leaned closer to him. "Mmm..how about tonight? You want to come by later?" "Oh you know I do." [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] pulled [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] in a bit tighter. "I just gotta run to the shop, grab some supplies and run it back to the lab, you know? But I'll be over after that." [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] bid farewell to his friends and continued on. "Don't be late." [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] grinned as [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] walked off into the [[Three Nail Market]] He kept walking, past the last of the shouting vendors, deeper into the crooked backstreets. Lamps flickered weakly, casting his long shadow ahead of him. He turned a corner. And froze. [[Hella]] stood ten feet ahead, framed in the soft wash of a broken streetlamp. Pale as snow and in a small, disheveled black dress she stared at him, smiling an unsettling smile. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stopped cold. He didn’t recognize her, but something in his gut screamed get the fuck away from her. "You...need something, sugar?" [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] asked. She didn’t answer. Just stared. Her grin was too wide. Too still. He forced a chuckle. “What you lookin' for tonight, honey? You lookin' for a little bit of that [[Luxyn|Glow]]? Still nothing. Just that smile. "You...You need some [[ECONOMY|slugs]]?" [[Hella]] just watched [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] getting more uncomfortable by the moment. "Fuck bitch I ain't got time for this..." He took a slow step forward, angling to pass. [[Hella]] moved with him—one step, smooth, precise, blocking his path. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] frowned. “You need to get the fuck outta my way.” She didn’t. He took another step. “Last warning.” [[Hella]] opened her mouth. A burst of green mist sprayed from between her lips, catching him full in the face. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] cried out, "What the fuck?!" stumbling back, hands clawing at his eyes. The world tilted. He hit the ground, hard. Blood immediately pooling around his head from the impact. His sunglasses skidding off down the cobblestone. [[Hella]] stepped forward, calm as a shadow, she had a black rope now in her hands. She looked down at him, eyes shining. “You're next,” she whispered.
# THE AFTERBURN A long marble table stretched under the arched windows of the Duke’s private chamber, candles flickering along its length. Velvet drapes hung still. The skyline of [[Ashmoor]] loomed outside, ghosted in fog. [[The Duke]] sat at the head of the table, sipping dark liquor from a crystal tumbler. Beside him, [[Emily Burton|Emily]], his wife, stirred a cup of pale tea. Across from them, [[General Colt]] of the Loyalist Guard, [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], and [[Raynar Ventura]] shared in casual conversation—laughter, veiled threats, and cold smiles. “I trust everything’s in place for my announcement then?” [[the Duke]] asked, eyes flicking toward [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]]. [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] nodded. “Everything. Mr. [[Owen McCready|McCready]] at [[TTV Studios]] will broadcast your address live to the territories. He's assured me cameras and crew will be here the morning of.” [[The Duke]] nodded and looked to [[General Colt|Colt]]. “And the [[Loyalist Guard]] is prepared for any opposition throughout the territories?” [[General Colt|Colt]] didn’t speak. [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] did. “We’ve got boots across Tribucia. If anybody tries to rally a crowd, we'll stomp it out. Quick.” [[The Duke]] looked pleased and turned his attention back to [[Raynar Ventura]]. "And what of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]? Have they made their intentions of attending the festival known yet?" [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] paused, "Well, My Duke, invitations were delivered. I've been told to [[Mark Jeffrey]] directly. However there has been no response as of yet, I'm afraid." [[The Duke]] nodded and looked out the window for a moment, before addressing Raynar once again. "I see. Has there been word from [[Lyla Bonetooth|Bonetooth]] and the [[Rustwater Raiders]] yet?" "Only a report of [[the Black Marauder]] cutting down the [[Water#Grave Bay|Grave Bay]] coast towards [[Steeltown]], My Duke." [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] said. "It seems they're heading to where they should be. Uh, one other matter I should bring to your attention My Duke, it seems one of our [[Loyalist Guard]]s in [[Gutter Row]] had their head impaled with what appears to be a large spike-like object. We know this because we found his partner handcuffed, screaming, covered in piss..." Raynar chuckled. "...and tossed inside a dumpster. He claims the [[Gutter Row]] boogeyman did it but has yet to explain what he was doing there in the first place. We're pressing him for more accurate info."[[03 - The Devil In The Row|*]] [[The Duke]] listened to Raynar. "I see. Keep me abreast of the situation." [[Emily Burton|Emily]] blinked, setting her tea down gently. “You keep dancing around the topic, My Duke. What’s the announcement?” [[The Duke]] leaned back in his chair, fingers steepled. “Ah, my dear. Well, due to production and manufacturing costs rising across Tribucia, a 70% tax increase on fuel out of [[Charspire]]. Food out of [[Threshton]]. And steel out of [[Steeltown]] will be necessary to continue on the enlightened path we are on, you see. I'll announce the increase at the Festival and will be in effect 1st day of [[CALENDAR|Greensun]].” [[Emily Burton|Emily]] sat up straighter, eyes narrowing. “What? But the taxes on basic necessities are already high enough. That’ll ruin people. They already can’t afford to survive. [[Jacoban Clay]] doesn't need another home in [[Ashmoor#Diamond Valley]]. He doesn't need to raise the costs of anything if he so chooses!”

METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/04.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lash Hawkins","character/Nico Murray","character/Marco Murray","character/Rosa Murray","character/Ava Victoria","character/Hella",{"cover":"04.png"}],"tags":["chapter","chapter4","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Lash Hawkins breaks from the Murray Boys and sparks a fierce feud with Nico Murray, but just as his solo Luxyn empire begins to rise, a quiet street and a pale stranger bring it all to a sudden and deadly halt.","created":"2025/05/24 17:32:29","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:15"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) [[The Duke]] turned his head slightly at his wife. His eyebrows furrowing slightly. “It’s necessary. [[Charspire]]’s furnaces don’t fuel themselves. The Guard doesn’t march for free. This palace, this territory, all of [[Ashmoor]]—it requires sacrifice. Sacrifice, I might add, that contributes to your...delicate...way of life here at [[The Silo]]. Isn't that right, dear?”

[[Emily Burton|Emily]] looked around the table, searching for support, but found none. [[General Colt]] stared at his drink. [[Raynar Ventura]] looked at the ceiling. [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] simply sat there, shoulders square, gaze locked.

“Disgraceland is starving,” [[Emily Burton|Emily]] said. “This won’t bring order. It’ll bring riots. Blood.”

“Then let them bleed. The only way Tribucia continues on, even thrives in the new world is by sacrifice for the greater good of our new nation. If Tribucia is truly to become a utopia then we need too weed out the weak. It's necessity." [[The Duke]] smiled faintly, his voice low.  "Trust me, my dear. I know what is best for you, for our people, for this entire nation.”

[[Emily Burton|Emily]] pressed her lips together. Her voice, when it came, was quiet and sharp. “You forget what desperation breeds.”

[[Sgt. Rottwyler|Rottwyler]]’s eyes snapped to her. Cold. Unmoving. A predator beneath the uniform. [[The Duke]] glared at his wife, "And you forget your place. By all means, my grand Duchess, if you want to go live in [[Gutter Row]] with the rats instead of here at the palace, be my guest." He snarled.

[[Emily Burton|Emily]] didn’t flinch. But she said nothing more and took a long sip of her tea.

# Chapter 03:

#### _Moonday night, 7th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When two off-duty [[Loyalist Guard]] take their power trip too far behind [[Hollow House]], they come face to face with a shadow the city pretends doesn’t exist. As [[Shana]] fights for survival, a chain rings through the alley, and with it, [[The Grim Man]] delivers his silent judgment. Blood hits brick, legend becomes real, and a quiet pact is sealed in the dark.

And somewhere else in [[Steeltown]], a message is delivered. Not everyone welcomes it.

131.title: 03 - The Devil In The Row
131.path: DISGRACELAND/03 - The Devil In The Row.md

metadata.description: When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.

131.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[03 - The Devil In The Row]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/03.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/The Grim Man","character/Shana"],"tags":["chapter","chapter3","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.","created":"2025/05/23 09:05:27","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:11"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ### The Devil In The Row The back door to [[Hollow House]] moaned on its hinges as [[Shana]] pushed it open, the sounds of [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] blared from the small television set behind her. She stepped into the alley like she owned it, because she did. Behind the club was narrow and slick with old rain, the cobblestones uneven, glinting faintly in the gutterlight that poured from a rusted fixture above the door. The scent was a mix of wet trash, coppery old blood, and perfume that clung to her coat like a memory she hadn’t shaken off yet. Posters hyping the upcoming [[Bobby Cutman]] vs. [[Bastian Redd]] fight were plastered all over the old walls. She exhaled slow, struck a match against the brick, and lit a roseleaf cigarette. The tip flared orange, glowing like a signal in the dark. She leaned her back to the wall, tilted her head up, and closed her eyes. It had been a good night. No trouble, full house, tips generous. The girls were asleep or drunk or busy. She had fifteen minutes to herself, and she was going to make them count. That’s when she heard the boots. Heavy steps, staggered rhythm, scraping and clunking against the stone. Two shadows rounded the mouth of the alley, backlit by the neon hum of [[GUTTER ROW]]’s signage. Tall, armored, but sloppy. [[Loyalist Guard]] — off-duty by the stink of them. One had his helmet half-off, dangling from the strap. His face was round, pale, and shiny with sweat. The other was leaner, sharper, with a scar slicing through his eyebrow and down his cheek like someone had tried to write a message in his face. “Hey now,” the fat one said, voice slurring just enough to smell the booze on it. “Ain’t this a rare treat.” The scarred one smiled with too many teeth. “Evening, love. Didn’t know [[Hollow House]] did alley service.” [[Shana]] didn’t move. She took another drag, let the smoke drift lazily from her lips. “We don’t. Move along.” The fat one squinted. “Wait a minute. That’s [[Shana]], ain’t it? The Rat Queen herself. Thought you’d be taller.” [[Shana]] flicked ash onto the ground. “And I thought [[Loyalist Guard]] were fine, upstanding citizens. Looks like we’re both disappointed.” The scarred one laughed, stepped in closer, boots scraping. He smelled like sweat and engine grease and the sour tang of cheap distillery hooch. “Relax, sweetheart. We’re just being neighborly. Share a smoke with your heroes.” “You’re not my heroes,” [[Shana]] said, eyes steady. “You’re two half-drunk pigs who think a badge makes your dick bigger. Go home.” The fat one’s face twitched. “You got a sharp mouth for a whore.” [[Shana]] didn’t blink. “And you’ve got a loose grip on your lips for a man talking out of line.” That landed. The fat one took a step forward, reaching for her arm. [[Shana]] didn’t wait. She slapped his hand away and jabbed a knuckle into his throat with practiced speed. He gagged, stumbled back, coughing and grabbing at his neck. The scarred one snarled and lunged from behind. His arm wrapped around her shoulders, the other clamping hard over her mouth. [[Shana]] kicked back, heels catching his shin, but he held tight. “Feisty little bitch, ain't ya?” he muttered into her ear. “Let’s take this somewhere quieter.” The fat one recovered, red-faced and furious. “Gonna make you beg now, you cunt.” They dragged her deeper into the alley, past the dumpsters and the rotting crates, down where the lights didn’t reach. [[Shana]]’s scream was muffled by a dirty glove, her legs kicking, hands clawing at the scarred one’s arms. Her cigarette hit the ground behind them, still glowing faint. No one came. No one ever did. Not back here.
The guards shoved [[Shana]] down hard behind the dumpster, her back hitting the bricks with a grunt. She scrambled to her feet, teeth bared, eyes blazing. "Come on, you pathetic fucks," she spat, fists raised. "Let’s see if your cocks can still work after I twist them off." The fat one laughed as he cracked his knuckles. "Still got bite. That’s cute." The scarred one moved first, fast and brutal, slamming a fist into her stomach. [[Shana]] doubled over, gasping, but didn’t fall. The fat one grabbed her by the shoulders and threw her against the dumpster. Her skull rang against the metal with a dull thud. "Fucking bitch," the scarred one hissed, pulling at her coat. "You’re gonna be thanking us when we're through with ya." "Flip for it?" the fat one said, already unbuckling his belt. "Nah," his partner replied, grinning. "Let’s make it a game. First one to finish gets her teeth as a souvenir." They both laughed, rough and hungry. [[Shana]] lashed out, raking her nails across the scarred one’s cheek. He roared, punched her across the face, and blood sprayed from her lip. Her legs folded. They moved in. _CLANG._ Then they froze. A metallic echo cracked through the alley, sharp and final, like a starting bell in hell. Both men turned their heads. He was there. Standing twenty feet down the alley, half-shrouded in shadow. A long coat hanging still around his tall frame, soaked in the dark. One arm held out, the end of a thick iron chain looped around his hand. At the far end, a long spike rested on the cobblestone, the tip stained and gleaming. His ominous white hockey mask almost glowing in the shadows. [[The Grim Man]]. The fat one squinted. "What the fuck is this, costume night?" The scarred one shifted nervously. "It’s him. The fucking chain freak." [[The Grim Man]] didn’t move. Didn’t speak. Just stood there, the chain twitching once, slow and deliberate. "Back off," the fat one barked. "This ain’t your business, freak." No reply. Only the sound of the spike tapping the cobblestone as [[The Grim Man]] slowly lifts and drops the chain. _Tap. Tap. Tap. Tap._ The scarred one took a breath, forcing a smile. "You gonna play superhero now? Try to stop us?" The chain shifted again. _Tap. Tap. Tap._ The fat one spat. "You think you scare me? I’ll fuckin’ gut you."
