metadata.description: When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.

132.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[03 - The Devil In The Row]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/03.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/The Grim Man","character/Shana"],"tags":["chapter","chapter3","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.","created":"2025/05/23 09:05:27","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:11"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) The chain shifted again. _Tap. Tap. Tap._ The fat one spat. "You think you scare me? I’ll fuckin’ gut you." They let go of [[Shana]], turning to face him fully. One drew a small baton. The other, a stubby, rusted sidearm. They advanced slowly, trying to circle him. [[The Grim Man]] didn’t move. Didn’t breathe. Didn’t care.
The alley exploded with movement. [[The Grim Man]] snapped his arm forward, the chain ripping through the air with a banshee’s wail. The spike struck the fat guard just above the nose and kept going, punching through his skull and out the back. Bone and blood splattered the brick. The body dropped like a puppet with cut strings, collapsing in a twitching heap before the scream even finished echoing. [[Shana]] stared, frozen in disbelief. One heartbeat, and the man who had been pawing at her was nothing but a pile of meat and steam. The scarred guard jolted into action, panic taking hold. He raised the pistol and squeezed the trigger, twice. Bullets screamed down the alley, ricocheting off the dumpster and sparking against the bricks. But [[The Grim Man]] was already gone, vanished into the shadows like he'd been swallowed whole. [[Shana]] ducked low behind the bins, her breath caught in her throat, heart pounding like a war drum. Her eyes scanned the darkness, desperate for a shape, a shadow, anything. All she saw was the fat guard’s body cooling in the gutter, the alley still choked with silence. She didn’t know whether to scream or laugh. "Shit, holy shit, fuck," the guard muttered, voice shaking as much as the gun in his hand. He backed away, breath sharp, feet scraping. Silence. Then a sound, faint and deliberate. _Tap._ The guard spun toward it, gun raised. Nothing there. Another step. Another breath. _Tap._ He pivoted again, wide-eyed, lips twitching with fear. He edged toward the dumpster, heart hammering. "Fuck you!" Peeked around it. Empty. He turned around, confused, then his mouth opened to call out again, maybe to plead, maybe to scream. _WHACK._ [[Shana]]’s boot hit him dead in the crotch. He collapsed forward with a strangled moan, both hands instinctively reaching down as the pistol slipped from his grip. [[The Grim Man]] was behind her in the same instant. No warning. No sound. Just presence. He moved like a guillotine, fast, final. One hand grabbed the guard’s collar, the other twisting his arm behind his back with bone-grinding force. The man shrieked, struggling, but it didn’t matter. [[The Grim Man]] was relentless. He yanked the cuffs from the guard’s belt and snapped them onto his wrists with a brutal click that echoed like a sentence passed. Then, without ceremony, he lifted him off the ground and walked him to the dumpster. The man’s boots scraped the stone. He screamed, begged, thrashed. Didn’t matter. [[The Grim Man]] smashed him with the butt of his spike one final time and hurled him headfirst into the bin. The lid slammed shut like a judge’s gavel. The alley went still.
[[Shana]] stood in the hush that followed, her breath steaming in the cold alley air. Blood painted her mouth, but her eyes were steady. She turned slowly. [[The Grim Man]] was still there, standing like a statue at the alley’s edge, the chain coiled in one gloved hand. The mask turned toward her. He didn’t speak. He never did. [[Shana]] took a cautious step forward, then another, until she was close enough to see the scuffs on his boots, the dull sheen of dried blood on the spike. "Thank you," she said. Her voice was hoarse but steady. "For stepping in. For saving me there." She motioned to the dead guard on the ground. Grim Man didn’t move. She gave a half-laugh, bitter at the edges. "I’ve heard stories. They say you live in the walls. That you can smell blood in the air. That you don’t stop. Not for anyone." [[The Grim Man]] tilted his head slightly. Not a nod. Not a denial. Just... acknowledgment. "They call you the Grim Man," she continued, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand. Her voice was steadier now, threaded with something curious, something darker. "I heard you’re a ghost. Some say a demon. Had a drunk in here once who swore you saved him from a gut-stabbing in Charspire, right outside the glass foundry. He nearly pissed himself telling the story. Said he heard the chain before he saw the blood...and now I see why." She stepped closer. Close enough to smell the iron and rain still clinging to his coat. "But I don’t think you’re a ghost. I think you’re a man. A very, very dangerous man. The kind we need in Gutter Row, even if nobody wants to admit it." Still no answer. Her eyes flicked over his mask. "You're not gentle, or soft, or kind. But you make the monsters question if they should come out at night. And sometimes," she said, brushing a lock of red hair behind her ear, "it's good to know there is someone like you out there." She reached up, slow, deliberate, and wiped a smudge of blood off his mask with her thumb. Her fingers lingered a moment longer than they needed to. She looked him straight in the eyes behind that mask. "I owe you. You ever need something, anything, you come find me. Doesn’t matter what it is. I’ll make it happen." [[The Grim Man]] gave a slow nod. One motion. Measured. Heavy. Then he turned, melted into the shadows without a word, the chain dragging behind him. _Tap._ _Tap._ _Tap._ Until even that faded, and all that was left was the silence. [[Shana]] stood alone in the dark, staring after him. Then she reached into her coat, cleaned the blood from her face, dusted herself off, pulled out a second cigarette, and lit it with a steading hand, eyeing the dead guard. "Ember fuckin' damnit now I gotta deal with this...," she whispered. And the smoke curled into the night.

# THE AFTERBURN 


Inside the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]’s clubhouse, the low thump of old speakers mixed with the clink of bottles and the buzz of tired men swapping half-truths and bruises. [[Mark Jeffrey]] leaned over the table, sorting through ledgers that smelled faintly of blood and beer.

Across from him, [[Joe Ameen]] stared out the grimy front window, frowning.

"We got company," [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] said, tilting his head. "Loyalists. Two of 'em."

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] looked up slowly, chewing on a toothpick. "Fuck off. Uniformed?"

"Oh yeah. Full swagger. One of ‘em’s got a smile like he's Morris fuckin' Gable."

Mark rose and the two stepped outside to greet the unannounced visitors.

Two [[Loyalist Guard]] officers were already halfway across the lot, walking like they were posing for a recruitment poster. One held a black envelope sealed with wax, the Duke’s sigil stamped in silver.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] folded his arms. "You boys know where you are right now? Hollow House is in Gutter Row, not here..."

The smiling guard stopped, but the smirk didn’t leave his face. "We’re right where we’re supposed to be. On orders of The Duke. Why don't you show some good faith for once. The Duke wanted to...extend a hand...to the Wrecking Crew."

[[Joe Ameen]] barked a short laugh. "I got something I'll extend right back to ya."

The other guard, younger, eyes hard, stepped forward a half pace. "You wanna keep this civil, maybe you ease off the tone."

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] didn’t flinch, but he also doesn't let people get in [[Joe Ameen|Joe]]'s face. "You bring weapons into my yard, and now you wanna tell us how we're gonna talk on our own land? You better tell us why you're here. Now. Or I'm going to stop being such a good host, you know?"

The older guard raised the envelope. "Just an invitation. To the [[Ashmoor Festival]]. A celebration of unity. Brotherhood. Prosperity. Compliments of The Duke."

"Ha! The Duke wants us at his little festival?" [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] muttered.

He held out the envelope.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] took the envelope without looking at it, eyes locked on the guard.

"You done?"

The guard’s smile faded a notch. He gave a stiff nod. He looked at [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]] and his eyes narrowed. "Enjoy the evening."

The guards turned and left, boots echoing across the clubhouse lot.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] and [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] watched them go in silence.

[[Joe Ameen|Joe]] muttered, "The fuck was that? Since when does [[The Silo]] invite us to anything?"

"Maybe it's bait," [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] said, pulling out a lighter. He set the envelope aflame, held it for a beat, then lit his cigarette with the burning invitation.

He dropped the scorched paper and ground it under his boot.

Smoke curled past his lips.

"Fuck [[The Duke]]."

And the wind carried the ashes down the rough lot of the Wrecking Crew clubhouse.

# Chapter 02

#### _Alphaday, 6th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and the Rustwater Raiders are summoned to [[The Silo]] for a secret job, they’re ordered to smuggle a high-value prisoner to Steeltown — but the “prisoner” turns out to be a chain gang of slaves. As tensions rise aboard [[the Black Marauder]], Lyla must decide whether to complete the job or risk everything by defying [[The Duke]]. Meanwhile, a chilling vision haunts the [[Unseen Widows]]: a glimpse of the horrors still to come.

Tasked with transporting a "high-value prisoner" to Steeltown, Lyla discovers the cargo is actually a chain gang of slaves, forcing her to confront a **moral choice between loyalty to the Duke and an act of rebellion**. NOTE TITLE: [[02 - Ghosts On The Waves]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/lyladuke.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lyla Bonetooth","character/The Duke","character/Blacktide Cray","character/Clinton Firebay","character/Sgt. Rottwyler","character/Emily Burton"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter2"],"date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Summoned to The Silo for a secret job, Lyla Bonetooth discovers her “prisoner” is a chain gang of slaves, forcing her to choose between loyalty and rebellion aboard the Black Marauder, all while Prophet Veerah glimpses a terrifying future that threatens to eclipse them all.","created":"2025/05/22 13:53:04","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:07"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) --- # Ghosts on the Waves Fog clung to [[the Black Marauder]]’s hull like ghost fingers, stubborn and damp, reluctant to release its grip on the aging vessel. Inside the captain’s quarters, the air smelled of salt, brass polish, and wet leather. Knives pinned maps to the wall, their blades gleaming in the shifting lantern light. The room rocked gently with the tide, the low groan of the moorings echoing beneath the deck like a restless spirit. [[Lyla Bonetooth]] sat at her desk with boots kicked up, flipping a rusted coin between her fingers as she traced her eyes across the worn map. Rain drummed against the steel above in a steady rhythm. Nearby, [[Zadie Adeyemi]] polished a curved blade, its edge glinting as she sipped from a steaming tin cup. The quiet between them was not uncomfortable. It was the quiet of routine — of calm before the inevitable. A knock broke the rhythm. “Cap’n. Something came in on the long-hook,” came [[Clinton Firebay]]’s voice from outside. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] didn’t look up. “Didn’t order anything. Unless it’s rum or tickets to Cutman versus Redd, I ain’t interested.” The door creaked open and [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] stepped in, water trailing from his coat. “Wasn’t a delivery. Came sealed. Courier was Loyalist. Didn’t say a word. Just dropped it and peeled.” Now she looked up, one brow lifting. “Loyalist? Out here?” He tossed a wax-sealed envelope onto her desk. The red wax bore a familiar sigil — a black sun over cracked ground. The Duke’s personal seal. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] flicked her coin into the air, caught it, then stared at the envelope. “Well, shit. Guess it’s either a dinner invitation or a death sentence.” The door slammed open. [[Blacktide Cray]] barged in, rain-spattered and scowling. “Tell me that ain’t what I think it is.” “It’s not what you think it is,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said, deadpan. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] shot her a sidelong glare. “Then what is it, Bonetooth?” “It’s a letter. From the Silo.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] didn’t move for a long moment. Then: “Goddamnit, [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], I don’t have time for this shit today. Well, go on. Read it.” She opened it slowly, the crackle of the wax breaking loud in the silence. Her eyes skimmed the letter, jaw tightening. “So?” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] asked. “What’s the word?” She looked up, her voice even. “We’re invited to the Silo. Raynar Ventura signed it. Says The Duke wants to meet.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] began pacing, cracking his knuckles like they owed him money. “Hell no. That bastard doesn’t summon people unless he’s planning to hang 'em or buy 'em. Ain’t gonna be us.” “Could be legit,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] offered. “Could be leverage. Raiders have done dirt all across the coast — maybe he wants to hire us.” “Or bury us,” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] growled. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stood, letter dangling in one hand. Her gaze swept over both men, cool as a steel blade. “[[Blacktide Cray|Cray]], you’re wound tight enough to snap a mast. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]], you think too pretty. Me? I think if the wolf sends a dinner invite, you don’t ignore it — but you don’t show up unarmed either.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] leaned in, voice low. “We burn it. No trace, no trouble. No one ever got stabbed in the back by a letter they didn’t read.” “Problem is, we did read it,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] said. “And he knows we did. Ventura don’t send ghosts. He sends messengers he can hang if we don’t show.” “Let 'em hang,” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] muttered. “Be the first honest thing [[The Duke]]’s done all year.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]], quiet until now, set her knife spinning into the table, blade-first. “If it were a death sentence, we’d already be bleeding. He wants something. Question is — how much poison’s in the cup?” “We haven’t touched Loyalist cargo in years,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said, measured. “We never broke our agreement. He’d have no reason to want our heads.” The rain intensified. The hull groaned. “Could be a job. Could be a warning,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] said. “Could be he just wants to see if we still bow when summoned.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] scoffed. “And what? You wanna go kiss his boots?” “You ever see me kiss anyone’s boots, [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]?” “No. But I seen what happens when a mouth talks back at the Silo. Ends up sewn shut or fed to fish.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] leaned back, arms crossed. “She ain’t wrong to weigh it. But I’m with the captain. Whatever this is — we don’t ignore it.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] nodded slowly. “We go. Quiet, armed, and watching every shadow. Me. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]]. [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]]. Rest stay on the ship.” The others filtered in — [[Salt-Eye Marlow]], [[Darius Adeyemi]], [[Silas Vayne]] — just in time to catch the last line. “[[Silas Vayne|Silas]], [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]], [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] — you stay back,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] instructed. “Eyes on the Marauder. Anyone tries boarding, you gut ‘em or sink ‘em.” She turned to the wall furnace. One last look at the letter, then she tossed it in. The wax popped. The paper curled and blackened. “We got his message,” she said quietly. “Let’s go pay the [[The Duke|old fuck]] a visit.”
Evening blanketed the docks in a quilt of wet fog and grit. The cutter — a rust-streaked, repurposed patrol skiff — floated low in the water, tethered by ropes frayed like old nerves. Rain hissed off metal. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stepped aboard first, her coat heavy with water, her long dark hair clinging to her as she adjusts her eye-patch against the drizzle.

NOTE TITLE: [[02 - Ghosts On The Waves]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/lyladuke.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lyla Bonetooth","character/The Duke","character/Blacktide Cray","character/Clinton Firebay","character/Sgt. Rottwyler","character/Emily Burton"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter2"],"date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Summoned to The Silo for a secret job, Lyla Bonetooth discovers her “prisoner” is a chain gang of slaves, forcing her to choose between loyalty and rebellion aboard the Black Marauder, all while Prophet Veerah glimpses a terrifying future that threatens to eclipse them all.","created":"2025/05/22 13:53:04","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:07"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] grumbled curses as he checked the engine, knuckles scraped from the last fix. [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] climbed in without a word, rifle slung over one shoulder, a quiet shadow in the half-light. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] secured the last latch on the tarp-covered crate, then gave the Marauder a long look, like a man hoping it wouldn’t be the last time. Up on the dock, [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] sparked a crooked roll-up and squinted down through the gloom. “Don’t like this smell, Cap’n,” he called. “Smells like rot. One o’ them rotten-egg-threw-up shit kinda smells, ya know?” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] didn’t look up. “Spoken like a poet. Just watch the Marauder, [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]]. If we're not back in two hours come in swinging steel.” “I’ll keep the fire lit, dear,” he called back, flashing a grin of broken teeth. The engine coughed to life like a dying beast. Rain smeared the view as they pulled away, the Marauder dissolving behind them into silhouette — a phantom ship waiting in limbo. Floodlights knifed through the downpour as the Silo came into view. Armored towers flanked the approach. Propaganda banners sagged with rain — THE DUKE SEES ALL. STRENGTH THROUGH ORDER. On the dock, [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] waited. He stood broad-shouldered and military hat pulled low over his face, arms folded, smoke curling from a foul roll-up clinging to his lip. His teeth looked like someone had sanded them with rust. As they docked, he didn’t move. “Well well,” he drawled. “If it ain’t the harbor rats come crawlin’ to the palace.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] was off the skiff before it stopped rocking. “If I’d known your ugly-ass mug was the welcome mat, I’d’ve poured acid in my good eye before we rolled out.” Rottwyler stepped forward, and so did Cray. Close. Weapons close. Breath close. “Say it to my face, fishboy,” Rottwyler snarled. “I got orders to let you in — don’t say I got orders to let you leave.” “You think I need your permission to crawl back out of this sewer, you gopher lookin' mother fucker?” Cray growled, stepping right up to Rottwyler. It was seconds from snapping. “Enough.” The voice cut clean through the rain. [[Emily Burton]] emerged from the shadows, heels sharp on wet stone, a Loyalist aide holding a black umbrella over her like a halo. Jet-black coat, crimson gloves, golden-banded hat. Regal and razor-sharp. She didn’t look at Rottwyler. “Sergeant, fall back before your insecurity soils the floor.” His jaw clenched. He obeyed. [[Emily Burton|Emily]] turned to [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], eyes cool and unreadable. “Captain Bonetooth. A pleasure. I’m [[Emily Burton|Emily Burton]], Duchess of [[Ashmoor]]. I’ll be escorting you from here.” “Didn’t realize royalty still rowed out in the rain,” Lyla said. “Only when the company promises to be more interesting than those inside...” She turned. “Follow me. Let’s not keep the Grand Duke waiting.”
The corridor stretched on like the gullet of some great beast — stone too polished, sconces too golden, air too still. [[Emily Burton|Emily]] led them in silence, her umbrella now carried like a blade under one arm. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] walked just behind her, flanked by [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]], [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]], and [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]. No one spoke until Emily glanced sideways, her voice low. “You handle your crew well. Most men in your place would’ve let that pissing match with Rottwyler spiral.” “If I wanted to watch two dogs hump over turf, I’d visit Gutter Row,” Lyla replied dryly. Emily smiled faintly. “Then we share taste. And patience.” They passed under a heavy iron arch flanked by twin statues of the Duke in battle gear. Emily’s tone shifted—softer, deliberate. “You don’t like being here. But let me offer you something that might dull the edge.” Lyla’s eye narrowed. “Gonna tell me the Duke’s really a kind soul under all that blood and bullshit?” Emily laughed, quiet and real. “No. He’s exactly what he looks like, almost to a fault. But the world is uglier than he is. And sometimes... order is better than chaos, Captain.” Lyla didn’t answer. Her boots echoed hollowly in the silence that followed. They reached a set of towering black iron doors inlaid with gold filigree. Emily stopped. “This is where I leave you. Raynar will take it from here. Try not to look too amused — he hates that.” “Appreciate the walk, Duchess,” Lyla said. “You might not after what he asks of you.” Emily turned and strode away, her heels clicking in final punctuation. The doors opened. Inside was marble and velvet, propaganda screens flickering gently like coals. The Raiders were ushered into a waiting chamber. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] muttered, arms crossed. “Feels like a goddamn museum where the exhibits watch you.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] murmured, “They don’t like that we don’t bow.” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] added, “They don’t like that we’re breathing.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said nothing. Just stared at the velvet portraits, at the golden busts, at the rot hidden under the polish. Finally, [[Raynar Ventura]] arrived. Thin smile, ash-grey Loyalist uniform crisp enough to cut glass. “Captain Bonetooth. Apologies for the delay. The Duke is ready.” The Raiders followed him into a hall of black stone and mounted skulls. And at its end — seated behind a table of iron, a fireplace casting flickers across his tailored white suit — sat [[The Duke]]. “Ah… the infamous [[Rustwater Raiders]]. Salt-stained, smoke-slick, and somehow still standing. Welcome to [[Ashmoor]].” “Thank you, My Duke but we didn’t come for the tour,” said [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], cool and clear. He offered them seats. They didn’t move. [[The Duke]] smiled like a wolf with a napkin. “I have a transport that requires discretion. From the east wing docks to the [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] Docks in [[Steeltown]]. No flags. No questions.” “What kind of cargo?” Clinton asked, eyes narrowed.

NOTE TITLE: [[02 - Ghosts On The Waves]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/lyladuke.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/Lyla Bonetooth","character/The Duke","character/Blacktide Cray","character/Clinton Firebay","character/Sgt. Rottwyler","character/Emily Burton"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter2"],"date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Summoned to The Silo for a secret job, Lyla Bonetooth discovers her “prisoner” is a chain gang of slaves, forcing her to choose between loyalty and rebellion aboard the Black Marauder, all while Prophet Veerah glimpses a terrifying future that threatens to eclipse them all.","created":"2025/05/22 13:53:04","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:07"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) “What kind of cargo?” Clinton asked, eyes narrowed. “Prisoners,” said [[The Duke]]. “Dangerous. Important. But not ones I trust in Loyalist hands.” Lyla’s head tilted. “If they’re prisoners, why not take them to [[Coffin Island]]?” “Because I’m not locking them up,” The Duke said smoothly. “I’m moving them. Somewhere useful.” Zadie’s voice was a knife in the quiet. “Then what are they?” “They’re not citizens. They’re not registered. They’re currency.” Lyla’s face went blank. “They’re slaves.” The Duke didn’t blink. “Call it what you like. I call it necessity. Tribucia runs on steel, coal, and silence — and all three cost more than the markets can bear. The mines beneath [[Grave Bay]] would collapse without labor. The factories in [[Ashmoor]] would go dark without hands. These aren’t innocent bystanders, Captain. They’re prisoners. Criminals. And the rest? The rest sold themselves — families too poor to eat, fathers trying to buy medicine, mothers promised a better life for their children. They signed their names. I just keep the books balanced.” He rose, swirling amber liquid in a glass, voice low and deliberate. “You want to see a world without this? You’ll be knee-deep in chaos, raiders tearing apart grain caravans, mercs hijacking fuel rigs. Order requires sacrifice. Painful, yes. But necessary. If you care about stability, about keeping what's left of civilization from collapsing into another fire, then you already understand.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]]’s voice cut clean through the quiet. “Everybody in this room knows slavery gets exploited in Disgraceland. You can dress it up in policy and necessity, but we all know what it is. Chains. Collars. Flesh sold to grease the gears.” The Duke studied Lyla for a moment, wondering if it's worth his time and effort continuing this conversation.  “The Wrecking Crew doesn’t allow slaves in Steeltown, anyway.” Lyla said. “If you drop off a ship full of slaves on their shores, they're gonna take that as a direct insult. You sure you wanna do that?” “Which is why I’m not using Loyalists,” he replied. “I’m using you. Raiders. Shadows.” "Who would be stupid enough to smuggle slaves into Steeltown?" Lyla wondered. The Duke was beginning to get annoyed with this conversation. "Who the purchaser is - is of none of your concern, Miss Bonetooth..." "Captain." "What?" "My name is Captain Bonetooth." Lyla’s jaw flexed. “And if we refuse?” The Duke leaned back. “Then I find someone worse. Someone messier. If you care about these people, Captain… you’ll make sure they get there alive.” He listed terms: no interference for a year. Full access to Dead Waters. Slugs enough to last. The Duke shook hands with Lyla and the rest as they exited, pondering his offer. “You’ll be given route coordinates and slugs. Once received, the job is accepted,” [[Raynar Ventura|Ventura]] added as they left. “No renegotiation. No cancellation.” “Yeah, we got the message,” Cray muttered. Outside, the cargo waited. [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] marched forward with guards and prisoners. Chains clinked. Mud-soaked figures shivered in the rain — old men, scarred women, hollow-eyed children. One girl, maybe seven, looked up and locked eyes with Lyla. She didn’t cry. She didn’t speak. Just stared. Lyla’s breath hitched — sharp as a blade. And she said nothing.
The cutter slipped through the fog like a knife beneath skin, the Black Marauder looming ahead, waiting in grim silence. On the bridge, the air was thick with tension, the kind that made even the instruments feel too loud. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stood at the forward window, arms crossed tight against her chest. Rain trickled down the glass. Behind her, the crew gathered in knots — pacing, arguing, barely containing the storm building between them. [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] was the first to speak, voice tight with fury. “Slave running is cursed. We do this, we're gonna anger the Ember Saint. That ain’t cargo out there — it’s people.” [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]] nodded, arms folded. “Told ya it smelled wrong. Felt it in the water. Always trust the sea over a damn invitation from Satan himself.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] slammed his fist against the railing. “Screw the slugs. I ain't no filthy fuckin’ slave-runner. Let the Duke choke on his own mess.” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] kept his voice measured, but only just. “And then what? We turn and run? You think he won’t come after us? You think he doesn’t own half the damn ocean?” “Then let him come!” Cray barked. “Prick's already raising taxes on rations, fuel, repairs — everything. He’s begging for war.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] stepped forward, calm but sharp. “There’s more at stake than our pride here. We screw this up loud, and we’re painting targets on every refugee dock from here to Gutter Row.” Cray turned to her, disbelief flaring. “So we lie down? Pretend we didn’t see the chains?” Clinton cut in. “We play it smart. We take the job. We move the cargo. Then we flip the board when the time’s right. Slaves don’t stay free if we’re dead in the water.” A clang echoed from the stairwell. [[Silas Vayne|Silas]] stepped in, shaking off rain, lighting a cigarette with a hand that didn’t tremble. “Lot of noise in here for pirates,” he said. “Look. I get it. Nobody likes it. But those slaves? They ain’t ours. Not our fight, not our problem. Slugs are. And they’ll buy more freedom than outrage ever will.” Darius snapped, “You hear yourself? Talking like they’re sacks of grain.” Silas shrugged. “Grain don’t scream. That’s the problem.” Cray stepped toward him, fists curling. “So what, just ditch ‘em somewhere and keep the slugs? That’s low even for you.” Silas didn’t move. “You wanna save the world, be my guest. Just don’t sink this ship doing it.” Zadie moved between them. No words — just presence. A quiet barrier. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] hadn’t moved. She was staring out into the rain, but not seeing it.

Rottwyler","character/Emily Burton"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter2"],"date":"6th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"Summoned to The Silo for a secret job, Lyla Bonetooth discovers her “prisoner” is a chain gang of slaves, forcing her to choose between loyalty and rebellion aboard the Black Marauder, all while Prophet Veerah glimpses a terrifying future that threatens to eclipse them all.","created":"2025/05/22 13:53:04","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:07"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ##### FLASHBACK: A girl, maybe nine, crouched in the alley’s filth, cradling her younger sister beneath the overhang of a broken roof. The younger girl’s breath hitched in quiet sobs, face buried against the older one’s chest. Rain ran down their faces like tears not yet earned. The air stank of smoke and spoiled fish, and the sound of boots on wet stone sent both girls still. Shouting broke the quiet. A man’s voice — gruff, angry — and then two more, barking commands. The alley’s mouth filled with shadows. Figures surged forward, grabbing, wrenching. The older girl screamed as rough hands tore her away. Fingers scraped desperately down her sister’s back, trying to hold on, nails drawing blood. The younger one wailed — high, raw, animal. The last thing Lyla saw before the wagon door slammed shut was her sister’s outstretched arms, too small to stop anything. She ran. She ran until her chest burned and her feet bled, chasing the wagon’s ghost through curling mist. But the fog swallowed it all. Her legs finally gave way. She dropped to her knees in the gutter, broken and breathless, the scream still clawing at her throat. ##### NOW: [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]]’s voice, quiet but unshakeable, cut through the chaos. “We sail as planned. But we don’t make delivery.” The room stilled. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] was first to ask. “Where, then?” She turned to face them, face set like iron. “Somewhere the Wrecking Crew’ll see us coming.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] stared. “They'll sink us, it's suicide.” “No,” Lyla said. “It’s a signal.” The rain intensified. Zadie moved to Lyla’s side. No salute. No bow. Just a silent stand. Each of them turned inward as the rain drummed harder on the hull. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] busied himself clearing the nav panel, but his thoughts were elsewhere. He was weighing outcomes, survival odds, tradeoffs of principle. He had always been the tactician. And now? He was trying to convince himself this wasn’t suicide — just strategy with soul. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] checked a locker full of flares, fingers twitching, jaw clenched. His anger was volcanic, but under it, fear coiled tight. Not fear of death — fear of becoming something he hated. A slaver. A coward. He grunted and slammed the locker shut. Better to be damned for defiance. [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] double-checked the loadout on her rifle. She moved with precision, but her mind was elsewhere — tracing the look in that little girl's eyes. The quiet plea. Zadie didn’t pray. But in that moment, she came close. [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] worked in the hold, shifting crates with quiet reverence. He hummed a low, mournful tune under his breath — something old, from before the tides swallowed home. Each motion seemed part ritual, part resignation. [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]] ran a cloth over the controls. Slow, methodical. He muttered to himself about ghosts and tides and the way steel breathes before a storm. But he didn’t stop. He was too old to pretend there was ever a clean path in this world. [[Silas Vayne|Silas]] leaned in a corner, smoke curling from his lips. He said nothing, watched everything. The edge in his eyes dulled, but not gone. He didn’t believe in heroes. Still didn’t. But something about Lyla’s silence — and that child’s stare — had burrowed under his skin. No one spoke. But each of them, in their own way, was already moving. Not from command. From conviction. On the bridge, Lyla studied the charts. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] joined her, arms crossed. “You sure about this? Wrecking Crew might shoot first, ask questions never.” “[[Jimmy Douglass]] is smart,” she said. “He’ll know we wouldn’t come into their shores all bold unless we had a reason.” Cray frowned. “And what then? They just take the slaves and let us skip away?” Lyla’s eyes locked with his. “Well...yeah.” She folded the chart. The Black Marauder hummed to life. It had begun.
# THE AFTERBURN The sky was ash — not clouded, not storming, just dead. A dull black dome split by silent flashes of red lightning that never struck ground. Beneath it, a city burned. Not all at once. Not in rage. It burned with method, building by building, block by block. Collapsing inward like rotten teeth pulled one by one. Figures moved through the wreckage. Some crawled. Some limped. Some leapt — unnaturally, jaggedly, like puppets torn from tangled wire. They were not men. Not anymore. Twisted limbs of steel and flesh, wires dangling from exposed spines, eyes like shattered glass gleaming with static. One of them slammed through a wall like it was paper. Another dragged what might once have been a person — screaming, struggling — across hot concrete until the screaming stopped. In the distance, a towering thing stumbled through the smoke. It looked almost human. Almost. One half of its face was still skin. The other half was machinery pulsing with erratic red light. Its mouth opened, and something between a siren and a sob burst forth. Electricity danced across the rubble like insects, alive and feeding. And then — silence. [[Prophet Veerah]] woke with a gasp. Not a scream — her breath had no voice left. Her eyes glowed white in the dark, unblinking. Sweat poured down her face. Her veil had slipped from her head, revealing silvered hair plastered to her skin. Her fingers clawed at her bedding, but she didn’t move to rise. The candlelight flickered, shadows writhing like they too had seen the dream. She whispered only once, barely more than a breath: “It’s almost time.” Thunder rolled beyond the walls of the swamp. Something in the dark shifted. And watched.

# Chapter 01: 

#### _Temperday Afternoon, 1st of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

> When the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] brings its blood-soaked spectacle to [[Steeltown]], tensions explode as undefeated champion **[[Bobby Cutman|Bobby “The Iron Bull” Cutman]]** disrespects the crowd, the city, and the **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**. As security duty turns personal, **[[Abel May Jr.]]** steps up and steals the spotlight, triggering a ferocious standoff that nearly ignites a riot. But while the world watches [[Bobby Cutman]] rage, a shadowy offer is made — and behind the scenes, something far more dangerous is watching both men from the dark. Glory, power, and legacy hang in the balance… and in Disgraceland, not every fight ends in the ring.

NOTE TITLE: [[01 - Main Event Shadows]]

METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter1"],"cover":[["zz_media/abevsbob.png"]],"date":"1st of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When the WLL crashes into Steeltown, undefeated champ “The Iron Bull” Bobby Cutman sparks chaos with his insults, drawing Abel May Jr. into a volatile showdown that masks a darker threat lurking behind the spectacle","created":"2025/05/22 15:16:45","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:02"}

NOTE BLOCK CONTENT:

(cont'd) #### MAIN EVENT SHADOWS

The smoke hung low in [[Steeltown]].

Furnace Square, an old foundry turned death circus for the day in [[STEELTOWN#Barton|Barton]], vibrated with noise and sweat. Cracked concrete stretched between towering smokestacks. Bleachers—welded from scrap and desperation—shook under the weight of a feverish crowd. Rusted banners flapped like tattered war flags, the sigil of [[World Lucha Libre]] glowing faint red from a makeshift stage.

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stood with his arms crossed, sunglasses catching the flicker of stage pyros. He looked pissed just to be alive. Over the comms, a familiar voice broke the static.

"Ain't even noon and I already hate everyone here," [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] muttered.

"Hate it all you want, brother," [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] replied, calm as a man nursing whiskey on a Sunday. "Pay's better than a bounty run. Just keep the fighters from killin' each other before the bell."

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] scoffed. "Glorified blueshirts."

[[Katie Kowalski|Kowalski]] chimed in from her sniper’s perch above the square. "Broken Tower, twelve o'clock. Someone just dropped a flare."

"That was me," came [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]]'s voice, cheerful and unconcerned. "I get why you always tell me to keep the safety on. Lotta people starin’ at me now. Lotta people."

Then came the squeal of loudspeakers. Flames erupted skyward. Music erupted. The crowd answered in kind—a full-throated roar that echoed through the steel bones of the city.

[[Flint Garritt]] walked on stage like a snake oil messiah. His coat glinted with silver threads, gloves pristine, voice smooth as old bourbon.

"WELCOME," he called, arms outstretched, "to the HEART of HARD LIVING. To the fire pit of the East. To the belly of the beast—[[Steeltown]]!"

Cheers. Flares. Fists in the air. [[Steeltown]] howled back.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] paced like a preacher. "I'd like to thank our esteemed mayor, Mr. [[Ellis Westmount]], for hosting this event today as we travel around the great territories of Tribucia. The [[World Lucha Libre]] ain't just a sport. It's survival. It's blood and glory and truth—and TONIGHT... we're promotin' the fight of the decade!"

He paused, letting the tension build, then dropped the name: "BIG TITAN [[Bastian Redd]]!"

Smoke parted. The canyon king emerged.

Shirtless, painted ochre across the chest, a red pouch swinging from his neck, [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] moved like a carved monument given breath. On his way to the stage, he paused beside [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]].

"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]," he said with a nod.

[[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] nodded back. "Good luck out there, big man."

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] grunted. "Don't let him make you a headline."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] climbed the steps and took the mic. His voice rumbled low, reverent.

"[[Steeltown]]. You feel that? That stillness? That breath before the storm? That’s the land holdin’ still, waitin’ on the Final Reckoning. Not just the match. The moment."

He turned, facing the crowd. "[[Bobby Cutman]]—you wear that belt like it's carved into your chest. Undefeated. But we both know you bled. They saw me drag you to the edge. This third one? There ain’t no more questions. This ain't about gold. This is legacy. You call yourself The Iron Bull? Then charge. Just know—I eat bull for lunch."

The crowd erupted.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] grinned like a man who'd lit the fuse and stepped back. "And now," he drawled, "the REIGNING, UNDEFEATED, UNDISPUTED CHAMPION... [[Bobby Cutman|Bobby “The Iron Bull” Cutman]]!"

A low rumble from backstage. Then—he came.

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] stomped out, taped fists swinging, belt slung over his shoulder like a crown too heavy to share. He didn't wave. Didn't nod. He seized the moment by the throat.

He snatched the mic. His voice dripped venom.

"[[Steeltown]] jerkin' itself off over a ghost story," he growled. "Over a man who couldn’t finish the job. Newsflash, big man: **Almost** don’t make legends. Almost don’t keep my name stuck in your damn mouth."

He pointed to the crowd. "Y'all tattoo L’s on your neck and call it culture. You dress up rust and call it tradition. You cheer for the underdog not 'cause you believe—they never win—but because you wanna feel brave without ever takin' the hit yourselves. You're all spectators to your own misery."

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] paced the stage, snarling. "And you—[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]—what the fuck even are you? A rent-a-cop militia with daddy issues and dollar-store tattoos? You stand around lookin' hard 'cause deep down, you know you ain't ever gonna matter past these city limits."

He turned back to the audience, voice rising. "And [[Steeltown]]? City of rust, rats, and regrets. You pile your broken dreams in stacks, burn 'em for warmth, and call it living. Newsflash: the rest of us ain't lookin' at you to lead—they're laughin' at you."

His gaze locked on [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]. "And you, big canyon king? You're the mascot of the first settlers? You wanna talk legacy? The only thing you'll leave behind is a crater where your pride used to be. Final Reckoning? You're goddamn right it is. And I'm not just takin' your body—I’m takin’ your myth. I'm gonna leave your name in the dust with all these other wannabes."

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] raised a taped fist, extending his middle finger, veins bulging. "I'm the Iron Bull. I don't fight for fame. I fight to END people. And Final Reckoning? I end you and the legacy of your pathetic people."

The air cracked. [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] lunged. Security moved.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] shouted, "Save it for the ring, gentlemen!"

But the crowd had caught fire. Trash cans overturned. Flares shot up. The chant began: **[[STEELTOWN]]! [[STEELTOWN]]!**

The Wrecking Crew members advanced onto the stage. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] walked up to [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] and gently put his arms on the big man's chest, holding him back.

NOTE TITLE: [[01 - Main Event Shadows]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter1"],"cover":[["zz_media/abevsbob.png"]],"date":"1st of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When the WLL crashes into Steeltown, undefeated champ “The Iron Bull” Bobby Cutman sparks chaos with his insults, drawing Abel May Jr. into a volatile showdown that masks a darker threat lurking behind the spectacle","created":"2025/05/22 15:16:45","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:02"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) The Wrecking Crew members advanced onto the stage. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] walked up to [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] and gently put his arms on the big man's chest, holding him back. "Get your fuckin' hands off me, boy!" [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] roared as he shoved [[Jimmy Douglass]] hard to the ground. In an instant, [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stepped forward. He moved onto the stage like a storm in boots. Both Cutman and Redd gave Abel room. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] watched him for a moment and snorted, "What’re you supposed to be? The best this shithole’s got? You best stop eyein’ me like that, boy." He dropped the belt with a thud. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] slowly reached up and removed his sunglasses. Then, without looking, he hurled them into the crowd. The place went nuclear. [[Jimmy Douglass]] slowly rose to his feet, eyes locked on the confrontation. Everyone in the audience knows Abel May Jr. and they went wild for their hometown boy. They went forehead to forehead. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] sneered. "You got somethin' to say boy, or—" [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] snatched the mic. No theatrics. Just grit. "For once in your miserable life, shut the fuck up and listen. This is [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] country. And in [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] country... men who walk in thinkin’ they’re better than us leave on their fuckin’ knees." The eruption was instant. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] lunged. But the tide hit faster: [[Katie Kowalski|Kowalski]]. [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]]. [[Blueforce]]. Security. The ring swallowed them both. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] screamed as he was dragged off the stage. "You DEAD, motherfucker! I’ll put your fuckin’ body in the ground!" [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] didn’t move. Just watched. Didn’t even blink.
The crowd’s roar hadn’t even begun to fade when the violence began to simmer beneath the surface. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] fought like a man drowning—swinging wild against security, elbows landing, feet stomping. Plastic chairs clattered to the ground as [[Blueforce]] officers surged to surround him. [[Katie Kowalski|Kowalski]] had her rifle in hand, but the safety stayed on. Barely. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stood center stage, unmoved. His chest rose slow, unbothered. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] was chaos incarnate, teeth bared, screaming across the distance. “You DEAD, you jacked-up motherfucker!” [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] bellowed, spittle flying. “You think you made a statement? All you did was put a goddamn target on your back! You ain't no legend, you're a glorified security guard with a death wish! You don't belong in my ring, you belong under it—like the rest of this sewer city!” He thrashed against the grip of two guards, muscles flexing like steel cables. “This your hero, Steeltown? This your fuckin’ messiah? I’ll break him in front of you. I’ll drag his sorry ass around the ring by his fuckin’ dreadlocks and leave his teeth in the mat!” The veins in his neck bulged as he roared toward the crowd. “You rats cheerin’ for Wreckin’ Crew? Bunch of washed-up tough guys who couldn’t even make it in the minors. You got the nerve to stare me down like you got a chance? You fuckin’ worms. I’ll stomp your whole little street crew into the concrete and piss on your scrapheap bar after I’m done!” Then, turning his rage back to Abel, he spat the final blow: “You just made the worst fuckin’ mistake of your life. You don’t get to challenge a god and walk away. You get to watch everything you love BURN.” Two guards wrestled him back. One caught a fist to the gut. Another crumpled from a headbutt. [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] emerged from the curtains like a conductor walking into a storm. He leaned in close, just behind [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]]'s shoulder, voice low and smooth. Whatever he said worked, as [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] took one last look at Abel May then walked backstage. "That’s enough, champ,” [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] said evenly, slipping between bodies. “Save it for the cameras. You just guaranteed every home in Steeltown will be watching. Good job, big man.” [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] glared, nostrils flared, eyes bloodshot. He let the tension snap out in a shudder, chest heaving like a bellows, almost bull-like. Backstage, the Wrecking Crew was already in motion. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] walked with purpose, flanked by [[Katie Kowalski|Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]], and [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]]. They passed the holding tent where [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] was still being restrained. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] saw them—saw [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]]—and tried to surge forward again. A guard caught an elbow to the throat. Another got kicked square in the knee before he was swarmed by more Blueforce holding him back. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stopped. Turned. Met [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]]'s glare with a small smirk. “That’s two times today you got saved by the Blueshirts,” he said, calm as steel. [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] exploded again, bellowing like an animal. He was hauled back like a dog straining at the leash. He growled as [[Jimmy Douglass]] stopped. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] turned, voice like gravel. “You’re lucky Abel stepped in before I got up, you know? Cause I’d have slapped the taste out your fuckin’ mouth for touchin’ me.” [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] roared something unintelligible, drowning in his own fury. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] didn’t wait around for more. They walked off like men who’d just won a war they didn’t ask for. The crowd? Still howling. And somewhere in the back of it all, deep behind the noise and the rage, [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] smiled.
The Wrecking Crew clubhouse pulsed with heat and laughter. The air smelled of beer, smoke, and old leather—Steeltown perfume. Bottles clinked, pool balls cracked, boots scraped concrete. [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]] held court at the center, his voice loud and theatrical.

NOTE TITLE: [[01 - Main Event Shadows]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","story","chapter1"],"cover":[["zz_media/abevsbob.png"]],"date":"1st of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When the WLL crashes into Steeltown, undefeated champ “The Iron Bull” Bobby Cutman sparks chaos with his insults, drawing Abel May Jr. into a volatile showdown that masks a darker threat lurking behind the spectacle","created":"2025/05/22 15:16:45","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:02"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) "And this mountain-ass motherfucker just throws his shades into the crowd," [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]] boomed. "... and Cutman stares at Abe like he's lookin at [[El Santo]] and [[El Santo]] had better traps than him." The room howled. [[Rodney Blythe]], beer in hand, slapped the bar top. [[Mark Jeffrey]] held up his drink, his grin wide and careless. [[Selena Matissao]], sitting beside him, didn’t toast so much as leaned a bit closer to Mark, brushing his shoulder with hers, smiling sideways at her boys. It wasn’t just noise—it was connection. That rare kind of bond forged from years of near-deaths, busted knuckles, and shared silences. People who'd bled together and knew how to laugh about it afterward. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] felt it in the room like a heartbeat under the floorboards. A home where the walls didn't need to be pretty, just strong. Abel sat there smiling at his friends. "To [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]]—our brick wall," someone shouted. "To Abel!" the room echoed, loud enough to rattle the old HVAC unit. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] just nodded, sipping from a battered glass, eyes heavy-lidded but tracking everything. He gave a small nod, then stood. "Appreciate it, Crew. Gonna get some air." He rose slowly and stepped outside.
The alley behind the clubhouse was all cracked pavement and rusted fences. A barrel fire crackled low, spitting sparks at the stars. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] lit a cigarette and leaned against the wall, shoulders relaxing slightly. Then came the shift. A presence. A flicker of motion in the dark. His hand dropped to his belt. "Oh my man, you picked the wrong fuckin’ night," he said. [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] emerged from shadow, hands clasped behind his back like a schoolmaster. He smiled like a man offering poison in a chalice. "If it was a fight I wanted, I’d have brought cameras." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] didn’t move but sighed lightly. Smoke curled from his lip. "Say your piece, suit." [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] stepped closer, unfazed. "You didn’t steal the spotlight tonight, Abel. You became it. Whether you meant to or not, you just became a household name across Tribucia." He pulled a folded document from his coat and handed it out. "Standard contract. WLL. Full run. Main card. Your name in lights, your fists on syndication. The crowd chants your name, and the payout? Real enough to retire every Crew vet you’ve ever called brother...if you win." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] took it. Didn’t open it. "I ain't one to fight for show." [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] raised an eyebrow. "Then don’t. Fight for respect. Fight for your crew. Hell, fight just to shut [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] the fuck up. You’ve already got the people. All you need now… is the walk. And you and I both know you have it." [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] watched [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] moving like a snake. "It's legit, Mr May. No tricks. I saw a star today. I saw a lot of untapped potential in you." He gave a small nod, turning back to shadow. "You’ve got until the [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] vs. [[Bastian Redd|Redd]] fight. Come as my personal guest. Ringside seat. Name stitched into the leather." And with that, [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] vanished into the dark, leaving only the smoke and the sound of a slow-burning city. [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stood silent, watching the ember tip of his cigarette glow in the dark. The contract flapped lightly in the breeze. He didn’t look at it. Not yet.
# THE AFTERBURN **Earlier that day.** From the rooftops above the chaos, the chants of “STEELTOWN! STEELTOWN!” echoed like distant thunder. Flares hissed in the air. The world below burned with human heat—rage, pride, and spectacle. Two figures stood apart from it all. [[Hella]] leaned against a rusted girder, arms crossed, the glare of a magnesium flare briefly painting her pale features in white light. "Men and their stupid firecracker egos," she muttered, voice flat, unimpressed. “This is what they cheer for? This is what they live for?” [[Ora Razchek]] stood beside her, silent and still. He didn’t watch the match—he watched the men. His eyes tracked [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] and [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] like a scientist noting lab rats under stress. “It keeps them distracted,” Ora replied. His voice was quiet, dangerous. “Pre-occupied, you know? Until the real work begins.” A beat passed. Just long enough for the wind to shift. [[Hella]] spat into the dust. “Which one do you want?” [[Ora Razchek]] didn’t answer with words. He smiled—tight-lipped and cold. He nodded toward the man still standing, still unmoved, even as the ring was consumed by screaming fans and frantic security. "The big one." Below, [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stared down [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] like a statue in a storm. And far above them, two shadows watched as the first thread was pulled. A flare exploded overhead. The sky blinked red. The shadows deepened.
