147.title: Riley Thorne
147.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Riley Thorne]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_riley.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Protector of [[Prophet Veerah]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","stealth","assassin","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:53"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_riley.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Protector of [[Prophet Veerah]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - stealth - assassin - mirella - chapter5 --- # RILEY THORNE > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[riley.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Widow Blade **Alias/Nickname:** Ghost Knife **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Known in whispers only **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** Approx. mid-20s **Height:** 5'6" **Weight:** 120 lbs. **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Stealth operative, assassin **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], other Widows **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"Some people were born to fight. I was born to disappear."

Riley Thorne’s life was marked by loss before she could fully understand it. Born to a scavenger mother in the decaying wastelands of Disgraceland, she spent her earliest years rummaging through the bones of the old world. Her mother, fierce and resourceful, did her best to shield Riley from the brutal reality of the Duke’s rule. But no one could stay hidden forever. When Riley was just ten, her mother was captured and publicly executed by the Duke’s enforcers for stealing from one of the regime’s supply convoys. The image of her mother’s lifeless body swinging from the gallows burned into Riley’s memory, igniting a hatred that never cooled. Alone and afraid, Riley learned to survive by vanishing into the shadows. The ruins of the past became her refuge — broken concrete towers and rusted steel skeletons offering concealment. She scavenged scraps of food and salvaged discarded tools, slowly honing her skills. Over the years, whispers of rebellion reached her ears. Small pockets of resistance, desperate to overthrow the Duke, began to stir. By her late teens, Riley had aligned herself with one such group, using her stealth and cunning to sabotage supply lines and strike fear into the regime. But her actions earned her powerful enemies. During a high-stakes assassination attempt on one of the Duke’s top commanders, Riley was captured and left for dead, her body battered and broken. Yet death did not claim her. It was Veerah, enigmatic leader of the Unseen Widows, who found Riley on the brink of her end. Under Veerah’s care, Riley recovered. The Widows offered her something she hadn't known since her mother’s death — a family. With them, she became a weapon of silent vengeance. Her skill with daggers and short blades grew unmatched, and her ability to move unseen became legendary. Though she serves the Widows with loyalty, a lingering doubt remains. While Veerah’s visions guide the faction’s every step, Riley cannot shake the unease that comes with blind faith. She remains stoic and guarded, her heart still burdened by the weight of the past. Despite the blood she has spilled, there is still a spark of compassion within her. Riley fiercely protects her sisters in the Widows, seeing reflections of herself in the broken women Veerah has gathered. But as tensions rise in Disgraceland and the Duke’s hold tightens, Riley finds herself at a crossroads. Vengeance once defined her, but now she questions whether there is more to fight for. The path forward is uncertain, but one truth remains — Riley Thorne is not done surviving. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Riley is cold on the outside, simmering beneath with quiet intensity. She speaks little, listens much, and watches always. Distrustful by nature, she trusts only those who've bled beside her. Her loyalty, once earned, is absolute — but rarely given. **Vices:** Sleeplessness. Nightmares keep her awake, and when they don’t, she refuses rest out of guilt. She sharpens her blades obsessively, a ritual of control. Distrusts comfort. **Abilities:** Elite stealth operative. Master of knives and short blades. Can vanish in plain sight. Deep intuition for traps, movement, and enemy intent. Skilled in sabotage and infiltration. **Secrets:** Doesn’t fully believe in Veerah’s visions — and sometimes thinks about leaving. Still keeps a piece of her mother’s scarf hidden in her gear. **Beliefs:** Faith in Mirella, but more as metaphor than god. Believes in survival. In sisterhood. In making the powerful bleed. ## Role In Disgraceland Riley Thorne serves as one of the Widows' deadliest field agents — their silent blade, sent when the mission calls for precision, patience, and vanishing without a trace. She does not preach. She does not lead. She kills. And yet her actions hold weight among the Widows, especially the younger ones who look to her as proof that survival and strength are possible after tragedy. Where Veerah brings faith, Riley brings grit. Where Veerah inspires awe, Riley inspires caution. She is the shadow to the Prophet’s light — unseen, but always there.

148.title: Raina & Risa
148.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Raina & Risa]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_randr.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","twins","assassins","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:48"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_randr.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - twins - assassins - mirella - chapter5 --- # RAINA & RISA > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[randr.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Twin Blades of the Widows **Alias/Nickname:** The Sisters, The Split Curse **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Feared; spoken of like urban legends **Gender:** Female (identical twins) **Spouse:** None **Age:** Early 20s **Height:** 5'5" **Weight:** 118 lbs. each **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Twin assassins **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], [[Riley Thorne]], [[Nita Blackbird]], each other **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“You can’t kill what moves in two places at once.”

Raina and Risa were born into the unforgiving wastes of Disgraceland, twin daughters of a wandering trader and a mother who died before their third birthday. From their earliest days, the sisters were inseparable, bound by the unspoken understanding that survival meant staying together. Their father led a nomadic life, navigating the scorched remnants of the old world, bartering stolen scraps and scavenged goods. It wasn’t a life of comfort, but it was a life. That life ended the day their caravan crossed paths with the Duke’s enforcers. Accused of trading contraband and withholding supplies, their father was executed without trial. The twins were dragged away, separated, and sold into servitude. For years, they endured lives of torment — Raina forced into hard labor, Risa into the twisted entertainment of the Duke’s wealthy allies. But even apart, the sisters’ bond never broke. They clung to the hope of finding one another, whispering silent promises beneath the stars. When the time came, they made good on those promises. Raina escaped first, slaughtering a guard with a jagged scrap of metal. Risa’s liberation followed soon after, her captors falling to the ruthless precision of a stolen dagger. Reunited and stained with the blood of their tormentors, the sisters fled into the night. They were no longer victims — they were vengeance made flesh. It was Veerah who found them next, drawn by the shadows they left in their wake. The Unseen Widows offered them sanctuary and purpose. Raina, fierce and unrelenting, became a master of close-quarters combat, wielding her blades with ruthless efficiency. Risa, calculating and precise, embraced the art of silent death, her throwing stars finding their mark without fail. Together, they are a force of nature — twin specters feared even among the Duke’s most hardened enforcers. Though bound by their loyalty to the Widows, the sisters remain wary of Veerah’s unwavering belief in her visions. Unlike some of their sisters, Raina and Risa do not follow blindly. They follow each other. The world has taken everything from them, but as long as they stand side by side, the sisters of the Unseen Widows will never be broken. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Raina is raw fire — quick to strike, blunt, and driven by instinct. Risa is the cooling shadow — calm, clever, and dangerously observant. Together, they form a perfect balance of chaos and precision. They speak in unison when they wish to intimidate, but often communicate without words at all. **Vices:** They don't sleep unless the other is watching. Both suffer from fragmented nightmares, often reliving their separate captivities. Raina breaks things when angry. Risa journals in code no one else understands. **Abilities:** Raina is a brutal melee fighter — excels in confined combat, knife work, and disarming enemies with speed and strength. Risa specializes in ranged precision, poisons, and stealth infiltration. Together, they perform tandem attacks that overwhelm opponents before they understand what’s happening. **Secrets:** Each keeps scars the other has never asked about. Risa knows one of her captors still lives, and she hasn’t told Raina. Raina sometimes wonders if they'd survive being separated again — and dreads the answer. **Beliefs:** They believe in each other before anything else. Their faith in Mirella is quiet, ritualistic, and mostly tied to Veerah's influence — but they follow the Widow creed as long as it aligns with their bond. ## Role In Disgraceland Raina and Risa are among the most feared Widows in the field. Their synchronized tactics make them nearly impossible to counter — one distracts, the other kills. They are often deployed for missions requiring shock value, disruption, and psychological warfare. Their presence alone is enough to cause panic among Loyalist ranks. Though they outwardly serve Veerah, their true allegiance has always been to each other. To lose one would be to lose both — and if that ever happens, Disgraceland may tremble.

149.title: Prophet Veerah
149.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Prophet Veerah]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_veerah.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Prophet, Head of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","protagonist","widow","prophet","main","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:44"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_veerah.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: Prophet, Head of the [[Unseen Widows]] chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - protagonist - widow - prophet - main - mirella - chapter5 --- # PROPHET VEERAH > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[veerah.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Prophet and Head of the [[Unseen Widows]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Prophet **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Unknown **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** Widowed **Age:** Unknown **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 133 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Prophet cult leader **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Riley Thorne]] [[Len Vyne]] [[Nita Blackbird]] **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“The stars don’t scream. They whisper. And if you’re foolish enough to ignore them… they burn.”

Veerah was once no different from the countless forgotten souls of Disgraceland — another survivor scraping by in a world that had long since abandoned hope. But everything changed the night the visions began. Dreams of fragmented moments, distant faces, and twisted landscapes plagued her sleep. At first, she thought them the fevered remnants of hunger and exhaustion. But when those dreams started to unfold in reality — each detail as precise as she had seen — Veerah knew she had been touched by something far beyond comprehension. She called it a gift, though whether it was a blessing or a curse remains uncertain. In a world shattered by war and ruin, certainty is a rare commodity. Yet Veerah’s followers see her as a prophet, a vessel for divine truth. To them, her dreams are the whispered will of a higher power. The Unseen Widows formed around her, not merely as warriors but as devoted disciples. They believe every word that passes Veerah’s lips, seeing her as a guiding light in the perpetual darkness of Disgraceland. But Veerah is no mere oracle. Beneath the gilded tiara that crowns her golden hair is a mind sharpened by hardship. Before the Widows, she was a ghost, moving through the shadows, mastering the art of silent death. She learned the value of patience — the perfect kill is never rushed. Every flicker of light, every shifting shadow, became her allies. Now, she passes these lessons to her sisters, transforming them into assassins that strike without warning. They wear their veils and black garb like armor, their beauty a weapon as sharp as any blade. Veerah teaches them to use the desires of others to their advantage, understanding that seduction is as deadly as steel. Despite her growing legend, there are whispers of doubt that even Veerah cannot silence. Each vision takes its toll, leaving her exhausted and frayed. She claims to hear the voice of a higher being, but in the stillness of the night, she sometimes wonders if the voice is merely her own. The Widows know nothing of her uncertainty — to them, she is infallible. Yet the burden of prophecy weighs heavy. Every life taken by her word, every drop of blood spilled in her name, carves a deeper wound within her soul. Still, Veerah remains resolute. The Duke’s tyranny cannot go unanswered, and Disgraceland’s suffering will not endure forever. Whether her path is righteous or not, she will follow her visions until the end. And when the time comes, the Widows will be ready — their hands steady, their blades sharp, and their faith unwavering. For to defy Veerah is to defy fate itself. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Veerah is poised and enigmatic, radiating an eerie calm even in chaos. She’s introspective, deliberate, and unshakably confident in public — yet harbors private doubts she shares with no one. Her voice is soft, her words carry weight, and her silence says even more. > [!infobox] > > ![[veerah preach.png|260]] **Vices:** Keeps her pain to herself, refusing rest or comfort. Addicted to control — not power, but control. Occasionally indulges in rare, potent opiates to silence the visions **Abilities:** Vivid, often traumatic visions of the future; always accurate. Trained in silent movement, blade work, and psychological warfare. Inspires unwavering loyalty and obedience in her followers **Secrets:** She is no longer sure if the voice in her dreams is divine… or her own madness **Beliefs:** Her visions are sacred truths, whether from a god, a force, or something else ## Role In Disgraceland Veerah is the leader and prophet of the **Unseen Widows**, a cult-like faction of all-female assassins operating from the Drownlands. Feared, worshipped, and untouchable, she influences events from the shadows, shaping Disgraceland’s future one death at a time. Whether messiah or madwoman, she stands as a symbol of vengeance, destiny, and quiet terror.

150.title: Nita Blackbird
150.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Nita Blackbird]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_nita.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","scout","assassin","mirella"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:38"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_nita.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - scout - assassin - mirella --- # NITA BLACKBIRD > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[nita.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Widow Huntress **Alias/Nickname:** The Tracker **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Respected, quietly feared **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** Late 20s **Height:** 5'8" **Weight:** 135 lbs. **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Hunter, assassin, scout **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], [[Riley Thorne]], other Widows **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"The land remembers. And so do I."

Nita Blackbird was born into a resilient Indigenous community along the remnants of the Sinner's Sea, a people who held on to their traditions even as the world crumbled around them. She was taught to read the land, track game, and endure the harsh realities of a fractured world. Her family believed that survival wasn’t just about strength — it was about remembering who they were. That belief shattered the day the Duke’s enforcers came. They razed her village, claiming it was harboring rebels. Nita’s parents were killed in the slaughter, and her younger brother was dragged away in chains. Left for dead, Nita vowed to one day find him or at least make those responsible pay. For years, she wandered the desolate roads of Disgraceland, surviving through her skills and the whispers of the land. Her fierce reputation eventually caught the attention of the Unseen Widows. Veerah, the enigmatic leader, offered Nita a place among them — not just as a warrior, but as a symbol of retribution. The Widows moved like shadows, assassinating those who served the Duke and liberating those who suffered under his rule. Nita quickly became one of Veerah’s most trusted operatives. Her ruthless efficiency in the field, combined with her quiet compassion for the innocent, earned her respect within the ranks. Despite her loyalty, however, doubt lingers. While Veerah is revered as a prophet, Nita remains skeptical of her visions. The certainty with which Veerah commands the Widows unnerves her. Nita follows orders, but she watches — questioning whether the ends truly justify the means. Her gold bird emblem, stitched over her heart, serves as a reminder of her family and the freedom she fights for. Every mission she undertakes is another step toward avenging the past and preventing others from suffering the same fate. But Nita knows that one day, her loyalty to the Widows and her personal quest for justice may collide. The question is — when that day comes, which path will she choose? --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Nita is stoic, grounded, and fiercely intuitive. She speaks with purpose, rarely wastes breath, and moves through the world like she’s always listening for something most people can’t hear. She is protective, introspective, and commands respect with quiet authority. **Vices:** Obsessively carves notches into her gear — one for every life taken in her pursuit of justice. Refuses to stay in one place for too long. Prone to disappearing for days at a time to "clear her head." **Abilities:** Master tracker and wilderness scout. Exceptional with bows, blades, and snares. Reads terrain and movement like second nature. Knows when she’s being watched. Can move silently for miles. Deeply tuned to her surroundings. **Secrets:** She still believes her brother may be alive — and has followed rumors of him to places even the Widows avoid. Keeps a small carved animal figure from her childhood hidden in her satchel. **Beliefs:** Believes in justice more than vengeance, but often confuses the two. Skeptical of Veerah’s divine gift — she follows her out of loyalty and shared purpose, not blind faith. ## Role In Disgraceland Nita serves as the Unseen Widows' top scout, hunter, and survivalist. When a mission demands traversing dangerous terrain, uncovering hidden camps, or striking from the wilderness, Nita is sent. Her ability to stalk a target unseen across miles of broken country has earned her a ghostlike reputation. Veerah trusts her instincts, even if their beliefs don’t align. Among the Widows, Nita is both a warrior and a guardian — a symbol that there’s still honor in the fight. But her soul is divided, caught between duty to the Widows and a personal promise to a family she may never see again.

151.title: Len Vyne
151.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Len Vyne]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_len.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","defector","assassin","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/05 17:07:55"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_len.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - defector - assassin - mirella - chapter5 --- # LEN VYNE > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[len.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Widow Shade **Alias/Nickname:** The Knife That Smiles **Home Location:** Formerly Ashmoor **Public Reputation:** Ex-Loyalist traitor turned ghost **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** Late 20s or early 30s **Height:** 5'7" **Weight:** 127 lbs. **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Assassin, defector, zealot **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], former Loyalist commanders **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"I heard her speak. And I knew everything else had to die."

**Len Vyne** once wore the black and gray of the **Loyalist Guard**, a rising star in **[[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]]** assigned to strategic recon and field elimination. Cold, efficient, and utterly loyal, she carried out assassinations in the name of the Duke without question. Until the day she crossed paths with a woman in white, veiled in dusk, speaking softly to a crowd of the broken. **Veerah.** Something changed in Len that night. She claimed it wasn't madness or guilt — it was clarity. In Veerah’s voice, she heard not rebellion but truth. A truth so sharp it cut through years of training, doctrine, and blood. That same night, Len vanished from Loyalist records. Her barracks burned. Her commanding officer was found with his throat slit and his eyes removed. Weeks later, she appeared in the Drownlands, dagger in hand, kneeling before Veerah. Since then, **Len has served as one of the most lethal Widows**, a zealot whose devotion borders on religious obsession. She doesn’t kill for coin or politics. She kills for **Veerah**. She believes the Prophet’s visions are law — not prophecy, but premonition. And she’ll do anything to protect the woman who set her soul on fire. Her past as a Loyalist agent makes her dangerous beyond measure. She knows how the Guard thinks. She knows how they *fail*. She’s used every tactic she once taught others to break the back of the very system she helped uphold. To some Widows, she’s an asset. To others, she’s terrifying. To Veerah, she’s proof that even shadows can be reborn in the light. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Len is quiet but intense, often staring through people as if she’s dissecting their soul. She rarely speaks unless it’s about Veerah, and when she does, it sounds like scripture. She follows orders exactly — unless she thinks she knows better. Which she often does. **Vices:** Tattooed a kill tally from her Loyalist days across her ribs — refuses to remove it. Keeps her old uniform folded beneath her Widow garb, as a reminder. Occasionally “disappears” former Guard members she deems irredeemable, without permission. **Abilities:** Elite infiltration, psychological warfare, knowledge of Loyalist formations and tactics. Expert in silent takedowns, blade throwing, and pressure point combat. Can mimic Loyalist command codes to breach secure locations. **Secrets:** She still carries her Loyalist ID tag in a leather pouch around her neck. Talks to it before missions like it’s a penance. Some believe she’s heard Veerah's voice in her dreams — even when the Prophet sleeps soundless. **Beliefs:** Absolute faith in Veerah as a divine instrument. Sees the Faith of Mirella not as a religion but as a *directive*. Believes killing in Veerah’s name is a holy act. ## Role In Disgraceland Len is the Widow that slips through enemy lines before the rest even arrive. Her past as a Loyalist operative gives her insider knowledge that makes her indispensable — and unsettling. She is often dispatched alone, trusted to dismantle Loyalist strongholds from the inside out. To the Widows, she’s both weapon and warning: proof that the Duke's servants can be turned — and turned into nightmares.

## Biography

> “If you step into my market, you play by my math. You don’t like the numbers? Don’t come back.”


**Samson Knight**, known across Gutter Row as **Mr. Knight**, is the commanding leader of [[Third Row]] — the dominant street gang that controls the heart of the [[Three Nail Market]] in [[Vileby]]. A towering, broad-shouldered Black man with a clipped beard and eyes that don’t blink when they should, Samson carries the aura of someone who’s seen the worst and decided to become worse.

Born in a crumbling tenement on Row Three sometime in the 2150s, Samson was raised amid violence, ration lines, and betrayal. His mother worked market tables, his father disappeared during the Charspire riots, and by thirteen Samson was already known as a quiet enforcer who didn’t need to yell to make you fold. He climbed the ranks of the gang as muscle, but when the founders fell — Eddie to a back-alley bullet and Shad to the chaos of the [[Blackshift Massacre]] — he didn’t grieve. He moved.

In the fractured years that followed, when The Third Row splintered into infighting and ruin, Samson played a long game. He killed who he had to. Paid who he couldn’t. And whispered unity until it became law. By 2178, there was no one left to challenge him — not in the gang, not in the market.

Today, Mr. Knight runs the Three Nail Market like a quiet king. He doesn’t yell, doesn’t flinch, and doesn’t forget. He counts slugs by the firelight in the backrooms of bloodstained buildings, surrounded by killers who owe him their lives — or fear losing them.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Calm, calculating, immovable; speaks slowly but hits fast. Keeps control through presence, not theatrics.

**Vices:** 
Money, memory, and power — and maybe a taste for control that goes deeper than business.

**Abilities:** 
Expert at organization, intimidation, and maintaining order through layered fear. Brilliant strategist with unmatched street knowledge of Gutter Row.

**Secrets:** 
Keeps a black-bound book of names — debts owed, promises broken, and things that can't be forgiven. Some say it includes [[The Duke of Disgraceland]].

**Beliefs:** 
Loyalty is earned in blood. Money is the only true voice in Disgraceland. The past is a weapon — sharpen it.

## Role in Disgraceland
Samson Knight is the silent king of the streets, holding together the underworld economy of Gutter Row while ensuring the Three Nail Market stays open, profitable, and absolutely his.

## Biography

> “I don’t need to raise my voice. The room already belongs to me.”

**Sable Marris** grew up on the _rich edge of ruin_ — the daughter of a failed merchant who taught her two things before skipping town: how to count money, and how to count men. She learned to fend for herself early, moving through [[Vileby]]’s backdoor lounges and dust-shack casinos with poise and heat, using words as weapons and silk as armor. But she was never just chasing a man — she was chasing a throne.

Then came **Samson Knight**. She didn’t beg for his attention. She caught it. And held it. What started as mutual amusement turned to something more dangerous: trust.

Sable is the one woman who can speak plainly to Mr. Knight without drawing fire. She doesn’t walk behind him — she walks beside him, dressed to kill and twice as sharp. While the world sees her as a trophy of his empire, those who know better realize: she helps shape it.

Behind the scenes, Sable acts as a silent advisor, an event planner, and a social manipulator. She knows how to read power structures like blueprints. She knows who to bribe, who to blackmail, and when to disappear. She doesn’t pull the trigger, but she picks the target.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Graceful, deliberate, and iron-willed. Never loud, always heard.

**Vices:** 
Jewelry, red wine, slow jazz, and perfectly timed revenge.

**Abilities:** 
Influence, information gathering, manipulation. Knows how to break men using words alone.

**Secrets:** 
Keeps detailed records on every deal Knight has ever made — and a backup copy hidden outside the city.

**Beliefs:** 
Power is more beautiful when it’s quiet. Comfort is earned. And no man rules alone.

## Role in Disgraceland
Sable Marris is the unspoken empress of Samson Knight’s world — the velvet whisper behind his iron presence, helping him rule Gutter Row with subtlety, glamour, and cold precision.

## Biography

> “Words are just bullets with better aim, baby. And I don’t miss.”


**Tren Knight**, better known on the streets as **“Ninepack,”** is the slick-talking, sharp-dressing broker of [[The Third Row]] and the blood kin of [[Samson Knight]] — his little cousin, but nobody calls him that if they like their teeth.

With the looks of a prophet and the tongue of a hustler, Baby Nine was never built for the alleys or the blade. But he could sell heat to Charspire and talk a Loyalist guard into handing over their badge. From the time he was twelve, he was running side hustles, love notes, and dirty credits through the pipes of [[Vileby]], always one move ahead of his enemies and two steps behind the girls.

While [[Jailface]] cleans up messes, Baby Nine *prevents* them — or makes sure they turn a profit when they happen. He organizes the tribute flow, fences high-value goods, manages outside syndicate communications, and smooths tensions between rival crews with charm, smoke, and veiled threats. His connection to Mr. Knight gets him access, but his silver tongue keeps him indispensable.

He’s a poet when drunk, a savage when crossed, and a legend in bed — if his rhymes are to be believed.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Charismatic, fast-talking, smooth under pressure. Loves attention, but rarely loses control.

**Vices:** 
Women, wordplay, and private stashes of imported liquor. Keeps a book of poems he’s never shown anyone.

**Abilities:** 
Deal-making, double-speak, blackmail, negotiation. Can read a mark in seconds and flip them in minutes.

**Secrets:** 
Ninepack is rumored to be running quiet talks with a Threshton contact, despite Knight’s warnings. Whether it’s treason or business... only he knows.

**Beliefs:** 
Everything can be negotiated. Everyone wants something — your job is to find out what and charge double.

## Role in Disgraceland
Ninepack is the velvet tongue of The Third Row — a street poet with hustler instincts who makes sure the market never stops spinning, and no deal ever closes without a cut for Mr. Knight.

## Biography

> “He talks, I cut. That’s balance.”

**Malika Locke** walks through [[Gutter Row]] like she owns every shadow. Known as the ride-or-die of [[Ninepack]], she’s more than his girl — she’s his backup plan, his bodyguard, his bruiser, and sometimes, his conscience. Born and raised in the broken back alleys of Vileby, Malika earned her name the hard way — beating older boys in dice games and outrunning Loyalist patrols by the time she was ten.

She first met Ninepack during a chaotic street deal that went sideways. While others ran, she stepped in and bailed him out with a knife to someone’s throat and a smirk on her face. He talked slick. She didn’t care. But over time, their bond solidified — not just built on love, but on blood, danger, and a shared need to stay one move ahead of the streets.

Malika doesn’t say much in public, but her presence speaks volumes. She’s known for carrying two blades, moving like smoke through the Three Nail Market, and finishing fights her man never had to start. The only person she listens to is Ninepack, and even that depends on the mood.

She’s a legend in the making, feared by rivals and whispered about by Market kids who dream of being half as bad.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Calm until it’s time to strike. Observant, fast-thinking, loyal to a razor edge.

**Vices:** 
Dice games, fire whiskey, and putting men in their place. Keeps her late mother’s ring on a chain around her neck.

**Abilities:** 
Close-quarters combat, sleight of hand, stealth, tracking. Sharp instincts — she spots trouble before it speaks.

**Secrets:** 
Her real last name is **Vorneaux**, tying her to a disgraced Loyalist bloodline. She’s buried the past deep, but it has claws.

**Beliefs:** 
Trust no one except Ninepack. Loyalty is everything. And survival without love ain’t worth the scars.

## Role in Disgraceland
Malika Locke is the quiet fire beside Ninepack’s silver tongue — a lethal protector who watches his back and burns anyone who comes too close.

## Biography

> "I ain’t here to talk. I’m here to remember.”

Born into the gutter, raised by fists, and rebuilt in violence, **Jailface** is the scarred iron-fanged lieutenant of The [[Third Row]] and the personal enforcer of [[Samson Knight]]. His true name has been lost — maybe forgotten, maybe discarded — but his new name was earned the day a rival gang welded a prison brace to his skull and left him for dead in the ash canals. He survived. He came back. He didn’t speak a word. Just started cutting.

Jailface grew up just two blocks from Row Three, a street kid with nothing to lose and too much anger to bury. In the early days of the Row Wars, he worked underground pit fights to feed himself — one fight cost him most of his teeth. The next gave him a reputation. By the time the old guard of The Third Row had fallen apart, Jailface was a half-legend in Gutter Row already, known for finishing what others wouldn’t start.

When [[Samson Knight]] began consolidating power in the 2170s, Jailface didn’t challenge him. He offered him something else — silence, skill, and a debt of loyalty. Some say Samson was the one who found him after the brace incident, pulled him out of the filth, and gave him purpose. Since then, Jailface has been at Knight’s right side: a shadow in the alleys, a whisper before the blood hits the floor.

No one speaks directly to Jailface unless they’re invited. And no one runs in the [[Three Nail Market]] without his approval.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Unflinching, cold-blooded, and eerily quiet. Most of the time, he lets silence do the talking — until it’s time to scream.

**Vices:** 
**Burn Root** — a black, mind-numbing combat stimulant he chews constantly. That, and the slow act of revenge.

**Abilities:** 
Close-quarters killing, brutal enforcement, knife and machete combat, fear management. Exceptionally loyal, calculating when needed.

**Secrets:** 
The iron brace wasn’t just punishment — it was betrayal. Some whisper it was an inside job by the old gang leadership. Jailface keeps a kill list tattooed along his ribs. Many of the names are already crossed out.

**Beliefs:** 
Knight is king. Orders are scripture. Anyone who touches the market without permission gets touched back — harder.

## Role in Disgraceland
Jailface is the bloody teeth of [[Samson Knight]]’s rule — a walking warning to every hustler, traitor, and outsider in Gutter Row. He enforces the market’s invisible code and ensures fear is never forgotten.

Rottwyler]], [[General Colt]], [[Raynar Ventura]], [[Jacoban Clay]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Obey, and endure.”

His real name is long forgotten — or buried by design. To the people of Disgraceland, he is simply The Duke. A title taken, not earned. He wasn’t elected, appointed, or asked — he declared himself savior in the aftermath of the end of the world. And in a way, he was. Then again, so is a parasite to a corpse. Before the [[Tetra Bomb]], he had been a high-ranking officer in a private military firm during the final stages of the [[Water Wars]]. Brutal, efficient, and ideologically obsessed with order, he led sieges on fractured city-states and quelled rebellions under the banner of peace. He never blinked at atrocity. His uniform today — a patched-together bastardization of old-world military regalia — is stitched from the flags of defeated enemies, the epaulettes torn from bodies, medals self-assigned. When the [[Tetra Bomb]] dropped and the world fell silent, The Duke didn’t grieve. He saw opportunity. He took to the woods north of [[WATER#Faded Lake|Faded Lake]] and claimed an old estate once belonging to some long-dead tech mogul. There, he began The Rebuild — a militarized compound that eventually became [[Ashmoor]], with [[The Silo]] at its heart. The Silo is both symbol and weapon: a towering, welded-together grain hoard that feeds the loyal and starves the rest. The Duke believes that civilization failed because it became too soft. He teaches that the weak destroyed the world, and only by obedience, order, and iron-willed leadership can it be saved. His broadcasts are required viewing across Disgraceland — sermons of fear disguised as hope, always ending with his chilling motto: “Obey, and endure.” But behind his cold precision lies cruelty. He kidnapped [[Emily Burton]], a child at the time, years ago — the daughter of a dissenting scientist who disappeared soon after. She is now the Duke’s “First Lady”, a forced role inside his mansion-prison. He cannot bear children. He does not touch her. Yet he parades her as a symbol of dominance. The perfect wife. The perfect silence. But not forever. He hosts his weekly address, the [[State of Tribucia]] live every Alphaday on the [[TTV Studios|TTV Network]]. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Controlled and theatrical — he speaks like a preacher but rules like a butcher. He never yells, only issues decrees with unnerving calm and expects the world to obey. > [!infobox] > > ![[prop.png|260]] **Vices:** Delusions of legacy. He feeds on adoration, even if he has to manufacture it. Parades, statues, broadcasts — all scripted to reinforce the fantasy that he _saved_ the world, not conquered its corpse. **Abilities:** Tactical genius in psychological warfare and population control. A master propagandist who builds loyalty through fear, scarcity, and ritual. He can spot dissent in a crowd by a blink. **Secrets:** Deep beneath The Silo, he keeps a sealed chamber filled with relics of the old world — possibly tech, possibly something far darker — and he visits it alone, sometimes for hours, emerging shaken but silent. **Beliefs:** The strong must rule or all is lost. Emotion is rot. Freedom is a myth. The world didn’t end because of violence — it ended because men stopped _obeying._ His gospel: _“Obey, and endure.”_ ## Role In Disgraceland Self-declared ruler of United Tribucia. Created the militarized territory of **Ashmoor** around an old estate, now known as **The Silo**. Commands the **Loyalist Guard**, controls food distribution, and uses propaganda to keep control. Directly responsible for multiple atrocities across the land, all committed under the guise of “the greater good.” Hosts daily propaganda announcements across all of United Tribucia every night at 18:00 hrs. Mandatory viewing.

“FINGERS OFF!”

If [[The Duke]] is the mind of Disgraceland, Sgt. Rottwyler is the teeth. A mountain of a man with arms like tree trunks and a chest built for knocking down doors, Rottwyler is the absolute authority over the [[Loyalist Guard]] — the elite, brutal enforcers who maintain the Duke’s grip on the region. He speaks rarely, growls often, and listens never. His every word sounds like it’s been chewed up with gravel. He is feared more than The Duke himself, and that’s just how he likes it. Rottwyler was once a mercenary in the Carbine Wastes before the [[Tetra Bomb]] erased most of his former employers. When the smoke cleared, he rode east with nothing but a pack of ammo, a wounded dog, and a pocket full of Slugs. The Duke found him bloodied, half-starved, and still swinging. Instead of killing him, he offered him rank. Rottwyler never forgot that. His loyalty is absolute. So much so that, in a twisted public ceremony years ago, Rottwyler severed his own left pinky finger as a demonstration of obedience and lifelong service. Now, it’s tradition — every Loyalist must cut off their own pinky to join the Guard. Some faint. Some scream. Rottwyler just watches, cigar clenched between his teeth, eyes cold and unmoved. That cigar? It’s never gone. No one’s ever seen him without it — even when torturing prisoners or training recruits. It's said he lights it with the ashes of traitors. His breath smells like blood, tobacco, and disdain. Rottwyler has no family. No past. His body is all scar tissue and routine. Wake. Train. Patrol. Punish. Sleep. He lifts weights in the courtyard of The Silo every dawn, shirtless, while Loyalists stand in formation around him like statues. Dissent is weakness. Mercy is treason. The Duke is law. But not everyone believes he's unshakable. [[Emily Burton]] once said, in a whisper behind a locked door, “Even dogs break when they’re beaten enough.” --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Unflinching and sadistic — Rottwyler doesn’t speak unless it’s to bark an order, and he enjoys watching fear bloom in a man’s eyes more than he enjoys victory. **Vices:** Pain — giving it, not feeling it. He trains harder than any recruit, punishes weakness without hesitation, and carries an unholy satisfaction in the breaking of bones and spirits. **Abilities:** Near-superhuman strength and pain tolerance; master of close-quarters combat and battlefield tactics. His presence alone can quell riots, and his brutality keeps the Loyalist Guard sharp and afraid. **Secrets:** Beneath his bedframe, wrapped in oilcloth and sealed with wax, is the collar of the dog he rode east with — long dead, buried in Ashmoor's soil. He digs it up every year on the same night, sits with it, and says nothing for hours. **Beliefs:** The chain of command is sacred. The Duke saved his life, and loyalty to him is the only code that matters. Emotion is for corpses. _“Obey, or be buried.”_ ## Role In Disgraceland Sgt. Rottwyler is the iron fist of The Duke’s regime — commander of the Loyalist Guard and enforcer of obedience through sheer terror. Where The Duke speaks of order, Rottwyler ensures it, one broken jaw at a time.

159.title: Raynar Ventura
159.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Raynar Ventura]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_raynar.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"Associate to [[The Duke]]","chapters":["02 - Ghosts On The Waves","04 - Glowing Darkness"],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:00:01"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_raynar.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "Associate to [[The Duke]]" chapters: - 02 - Ghosts On The Waves - 04 - Glowing Darkness tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # RAYNAR VENTURA > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[raynar.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Associate to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Snake in the Grass **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Slimy **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 51 **Height:** 5'11" **Weight:** 158 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Associate **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I don’t need a weapon. I need a whisper. One well-placed truth does more damage than any bullet ever could.”

No one remembers where Raynar Ventura came from — and those who claim to are probably lying. Some say he was once a street magician in the ashes of Old Chicago. Others swear he was a bureaucrat before the bomb, cataloguing death tolls and hoarding water credits. What is known is that Raynar thrives in power vacuums. And Disgraceland is one big vacuum waiting to be filled. Raynar has no official rank. No uniform. No title beyond the vague and terrifying: “[[The Duke]]’s Listener.” But everyone knows who he is — the man in black with the smirk, the notebook, and the voice that never rises above a whisper. He walks freely between every region in [[DISGRACELAND]]. [[Territories/Steeltown]], [[GUTTER ROW]], even the edges of [[The Drownlands]] — always smiling, always listening. He’ll trade sugar with farmers in [[Threshton]], drink rotgut with pirates on [[Rustwater Bay]], and promise favors he has no intention of fulfilling. Because Raynar’s greatest weapon is information, and his loyalty belongs only to the man who pays him best — currently, that’s The Duke. But not even [[The Duke]] trusts him. Not really. Raynar has hundreds of informants, from desperate children to well-placed guards, all paid in Slugs, secrets, or future promises. He refers to them as “his little ears.” Some whisper for him out of fear, others out of greed. But no one ever meets Raynar twice the same way. Sometimes he's pleasant. Sometimes chilling. Always writing something in that black notebook, which no one's ever seen him part with. He’s in his late forties, slim and sharp, dressed in black like he's in permanent mourning for a world that never loved him back. His mustache is pencil-thin, his hair tighter than his smile. Some think he's a coward. Others think he’s untouchable. The truth is somewhere in between — because Raynar has survived this long by never being anywhere long enough to get shot. Colt despises him. Rottwyler has threatened him openly. [[Emily Burton]] can’t stand his stare. And yet… none of them dare cross him, because Raynar knows something on everyone. And when the walls begin to crumble, Raynar Ventura won’t be crushed beneath them. He’ll already be halfway to the next regime. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, sly, and unfazed — Raynar is never rattled, always watching, and speaks in a tone that makes even confessions sound polite. **Vices:** Manipulation for pleasure. He doesn’t just gather secrets — he _plays_ them, pitting people against each other like it’s a private game of dominoes. **Abilities:** Master manipulator, expert in surveillance, persuasion, and social camouflage. He can blend into any crowd, extract truths with a smile, and disappear before the fallout lands. **Secrets:** Hidden in the spine of his infamous black notebook is a single, yellowed photograph — a woman and child no one has ever seen, names scratched out. He never looks at it, but he always knows it’s there. **Beliefs:** Nothing lasts but leverage. Raynar doesn’t believe in sides, only in survival — and survival belongs to those who know _everything_ before it matters. ## Role In Disgraceland **Raynar Ventura** is Disgraceland’s whisper broker — a ghost in black who walks between factions, gathering power through silence and ink. He doesn’t rule, command, or fight… but when the dust clears, he’ll be the one holding the receipts.

160.title: Jacoban Clay
160.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Jacoban Clay]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_jacoban.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"Owner of [[Clay Industries]]","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:56"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_jacoban.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "Owner of [[Clay Industries]]" chapters: - tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # JACOOBAN CLAY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[jacoban.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Owner & Founder of [[Clay Industries]], Sponsor of [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] **Alias/Nickname:** Prick **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Selfish, smooth-talker, attractive **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** [[Soria Langston-Clay]] **Age:** 46 **Height:** 6'0" **Weight:** 184 lbs. **Date of Birth:** May 16th, 2140 **Occupation:** Owner of Clay Industries **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]], [[Soria Langston-Clay]], [[Raynar Ventura]], [[Morris Gable]], [[Francis Murray]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Morals don’t build empires. Steel does. And I own the furnace.”

The wealthiest man in Disgraceland. Few men in Gutter Row rise without getting dirt under their nails. Jacoban Clay didn’t just get dirt — he built an empire from it. The founder of Clay Millworks, Jacoban turned sweat, blood, and iron into wealth. He signed a deal with The Duke early on: free slave labor in exchange for endless shipments of metal — pipes, plates, shackles, weapons. Whatever the regime needed, Jacoban delivered. And he got rich. Fast. Unlike other industrialists, Jacoban wasn’t loud. He was calm. Calculated. Kept a clean shirt and a loaded pistol. While others begged for permits, Jacoban showed up with a sealed envelope and a nod from The Duke. Years later, while meeting with officials at The Silo, Jacoban saw a woman enter the room — dark hair pinned back, a red pendant resting just above her breasts, and a look in her eyes like she already owned the place. Her name was Soria Langston. And Jacoban decided then and there: she would be his. They married shortly after. Now, Jacoban lives lavishly in Ashmoor at her side, managing The Duke’s treasury and watching from behind velvet curtains. He still oversees his factories, still ensures the gears of war turn smoothly. But make no mistake — he didn’t marry Soria for love. He married her because together, they are untouchable. Or so they believe. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, composed, and opportunistic — Jacoban rarely raises his voice, preferring leverage over force and influence over spectacle. **Vices:** Greed masked as pragmatism. He doesn’t crave attention, only power — and he collects favors, secrets, and leverage like others collect art. **Abilities:** Gifted industrialist and financial manipulator; he can read contracts like confessionals and has a sixth sense for when to bribe, when to blackmail, and when to vanish a problem. **Secrets:** He keeps a hidden safe behind a false wall in his Ashmoor estate — filled not with money, but with dirt: letters, receipts, and signed orders that could destroy half of The Duke’s inner circle if released. **Beliefs:** Loyalty is a currency, nothing more. In Jacoban’s eyes, survival isn’t about strength — it’s about who controls the flow of iron, gold, and silence. ## Role In Disgraceland **Jacoban Clay** is the regime’s golden banker — the man behind the curtain who oils the war machine with slave labor and silence. He doesn’t seek the spotlight, but from the luxury of Ashmoor, he ensures the wealth keeps flowing and the truth stays buried.

161.title: Emily Burton
161.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Emily Burton]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"magicitem","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_emily.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"Wife of [[The Duke]]","chapters":["02 - Ghosts On The Waves"],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","main","protagonist","chapter02"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:42"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: magicitem NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_emily.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "Wife of [[The Duke]]" chapters: - 02 - Ghosts On The Waves tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - main - protagonist - chapter02 --- # EMILY BURTON > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[emily.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** The Grand Duchess of Tribucia **Alias/Nickname:** The Duchess **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Sympathetic **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** [[The Duke]] **Age:** 25 **Height:** 5'07" **Weight:** 128 lbs. **Date of Birth:** June 13th, 2161 **Occupation:** Duchess **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[Davis Pollard]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“They dressed me in silk and called it salvation. But silk burns too.”

They call her The Duchess, but she never asked for that name. Born just outside the ruins of Lansing to a family of tinkerers and scavengers, Emily Burton was bright, curious, and impossibly bold from a young age. Her father, a former engineer from before the blast, was part of a quiet circle rebuilding pre-Tetra tech in secret. Her mother kept a hidden school for the neighboring children. The Burtons were beloved by their community, but too smart, too outspoken, too dangerous for [[The Duke]]'s vision of order. When Emily was sixteen, the [[Loyalist Guard]]s came. [[The Duke]] offered the Burtons a choice: surrender their work and serve him… or be erased. Emily watched from the floorboards as her parents were executed in their home. She was taken in chains to [[Ashmoor]], where The Duke presented her on broadcast as his ward — a girl "rescued from chaos" by the guiding hand of Disgraceland’s ruler. Months later, he declared her his wife. His Duchess. It was theater. A grotesque display of dominance. The Duke, impotent and delusional, sought legacy through image, not blood. Now 22, Emily walks the halls of [[The Silo]] Mansion like a ghost in silk. She smiles for the cameras. She stands beside him on the balcony during broadcasts. Her voice is never heard — only her presence. But behind those blue eyes is a mind sharpened on silence. She is not broken. She is waiting. Watching. Emily understands the power her beauty holds. She knows the whispers in the halls, the jealous eyes of Loyalist wives, the quiet awe from the poor who see her as a living doll in a white dress. But she also knows that The Silo protects her, even if it’s a cage. There’s a bed of secrets under this place — guards who owe her favors, servants who tell her what they hear, a quiet network of sympathy she has cultivated one kind word at a time. She hates The Duke. Hates his hands, his voice, his fake faith. But she knows his routines. She knows when he sleeps. She knows what lies beneath the grain silo. And she knows that someday, if Disgraceland is to change... she might be the one to light the match. Emily Burton — _The Duchess_ in name only — is a poised, calculating survivor wrapped in the illusion of obedience. Raised by brilliant rebels and forced into a gilded cage by the man who slaughtered her family, she wears her silence like a blade honed by years of observation. She plays her role flawlessly: a porcelain figurehead in silk, offering smiles while quietly weaving a web of influence through whispered alliances and owed favors. Emily’s beauty is her camouflage, her intellect her weapon. She studies everyone — their habits, their weaknesses — waiting for the moment to strike. Her secret? Hidden in a locked drawer behind the mirror in her private chamber is a small brass pendant… the last creation her father ever built, which — unknown to all — contains a detailed schematic of The Silo’s underground network. She's not just waiting for revolution. She's designing it. --- ## Personality: **Temperament:** Calm, observant, and disarmingly gentle — Emily wields restraint like a blade, rarely showing anger but always calculating outcomes two steps ahead. **Vices:** Obsessive control. She rehearses her every move, word, and smile until perfection, terrified that one misstep will crack the mask and cost her everything. **Abilities:** Silently adept at manipulating people through subtle charm and emotional read. **Secrets:** She possesses a miniature pendant containing a full schematic of the Silo’s understructure — smuggled and salvaged from her father's hidden workshop the night of his execution. **Beliefs:** Emily no longer believes in saviors — only leverage. But deep down, she clings to her mother’s whispered lesson: “Knowledge is the only freedom worth dying for.” ## Role In Disgraceland **Emily Burton** is the silent symbol of the regime — paraded as The Duke’s dutiful Duchess, but in truth, a brilliant prisoner biding her time. She plays the part of perfection while quietly gathering the pieces to burn it all down. > [!rustwater]- Surprise > ![[embikini.png|600]]

162.title: Davis Pollard
162.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Davis Pollard]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_davis.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"[[The Duke]]'s Personal Slave","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","loyalist","slave","ashmoor","protagonist","el-santo"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:37"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_davis.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "[[The Duke]]'s Personal Slave" chapters: - tags: - character - loyalist - slave - ashmoor - protagonist - el-santo --- # DAVIS POLLARD > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[davis.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Slave to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Slave Boy **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** None **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 25 **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 158 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Slave **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[Emily Burton]], [[Jimmy Douglass|The Duke]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“They call me quiet like it’s weakness. But quiet people hear everything.”

Davis grew up working the sunburnt ranchlands of Threshton, the youngest of five boys. His family wasn’t loyal to the Duke—just scared enough to pretend they were. His mother died during a fuel riot when he was nine, trampled by panicked townsfolk. His father was arrested two years later for hoarding “unbranded slugs,” and Davis never saw him again. He was a quiet kid, smarter than most gave him credit for, with a knack for observing without speaking. People underestimated him, and he learned to survive by making himself small—until the night everything shattered. The night the Duke’s men raided Threshton under the guise of “security enforcement,” Davis was taken from his bunk, shackled, and thrown into a supply skiff bound for Ashmoor. Emily Burton was in the same transport, though they didn’t know each other then. Some of the others fought back. They didn’t survive the trip. Once in Ashmoor, Davis was handpicked—not because he was strong, but because he was pretty. The Duke likes his pets obedient and quiet. Davis was branded, collared, and renamed "Pollard" in the house records. But in his mind, he never let go of his real name. He became a ghost in the halls of The Dead Waters estate, tending to the Duke’s personal quarters, witnessing horrors no one should see, never allowed to speak unless spoken to. But through the years, he began learning secrets—whispers between the walls, the routines of guards, the Duke’s hidden fears. Davis isn’t a fighter. Not yet. But there’s something simmering beneath that quiet exterior. A seed of rebellion. He hasn’t forgotten who he is. And when the time comes, he may be the one holding the key—literally or figuratively—to taking the whole rotten empire down from the inside. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Quiet, observant, and deeply internal — Davis rarely speaks, but his silence isn’t fear. It’s focus. **Vices:** Self-blame. He carries every tragedy like it was his fault, even when it wasn’t. Especially when it wasn’t. **Abilities:** Expert eavesdropper and silent mover — Davis can memorize patrols, read lips, and vanish into shadow. He’s not trained for war, but he’s trained for survival in a gilded prison. **Secrets:** Tucked under a loose floorboard in his quarters is a scrap of cloth from his mother’s apron, wrapped around a key he stole from a distracted guard. He doesn’t know what it opens — yet. **Beliefs:** He doesn’t believe in heroes. But he _does_ believe in moments — that one right moment can change everything. And when his comes, he plans to be ready. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Davis Pollard** is a prisoner in silk sheets, a nobody in the Duke’s house who sees _everything._ He may not look like a threat… but one whisper in the right ear, one door unlocked at the wrong time, and he might be the one who ends it all.

163.title: General Colt
163.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[General Colt]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_colt.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#Knifedale|Knifedale]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"General of the [[Loyalist Guard]]","chapters":["04 - Glowing Darkness","05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:47"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_colt.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#Knifedale|Knifedale]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "General of the [[Loyalist Guard]]" chapters: - 04 - Glowing Darkness - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star - chapter5 --- # GENERAL COLT > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[colt.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** The 1st General of the Loyalist Guard **Alias/Nickname:** The General **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Hard-line military man **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** Unknown **Age:** 63 **Height:** 5'09" **Weight:** 176 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** General of the [[Loyalist Guard]] **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]], [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], [[Raynar Ventura]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >>

“Obedience is efficient. Loyalty is inefficient. I reward efficiency.”

If Sgt. Rottwyler is The Duke’s hammer, General Colt is his scalpel. Colt was born in a sealed military bunker somewhere deep in the Upper Peninsula during the final years of the [[Water Wars]]. The son of officers, he was raised on cold meals, colder lectures, and war manuals instead of bedtime stories. When the [[Tetra Bomb]] dropped, he was one of the few with enough tactical foresight to see which way the power was shifting — and moved quickly to align himself with the rising Duke. He doesn’t believe in loyalty. He believes in utility. While Sgt. Rottwyler commands the troops through fear and brute dominance, Colt oversees operations, strategy, and propaganda. He coordinates fuel shipments, monitors dissenters, and signs off on disappearances. Nothing happens without his mark on it — from the placement of radio towers to which town gets its power back first after an outage. [[The Duke]] trusts him. Or at least needs him. Colt knows this — and uses it. There is no warmth in the man. He never married. Never took a lover. His life is a ledger of useful actions and eliminated threats. He believes The Duke’s vision for [[DISGRACELAND]] is flawed, but necessary. He sees himself as a stabilizer — keeping the regime from crumbling under the weight of its own absurdity. He finds Rottwyler repugnant — a snarling dog too eager to punish when a whisper could silence more effectively. The two men hate each other, but both know a war within the Guard would burn them both. So they maintain a quiet truce, marked by veiled threats and stiff nods in the war room. Colt is never without his gloves, a sharp uniform, and a plan. He keeps stacks of black notebooks in his quarters, filled with observations, patterns, and projections. Rumors say he knows every possible outcome of a rebellion, including what to do if The Duke himself dies. The only thing he fears… is chaos. And deep down, he knows: chaos is coming. ## Personality **Temperament:** Precise, clinical, and coldly analytical — Colt doesn’t act on emotion, only on probability and outcome. > [!infobox] > > ![[coltwalk.png|260]] **Vices:** Control through information. He hoards data, monitors everyone, and plays puppet master with towns, people, and perception like pieces on a war board. **Abilities:** Master strategist and tactician with an unmatched ability to predict political unrest, manipulate public sentiment, and suppress rebellion before it ignites. **Secrets:** Buried in his ledgers is a full contingency plan detailing how to dissolve The Duke’s regime from within — and replace it with something leaner, smarter, and far more terrifying. **Beliefs:** Order is survival. The Duke is flawed, but necessary… for now. Sentiment is a liability, and mercy is a luxury only victors can afford. ## Role In Disgraceland **General Colt** is the unseen architect behind Disgraceland’s machinery — controlling supply lines, information flow, and political stability with ruthless efficiency. While The Duke preaches obedience and Rottwyler enforces it, Colt ensures the entire system doesn’t collapse under its own brutality.

164.title: Brady & Brody
164.content:
NOTE TITLE: [[Brady & Brody]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_bandb.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"[[The Duke]]'s Bodyguards","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:32"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_bandb.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "[[The Duke]]'s Bodyguards" chapters: - tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # BRADY & BRODY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[bandb.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Bodyguards to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Twins **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Feared **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** Unknown **Height:** 6'2" **Weight:** 268 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Bodyguards **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[Emily Burton]], [[Jimmy Douglass|The Duke]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Who you want dead, boss?”

They don’t talk much. Don’t need to. Just the thud of their boots on tile is enough to make most folks piss themselves. Brady and Brody — names nobody’s sure they were actually born with — are twin towers of raw, twisted muscle. Always seen together, always looming just a few paces behind The Duke like a matched set of executioners. They’re dressed identically in stained white tank-tops and camouflage pants, belts always tight, fists always clenched. Brady is the bald one with the eye patch and the pin-up girl tattooed on his arm. Brody keeps a flat-top like he’s still pretending to pass inspection. Neither has a neck to speak of. They are not right, and everyone knows it. Locals whisper that the twins weren’t born so much as grown, that their freakish size and thick skulls are the legacy of the Tetra Bomb — that their mother died during childbirth and their father was one of the scientists vaporized in the blast. Others claim they were found in a crumbling bunker, half-feral, feeding on rats and old boots. The truth doesn’t matter. What matters is that they are loyal to The Duke to the bone, and they kill without question. They serve as The Duke’s personal bodyguards, but their duties often stretch into punishment, intimidation, and the occasional public execution. The Duke trots them out during speeches to stand behind him like slabs of meat on legs, staring straight ahead, breathing loud and slow. It’s part of the show. And the people eat it up — or choke on it. They don’t talk much. But when they do, it’s usually the same thing. “Who you want dead, boss?” They're dim, no doubt about that, but not useless. There’s a sort of base cunning in how they move — pack animal instinct. When one starts a fight, the other finishes it. They’ve never been seen apart, never seen sleeping, and no one knows what they do when they’re not standing behind The Duke. There’s a growing fear that the twins aren’t done changing, that whatever weird residue the Tetra Bomb left in their blood is still brewing. That they might get stronger. Or worse… smarter. And if that happens? God help us all. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Silent, violent, and always alert — they don’t speak unless commanded, and they don’t stop once set in motion. **Vices:** Brutality for its own sake. They enjoy breaking bones like others enjoy cracking jokes. **Abilities:** Superhuman strength, uncanny pain resistance, and perfect synchronicity — they fight like a hive mind, overwhelming enemies through sheer force and monstrous stamina. **Secrets:** Beneath Brady’s bunk is a rusted metal lunchbox. Inside? A collection of baby teeth — not their own. No one knows who they belonged to… or why he keeps them. **Beliefs:** The Duke is law. The Duke is god. Their world is black and red — kill or be killed, protect the boss, and crush everything that doesn’t kneel. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Brady and Brody** are the Duke’s twin shadows — his blunt instruments of terror and punishment. Where words fail, they arrive. And when they arrive, things _end_.
