(cont'd) #### MAIN EVENT SHADOWS

The smoke hung low in [[Steeltown]].

Furnace Square, an old foundry turned death circus for the day in [[STEELTOWN#Barton|Barton]], vibrated with noise and sweat. Cracked concrete stretched between towering smokestacks. Bleachers—welded from scrap and desperation—shook under the weight of a feverish crowd. Rusted banners flapped like tattered war flags, the sigil of [[World Lucha Libre]] glowing faint red from a makeshift stage.

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] stood with his arms crossed, sunglasses catching the flicker of stage pyros. He looked pissed just to be alive. Over the comms, a familiar voice broke the static.

"Ain't even noon and I already hate everyone here," [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] muttered.

"Hate it all you want, brother," [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] replied, calm as a man nursing whiskey on a Sunday. "Pay's better than a bounty run. Just keep the fighters from killin' each other before the bell."

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] scoffed. "Glorified blueshirts."

[[Katie Kowalski|Kowalski]] chimed in from her sniper’s perch above the square. "Broken Tower, twelve o'clock. Someone just dropped a flare."

"That was me," came [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]]'s voice, cheerful and unconcerned. "I get why you always tell me to keep the safety on. Lotta people starin’ at me now. Lotta people."

Then came the squeal of loudspeakers. Flames erupted skyward. Music erupted. The crowd answered in kind—a full-throated roar that echoed through the steel bones of the city.

[[Flint Garritt]] walked on stage like a snake oil messiah. His coat glinted with silver threads, gloves pristine, voice smooth as old bourbon.

"WELCOME," he called, arms outstretched, "to the HEART of HARD LIVING. To the fire pit of the East. To the belly of the beast—[[Steeltown]]!"

Cheers. Flares. Fists in the air. [[Steeltown]] howled back.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] paced like a preacher. "I'd like to thank our esteemed mayor, Mr. [[Ellis Westmount]], for hosting this event today as we travel around the great territories of Tribucia. The [[World Lucha Libre]] ain't just a sport. It's survival. It's blood and glory and truth—and TONIGHT... we're promotin' the fight of the decade!"

He paused, letting the tension build, then dropped the name: "BIG TITAN [[Bastian Redd]]!"

Smoke parted. The canyon king emerged.

Shirtless, painted ochre across the chest, a red pouch swinging from his neck, [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] moved like a carved monument given breath. On his way to the stage, he paused beside [[Abel May Jr.|Abel]].

"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]," he said with a nod.

[[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] nodded back. "Good luck out there, big man."

[[Abel May Jr.|Abel]] grunted. "Don't let him make you a headline."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] climbed the steps and took the mic. His voice rumbled low, reverent.

"[[Steeltown]]. You feel that? That stillness? That breath before the storm? That’s the land holdin’ still, waitin’ on the Final Reckoning. Not just the match. The moment."

He turned, facing the crowd. "[[Bobby Cutman]]—you wear that belt like it's carved into your chest. Undefeated. But we both know you bled. They saw me drag you to the edge. This third one? There ain’t no more questions. This ain't about gold. This is legacy. You call yourself The Iron Bull? Then charge. Just know—I eat bull for lunch."

The crowd erupted.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] grinned like a man who'd lit the fuse and stepped back. "And now," he drawled, "the REIGNING, UNDEFEATED, UNDISPUTED CHAMPION... [[Bobby Cutman|Bobby “The Iron Bull” Cutman]]!"

A low rumble from backstage. Then—he came.

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] stomped out, taped fists swinging, belt slung over his shoulder like a crown too heavy to share. He didn't wave. Didn't nod. He seized the moment by the throat.

He snatched the mic. His voice dripped venom.

"[[Steeltown]] jerkin' itself off over a ghost story," he growled. "Over a man who couldn’t finish the job. Newsflash, big man: **Almost** don’t make legends. Almost don’t keep my name stuck in your damn mouth."

He pointed to the crowd. "Y'all tattoo L’s on your neck and call it culture. You dress up rust and call it tradition. You cheer for the underdog not 'cause you believe—they never win—but because you wanna feel brave without ever takin' the hit yourselves. You're all spectators to your own misery."

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] paced the stage, snarling. "And you—[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]—what the fuck even are you? A rent-a-cop militia with daddy issues and dollar-store tattoos? You stand around lookin' hard 'cause deep down, you know you ain't ever gonna matter past these city limits."

He turned back to the audience, voice rising. "And [[Steeltown]]? City of rust, rats, and regrets. You pile your broken dreams in stacks, burn 'em for warmth, and call it living. Newsflash: the rest of us ain't lookin' at you to lead—they're laughin' at you."

His gaze locked on [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]. "And you, big canyon king? You're the mascot of the first settlers? You wanna talk legacy? The only thing you'll leave behind is a crater where your pride used to be. Final Reckoning? You're goddamn right it is. And I'm not just takin' your body—I’m takin’ your myth. I'm gonna leave your name in the dust with all these other wannabes."

[[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] raised a taped fist, extending his middle finger, veins bulging. "I'm the Iron Bull. I don't fight for fame. I fight to END people. And Final Reckoning? I end you and the legacy of your pathetic people."

The air cracked. [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] lunged. Security moved.

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] shouted, "Save it for the ring, gentlemen!"

But the crowd had caught fire. Trash cans overturned. Flares shot up. The chant began: **[[STEELTOWN]]! [[STEELTOWN]]!**

The Wrecking Crew members advanced onto the stage. [[Jimmy Douglass|Jimmy]] walked up to [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] and gently put his arms on the big man's chest, holding him back.

# Chapter 02

#### _Alphaday, 6th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When [[Lyla Bonetooth]] and the Rustwater Raiders are summoned to [[The Silo]] for a secret job, they’re ordered to smuggle a high-value prisoner to Steeltown — but the “prisoner” turns out to be a chain gang of slaves. As tensions rise aboard [[the Black Marauder]], Lyla must decide whether to complete the job or risk everything by defying [[The Duke]]. Meanwhile, a chilling vision haunts the [[Unseen Widows]]: a glimpse of the horrors still to come.

Inside the captain’s quarters, the air smelled of salt, brass polish, and wet leather. Knives pinned maps to the wall, their blades gleaming in the shifting lantern light. The room rocked gently with the tide, the low groan of the moorings echoing beneath the deck like a restless spirit. [[Lyla Bonetooth]] sat at her desk with boots kicked up, flipping a rusted coin between her fingers as she traced her eyes across the worn map. Rain drummed against the steel above in a steady rhythm. Nearby, [[Zadie Adeyemi]] polished a curved blade, its edge glinting as she sipped from a steaming tin cup. The quiet between them was not uncomfortable. It was the quiet of routine — of calm before the inevitable. A knock broke the rhythm. “Cap’n. Something came in on the long-hook,” came [[Clinton Firebay]]’s voice from outside. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] didn’t look up. “Didn’t order anything. Unless it’s rum or tickets to Cutman versus Redd, I ain’t interested.” The door creaked open and [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] stepped in, water trailing from his coat. “Wasn’t a delivery. Came sealed. Courier was Loyalist. Didn’t say a word. Just dropped it and peeled.” Now she looked up, one brow lifting. “Loyalist? Out here?” He tossed a wax-sealed envelope onto her desk. The red wax bore a familiar sigil — a black sun over cracked ground. The Duke’s personal seal. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] flicked her coin into the air, caught it, then stared at the envelope. “Well, shit. Guess it’s either a dinner invitation or a death sentence.” The door slammed open. [[Blacktide Cray]] barged in, rain-spattered and scowling. “Tell me that ain’t what I think it is.” “It’s not what you think it is,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said, deadpan. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] shot her a sidelong glare. “Then what is it, Bonetooth?” “It’s a letter. From the Silo.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] didn’t move for a long moment. Then: “Goddamnit, [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], I don’t have time for this shit today. Well, go on. Read it.” She opened it slowly, the crackle of the wax breaking loud in the silence. Her eyes skimmed the letter, jaw tightening. “So?” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] asked. “What’s the word?” She looked up, her voice even. “We’re invited to the Silo. Raynar Ventura signed it. Says The Duke wants to meet.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] began pacing, cracking his knuckles like they owed him money. “Hell no. That bastard doesn’t summon people unless he’s planning to hang 'em or buy 'em. Ain’t gonna be us.” “Could be legit,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] offered. “Could be leverage. Raiders have done dirt all across the coast — maybe he wants to hire us.” “Or bury us,” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] growled. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stood, letter dangling in one hand. Her gaze swept over both men, cool as a steel blade. “[[Blacktide Cray|Cray]], you’re wound tight enough to snap a mast. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]], you think too pretty. Me? I think if the wolf sends a dinner invite, you don’t ignore it — but you don’t show up unarmed either.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] leaned in, voice low. “We burn it. No trace, no trouble. No one ever got stabbed in the back by a letter they didn’t read.” “Problem is, we did read it,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] said. “And he knows we did. Ventura don’t send ghosts. He sends messengers he can hang if we don’t show.” “Let 'em hang,” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] muttered. “Be the first honest thing [[The Duke]]’s done all year.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]], quiet until now, set her knife spinning into the table, blade-first. “If it were a death sentence, we’d already be bleeding. He wants something. Question is — how much poison’s in the cup?” “We haven’t touched Loyalist cargo in years,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said, measured. “We never broke our agreement. He’d have no reason to want our heads.” The rain intensified. The hull groaned. “Could be a job. Could be a warning,” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] said. “Could be he just wants to see if we still bow when summoned.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] scoffed. “And what? You wanna go kiss his boots?” “You ever see me kiss anyone’s boots, [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]?” “No. But I seen what happens when a mouth talks back at the Silo. Ends up sewn shut or fed to fish.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] leaned back, arms crossed. “She ain’t wrong to weigh it. But I’m with the captain. Whatever this is — we don’t ignore it.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] nodded slowly. “We go. Quiet, armed, and watching every shadow. Me. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]]. [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]]. Rest stay on the ship.” The others filtered in — [[Salt-Eye Marlow]], [[Darius Adeyemi]], [[Silas Vayne]] — just in time to catch the last line. “[[Silas Vayne|Silas]], [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]], [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] — you stay back,” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] instructed. “Eyes on the Marauder. Anyone tries boarding, you gut ‘em or sink ‘em.” She turned to the wall furnace. One last look at the letter, then she tossed it in. The wax popped. The paper curled and blackened. “We got his message,” she said quietly. “Let’s go pay the [[The Duke|old fuck]] a visit.”
Evening blanketed the docks in a quilt of wet fog and grit. The cutter — a rust-streaked, repurposed patrol skiff — floated low in the water, tethered by ropes frayed like old nerves. Rain hissed off metal. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stepped aboard first, her coat heavy with water, her long dark hair clinging to her as she adjusts her eye-patch against the drizzle.

If you care about stability, about keeping what's left of civilization from collapsing into another fire, then you already understand.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]]’s voice cut clean through the quiet. “Everybody in this room knows slavery gets exploited in Disgraceland. You can dress it up in policy and necessity, but we all know what it is. Chains. Collars. Flesh sold to grease the gears.” The Duke studied Lyla for a moment, wondering if it's worth his time and effort continuing this conversation.  “The Wrecking Crew doesn’t allow slaves in Steeltown, anyway.” Lyla said. “If you drop off a ship full of slaves on their shores, they're gonna take that as a direct insult. You sure you wanna do that?” “Which is why I’m not using Loyalists,” he replied. “I’m using you. Raiders. Shadows.” "Who would be stupid enough to smuggle slaves into Steeltown?" Lyla wondered. The Duke was beginning to get annoyed with this conversation. "Who the purchaser is - is of none of your concern, Miss Bonetooth..." "Captain." "What?" "My name is Captain Bonetooth." Lyla’s jaw flexed. “And if we refuse?” The Duke leaned back. “Then I find someone worse. Someone messier. The Duke shook hands with Lyla and the rest as they exited, pondering his offer. “You’ll be given route coordinates and slugs. Rottwyler]] marched forward with guards and prisoners. Chains clinked. Mud-soaked figures shivered in the rain — old men, scarred women, hollow-eyed children. One girl, maybe seven, looked up and locked eyes with Lyla. She didn’t cry. She didn’t speak. Just stared. Lyla’s breath hitched — sharp as a blade. And she said nothing.
The cutter slipped through the fog like a knife beneath skin, the Black Marauder looming ahead, waiting in grim silence. On the bridge, the air was thick with tension, the kind that made even the instruments feel too loud. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] stood at the forward window, arms crossed tight against her chest. Rain trickled down the glass. Behind her, the crew gathered in knots — pacing, arguing, barely containing the storm building between them. [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] was the first to speak, voice tight with fury. “Slave running is cursed. We do this, we're gonna anger the Ember Saint. That ain’t cargo out there — it’s people.” [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]] nodded, arms folded. “Told ya it smelled wrong. Felt it in the water. Always trust the sea over a damn invitation from Satan himself.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] slammed his fist against the railing. “Screw the slugs. I ain't no filthy fuckin’ slave-runner. Let the Duke choke on his own mess.” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] kept his voice measured, but only just. “And then what? We turn and run? You think he won’t come after us? You think he doesn’t own half the damn ocean?” “Then let him come!” Cray barked. “Prick's already raising taxes on rations, fuel, repairs — everything. We screw this up loud, and we’re painting targets on every refugee dock from here to Gutter Row.” Cray turned to her, disbelief flaring. “So we lie down? Pretend we didn’t see the chains?” Clinton cut in. “We play it smart. We take the job. We move the cargo. Then we flip the board when the time’s right. [[Silas Vayne|Silas]] stepped in, shaking off rain, lighting a cigarette with a hand that didn’t tremble. “Lot of noise in here for pirates,” he said. “Look. I get it. Nobody likes it. But those slaves? They ain’t ours. Not our fight, not our problem. Slugs are. And they’ll buy more freedom than outrage ever will.” Darius snapped, “You hear yourself? [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] hadn’t moved. She was staring out into the rain, but not seeing it.

[[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] climbed in without a word, rifle slung over one shoulder, a quiet shadow in the half-light. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] secured the last latch on the tarp-covered crate, then gave the Marauder a long look, like a man hoping it wouldn’t be the last time. Up on the dock, [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] sparked a crooked roll-up and squinted down through the gloom. “Don’t like this smell, Cap’n,” he called. “Smells like rot. One o’ them rotten-egg-threw-up shit kinda smells, ya know?” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] didn’t look up. “Spoken like a poet. Just watch the Marauder, [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]]. If we're not back in two hours come in swinging steel.” “I’ll keep the fire lit, dear,” he called back, flashing a grin of broken teeth. The engine coughed to life like a dying beast. Rain smeared the view as they pulled away, the Marauder dissolving behind them into silhouette — a phantom ship waiting in limbo. Floodlights knifed through the downpour as the Silo came into view. Armored towers flanked the approach. Propaganda banners sagged with rain — THE DUKE SEES ALL. STRENGTH THROUGH ORDER. On the dock, [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] waited. He stood broad-shouldered and military hat pulled low over his face, arms folded, smoke curling from a foul roll-up clinging to his lip. His teeth looked like someone had sanded them with rust. As they docked, he didn’t move. “Well well,” he drawled. “If it ain’t the harbor rats come crawlin’ to the palace.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] was off the skiff before it stopped rocking. “If I’d known your ugly-ass mug was the welcome mat, I’d’ve poured acid in my good eye before we rolled out.” Rottwyler stepped forward, and so did Cray. Close. Weapons close. Breath close. “Say it to my face, fishboy,” Rottwyler snarled. “I got orders to let you in — don’t say I got orders to let you leave.” “You think I need your permission to crawl back out of this sewer, you gopher lookin' mother fucker?” Cray growled, stepping right up to Rottwyler. It was seconds from snapping. “Enough.” The voice cut clean through the rain. [[Emily Burton]] emerged from the shadows, heels sharp on wet stone, a Loyalist aide holding a black umbrella over her like a halo. Jet-black coat, crimson gloves, golden-banded hat. Regal and razor-sharp. She didn’t look at Rottwyler. “Sergeant, fall back before your insecurity soils the floor.” His jaw clenched. He obeyed. [[Emily Burton|Emily]] turned to [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], eyes cool and unreadable. “Captain Bonetooth. A pleasure. I’m [[Emily Burton|Emily Burton]], Duchess of [[Ashmoor]]. I’ll be escorting you from here.” “Didn’t realize royalty still rowed out in the rain,” Lyla said. “Only when the company promises to be more interesting than those inside...” She turned. “Follow me. Let’s not keep the Grand Duke waiting.”
The corridor stretched on like the gullet of some great beast — stone too polished, sconces too golden, air too still. [[Emily Burton|Emily]] led them in silence, her umbrella now carried like a blade under one arm. [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] walked just behind her, flanked by [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]], [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]], and [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]]. No one spoke until Emily glanced sideways, her voice low. “You handle your crew well. Most men in your place would’ve let that pissing match with Rottwyler spiral.” “If I wanted to watch two dogs hump over turf, I’d visit Gutter Row,” Lyla replied dryly. Emily smiled faintly. “Then we share taste. And patience.” They passed under a heavy iron arch flanked by twin statues of the Duke in battle gear. Emily’s tone shifted—softer, deliberate. “You don’t like being here. But let me offer you something that might dull the edge.” Lyla’s eye narrowed. “Gonna tell me the Duke’s really a kind soul under all that blood and bullshit?” Emily laughed, quiet and real. “No. He’s exactly what he looks like, almost to a fault. But the world is uglier than he is. And sometimes... order is better than chaos, Captain.” Lyla didn’t answer. Her boots echoed hollowly in the silence that followed. They reached a set of towering black iron doors inlaid with gold filigree. Emily stopped. “This is where I leave you. Raynar will take it from here. Try not to look too amused — he hates that.” “Appreciate the walk, Duchess,” Lyla said. “You might not after what he asks of you.” Emily turned and strode away, her heels clicking in final punctuation. The doors opened. Inside was marble and velvet, propaganda screens flickering gently like coals. The Raiders were ushered into a waiting chamber. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] muttered, arms crossed. “Feels like a goddamn museum where the exhibits watch you.” [[Zadie Adeyemi|Zadie]] murmured, “They don’t like that we don’t bow.” [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] added, “They don’t like that we’re breathing.” [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]] said nothing. Just stared at the velvet portraits, at the golden busts, at the rot hidden under the polish. Finally, [[Raynar Ventura]] arrived. Thin smile, ash-grey Loyalist uniform crisp enough to cut glass. “Captain Bonetooth. Apologies for the delay. The Duke is ready.” The Raiders followed him into a hall of black stone and mounted skulls. And at its end — seated behind a table of iron, a fireplace casting flickers across his tailored white suit — sat [[The Duke]]. “Ah… the infamous [[Rustwater Raiders]]. Salt-stained, smoke-slick, and somehow still standing. Welcome to [[Ashmoor]].” “Thank you, My Duke but we didn’t come for the tour,” said [[Lyla Bonetooth|Lyla]], cool and clear. He offered them seats. They didn’t move. [[The Duke]] smiled like a wolf with a napkin. “I have a transport that requires discretion. From the east wing docks to the [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] Docks in [[Steeltown]]. No flags. No questions.” “What kind of cargo?” Clinton asked, eyes narrowed.

[[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] was first to ask. “Where, then?” She turned to face them, face set like iron. “Somewhere the Wrecking Crew’ll see us coming.” [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] stared. “They'll sink us, it's suicide.” “No,” Lyla said. “It’s a signal.” The rain intensified. [[Clinton Firebay|Clinton]] busied himself clearing the nav panel, but his thoughts were elsewhere. He was weighing outcomes, survival odds, tradeoffs of principle. He had always been the tactician. His anger was volcanic, but under it, fear coiled tight. Not fear of death — fear of becoming something he hated. A slaver. A coward. He grunted and slammed the locker shut. The quiet plea. Zadie didn’t pray. But in that moment, she came close. [[Darius Adeyemi|Darius]] worked in the hold, shifting crates with quiet reverence. He hummed a low, mournful tune under his breath — something old, from before the tides swallowed home. Each motion seemed part ritual, part resignation. [[Salt-Eye Marlow|Salt-Eye]] ran a cloth over the controls. Slow, methodical. He muttered to himself about ghosts and tides and the way steel breathes before a storm. But he didn’t stop. He was too old to pretend there was ever a clean path in this world. [[Silas Vayne|Silas]] leaned in a corner, smoke curling from his lips. He said nothing, watched everything. The edge in his eyes dulled, but not gone. He didn’t believe in heroes. Still didn’t. But something about Lyla’s silence — and that child’s stare — had burrowed under his skin. No one spoke. But each of them, in their own way, was already moving. Not from command. From conviction. On the bridge, Lyla studied the charts. [[Blacktide Cray|Cray]] joined her, arms crossed. “You sure about this? Wrecking Crew might shoot first, ask questions never.” “[[Jimmy Douglass]] is smart,” she said. “He’ll know we wouldn’t come into their shores all bold unless we had a reason.” Cray frowned. “And what then? They just take the slaves and let us skip away?” Lyla’s eyes locked with his. “Well...yeah.” She folded the chart. The Black Marauder hummed to life. It had begun.
# THE AFTERBURN The sky was ash — not clouded, not storming, just dead. A dull black dome split by silent flashes of red lightning that never struck ground. Beneath it, a city burned. Not all at once. Not in rage. It burned with method, building by building, block by block. Collapsing inward like rotten teeth pulled one by one. Figures moved through the wreckage. Some crawled. Some limped. Some leapt — unnaturally, jaggedly, like puppets torn from tangled wire. They were not men. Not anymore. Twisted limbs of steel and flesh, wires dangling from exposed spines, eyes like shattered glass gleaming with static. One of them slammed through a wall like it was paper. Another dragged what might once have been a person — screaming, struggling — across hot concrete until the screaming stopped. In the distance, a towering thing stumbled through the smoke. It looked almost human. Almost. One half of its face was still skin. The other half was machinery pulsing with erratic red light. Its mouth opened, and something between a siren and a sob burst forth. Electricity danced across the rubble like insects, alive and feeding. And then — silence. [[Prophet Veerah]] woke with a gasp. Not a scream — her breath had no voice left. Her eyes glowed white in the dark, unblinking. Sweat poured down her face. Her veil had slipped from her head, revealing silvered hair plastered to her skin. Her fingers clawed at her bedding, but she didn’t move to rise. The candlelight flickered, shadows writhing like they too had seen the dream. She whispered only once, barely more than a breath: “It’s almost time.” Thunder rolled beyond the walls of the swamp. Something in the dark shifted. And watched.

# Chapter 03:

#### _Moonday night, 7th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When two off-duty [[Loyalist Guard]] take their power trip too far behind [[Hollow House]], they come face to face with a shadow the city pretends doesn’t exist. As [[Shana]] fights for survival, a chain rings through the alley, and with it, [[The Grim Man]] delivers his silent judgment. Blood hits brick, legend becomes real, and a quiet pact is sealed in the dark.

And somewhere else in [[Steeltown]], a message is delivered. Not everyone welcomes it.

# THE AFTERBURN 


Inside the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]’s clubhouse, the low thump of old speakers mixed with the clink of bottles and the buzz of tired men swapping half-truths and bruises. [[Mark Jeffrey]] leaned over the table, sorting through ledgers that smelled faintly of blood and beer.

Across from him, [[Joe Ameen]] stared out the grimy front window, frowning.

"We got company," [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] said, tilting his head. "Loyalists. Two of 'em."

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] looked up slowly, chewing on a toothpick. "Fuck off. Uniformed?"

"Oh yeah. Full swagger. One of ‘em’s got a smile like he's Morris fuckin' Gable."

Mark rose and the two stepped outside to greet the unannounced visitors.

Two [[Loyalist Guard]] officers were already halfway across the lot, walking like they were posing for a recruitment poster. One held a black envelope sealed with wax, the Duke’s sigil stamped in silver.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] folded his arms. "You boys know where you are right now? Hollow House is in Gutter Row, not here..."

The smiling guard stopped, but the smirk didn’t leave his face. "We’re right where we’re supposed to be. On orders of The Duke. Why don't you show some good faith for once. The Duke wanted to...extend a hand...to the Wrecking Crew."

[[Joe Ameen]] barked a short laugh. "I got something I'll extend right back to ya."

The other guard, younger, eyes hard, stepped forward a half pace. "You wanna keep this civil, maybe you ease off the tone."

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] didn’t flinch, but he also doesn't let people get in [[Joe Ameen|Joe]]'s face. "You bring weapons into my yard, and now you wanna tell us how we're gonna talk on our own land? You better tell us why you're here. Now. Or I'm going to stop being such a good host, you know?"

The older guard raised the envelope. "Just an invitation. To the [[Ashmoor Festival]]. A celebration of unity. Brotherhood. Prosperity. Compliments of The Duke."

"Ha! The Duke wants us at his little festival?" [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] muttered.

He held out the envelope.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] took the envelope without looking at it, eyes locked on the guard.

"You done?"

The guard’s smile faded a notch. He gave a stiff nod. He looked at [[Joe Ameen|Ameen]] and his eyes narrowed. "Enjoy the evening."

The guards turned and left, boots echoing across the clubhouse lot.

[[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] and [[Joe Ameen|Joe]] watched them go in silence.

[[Joe Ameen|Joe]] muttered, "The fuck was that? Since when does [[The Silo]] invite us to anything?"

"Maybe it's bait," [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]] said, pulling out a lighter. He set the envelope aflame, held it for a beat, then lit his cigarette with the burning invitation.

He dropped the scorched paper and ground it under his boot.

Smoke curled past his lips.

"Fuck [[The Duke]]."

And the wind carried the ashes down the rough lot of the Wrecking Crew clubhouse.

NOTE TITLE: [[03 - The Devil In The Row]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/03.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/The Grim Man","character/Shana"],"tags":["chapter","chapter3","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.","created":"2025/05/23 09:05:27","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:11"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ### The Devil In The Row The back door to [[Hollow House]] moaned on its hinges as [[Shana]] pushed it open, the sounds of [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] blared from the small television set behind her. She stepped into the alley like she owned it, because she did. Behind the club was narrow and slick with old rain, the cobblestones uneven, glinting faintly in the gutterlight that poured from a rusted fixture above the door. The scent was a mix of wet trash, coppery old blood, and perfume that clung to her coat like a memory she hadn’t shaken off yet. Posters hyping the upcoming [[Bobby Cutman]] vs. [[Bastian Redd]] fight were plastered all over the old walls. She exhaled slow, struck a match against the brick, and lit a roseleaf cigarette. The tip flared orange, glowing like a signal in the dark. She leaned her back to the wall, tilted her head up, and closed her eyes. It had been a good night. No trouble, full house, tips generous. The girls were asleep or drunk or busy. She had fifteen minutes to herself, and she was going to make them count. That’s when she heard the boots. Heavy steps, staggered rhythm, scraping and clunking against the stone. Two shadows rounded the mouth of the alley, backlit by the neon hum of [[GUTTER ROW]]’s signage. Tall, armored, but sloppy. [[Loyalist Guard]] — off-duty by the stink of them. One had his helmet half-off, dangling from the strap. His face was round, pale, and shiny with sweat. The other was leaner, sharper, with a scar slicing through his eyebrow and down his cheek like someone had tried to write a message in his face. “Hey now,” the fat one said, voice slurring just enough to smell the booze on it. “Ain’t this a rare treat.” The scarred one smiled with too many teeth. “Evening, love. Didn’t know [[Hollow House]] did alley service.” [[Shana]] didn’t move. She took another drag, let the smoke drift lazily from her lips. “We don’t. Move along.” The fat one squinted. “Wait a minute. That’s [[Shana]], ain’t it? The Rat Queen herself. Thought you’d be taller.” [[Shana]] flicked ash onto the ground. “And I thought [[Loyalist Guard]] were fine, upstanding citizens. Looks like we’re both disappointed.” The scarred one laughed, stepped in closer, boots scraping. He smelled like sweat and engine grease and the sour tang of cheap distillery hooch. “Relax, sweetheart. We’re just being neighborly. Share a smoke with your heroes.” “You’re not my heroes,” [[Shana]] said, eyes steady. “You’re two half-drunk pigs who think a badge makes your dick bigger. Go home.” The fat one’s face twitched. “You got a sharp mouth for a whore.” [[Shana]] didn’t blink. “And you’ve got a loose grip on your lips for a man talking out of line.” That landed. The fat one took a step forward, reaching for her arm. [[Shana]] didn’t wait. She slapped his hand away and jabbed a knuckle into his throat with practiced speed. He gagged, stumbled back, coughing and grabbing at his neck. The scarred one snarled and lunged from behind. His arm wrapped around her shoulders, the other clamping hard over her mouth. [[Shana]] kicked back, heels catching his shin, but he held tight. “Feisty little bitch, ain't ya?” he muttered into her ear. “Let’s take this somewhere quieter.” The fat one recovered, red-faced and furious. “Gonna make you beg now, you cunt.” They dragged her deeper into the alley, past the dumpsters and the rotting crates, down where the lights didn’t reach. [[Shana]]’s scream was muffled by a dirty glove, her legs kicking, hands clawing at the scarred one’s arms. Her cigarette hit the ground behind them, still glowing faint. No one came. No one ever did. Not back here.
The guards shoved [[Shana]] down hard behind the dumpster, her back hitting the bricks with a grunt. She scrambled to her feet, teeth bared, eyes blazing. "Come on, you pathetic fucks," she spat, fists raised. "Let’s see if your cocks can still work after I twist them off." The fat one laughed as he cracked his knuckles. "Still got bite. That’s cute." The scarred one moved first, fast and brutal, slamming a fist into her stomach. [[Shana]] doubled over, gasping, but didn’t fall. The fat one grabbed her by the shoulders and threw her against the dumpster. Her skull rang against the metal with a dull thud. "Fucking bitch," the scarred one hissed, pulling at her coat. "You’re gonna be thanking us when we're through with ya." "Flip for it?" the fat one said, already unbuckling his belt. "Nah," his partner replied, grinning. "Let’s make it a game. First one to finish gets her teeth as a souvenir." They both laughed, rough and hungry. [[Shana]] lashed out, raking her nails across the scarred one’s cheek. He roared, punched her across the face, and blood sprayed from her lip. Her legs folded. They moved in. _CLANG._ Then they froze. A metallic echo cracked through the alley, sharp and final, like a starting bell in hell. Both men turned their heads. He was there. Standing twenty feet down the alley, half-shrouded in shadow. A long coat hanging still around his tall frame, soaked in the dark. One arm held out, the end of a thick iron chain looped around his hand. At the far end, a long spike rested on the cobblestone, the tip stained and gleaming. His ominous white hockey mask almost glowing in the shadows. [[The Grim Man]]. The fat one squinted. "What the fuck is this, costume night?" The scarred one shifted nervously. "It’s him. The fucking chain freak." [[The Grim Man]] didn’t move. Didn’t speak. Just stood there, the chain twitching once, slow and deliberate. "Back off," the fat one barked. "This ain’t your business, freak." No reply. Only the sound of the spike tapping the cobblestone as [[The Grim Man]] slowly lifts and drops the chain. _Tap. Tap. Tap. Tap._ The scarred one took a breath, forcing a smile. "You gonna play superhero now? Try to stop us?" The chain shifted again. _Tap. Tap. Tap._ The fat one spat. "You think you scare me? I’ll fuckin’ gut you."

NOTE TITLE: [[03 - The Devil In The Row]] METADATA:{"cover":[["zz_media/03.png"]],"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter","character/The Grim Man","character/Shana"],"tags":["chapter","chapter3","story"],"date":"7th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"When two off-duty Loyalist Guards go too far behind Hollow House, they cross paths with the silent wrath of The Grim Man, and as blood stains the alley, a brutal legend is made real and a warning ripples through Steeltown, uninvited and unwelcome.","created":"2025/05/23 09:05:27","modified":"2025/06/06 20:56:11"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) The chain shifted again. _Tap. Tap. Tap._ The fat one spat. "You think you scare me? I’ll fuckin’ gut you." They let go of [[Shana]], turning to face him fully. One drew a small baton. The other, a stubby, rusted sidearm. They advanced slowly, trying to circle him. [[The Grim Man]] didn’t move. Didn’t breathe. Didn’t care.
The alley exploded with movement. [[The Grim Man]] snapped his arm forward, the chain ripping through the air with a banshee’s wail. The spike struck the fat guard just above the nose and kept going, punching through his skull and out the back. Bone and blood splattered the brick. The body dropped like a puppet with cut strings, collapsing in a twitching heap before the scream even finished echoing. [[Shana]] stared, frozen in disbelief. One heartbeat, and the man who had been pawing at her was nothing but a pile of meat and steam. The scarred guard jolted into action, panic taking hold. He raised the pistol and squeezed the trigger, twice. Bullets screamed down the alley, ricocheting off the dumpster and sparking against the bricks. But [[The Grim Man]] was already gone, vanished into the shadows like he'd been swallowed whole. [[Shana]] ducked low behind the bins, her breath caught in her throat, heart pounding like a war drum. Her eyes scanned the darkness, desperate for a shape, a shadow, anything. All she saw was the fat guard’s body cooling in the gutter, the alley still choked with silence. She didn’t know whether to scream or laugh. "Shit, holy shit, fuck," the guard muttered, voice shaking as much as the gun in his hand. He backed away, breath sharp, feet scraping. Silence. Then a sound, faint and deliberate. _Tap._ The guard spun toward it, gun raised. Nothing there. Another step. Another breath. _Tap._ He pivoted again, wide-eyed, lips twitching with fear. He edged toward the dumpster, heart hammering. "Fuck you!" Peeked around it. Empty. He turned around, confused, then his mouth opened to call out again, maybe to plead, maybe to scream. _WHACK._ [[Shana]]’s boot hit him dead in the crotch. He collapsed forward with a strangled moan, both hands instinctively reaching down as the pistol slipped from his grip. [[The Grim Man]] was behind her in the same instant. No warning. No sound. Just presence. He moved like a guillotine, fast, final. One hand grabbed the guard’s collar, the other twisting his arm behind his back with bone-grinding force. The man shrieked, struggling, but it didn’t matter. [[The Grim Man]] was relentless. He yanked the cuffs from the guard’s belt and snapped them onto his wrists with a brutal click that echoed like a sentence passed. Then, without ceremony, he lifted him off the ground and walked him to the dumpster. The man’s boots scraped the stone. He screamed, begged, thrashed. Didn’t matter. [[The Grim Man]] smashed him with the butt of his spike one final time and hurled him headfirst into the bin. The lid slammed shut like a judge’s gavel. The alley went still.
[[Shana]] stood in the hush that followed, her breath steaming in the cold alley air. Blood painted her mouth, but her eyes were steady. She turned slowly. [[The Grim Man]] was still there, standing like a statue at the alley’s edge, the chain coiled in one gloved hand. The mask turned toward her. He didn’t speak. He never did. [[Shana]] took a cautious step forward, then another, until she was close enough to see the scuffs on his boots, the dull sheen of dried blood on the spike. "Thank you," she said. Her voice was hoarse but steady. "For stepping in. For saving me there." She motioned to the dead guard on the ground. Grim Man didn’t move. She gave a half-laugh, bitter at the edges. "I’ve heard stories. They say you live in the walls. That you can smell blood in the air. That you don’t stop. Not for anyone." [[The Grim Man]] tilted his head slightly. Not a nod. Not a denial. Just... acknowledgment. "They call you the Grim Man," she continued, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand. Her voice was steadier now, threaded with something curious, something darker. "I heard you’re a ghost. Some say a demon. Had a drunk in here once who swore you saved him from a gut-stabbing in Charspire, right outside the glass foundry. He nearly pissed himself telling the story. Said he heard the chain before he saw the blood...and now I see why." She stepped closer. Close enough to smell the iron and rain still clinging to his coat. "But I don’t think you’re a ghost. I think you’re a man. A very, very dangerous man. The kind we need in Gutter Row, even if nobody wants to admit it." Still no answer. Her eyes flicked over his mask. "You're not gentle, or soft, or kind. But you make the monsters question if they should come out at night. And sometimes," she said, brushing a lock of red hair behind her ear, "it's good to know there is someone like you out there." She reached up, slow, deliberate, and wiped a smudge of blood off his mask with her thumb. Her fingers lingered a moment longer than they needed to. She looked him straight in the eyes behind that mask. "I owe you. You ever need something, anything, you come find me. Doesn’t matter what it is. I’ll make it happen." [[The Grim Man]] gave a slow nod. One motion. Measured. Heavy. Then he turned, melted into the shadows without a word, the chain dragging behind him. _Tap._ _Tap._ _Tap._ Until even that faded, and all that was left was the silence. [[Shana]] stood alone in the dark, staring after him. Then she reached into her coat, cleaned the blood from her face, dusted herself off, pulled out a second cigarette, and lit it with a steading hand, eyeing the dead guard. "Ember fuckin' damnit now I gotta deal with this...," she whispered. And the smoke curled into the night.

[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] grinned at her. [[Ava Victoria|Ava]] leaned closer to him. "Mmm..how about tonight? You want to come by later?" "Oh you know I do." Pale as snow and in a small, disheveled black dress she stared at him, smiling an unsettling smile. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stopped cold. # THE AFTERBURN A long marble table stretched under the arched windows of the Duke’s private chamber, candles flickering along its length. Velvet drapes hung still. The skyline of [[Ashmoor]] loomed outside, ghosted in fog. [[The Duke]] sat at the head of the table, sipping dark liquor from a crystal tumbler. Beside him, [[Emily Burton|Emily]], his wife, stirred a cup of pale tea. Across from them, [[General Colt]] of the Loyalist Guard, [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], and [[Raynar Ventura]] shared in casual conversation—laughter, veiled threats, and cold smiles. “I trust everything’s in place for my announcement then?” [[the Duke]] asked, eyes flicking toward [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]]. [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] nodded. “Everything. Mr. [[Owen McCready|McCready]] at [[TTV Studios]] will broadcast your address live to the territories. He's assured me cameras and crew will be here the morning of.” [[The Duke]] nodded and looked to [[General Colt|Colt]]. “And the [[Loyalist Guard]] is prepared for any opposition throughout the territories?” [[General Colt|Colt]] didn’t speak. [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] did. “We’ve got boots across Tribucia. If anybody tries to rally a crowd, we'll stomp it out. Quick.” [[The Duke]] looked pleased and turned his attention back to [[Raynar Ventura]]. "And what of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]? Have they made their intentions of attending the festival known yet?" [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] paused, "Well, My Duke, invitations were delivered. I've been told to [[Mark Jeffrey]] directly. However there has been no response as of yet, I'm afraid." [[The Duke]] nodded and looked out the window for a moment, before addressing Raynar once again. "I see. Has there been word from [[Lyla Bonetooth|Bonetooth]] and the [[Rustwater Raiders]] yet?" "Only a report of [[the Black Marauder]] cutting down the [[Water#Grave Bay|Grave Bay]] coast towards [[Steeltown]], My Duke." [[Raynar Ventura|Raynar]] said. "It seems they're heading to where they should be. Uh, one other matter I should bring to your attention My Duke, it seems one of our [[Loyalist Guard]]s in [[Gutter Row]] had their head impaled with what appears to be a large spike-like object. We know this because we found his partner handcuffed, screaming, covered in piss..." Raynar chuckled. "...and tossed inside a dumpster. He claims the [[Gutter Row]] boogeyman did it but has yet to explain what he was doing there in the first place. We're pressing him for more accurate info."[[03 - The Devil In The Row|*]] [[The Duke]] listened to Raynar. "I see. Keep me abreast of the situation." [[Emily Burton|Emily]] blinked, setting her tea down gently. “You keep dancing around the topic, My Duke. What’s the announcement?” [[The Duke]] leaned back in his chair, fingers steepled. “Ah, my dear. Well, due to production and manufacturing costs rising across Tribucia, a 70% tax increase on fuel out of [[Charspire]]. Food out of [[Threshton]]. And steel out of [[Steeltown]] will be necessary to continue on the enlightened path we are on, you see. I'll announce the increase at the Festival and will be in effect 1st day of [[CALENDAR|Greensun]].” [[Emily Burton|Emily]] sat up straighter, eyes narrowing. “What? But the taxes on basic necessities are already high enough. That’ll ruin people. They already can’t afford to survive. [[Jacoban Clay]] doesn't need another home in [[Ashmoor#Diamond Valley]]. He doesn't need to raise the costs of anything if he so chooses!”

(cont'd) [[The Duke]] turned his head slightly at his wife. His eyebrows furrowing slightly. “It’s necessary. [[Charspire]]’s furnaces don’t fuel themselves. The Guard doesn’t march for free. This palace, this territory, all of [[Ashmoor]]—it requires sacrifice. Sacrifice, I might add, that contributes to your...delicate...way of life here at [[The Silo]]. Isn't that right, dear?”

[[Emily Burton|Emily]] looked around the table, searching for support, but found none. [[General Colt]] stared at his drink. [[Raynar Ventura]] looked at the ceiling. [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] simply sat there, shoulders square, gaze locked.

“Disgraceland is starving,” [[Emily Burton|Emily]] said. “This won’t bring order. It’ll bring riots. Blood.”

“Then let them bleed. The only way Tribucia continues on, even thrives in the new world is by sacrifice for the greater good of our new nation. If Tribucia is truly to become a utopia then we need too weed out the weak. It's necessity." [[The Duke]] smiled faintly, his voice low.  "Trust me, my dear. I know what is best for you, for our people, for this entire nation.”

[[Emily Burton|Emily]] pressed her lips together. Her voice, when it came, was quiet and sharp. “You forget what desperation breeds.”

[[Sgt. Rottwyler|Rottwyler]]’s eyes snapped to her. Cold. Unmoving. A predator beneath the uniform. [[The Duke]] glared at his wife, "And you forget your place. By all means, my grand Duchess, if you want to go live in [[Gutter Row]] with the rats instead of here at the palace, be my guest." He snarled.

Neon signs buzzed overhead, casting sickly pink and green light across the wet cobblestones. Hawkers barked over each other from metal stalls, selling everything from fake teeth to real nightmares. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] grinned like a man who thought the world should kiss his rings. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] didn’t move. Just waited. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] spotted him and peeled off from the flow, stepping up like they were old friends. “[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]], baby. Hope you haven't been waiting long, I was just..uh.. getting aquainted with my new friends here.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] grins and the girls laugh. “Just waiting on you,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said, flicking ash at his feet. “Didn’t want to interrupt your strut.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] chuckled, flashing teeth. “So, what you doing calling me down here to this shithole for, [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]? They’re talking.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]] stepped forward, close enough for his breath to sour the air between them. “You know what you’re doing? You realize this ain’t ‘fuckin DIY Drug Week,’ right? You start pushing your shit in our streets, you ain’t just quitting. You’re competing. You’re coming at the Murray Boys.” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] smiled. Not wide. Just enough. “I know exactly what the fuck I'm doing, [[Nico Murray|Nico]]. Now run on home and tell Daddy for me.” “You dumb piece of shit.” [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s face went red. The girls looked nervous now, backing up a step. “You think Marco’s gonna let you live?” “I think I’m not scared of you,” [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] said. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] snapped—swung wild, fast. But [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] moved faster, ducking the punch like he’d seen it in a dream. Then his hand whipped out—crack—a slap across [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s face that turned heads. Not a brawl. Not a beatdown. Just enough to humiliate. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] staggered, blinking, the left side of his face going bright red. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stepped closer, voice low. “You wanna be your old man so bad, [[Nico Murray|Nico]], but you ain’t got the brains or the balls. You’re just a boy playin’ gangster. Oh, and tell your mom I said hello.” The blonde’s jaw dropped. The buzzcut girl laughed once, sharp and loud before covering her mouth. [[Nico Murray|Nico]]’s breath hissed through his teeth. His fists clenched. Then he turned and walked. Fast. The girls hesitated—then followed. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] stayed a while longer, finishing his smoke. The market didn’t care. It moved on like always. But something had just shifted under its skin.
[[Nico Murray|Nico]] stomped up the stone path to the Murray House, boots loud against the wet cobbles. The home was an old mansion in the old days that had been renovated over the years into a large, two story townhome. The walk from Three Nail Market hadn’t cooled his blood—if anything, it had stoked the fire. The slap still burned. Inside, the house was all shadows and golden trim—Tribucian wealth soaked in old violence. He found [[Rosa Murray]], his mother, in the sitting room, ledger open, pen tapping in rhythm. [[Marco Murray|Marco]]]] sat nearby, slow-burning a cigar, watching smoke curl toward the chandelier, reading over that day's edition of the [[Tribucia Tribute]]. “What happened?” [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]] asked without looking up. [[Nico Murray|Nico]] pulled off his coat and tossed it at a chair. “Lash fuckin' [[Lash Hawkins|Hawkins]] happened. He’s out. Says he’s not pushing [[Luxyn]] for us anymore.” That got their attention. [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]]’s pen stopped. [[Marco Murray|Marco]] exhaled a long stream of smoke. "The boy is out?" [[Marco Murray|Marco]] inquired.

# Chapter 05:

#### _Temperday, 8th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

In the fog-choked wilds of [[The Drownlands]], twin hunters [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] and [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] complete the sacred rite to become Unseen, pledging their lives to the goddess Mirella. With [[Riley Thorne]] guiding them, they embark on their quest to become Widows and find an unlikely first kill.

Meanwhile, far from the mire, [[Ava Victoria]] searches the chaos of [[Gutter Row]] for the vanished [[Lash Hawkins]], forcing an uneasy alliance with [[Nico Murray]] as shadows gather and secrets deepen.

# THE AFTERBURN 


Three Nail Market swelled with steam, smoke, and shouting.

[[Ava Victoria]] shouldered her way through the crowd, desperation souring her sweat. She darted past fishmongers and pipe-hawkers, past screaming kids and drunk old women pissing in the gutter. Her eyes scanned every stall, every alley, every scrap of shadow.

"[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]?!" she shouted at a knot of gamblers. "You seen [[Lash Hawkins]]?!"

No one answered. One man laughed in her face. Another turned his back.

She cursed under her breath, spun around, and nearly collided with [[Nico Murray]].

"You! You motherfucker!"

[[Nico Murray|Nico]] raised his hands, startled. "Whoa, [[Ava Victoria|Ava]], easy—"

"Don’t ‘easy’ me! Where the fuck is he?!"

"Who? [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]? What’re you talking about?"

"Don’t play dumb with me, [[Nico Murray|Nico]]!" she hissed. "He’s gone! I’ve been looking for him since last night and no one knows shit!"

[[Nico Murray|Nico]] frowned. "I haven’t seen him. Not since last evening..."

He paused.

"He slapped me outside the market. I left after that."

[[Ava Victoria|Ava]] stared at him, jaw tight, eyes full of fire and confusion.

"That’s it?"

"That’s it," Nico said. "I swear."

A long silence. [[Ava Victoria|Ava]]’s breathing slowed. Her shoulders dropped, just a little.

"Fuck," she muttered. "Sorry. I just—something’s wrong."

"Yeah," [[Nico Murray|Nico]] said. "It seems that way."

For reasons he couldn’t name, something twisted in his gut. A feeling like guilt—or maybe dread.

"I’ll help you look," he said.

[[Ava Victoria|Ava]] narrowed her eyes. "If your family—if the [[Murray Boys|Murrays]] had anything to do with this..."

"They didn’t," [[Nico Murray|Nico]] said, sharper now. "We didn’t. I promise."

He held her gaze.

She held it back.

For now, it was enough.

The narrative highlights the harsh realities of their world, from brutal military training under General Colt, chosen by the twins as their first target, to the cutthroat environment of Gutter Row. --- # SIGHT UNSEEN The marsh whispered. Thick fog draped over twisted reeds and drowned cypress roots. Every step sank with a quiet suck into the muck, and somewhere beyond the gray haze, a fat boar grunted and rooted through the brush. Oblivious. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] crouched low, still as bone. A flick of her fingers. A tilt of her head. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] moved in tandem, ghostlike through the slush. No words. Just the silent code they had shared since birth—eyes, hands, breath. The boar shuffled forward, snorting at a patch of damp ferns. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] pulled the bow from her back in a single slow motion. Drew. Held. Let the arrow loose. The boar screamed and charged three feet before [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] exploded from the scrub. Her blade kissed the throat in one swift arc, spraying steam and blood into the cold air. The marsh went silent again. They knelt by the corpse, hands blood-wet, grinning. "[[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] will feast well," [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] said. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] nodded. "It's good meat. We honor her with this." The sisters worked in rhythm, stringing the boar with braided vine and slinging it between them on a rough pole. As they moved through the mist, their shapes blurred into the wild. At the edge of the bush, [[Riley Thorne]] waited. Cloak damp, one hand on the hilt of her curved blade, the other flipping a carved bone token over and over. "Well done. That was clean and silent, you were Unseen" Riley said, eyes flicking from the boar to the twins. "You're almost ready." [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] smirked. "Almost?" "You want the rite," Riley said, stepping aside to let them pass. "You need more than blood. You need fire." [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] grinned, teeth sharp in the gloom. "Then let's burn." The fog swallowed them whole as they made their way back to the compound.
They stepped from the wild into the compound’s tangled clearing, a wide sprawl of land nestled deep in the mire. Earthen huts rose from the muck like fungi, their walls packed with clay and root, thatched with swampgrass and reeds. Raised walkways of scavenged planks and knotted vines connected the homes, elevated just enough to stay dry above the constant wet. Smoke drifted up from clay chimneys, and voices carried through the mist—low songs, soft prayers, the sound of knives being sharpened. Lanterns swung from skeletal tree limbs, casting flickers across pools of stagnant water and mud-slick trails. Totems made of bone, wood, and twisted iron lined the perimeter, watching in silence. Animal skulls, carved with runes and hung with swamp lilies, marked thresholds. The air was thick with the scents of wet moss, rendered fat, and incense smoke. [[Len Vyne]] waited at the threshold, arms crossed, hood thrown back to show her dark cropped hair. "You're back just in time," she said. "Come. [[Prophet Veerah]] has seen something. She's gathered the sisters." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] exchanged a glance with the twins, then nodded. They followed Len through the winding paths between huts, past hanging charms and smoldering braziers, until they reached the sermon stand—a moss-slick platform built beneath the roots of a fallen oaktree, its bark etched with symbols of Mirella's many faces. [[Prophet Veerah]] stood tall above a semicircle of gathered sisters, no less than a dozen in all. Her black robe was wet from the knees down, her eyes bright with vision-madness. She held a staff capped with a hollowed horn, which she tapped thrice on the wood. When she saw [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] and the twins approach, she smiled. "And how did they do?," she called. The group walked forward. "Excellent, Sister." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] began. "The twins made sure we have an offering to [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] tonight." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] looked at the twins pleased as they bowed slightly to her. They joined the crowd. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] raised her arms, voice ringing like thunder through the still fog. "I was graced last night, sisters. I was graced by the beloved [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] in my dreams. And as thankful as I am that [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] has chosen me to speak with, what she has shown me fills me with pain." She turned slowly, letting her gaze fall on each face. "She showed me fire," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said, her voice high and trembling. "A war not yet born, but near. I saw creatures of metal and flesh, things with half human, half mechanical bodies but endless, unsatiating hunger. They tore through the land like rot through fruit, killing all. I saw no banners, no flags, no names. Only blood. Only screaming." The crowd stirred. Some crossed themselves. Others reached for blades. "I do not know these beasts," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said. "Where they come from or what they want. But the vision was true. And [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]'s hand guided it." She stepped forward, eyes gleaming.

"This is her warning. If we do not act, they will come. They will raze the land. They will burn our goddess from root to bloom. We, the Widows, must stop it before it begins." A murmur of fear and fire spread through the gathered sisters. Some knelt. Others muttered prayers. A few whispered doubts. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] met the twins’ eyes again. No words. Just understanding.
The door to [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]]’s cabin creaked open under Riley’s hand. Inside, the space was dim and warm, thick with the scent of moss, sage smoke, and damp wood. Clay effigies of Mirella lined the walls, their many eyes carved deep and unblinking. Bundles of dried herbs hung from the ceiling, swaying gently with each breath of the wind. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] sat cross-legged near the hearth, the flicker of the fire painting her face in amber and shadow. She looked up as the trio entered. "Come. Sit." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]], [[Raina & Risa|Risa]], and [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] did as she asked, settling onto low cushions across from her. The warmth from the fire crackled between them. "[[Riley Thorne|Riley]]," [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] said, her voice soft but steady. "Are they ready?" [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] didn’t hesitate. "I believe they are. They hunt like shadows. Move like breath. Think as one." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]]’s eyes moved to the twins. "And you? Are you ready to leave behind the seen world and walk among the unseen?" [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] and [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] nodded in perfect sync. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] spoke first. "We are." [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] followed. "Yes, sister." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] studied them for a long moment, her expression unreadable. Then she rose. "Very well. Follow me." She led them out of the cabin into the chill evening air, the fog curling around their feet like curious spirits. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] trailed behind, silent, watchful. They followed a narrow trail that wound through ferns and roots slick with dew until it opened into a wide clearing perched on a small cliff. Below, [[The Drownlands]] sprawled into forever—a tapestry of water and green and gray, with ghostlights flickering in the far marsh. At the center of the clearing sat a blackened cauldron on a ring of carved stone. Strange sigils had been etched into the earth around it, faintly glowing with swamplight. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] approached the cauldron and knelt. She scooped mud from the base of a tree, added crushed bark, moss, strands of vine, and flecks of lichen from a stone. As she stirred the dark mixture with a wooden rod carved like a spine, she spoke. "This is her body," she said. "The land, the water, the sky. All that grows and rots. [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] is not above us. She is not distant. She is everything." The twins stood still, watching the motion of her hand, the rhythm of her words. "To walk with her, to speak her name in truth, you must consume her. Let her roots take hold in your blood. Let her breath mix with your own." [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] pulled two small clay cups from a pouch at her waist and filled them with the viscous, earthy brew. She rose and held them out. "Do you pledge your lives to [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]?" "We do," the twins said together. "Then drink. Become Unseen." The twins took the cups. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] drank first. The taste was bitter and alive, like wet leaves and iron. [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] followed, her throat working as she swallowed the body of a goddess. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] watched, eyes dark and full of fire. When they finished, she smiled. "You are now Unseen to man. Only [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] watches you now." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] gave a quiet nod of approval, the corner of her mouth twitching in pride. But [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] wasn’t finished. "But to fulfill your pledge, to become a Widow," she said, stepping closer, her tone sharpening like a blade drawn from its sheath, "you must each offer one life to the earth. One man each. Killed by your hand. Not for sport. Not for anger. To remove the male influence over your life and return their blood to their rightful mother, [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]]." The wind shifted, carrying the scent of rain. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] and [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] did not flinch. "We understand," said [[Raina & Risa|Risa]]. "We’re ready," said [[Raina & Risa|Raina]]. [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]] closed her eyes and raised her head to the sky. "Then [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]] guide your blades. And may the Drownlands drink deep." The clearing held its breath, and the sisters did not speak again.
A short time later, the trio emerged from the mire's tangle at the edge of [[The Drownlands]]. The air was heavy with brine and rot, the boundary between swamp and sea soft and shifting. To the east, Grave Bay opened wide and gray, waters choppy beneath a veiled sky. Out on the horizon, [[The Black Marauder]] moves fast through the waters, outlines cut a dark silhouette against the surf, its sails fat with wind, headed toward distant [[Steeltown]]. [[Raina & Risa|Risa]] shaded her eyes. "That’s the [[The Black Marauder|Marauder]]. They’re moving fast." "Oh wow, I've never seen it in person! [[Raina & Risa|Raina]] quipped. [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] nodded. "They're an impressive group. Loyal to nobody. They've attacked Loyalist, Wrecking Crew, Rancher's and everybody in between. They're led by a woman named [[Lyla Bonetooth|Bonetooth]]" "A woman leads the Raiders?" "Yes. A formidable one by all accounts too." [[Riley Thorne|Riley]] responded. At the center, barking commands like a man possessed, stood [[General Colt]]. Slim, bald and grim, his armor gleamed beneath the gray sun. His voice cracked through the air like breaking bones.

"Again! Again! That’s not a charge, that’s a piss-soaked stumble!"

When one recruit faltered, knees buckling in the mud, [[General Colt|Colt]] marched over like a stormfront. He didn’t hesitate. Grabbed the coiled whip from the rack and lashed it hard. Once. Twice. A third time that ripped cloth and drew blood.

"Useless! Fucking disgraceful! You shame the Guard!"

He kept going. Four. Five. Six. The recruit cried out, but [[General Colt|Colt]] didn’t stop. Not until the boy was curled into himself, trembling, the back of his tunic in tatters.

"On your feet!" [[General Colt|Colt]] roared, spittle flying. "Or I’ll break every bone you’ve got and send your mother the teeth!"

The recruit weakly tried to get up but [[General Colt|Colt]] planted his boot hard into his ribs. Even the other recruits had frozen, unmoving, their faces pale.

[[General Colt|Colt]]’s chest heaved as he dropped the whip and turned away like nothing had happened.

[[Raina & Risa|Risa]]’s jaw clenched.

# Chapter 06:

#### _Middleday, 9th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

When the feared [[The Black Marauder|Black Marauder]] makes an unannounced appearance in [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]], panic erupts—but what follows is anything but a raid. Tensions flare and strange allies are made, forcing the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] to weigh principle against pragmatism. 

Across the sea of dust in the Bloodroot Canyons, #1 [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] contender [[Bastian Redd]] is offered a chance at destiny—but at a cost that could redefine everything he stands for.

# THE AFTERBURN

In the wind-carved hollows of the Bloodroot Canyons of [[Threshton]], the air smelled of red dust and pine smoke. The sun had begun its slow descent behind the fractured stone spires, casting long, jagged shadows across the camp. Tents stitched from hide and nylon stood in a loose circle, smoke rising from a central fire where a few of [[Bastian Redd]]’s kin prepared dried meat and strong tea.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stood shirtless beneath a bone-hung awning, his braided hair damp with sweat, muscles slick and coiled as he pounded into a weathered heavy bag that swung from a tree limb. Each hit echoed through the canyon like distant thunder. His knuckles were taped raw. His breath came in controlled bursts.

From the ridge above, a slow clap sounded.

[[Flint Garritt]] descended the slope with that same lopsided grin he wore on every promotion poster in [[Disgraceland]]. Impeccable boots crunched red gravel, and a leather bag swung at his side.

"You look ready, [[Bastian Redd|Redd]]."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] didn’t stop punching. "[[Flint Garritt]]. What are you doing on my land? I didn't think you made house calls."

"I don’t, usually." [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] said, stepping under the awning. "But this ain’t just any usual fight, is it? You're 0 and 2 against [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]], [[Bastian Redd|Redd]]. It's now or never."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] finally stopped, wiping his brow with the back of his arm. He gave [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] a long, measuring look. "So what’s this?"

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] pulled a chair close with his foot. "To be blunt, I’m sick of [[Bobby Cutman]] holdin’ that belt. He’s stale. The company needs fresh blood. A new direction. I want **you** to be the new face of the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]]."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]’s eyes narrowed, then drifted back to the bag. "Yeah, that’s the plan."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] smiled. "Of course it is, of course it is. And I have every confidence in you, [[Bastian Redd|Bastian]]. Just...maybe I could offer a little help."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] threw a quick jab. "Don’t need help training."

"Not that kind of help."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] unzipped the leather bag and laid out two sleek, gleaming fight gloves. Heavy. Slightly too heavy. They thudded against the table like iron weights.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] walked over, picked one up. His brow furrowed at the heft.

"You want me to cheat?" he asked, voice low. "These gloves are loaded. I’d kill [[Bobby Cutman|Cutman]] wearin’ these."

"If the [[Church Of The Ember Saint|Ember Saint]] decides that then...," [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] shrugs. "It’s time the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] evolved. I’m just trying to help it along. You win, and the world’s yours. Fame, sponsors, the belt... Everything."

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stared at the gloves.

The sun dipped lower, a wolf’s howl curling through the canyons.

He shook his head. "Nah."

He tossed the gloves at [[Flint Garritt|Flint]]’s feet. "I’m gonna beat him clean. Or I’m not gonna beat him at all."

[[Flint Garritt|Flint]] crouched, picked them up with a smirk. "Suit yourself. Hope you’ve got what it takes. Because there ain’t gonna be any rematches."

Without another word, [[Flint Garritt|Flint]] turned and strode out of camp, his silhouette shrinking against the bleeding sunset.

[[Bastian Redd|Bastian]] stood there alone, fists clenched, the wind tugging at the edge of the heavy bag.

"I used to keep a picture of you I cut from the newspaper in my medbag. When I was stuck in the Underslums hospital, I told myself, ‘If [[Lyla Bonetooth]] can carve her way through the Iron Strait with nothing but a harpoon and spite, then I can survive a week of infected bite wounds and stolen antibiotics.’" Lyla smiled, visibly touched. [[Katie Kowalski|Katie]] turned to [[Selena Matissao|Selena]], who was watching and smiling and mouthed silently, **She winked at me**! The dingy scraped against the beach. "It was nice finally meeting you, [[Mark Jeffrey|Mark]]. Thank you for your help."

Meanwhile, a subplot reveals **Bastian Redd** grappling with a difficult choice: he refuses a promoter's offer to use **loaded gloves to cheat** in an upcoming fight against Bobby Cutman, emphasizing his commitment to fighting fairly. --- # SHOWDOWN IN GAGE PARK The last threads of dusk clung to the edges of [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]], casting a copper sheen over the wet stones of the pier. A chorus of gulls wheeled overhead, their cries mixing with the dull slap of waves against dock pilings and the lazy creak of moored skiffs. The air carried the sharp tang of fish guts and brine, undercut with the earthy musk of coal smoke drifting from distant furnaces deeper in [[Steeltown]]. Marlo Griggs, shoulders hunched beneath a faded canvas coat, tied the last loop on a crate of eel-baskets and nudged it closer to the bait shack. The day had been long, the catch half what it should've been, but that was how it always went this early in the season. He wiped his hands on his trousers and turned toward Lenny and old Rick, who were hunched over a gutted mackerel, squabbling like gulls. "I’m tellin’ you, that thing’s been dead since dawn," Lenny said, flicking a scale off his knuckle. "Smells like it marinated in piss." "Better than yours," Rick shot back, jabbing a fillet knife into the air. "I’ve seen pond frogs with more meat on 'em. You fishin’ with a net or a noose?" Marlo chuckled, reaching for his cigarette tin. "Least I don’t owe half the wharf a lunch tab, Rick. You still duckin’ Olga at the chow tent?" Rick grunted. "She overcharges. A full slug for boiled rockfish and week-old taters? Highway robbery." "She overcharges you 'cause you keep callin’ her Ma even though she’s twenty-two," Lenny added with a snort. Marlo barked a laugh, the tension of the day momentarily forgotten. He flicked a match to life with his thumbnail, shielding the flame from the wind. "Alright, boys, I’m callin’ it. Try not to stab each other ‘fore sun-up." He turned to spit into the bay then he saw it. Far out on the graying mirror of [[Water#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]], something vast and black was sliding in—too big for a fishing vessel, too fast for a merchant lug. It moved like a shadow uncoiling from the horizon, cutting through fog and smoke with a purposeful hunger. Marlo squinted, letting the match gutter out between his fingers. "[[El Santo]] be damned," he muttered. "No... no, no, that can’t be..." The flag unfurled first—tattered, midnight-red, a skull daubed in crude tar strokes, grinning wide beneath a crown of thorns. [[The Black Marauder]]. Marlo’s stomach lurched. He staggered back a step, eyes wide. "Oi! Lenny! Rick! You seein’ this?" he hollered, voice cracking like a rope under strain. Others turned. Muttered disbelief gave way to hushed curses, sharp inhalations. Then a scream—a mother dragging her twin boys toward the alley behind Sykes’ Alehouse. Nets dropped, knives forgotten. Men who’d spent thirty years gutting catfish bolted like colts at cannonfire. "They’re comin’ in!" Marlo shouted. "They’re comin’ to dock! Raiders!" The panic spread like oil on water. Someone overturned a cart. Dogs barked. A gang of boys scattered, their laughter shrill with fear. Marlo turned, feet already moving. He shoved past crates and barrels, heart pounding like a smith’s hammer. As he rounded the fishmonger’s corner, a heavy shoulder slammed into his. "Shit, Marlo! Watch it!" It was Lenny—tall, burly, still holding a dripping string of river perch. "No time!" Marlo gasped. "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]’s gotta know. Now." Lenny blinked, paling. "[[El Santo]] preserve us. Go, man. Go fast." Marlo didn’t need the push, but he got one anyway. Then he was gone, boots hammering the cobbles, ducking under laundry lines, leaping gutters, racing for the glow of [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] club house, each step an echo of war drums on the wind.
The deck of [[The Black Marauder]] groaned beneath the weight of salt-crusted timbers and the anticipation of her crew. Fog curled along the railings like ghost fingers, and the sails flapped low and heavy in the windless lull before action. From the forecastle, [[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]] looked like an overturned ant hill—figures scattering, smoke rising, and voices faintly shrieking in the distance. [[Blacktide Cray]] stood at the prow, arms folded, his long oilskin coat whispering against his boots. His face was unreadable under his long, unkempt hair and beard, but his jaw shifted with a slow grind of teeth. Beside him stood [[Lyla Bonetooth|Captain Lyla Bonetooth]], red scarf tied back around her black hair, eye-patch shining in the sunlight, knuckles tight on the hilt of her belt-knife. [[Silas Vayne]] leaned against the rail, picking grime from under his nails with a needle blade. "Maybe this was a bad idea," [[Blacktide Cray]] muttered, voice low like thunder before the break. [[Silas Vayne]] spat into the sea. "The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]]'s gonna hit us hard. They really don't like un-announced visits to their territory. " [[Blacktide Cray]] nodded once. "You're not wrong. We need to be ready."

# Chapter 07:

#### _Restday, 11th of [[CALENDAR|Bloomsun]], 2186_

On the eve of a state-sponsored broadcast, tensions erupt behind the scenes at [[TTV Studios]] as [[Jaden Kade]] clashes with [[Morris Gable]] over art, loyalty, and control. With tempers high and luxyn coursing through his veins, Jaden spirals from resistance into rooftop chaos when the unhinged [[Scumbag]] crashes the night with blood on his mind. 

As the broadcast looms and makeup covers bruises, the show must go on—but in the margins of the signal, something darker begins to stir just out of frame.
