# THE AFTERBURN

Somewhere far below the earth, in a room that reeked of rust and antiseptic, [[Lash Hawkins]] woke up screaming.

He was strapped to a makeshift gurney, wrists and ankles bound with thick leather, tubes winding from his arms, his chest, his skull. Wires pulsed in the gloom. A single industrial light flickered above him.

Panic hit like a hammer. [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] thrashed, yelling, wild-eyed. “HELLO?! WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS?! SOMEBODY HELP ME!”

Footsteps answered.

Heavy. Measured. Purposeful.

The steel door creaked open. Slow. Deliberate.

[[Ora Razchek]] stepped into the room, long dark coat swaying with each step. He didn’t speak. Just watched.

[[Lash Hawkins|Lash]] glared at him, breath heaving. “Who the fuck are you?! What the fuck is this?!”

[[Ora Razchek|Ora]] knelt beside the gurney, leaned close, his voice calm as ice.

“I am your new father. And you are home.”

He slid a long, gleaming needle from his coat and pressed it into a port drilled into [[Lash Hawkins|Lash]]'s skull. [[Hella]] watched from the doorway, smiling.

[[Lash Hawkins]]’ scream echoed off the concrete, high and ragged, vanishing into the tunnels below Ora's mansion.

NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) "You're the coward," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] muttered, turning away, seething. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] stepped in front of him. "Listen. I know this is against everything you stand for. I respect that, okay? But here’s some advice—just do the show. Play the set. Make [[The Duke]] happy. Then maybe... maybe we all keep breathing a little longer." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] didn’t respond. He just shook his head slowly, like the weight of it might crack his neck. Behind them, [[Morris Gable]] sat watching the entire exchange, cigar smoke curling above his head in tired spirals. He rubbed his temples, eyes squeezed shut for a moment, muttering under his breath. “Too old for this shit.” [[The Wanderers]] were good. Too good. And the people loved them. Almost insisted they were the band on this show every night. But [[Jaden Kade]] was a sparkplug in a room full of leaking gas. Not what [[Morris Gable|Morris]] wanted for his nice, clean bedtime circus. Not at all. Finally, [[Morris Gable]] stood up, straightening his suit and raising his voice across the stage. "Owen's right, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. Just play the damn festival and move on. You’re not gonna win this one." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] spun, livid. “Why don’t you fuck off, [[Morris Gable|Morris]]? You’re the biggest fucking sell-out in this building.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]]’s mouth curled as he marched forward. “You think this is easy? You think keeping this place intact—keeping people sane—is selling out?” “I think you’ve spent a decade making nice with a dictator and calling it peace.” “I’ve spent a decade giving people one hour—**one fucking hour**—where they don’t have to remember how fucked their lives are. That matters. That counts!” “Counts toward what?” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] barked. “Keeping them quiet? Keeping them comfortable while they’re crushed under [[The Duke]]’s heel? You’re not saving anybody. You’re a goddamn mouthpiece.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] pointed the lit end of his cigar at [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. “And you—if you pulled your head out of your ass for five seconds—might see that not everything is solved with a fucking guitar riff and a temper tantrum.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] stepped closer, eyes narrowing. “You think you’re helping them by numbing them? You think anesthetizing their pain is some noble cause?” “I think one good night’s sleep might keep a man from putting a bullet in his brain, or someone elses,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shot back. “I think a joke, a song, a smile at the right hour—it can be the thread a soul holds onto. You ever consider that?” “You're not threading hope,” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] growled. “You're threading distraction. Entertainment is just another leash.” “And your music's not?” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] challenged. “You don’t think some lost kid hears your lyrics and finds just enough strength to keep going? Don’t act like you’re above this. We’re both in the same poison sea, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. I’m just swimming with my head up.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]’s face shifted, just slightly. There was a flicker of doubt behind the fury, but it drowned fast. “I sing the truth,” he said. “You broadcast sedatives.” “And maybe sometimes the truth needs a lullaby to be heard,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said, more quietly now. The air between them tightened, and for a moment, neither spoke. They stood under the studio lights, both men worn thin, standing on opposite sides of a line too tangled to trace. The room was silent except for the hum of the lights. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]’s chest heaved once. Then again. But he didn’t reply. He looked away, eyes dark. He hated to admit it. But [[Morris Gable]] wasn’t entirely wrong.
The heavy studio doors creaked open with a hiss of pressurized air, letting in a sliver of cooler hallway breeze and the familiar silhouette of [[Warren Scottyard]]. Dapper in his powder-grey suit and steel-blue tie, the anchor for [[TTV Evening News]] walked in with a raised brow and a smirk already tugging at the corner of his lips. "Fellas, we could hear you from the studio over," [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] said, voice low and polished as ever. "Everything alright in here, or did the show start early?" [[Morris Gable]] waved a hand, exhaling smoke through his nose. "Everything’s fine. We just got hit with some... surprising news." [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] stepped closer, clasping [[Morris Gable|Morris]]’s shoulder briefly in a show of camaraderie. He glanced over toward the wings, where [[Jaden Kade]] had stormed off. "Need a hand dealing with that one?" he asked quietly, nodding toward the exit. [[Morris Gable|Morris]] let out a sigh, dragging from his cigar again. "Kid reminds me of myself. Back when I thought a microphone was a weapon and not a leash. Idealistic. Angry. Just trying to do right by people." [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] smiled faintly. "People don’t watch your show out of obedience, Morris. They watch because they love you. You give them something they don’t get anywhere else. You're an anchor in a chaotic sea. There is honor in that." "Thanks," [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said after a beat. "Sometimes I forget myself." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] adjusted his jacket. "So what’s on tap for the [[TTV Evening News|Evening News]] tonight, Warren?" [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]]'s voice flattened with the ease of a man used to reading horror with a smile. "Oh just an update on that [[Loyalist Guard]] and the whore who turned up dead in [[Gutter Row]] [[Hymn From A Dead Girl|*]]. Looks like it was "ritualistic", the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackshirts]] are saying. Blood symbols. Twisted shit. And a deadbeat [[Luxyn]] dealer’s gone missing [[04 - Glowing Darkness|*]], shockingly also in [[Gutter Row]]. Supposedly important." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] gave a dry chuckle, shaking his head. "Ah, Disgraceland. Never a dull night."

Both men crashed into cables and rooftop clutter, neon flickering behind them. [[Scumbag]] was laughing, blood in his teeth. He dove for the machete—fingers closing around the hilt just before Jaden could reach it. “Song’s over,” he growled, raising the blade high. **Crack!** A gunshot sliced the air. Both men froze. Across the rooftop stood [[Morris Gable]] held a smoking pistol, still aimed at Scumbag, coat flapping in the rooftop wind, face grave. Beside him, [[Cassidy LaRue]] stood strong. [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] ran to [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], dropping to her knees beside him. [[Scumbag]] hissed and bolted. [[Morris Gable|Morris]] yelled, “Stop!”—but the madman dove for the ledge and vanished. They rushed to the edge. Below—nothing. Just the wind, the city, and the night swallowing him whole.
Backstage at [[TTV Studios]], the energy buzzed like frayed wires. Last-minute checks. Cables getting duct-taped down. Staffers whispering into headsets. The countdown to midnight had begun, and in five minutes, _[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]_ would beam across [[Disgraceland]]. [[Jaden Kade]] sat on a low folding chair near a makeup mirror, half in script notes, half in a haze. A makeup artist dabbed gently at the bruises and cuts mottling his jaw. The wounds from [[Scumbag]]’s fists weren’t shallow, but she was good—too good. By the time she finished, he looked like he hadn’t fought for his life on a rooftop an hour ago. "How you holding up?" came [[Morris Gable]]’s voice. [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] turned as [[Morris Gable|Morris]] approached. The older man looked tired but solid. They locked eyes. "I’m okay," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, standing up. He extended his hand. "Thanks for saving my ass." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shook it, firm and real. "Don’t mention it. Your girl came flying into the studio, screaming like [[Faith of Mirella|Mirella]], we assumed she was just on [[Luxyn]] until I started actually listening to what she was saying." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] smiled, and so did [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]]. He studied [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] for a beat. "Cameras won’t linger on you tonight. Just a few crowd pans. You’ll be alright. The makeup’s solid." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] gave a small nod, then [[Morris Gable|Morris]] asked, "You know who that guy was?" "Nope. But if I ever see him again," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, eyes narrowing, "I’m gonna kill him."
In a darkened room somewhere in Disgraceland, the only light came from a battered television. A tube set, humming quietly, its screen flickering black-and-white shadows. Onscreen, the show was beginning. A cheerful announcer’s voice filled the room: “Live from [[TTV Studios]] in beautiful [[CHARSPIRE#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]]—it’s [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]! Featuring, [[The Wanderers]]!” [[Scumbag]] stood in the shadows, still coated in the grime and dried blood of the rooftop. His eye was swollen, his lip split, his fingers twitching. As the television cut to [[Jaden Kade]] on stage, guitar slung low, [[Scumbag]]’s grin returned but his eyes were dead. He leaned in toward the screen. “Oh, I’m comin’ for you now, boy,” he whispered. The glow of the TV lit up the edges of his teeth.

NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) [[Morris Gable|Morris]] gave a dry chuckle, shaking his head. "Ah, Disgraceland. Never a dull night." They shook hands, a quiet moment of real friendship between the showmen. "We’ll do dinner soon," [[Warren Scottyard|Warren]] said, already turning toward the door. "We better. Before one of us ends up as a headline." [[Warren Scottyard]] vanished down the hall with a wave, and [[Owen McCready]] reappeared in his place, headset around his neck, face pinched. "You ready for full rehearsal?" [[Morris Gable|Morris]] nodded. "Let’s get it over with." But both men glanced toward the band pit and realized it at the same time. [[Jaden Kade]] never came back. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] cursed. "Ember fuckin’ damnit. This fuckin’ kid." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] dragged a hand down his face. "How the hell are we supposed to do the show with no music?" [[Owen McCready|Owen]] grunted. "I’ll go talk to the rest of [[The Wanderers]]. Maybe one of them knows where he ran off to." As [[Owen McCready|Owen]] jogged off toward the band’s green room, Morris returned to his desk, the studio suddenly colder and emptier. He sank into the chair, cigar balanced on the ashtray’s edge, and leafed through his script notes with a scowl. When [[Owen McCready|Owen]] returned minutes later, his face was grim. "He’s not with the others. They say they haven’t seen him since you two had your little discussion." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] stood, furious now. "Little fucking prick. Someone find his girlfriend. [[Cassidy LaRue|LaRue]]. Get her down here! I’m not getting hung because this kid had a tantrum and did something stupid!" The laughter sign flickered on and off.
High above the glowing grid of [[Charspire#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]], past rusting antennae and busted floodlamps, the rooftop of [[TTV Studios]] breathed a quieter kind of air. Faintly electric, threaded with the ozone tang of static and old rain. The skyline stretched wide, a serrated line of crooked towers and blinking lights. [[Jaden Kade]] sat on the ledge, boots dangling over a drop too high to measure, his shoulder pressed against [[Cassidy LaRue]]'s. The rooftop had become their secret escape—a sanctuary where the lights of the city couldn’t quite catch them, and the noise below turned into nothing more than hum and shimmer. [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] pulled a tiny silver bag from her coat pocket and shook it with a grin. "Got something new. They’re calling it [[Luxyn|Lash’s Glow]]. Strongest shit I’ve ever had." [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] took the bag, inspecting the shimmering powder like it might speak. He set [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]]’s compact mirror across his thigh, tapped out a delicate line, and dragged his finger under his nose with the precision of a practiced sinner. The powder flared, burned, sang. His head tilted back, and the night cracked open. Electricity poured through his spine, and his eyes began to glow white—pure and hot like starshine. "You look cute when you glow," [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] said, already laying out her own line with a giggle. She snorted it clean, head tilting, laughter dancing in her throat. They sat there, side by side, haloed by the city's broken aurora. "They want me to play the [[Ashmoor Festival]]," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] murmured. “[[The Duke]] sent word to [[Owen McCready|McCready]] today. Fucking asshole is forcing me to do it. Like I’m a goddamn wind-up doll." "Nah, fuck that noise, [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]].," [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] said, tucking a strand of hair behind her ear. "Ditch it. Come be with me instead." He smiled lazily, wrapping her in his arm. " Baby, I might just do that." "And those two old, out-of-touch fuck-faces," Cassidy muttered. "[[Owen McCready|McCready]] and [[Morris Gable|Gable]] just keep opening their mouth wider, begging their [[The Duke|Duke]] for more!" [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] laughed. "I think about quitting every damn day. But then Restday rolls around and the [[Economy|slugs]] hit my hand, and I say ‘one more week.’ One more week I'll listen to [[Morris Gable]] drone on and on about pointless bullshit while we all live in hell..." [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] leaned in, eyes still lit. "You don’t need the slugs. We’d get by. Hell, maybe [[The Wanderers]] go on tour. Take this fight on the road." They did another bump, this one longer. The glow in their eyes flared brighter, almost eerie now. "You think if I stay long enough," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] asked, "I’ll end up like [[Morris Gable|Gable]]? Another old out-of-touch fuck-face shillin' bedtime stories for [[The Duke]]?" [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] kissed him, hard and laughing. "I won’t let that happen." They kissed again, tangled in glow and rooftop wind. Her hand slid along his jaw as she laughed, high on hope and narcotics. Then a noise like a step and a voice—dry, ragged, theatrical—slithered from the dark.
"Well now... isn’t this a sweet little tune." [[Cassidy LaRue|Cassidy]] and [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] jolted upright, glowing white eyes scanning the rooftop. A figure stepped out from the shadows near the stairwell hatch—grinning wide, head tilted like a curious vulture. It was [[Scumbag]]. A noose around his neck, a machete in his hand a smile on his face.
The second [[Scumbag]] emerged from the shadows, [[Jaden Kade]] was on his feet. He planted himself between the intruder and [[Cassidy LaRue]], glowing eyes locked and unwavering. "You need to get the fuck outta here," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] said, voice low and coiled. [[Scumbag]] tilted his head, amused, machete dangling loosely in one hand. “Y’know, I don’t usually find people up here. I like the quiet solitude, ya know? Nothing but me and the hawks. I like to think of rooftops as... **my** nest.” [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] squinted. "What in the ember fuck are you talking about?"

NOTE TITLE: [[07 - The Spotlight Lies]] METADATA:{"cssclasses":["b-sides-script","chapter"],"tags":["chapter","chapter7","story"],"date":"11th of Bloomsun, 2186","description":"As Jaden Kade defies the spotlight and faces a rooftop showdown with a madman, the quiet hum of a deeper terror begins to bleed through tunnels below Disgraceland.","cover":[["zz_media/071.png"]],"created":"2025/06/06 19:05:27","modified":"2025/06/09 14:16:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: (cont'd) ``` > [!world]- SPOILERS > Chapter 07 focuses on the escalating conflict between musician Jaden Kade and TV host Morris Gable within TTV Studios. Their clash revolves around the network's increasing subservience to "The Duke" and Jaden's refusal to be a propaganda tool, culminating in a **physical confrontation on the rooftop** where Jaden and his girlfriend Cassidy LaRue are attacked by the deranged Scumbag, only to be saved by Morris. Meanwhile, a chilling subplot reveals that **Lash Hawkins, a Luxyn dealer, has been abducted and experimented upon** by Ora Razchek and Hella, highlighting a deeper, sinister terror beneath the city that bleeds into the narrative's margins. --- # THE SPOTLIGHT LIES The air inside [[TTV Studios]] was stale with old spotlight heat and fresh sweat. Even this high in the smog-choked towers of [[Charspire#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]], the scent of melted wires, recycled air, and dust clung to every velvet curtain and chrome edge. The set of [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] stood beneath the skeletal glow of rigged lights—too bright, too clinical, a lie bathed in amber. The laugh sign blinked faintly in the background, ignored. No audience yet. Not for rehearsals. Just ghosts in folding chairs and the ever-present hum of the machine. [[Morris Gable]] sat hunched at his mahogany desk, his frame stiff and angular in a powder blue suit too cheerful for his expression. He flipped through cue cards with mechanical precision, but each card only seemed to sour his mood further. The cigarette in his left hand burned unnoticed, a long ash curling toward the desk like a dying question mark. Morris sighed and took a long look over at his house band tuning up. Across from him stood [[Owen McCready]], clipboard in hand, expression blank as a brick wall. The station manager had the posture of a man who’d stopped caring years ago. “You want me to read this,” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] said, shaking the final card like a threat. "Is this for real? This can't be for real." “It’s a directive,” [[Owen McCready|Owen]] replied flatly. “Straight from [[The Duke]]'s Office. You think I wrote that shit, c'mon Morris..” [[Morris Gable]] let out a bitter chuckle, tapping ash into his half-empty coffee mug. “The man has his fingers so far up this place, I’m surprised you don’t smell like [[Emily Burton]].” [[Owen McCready|McCready]] chuckled. “You still cash the checks.” [[Morris Gable|Morris]] shot him a look, lips pursed, then tossed the stack down with a slap. “Fine. But when I choke on propaganda, you’re cleaning it off the prompter.” At the far end of the stage, the soft buzz of tuning instruments cut through the tension. [[The Wanderers]]—house band by day, insurgent poets by night—were setting up under low lights. Cables coiled like veins at their feet. The lead singer, [[Jaden Kade]], tall and sharp as a broken guitar string, plucked at his Telecaster with an absent hand, his attention locked on the exchange between [[Morris Gable|Gable]] and [[Owen McCready|McCready]]. He watched closely. Too closely. And he noticed something odd. [[Morris Gable|Gable]] kept looking over—toward him. Not just glancing. Watching. Measuring. “What the hell’s that about?” [[Jaden Kade]] muttered under his breath, eyes narrowing. [[Owen McCready|McCready]] handed [[Morris Gable|Morris]] a marked-up script, then stepped back toward the shadowed monitors, waving a tired hand. “Dry-run. From the top.” Something in [[Morris Gable]] shifted. Shoulders squared. Smile flipped on like a switch. His voice became smoother, glossier, as if slathered in syrup and selling snake oil by the bottle. “Good evening, fine citizens of [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]]!” He rolled into the page, selling the new segment like it wasn’t poison. His voice wrapped itself around every word of the Duke's decree like velvet around a switchblade. “And this year’s [[Ashmoor Festival]] promises to be the most dazzling yet! Games, prizes, decadent food! Dueling dancers, gold-leaf pies, and the finest poppers this side of [[Steeltown]]! And—don’t miss the highlight..." [[Morris Gable|Morris]] paused awkwardly. Looking directly at Jaden Kade. "A..a special live performance by none other than... [[Jaden Kade]] and [[The Wanderers]]!” The last line echoed. A gunshot in the silence. [[Jaden Kade]] blinked. His fingers froze on the strings. “Are you fucking kidding me?!” he shouted across the soundstage, voice bouncing off the rafters like a riot flare. Instruments clattered as the rest of [[The Wanderers]] looked up, stunned. "Owen!” [[Morris Gable]] paused, still smiling—but the mask had cracked. The cameras weren’t rolling yet. But the war had just begun.
[[Jaden Kade]] was already halfway across the stage, his boots clapping hard against the plywood floor as he stormed toward [[Owen McCready]]. "What the fuck, [[Owen McCready|Owen]]? What the fuck is this bullshit?" [[Owen McCready|Owen]] held his ground but raised both hands, placating. "[[Jaden Kade|Jaden]], come on, man, it came straight from [[The Duke]] himself. Not my call." "I don't play music for fascists!" [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] snapped. [[Owen McCready|Owen]] gestured around the studio helplessly. "You do every night, man. You think fascists don't tune in to [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]? C'mon." "That was never the deal," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] hissed. "We signed on to play here. **Here.** The studio. No stages. No rallies. No propaganda carnivals." [[Owen McCready|Owen]] looked pained, tired. "I know. I know. I wouldn’t have roped you in if I’d known this was coming down the pipe. But orders are orders. You want to argue? Take it up with [[The Duke]]. I'm just the messenger." "You're the coward," [[Jaden Kade|Jaden]] muttered, turning away, seething.

NOTE TITLE: [[Abel May Jr.]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"journal","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_abel.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Steeltown]]","territory":"[[Steeltown]]","district":"[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]","faction":"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","role":"Enforcer of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","06 - Showdown In Gage Park"],"tags":["character","protagonist","steeltown","wrecking_crew","el-santo","chapter01","chapter06"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 10:42:43"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: journal NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_abel.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Steeltown]]" territory: "[[Steeltown]]" district: "[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]" faction: "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" role: "Enforcer of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - protagonist - steeltown - wrecking_crew - el-santo - chapter01 - chapter06 --- # ABEL MAY JR. > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[abel.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Enforcer of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Alias/Nickname:** Big Bad Abe **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Fearsome, loyal, quietly haunted **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 38 **Height:** 6'5" **Weight:** 280 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 21st of Whitetide, 2148 **Occupation:** Enforcer, Bodyguard **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Known Associates:** [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]], [[Joe Ameen]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I ain’t a hero. I’m just the guy who makes sure the hero gets to stand back up.”

**Abel May Jr.** is the wall you hit when you run out of bad ideas. Towering, scarred, and sharp-eyed, he’s the Crew’s sledgehammer — the one who doesn’t swing unless it counts, and when it counts, nothing gets back up. Years ago, Jimmy and Mark found him bleeding out in the mud after a failed Duke ambush. They saved him. He’s been saving them right back ever since. Now Abel walks the line between warrior and anchor. He speaks few words. Lets his fists say the rest. But around a fire, drink in hand, he’ll sing songs that could level hearts — about family, loss, and things broken long ago. His cousins, [[Brady & Brody]] Grody, are monsters in service to the Duke. Abel calls them “the pet freaks” — but every year, he writes them a letter. Unsent. Unopened. He doesn’t know if he wants to forgive them or put them down. He fights for the Crew like they’re blood. Because for him, they are. And if Jimmy’s the rebel’s flame, and Mark the brain, Abel’s the concrete — unshakable, unmovable, and still standing when everyone else falls. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Silent, strong, and deadly — Abel leads with presence, not volume. Calm until provoked. Then the earth shakes. **Vices:** Whiskey and sorrow songs — he drinks to forget, and sings to remember. **Abilities:** One-man wrecking crew. His fists hit like warhammers, and his presence alone clears rooms. **Secrets:** A locked ammo box under his bunk contains years of unsent letters to his cousins. Even monsters leave shadows behind. **Beliefs:** Family is chosen. And if you stand with the Crew, he’ll bury whoever tries to bring you down — even if they share his blood. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Abel May Jr.** is the wrecking part of the Wrecking Crew — the Crew’s immovable defender, bruiser, and bruised soul. He may not speak often, but when he does, people shut up and listen. ---

##  **[[Ashmoor Festival of Unity]]**

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Ashmoor Festival
> ![[unity.png|500]]  

**Date:** 14th of **[[CALENDAR|BLOOMSUN]]**  
**Type:** Propaganda Celebration  
**District Held:** [[Ashmoor#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]], [[Ashmoor]]
**Established by:** [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland

The **Ashmoor Festival of Unity**, often shortened to *Unity Day* or mockingly called *Duke’s Day*, is an annual celebration held on the 14th of **[[CALENDAR|BLOOMSUN]]** — commemorating the official founding and “rebuilding” of [[Ashmoor]] by [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland. It marks the beginning of the modern era in [[Ashmoor]] and serves as a symbol of Loyalist control, prosperity (for some), and enforced gratitude.

---

### 🎉 **Common Practices**

- **Parades** featuring Loyalist military units, schoolchildren waving banners, and mechanized floats sponsored by Clay Industries and other regime-aligned entities.
- **Concerts** held in the [[Ashmoor]] Central Plaza, showcasing government-approved artists and propaganda anthems.
- **The Grand Address**, a live broadcast from [[The Silo]], where The Duke speaks directly to the people of United Tribucia.
- **“Unity Tokens”** — ration boosters, entertainment passes, or temporary curfew lifts handed out in richer districts, sparking envy in the poor sectors.

---

### 🏙️ **Cultural Notes**

- The festival is **lavishly celebrated by the wealthy and loyal** in [[Ashmoor]], complete with masquerade balls and private rooftop galas.
- For citizens in regions like [[Steeltown]] or [[The Drownlands]], the day is **seen as a cruel farce** — a reminder of their suffering and exclusion from the so-called prosperity.
- Despite the cynicism, **many across Disgraceland still look forward to it** as a day of relief: no work, lighter patrols, and a chance to gather, drink, and complain in peace.

---

### 💬 **Quotes**

> “Every BLOOMSUN, he stands there in white and tells us we should be thankful. I stand there in grease and wonder how the fuck he sleeps at night.”  
> — [[Dusty Dillon]], overheard in [[Steeltown]]

> “It’s not a holiday. It’s a mirror. And some folks just don’t like what they see in it.”  
> — [[Morris Gable]], *Night Time with Morris Gable* (Episode #742)

NOTE TITLE: [[ASHMOOR]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","ashmoor","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/ashmoor.png","Alignment":"Unlawful Evil","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"elite class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Soria Langston-Clay"]],"region":["North-East Tribucia"],"size":"Township","population":"22,000","religion":["Church of the Ember Saint"],"exports":["Power, Authority"],"imports":["Everything"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/04 11:11:38"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - ashmoor - territory cover: zz_media/ashmoor.png Alignment: Unlawful Evil Government: Mayor reputation: elite class politics: Mayor leader: [[Soria Langston-Clay]] region: - North-East Tribucia size: Township population: 22,000 religion: - Church of the Ember Saint exports: - Power, Authority imports: - Everything --- # ASHMOOR

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎SOUTH OF DIAMOND VALLEY, ASHMOOR > ![[ashmoor.png|400]] Ashmoor is the glittering jewel of the ruined world. The polished lie at the heart of Disgraceland. This is where [[The Duke]] sits on his rusted throne in [[The Silo]], surrounded by towers of steel and glass rising like teeth from the carcass of the old world. In the years following the [[Tetra Bomb]], Ashmoor was the first region rebuilt, and it shows. Roads are paved. Lights stay on. The air smells of expensive oil and perfumed sewage. While the rest of Tribucia struggles and rots, Ashmoor gleams with a fresh coat of power. At the center of Ashmoor is [[The Silo]], a towering spire of metal and surveillance that houses The Duke’s command center, archives, and inner sanctum. Surrounding it are sprawling districts like [[ASHMOOR#Diamond Valley|Diamond Valley]], known for its manmade lake and private boat clubs, and [[ASHMOOR#Knifedale|Knifedale]], home of the Loyalist Guard. [[ASHMOOR#Hush Town|Hush Town]], a walled off fortress of doomsday cottages the elite of Tribucia plan to escape to in case of revolt. Law enforcement in Ashmoor is handled by the [[Greenforce]], a brutal, heavily equipped police unit known as the _Green Shirts_ by locals. Their armor is olive-dipped and their tactics are blunt. They do not ask questions. They do not negotiate. They are loyal to the Duke alone, and every citizen knows it. In Ashmoor, smiling wrong gets you watched. Speaking wrong gets you disappeared. This is not a place for dreamers. It’s a city of deals, debt, and double-crosses—where power is currency and silence is survival.

Districts

#### The Silo A gleaming rot at the heart of Ashmoor. The Silo isn’t just the name of the white-stone palace where [[The Duke]] resides, it's the name of the district built around it — a carefully manicured 11-mile zone carved out of privilege and paranoia. Security checkpoints dot the streets, and visitors walk with straight backs and quiet mouths. Grave Bay laps softly at the Silo’s edge, but the real danger is inside, where whispered orders reshape Disgraceland by the hour. --- #### Diamond Valley Polished to a shine no one asked for, Diamond Valley is where the power sleeps. Renovated plantation homes line the hills, each more obscene than the last. [[Jacoban Clay]] & [[Soria Langston-Clay]]. [[Flint Garritt]]. [[Warren Scottyard]]. These are the names carved into the gates, each estate fenced and flanked by private guards. The streets are smooth, the lawns trimmed, and the silence enforced. Diamond Valley doesn’t just house the elite — it hides them. --- #### Amber Valley Just a little further out from the rotunda glamour of Diamond Valley lies Amber, the quieter cousin with a matching bloodline. The properties here are still large, still clean, but the fences are lower and the names on the mailboxes carry a little less weight. Rising stars, minor Loyalist officials, and ambitious merchants make their homes here, hoping one day to be invited uphill. It’s all glass, stucco, and ambition. --- #### Homa Point Named for Homa Bahram, the explorer who never made it back, Homa Point juts out over rocky cliffs and stares down the Wildlands with stubborn defiance. The district carries a kind of haunted reverence, more memorial than neighborhood. There are some settlements here — modest cabins, weather posts, and ranger stations — but most folks avoid it. The wind screams at night, and some say it carries Homa’s last breath. --- #### Greencove Greencove is a rare pocket of quiet in Ashmoor — a northern stretch of forest bordering the eerie Faded Lake. It’s mostly used by wealthy hunters, off-duty officers, and those who need to disappear for a few days. Old wood lodges creak beside still waters, and mist curls through the trees like it’s listening. Locals say the lake whispers at dawn. Nobody’s tried to prove it. --- #### Hush Town A fortress disguised as a retreat. Hush Town is a walled district pressed up against Faded Lake and brushing the edge of [[The Drownlands]]. Behind its reinforced gates lie massive doomsday cottages — panic mansions, really — built for the elite in case Ashmoor burns. Bunkers, satellite dishes, emergency stores. It’s where the powerful plan to wait out the end of the world. The place is armed to the teeth, but they still call it a “getaway.” --- #### Knifedale Knifedale cuts through the territory like its name implies. Home to the main Loyalist Guard training compound and the largest base in Ashmoor, it’s a district of barracks, kill-houses, and saluting. New recruits bleed on the gravel here while high-ranking officers bark from polished steps. Most civilians aren’t allowed in, but the ones who live nearby have learned to sleep through gunfire and marching boots. ---

"This city's full of ghosts and goddamn scum. I ain't afraid of either."

[[Ava Victoria]] grew up where the saltwater met the sludge in [[Gutter Row]], daughter of a dockside jazz singer and a stevedore who vanished one payday night and never came back. She was raised behind locked doors and smoky curtains, the kind of kid who learned early to clock a man’s intent by the tilt of his glass. The streets gave her steel, the music gave her soul, and the men she didn’t bury gave her lessons. By sixteen, she was running dice tables and patching up bleeding friends with a cigarette hanging off her lip. She was beautiful, sure, but more dangerous than she looked — because she knew the city _saw_ her, and she knew how to use it. She's had offers. The kind that come with diamonds, or contracts. She took none of them. Said she'd rather die on her own feet than live kneeling under someone's dream. Now she floats between scenes — part-time bartender, full-time observer, with her ear to the bricks and her eye on everything. Folks think she’s just another local fixture. But underneath the gold and denim and smirk, there’s a fuse burning short. The moment [[Lash Hawkins]] vanishes, she stops being background. And starts being the storm. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Calm until she’s not. Holds her tongue like a blade. Doesn’t lash out — she strikes. **Vices:** Cigarettes. Punching men who talk slick. Running toward the gunfire instead of away from it. **Abilities:** Reads a room like scripture. Streetwise, sharp reflexes, fast with a blade and faster with a lie. Can talk her way out of anything, or fight her way out if she prefers. **Secrets:** Once killed a man in another city. Never told a soul. Keeps the ring he was wearing in a velvet pouch in her jacket lining. **Beliefs:** You only get one shot to do right by people. Blood isn’t thicker than loyalty. And no one gets out clean — but some deserve the chance to try. ## Role In Disgraceland Initially appears as a minor figure in Chapter 4, greeting [[Lash Hawkins]] at the pier. But when Lash disappears, Ava becomes the first to notice, the first to care, and the first to start pulling on threads. Eventually, she becomes the reluctant hero of the search.

# Backburn Shows

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Backburn Show
> ![[bbshow.png|450]]  

## Overview  
**Backburn Shows** or Backburners are informal, often spontaneous music gatherings that erupt across Disgraceland — in alleyways, ruins, scrapyards, and fields. Named for the way they *"burn backward"* through neighborhoods like wildfire, these gatherings start as small jams and quickly swell into full-blown, pulse-throbbing performances under rusted scaffolding or broken moonlight.  

Though technically illegal under United Tribucian law for *“encouraging non-sanctioned assembly and the performance of subversive lyrics,”* Backburns are sacred to the common folk. Here, no stage, no tickets, no rules — just sound and sweat and something that almost feels like freedom.

---

## Origins  
The term *Backburn* was first coined by early street poets in [[Steeltown]] who described the way word of a jam would spread backward through the districts, lighting up ears long before boots hit gravel. These fires of rhythm couldn’t be contained.  

Legends say both [[Dusty Dillon]] and [[Jaden Kade]] first turned heads during midnight Backburns — one behind a collapsed factory furnace, the other in the shell of a bombed-out theater in [[Charspire]]. Their sounds — gritty, defiant, unfiltered — became the anthems of the ignored.

---

## Common Locations
- **[[Steeltown]]**: Often in rusted-out loading bays, rooftops, or inside gutted rail cars.  
- **[[Gutter Row]]**: Hidden courtyards off the [[Three Nail Market]], where drums and synths echo through poison-lit alleys.  
- **[[Charspire]]**: In old mine shafts, scorched lots, or beneath scaffolds during [[Loyalist Guard#Redforce|Redforce]] shift changes.  
- **[[The Drownlands]]**: Rare, but when they happen — eerie, swamp-lit, and whispered about for months.  
- **[[Threshton]]**: Usually tied to secret Rancher celebrations, shielded by crops and prairie silence.

---

## Enforcement & Rebellion  
[[TTV Studios]] and the [[Loyalist Guard]] officially denounce Backburn Shows as breeding grounds for *“anti-Tribucian messaging and sedition.”* Patrols are dispatched to break them up, but the gatherings shift fast — and locals protect them like sacred rites.  

Whispers claim even some lower-ranking Loyalists attend in secret, pulling caps low and mouthing lyrics with fire in their throats.

---

## Cultural Role  
Backburns aren’t just about music. They’re grief rituals. Love letters. Acts of war. Here, banned instruments wail, forbidden words fly, and hope lives for three chords longer than it should.  

Some say if you listen hard enough, you’ll hear the future humming through the static.

“This is the last time. Win or lose, only one of us walks forward.”

**[[Bastian Redd]]** was born beneath the blood-orange sky of the Bloodroot Canyons, where legends say the rocks remember every soul buried in the sand. Orphaned young and raised by wandering kinfolk and quiet storms, he learned to fight not in gyms or rings, but on cliff edges, under torchlight, with nothing but bone and grit. He carries the silence of that land with him — heavy, holy, and unforgiving. Painted in sacred ochre and bearing the sigils of forgotten tribes, Bastian doesn’t just step into the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] ring — he _arrives_ like an omen. Wrapped fists. Bare chest. Eyes like fire before a lightning strike. His entrance is a ritual. His opponents don’t just lose — they fall like sinners in a sermon. No music. No pyrotechnics. Just that red pouch swaying on his neck — rumored to contain the ashes of someone important, though no one dares ask who. He’s not chasing fame, belts, or broadcast deals. He’s fighting because something calls him to. Some say it’s ancestral duty. Others think he’s haunted by a vision he won’t speak aloud. One thing is certain: when [[Bastian Redd]] fights, the whole arena feels it in their teeth — like thunder rolling under their ribs. **Bastian Redd** is a towering native of the Bloodroot Canyons, in west [[Threshton]]. Standing 6'8" and weighing 325 lbs, he's a mountain of a man — stoic, scarred, and spiritual. He entered the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] late in life after dominating outlaw pits and tribal gauntlets. His presence in the ring is mythic. War drums echo as he walks barefoot through the arena, red ochre paint across his shoulders, chest bare, face marked in ritual. Chanting crowds fall into reverent silence as he steps into the light. He has no entourage. No mask. No gimmicks. Just a purpose. **Record:** 94-3 **Losses:** - One clean loss to [[Bobby Cutman]] in a brutal, close match - One controversial DQ (many call it rigged) — also to Cutman - One early-career loss in an outlaw fight Now, with a third and final title shot sanctioned by [[Flint Garritt]] himself, Bastian returns not just to fight — but to finish something that never ended. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Bastian Redd is slow to speak and quick to move. He’s quiet, focused, and always composed, like a man who’s already visualized every outcome before he steps into the ring. He doesn’t flinch, doesn’t taunt, and doesn’t play for the crowd — he fights like he’s in a sacred rite, because to him, he is. **Vices:** He holds grudges the way others hold breath — deep, long, and silent. He doesn’t trust the [[World Lucha Libre|WLL]] or the business behind it, refusing all sponsorships, public interviews, or endorsements. Off-camera, he lives simply and avoids the spotlight. But those who cross him — especially those who disrespect the ceremony of the fight — don’t get second chances. **Abilities:** Bastian’s strength is raw and terrifying, but it’s his composure that truly breaks opponents. He never rushes. Every strike is intentional, every grapple exact. He can weather pain with inhuman endurance and finish fights in silence. More than once, he’s been accused of fighting in a trance — like he’s somewhere else entirely. **Secrets:** He never speaks of his childhood, but some claim he was trained in a hidden tradition that fuses combat with spiritual vision. He wears a small red leather pouch around his neck at all times — no one knows what’s inside. And before every fight, he vanishes for three days with no explanation, no handlers, no word. **Beliefs:** Bastian believes pain is a sacred offering and that a true fight is a test of spirit, not just muscle. To him, wrestling is not sport — it is war ritual. He sees [[Bobby Cutman]] not as a rival, but as the only man capable of completing the prophecy he believes was given to him by the land itself. He does not fear death in the ring. He expects it. ## Role In Disgraceland Bastian Redd is the immovable force returning to test the unstoppable champion. He’s the only man who’s ever shaken [[Bobby Cutman]] — and in this final match, he intends to bring more than pain. He intends to bring meaning.

"Life's just a crooked hand of cards, darlin'. I don't cheat. I just play smarter."

One day, few years back, Beau found himself seated at the infamous Red Widow table — a high-stakes game hosted by a dying cattle baron named **Olin Vex**, too proud to admit his empire was crumbling under the weight of his addictions. Beau, ever the opportunist, kept his tells hidden behind gold-rimmed glasses and a honeyed drawl. When the dust settled, Vex was broke, crying, and dead of a heart attack. Beau walked out with the deed to [[Hangman's Ranch]] in one hand and a glass of Widow’s Whiskey in the other. Since then, Beau’s made Hangman’s Ranch into a place of mystique. It ain't the biggest spread in Threshton, but it *feels* like it is. The saloon girls drift in and out of his halls, and the locals whisper tales about what really happens in his smoke-filled parlor. Nobody knows how he keeps his cattle so well-fed while other ranchers starve — some say he’s got deals with the pirates out of [[Rustwater Bay]], or even with [[The Duke’s]] men. Others say he cheats death at the same table he cheated Vex. Beau dresses like a king, even if his boots are scuffed with blood. Emerald coats, ruffled shirts, rings on every finger — it’s all part of the performance. He likes being seen, likes the spotlight. But he’s got that killer instinct under the charm. The man smiles when he talks, even if he’s promising to burn your barn down. The [[Rancher Collective]] sees him as a necessary evil — valuable when negotiating, dangerous when crossed. [[Turner Anderson]] trusts him about as far as he can spit, but damn if Beau ain’t handy at turning the odds. He'll fight if he has to, but he’d rather win with cards or charm. And if he does pull a blade… you won’t see it coming. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Flamboyant and silver-tongued. Loves theatrics, hates boredom, always five steps ahead. Never lets you see the real hand he’s playing. **Vices:** Whiskey, games of chance, beautiful trouble. Lies like he breathes — effortlessly and often. **Abilities:** Master manipulator and world-class gambler. Excellent negotiator and speaker — can talk a guard into dropping his rifle. Skilled with hidden blades and sleight of hand. Knows how to move goods (and secrets) through dangerous territory. **Secrets:** Keeps coded ledgers of every secret deal he's made — including one with a Loyalist Guard captain. Still corresponds with a widow in Gutter Row whose son he once saved — and may have fathered. Believes the Duke’s downfall will be economic, not bloody — and is already moving to profit from it. **Beliefs:** Chaos is a ladder, and he intends to climb. The gods are gamblers, and he’s their favorite piece. Trust is just another currency — and it's always inflating. ## Role In Disgraceland Beau DuNoir is the wildcard of the Rancher Collective — the man who wins wars before the shooting starts. He’s the negotiator, the wheeler-dealer, the man you send when you need a dirty job cleaned up with style. While Turner builds, and Freddy protects, Beau ensures Threshton stays just slippery enough to survive. He’s a snake in a velvet coat — and sometimes, that’s exactly what you need. ## Appearances > - [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

# THE BLACKSHIFT MASSACRE

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
> **Date:** **2165** (21 years ago)
> **Location:** Blackshift Pit Mine, [[Charspire]]
> **Summary:** The **Blackshift Massacre** marks the most infamous atrocity committed by the [[Final Force]]. What began as a workers’ rebellion over deadly conditions and starvation rations in the Blackshift Pit ended in blood and infamy.  
[[The Duke]] ordered the FF to the site, seeking to end the standoff. He never gave a direct kill order, but the FF’s then-commander (now deceased) chose brute force.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Final Force
>> ![[bs.png|400]]

## The Massacre  
- **FF troopers**—including a young [[Sgt. Rottwyler]]—stormed the mine.
- All workers—men, women, and children—were massacred.  
- Survivors and witnesses claim the FF unleashed their arsenal without warning or mercy.
- The ground ran red and the smoke from burning equipment choked [[Charspire]] for days.

## Aftermath  
- [[The Duke]]’s silence and slow public response fueled outrage across Disgraceland.
- Only after mounting public fury did the regime admit the “grave mistake.” The families were all paid to keep quiet.
- The original FF commander died mysteriously within months; some say as penance, others say as a cover-up.

## The Reporter  
- A young, unnamed reporter for the **Tribucia Tribute** was on-site—hidden, taking photos.
- Their images, smuggled out and widely copied, became iconic symbols of state brutality.
- The reporter’s work fueled dissent and memorialized the massacre for future generations.

## Raynar Ventura’s Role  
- [[Raynar Ventura]] entered the Duke’s orbit soon after the Blackshift Massacre, seizing the opportunity to ingratiate himself during the Duke’s lowest moment.
- Ventura used his political cunning to help reshape the Duke’s public image, controlling the narrative and managing fallout in the aftermath.

## Legacy  
- “Blackshift” is now a curse in [[Charspire]] and across Disgraceland.
- Annual vigils and underground art keep the memory alive.
- The massacre’s infamy permanently stained the Duke’s rule; whispers about what happened that day still spread.
- Many see this as the moment the public learned the true cost of the Duke’s iron rule—and the birth of widespread dissent.

“If I have to explain the rules, you’re already too close to breaking them.”

Blacktide Cray is a man who commands attention without ever needing to ask for it. Towering over most of the crew, his massive frame and unrelenting presence make him a force to be reckoned with. Broad-shouldered, with a thick beard that frames his scarred face, he rarely speaks, allowing his sheer presence to do the talking. But when he does break his silence, his voice rumbles like distant thunder. Always has his trusty parrot side-kick, Parrot, with him. No one aboard the [[The Black Marauder]] truly knows where Cray came from, though the whispers follow him like a shadow. Some say he was once a slave trader, a man who profited off misery and chains. Others claim he hated the life forced upon him, driven by the cruelty of the trade until the day he snapped—killing his own master and setting those in bondage free. Whether the rumors are true or merely fragments of fearful speculation, Cray does not say. And no one dares ask. His path crossed with Capt. [[Lyla Bonetooth]] years ago, long before the [[Rustwater Raiders]] earned their fearsome reputation. It was in a grimy tavern along the [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] where Cray's stoic demeanor cracked for the first time. A drunken brawl erupted, and Lyla, ever one to challenge danger head-on, found herself outnumbered. Without hesitation, Cray intervened. The giant’s fists struck like hammers, and the chaos ended almost as quickly as it had begun. When the dust settled, Lyla offered him not only a drink but a job. She saw in him something few others could—a man searching for purpose. Cray accepted without a word. Now the ship’s first officer, Cray serves as the solid backbone of [[the Black Marauder]]. He enforces [[Silas Vayne]]'s orders and ensures Lyla’s commands are followed without question. Though Silas is the ship’s voice and cunning hand, Cray is the muscle that ensures loyalty. His judgment is rarely questioned, and when it is, the dissent seldom lasts long. Despite his fearsome reputation, there is one soul aboard [[the Black Marauder]] who can break through Cray’s hardened exterior—his parrot, Jackie. The vibrant green bird perches proudly on Cray’s shoulder, screeching obscenities in a voice that echoes across the deck. No one knows where Jackie learned to curse with such imaginative flair, though many suspect Silas had a hand in it. Regardless, the parrot is as much a part of the crew as any pirate, and Cray’s gruff affection for the foul-mouthed creature is undeniable. While the truth of Blacktide Cray’s past remains a mystery, his loyalty to [[Lyla Bonetooth]] is unquestionable. He fights not for gold or glory, but for the belief that the Black Marauder gave him something no other ship or shore could—a second chance. And so he sails on, a silent guardian of the [[Rustwater Raiders]], with Jackie’s squawks of profanity heralding his every step. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Stoic, restrained, and thunderous when pushed — Cray speaks rarely, but when he does, it’s with the weight of a man who’s already made up his mind. **Vices:** Violence held in check. Cray is always one breath away from snapping a man in half — and sometimes, that breath’s not worth taking. **Abilities:** Unmatched in hand-to-hand combat, intimidation, and enforcement; Cray is a walking siege engine who ensures discipline aboard the Black Marauder without ever raising his voice. **Secrets:** Tucked inside a rusted locket he wears beneath his shirt is a faded photo — a woman and child no one has ever seen. When asked, Cray just walks away. **Beliefs:** Redemption is earned, not given. Cray believes loyalty is sacred, and the crew that saved him is the only cause worth swinging for. ## Role In Disgraceland **Blacktide Cray** is the first officer of the _Black Marauder_, Captain Bonetooth’s silent protector and the ship’s living code of consequence. With one eye on the crew and one fist always ready, he doesn’t speak often — but when he moves, _everything listens_.

“I don’t fight for free. I fought for survival once — never again.”

Standing 6'9" and weighing 350 lbs, **[[Bobby Cutman]]** is a mountain in motion — feared, revered, and never beaten. Bald-headed, with a thick black beard like a wall of steel wire, he looks like he was carved out of the mines of [[Charspire]] themselves. Signed by [[Flint Garritt]] nearly a decade ago on size alone, Cutman proved himself more than just muscle. He dominated the inaugural WLL tournament, flattening every opponent in his path. Since that day, he has remained the undefeated champion with a staggering **163-0** record. The people call him *The Iron Bull*, and they don’t say it lightly. He moves like a freight train and hits like one too. Though beloved by fans and children alike, there’s always a hush when he walks into a room — because even in peace, he radiates danger. He is one of the few celebrities left in Disgraceland, a symbol of indestructibility. But when asked to settle a dispute or handle a grudge outside the ring, he simply says: “I only lucha for money now.” --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Calm. Reserved. Intimidating. He rarely speaks and never boasts. His silence speaks louder than any promo. He’s not interested in drama — only dominance. **Vices:** Keeps to himself. Drinks expensive whiskey in private. Occasionally disappears for days with no explanation. Never answers questions about the world before WLL. **Abilities:** Near-unstoppable brute strength. Shockingly fast reflexes for his size. **Secrets:** May have ties to underground pit-fighting circuits in the early post-bomb years. **Beliefs:** The ring is the last honest place in Disgraceland. ## Role In Disgraceland Undisputed champion of the **World Lucha Libre (WLL)**. A living myth in the ring — and a silent warning outside of it. Cutman is what happens when pain meets purpose.

NOTE TITLE: [[Brady & Brody]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_bandb.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"[[The Duke]]'s Bodyguards","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:32"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_bandb.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "[[The Duke]]'s Bodyguards" chapters: - tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # BRADY & BRODY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[bandb.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Bodyguards to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Twins **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Feared **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** Unknown **Height:** 6'2" **Weight:** 268 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Bodyguards **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[Emily Burton]], [[Jimmy Douglass|The Duke]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Who you want dead, boss?”

They don’t talk much. Don’t need to. Just the thud of their boots on tile is enough to make most folks piss themselves. Brady and Brody — names nobody’s sure they were actually born with — are twin towers of raw, twisted muscle. Always seen together, always looming just a few paces behind The Duke like a matched set of executioners. They’re dressed identically in stained white tank-tops and camouflage pants, belts always tight, fists always clenched. Brady is the bald one with the eye patch and the pin-up girl tattooed on his arm. Brody keeps a flat-top like he’s still pretending to pass inspection. Neither has a neck to speak of. They are not right, and everyone knows it. Locals whisper that the twins weren’t born so much as grown, that their freakish size and thick skulls are the legacy of the Tetra Bomb — that their mother died during childbirth and their father was one of the scientists vaporized in the blast. Others claim they were found in a crumbling bunker, half-feral, feeding on rats and old boots. The truth doesn’t matter. What matters is that they are loyal to The Duke to the bone, and they kill without question. They serve as The Duke’s personal bodyguards, but their duties often stretch into punishment, intimidation, and the occasional public execution. The Duke trots them out during speeches to stand behind him like slabs of meat on legs, staring straight ahead, breathing loud and slow. It’s part of the show. And the people eat it up — or choke on it. They don’t talk much. But when they do, it’s usually the same thing. “Who you want dead, boss?” They're dim, no doubt about that, but not useless. There’s a sort of base cunning in how they move — pack animal instinct. When one starts a fight, the other finishes it. They’ve never been seen apart, never seen sleeping, and no one knows what they do when they’re not standing behind The Duke. There’s a growing fear that the twins aren’t done changing, that whatever weird residue the Tetra Bomb left in their blood is still brewing. That they might get stronger. Or worse… smarter. And if that happens? God help us all. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Silent, violent, and always alert — they don’t speak unless commanded, and they don’t stop once set in motion. **Vices:** Brutality for its own sake. They enjoy breaking bones like others enjoy cracking jokes. **Abilities:** Superhuman strength, uncanny pain resistance, and perfect synchronicity — they fight like a hive mind, overwhelming enemies through sheer force and monstrous stamina. **Secrets:** Beneath Brady’s bunk is a rusted metal lunchbox. Inside? A collection of baby teeth — not their own. No one knows who they belonged to… or why he keeps them. **Beliefs:** The Duke is law. The Duke is god. Their world is black and red — kill or be killed, protect the boss, and crush everything that doesn’t kneel. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Brady and Brody** are the Duke’s twin shadows — his blunt instruments of terror and punishment. Where words fail, they arrive. And when they arrive, things _end_.

# 📜 Disgraceland Holidays & Events

---

## 🧊 1st of Frostsun — New Year's Day

**Type:** Survival Celebration  
**Meaning:** Marks the first day of the new year. Unlike pre-fall celebrations, Disgraceland's New Year is grim — a hard-earned survival marker, not a party.  
**Common Practices:** Fires are lit. Families gather quietly if they can. Simple meals are shared. Thanks are given for surviving another brutal year.  
**Cultural Notes:** In poor territories, it's seen as a somber day. In [[Ashmoor]], elites sometimes hold small balls or ceremonies.

---

## 🥊 15th–20th of Rainsun (Every 4 Years) — Noche de Lucha

**Type:** Fighting Tournament  celebrating [[El Santo]]
**Meaning:** A brutal one night, 16 man, single elimination tournament where champions from across Disgraceland battle for the title of **Grand Luchador**.  A festival celebrating [[El Santo]] takes place in the days before and after.
**Common Practices:** Street festivals, underground gambling, regional pride matches.  
**Cultural Notes:** Winning [[Noche de Lucha]] brings instant fame, wealth, and influence. It's the single most-watched event in Disgraceland, broadcast even into the poorest zones.

---

## 🏛️ 14th of Bloomsun — Ashmoor Festival

**Type:** Propaganda Celebration  
**Meaning:** Celebrates the official founding and rebuilding of [[Ashmoor]] by [[The Duke]].  
**Common Practices:** Parades, concerts, speeches praising The Duke and Ashmoor’s prosperity.  
**Cultural Notes:** Mostly celebrated by the rich and loyal. Poorer citizens in other regions see it as a sick joke.

---

## ⚫ 23rd of Searsun — Blackshift Massacre Memorial Day

**Type:** Day of Mourning  
**Meaning:** Remembrance of the workers and miners slaughtered by [[Final Force]] during the [[Blackshift Massacre]].  
**Common Practices:** Silent marches. Black flags hung over doors. Work stoppages (illegal but widespread).  
**Cultural Notes:** Especially honored in [[Charspire]] and [[Steeltown]]. [[Ashmoor]] officials pretend to recognize it but barely mention it.

---

## ☢️ 4th of Ambertide — Anniversary of the Tetra Bomb

**Type:** Global Remembrance  
**Meaning:** Marks the catastrophic detonation of the [[Tetra Bomb]], which ended the [[Water Wars]] but shattered the world.  
**Common Practices:** Bells toll at noon. Some regions observe full-day fasts. Others light black candles in memory.  
**Cultural Notes:** Bitterness, resentment, and anti-Duke sentiment runs high on this day. Guard patrols are quietly doubled in vulnerable cities.

---

## 🌾 30th of Ambertide — Harvest Festival

**Type:** Survival Feast  
**Meaning:** Final harvest feast before The Withering season begins. Families and communities gather to celebrate the earth’s last bounty.  
**Common Practices:** Large feasts. Marriages and pacts often made. Debts are expected to be settled before sundown.  
**Cultural Notes:** If harvests are bad, tensions and violence can break out during or after the festival.

---

## ⚒️ 18th of Hollowtide — Worker's Day (Steeltown & Charspire Only)

**Type:** Labor Honor Day  
**Meaning:** Celebrates the contributions — and exploitation — of laborers who keep Disgraceland functioning.  
**Common Practices:** Speeches, rallies, strikes (often illegal).  
**Cultural Notes:** Only officially recognized in [[Steeltown]] and [[Charspire]]. Heavily monitored. Arrests and disappearances spike after rallies.

---

## 🌑 30th of Hollowtide — Dark Night

**Type:** Forced Anarchy Observance  
**Meaning:** Marks the anniversary of a failed rebellion against [[The Duke]]. As punishment and reminder, all [[Loyalist Guard]]s are ordered to stand down for one night.  
**Common Practices:** Murders, looting, revenge killings, liberations. Citizens barricade themselves inside or participate in the chaos.  
**Cultural Notes:** [[Ashmoor]] remains protected by [[Final Force]]. Everywhere else becomes lawless.  
**Quote:** > "One night of freedom. One lifetime of chains."

“Fuck you, you bitch! You filthy little gutter rat!” - Cassidy to Soria Langston-Clay

Cass LaRue is the last girl you’re supposed to bring home and the first to drag you out when you should be sleeping. She’s got peroxide-blonde hair hacked off at the chin, eyes like melting chrome, and a laugh that always sounds a little too close to screaming. Born in the gutter-alleys of Gutter Row, she started out running amphetamines for the Calavera Union and wound up singing backup in backroom bands that played for liquor and leftover pills. Cass’s voice is sweet, but her mouth is poison — she’s never learned to back down, never cared to apologize, and never let heartbreak slow her down for more than a night. Cass and Jaden met at a blackout party in a half-collapsed speakeasy, and by dawn they’d broken up twice, kissed four times, and stolen a cop’s boots together. She moves through his life like a storm: always one step ahead of the law, always one drink away from disaster, always looking for the next thrill. She’s Jaden’s biggest mistake and his favorite muse. She feeds his wildest instincts — and he’s never written a better song since she showed up. Some say she’s trouble, some say she’s cursed, but nobody ever forgets her. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Chaotic, impulsive, fearless. Cass laughs at danger, spits at authority, and treats every moment like it’s her last. She’s volatile as hell but can turn soft and affectionate in private — especially when she thinks nobody’s looking. Wildly protective of her friends, but just as likely to screw them over if the mood suits her. **Vices:** Anything that burns, buzzes, or blurs the world — liquor, pills, cheap amphetamines, and raw adrenaline. Gets off on breaking into forbidden places. Never met a drug she wouldn’t try once. Loves starting fights with people twice her size. > [!infobox] > > ![[jadencassidy.png|224]] **Abilities:** Sharp-tongued singer with a voice that can flip from velvet to razor wire. Expert at sneaking, lying, and finding hidden ways into any building in Disgraceland. Knows every fence, runner, and dealer from Steeltown to Charspire. Plays dirty harmonica, mean backup guitar, and can turn a riot into a party — or the other way around. **Secrets:** Cass once double-crossed the Calavera Union on a major drug deal and barely escaped with her life. She’s living under a fake name, and there’s still a bounty out for her — only a handful know her real past. She’s haunted by a year she can’t remember, spent in some “clinic” outside Ashmoor — and every so often, she has gaps in her memory she can’t explain. **Beliefs:** The world is doomed, so live while you can. Trust no one, especially lovers, but die for your friends if you have to. Music is the last honest thing left in Disgraceland, and every note is a middle finger to The Duke. If there’s a hell, it probably looks a lot like home. ## Role In Disgraceland Cass is the fire Jaden can’t quit — muse, partner-in-crime, and sometimes the only thing keeping him from burning out for good. Together, they’re the heartbeat and headache of Disgraceland’s outlaw scene, legends in the making, or on their way to self-destruction. ## Appearances > [!rustwater]- Surprise >

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎CHARSPIRE > ![[chars.png|400]] Charspire is a choking wound in the heart of Disgraceland — a sprawling industrial hellscape belching smoke into the sky day and night. The air is thick with soot, the ground slick with oil, and the people look half-dead before they even finish their morning shift. This is where machines come to feed and men come to die. Massive factories grind endlessly through the days, pulling ore from the black guts of [[CHARSPIRE#Smashstock|Smashstock]] The city is ruled by Mayor [[Gorren Brile]], a bloated rat of a man whose appointment came directly from **[[The Duke]]** himself. Short, round, and always sweating, **Brile** lords over the region like he’s royalty — perched high in his rust-stained tower, surrounded by sycophants and paid women. He wears a cracked monocle like it gives him class, but everyone knows he’s filth. He’s not just corrupt, he _is_ corruption. A man with no loyalty, no shame, and no bottom. If selling his own mother would buy him another month in power, he’d ask for a discount on the rope. The streets of [[CHARSPIRE#Dog City|Dog City]] and [[CHARSPIRE#Burnt Coast|Burnt Coast]] are a mess of flickering red lights, chainlink fences, and hunger. Workers drag their boots through blood-slick alleys to get to illegal bunkhouses, while gangs patrol the districts with homemade blades and black market guns. Brile’s enforcers, the **[[Redforce]]** — or _Red Shirts_, as the people bitterly call them — stomp through neighborhoods like gods in cheap uniforms. They don’t solve problems. They cause them. If you’re poor and bleeding, you stay that way. If you complain, you disappear. There’s one district where the lights never go out — [[CHARSPIRE#Fistfront|Fistfront]]. Part brothel, part trap, it’s where Brile indulges most of his appetites. Drugs, girls, men, slaves, whatever. Nobody keeps count anymore. It’s a festering playground for the worst kind of men, and the only ones who rise here are the ones who’ve already given up their souls. But even here, the fires of revolt still flicker in shadow. Whispers in the alleys. Weapons stashed beneath bunkbeds. Maps hidden under floorboards. One day, Charspire will burn — and not from the furnaces this time.

Districts

#### Gravenwild A little less choked, a little more forgotten — Gravenwild sits on the western edge of Charspire like a cigarette burn on a silk sheet. It's rural by Charspire standards, but it hosts [[TTV Studios]], the black heart of propaganda where [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] and the [[TTV Evening News]] drip-feed the public their nightly lullabies. The fields are dry, the roads cracked, but the broadcast towers shine like teeth. Gravenwild keeps smiling, even when nobody’s watching. --- #### Dog City Stacked metal and spit. Dog City’s a tangled shantytown built from shipping crates, scrap, and hope that never arrived. It houses the miners and laborers of [[CHARSPIRE#Smashstock|Smashstock]], packed in shoulder-to-shoulder and drunk off fumes. Kids play in soot, women barter for water, and every fourth face’s got a scar worth hearing about. Call it what it is — a kennel for broken workers waiting to be put down. --- #### Burnt Coast As clean as Charspire ever gets. The Burnt Coast stretches along the Dead Waters’ edge, lined with weary trees and soot-washed skies. Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] lives here, tucked in his polished estate, away from the stink of his city. The district’s name comes from the fires that used to rage here after the [[Tetra Bomb]] fallout, but these days, it’s calm. Quiet. Dangerous in a different way. --- #### Smashstock This is where the air chews back. Smashstock is a sprawling industrial hell where [[Clay Industries]] runs the mines and furnaces without pause. Smoke chokes the sky, the ground trembles with drills, and the people — if you can call them that — are worked like mules. Slaves, mostly. It’s also where the [[Blackshift Massacre]] happened, when a protest was met with fire and steel. Nobody speaks of it out loud. But everyone remembers. --- #### The Molten Zone Northern Charspire is home to something worse than just smoke and ash. The Molten Zone is a cordoned-off wasteland, where slag fields glow under cracked earth and old structures hum with buried power. [[The Duke]]’s signs call it “Restricted.” Locals call it cursed. Rumor has it something was unearthed during a deep-core dig — not a resource, but a structure. Now RedForce patrols the perimeter in shifts, and anyone caught inside gets vaporized or vanishes. Maybe both. --- #### Fistfront Where [[Gutter Row]] spills into Charspire like a cut that won’t clot. Fistfront’s got the shops, food stalls, and scavenger markets that [[CHARSPIRE#Dog City|Dog City]] doesn’t. It’s where desperate folks go to trade stories for bullets, or meat for meds. The guards patrol here more often, but not out of kindness — this is the corridor where loyalty is bought, sold, and lost. Nobody smiles in Fistfront unless they’re selling something or about to steal it. ---

# 🔥 Church of the Ember Saint


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of the Ember Saint
> ![[es.png|400]]  

> **"Through the flames, we rise. Through the ashes, we endure."**

The **Church of the Ember Saint** is the wealthiest and most widespread faith in Disgraceland’s modern era. Born in the ashes of an ancient city, the church reveres the legendary figure who braved the flames to save all he could—known simply as the **Ember Saint**.  
Wherever there is fire, there is hope. Followers believe suffering is a forge, and the faithful emerge stronger for it. In public, Ember Saints are grand and generous. In private, they are hard as iron.


## Core Beliefs

- **The Ember Saint:**  
  The first and greatest of the faithful, the Ember Saint walked through fire untouched, saving hundreds during the great blaze of Prattia. His deeds are both myth and moral code.
- **The Flame Endures:**  
  Fire purifies, but it does not destroy. Each trial faced is a test, a chance to be reforged.
- **Service is Salvation:**  
  To help others is sacred. To hoard wealth or power is heresy.
- **Ashes Remember:**  
  The past is not forgotten. Every ember is a spark of memory, kept alive through story and ritual.

---

## History

- **The Burning of Prattia:**  
  Legends tell of a fire that nearly destroyed the greatest city of the old world. The Ember Saint emerged, saving lives, guiding the lost, and inspiring a movement.
- **Rise to Power:**  
  The faith spread through charity and spectacle. Ornate cathedrals rose, and the faith’s leaders became rich and influential.
- **Survival and Renewal:**  
  The Church survived wars, disasters, and purges. Even now, after so much has been lost, their temples (ruined or not) remain symbols of hope.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Ember Book:**  
  Holy scripture containing parables of the Ember Saint’s deeds and teachings. Each tale ends with a question or lesson for the reader.
- **Rites of Passing:**  
  The dead are cremated, and a single ember is given to their family. The flame symbolizes the spirit’s endurance.
- **Day of Ember:**  
  Once a month, believers light a communal fire at dusk, sharing stories and food with neighbors and strangers alike.
- **Saint’s March:**  
  On the anniversary of the Great Fire, followers parade through the city with lanterns, chanting and singing hymns until sunrise.

---

## Symbols

- **The Burning Halo:**  
  A golden ring of flame, often painted above doors or tattooed on the chest.
- **The Unburned Hand:**  
  A palm surrounded by stylized fire, representing protection and sacrifice.

---

## Structure

- **High Flame (Pontiff):**  
  The supreme leader of the church, chosen from the Council of Embers.
- **Council of Embers:**  
  Senior clergy who oversee regions, temples, and doctrine.
- **Redrobes:**  
  Priests and priestesses who serve the faith, recognized by their long, hooded ember-red robes.
- **Lay Faithful:**  
  Everyday followers, often organized into charitable guilds and work crews.

---

## Influence

- **Wealth:**  
  The church controls enormous wealth, much of it redistributed through charity—but some suspect greed and corruption at the top.
- **Architecture:**  
  Their cathedrals are renowned for marble, glass, and gold—most now ruined or gutted, but a few remain standing as beacons.
- **Festivals:**  
  Ember celebrations bring people together, even nonbelievers.

---

## Holy Days

- **Ember Day (monthly):**  
  A night of communal fire, feasting, and storytelling.
- **Saint’s Vigil (anniversary of the Great Fire):**  
  All-night procession, ending at dawn with the lighting of the Grand Flame.
- **The Forging:**  
  Every five years, followers gather for a mass ritual of renewal and oaths—new Redrobes are anointed here.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "No one is alone in the fire."
- "Flames do not ask who is worthy—they burn, and we endure."
- "The ember you carry lights the way for others."

---

## Notable Figures

- **The Ember Saint:**  
  Legendary founder, both a man and a myth.
- **High Flame Parvelius:**  
  (Placeholder for current leader—customize or name as needed.)

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Ancient rivals—Ember faith believes in action, Stillborns in patient waiting.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Somewhat opposed—fire and earth rarely mix, and their outlooks clash.
- **El Santo:**  
  Mutual respect, especially among Steeltown’s poor, though their doctrines rarely overlap.

---

> *“In every ash is the story of survival.”*

“I smile so I don’t burn the world down. Don’t give me a reason to stop.”

Clinton Firebay wears his charm like armor — a grin too easy, a gaze too knowing. He’s got the swagger of a man who’s outrun death and the scars to prove it. Tall, broad, and sun-bronzed, his windswept blond hair and deep-set eyes catch attention before he ever speaks. But make no mistake — the fire in him isn’t for show. It’s real. And it’s dangerous. Raised on the salt-heavy winds of Rustwater Bay, Clinton’s earliest memories are waves and fishnets, learning the pulse of the water from a father who treated the lake like scripture. But after the Tetra bomb turned the skies black and the coasts into ash, Clinton lost everything. His family, his home, and his purpose — swallowed by fire. Something dark took root in him that day. His temper, once manageable, turned into a storm. He drank too much, fought too often, and landed in too many jails. That’s where he met [[Silas Vayne]] — a mirror in many ways. Silas saw the burn in Clinton and chose to steer it, not snuff it. The two became thick as blood, and when Silas joined the [[Rustwater Raiders]], Clinton followed. Now a key figure aboard the _Black Marauder_, Clinton is their master of tides — able to sense shifts in current like a sixth sense. Some say he was born with the lake in his blood, others whisper it’s something darker. He can thread a pirate ship through needle-thin ruins and steer blind through a fog no compass can read. But the man beneath the charm is fraying. Clinton tries to laugh, flirt, and drink the pain away. He hides behind bravado. But when that mask cracks, he becomes something else — a weapon. And that weapon doesn't stop until everything around it is broken. He’s older than most on the ship and remembers the world before. He pretends it doesn’t haunt him — but it does. The only tether he has left is Silas, who seems to be the only one that can reach through the fire and pull him back. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Charismatic and easygoing until his fuse hits the end. Clinton talks like a poet but explodes like a cannon. **Vices:** Rage, liquor, guilt — his holy trinity. He can’t stop smiling because he knows what happens when he doesn’t. **Abilities:** Unparalleled navigator of Rustwater Bay and Gravelake. Feels the lake like a second skin. Also vicious in hand-to-hand combat — especially if cornered. **Secrets:** A box of his father’s waterlogged journals lies hidden beneath a floorboard near the galley. He won’t read them. But he also won’t throw them away. **Beliefs:** Forget the past. Burn it. The only way forward is with the wind at your back and no map in your hands. ## Role in Disgraceland **Clinton Firebay** is the _Black Marauder’s_ guiding wind and secret storm. He is the beating heart of the crew’s direction — both their compass and their chaos.
