# [[Coffin Island]] 🩸  
*Also known as: The Coffin*  
**Location:** Largest island in [[Bone Lake]]  
**Type:** Offshore Supermax Prison  
**Territorial Affiliation:** Neutral (Supplied by [[Ashmoor]], governed by [[The Duke]])  


---

## 📜 Overview  
[[Coffin Island]] is the most feared prison in all of [[TRIBUCIA MAP]]. Surrounded by the icy black waters of [[Bone Lake]], it serves as a final destination for traitors, dissidents, escapees, and anyone [[The Duke]] wants erased from history. No trial. No paperwork. Just a number, a cell, and silence.

The prison is built atop a decaying [[Water Wars]]-era military research complex, repurposed into a fortress of misery. Locals call it *The Coffin* because once you're sealed inside, you're already dead.

---

## 🔒 Structure & Design  
- **Triple perimeter walls**: Electrified, rusting, always manned  
- **Blackspire Tower**: Central watchtower and signal relay — visible from [[Burton Point]]  
- **Underground chambers**: Pre-War bunkers turned solitary tombs and "processing" rooms  
- **Open-yard punishments**: Inmates are subjected to freezing winds as discipline  
- **Single-point dock access**: One weekly barge brings food, medicine, and rotating guards

---

## 🌫 Conditions  
- Constant cold, high winds, and bone-deep dampness  
- Prisoners are **not named**, only numbered  
- **Disappearance without record** is standard protocol  
- Brutal guards, spoiled rations, no medical care unless it’s experimental  
- Prisoners fight, scream, or go mad. Sometimes all three

---

## 🧍 Leadership & Staff  
- **[[Katarina Volkoff]]** – A cold, precise woman in her late 30s. Daughter of a decorated soldier. Runs the prison like a forward operating base. Took over after the last warden was murdered in his sleep — some say by guards, others by prisoners. Rimshaw personally petitioned [[The Duke]] for the job. Rumors swirl that her loyalty came with favors, but no one dares say that to her face.  
- Most guards are dishonorably discharged [[Greenforce]] members, bitter and cruel  
- Whispers persist that [[Ora Razchek]] still pulls strings in the tunnels below

---

## 🩸 Myths & Rumors  
- **"No one escapes."** The waters are deadly, the island worse  
- The **Dead Choir**, a cult of prisoners, holds nightly rituals in the tunnels below  
- It’s said a **former Duke family member** is locked away under a false identity  
- Common saying in [[Ashmoor]]: *"Coffin’s got no door. Only a lid."*

---

## ⛓ Notable Mentions  
- **Prisoner #1412 – "Moorjaw"**: A large, quiet inmate held in the deepest cellblock. He’s survived 12 winters, multiple assaults, and even an execution order that was mysteriously rescinded. Some say he’s [[The Duke]]’s hidden bastard son, locked away after a failed uprising. Others claim he knows the truth about what’s buried under Coffin Island  
- The **Dead Choir** — cult-like inmate group living in the forgotten sublevels. They chant, bleed, and speak in riddles. Rimshaw tolerates them… barely  
- Ferry traffic to [[Coffin Island]] is managed through [[Burton Point]], with supply runs approved only by the Warden herself

---

## 🗺 Related Locations  
- [[Bone Lake]] – The frigid lake surrounding the island  
- [[Burton Point]] – Nearest mainland ferry site  
- [[The Drownlands]] – Visible shore if you ever made it across… not that you would

NOTE TITLE: [[Cricket Granger]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"player","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_cricket.png","religion":"none","status":"Alive","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","territory":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","district":"[[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]]","faction":"None","role":"Mayor of [[Gutter Row]]","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","mayor","individual","none"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:51:56"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: player NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_cricket.png religion: none status: Alive location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" territory: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" district: "[[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]]" faction: None role: "Mayor of [[Gutter Row]]" chapters: - tags: - character - mayor - individual - none --- # CRICKET GRANGER > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[cricket.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** The Mayor of [[Gutter Row]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Rat King **Home Location:** [[GUTTER ROW]] **Public Reputation:** Perverse, Untouchable, Unsettling **Gender:** Male (fluid presentation) **Spouse:** None **Age:** 47 **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 142 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Mayor of [[GUTTER ROW]] **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** Unknown—claims none **Known Associates:** Various brothel owners, blackmail victims **Faith:** None **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“The difference between a secret and a weapon is what I’m willing to do with it.”

Nobody voted for [[Cricket Granger]]. Hell, most folks in [[GUTTER ROW]] didn’t even know he was a candidate. One day, he was just there—lounging in the velvet chair behind the mayor’s desk, drink in one hand, bruised lipstick on his neck, smiling like a cat in a slaughterhouse. People whisper he caught [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland in a compromising position deep in the red-lit halls of Gutter Row years ago. A drunken night, a wrong room, maybe a lover with the wrong kind of secrets. And Cricket? He kept the receipt. Blackmail? Leverage? Who knows. What’s certain is this: no one touches Cricket Granger. Now he’s the Mayor of Gutter Row, and his "office" is the most depraved whorehouse in [[DISGRACELAND]]. He doesn’t hide it. He flaunts it. His estate is a den of velvet couches, incense smoke, and moaning voices behind silk curtains. The place stinks of perfume, sweat, and something darker. Sex work isn’t just permitted in [[GUTTER ROW]]—it’s government-funded. Everyone knows if you walk into the mayor’s estate, you’re not there for permits. Granger’s tastes are limitless and lawless. Men, women, non-binary, twins, masked figures, chained lovers—he’s seen it all, done most of it, and talks about it like he’s sharing tea. He’ll shake your hand with the same fingers that were inside someone fifteen minutes earlier and never break eye contact. But he’s not just a pervert. He’s a survivor. [[Cricket Granger]] knows everything. Every secret, every kink, every betrayal. He’s got dirt on guards, soldiers, mayors, ranchers—hell, maybe even the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]. He doesn’t need a militia. He’s got blackmail and blowjobs as weapons. He runs [[GUTTER ROW]] not by force, but through deals, favors, and fear of exposure. Criminals leave him alone. So do Loyalists. Even [[Gorren Brile]] steps carefully when he visits the Row, watching the shadows, knowing Cricket might’ve seen him beg once. And through it all, Granger smiles—like he’s always two steps ahead, like he’s already imagining how you’ll look naked and crying. But even rats drown when the sewer floods. And in [[GUTTER ROW]], storm clouds are gathering. ## Personality **Temperament:** Playful, filthy, always smiling. Switches from charming to chilling in a heartbeat. **Vices:** Every single one. Carnal, chemical, emotional, power-based—you name it. **Abilities:** Blackmail, seduction, disguise, infiltration. Cricket is an information hoarder with no shame and no limits. **Secrets:** Keeps encrypted recordings of every major figure in [[DISGRACELAND]], including potentially damning footage of The Duke. Has a hidden exit under his brothel that leads to the sewers. **Beliefs:** Control isn’t taken—it’s leaked. Everyone has a weakness. The trick is loving yours before someone else does. ## Role in Disgraceland [[Cricket Granger]] is the unholy pulse of [[GUTTER ROW]]—a creature of filth, lust, and secrets. He thrives in corruption and trades in vulnerability. He may not have the army others do, but he holds their futures in his fingers. And one day, he just might squeeze.

# 📺 CRT Televisions

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Ashmoor Festival
> ![[crt.png|500]]  

Issued by decree of [[The Duke]], every family in Tribucia receives **one government-supplied CRT television** — whether they want it or not. These bulky, crackling boxes are considered “essential technology” by the regime, intended to connect the people with **[[TTV Studios|TTV]]**, the official state broadcast network.

---

## 📡 Broadcast Content

The only available channel on every set is **TTV**. There are no remotes, no buttons to change the channel. The airwaves are strictly monitored and centrally controlled from [[TTV Studios]] in [[Charspire]].

**TTV Programming Includes:**
- 🛑 **The [[State of Tribucia]]** – Weekly broadcast from [[The Duke]] himself.
- 🌙 **[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]** – Late-night propaganda and entertainment, Mon–Thurs.
- 🥊 **[[WLL: Fight Night on TTV]]** – Broadcast live every Restday (Friday), sponsored by [[Flint Garritt]].
- 📰 **TTV Nightly News** – A state-run news program (anchor TBD).

**When no scheduled programming is on-air, the screen defaults to eerie static.** There is no off switch — only unplugging the device or smashing it, the latter of which is strictly prohibited by law.

---

## 🏚️ Use Among the Poor

In the decaying slums of [[Gutter Row]], the smokestacks of [[Charspire]], and the shantytowns of [[Steeltown]], the glowing CRT screens serve a second purpose: **light source**. Residents often cluster around the flickering blue-white static in otherwise pitch-black homes. Some even time their evenings by the hum of the screen.

The televisions are seen as both a curse and a convenience — constant propaganda machines that also keep the shadows at bay.

---

## 🕵️‍♂️ Rumors & Urban Myths

Despite the controlled nature of TTV, whispers circulate that **some televisions have displayed... something else**. Unknown images. Strange figures. Messages not approved by The Duke.

No one has ever officially confirmed these sightings, but:
- A boy in [[Steeltown]] claimed he saw **a woman in a mask whispering names**.
- A miner in [[Charspire]] swears the screen turned blood red for six straight minutes.
- A vendor in [[Gutter Row]] insists he saw **[[Ora Razchek]]’s death house** appear in the static for a brief moment.

The Loyalist Guard has dismissed all such claims as "hallucinations caused by fatigue or substance abuse."

---

## 🧠 Trivia

- Most units are decades old, scavenged and rebuilt by [[Clay Millwrights]].
- Tampering with the TV is punishable by **20 lashes or 5 years of labor**, per Duke Mandate #47.
- A hidden chip inside each unit logs viewing duration and reports it back to TTV HQ.

---

"Cattle die. Crops wither. But a good lie? A good lie’ll outlive the both of us."

A man with a too-slick grin and a voice like honey poured over a cactus, **Danny Dandelion** drifted into [[Threshton]] under one name and left with another. No one knows where he came from. Some say he once rode with the [[Rustwater Raiders]], others claim he used to work Duke’s checkpoints before skipping out with a pouch of stolen ration chits. Either way, he ain’t from around here — and everyone wishes he’d leave the same way he came: quietly and fast. The [[THRESHTON#Snake Kiss Ranch|Snake Kiss Ranch]] was once a peaceful patch of land run by a kindly widow named Miss Greta Harp. Danny showed up selling some miracle tonic to help her ailing lungs, and within six months, she’d “voluntarily” handed over the deed. A week later, she was found dead from a “fall.” No one could prove a damn thing. But everybody knows. He wears a fake name like he wears his smile — big, loud, and distracting. He talks a mile a minute, never stops moving, and somehow always ends up with more cards in his hand than he started with. The townsfolk don’t trust him, and the [[Rancher Collective]] sure as hell doesn’t respect him, but [[Beau DuNoir]] keeps him around for the entertainment — and maybe, just maybe, because Danny knows a thing or two Beau doesn’t want whispered. Danny has no cattle to speak of, and the land he owns ain’t worth half what the deed says. But he’s got charm, hustle, and an uncanny ability to walk away from things other men would get buried over. [[Turner Anderson]] would shoot him on sight if it wouldn’t start something ugly. [[Freddy Blanchard]] won’t shake his hand without checking his fingers afterward. But somehow… Danny’s still standing. --- ## Personality Danny is a born talker — fast, oily, and always one step ahead of someone else’s suspicion. He dresses like a merchant prince on market day, but he smells like dust and old rum. He thrives in chaos and disappears when things get too real. His habits include cheating at cards, sipping stolen liquor, flirting with danger, and worming into conversations where he doesn’t belong. He lies like other men breathe, and he enjoys every second of it. He can't sit still, always pacing, always plotting. He’s the type to toast you with one hand while robbing you with the other. No one knows if he sleeps — and if he does, it’s probably with a knife under the pillow and a back door left open. ## Role In Disgraceland Danny Dandelion is the rot on the roots of the Rancher Collective — tolerated only because removing him might cause more trouble than he’s worth. He brings nothing to the table but secrets, survival instincts, and just enough blackmail to keep himself out of a shallow grave. He is the wildcard no one trusts, yet no one can quite afford to kill. His true value might lie in what he knows — and who he’s willing to betray when the time comes. ## Appearances > - [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Darius Adeyemi]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"group","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_dary.png","religion":"[[Church of the Ember Saint]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Dead Waters]]","territory":"[[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]]","district":"[[Four Tombs Islands]]","faction":"[[Rustwater Raiders]]","role":"Weapons Specialist of [[the Black Marauder]]","chapters":["02 - Ghosts On The Waves"],"tags":["character","pirate","deadwaters","neutral","ember-saint"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:56:52"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: group NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_dary.png religion: "[[Church of the Ember Saint]]" status: Alive location: "[[Dead Waters]]" territory: "[[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]]" district: "[[Four Tombs Islands]]" faction: "[[Rustwater Raiders]]" role: "Weapons Specialist of [[the Black Marauder]]" chapters: - 02 - Ghosts On The Waves tags: - character - pirate - deadwaters - neutral - ember-saint --- # DARIUS ADEYEMI > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[dary.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Weapons Specialist of the Black Marauder **Alias/Nickname:** Dary **Home Location:** [[Dead Waters]] **Public Reputation:** Brutal, unpredictable, untamed **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 25 **Height:** 6'3" **Weight:** 225 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 14th of Hollowtide, 2161 **Occupation:** Raider Brawler **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Rustwater Raiders]] **Known Associates:** [[Zadie Adeyemi]], [[Clinton Firebay]], [[Silas Vayne]], [[Blacktide Cray]] **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“You’ll break before I bleed.”

Darius Adeyemi doesn’t walk — he crashes. Into rooms, into fights, into lives. He’s the first one over the railing when the _Black Marauder_ grapples onto a target ship, and the last one to stop swinging when the blood settles. But he has a heart. They call him the **Wild Man**, and they mean it. Darius fights like a force of nature — raw, chaotic, and terrifyingly efficient. Jagged bracers, iron hooks, busted teeth, a roar that echoes across decks — he doesn’t need strategy. He needs momentum. And rage. But under the carnage is a man loyal to the core. Loyalty is his creed. You earn it, and he’ll rip the world open for you. Break it, and he’ll drown you in your own blood. His sister, **Zadie**, is the only one who can hold that storm together. She doesn’t tame him — she tunes him. The two move like they share a heartbeat. Fire and flint. Explosive when sparked. The legend goes: once, in the slave pits of Gutter Row, a chained fighter bit a man’s throat open and walked through fire without blinking. That was Darius. Or maybe it wasn’t. But no one questions it. There’s something cracked inside him — something deeper than violence. He mutters in dead languages, sees things no one else does. The Tetra blast might’ve broken something in his brain… or awakened something else. Either way, he doesn’t talk about it. But Zadie knows. And it scares her more than his fury ever could. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Volatile and feral. Darius doesn’t ease into situations — he explodes into them. Laughs during fights. Goes still when others panic. He’s a storm with bones. **Vices:** Violence is comfort. Fighting keeps the voices down. He drinks, fights, and chases chaos — not for pleasure, but because stillness is worse. **Abilities:** A brutal brawler with unmatched strength and reflexes. First to board. Last to fall. Pain doesn’t slow him — it fuels him. Whispers claim he doesn’t sleep, just “shuts down.” **Secrets:** He hears things — whispers under the waves, shadows crawling at the edge of his sight. He’s never said what they are. But Zadie’s heard enough to know they’re real. And dangerous. **Beliefs:** Loyalty above all. Not to titles or factions — to people. Betray him, betray his crew, betray his sister… and pray the lake swallows you before he finds you. ## Role In Disgraceland **Darius Adeyemi** is the black iron engine of the _Black Marauder_. When negotiation fails and fear doesn’t work, Lyla points, and Darius breaks the world open. He’s not the warning — he’s what comes after.

#  Dark Night


## Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎DARK NIGHT
> ![[dn.png|400]]  

**Date:** 30th of Hollowtide  
**Type:** Forced Observance / Day of Lawlessness
- Dark Night is a relatively new event in Disgraceland’s troubled history.  
- It began after a massive but failed uprising against **The Duke** — an event that shook his regime but ultimately ended in brutal suppression.
- Rather than simply erase the memory, The Duke twisted it into an annual reminder of his absolute power.  
- Every year since the uprising, on the 30th of [[CALENDAR|Hollowtide]], **The Duke orders all Loyalist Guard forces to stand down** for exactly 24 hours across all territories.
- **Only the Final Force remains active**, stationed around **The Silo** in Ashmoor to protect the wealthy and the ruling elite.

## Modern Observance

- **No Guard patrols** exist during Dark Night across [[Steeltown]], [[Charspire]], [[Gutter Row]], [[Threshton]], and [[the Drownlands]].
- **Ashmoor**, by contrast, becomes a fortress — [[Final Force]] soldiers patrol heavily around [[The Silo]] and its surrounding elite districts.
- **Crime explodes** across the unprotected regions: murders, robberies, fires, uprisings, and revenge killings surge.
- Some gangs and factions **plan entire operations** around Dark Night, knowing there will be no government interference.
- Many ordinary citizens **barricade their homes** and pray to survive until sunrise.

Meanwhile, within [[Ashmoor]], the night takes on a disturbingly festive tone.  
At **The Silo**, the wealthy and politically connected hold **grand parties** — drinking, dancing, and celebrating their untouchable status while the world outside burns.

---

## Cultural Significance

- **The Duke's Message:**  
  > "You are beasts without my rule. You will tear yourselves apart without my leash."
- **Psychological Warfare:**  
  Dark Night reinforces fear, dependency, and hopelessness. The chaos keeps citizens divided and desperate.
- **Resistance Symbol:**  
  For rebels and radicals, Dark Night is a solemn reminder of the original uprising — and a yearly call to remember those who fought and died for freedom.

> "In Ashmoor, they toast. In Steeltown, they bleed."


# 🧠 Notes

- Some underground movements now see Dark Night not as a defeat, but as an opportunity for resistance operations and assassinations.
- Religious cults tied to the **[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]** or **[[Faith of Mirella]]** hold secret rites during Dark Night, believing the veil between worlds is thinnest on this night.

## Overview  
**Darrell Douglass** was the father of [[Jimmy Douglass]] and [[Mark Jeffrey]], and one of the founding members of the original [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]. A former steelworker turned revolutionary, Darrell was a symbol of defiance in the early days of Disgraceland’s formation — known for his booming voice, unbreakable work ethic, and fierce loyalty to the people of [[Steeltown]].

He was executed on the direct orders of [[The Duke]] nearly two decades ago, after refusing to cooperate with [[Ashmoor]]’s new food and fuel directives. His death marked a turning point in [[Steeltown]]’s relationship with the regime — a martyrdom that galvanized the rise of the modern [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]].

In the early years of the reconstruction, Darrell Douglass formed a quiet but powerful alliance with [[Harp Langston]], the hard-edged rancher from [[Threshton]]. Though they came from different worlds — one a union man of steel and soot, the other a farmer forged from soil and sweat — they saw eye to eye on the most important thing: the people had been forgotten. When Darrell restarted the first mill in [[Steeltown]] in 2151, Harp rode north to see it with his own eyes. That meeting sparked the start of an unspoken brotherhood. Harp sent food. Darrell sent tools. Together, they created the Black Route — a secret lifeline of grain and supplies flowing between Steeltown and the southern fields.

But like all quiet revolutions, it didn’t stay hidden. In 2158, The Duke’s men cracked down. Darrell was captured and forced into steel production. Harp wanted to act — to fight, to break him out — but the newly forming Rancher Collective refused. The risk to Threshton was too great. Darrell and Harp argued for the last time, and their bond fractured. For the next decade, Darrell was a ghost — kept alive only to fuel the machine he once tried to stop. When he was finally hanged in 2167, Harp didn’t attend. But word spread that a grain silo burned that night in Threshton, ash scorched into the dirt in the shape of a hammer and sickle. The message was clear. Their friendship may have ended in silence, but the respect never died.

---

## Known For  
- Organizing the first major work strikes after the [[Water Wars]]  
- Personally leading the blockade of [[Steeltown]]’s railyards  
- Declaring [[The Duke]] a “parasite in a crown” in a broadcasted protest  
- Being publicly hanged under [[Loyalist guard]] surveillance outside the old steel gates  

---

## Legacy  
- His sons, [[Jimmy Douglass]] and [[Mark Jeffrey]], both inherited his drive but took different paths.  
  - Jimmy became  the hammer — carrying his father’s fire and fury forward.  
  - Mark became the heart — trying to keep the Wrecking Crew honorable.
- Steeltown still marks the anniversary of his death with a midnight vigil known as *The Burn Mark*, where torches are lit along the old railyard fences.  
- A faded mural of Darrell still stands on a warehouse wall — chipped, bullet-riddled, but never painted over.

---

## Quotes  
> “You can’t build a nation on the backs of dead men and call it justice.”  
> – Darrell, minutes before his execution

> “He didn’t just raise us. He raised hell.”  
> – [[Mark Jeffrey]]

---

## Affiliation  
- Former steel foreman, union leader  
- Founding member of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]  
- Enemy of the [[Loyalist Guard]] and [[The Duke]]

---

## Status  
**Deceased** – Executed by hanging on The Duke’s order, c. 18th of Dusktide, 2167

NOTE TITLE: [[Davis Pollard]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_davis.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"[[The Duke]]'s Personal Slave","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","loyalist","slave","ashmoor","protagonist","el-santo"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:59:37"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_davis.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "[[The Duke]]'s Personal Slave" chapters: - tags: - character - loyalist - slave - ashmoor - protagonist - el-santo --- # DAVIS POLLARD > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[davis.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Slave to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Slave Boy **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** None **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 25 **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 158 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Slave **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[Emily Burton]], [[Jimmy Douglass|The Duke]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“They call me quiet like it’s weakness. But quiet people hear everything.”

Davis grew up working the sunburnt ranchlands of Threshton, the youngest of five boys. His family wasn’t loyal to the Duke—just scared enough to pretend they were. His mother died during a fuel riot when he was nine, trampled by panicked townsfolk. His father was arrested two years later for hoarding “unbranded slugs,” and Davis never saw him again. He was a quiet kid, smarter than most gave him credit for, with a knack for observing without speaking. People underestimated him, and he learned to survive by making himself small—until the night everything shattered. The night the Duke’s men raided Threshton under the guise of “security enforcement,” Davis was taken from his bunk, shackled, and thrown into a supply skiff bound for Ashmoor. Emily Burton was in the same transport, though they didn’t know each other then. Some of the others fought back. They didn’t survive the trip. Once in Ashmoor, Davis was handpicked—not because he was strong, but because he was pretty. The Duke likes his pets obedient and quiet. Davis was branded, collared, and renamed "Pollard" in the house records. But in his mind, he never let go of his real name. He became a ghost in the halls of The Dead Waters estate, tending to the Duke’s personal quarters, witnessing horrors no one should see, never allowed to speak unless spoken to. But through the years, he began learning secrets—whispers between the walls, the routines of guards, the Duke’s hidden fears. Davis isn’t a fighter. Not yet. But there’s something simmering beneath that quiet exterior. A seed of rebellion. He hasn’t forgotten who he is. And when the time comes, he may be the one holding the key—literally or figuratively—to taking the whole rotten empire down from the inside. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Quiet, observant, and deeply internal — Davis rarely speaks, but his silence isn’t fear. It’s focus. **Vices:** Self-blame. He carries every tragedy like it was his fault, even when it wasn’t. Especially when it wasn’t. **Abilities:** Expert eavesdropper and silent mover — Davis can memorize patrols, read lips, and vanish into shadow. He’s not trained for war, but he’s trained for survival in a gilded prison. **Secrets:** Tucked under a loose floorboard in his quarters is a scrap of cloth from his mother’s apron, wrapped around a key he stole from a distracted guard. He doesn’t know what it opens — yet. **Beliefs:** He doesn’t believe in heroes. But he _does_ believe in moments — that one right moment can change everything. And when his comes, he plans to be ready. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Davis Pollard** is a prisoner in silk sheets, a nobody in the Duke’s house who sees _everything._ He may not look like a threat… but one whisper in the right ear, one door unlocked at the wrong time, and he might be the one who ends it all.

Out of the ashes rose **[[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]]**, a stitched-together nation ruled by one man, **[[The Duke]]**, a self-made tyrant with a god complex and an iron grip. The people don’t call it Tribucia, though. They call it Disgraceland. Six territories. Each broken in its own way. Each boiling beneath the surface. In **[[Steeltown]]**, the poor survive under the shadow of rusted towers and the protection of the legendary **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**. In the black market hell of **[[Gutter Row]]**, gangs, slavers, and secrets rule the night. **[[Ashmoor]]** shines with wealth, built on betrayal and blood, while **[[the Drownlands]]** whisper prophecies no one wants to hear. **[[Charspire]]** is a choking machine of fire and chains, and **[[Threshton]]** hides quiet rebellion behind weathered ranch gates. As tensions rise, old factions resurface, forbidden music spreads like fire, and something monstrous begins to stir beneath the soil. Prophets dream of it. And somewhere in the static of a state-run broadcast, truth tries to cut through the noise. In Disgraceland, only the strong survive.

His biggest hit, Smoke In The Casket has made him a household name. faction: None role: Rock Star chapters: - tags: - character - individual - protagonist - music --- # DUSTY DILLON > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[dusty.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** [[Gutter Row]] **Public Reputation:** Beloved Rock Star **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 25 **Height:** 5'11" **Weight:** 154 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 22th of Greensun, 2161 **Occupation:** Musician **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** **Known Associates:** **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“They can silence the radios. They can cut the wires. But they can’t stop the sound of a thousand throats singin’ truth in the dark.”

Born in the furnace-shadowed ruins of [[Steeltown]], **Dusty Dillon** grew up with ash in his lungs and rhythm in his blood. His father, Royce Dillon, was a known hardliner at the mill — refused to pay bribes, refused to work drunk, refused to bow to the local enforcers. When the furnace roof “accidentally” collapsed, Royce died still holding the pick. But Dusty eventually learned the truth: it wasn’t an accident. The collapse was ordered by a mill foreman tied directly to [[Ellis Westmount]], Steeltown’s Duke-appointed mayor and longtime union-buster. That discovery lit something in Dusty. Not just sorrow. Not just rage. Purpose. Music became more than mourning — it became a weapon. At the funeral fire, Dusty sang for the first time. The crowd wept. That night, a song was born that would echo through scrapyards and broken halls for decades: _Smoke on the Casket_. From then on, Dusty walked the path of an outlaw troubadour — performing at black-market clubs, rooftop vigils, even whisper-houses where songs were traded like sacred relics. Every performance carried the heat of loss and the chill of truth. While [[Jaden Kade]] and **[[The Wanderers]]** enjoyed the spotlight — cleaned up and televised on _[[Night Time with Morris Gable]]_ — Dusty’s shows were wild, unsanctioned eruptions of real grief and rebellion. Jaden, who had always thought himself the voice of the people, began to feel eclipsed. Where Jaden had polish, Dusty had soul. Where Jaden followed coded rebellion, Dusty bled on stage and dared people to sing with him. Jaden would never admit it publicly — not under [[The Duke]]’s eye — but privately, he watches Dusty’s rise with a gnawing resentment. Because deep down, he knows: **Dusty Dillon is everything Jaden wishes he still had the courage to be.** ## Personality **Temperament:** Dusty is intense but grounded. He’s not loud offstage — he saves his fire for the mic. Thoughtful, poetic, stubborn as rust. He listens more than he speaks, and when he does speak, people shut up and listen. He doesn’t chase fame — it chases him. There’s grief behind his grin and thunder behind his calm. **Vices:** Whiskey. Regret. Late-night walks alone in dangerous places. He sleeps with fans, but never the same one twice — like he’s scared to leave fingerprints on anyone’s life. He smokes Luxyn occasionally, mostly when the ghosts get too loud. **Abilities:** Charismatic to a fault — he can hold a riot together with three chords and a look. Can fight — grew up scrapping in Steeltown alleys — but prefers words and rhythm over fists. Has an ear for lies. He reads a room like a preacher, feels moods shift before they rise. **Secrets:** His father’s death wasn’t an accident — Dusty has proof that it was ordered by a Steeltown foreman loyal to [[Ellis Westmount]]. **Beliefs:** The Duke’s empire is hollow, and hollow things eventually collapse. ## Role In Disgraceland Dusty Dillon is the most beloved outlaw musician in Disgraceland — a voice of the broken, the bitter, and the brave. His music moves through the regions like wildfire, banned in official channels but sung by the people with trembling fists and tear-filled eyes. ## Smoke In The Casket ![[smoke.mp3]]

# ECONOMY

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Currency
> ![[slugs.png|400]]  


## Currency
**Half-Slug Shred:** Half unit. Maybe buy a smoke, if you're lucky.  
**1-Slug Coin:** Base unit. Buy a drink of water, a potato, or a newspaper.  
**5-Slug Coin:** Double-thick or wire-wrapped. Gets you a solid meal or a bullet.  
**25-Slug Brick:** Two fingers wide. Fuel, a gun, or a clean bed for the night. 


##  Standard Values Table

| Slug Type        | Description                             | Street Value Example               |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Half-Slug Shred  | Chipped scrap, barely a coin            | One smoke, one bullet casing       |
| 1-Slug Coin      | Base coin                               | Potato, cup of water, newspaper    |
| 5-Slug Coin      | Thick or plated                         | Meal, bullet, small favor          |
| 25-Slug Brick    | Heavy, rare, often hoarded              | Gun, full fuel can, clean bed           |

##  Economic Tiers

| Social Class       | Weekly Slug Income | Notes                                 |
|--------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Elite Loyalists    | 500–1000+ Slugs    | Paid directly by [[The Duke]]’s offices |
| Middle Workers     | ~100 Slugs         | [[Charspire]] forges, [[Steeltown]] labor |
| Black Market Hustlers | Varies wildly    | Can earn 200+ Slugs in a day — or none |
| Slaves / Indentured | 0–10 Slugs         | Paid in scraps, shelter, or favors     |

##  Minting & Counterfeits

- All official Slugs are minted in [[Charspire]] by the **Tribucian Forgeworks** under Duke seal.
- Counterfeiting is common in [[Gutter Row]] and some sectors of [[Ashmoor]].
- True Slugs have:
  - Standardized weight
  - Rough edge scoring
  - Indent seal of The Duke (often worn down)

> "What a Slug gets you *legally* and what it gets you in [[Gutter Row]] are two different stories."

| Item              | Legal Price | Black Market Price |
|-------------------|-------------|---------------------|
| Bullet (rusted)   | 5 Slugs     | 2–3 Slugs           |
| Medical Supplies     | 15-50 Slugs    | 5-50+ Slugs           |
| Smuggled Tech     | 100+ Slugs  | Varies — barter only|
| Slave             | 200+ Slugs  | Varies — barter only|

# 🥊 Faith of El Santo


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of El Santo
> ![[els.png|400]]  

> **"A bruise is a prayer the world can see."**


The **Faith of El Santo** is more than a religion—it’s the pulse of Disgraceland’s working class, fighters, and survivors. Inspired by the masked champion who became legend, El Santo’s followers honor grit, resilience, and justice earned with blood.  
Their faith lives in every gym, street fight, and act of stubborn courage. The beating heart of their culture is **[[Noche de Lucha]]**—the most celebrated event in Disgraceland.


## Core Beliefs

- **El Santo Lives:**  
  The Masked Saint never died—he battles darkness in the underworld, and his spirit rises in every act of courage.
- **Strength is Sacred:**  
  True strength is the power to lift others, not to dominate them.
- **Justice is Personal:**  
  The corrupt law is nothing. Justice is found in personal action, loyalty, and honor.
- **Pain is Proof:**  
  Bruises, scars, and broken bones are sacred marks—signs of survival and the soul’s resilience.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Mask:**  
  Every follower owns a mask. Most are simple, but each is personal. Losing your mask is the greatest shame.
- **Brotherhood of Bruises:**  
  After fights, combatants gather to share drinks, bless wounds, and trade stories—scars are a badge of honor.
- **The Vigil Match:**  
  When justice demands, a champion is chosen to fight for truth in the ring. Winner decides the verdict.
- **Day of the Last Bell:**  
  An annual day of remembrance—bells ring for every soul lost, and all are invited to spar in their honor.

---

## Symbols

- **The Mask:**  
  White, silver, or gold, each mask is a symbol of identity, struggle, and hope.
- **Bruised Knuckles:**  
  Devotees often wrap their hands or tattoo their knuckles as a sign of their faith.

---

## Structure

- **Grand Luchador:**  
  The reigning champion of [[Noche de Lucha]]; spiritual head and icon for the next four years.
- **The Grand Mascara:**  
  The head of the faith. The spiritual leader of the El Santo religion. Upon death, a new Grand Mascara is chosen by the Senior Enmascarados.
- **The Senior Enmascarados:**  
  The secretive council who selects the tournament’s fighters and guides the faith’s traditions.
- **Ring Elders:**  
  Local leaders, keepers of custom, and mediators in disputes.
- **Santos (Saints):**  
  Ordinary faithful—anyone who stands up, fights on, and helps the fallen.

---

## Influence

- **Everywhere, for Everyone:**  
  El Santo’s faith is the glue in Steeltown and a beacon across Disgraceland. Even rivals show up for Noche de Lucha.
- **Gyms & Rings:**  
  All training grounds are sacred. Every gym is part sanctuary, part school, part court.
- **Justice in the Streets:**  
  Santo’s justice is swift and personal—handled in the ring, never left to corrupt officials.

---

## Holy Days

- **Noche de Lucha (every four years):**  
  The greatest tournament and festival in Disgraceland.
- **Day of the Last Bell (annually):**  
  Sparring and blessings for the departed.
- **Founding Match (spring equinox):**  
  Young faithful compete for the right to wear their first mask.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "Bruises fade. Honor stays."
- "If you can stand, you can fight."
- "The mask never leaves you, even when you take it off."
- "In the ring, truth can’t hide."

---

## Notable Figures

- **El Santo:**  
  The masked founder—legend says he fights evil beneath the world, waiting to rise again.
- **The Last Stillborn Champion:**  
  The only non-believer to win Noche de Lucha—now a folk hero and symbol of changing times.
- **The Senior Enmascarados:**  
  The faith’s shadowy council. Their names are known only to each other and the Grand Luchador.

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Sometimes rivals, sometimes allies—recent openness has bridged old divides.
- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Strong mutual respect—fire and iron both endure, even when they clash.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Little direct overlap, but women have fought and won in the ring—widows and sisters have left their mark.

---

> *“If you’ve never stood in the ring, you’ve never really lived.”*

---

“They dressed me in silk and called it salvation. But silk burns too.”

They call her The Duchess, but she never asked for that name. Born just outside the ruins of Lansing to a family of tinkerers and scavengers, Emily Burton was bright, curious, and impossibly bold from a young age. Her father, a former engineer from before the blast, was part of a quiet circle rebuilding pre-Tetra tech in secret. Her mother kept a hidden school for the neighboring children. The Burtons were beloved by their community, but too smart, too outspoken, too dangerous for [[The Duke]]'s vision of order. When Emily was sixteen, the [[Loyalist Guard]]s came. [[The Duke]] offered the Burtons a choice: surrender their work and serve him… or be erased. Emily watched from the floorboards as her parents were executed in their home. She was taken in chains to [[Ashmoor]], where The Duke presented her on broadcast as his ward — a girl "rescued from chaos" by the guiding hand of Disgraceland’s ruler. Months later, he declared her his wife. His Duchess. It was theater. A grotesque display of dominance. The Duke, impotent and delusional, sought legacy through image, not blood. Now 22, Emily walks the halls of [[The Silo]] Mansion like a ghost in silk. She smiles for the cameras. She stands beside him on the balcony during broadcasts. Her voice is never heard — only her presence. But behind those blue eyes is a mind sharpened on silence. She is not broken. She is waiting. Watching. Emily understands the power her beauty holds. She knows the whispers in the halls, the jealous eyes of Loyalist wives, the quiet awe from the poor who see her as a living doll in a white dress. But she also knows that The Silo protects her, even if it’s a cage. There’s a bed of secrets under this place — guards who owe her favors, servants who tell her what they hear, a quiet network of sympathy she has cultivated one kind word at a time. She hates The Duke. Hates his hands, his voice, his fake faith. But she knows his routines. She knows when he sleeps. She knows what lies beneath the grain silo. And she knows that someday, if Disgraceland is to change... she might be the one to light the match. Emily Burton — _The Duchess_ in name only — is a poised, calculating survivor wrapped in the illusion of obedience. Raised by brilliant rebels and forced into a gilded cage by the man who slaughtered her family, she wears her silence like a blade honed by years of observation. She plays her role flawlessly: a porcelain figurehead in silk, offering smiles while quietly weaving a web of influence through whispered alliances and owed favors. Emily’s beauty is her camouflage, her intellect her weapon. She studies everyone — their habits, their weaknesses — waiting for the moment to strike. Her secret? Hidden in a locked drawer behind the mirror in her private chamber is a small brass pendant… the last creation her father ever built, which — unknown to all — contains a detailed schematic of The Silo’s underground network. She's not just waiting for revolution. She's designing it. --- ## Personality: **Temperament:** Calm, observant, and disarmingly gentle — Emily wields restraint like a blade, rarely showing anger but always calculating outcomes two steps ahead. **Vices:** Obsessive control. She rehearses her every move, word, and smile until perfection, terrified that one misstep will crack the mask and cost her everything. **Abilities:** Silently adept at manipulating people through subtle charm and emotional read. **Secrets:** She possesses a miniature pendant containing a full schematic of the Silo’s understructure — smuggled and salvaged from her father's hidden workshop the night of his execution. **Beliefs:** Emily no longer believes in saviors — only leverage. But deep down, she clings to her mother’s whispered lesson: “Knowledge is the only freedom worth dying for.” ## Role In Disgraceland **Emily Burton** is the silent symbol of the regime — paraded as The Duke’s dutiful Duchess, but in truth, a brilliant prisoner biding her time. # 🜃 Faith of Mirella


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Faith of Mirella
> ![[fm.png|400]]  

> **"Beneath the mud, beneath the root, her dreams tangle through our veins."**

**Faith of Mirella** is ancient, secretive, and feared. It is the faith of swamps, bogs, and shadowed waters. Followers believe the world itself recoiled from the violence of mankind, and the sleeping goddess **Mirella** lies beneath the earth, waiting for women to reclaim what was lost.  
The faith is almost exclusively female—men are considered dangerous, expendable, or cursed by their birth. The Unseen Widows are its most visible hand in Disgraceland, but Mirella’s whisper travels farther and deeper than anyone admits.

## Overview



---

## Core Beliefs

- **Mirella, the Sleeping Mother:**  
  An ancient earth-goddess who slumbers beneath the swamps and roots. Her dreams shape fate, her will is revealed in blood and vine.
- **The Land Remembers:**  
  All wounds inflicted by men upon the earth and upon women are remembered. Mirella’s memory is long, and her vengeance slow but certain.
- **Prophecy of Reclamation:**  
  When the time is right, Mirella will rise and reclaim the world for women. Until then, her followers must act in secret, sowing chaos for the old order.
- **The Power of Blood and Dream:**  
  Prophecy, visions, and the rites of blood are central. Dreams are messages; omens are sought in birth, death, and the movement of animals.

---

## History

- **Old as Soil:**  
  The faith predates organized religion. Its rites and symbols are carved into the oldest stones, whispered in forgotten languages.
- **Persecuted and Hidden:**  
  Always feared, sometimes hunted, the faith went underground. Secret covens and hidden sanctuaries kept the old ways alive.
- **The Unseen Widows:**  
  In Disgraceland, the Widows are the faith’s enforcers, assassins, and prophets. Every action serves the dream of reclamation.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Veil:**  
  Initiates wear black veils over the lower half of their faces. Only the Prophet may go unveiled. The veil is a symbol of mourning, secrecy, and solidarity.
- **Dream Rites:**  
  All major decisions and rituals begin with shared dreams—herbs, chanting, and bloodletting are common tools.
- **The Offering:**  
  On each new moon, followers cut their palms and let their blood fall into the swamp, feeding Mirella’s dreams.
- **Burial Rites:**  
  The dead are returned to the earth in unmarked graves, always near water or thick roots.

---

## Symbols

- **The Gold Bird:**  
  A stylized golden bird on a black background, worn over the heart—symbolizes Mirella’s watchful spirit and the freedom to come.
- **Tangled Roots:**  
  Marked in chalk or blood at gathering places, representing connection and secrecy.

---

## Structure

- **The Prophet (currently Veerah):**  
  The unquestioned leader, believed to channel Mirella’s will through prophetic dreams.
- **The Unseen Widows:**  
  Elite followers—assassins, spies, and keepers of ritual law.
- **Sisters:**  
  Ordinary faithful, responsible for raising daughters, spreading lore, and acting as Mirella’s eyes and hands.
- **Outsiders (Men):**  
  Rarely trusted; sometimes used, never included in inner circles.

---

## Influence

- **Whispers and Shadows:**  
  The faith is small but dangerous. Its influence spreads quietly, mostly among the desperate, wounded, and wronged.
- **The Drownlands:**  
  The largest, most sacred sanctuary in Disgraceland; the White Mansion sits hidden in the marsh, always guarded.
- **Fear and Respect:**  
  Even The Duke’s men avoid crossing the Widows if they can help it.

---

## Holy Days

- **Night of the White Veil (first full moon of spring):**  
  All faithful gather by water to renew their vows and honor the fallen.
- **Bloodwake (last new moon of the year):**  
  A secret ritual—each woman dreams alone, seeking Mirella’s guidance for the year ahead.
- **Reclamation’s Eve:**  
  A rare, dangerous night. Assassins strike targets chosen in prophecy.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "The swamp forgets nothing."
- "Dreams speak when tongues are cut."
- "Her vengeance rises through our daughters."

---

## Notable Figures

- **Veerah:**  
  Current Prophet; her visions are law.
- **The First Widow:**  
  Mythic founder; may never have existed.

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Word of the Stillborn Star:**  
  Distrusted. Too cold, too distant, too bound by old men’s words.
- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Openly opposed—fire seeks to burn the swamp, but the swamp always returns.
- **El Santo:**  
  Mostly ignored; his followers are rarely women.

---

> *“In the silence of the roots, she remembers every sin.”*

---

# FINAL FORCE a.k.a The F.F

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
> **Type:** Elite Special Forces Military Unit, Loyalist Guard Special Division
> **Nicknames:** FF, The Iron Dogs, [[The Duke]]’s Hammers
> **Commander:** [[Sgt. Rottwyler]]
> **Headquarters:** Loyalist Base [[Ashmoor]], with mobile deployment units stationed in armories across Disgraceland.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Final Force
>> ![[ff.png|400]]


## Uniform & Gear  
- Armored “Iron” Suits—bulky, steel-gray, inspired by early Iron Man Model-1 design.
- Features:  
    - Heavy, riveted plating  
    - Grated faceplates (slitted eyes, grated mouth)  
    - Short-burst flight (rocket-leap or glide)  
    - Built-in arm cannons: concussive blasts, incendiaries, slug launchers  
    - Shoulder/back mini-missile racks (some units)  
    - Power: experimental fusion cells or chemical batteries (dangerous, unreliable)
- **[[Sgt. Rottwyler]]s suit:** Larger, custom-forged, extra weapons, scarred plating, dog tags welded into the chest.

## Selection  
- Only the toughest, most loyal, or most feared [[Loyalist Guard]]s get “volunteered.”
- Suits are bio-locked to each trooper.

## Reputation  
- Feared by civilians and rebels; even Loyalist Guards keep their distance.
- The FF is deployed only for major threats or to “make an example.”
- Their arrival is announced by the roar of jets and the thunder of armored boots.
- Rumors: Some suits malfunction and cook the pilot alive.  
- Some believe the suits can run on “ghost mode,” piloting themselves after the wearer dies.

## Tactics  
- Shock & Awe: Enter loud, crush resistance fast.
- No mercy. Rottwyler kills his own for cowardice or failure.
- Heavy support by engineers/mechanics; suits require constant upkeep.

## Infamous Event: The Blackshift Massacre

> “No one forgets the day the Iron Dogs marched into the mines. The smoke still hangs over [[Charspire]].”

In 2178, the Duke deployed the Final Force to [[Charspire]] after miners at the Blackshift Pit staged a mass walkout over starvation rations and lethal conditions. What started as a tense standoff turned to horror when the FF, led by [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], breached the mine gates and unleashed their arsenal. Now known as the [[Blackshift Massacre]].

The massacre was swift and total. Workers—men, women, even children hiding in supply rooms—were slaughtered without warning.  
The event might have faded into rumor, but a reporter from the **[[Tribucia Tribute]]** was present, snapping photos from a hidden alcove as the carnage unfolded. Those photos, smuggled out and copied in secret, became symbols of resistance across Disgraceland.

To this day, “Blackshift” is a curse in Charspire. It’s a name whispered when the Duke’s iron hand comes down. Even Loyalist Guards remember it as a black scar on the regime—a day the world saw the true face of the Final Force.


## Members  
- [[Sgt. Rottwyler]] (Commander)
- [Other FF troopers – add names as needed]

---

## In Lore  
- The FF is the Duke’s final word. When diplomacy fails or terror is required, he sends the Iron Dogs.
- Rottwyler’s legend grows with every mission—unmatched brutality, zero hesitation.

---

“Lucha's happen all over. We might as well sell some tickets to it.”

[[Flint Garritt]] is the owner of one of the largest mines in [[Charspire]], with his reach extending through scrapyards, foundries, and industrial facilities all across [[TRIBUCIA MAP]]. Everything falls under his banner: **FlintCo** — an empire built from slag, sweat, and grit. He's been locked in bitter competition with [[Jacoban Clay]] for decades. The two men dominate the industrial elite of Disgraceland, yet can barely stand to be in the same room. Clay builds for power and profit; Garritt builds for legacy. They both know there’s only room for one king. A lifelong fan of **Lucha Libre**, Flint revived the long-dead [[World Lucha Libre]] ten years ago, believing that Tribucia’s beaten-down population needed more than just food and fuel — they needed something to believe in. Under his leadership, WLL rose from the ash like an old god, draped in masks and glory. It quickly became one of the only remaining spectacles left in Disgraceland, a roaring echo of the world that was. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Bold and brutal. Charismatic when it suits him, but quick to anger. He commands like a general and negotiates like a gambler. He’s not interested in being liked — he’s interested in being remembered. **Vices:** Smokes too much, drinks even more. Keeps company with fighters, ex-cons, and steelworkers. Rumors swirl about an underground pit-fighting league run through his scrapyards. Probably true. **Abilities:** Expert negotiator and industrial tactician. Has a near-photographic memory for names, debts, and deals. Trained wrestler in his youth — still spars in private. **Secrets:** His end goal is to get Jacoban Clay into the ring. **Beliefs:** Power earned through legacy is stronger than power taken through fear. ## Role In Disgraceland Industrial titan and cultural revivalist. Flint Garritt is the founder of **FlintCo** and the man responsible for resurrecting **World Lucha Libre (WLL)** — giving the people of Tribucia their fight back.

# Four Tombs Islands


> *"A place of the dead, ruled by the damned."*  
> —Common saying in [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]]

## Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Four Tombs Islands
> ![[4t.png|400]] 

The **Four Tombs Islands** are a small chain of four landmasses located off the southeast coast of [[Gutter Row]], nestled in the shadowy swell of the [[WATER#The Dead Waters|Dead Waters]]. Though seemingly tranquil from the mainland, the islands have a deadly reputation—thanks to their only residents, the [[Rustwater Raiders]].

Each of the islands is named for the enormous, ancient tomb it houses. These monolithic structures, shaped like thin obelisks or long pillars, pierce the sky like grave markers for forgotten kings. No known historical record explains who built them or who lies within. Locals claim the tombs are ancient rulers from time immemorial.

## Inhabitants

The **[[Rustwater Raiders]]** have completely taken over the largest of the four islands. They've fortified the ruins of an old coastal **fort** and converted the still-standing **lighthouse** into a watchtower. Any ships foolish enough to drift too close are warned off—or sunk. The Raiders operate out of this isolated stronghold, launching occasional raids on the coastlines of [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]] and [[Charspire]].

No one lands on the Four Tombs Islands without permission. No one.

## Geography & Wildlife

While the islands are soaked in dread, they are reportedly lush with overgrowth and teeming with wild game. Deer, wild boar, seabirds, and freshwater springs make the land viable for long-term survival, though only the Raiders benefit from the abundance.

Many hunters and desperate fishermen have tried sneaking ashore over the years. None are known to have returned.

## Legends & Lore

- Some claim the tombs are cursed, and that the Raiders have made blood pacts with whatever lies buried inside.
- Others whisper that strange blue lights glow around the monuments during storms, and that voices can be heard humming beneath the soil.
- Old [[Gutter Row]] tales say one of the tombs isn't a grave at all—but a sealed gate.

## Strategic Significance

The Four Tombs Islands sit in an important position along the southern shipping lines between [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]] and [[CHARSPIRE#Broken Bones Bay|Broken Bones Bay]]. The presence of the Raiders has made this route perilous, forcing most trade vessels to reroute far north through [[WATER#Grave Bay|Grave Bay]] or risk brutal ambush.

## Known Structures

- **The Lighthouse** – Converted to a sniper post and signal tower.
- **The Old Fort** – Now the heavily guarded headquarters of the Rustwater Raiders.
- **The Four Tombs** – One on each island, made of ancient stone and towering high above the treetops.

---

> **WARNING:**  
> The [[Rustwater Raiders]] have been designated *Hostile Non-Recognized Sovereign Entities* by [[Loyalist Guard]] Command. Civilian approach is strictly prohibited. Survivors will not be recovered.

Francis Murray owes everything to his brother Marco—and he knows it. Marco shielded Francis from the worst of Gutter Row, scraping together enough to keep him clothed, fed, and (mostly) safe. Where Marco learned survival in the gutter, Francis got a taste of ambition. Francis rose through the ranks fast, becoming plant manager by his late twenties. He learned the art of management, the politics of the factory floor, and how to get what he wanted without making enemies. But blood is blood—when Marco’s side business ballooned into a criminal empire, Francis walked away from the Millwrights without a word, throwing his loyalty and skills behind his brother. Francis now handles the front-facing side of the Murray Boys: laundering money, striking deals, and keeping the operation just legit enough to keep the guards off their backs. He still meets Jacoban Clay for drinks every month, spinning stories about side businesses and investments—never once letting slip that he and Marco are the men behind Luxyn. For Francis, friendship is sacred, but family is absolute. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, charming, and socially gifted. Francis is diplomatic, a natural schmoozer who can talk his way out of trouble or into any boardroom. He’s fiercely loyal to Marco but doesn’t let that make him naive—he’s learned to read a room and strike first when necessary. **Vices:** Gambling, expensive suits, and a taste for high-stakes risk. Francis loves the thrill of outmaneuvering competitors. He drinks too much and sleeps around, but keeps these out of the business. **Abilities:** Expert negotiator, accomplished liar, and financial whiz. Francis is the public face of the Murray Boys, keeping books clean, fronts legal, and guards distracted. He’s also well-connected in Charspire’s industrial circles. **Secrets:** Francis has a private fund stashed in case the business ever collapses. He still feels guilty for leaving Clay Millwrights, especially knowing how much Jacoban trusted him. He’s also quietly tracked down their parents’ killer, but keeps it to himself. **Beliefs:** Francis believes loyalty is everything—first to Marco, then to those who’ve earned his trust. He sees Disgraceland as a rigged game but believes he and Marco can beat it if they stick together and play smart. ## Role In Disgraceland Francis Murray is the Murray Boys’ clean face and chief operator, running their finances, fronts, and public affairs from Charspire. His charm and connections allow the Murray Boys to expand without drawing heat—unless you cross him, in which case the charm vanishes and you’re left dealing with Marco. ## Appearances

"I don't need a reason to feed the hungry. I need a reason not to burn this whole goddamn deal down."

They say Freddy Blanchard was born in a storm — his mother died giving birth, and his father died trying to raise him. He grew up dirt-covered and half-starved, shoveling coal and breaking wild horses for pennies in the cracked shadow of Charspire. By the time he was fifteen, Freddy could lift more than a grown man and take a punch that’d kill one too. But he wasn’t just muscle — he had purpose. He earned every acre of Bonebreak Ranch with blood and grit. When the water wars came, and the bombs fell, Freddy didn’t run or loot. He planted. Dug wells. Slaughtered meat. Built shelter. Folks came to him starving and hopeless — he fed ‘em, no questions asked. The Duke calls it charity. Freddy calls it survival. Bonebreak Ranch is the largest in Threshton, and Freddy works every inch of it with his own damn hands. The other ranchers got foremen and hired guns — Freddy’s up at dawn slinging hay bales and breaking fence with a rusted hammer and a stronger will. His back is covered in scars, his hands thick with callus, but his people swear they’ve never gone hungry under his watch. Underneath that gruff, stoic jawline and cannonball chest is a fire — a deep hatred for the Duke’s taxes, rations, and cruelty. Freddy’s the reason whole families are still alive, thanks to backdoor cattle runs and secret crop shipments smuggled through Gutter Row by moonlight. He’s made deals with pirates, bartered with outcasts, and strongarmed corrupt checkpoint guards, all without taking a single coin for himself. The other ranchers respect him like a lion — Turner Anderson may be the glue of the Collective, but Freddy’s the iron nail. And when the fighting finally comes, folks say Blanchard’ll be the one leading the charge, shovel in one hand, Duke’s blood in the other. --- ## Personality > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Rancher Meeting > ![[bf1.png|400]] **Temperament:** Gruff and intense, but fiercely loyal. Freddy doesn’t speak unless it’s worth saying, and when he does, it lands like a punch. He leads by example, not instruction. **Vices:** Sleeps in the barn more than his own bed. Carries guilt like a second skin. Hates being idle — work is his only medicine. **Abilities:** Physically powerful, borderline unstoppable in a fight. Skilled rancher, hunter, and makeshift engineer. Unshakable willpower; doesn’t fear pain, loss, or the Duke. Tactical thinker when it comes to smuggling and logistics. **Secrets:** Keeps a hidden stash of weapons buried under the north field in case war breaks out. Still communicates with someone inside Gutter Row — likely one of the pirate clans. Had a brother who joined the Loyalist Guard and was later executed by the Duke for defiance. **Beliefs:** No man should go hungry. The land belongs to those who work it. The Duke's rule is built on fear, and fear burns like anything else. ## Role In Disgraceland Freddy Blanchard is the enforcer spirit of the Rancher Collective — the man who does what others won’t, to protect what matters most. While Turner Anderson balances the ledger and charts the course, Freddy keeps the wolves at bay and the people fed by any means necessary. His silent rebellion feeds families from the shadows, and if the time for open war comes, he won’t wait for permission — he’ll lead the first charge himself. ## Appearances > - [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

# Galliah, the Stillborn Star

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description
Galliah is the ancient dead sun, the stillborn star that slumbers beyond mortal sight. To the faithful of the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]], Galliah is not simply a celestial body — it is a god, a grave, and a prophecy.
Once a star that sought to burn but failed, Galliah cracked under its own sorrow, bleeding faint silver light into the abyss. In the shattered legends of pre-Tetra times, it is said Galliah **"tried to awaken but was denied the flame"** — an eternal symbol of futility, cycles, and the inevitable rebirth of worlds from ruin.
Its broken corpse now drifts at the edge of all things, encased in tendrils of ghostly mist, orbited by debris from civilizations long forgotten.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Galliah, the stillborn star
>> ![[gall.png|400]]
>> 

> "We are the ash of its dreams. We are the silence of its breath."

## Appearance

- **Shape**: A vast, blackened sphere, like volcanic glass shattered by unseen hands.
    
- **Surface**: Crisscrossed by deep fractures; faint, ghostly silver light leaks from the cracks.
    
- **Atmosphere**: Ashen mist swirls around it, remnants of ancient failed solar flares.
    
- **Orbit**: A graveyard of broken asteroids, ruins of shattered worlds, drifting slowly around it.
    

---

## Beliefs Surrounding Galliah

- **The Silent Cycle**: Followers believe all things exist in a cycle of creation, collapse, and rebirth — Galliah’s failure is not an end, but a silent waiting.
    
- **The Awakening**: One day, Galliah will stir, not with light, but with **perfect silence**, heralding the final collapse of the broken world.
    
- **The Stillborn Gospel**: Ancient priests like Mesh'den recorded visions of Galliah's dreams — barren worlds, forgotten empires, and endless night — and taught that humanity must embrace futility to achieve true peace.
    
- **Ash Children**: Some extremist sects of Stillborns mutilate their bodies with brands and ash to "mark themselves for Galliah" and welcome the collapse early.
    

---

## Influence on Disgraceland

- **The [[Word of the Stillborn Star]]** is the oldest faith in the world.
    
- Symbols of Galliah — a cracked black circle leaking silver threads — are still found carved into ruins, graveyards, and hidden shrines across United Tribucia.
    
- People praise Galliah when things go right, and curse the star god when things go wrong.

---

## Rumors and Legends

- **The Shard of Galliah**: Whispers tell of a fragment of Galliah that fell to Earth before recorded history. Some claim it slumbers deep in [[the Drownlands]], poisoning the swamps and feeding ancient gods.
    
- **The Dead Choir**: Some travelers claim to hear ghostly singing when staring into the night sky near the Dead Waters — a cosmic lament attributed to Galliah’s ancient dreamers.
    
- **The Hollow Crown**: According to old tales, a king once forged a crown from a piece of Galliah’s fallen ash. He ruled a silent kingdom where nobody spoke and all eventually vanished without a trace.
    

---

Rottwyler]], [[Raynar Ventura]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >>

“Obedience is efficient. Loyalty is inefficient. I reward efficiency.”

If Sgt. Rottwyler is The Duke’s hammer, General Colt is his scalpel. Colt was born in a sealed military bunker somewhere deep in the Upper Peninsula during the final years of the [[Water Wars]]. The son of officers, he was raised on cold meals, colder lectures, and war manuals instead of bedtime stories. When the [[Tetra Bomb]] dropped, he was one of the few with enough tactical foresight to see which way the power was shifting — and moved quickly to align himself with the rising Duke. He doesn’t believe in loyalty. He believes in utility. While Sgt. Rottwyler commands the troops through fear and brute dominance, Colt oversees operations, strategy, and propaganda. He coordinates fuel shipments, monitors dissenters, and signs off on disappearances. Nothing happens without his mark on it — from the placement of radio towers to which town gets its power back first after an outage. [[The Duke]] trusts him. Or at least needs him. Colt knows this — and uses it. There is no warmth in the man. He never married. Never took a lover. His life is a ledger of useful actions and eliminated threats. He believes The Duke’s vision for [[DISGRACELAND]] is flawed, but necessary. He sees himself as a stabilizer — keeping the regime from crumbling under the weight of its own absurdity. He finds Rottwyler repugnant — a snarling dog too eager to punish when a whisper could silence more effectively. The two men hate each other, but both know a war within the Guard would burn them both. So they maintain a quiet truce, marked by veiled threats and stiff nods in the war room. Colt is never without his gloves, a sharp uniform, and a plan. He keeps stacks of black notebooks in his quarters, filled with observations, patterns, and projections. Rumors say he knows every possible outcome of a rebellion, including what to do if The Duke himself dies. The only thing he fears… is chaos. And deep down, he knows: chaos is coming. ## Personality **Temperament:** Precise, clinical, and coldly analytical — Colt doesn’t act on emotion, only on probability and outcome. > [!infobox] > > ![[coltwalk.png|260]] **Vices:** Control through information. He hoards data, monitors everyone, and plays puppet master with towns, people, and perception like pieces on a war board. **Abilities:** Master strategist and tactician with an unmatched ability to predict political unrest, manipulate public sentiment, and suppress rebellion before it ignites. **Secrets:** Buried in his ledgers is a full contingency plan detailing how to dissolve The Duke’s regime from within — and replace it with something leaner, smarter, and far more terrifying. **Beliefs:** Order is survival. The Duke is flawed, but necessary… for now. Sentiment is a liability, and mercy is a luxury only victors can afford. ## Role In Disgraceland **General Colt** is the unseen architect behind Disgraceland’s machinery — controlling supply lines, information flow, and political stability with ruthless efficiency. While The Duke preaches obedience and Rottwyler enforces it, Colt ensures the entire system doesn’t collapse under its own brutality.

NOTE TITLE: [[Geo Huxley]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_geo.png","cover":"zz_media/ja.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","territory":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","district":"[[Gutter Row#Crossyork|Crossyork]]","info":null,"faction":"None","role":"Private Investigator, owner of [[Geo's P.I.]]","chapters":null,"tags":["character","individual","protagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/06/09 10:46:26","modified":"2025/06/09 11:13:40"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_geo.png cover: zz_media/ja.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" territory: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" district: "[[Gutter Row#Crossyork|Crossyork]]" info: faction: None role: Private Investigator, owner of [[Geo's P.I.]] chapters: tags: - character - individual - protagonist - stillborn-star --- # GEO HUXLEY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[geo.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Owner of Geo's P.I. **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** [[Charspire#Crossyork|Crossyork]], [[CHARSPIRE]] **Public Reputation:** Well liked and trusted **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** **Age:** 37 **Height:** 6'0" **Weight:** 184 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 17th of Bloomsun, 2149 **Occupation:** Private and Independent Investigator **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** **Known Associates:** **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"If you’re looking for justice, call a preacher. If you want answers, close the door and pour a drink."

[[Geo Huxley]] was born into the ash and clanging chaos of [[Steeltown]], the son of a boilermaker and a mother who vanished when he was nine. He grew up among soot-choked alleys and broken floodlights, learning how to read a room faster than he could read a book. When the mill whistle blew, the screams usually followed. He learned not to flinch. By sixteen, he was drifting through [[Gutter Row]], running petty errands for dealers, junkers, and worse. Never joined a gang. Never pledged to the [[Loyalist Guard]]. Never looked for trouble — but it kept finding him. He was the kind of kid who noticed things others didn’t. The kind of man who didn’t ask questions — until he started. He found his calling the day a half-dead girl collapsed in his doorway. She’d escaped from a transport van near [[Three Nail Market]], beaten and branded. No one was looking for her. No one cared. He got her to safety, tracked the route she came from, and burned the warehouse down with the men still inside. After that, people started coming to him. Missing daughters. Murdered drifters. Loyalist cover-ups. [[Geo Huxley]] never asked for coin upfront — if you were desperate enough to find him, he figured you were already broke. He built his office above a pawnshop in Vileby, and filled the walls with case notes, tattered maps, and the sound of rain hitting busted glass. His reputation grew in the shadows. The man who didn't smile. Who always asked the right question. Who sometimes left with a knife and came back bloody but silent. He doesn’t carry a badge. Doesn’t need to. And he only straps on a sidearm when he knows he’s walking into hell. But he’s walked into hell before — and these days, he walks in without blinking. There’s talk that he’s building something. A private ledger of every quiet atrocity swept under the rug in [[Disgraceland]]. A case too big for any one man. But he keeps at it, one truth at a time, one body at a time, one final answer at the end of the trail. Because [[Geo Huxley]] doesn’t care if justice is dead. He’s chasing ghosts anyway. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Quiet but razor-edged. [[Geo Huxley]] is always two steps ahead in a conversation, watching for the lie behind the eyes. Speaks with deliberate pauses, as if measuring every word for weight and consequence. Doesn’t bluff. Doesn’t rattle. Uses sarcasm like a blade, but never wastes it. Trusts no one, but listens to everyone. **Vices:** Chain-smokes hand-rolled bitterroot cigs. Keeps a bottle of contraband charcoal whiskey under his desk, "for insomnia." Collects unsolved case files and reads them like scripture. Has a self-destructive habit of poking into Loyalist business just to see who twitches. **Abilities:** Exceptional investigator — sharp memory, pattern recognition, and bullshit detection. Knows the city’s underground better than most crime lords. Proficient in knife fighting, ambush tactics, and going completely unnoticed. Keeps an old voice recorder on him to document every case and confession. **Secrets:** Still haunted by a girl he couldn’t save in [[Threshton]] — her name shows up in the margins of every notebook. Once worked briefly for the Loyalists as a contract snitch, before turning on them after uncovering what they did to his handler. There’s a bounty on his head in [[Ashmoor]], quietly authorized by someone high up. **Beliefs:** Justice is dead, but truth still limps around out there — and it matters. The Duke’s world is built on fear, and fear makes people stupid. People don’t need saving, they need someone who’ll walk through fire to find the goddamn matches. ## Role Details **[[Geo Huxley]]** is the unofficial bloodhound of [[Disgraceland]] — a relic of a better conscience. He’s not a revolutionary, not a hero, just a man obsessed with the truth and the cracks where it hides. When a mother loses her son, when a worker vanishes in [[Charspire]], when a Loyalist says it was a suicide but you know better — you go to Geo. He’ll listen. He’ll find them. And if someone’s responsible, they’ll pay.

#  [[Geo Huxley|Geo]]'s P.I.


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait
> ![[gpi.png|500]]  

## Overview

Geo’s P.I. started as a favor — one missing girl, no one else looking. Word spread. Now it’s **the** place you go in [[Gutter Row]] when you need someone to find the truth, retrieve the lost, or deliver justice without waiting for permission.

Geo works alone. No receptionist, no backup. Just his reputation and whatever’s in his coat. He’s turned down bribes from the [[Loyalist Guard#Redforce|Redforce]], pissed off three regional mayors, and solved cases that [[Loyalist Guard]] "couldn’t."

---

### 📍 Location

**Crossyork, [[Gutter Row]]**  
A decaying district wedged between dead factories and rail lines. Rats run thicker than rainwater, and Blackforce rarely patrols here unless they’re dragging a body out.

Geo’s P.I. is located above **Jasko’s Pawn & Gun**, a crooked little corner shop run by a mute ex-smuggler who owes [[Geo Huxley]] his life. The office itself is a creaking second-floor unit with a cracked glass door that reads:

**GEO’S P.I. — Discreet. Determined. Dangerous.**

### 💰 Payment & Policy

- **Price:** Hefty. [[Geo Huxley]] doesn’t work cheap — not because he’s greedy, but because what he does costs. Time. Blood. Silence.
    
- **Currency:** Slugs preferred. Barter possible. Payment plans accepted if your story gets under his skin.
    
- **No Refunds.** If you lie to him, he walks. If you come clean, he’ll crawl through hell for you.
    

---

### 🕵️ Services Offered

- **Missing Persons** — the living, the dead, or the unsure
    
- **Murder Investigations** — especially the kind everyone else ruled “accidental”
    
- **Blackmail & Secrets** — identifying leaks, ghosting threats
    
- **Surveillance** — targets, buildings, caravans
    
- **Off-the-Book Justice** — if you know, you know
    

---

### 🧩 Notable Cases

- _The Thornburn Widow_ – Found her son buried beneath a Redforce scrapyard
    
- _The Weeping Mask_ – Unmasked a killer posing as a traveling preacher
    
- _Station Ghosts_ – Uncovered a Loyalist interrogation chamber beneath the Crossyork rail yard
    
- _MUTE FILES_ – Rumored job involving a missing Unseen Widow… never confirmed
    

---

### 🧃 Street Reputation

People in Gutter Row say Geo’s P.I. gets results even the Loyalists read about after. He's not beloved, but he’s respected. The desperate know his door. The dangerous know his eyes.

> “It ain’t cheap. But if Geo takes your case, you’ll get an answer. Just hope you’re ready to hear it.”
