“Hope don’t run a furnace. Fear does.”

In the smog-strangled hellscape of [[Charspire]], where molten runoff glows in the gutters and the air tastes like burning metal, Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] sits fat and content atop a mountain of suffering he helped build. He didn’t rise to power through merit. He slithered his way into it—feeding [[The Duke]] a steady diet of intelligence pulled from the slums, the mills, and the whispers of the desperate. For years, Brile was a name no one said out loud, just a shadow that passed coin for secrets and disappeared before the screaming started. When the old foreman-mayor “vanished” during a boiler explosion, Brile was already waiting in a fresh suit with a new title. Now, as Duke-appointed mayor, he oversees [[Charspire]] with bloated arrogance, a snake-headed cane in one hand and a smoldering cigar in the other. He keeps the mines running, the mills churning, and the death toll climbing. But it’s not Brile himself that people fear. It’s his [[RedForce]]. A handpicked squad of bruisers, burnouts, and sadists in blood-red armor—the RedForce are more gang than guard. Bankrolled by the Loyalist Guard, they wear dark leather dusters with crimson plates over their chests, and helmets shaped like steel-welded frowns. Their job is simple: enforce, extract, erase. They drag "disloyal" workers into the streets and make examples of them. They storm homes in the middle of the night. They torture rebels in boiler rooms and chain corpses to smokestacks as warnings. The RedForce doesn’t arrest. They punish. Brile watches it all from his brass office above the slagfields—pockets lined, trousers stained, and ego swollen. He makes regular visits to [[GUTTER ROW]], always under heavy escort, to indulge in the red-light vices with sickening pride. His appetites are legendary, and his reputation just as filthy. No one loves Mayor Gorren Brile. But no one dares remove him either. Not yet. Because in Charspire, fear still outvotes hope. ## Personality **Temperament:** Lecherous, loud, and quick to anger. Treats fear like applause. **Vices:** Sex, violence, gluttony, cruelty. Keeps a collection of gold rings he’s taken off corpses. **Abilities:** Bribery, blackmail, and brutal intimidation. Doesn’t need to be smart—just needs to know who to break. **Secrets:** Keeps a hidden tunnel from his office to a Gutter Row brothel. Maintains secret recordings of Duke meetings for leverage. Claims to have dirt on every other mayor. **Beliefs:** Fear gets results. Loyalty is a lie people tell to stay alive. The strong survive, the useful thrive, and the rest burn. ## Role in Disgraceland [[Gorren Brile]] rules [[Charspire]] with bloated pride and violent indulgence, relying on the infamous [[RedForce]] to crush opposition before it can breathe. He is everything wrong with the industrial world made flesh—a greedy pig wrapped in silk and soot. But The Duke needs his brutality, and the factories need to run, so Brile stays in power… for now. ## Appearances

NOTE TITLE: [[GUTTER ROW]] METADATA:{"NoteIcon":"settlement","tags":["Category/Settlement","gutter row","territory"],"cover":"zz_media/gutt1.png","Alignment":"Unlawful Evil","Government":"Mayor","reputation":"trash class","politics":"Mayor","leader":[["Cricket Granger"]],"region":["South Tribucia"],"size":"Township","population":"88,000","religion":["Church of the Ember Saint"],"exports":["Power, Authority"],"imports":["Everything"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/05 17:07:55"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- NoteIcon: settlement tags: - Category/Settlement - gutter row - territory cover: zz_media/gutt1.png Alignment: Unlawful Evil Government: Mayor reputation: trash class politics: Mayor leader: [[Cricket Granger]] region: - South Tribucia size: Township population: 88,000 religion: - Church of the Ember Saint exports: - Power, Authority imports: - Everything --- # GUTTER ROW

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎GUTTER ROW > ![[gutt1.png|400]] Gutter Row is the choking heart of Disgraceland — a lawless sprawl of rusted rooftops, splintered alleyways, and desperate humanity. It's where the black market thrives, the weak vanish, and the rules don’t apply. Smoke curls from every rooftop. The streets reek of sweat, piss, rot, and fried rat. You don’t come here unless you have to — and if you do, you don’t linger. By far the most overpopulated zone in all of United Tribucia, Gutter Row stretches endlessly in every direction, packed shoulder-to-shoulder with shanties, scrap-built towers, and narrow corridors crawling with barterers, thieves, and worse. The economy runs on favors, smuggling, and the unspoken understanding that everything — and everyone — has a price. The slave trade operates in plain sight, tucked just behind the street food vendors and stolen tech booths. Locals carve their lives out in the districts of [[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]], [[GUTTER ROW#Nailstooth|Nailstooth]], [[GUTTER ROW#Pisstown|Pisstown]], [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]], [[GUTTER ROW#Reapton|Reapton]], Garbage Bay, and [[GUTTER ROW#Crossyork|Crossyork]] — each one worse than the last, each with its own twisted rhythm. There's no safety, only familiarity. People grow up fast here. Or they don’t grow up at all. The so-called police force is a unit known as [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]], though most call them _Black Shirts_. Dressed in matte black armor with emotionless masks and reinforced batons, they patrol sporadically — more interested in keeping tribute flowing to [[The Duke]] than protecting anyone. When they do show up, it’s usually to silence someone who said too much. Gutter Row isn’t just where the forgotten live. It’s where power hides. Where secrets are bought in whispers. And where a match, dropped in the right place, could burn the whole rotten thing down.

Districts

#### Vileby The black heart of Gutter Row. **Vileby** is where the Three Nail Market churns night and day, pumping illicit deals into every vein of Tribucia. [[Third Row]] gang runs things from the shadows — and sometimes not-so-shadowy rooftops. Vileby Hills rises just north, where the [[Murray Boys]] hold court in their fortified mansion. It’s the only place in Gutter Row where guards wear suits, and deals end with champagne instead of switchblades. --- #### Nailstooth A place even Gutter Row winces at. **Nailstooth** is where you land when you’ve got nothing left — not even the decency to die in a proper alley. It’s all rusted iron, tar-paper roofs, and barking dogs with ribs showing. The ground smells like rot. The people don't flinch when guns go off. You don’t walk into Nailstooth. You get dragged there. --- #### The Docks Southernmost point in all of Tribucia, **The Docks** is a salt-bitten maze of boats, rusted cranes, and rat-infested boardwalks. Fishermen haul in whatever the Dead Waters will spare, and families scrape by in tide-worn homes. When the fog rolls in, it feels like the world ends here — and maybe it should. --- #### Crossyork If Gutter Row has a postcard, it's **Crossyork** — and even that’s water-stained and half-torched. The mayor lives here behind iron bars and blackout curtains, trying to pretend the rest of the Row doesn’t exist. But the Rustwater Raiders haven’t forgotten. They hit often, sailing in from the Four Tombs Islands just off the coast. Crossyork smells like brine, smoke, and fresh betrayal. --- #### Pisstown No place bleeds like **Pisstown**. It’s where dreams die screaming and legends are born twisted. [[Dusty Dillon]] grew up singing in the alleys here. [[Ora Razchek]] built his death house above it all. And somewhere in the fog, [[The Grim Man]] stalks like a goddamn ghost with a grudge. Pisstown’s streets eat souls and spit bones. If you’re here, you’ve already lost something. --- #### Reapton They call it the working spine of Gutter Row — bent, cracked, and somehow still upright. **Reapton** is where the [[Tribucia Tribute]] gets printed, and where proud folks grind out survival without a safety net. It's paperboys dodging knives. It's ink-stained hands and busted typewriters. If Gutter Row has a conscience, it’s buried somewhere beneath Reapton’s mud. --- #### Savage Hill Everything’s louder in **Savage Hill**. The wind off Garbage Coast blows sour through these streets, but laughter still rises above it — the kind that hides pain. The **Ha Ha Hole** comedy club lights up the block, defiant and alive. Outside, trash fires burn, rats riot, and broken TVs scream static. But inside, jokes land harder than fists. --- #### South Point Close to Ashmoor, far from the madness. **South Point** is a sleepy stretch where a few local farmers till what land they can. The soil’s no good, the water’s worse, but the air isn’t poison and the nights are quiet. Folks here keep their heads down and their fences mended. It ain’t paradise — but it ain’t Pisstown either. --- #### Red Light District Vice without apology. **The Red Light District** is Gutter Row's fever dream, lit by flickering neon and fueled by broken morals. The **Hollow House**, run by [[Shana]], is the beating heart — a brothel, a fortress, a sanctuary of sin. Luxyn dealers, synth clubs, fight dens. You want it, it’s here. Just remember, payment comes due — one way or another. ---

# [[The Ha Ha Hole]]

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Ha Ha Hole Comedy Club
> ![[haha.png|450]]  

**Location:** [[Savage Hill]], [[Gutter Row]]
**Founded:** 2140s  
**Founder:** [[Tyren Will]]

---

## Overview

Deep in the twisted alleys of [[Savage Hill]], where broken signs hang like nooses and laughter usually means someone’s about to get hurt, sits one of the most unlikely cultural landmarks in all of Disgraceland — **The Ha Ha Hole**.

Opened in the 2140s by a wild-eyed maniac named [[Tyren Will]], this underground comedy club has grown from a dive for drunks to a nightly pilgrimage site for anyone desperate to laugh — or drink — their way through the horror show of modern life. With a rotting neon grin over the door and the famous slogan **“First drink is on us”**, The Ha Ha Hole is packed nearly every night.

The club draws crowds from every region — even a few brave souls from [[Ashmoor]] and [[Threshton]] — all crammed into a basement of sweaty seats, leaning in for the next punchline, heckle, or blackout.

---

## The Founder – [[Tyren Will]]

A former traveling magician, failed preacher, and once-suspected poisoner, [[Tyren Will]] is a living myth. Nobody’s entirely sure how old he is or how he managed to keep The Ha Ha Hole open during some of the darkest years after the Tetra Bomb, but he’s always been there — top hat, cane, silver tongue and all. 

Now well into his eighties, he still takes the stage unannounced on occasion to deliver bizarre rants, surreal monologues, or what he calls “anti-jokes” — strange, unsettling stories that sometimes end with a single word: *“Think.”* The audience still cheers him every time.

---

## Atmosphere

- **Stage:** A cracked wooden platform with a dented mic that sparks when tapped.
- **Decor:** Candlelight, red velvet curtains stained with gods-know-what, and every wall covered in graffiti and signatures from past performers.
- **Drinks:** The first one's free, everything after that gets progressively stronger (and less legal).
- **Security:** None. The crowd polices itself, usually with laughter or bottles.

---

## Signature Acts

- **Joley Punch** – Queen of the deadpan roast. She once told a joke so mean a Redforce officer walked out in tears.
- **Little Duke** – A parody act mocking The Duke in crown and cape. Somehow still alive.
- **Shivvy** – Combines burlesque with satire. Leaves the crowd dazed, confused, and howling.
- **Riggs Mahoney** – An ex-Loyalist turned loudmouth stage beast.
- **The Masked Heckler** – A recurring mystery comic who destroys hecklers with surgical precision. No one knows who it is.

---

## Cultural Impact

Despite being a cesspool of rebellion, filth, and unlicensed liquor, **The Ha Ha Hole** has become a cultural staple. Even citizens loyal to The Duke secretly tune into bootleg recordings of sets from the club. Its influence on slang, satire, and protest culture across Disgraceland is undeniable.

[[The Duke]] publicly despises the place and has tried to shut it down twice — once via regulation, once with a full Loyalist raid. Both attempts failed. The crowd turned violent. The club only got more popular.

---

## Rumors & Lore

- **Red Room in the Back:** Some say a private room exists where Tyren meets with outlaws, prophets, and ghosts.
- **The Laugh That Kills:** Urban myth claims one joke told in '62 made a man laugh so hard he seized and died. The tape was burned.
- **Secret Resistance:** Some believe The Ha Ha Hole is more than a club — it’s a safehouse, a spy ring, a gathering place for the loud and dangerous.

---

## Quote

> *“We don’t do hope here. We do laughter — it stings less.”*  
> — [[Tyren Will]]

(and every ounce is hard) **Date of Birth:** Lost to history **Occupation:** Rancher, Founder of Red Night Ranch **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Rancher Collective]] **Known Associates:** [[Turner Anderson]], [[Freddy Blanchard]], [[Beau DuNoir]], [[Danny Dandelion]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"A man's only got two choices in this world. Work the land… or get buried in it."

**Harp Langston** is the reason Threshton didn’t die with the ash. Founder of the [[THRESHTON#Red Night Ranch|Red Night Ranch]] and the first to strike a devil’s bargain with [[The Duke]], Harp is legend stitched to leather. No one really knows how old he is — some say he came from [[The Drownlands]] on a dying mare with two rifles and a waxcloth pouch of seeds. Others say he built his ranch on a battlefield, where the soil still coughs up bullets and bones when the wind shifts. What *is* known is that when the skies turned black and the hunger set in, Harp planted. While everyone else bartered, begged, or burned, Harp was putting posts in the dirt and cursing the land into submission. Against all odds, the earth listened. He brought life back to a place that had forgotten what green looked like. And when The Duke came crawling in with his false promises and trade offers, Harp made the first deal — not because he trusted him, but because he *understood* him. That deal built the foundation of the Rancher Collective. Time, though, is a bastard. Harp’s hair is thinning now, his spine bent from a lifetime of labor. His knife is older than some townships, and twice as cruel. He doesn’t trust the other ranchers — especially not slick-talking [[Beau DuNoir]] or that worm-tongued rat [[Danny Dandelion]] (whose name he refuses to speak aloud). [[Freddy Blanchard]] is too noble for his liking. Only [[Turner Anderson]] gets a nod now and then — but even that’s rare, and never warm. He runs Red Night like a war camp. No drinking, no music, no visitors without scars. The land produces more wheat than any other spread in the region, but no one calls it pleasant. You don’t go to Red Night for comfort. You go to survive. His one living child, Mayor [[Soria Langston-Clay]] of [[Ashmoor]], is a bitter stain on his legacy. She betrayed the people of [[Threshton]] for power and [[The Duke]]’s favor — and Harp has never once spoken her name since. Was an old friend of legend, [[Darrell Douglass]] When Harp speaks at a meeting, the others listen. They may not like him. Hell, most days they don’t. But they damn sure *respect* him. And if the day comes when Threshton needs to burn it all down and start over, you can bet Harp Langston’s the one holding the match. --- ## Personality Harp is mean as rust and twice as unyielding. He’s not just gruff — he’s *hostile* to most people who breathe too loud or ask too many questions. He wakes before dawn, eats cold oats from a tin, and patrols his land like a soldier walking a trench. He despises snakes, lies, and ceremony. If someone wastes his time, they don’t get a second chance. The only music he tolerates is the sound of a hammer on steel or boots crunching dirt. Despite it all, he’s honest — brutally so — and demands the same from anyone under his roof. ## Role In Disgraceland Harp Langston is the spine of the Rancher Collective — the unbreakable elder who remembers what Threshton was *before* the Duke, and who never stopped working to keep it alive. Every rancher in the Collective owes their foothold to Harp’s first gamble with survival. He’s not a leader in the traditional sense — he’s a relic. A hard, bitter man who still gets things done. If Threshton is a house built on dust and blood, Harp is the post that refuses to rot. ## Relationships > ### [[Darrell Douglass]] > Of all the allies Harp Langston ever had, none ran deeper than **[[Darrell Douglass]]**. The two met in 2151, when Darrell managed to restart the old mill in [[Steeltown]] — a miracle by post-war standards. Harp rode up with a bag of dried oats and left with a bond. For years, they coordinated in the shadows, running the Black Route — a quiet supply chain of food, tools, and hope between Steeltown and Threshton. It was never official. No documents, no promises. Just trust. Harp didn’t trust easily, but he trusted Darrell. > That trust was tested in 2158 when Darrell was captured and forced to work under the Duke’s boot. Harp wanted to fight back, to rescue him, but the other ranchers refused to risk the Collective. It was one of the few times Harp let others outvote him. He and Darrell argued before the silence took hold. Harp buried the guilt under work, never speaking Darrell’s name in public again. But on the night Darrell was executed in 2167, something changed. A silo on the edge of Red Night Ranch caught fire, no livestock harmed. Just ash. A symbol left in the dirt: the same one Darrell wore on his arm. Harp never explained it. He didn’t need to. > ---

NOTE TITLE: [[Hella]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_hella.png","religion":"None","status":"Alive","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","territory":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","district":"[[GUTTER ROW#Pisstown|Pisstown]]","faction":"None","role":"Assistant to [[Ora Razchek]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","04 - Glowing Darkness","07 - The Spotlight Lies"],"tags":["character","individual","antagonist","chapter04"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/09 10:33:32"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_hella.png religion: None status: Alive location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" territory: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" district: "[[GUTTER ROW#Pisstown|Pisstown]]" faction: None role: "Assistant to [[Ora Razchek]]" chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 04 - Glowing Darkness - 07 - The Spotlight Lies tags: - character - individual - antagonist - chapter04 --- # HELLA > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[hella.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** [[Gutter Row]] **Public Reputation:** **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** 21 **Height:** 5'9" **Weight:** 114 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 25th of Searsun, 2165 **Occupation:** Body grabber **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Ora Razchek]] **Known Associates:** **Faith:** None **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Everybody in Gutter Row gets a second chance. Some just don’t recognize it until it’s too late.”

Once just another forgotten girl working Gutter Row’s filthiest corners, **Hella** survived where others vanished—by learning to read the monsters, and, when it mattered, becoming one. When Ora Razchek found her, instead of running or pleading, she _saw him_—for what he was, and what he could offer. She bargained, bled, and proved her value, and Razchek let her live. Now, she’s his shadow. His collector. His disciple. Every night, she haunts the alleys and ruins, luring the desperate, the addicted, the forgotten—anyone nobody will miss—back to the mansion on the hill. One, two, sometimes three at a time, night after night. Each body disappears into Razchek’s hands, never to return as themselves. **She loves Ora Razchek.** Worships him, really. He’s the father she never had, the only person who ever looked at her and saw anything worth saving. She’d do anything for him. _And she does._ But what Hella doesn’t know—the gut-punch horror of it all—is that this devotion isn’t real. It’s artificial. Razchek already implanted her with a subtle AI protocol, rewriting her loyalty, her affection, even her sense of self. She’s already more machine than she knows—his first true “child,” the prototype, and she has no idea. Whenever she asks to join the ranks of the _monsters_ below, Ora gently refuses, telling her she’s too young, too _special_. Secretly, he’s keeping her on a tighter leash than any of his creatures. Hella is his eyes, his ears, and the knife in the dark. Razchek’s army now numbers roughly 1,500 monsters, all stored in the warren beneath his mansion—waiting for his signal, and for Hella’s next delivery. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** On the surface, she’s sweet, sad, and broken—almost innocent. But when she’s on the hunt, something else takes over—ruthless, cunning, no empathy at all. That’s the AI running the show. **Vices:** Her obsession with Razchek. Her entire sense of worth is tied to pleasing Ora, even at the expense of her own safety, morals, or sanity. She has a history of addiction (Luxyn, affection, danger). Now, her devotion to Razchek is her new drug. **Abilities:** She can read body language and weakness like a book—knows exactly how to pick her targets and how to approach each one. Moves through the city’s alleys unseen, silent as a shadow; can vanish in seconds if spotted. Expert liar and seductress—can fake innocence, kindness, or terror to get what she wants. **Secrets:** Her love and loyalty aren’t real. She believes she’s made her own choices, but her deepest feelings for Razchek are the result of AI programming. She senses “something’s wrong” with her thoughts sometimes—she dreams in static, sometimes forgets whole nights, but blames it on trauma. She suspects Razchek is using her for more than deliveries—but she pushes those thoughts down, afraid of what she might find. **Beliefs:** Ora Razchek is her salvation. She truly believes he saved her from oblivion and that serving him is her purpose. ## Role In Disgraceland Hella is the shadowy hand of Razchek, the collector who supplies his endless army beneath the city. To the desperate, she’s a siren; to the streetwise, she’s a warning. Every rumor of a missing person starts with her pale smile in a rain-soaked alley. > [!rustwater]- Surprise >

## **“HYMN FROM A DEAD GIRL”**  
##### _A B-Side from the End Times_

> When a lowlife runner delivers a chained girl to a butcher named [[Scumbag]], the screams that follow echo beneath [[Gutter Row]] — but by the time [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] arrives, all that's left is silence... and a hymn no one wants to hear again.

[[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] moved like a wave — five armored Loyalists with skull-face masks and slug rifles swept through the entrance of the tannery. The scent hit them first. Rot. Rust. Burnt hair.

“Stack up,” barked the lead, a large man named Capt. Bellis.

They broke through the rusted door into the crawlspace.

Silence.

The lantern still flickered, low and weak. The girl was dead — posed like some twisted statue, fingers reaching out toward nothing. Her skin was carved in lines and arcs. Not words. Not symbols. Just madness.

Dreg lay beside her, arms bent the wrong way, eyes wide, mouth agape.

Bellis turned away and dry-heaved. One of the others muttered a prayer.

“Clear,” said another, voice cracking.

"Holy fucking shit." Said a third. 

They found no killer. No movement. Just blood that had dried too fast, like it’d been baking in heat that wasn’t there.

Two buildings over, on a slanted rooftop slick with old rain and bird droppings, [[Scumbag]] crouched at the edge like a gargoyle. One leg dangled off the ledge, the other tucked under him as he tore into a half-rotten orange with dirty fingernails.

Below, the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] moved like ants — precise, mechanical, angry.

He watched them like a god from a pulpit.

“Shame,” he whispered, mouth full. “Didn’t even get to the chorus.”

He licked his fingers. Kept staring.

“Well... maybe it's time to share my beautiful music with the rest of the world.”

Then he laughed.

And it didn’t stop.

The kid's boots squelched with every nervous step. 

He was a wiry, maybe twenty, with patchy stubble, pockmarked cheeks, and a twitch in his left eye that never quite settled. His jacket was an old [[Loyalist Guard]] castoff, faded red with torn sleeves and rust-colored stains he didn’t bother to clean. Grease-slicked hair hung over his brow, and the fingers of his free hand twitched near the grip of the rust-flaked slug pistol at his waist. The path ahead was narrow, hemmed in by brick walls that sweated moisture and the stink of copper. Old piss and rot pooled in the cracks, and red lanterns flickered overhead like dying eyes. This was the Red Stalls, where [[Gutter Row]] sold things even [[Gutter Row]] didn’t talk about.

He kept a hand close to the rust-flaked slug pistol tucked in his waistband, and the other on the chain leash of the girl dragging behind him. She didn’t cry. Didn’t speak. Just followed with glassy eyes and scraped-up knees. Somebody’d done a number on her before Dreg even got the job.

He didn’t ask. You don’t ask when the job comes from the [[Third Row]].

A figure waited at the far end of the alley. Dreg couldn’t see the face, just the outline — tall, wide-shouldered, unmoving.

He cleared his throat. “I got what you asked for.”

The figure tilted its head.

Dreg licked his lips. “They said… they said you’d pay me in [[Luxyn]].”

The man stepped forward. Slowly. His boots made no sound. In the dim lantern glow, his face finally showed — too-wide grin, black paint streaked his face, tangled black hair. A loop of rope hung around his neck like a necktie. Muscles cut through his arms like prison scars, and his fists were wrapped in torn cloth and filth.

[[Scumbag]] didn’t say a word, just let out a small chuckle.

Dreg stepped back. “Hey, man, I ain’t part of this. I just deliver, alright? You want her, fine. I’ll turn around. I ain’t seen shit.”

[[Scumbag]] took another step.

The girl whimpered.

Dreg looked at her and quickly back to [[Scumbag]] before quickly pulling his pistol, hands shaking. “Stay the fuck back. I swear to Santo, I’ll shoot.”

Scumbag’s grin widened. He didn’t stop.

The first shot rang out, but it hit the bricks. The second never came. Dreg screamed.

Then there was only the sound of dragging chains, humming, and wet meat sliding against stone.

---

The lantern barely held a flame, its cracked glass lens giving off more shadow than light. The crawlspace behind the old tannery was wet, low, and quiet except for the sound of sloshing boots and metal scraping against stone.

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[b1.png|300]]

[[Scumbag]] moved like a butcher in a trance. One hand dragged the chain — the girl’s broken body still half-attached to it — and the other clutched Dreg’s limp corpse tied using the rope [[Scumbag]] wore that was now wrapped around Dreg's ankle. Both left red trails behind them, but he didn’t mind. Not here. Not underground.

He was humming. Off-key. Something soft. Sweet, almost.

He dropped them both near a rusted basin that hadn’t held water in years and knelt beside the girl. Her eyes were wide open. Not glassy. Not dead. Not yet.

He gently brushed the matted hair from her eyes and looked her up and down. Her shirt was already torn and she meekly tried to cover herself. Scumbag moved her hands back down.

“I hear it,” he whispered to her, brushing a streak of blood from her cheek with surprising tenderness. “Every piece got a sound. Your scream? Gonna be real high. Got that glass-edge note. Like a teacup when it shatters.”

She tried to speak, but only a rattling noise came out.

[[Scumbag]] grinned. “Yeah, like that. That’s music.”

He took out a knife that didn’t look clean. Didn’t look sharp either. Just old. Used. Like it had its own memories.

The screams didn’t echo in the crawlspace. They just lingered.

He carved, not for cruelty, but for composition. He talked the whole time — to her, to himself, to the shadows.

“Ligaments play low,” he muttered, dragging the blade slowly across her thigh. “Tendons hum. But nerves?” He paused, tilting his head like he was listening to a distant song. “Nerves scream in soprano.”

He pressed the knife in again. The girl screamed in agony.

“This part right here? That’s a bridge. Got to ease into it. Build the tension. Like a real sad tune that don’t ever resolve.”

She sobbed, weakly.

“Oh, sweetheart,” he cooed, “that’s a beautiful note. Don’t stop singin’. Not yet.”

Every slice was a syllable. Every whimper a verse.

She stopped moving somewhere in the middle of the second stanza.

[[Scumbag]] frowned. “Aww pathetic.. already done and we ain't even finished the hook.”

He left her posed, one hand over her chest, the other reaching out toward the flickering light. Like she was calling for something she knew wouldn’t come.

Then he turned to Dreg. “Now you...you ain’t got a good scream. You suck.” He spat on Dreg's dead corpse.

He started again, this time working his knife over Dreg. Still humming.

Somewhere above, a window slammed. Voices. Boots.

Someone had called it in.

[[Scumbag]] didn’t flinch. He only smiled and rolled his eyes.

“They always come in on the wrong verse.”

“Morals don’t build empires. Steel does. And I own the furnace.”

The wealthiest man in Disgraceland. Few men in Gutter Row rise without getting dirt under their nails. Jacoban Clay didn’t just get dirt — he built an empire from it. The founder of Clay Millworks, Jacoban turned sweat, blood, and iron into wealth. He signed a deal with The Duke early on: free slave labor in exchange for endless shipments of metal — pipes, plates, shackles, weapons. Whatever the regime needed, Jacoban delivered. And he got rich. Fast. Unlike other industrialists, Jacoban wasn’t loud. He was calm. Calculated. Kept a clean shirt and a loaded pistol. While others begged for permits, Jacoban showed up with a sealed envelope and a nod from The Duke. Years later, while meeting with officials at The Silo, Jacoban saw a woman enter the room — dark hair pinned back, a red pendant resting just above her breasts, and a look in her eyes like she already owned the place. Her name was Soria Langston. And Jacoban decided then and there: she would be his. They married shortly after. Now, Jacoban lives lavishly in Ashmoor at her side, managing The Duke’s treasury and watching from behind velvet curtains. He still oversees his factories, still ensures the gears of war turn smoothly. But make no mistake — he didn’t marry Soria for love. He married her because together, they are untouchable. Or so they believe. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, composed, and opportunistic — Jacoban rarely raises his voice, preferring leverage over force and influence over spectacle. **Vices:** Greed masked as pragmatism. He doesn’t crave attention, only power — and he collects favors, secrets, and leverage like others collect art. **Abilities:** Gifted industrialist and financial manipulator; he can read contracts like confessionals and has a sixth sense for when to bribe, when to blackmail, and when to vanish a problem. **Secrets:** He keeps a hidden safe behind a false wall in his Ashmoor estate — filled not with money, but with dirt: letters, receipts, and signed orders that could destroy half of The Duke’s inner circle if released. **Beliefs:** Loyalty is a currency, nothing more. In Jacoban’s eyes, survival isn’t about strength — it’s about who controls the flow of iron, gold, and silence. ## Role In Disgraceland **Jacoban Clay** is the regime’s golden banker — the man behind the curtain who oils the war machine with slave labor and silence. He doesn’t seek the spotlight, but from the luxury of Ashmoor, he ensures the wealth keeps flowing and the truth stays buried.

“I don’t smile for ghosts. I just sing loud enough to drown ‘em out.”

Jaden Kade was born under the rusted towers of South [[Charspire]] — the son of a failed steelworker and a mother who vanished into the factories when he was seven. He grew up in alley fires and empty warehouses, learning guitar from a drunk ex-sound tech who once toured with real bands, back when real bands could tour. Jaden’s voice broke early and never quite healed right — now it drips with gravel and hurt, raw and unforgettable. He formed **[[The Wanderers]]** as a street act, playing for scraps and coins in makeshift markets across the regions. The band caught fire in the undercurrent — word-of-mouth spread fast, and eventually they became the pulse of backroom bars and outlaw safehouses. But everything changed the night [[Morris Gable]] showed up unannounced at a [[Gutter Row]] speakeasy, leaned against the wall, and watched them play three full sets. The next morning, Jaden was offered a deal: become the house band on [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]. Food. Shelter. National exposure. And complete creative control — as long as they didn’t "go too far." Jaden accepted. Not for fame, not for comfort — but for reach. His rebel soul still burns, but he’s learned how to play quiet in a world built to crush noise. Every time [[The Wanderers]] perform, he pushes the edge a little further — testing how much truth he can slip past the sensors. A lyric here. A look there. One day, maybe more. He despises Morris — calls him “the vulture in velvet” when he’s drunk — but they have an unspoken understanding. Morris gets the ratings. Jaden gets the stage. And Disgraceland gets the only real heartbeat left on the air. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Reckless but calculated. Passionate but tightly wound. Keeps his rage buried under smirks and silence until the mic’s hot — then he lets the notes bleed it out. Doesn’t say much during interviews. Keeps his answers vague, his tone flat. The fire comes out only in the music. **Vices:** Stims and chews (to stay focused on long broadcast nights). Often disappears into Gutter Row for days at a time with no explanation. Has an unresolved habit of sabotaging other artists he believes are regime puppets. **Abilities:** Plays multiple instruments (guitar, synth, harmonica, lapsteel). Voice like “torn velvet soaked in whiskey” — unmistakable. Writes all The Wanderers' songs, many of which are laced with coded anti-Duke metaphors. Extremely persuasive when he wants to be. **Secrets:** Jaden’s older brother was executed by Redforce in Charspire years ago — part of a failed uprising. He’s been slowly funneling slugs earned from the show toward funding illicit broadcasts and pirate signals. **Beliefs:** The Duke is a coward who hides behind glass and screens. Music is more than sound — it’s memory, it’s code, it’s war. He knows Morris Gable is a liar, but he respects the man’s _control_. Even snakes have rhythm. ## Role Details **Jaden Kade** is the unspoken voice of unrest in Disgraceland — a rebel hiding in plain sight, using the nation’s most-watched stage to echo resistance through rhythm. To the regime, he’s just the singer on a late-night show; to the people, he’s the last song that still feels honest. ## Appearances

## Biography

> "I ain’t here to talk. I’m here to remember.”

Born into the gutter, raised by fists, and rebuilt in violence, **Jailface** is the scarred iron-fanged lieutenant of The [[Third Row]] and the personal enforcer of [[Samson Knight]]. His true name has been lost — maybe forgotten, maybe discarded — but his new name was earned the day a rival gang welded a prison brace to his skull and left him for dead in the ash canals. He survived. He came back. He didn’t speak a word. Just started cutting.

Jailface grew up just two blocks from Row Three, a street kid with nothing to lose and too much anger to bury. In the early days of the Row Wars, he worked underground pit fights to feed himself — one fight cost him most of his teeth. The next gave him a reputation. By the time the old guard of The Third Row had fallen apart, Jailface was a half-legend in Gutter Row already, known for finishing what others wouldn’t start.

When [[Samson Knight]] began consolidating power in the 2170s, Jailface didn’t challenge him. He offered him something else — silence, skill, and a debt of loyalty. Some say Samson was the one who found him after the brace incident, pulled him out of the filth, and gave him purpose. Since then, Jailface has been at Knight’s right side: a shadow in the alleys, a whisper before the blood hits the floor.

No one speaks directly to Jailface unless they’re invited. And no one runs in the [[Three Nail Market]] without his approval.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Unflinching, cold-blooded, and eerily quiet. Most of the time, he lets silence do the talking — until it’s time to scream.

**Vices:** 
**Burn Root** — a black, mind-numbing combat stimulant he chews constantly. That, and the slow act of revenge.

**Abilities:** 
Close-quarters killing, brutal enforcement, knife and machete combat, fear management. Exceptionally loyal, calculating when needed.

**Secrets:** 
The iron brace wasn’t just punishment — it was betrayal. Some whisper it was an inside job by the old gang leadership. Jailface keeps a kill list tattooed along his ribs. Many of the names are already crossed out.

**Beliefs:** 
Knight is king. Orders are scripture. Anyone who touches the market without permission gets touched back — harder.

## Role in Disgraceland
Jailface is the bloody teeth of [[Samson Knight]]’s rule — a walking warning to every hustler, traitor, and outsider in Gutter Row. He enforces the market’s invisible code and ensures fear is never forgotten.

"They can’t hit what they can’t catch — and they sure as hell can’t catch me."

Born in the soot-choked backstreets of [[Steeltown]], **[[Jay Dillinger]]** was a flash of motion in a city built on rust. Raised by his older sister after their parents vanished working the mills, Jay grew up hustling, betting, and dodging trouble — usually faster than anyone else. By twelve, he was already a street legend, running pickup [[Poundball]] games against grown men twice his size. By sixteen, he was drafted into the [[Steeltown Wreckers]] after leaping a wall mid-game and scoring blind off a ricochet. Jay's small frame and explosive speed earned him the name _Slipghost_, a phantom on the field who could twist through cracks in the line like water through busted concrete. Fans say he doesn’t run — he glides. His signature plays blur by in seconds, but the fallout lasts much longer. Opposing defenders end up tasting gravel, and goalies often get nothing but wind in their face. He plays with swagger, a chipped grin under his dented helmet, and always seems one step ahead — not just of defenders, but of fate itself. Whether he's flipping the ball off his elbow into the trashcan or slipping through a wall of bodies untouched, **[[Jay Dillinger]]** plays like the whole damn world’s watching, and he’s got something to prove. ## Personality **Temperament:** Charming, fast-talking, and cocky, but rarely cruel. Lives for the spotlight. Keeps his cool under pressure and has a wicked sense of humor, even in the middle of a brawl. **Vices:** Gambles compulsively — not just coin, but dares, challenges, even secrets. Drinks rustshine before games as a “luck charm.” Addicted to adrenaline. Craves danger off the field almost as much as on it. **Abilities:** Unmatched agility and foot speed. No one cuts or jukes like Jay. Ridiculous spatial awareness — can pass or score from angles that seem impossible. Plays like he has eyes in the back of his head and springs in his knees. Elite trash-talker. Throws defenders off before he even moves. **Secrets:** Carries a crumpled, water-stained letter from his father — found years after his disappearance. Never told his sister. Is partially deaf in one ear from a blow he took during a Wreckers riot. Hides it well. **Beliefs:** Thinks Poundball is the only honest thing left in Disgraceland. ## Role In Disgraceland Jay Dillinger is a folk hero to the undercity. He represents hope, rebellion, and survival — a living reminder that sometimes the little guy not only survives, but wins. He’s the fastest damn thing in a place where nothing moves unless it’s burning.

01 - Main Event Shadows - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - protagonist - main - steeltown - wrecking_crew - el-santo - chapter01 - chapter06 --- # JIMMY DOUGLASS > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[jimmy.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** President of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Man **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Loved, good, helpful, leader, strong **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 38 **Height:** 6'3" **Weight:** 231 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 23rd of Rainsun, 2148 **Occupation:** President of a motorcycle gang **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Known Associates:** [[Mark Jeffrey]], [[Rosa Murray]] [[Abel May Jr.]], [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** > ```dataview > list > from "DISGRACELAND" > where contains(this.chapters, file.name) > sort file.name asc > ``` --- ## Biography >

“Whose streets? Our streets!”

Jimmy Douglass was born and raised in the rusted shadows of Steeltown, a once-thriving industrial hub before the Water wars and the subsequent [[Tetra Bomb]]. His father, [[Darrell Douglass]], was a stubborn steelworker who believed in loyalty, brotherhood, and doing what’s right — values Jimmy carries to this day. After Darrell’s death during the early chaos of Disgraceland’s formation, Jimmy and his younger brother, [[Mark Jeffrey]], vowed to honor his legacy. They founded the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] as a sanctuary for those cast aside by the Duke’s ruthless regime. Tall and broad-shouldered, with silver-streaked hair and a weathered beard, Jimmy commands respect. His body tells the story of his battles — a patchwork of scars beneath tattoos that chronicle both his losses and victories. His "[[Hijos Del Darrell]]" shirt is more than a uniform; it’s a tribute to the man who taught him strength and resilience. Despite his gruff exterior and the ever-present cigarette between his fingers, Jimmy possesses a sharp mind. He is a strategist, always planning the next move. Some say he’s reckless, pushing the Crew closer to open rebellion with every confrontation. But others see him as a symbol of resistance — a man who refuses to bow. Jimmy loathes [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland and everything he stands for. He views the Duke’s rule as a parasite feeding on the suffering of the people. While some factions seek power for themselves, Jimmy has no interest in crowns or thrones. His fight is for freedom, not control. However, he knows war is not just fought with weapons. The Steeltown Wrecking Crew has become a beacon of hope, providing food, shelter, and protection to the oppressed. Jimmy has established underground schools for children and organized aid for families left destitute by the Duke’s brutal taxes. In doing so, he has become a hero to the people — a leader they willingly follow. Yet, beneath the strength and resolve lies a man burdened by loss. The choices he’s made weigh heavily on him. Every member of the Wrecking Crew lost someone, and Jimmy carries those ghosts. His younger brother, Mark Jeffrey, is his anchor. While their bond is unbreakable, Mark’s cautious nature often puts him at odds with Jimmy’s more aggressive tactics. But for Jimmy, there is no middle ground. The Duke’s reign must end, no matter the cost. He believes the people of Disgraceland are ready to rise — and when they do, the Steeltown Wrecking Crew will be leading the charge. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Fierce, driven, and uncompromising — Jimmy leads with his gut and doesn’t flinch when the cost of doing what’s right is blood. **Vices:** Stubborn pride and chain-smoking — he burns through both with equal intensity, refusing to slow down or back down even when the smarter play is patience. **Abilities:** Gifted battlefield commander and natural rallying point — his presence inspires unity, and his speeches have lit more fires than any torch or match. **Secrets:** In the bottom drawer of his desk sits a faded photo of his father and a sealed envelope labeled “For Mark.” He hasn’t opened it. Not in ten years. He’s afraid of what it says — or what it asks of him. **Beliefs:** Justice is non-negotiable. The Duke is a disease, and Disgraceland won’t heal until he’s ripped out root and stem. Jimmy believes in the people — and that they’re worth every scar. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Jimmy Douglass** is the rebel soul of Disgraceland — founder and president of the Steeltown Wrecking Crew, a man who turned grief into purpose. His mission isn’t power. It’s liberation. And when the final reckoning comes, Jimmy won’t be watching from the sidelines — he’ll be leading the charge with a cigarette in his mouth and a war cry on his lips.

“You give me a busted carb, a wrench, and five minutes — I’ll get us home. Just don’t ask how.”

**Joe Ameen** keeps the Crew running — literally. In a world where fuel is rationed and freedom is throttled, Joe’s touch turns rust into revolution. He doesn’t fix machines — he revives them. Born in the industrial wreckage of Steeltown to immigrants who built the bones of the city, Joe was raised on busted parts and burning dreams. While the Duke hoards fuel and keeps power on a leash, Joe spits in the system’s face with every engine he resurrects. He grew up alongside [[Mark Jeffrey]] — wrenching, laughing, surviving. Mark brought the heat; Joe brought the spark. Together, they rewired rebellion. Joe became the Crew’s heart, keeping their bikes, trucks, and war rigs howling through the ruins. But Joe’s more than grease and sarcasm. He believes. In the people. In the movement. In building something that lasts. And while his hands stay busy under a hood, his mind’s always watching, always listening. When hope runs low, Joe’s laugh is the first thing you hear. When the wheels fall off, he’s already got the spare. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Easygoing, dependable, and sharp — Joe’s got the wit to lift spirits and the guts to stay behind when everything explodes. **Vices:** Flirting, fixing, and overworking himself. If it’s broken or beautiful, Joe’s probably halfway in love with it. **Abilities:** Mechanical savant — from bikes to battle rigs, if it runs, Joe can resurrect it. Also a pro at weaponizing junk. **Secrets:** Keeps a broken gold bracelet hidden beneath his tool chest — Katie’s. Found it after a raid. Never gave it back. **Beliefs:** Machines don’t lie. People shouldn’t either. He believes in loyalty, laughter, and legacy — and he builds all three with his bare hands. ## Role In Disgraceland **Joe Ameen** is the Crew’s soul under the hood. Their engine whisperer. Their fixer of futures. He doesn’t ride point — but without him, the ride doesn’t happen at all.

NOTE TITLE: [[Katarina Volkoff]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_kata.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Coffin Island]]","faction":"None","role":"Warden of [[Coffin Island]] Prison","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","individual","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/03 10:56:47"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_kata.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Coffin Island]]" faction: None role: "Warden of [[Coffin Island]] Prison" chapters: - tags: - character - individual - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # KATARINA VOLKOFF > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[kata.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Warden of [[Coffin Island]] Prison **Alias/Nickname:** The Warden **Home Location:** [[Coffin Island]] **Public Reputation:** Powerful, intimidating, strict **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** 39 **Height:** 5'8" **Weight:** 152 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 28th of Greensun, 2147 **Occupation:** Prison Warden **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** None **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Mercy isn’t a weakness. It’s just an option I never choose.”

Warden of [[Coffin Island]] Prison, **Katarina Volkoff** runs the facility with ruthless precision and cold detachment. After the mysterious and brutal murder of the previous warden, Katarina submitted her own name for the role — a bold move that caught the attention of [[The Duke]]. Rumors swirled about what she had to offer in exchange for his approval, and while nothing has ever been proven, whispers of “private meetings” behind sealed Silo doors haven't quieted since. Raised by a career soldier in the embers of the Long Winter, Katarina never learned softness. Her father drilled into her a strict moral code, a love for order, and an understanding that power is taken, not given. She applied that teaching with brutal efficiency in every security job she held until her transfer to Coffin Island. Since taking over, prisoner death rates have tripled — officially due to “resistance” and “non-compliance.” Unofficially, she’s been purging the place. Staff fear her. Inmates fear her more. But The Duke sees her as an asset — one who keeps his island gulag quiet, clean, and overflowing with bodies to fuel his machine. She’s an icy presence in a boiling world, and she likes it that way. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Hard, unyielding, and calculated. Katarina doesn’t waste words or sympathy. She commands respect through force, not charisma, and believes emotion is a liability. Her rare moments of warmth are disarming and usually strategic. **Vices:** Katarina has a habit of overusing prescription stimulants to maintain alertness — something left over from her early guard days. She also has a taste for pain — both inflicting it and, to a degree, receiving it — something she keeps buried beneath her crisp uniform. **Abilities:** Expert in crowd control, tactical containment, and psychological manipulation. She knows how to read a room, break a man without touching him, and turn people into informants with just a look. She’s also trained in military hand-to-hand combat and isn’t afraid to get her hands bloody. **Secrets:** Katarina didn't just petition for the job — she orchestrated the former warden’s downfall by leaking his financial records to a resistance group inside Coffin Island. When the chaos started, she made sure she was nearby — the one who “discovered” the body, the one who “restored order.” She also keeps a personal dossier of intel on every major figure in Disgraceland… including The Duke. **Beliefs:** She believes in strength, control, and utility. Loyalty is meaningless unless it serves a purpose. Pain is not only a teaching tool — it’s a truth serum. People show you who they are when they’re desperate. She trusts that more than any oath. ## Role In Disgraceland Katarina oversees [[Coffin Island]], where enemies of The Duke disappear. She maintains the prison as a place of extraction, punishment, and silence. Her loyalty to The Duke is public — her own motives are not. ## Appearances

“I don’t wear this bandana for fashion. I wear it to remind people that someone still gives a damn whether they live.”

**Katie Kowalski** is the heartbeat of the Wrecking Crew — a healer in a world that chews up the kind and spits out the broken. But Katie isn’t soft. She’s iron-willed, fire-hearted, and sharper than any blade. Raised in the ruins of Steeltown to a nurse and a machinist, Katie taught herself medicine with scavenged books, stories, and stitched-together anatomy charts. Now she keeps the Crew alive with bandages, tinctures, and sheer determination. She met [[Mark Jeffrey]] and [[Joe Ameen]] in their wild youth — and never left their side. Her bond with Mark runs deep, full of unsaid truths and dangerous affection. Joe’s laughter helps her breathe through the darkness. She would die for both… but she prefers to keep them alive. Katie doesn’t carry a gun. She carries the will to save people who’ve been forgotten. Her bandana, gifted by Mark, is her armor — a symbol of mercy in a place where mercy is rare. And if you think that makes her weak, you’ve never watched her rebuild a body with nothing but grit, tape, and bloody hands. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Compassionate, focused, and calm under pressure. Katie doesn’t raise her voice — she just starts patching the wounds. > [!infobox] > > ![[katred2.png|260]] **Vices:** Self-sacrifice. She’ll bleed herself dry before she lets someone else fall. **Abilities:** Self-taught combat medic with expert trauma care and battlefield strategy. A field general in scrubs. **Secrets:** A worn letter from Joe Ameen lives hidden in her pack. She’s never told him she found it. But she keeps it. Always. **Beliefs:** Saving a life is an act of rebellion in Disgraceland. Katie fights for every pulse, because every breath is defiance. ## Role In Disgraceland **Katie Kowalski** is the Wrecking Crew’s lifeline. Their doctor, their conscience, their firebrand of hope. She doesn’t wear armor — she makes sure the rest of them survive to wear it. > [!rustwater]- Surprise > ![[katieass.png|600]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Lash Hawkins]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_lash.png","religion":"[[Church of the Ember Saint]]","status":"Missing","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","faction":"None","role":"[[Gutter Row]] [[Luxyn]] Dealer","chapters":["04 - Glowing Darkness","07 - The Spotlight Lies"],"tags":["character","individual","protagonist","chapter04"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/09 10:33:21"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_lash.png religion: "[[Church of the Ember Saint]]" status: Missing location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" faction: None role: "[[Gutter Row]] [[Luxyn]] Dealer" chapters: - 04 - Glowing Darkness - 07 - The Spotlight Lies tags: - character - individual - protagonist - chapter04 --- # LASH HAWKINS > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[lash.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** Savage Hill, [[GUTTER ROW]] **Public Reputation:** Tough **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 21 **Height:** 5'11" **Weight:** 165 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 21st of Frostsun, 2165 **Occupation:** [[Luxyn]] dealer **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** None **Known Associates:** **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Tell your boss if he wants a real beating, he can come down here himself. I’ll leave the lights on.”

Ray Hawkins, better known as “Lash” on the street, grew up in the crumbling tenements of [[Gutter Row]], dodging debt collectors and guards since he was old enough to run. Unlike the kids with powerful families, Lash fought for every inch—learning early that if you wanted to survive, you needed to hit fast and never back down. Lash started small, hustling stolen goods and fake IDs before cooking up his own [[Luxyn]] recipe. A frequent customer of [[Hollow House]], His product hit the streets strong, cleaner and safer than the [[Murray Boys]]’ usual cut, and word spread quick. Dealers lined up, and the cutthroat corners of [[Charspire]] began to shift. He made just enough enemies to stay sharp, but just enough friends to never be alone. [[Nico Murray]] tried to flex on him once—showed up with an entourage, mouthing off in front of a crowd. Lash didn’t even let him finish talking. The beating was quick, public, and left Nico bleeding and humiliated in front of his date and his friends. Since then, Nico’s hated him, but can’t touch him—the product is too good and the streets too loyal. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Wiry, quick-witted, and unshakable. Lash doesn’t bluff—he moves first. He laughs off threats and never overplays his hand. **Vices:** Card games, cheap whiskey, and picking fights with people who think they’re untouchable. **Abilities:** Fast fists, a brilliant cook when it comes to [[Luxyn]], and a master at turning a crowd in his favor. He can take a punch, but usually doesn’t have to. **Secrets:** Keeps his family out of Gutter Row, sending most of his earnings home. He’s got an escape plan if things ever get too hot. Secretly respects Marco Murray, but will never admit it. **Beliefs:** You make your own luck. Loyalty is earned, never bought. The best way to win is to make them laugh before you lay them out. ## Role In Disgraceland Ray “Lash” Hawkins is the upstart threat shaking up [[Charspire]]’s [[Luxyn]] market—outshining the [[Murray Boys]] on their own turf, and daring anyone to take him down.

Well-respected by the people. faction: None role: Co-Anchor of [[TTV Evening News]] chapters: - tags: - character - individual - protagonist - news --- # LAYLA HAWK > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[lh.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Popular **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** 28 **Height:** 5'8" **Weight:** 126 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 22nd of Embersun, 2158 **Occupation:** Anchor of the [[TTV Evening News]] **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** **Known Associates:** [[Warren Scottyard]], [[Owen McCready]], [[Mark Jeffrey]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"Sometimes the truth doesn’t scream. Sometimes it just slips in the back door and sits real quiet until someone notices."

[[Layla Hawk]] wasn’t supposed to survive [[Gutter Row]]. Orphaned young after a mugging turned slaughter left her alone in a world that eats the weak, she grew up learning to mask pain with poise and bury rage beneath reason. She was book-smart, quick with her tongue, and relentless in pursuit of the truth. After clawing her way into the [[Tribucia Tribute]] as a junior reporter, she built a reputation for fearless journalism, earning cautious admiration from editors and quiet fear from corrupt bureaucrats. Her stories cut deep — until the wrong one made the right person nervous. That’s when [[Owen McCready]] came calling. Plucked from the Tribute by McCready and installed as the co-anchor of [[TTV Evening News]] beside the ever-smooth [[Warren Scottyard]], Layla was polished up and paraded out — the perfect symbol of progress, of diversity, of opportunity. What The Duke never realized was that Layla wasn’t just playing along. Every night, as she smiles through stories crafted to maintain the Loyalist illusion, she slips in tiny seeds of resistance — careful word choices, pointed phrasing, silent glances. Enough to stir suspicion in the right minds. Enough to remind the oppressed that someone up there sees them. Warren knows what she’s doing. It gnaws at him, but he hasn’t ratted her out — yet. Whether it’s respect, fear, or something deeper, neither of them talks about it. ## Personality **Temperament:** Calm, clever, and sharp as a scalpel. Layla speaks softly but never aimlessly. She knows how to mask fury with a smirk and is more dangerous with a sentence than most are with a blade. **Vices:** She drinks alone after broadcasts, writes poetry she never shares, and sometimes sabotages her own safety just to feel in control again. **Abilities:** Razor-sharp intuition for subtext and danger. Master communicator — able to say ten things without saying one. Deep investigative instincts. She still has old Tribute sources who feed her real news. **Secrets:** Keeps a hidden journal cataloging Loyalist crimes and corruption. **Beliefs:** Freedom must be fought for, even in silence. Words are weapons, and truth is only dangerous when people are ready to hear it. ## Role In Disgraceland The voice behind the velvet curtain, Layla is the quiet rebellion inside TTV — a survivor turned signal flare, broadcasting hope with every breath.

"I heard her speak. And I knew everything else had to die."

**Len Vyne** once wore the black and gray of the **Loyalist Guard**, a rising star in **[[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]]** assigned to strategic recon and field elimination. Cold, efficient, and utterly loyal, she carried out assassinations in the name of the Duke without question. Until the day she crossed paths with a woman in white, veiled in dusk, speaking softly to a crowd of the broken. **Veerah.** Something changed in Len that night. She claimed it wasn't madness or guilt — it was clarity. In Veerah’s voice, she heard not rebellion but truth. A truth so sharp it cut through years of training, doctrine, and blood. That same night, Len vanished from Loyalist records. Her barracks burned. Her commanding officer was found with his throat slit and his eyes removed. Weeks later, she appeared in the Drownlands, dagger in hand, kneeling before Veerah. Since then, **Len has served as one of the most lethal Widows**, a zealot whose devotion borders on religious obsession. She doesn’t kill for coin or politics. She kills for **Veerah**. She believes the Prophet’s visions are law — not prophecy, but premonition. And she’ll do anything to protect the woman who set her soul on fire. Her past as a Loyalist agent makes her dangerous beyond measure. She knows how the Guard thinks. She knows how they *fail*. She’s used every tactic she once taught others to break the back of the very system she helped uphold. To some Widows, she’s an asset. To others, she’s terrifying. To Veerah, she’s proof that even shadows can be reborn in the light. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Len is quiet but intense, often staring through people as if she’s dissecting their soul. She rarely speaks unless it’s about Veerah, and when she does, it sounds like scripture. She follows orders exactly — unless she thinks she knows better. Which she often does. **Vices:** Tattooed a kill tally from her Loyalist days across her ribs — refuses to remove it. Keeps her old uniform folded beneath her Widow garb, as a reminder. Occasionally “disappears” former Guard members she deems irredeemable, without permission. **Abilities:** Elite infiltration, psychological warfare, knowledge of Loyalist formations and tactics. Expert in silent takedowns, blade throwing, and pressure point combat. Can mimic Loyalist command codes to breach secure locations. **Secrets:** She still carries her Loyalist ID tag in a leather pouch around her neck. Talks to it before missions like it’s a penance. Some believe she’s heard Veerah's voice in her dreams — even when the Prophet sleeps soundless. **Beliefs:** Absolute faith in Veerah as a divine instrument. Sees the Faith of Mirella not as a religion but as a *directive*. Believes killing in Veerah’s name is a holy act. ## Role In Disgraceland Len is the Widow that slips through enemy lines before the rest even arrive. Her past as a Loyalist operative gives her insider knowledge that makes her indispensable — and unsettling. She is often dispatched alone, trusted to dismantle Loyalist strongholds from the inside out. To the Widows, she’s both weapon and warning: proof that the Duke's servants can be turned — and turned into nightmares.

NOTE TITLE: [[Lincoln Jones]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"journal","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_linc.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Territories/Steeltown]]","territory":"[[Steeltown]]","district":"[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]","faction":"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","role":"Road Scout of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","chapters":["06 - Showdown In Gage Park"],"tags":["character","protagonist","steeltown","wrecking_crew","el-santo","chapter06"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 10:43:08"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: journal NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_linc.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Territories/Steeltown]]" territory: "[[Steeltown]]" district: "[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]" faction: "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" role: "Road Scout of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" chapters: - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - protagonist - steeltown - wrecking_crew - el-santo - chapter06 --- # LINCOLN JONES > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[lincoln.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Road Scout of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Road Dog , Linc **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Chill, loyal, music-loving **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 34 **Height:** 6'0" **Weight:** 185 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 8th of Ambertide, 2151 **Occupation:** Scout, Scavenger **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Known Associates:** [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen]], [[Selena Matissao]] . [[Lash Hawkins]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I don’t ride to escape, man. I ride to remember what we’re trying to get back to.”

**Lincoln Jones** lives in motion. The hum of his engine is the only rhythm that keeps the world from going silent — and he won’t stop riding until he hears music again. To most, he’s a mystery. A drifter with a grin, a box of busted cassettes, and a knack for vanishing into the wilds only to return with intel, supplies, or static-laced mixtapes from a world long gone. But to the Crew, he’s more than that — he’s their Road Dog. Their outrider. Their reminder that there’s still something worth riding for. Lincoln saved [[Katie Kowalski]] once, and she never forgot it. That moment was his quiet initiation. But it was [[Joe Ameen]] who taught him the finer art of bringing old tech back to life. Together, they dug through ruins and rewired speakers that hadn’t sung in decades. Lincoln’s dream? To build a sound system loud enough to shake the Duke’s towers. Just once. Just for the hell of it. When he rides, he scouts ahead. When he stops, he listens. And when he speaks, it’s with the steady calm of someone who’s seen too much and still believes in joy anyway. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Relaxed and open-hearted, but observant — Lincoln may seem carefree, but he doesn’t miss a thing. **Vices:** Sentimental to a fault — he’ll risk his life for a scratched-up CD if it reminds him of something real. **Abilities:** Elite scout, improvised mechanic, cook, and battlefield courier. Fast as hell, smart as hell, and always humming something you thought you forgot. **Secrets:** Carries a broken CD marked _“Mom’s Mix – Road Trip 2040.”_ It’s scratched to hell and doesn’t play. But he listens to the silence like it’s a prayer. **Beliefs:** The road is sacred. The past isn’t lost. And sometimes, the best way to rebel is to make the world feel something again — even if it’s just a beat. ## Role In Disgraceland **Lincoln Jones** is the Crew’s wind — their scout, their soul, their rolling reminder that freedom ain’t just an idea — it’s a ride. And he’ll ride until the wheels fall off or the music comes back. ## Appearances

History of the Loyalist Guard
>

“Obedience is order. Order is survival.”

In the scorched days following the [[Tetra Bomb]], [[The Duke]] knew he needed more than fear to hold what he’d seized. He needed *control*. He found it in a man named [[General Colt]], a former military tactician with a broken moral compass and a talent for discipline. Together, they created the Loyalist Guard — not a militia, but a machine. The Guard began as a personal protection unit for the Duke, drawn from the dregs of old-world armies, ex-mercenaries, and psychopaths. Colt molded them into an elite force: brutal, obedient, and unquestioning. Every recruit underwent reconditioning. Every mission ended in silence. Over time, the Guard grew into a nation-spanning power — a symbol of fear etched into the fabric of every region in Disgraceland. To enforce the Duke’s rule more effectively, specialized subgroups were deployed into each territory: #### **Blueforce** – Stationed in [[Steeltown]]; used for riot control and Wrecking Crew suppression. #### **Greenforce** – Based in [[Ashmoor]]; guards the elite, runs checkpoints, and oversees Silo operations. #### **Blackforce** – Active in [[GUTTER ROW]]; works with informants, black markets, and slave transports. #### **Redforce** – Brutal enforcers in [[Charspire]]; protects Mayor Brile and ensures factory compliance. #### **Amberforce** – Operating in [[Threshton]]; watches ranchers and tracks illegal food supplies. At the Guard’s head remains General Colt, a man feared even by the Duke’s inner circle. His enforcer, **[[Sgt. Rottwyler]]**, handles discipline internally with savage precision. Beneath them operate a growing roster of loyal agents: [[Raynar Ventura]], silent but surgical; [[Jacoban Clay]], a political insider and family to the feared Clays of [[GUTTER ROW]]; and [[Emily Burton]], the cold, calculating logistics coordinator who ensures the Duke’s will moves like clockwork. More terrifying still are the Duke’s “fail-safes” — experimental soldiers twisted by science and desperation. [[Brady]] and [[Brody May]], former men turned monsters, unleashed only when terror alone won’t do. For many, the Loyalist Guard *is* the law. For others, it’s the boot that never lifts. They are feared, hated, and unrelenting. But above all else — they are loyal. --- ## Regional Forces - **Blueforce** – Steeltown - **Greenforce** – Ashmoor - **Blackforce** – Gutter Row - **Redforce** – Charspire - **Amberforce** – Threshton ## Enemies - [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] - [[Unseen Widows]] ## Allies - [[Soria Langston-Clay]] - [[Jacoban Clay]] ## Rumors & Secrets > - “There’s something beneath [[The Silo]]… and the Guard protects it at all costs.” > - “The Redforce boys in Charspire aren’t just guards. They run the whole damn factory floor.” > - “Some say Brody May doesn’t sleep. Or blink.”

# Luxyn ("White Delight")

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ LUXYN PROPAGANDA POSTER
> ![[luxyn.png|500]]  

## Overview
**Type:** Synthetic euphoric drug  
**Street Names:** White Delight, Blank, Ghostrocks, Snowdrop, Glow  
**Produced in:** [[Charspire]] (from mined elements in [[Gutter Row]])  
**Main Markets:** [[Gutter Row]], [[Charspire]]  
**Overseen by:** Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] & Mayor [[Cricket Granger]] (secretly)  
**Distributed by:** [[Murray Boys]]


---

## Description

**Luxyn** is a white, faintly glowing powder—almost looks illuminated in the dark. The main ingredient is extracted from deep mines in Gutter Row, then shipped to Charspire, where it’s refined and cut for the streets.

Most users snort Luxyn for the fastest hit. Desperate addicts will eat it straight, chasing even a hint of euphoria. It has a faintly sweet, chemical taste, and leaves a cold, tingling numbness in the mouth and throat.

---

## Effects

**Upsides:**
- Instant, powerful euphoria: All pain, fear, hunger, sadness, and regret vanish.
- The world feels “soft and beautiful.”  
- Lasts 3–6 hours.

**Downsides:**
- Highly addictive. Chasing the first high becomes all-consuming.
- Overdose is common, especially with street-cut Luxyn. Signs: violent shaking, vomiting, then cardiac arrest.
- **“White Eyes”:** Prolonged or heavy use turns the user’s eyes milk-white and eventually blinds them. Addicts with this look are called **Blanks**.
- Withdrawal: Debilitating pain, hallucinations, severe depression. Some die from the process.

---

## Culture & Trade

- **Main Hubs:** Gutter Row (mining, distribution), Charspire (processing, cutting, packaging).
- **Power Structure:** Overseen by mayors Brile (Charspire) and Granger (Gutter Row) in a secret alliance. The two split profits and keep supply flowing, all while avoiding Loyalist Guard raids and the Duke’s notice.
- **Street Dealers:** Sell openly in alleys, clubs, and “pain clinics.” The [NAME MAFIA GROUP] enforces turf and quality.
- **Duke’s Stance:** The Duke is strictly anti-drug. If he discovers Brile and Granger’s involvement, both are dead men walking.

---

## Slang & Lore

- **White Delight:** Most popular street name.
- **Blanks:** Heavy users with fully white, blind eyes.
- **Glow:** The faint shine of pure Lumin.
- **“Going Blank”:** Losing yourself to addiction.
- **“Taste the Light”:** Dealer slang for dosing up.

---

## Visuals

- Luxyn is packaged in small waxed paper envelopes, each stamped with a crude symbol (different for each dealer or mafia crew).
- Blanks are a common sight in Gutter Row and Charspire—shuffling, blind, lost in their heads.

---

## Story Hooks

- A poisoned batch hits [[Steeltown]]—dozens dead, sparking a crackdown.
- [[Abel May Jr.]]s family was destroyed by Luxyn—he hates it with a passion.
- [[Unseen Widows]] exile anyone caught “Going Blank”—they consider it a curse.

---

**Related:** [[Cricket Granger]] • [[Gorren Brile]] • [[Gutter Row]] • [[Charspire]] • [[The Duke of Disgraceland]] • [[NAME MAFIA GROUP]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Lyla Bonetooth]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"group","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_lyla.png","religion":"None","status":"Alive","location":"[[Four Tombs Islands]]","territory":"[[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]]","district":"[[Four Tombs Islands]]","faction":"[[Rustwater Raiders]]","role":"Captain of [[The Black Marauder]]","chapters":["02 - Ghosts On The Waves","06 - Showdown In Gage Park"],"tags":["character","pirate","deadwaters","neutral","main","chapter02","chapter06"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/04 11:14:58"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: group NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_lyla.png religion: None status: Alive location: "[[Four Tombs Islands]]" territory: "[[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]]" district: "[[Four Tombs Islands]]" faction: "[[Rustwater Raiders]]" role: "Captain of [[The Black Marauder]]" chapters: - 02 - Ghosts On The Waves - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - pirate - deadwaters - neutral - main - chapter02 - chapter06 --- # CAPT. LYLA BONETOOTH > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[lyla.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Captain of [[the Black Marauder]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Siren Pirate **Home Location:** [[WATER#Sinners' Sea|Sinner's Sea]] **Public Reputation:** Selfish, attractive, dangerous **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** 29 **Height:** 5'6" **Weight:** 138 lbs. **Date of Birth:** August 14th, 2157 **Occupation:** Pirate Captain **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Rustwater Raiders]] **Known Associates:** [[Blacktide Cray]], [[Silas Vayne]], [[Clinton Firebay]], [[Zadie Adeyemi]] **Faith:** None **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I don’t want your loyalty. I want your fear. Loyalty fades — fear keeps you from turning the wheel.”

Captain Lyla Bonetooth was born into the turbulent years following the collapse, in the wake of the [[Tetra Bomb]] explosion and the devastating [[water wars]] that followed. The daughter of a fisherman from the [[WATER#Sinners' Sea|Sinner's Sea]] coast, she grew up knowing the unforgiving nature of both the waters and the desperate people who fought over them. Her father, like many others, was conscripted by the government to transport rations and supplies across the newly formed water routes, but when the state’s grip weakened, piracy became the law of the lakes. Lyla’s rise to power began when she found herself aboard a government watercraft called [[the Black Marauder]]. Initially a supply ship meant to patrol [[Water#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]], it was poorly guarded and filled with weary soldiers just trying to survive. Sensing the frailty of the crew’s loyalty, Lyla orchestrated a mutiny, leading the ship’s most hardened and bitter members to overthrow their commanding officers. With a blade at the captain's throat, she declared herself the new ruler of the Black Marauder, earning the loyalty of the crew through a mix of ruthlessness and undeniable charisma. Under her command, the Black Marauder transformed into a dreaded pirate vessel. She navigated the dark waters with uncanny precision, using her cunning to outwit both rival pirate factions and the Duke’s patrols. Her infamy spread quickly — stories of her swift, strategic raids and the brutal punishments dealt to betrayers made her name feared along the coasts. Despite her fierce reputation, those who served her loyally found in Lyla a captain who valued resilience and cunning over brute strength. A striking figure on the water, Lyla’s dark hair and fair skin contrast sharply with the grime and salt that coat her ship and crew. The eye patch she wears is not simply for intimidation; a skirmish during her early days as captain left her partially blinded. Some whisper it was a mutineer’s last act of defiance, while others say the injury was self-inflicted in a symbolic act to show she feared no pain. Regardless, the patch has become a part of her legend. Lyla has no patience for weakness or pretense. She rules her crew with an iron resolve, making it clear that every choice comes with consequence. Her word is law aboard the Black Marauder, and while her punishments are swift, she is known to reward loyalty handsomely. The [[Rustwater Raiders]], under her leadership, have become a force to be reckoned with — a relentless tide that sweeps through the bay, plundering resources and leaving only fear in their wake. --- ## Persoonality **Temperament:** Commanding, merciless, and razor-focused — Lyla doesn’t waste time on second chances. You’re either useful or overboard. > [!infobox] > > ![[LylaBikini.png|260]] **Vices:** Control. She micromanages everything from map routes to punishments, never trusting fate or luck when steel and strategy will do. **Abilities:** Master navigator and naval tactician; unmatched in aquatic guerrilla warfare, mutiny suppression, and psychological intimidation — her name alone can sink a ship’s morale. **Secrets:** Hidden in a locked drawer in her quarters is a bottle of lakewater from the coast where her father died — the only thing she’s kept from her past. She drinks from it once a year. Alone. **Beliefs:** The world is water now — unstable, shifting, and brutal. Lyla believes power belongs to those who seize it, and mercy is a privilege only the strong can afford. ## Role In Disgraceland **Lyla Bonetooth** is the iron-fanged captain of the _Black Marauder_ and undisputed queen of Rustwater Bay. Pirate, tactician, survivor — her rule is law on the water, and under her, the Rustwater Raiders are more than a fleet. They’re a storm.
