## Biography

> “He talks, I cut. That’s balance.”

**Malika Locke** walks through [[Gutter Row]] like she owns every shadow. Known as the ride-or-die of [[Ninepack]], she’s more than his girl — she’s his backup plan, his bodyguard, his bruiser, and sometimes, his conscience. Born and raised in the broken back alleys of Vileby, Malika earned her name the hard way — beating older boys in dice games and outrunning Loyalist patrols by the time she was ten.

She first met Ninepack during a chaotic street deal that went sideways. While others ran, she stepped in and bailed him out with a knife to someone’s throat and a smirk on her face. He talked slick. She didn’t care. But over time, their bond solidified — not just built on love, but on blood, danger, and a shared need to stay one move ahead of the streets.

Malika doesn’t say much in public, but her presence speaks volumes. She’s known for carrying two blades, moving like smoke through the Three Nail Market, and finishing fights her man never had to start. The only person she listens to is Ninepack, and even that depends on the mood.

She’s a legend in the making, feared by rivals and whispered about by Market kids who dream of being half as bad.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Calm until it’s time to strike. Observant, fast-thinking, loyal to a razor edge.

**Vices:** 
Dice games, fire whiskey, and putting men in their place. Keeps her late mother’s ring on a chain around her neck.

**Abilities:** 
Close-quarters combat, sleight of hand, stealth, tracking. Sharp instincts — she spots trouble before it speaks.

**Secrets:** 
Her real last name is **Vorneaux**, tying her to a disgraced Loyalist bloodline. She’s buried the past deep, but it has claws.

**Beliefs:** 
Trust no one except Ninepack. Loyalty is everything. And survival without love ain’t worth the scars.

## Role in Disgraceland
Malika Locke is the quiet fire beside Ninepack’s silver tongue — a lethal protector who watches his back and burns anyone who comes too close.

## Appearances

NOTE TITLE: [[Marco Murray]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_marco.png","religion":"[[Church of the Ember Saint]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","territory":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","district":"[[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]","faction":"[[Murray Boys]]","role":"Don of the [[Murray Boys]]","chapters":["04 - Glowing Darkness"],"tags":["character","antagonist","murray","chapter04"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:06","modified":"2025/06/05 17:07:55"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_marco.png religion: "[[Church of the Ember Saint]]" status: Alive location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" territory: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" district: "[[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]" faction: "[[Murray Boys]]" role: "Don of the [[Murray Boys]]" chapters: - 04 - Glowing Darkness tags: - character - antagonist - murray - chapter04 --- # MARCO MURRAY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[marco.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Don of the [[Murray Boys]] Crime Family **Alias/Nickname:** The Don Mega **Home Location:** Vileby, [[Gutter Row]] **Public Reputation:** Feared **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** [[Rosa Murray]] **Age:** 52 **Height:** 6'0" **Weight:** 264 lbs. **Date of Birth:** August 11th, 2134 **Occupation:** Head of the Murray Boys, Drug runner **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Murray Boys]] **Known Associates:** Francis Murray, [[Gorren Brile]], [[Cricket Granger]] **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“People talk about luck, but luck’s just a knife in your back waiting for you to turn around. I make my own chances.”

Marco Murray grew up fast and hard in the alleys of [[Gutter Row]]. Orphaned before he hit his teens, Marco did whatever it took to keep his younger brother alive—odd jobs, hustling, petty theft, never trusting the system that chewed up his parents and spat out their bones. [[Gutter Row]]’s filth and violence became his school. Marco learned to keep his head down, keep his hands quick, and never, ever let the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] get close. As a young man, Marco found his true calling in the city’s shadows. The Luxyn trade started small—just a way to put food on the table, a little light in the dark. But Marco had a knack for reading people, for sniffing out opportunities and weaknesses. In time, what began as survival turned into a business. He brought his brother Francis in when the money got too heavy for one man to carry. The Murray Boys ran their outfit smart: low profile, high profit, never greedy enough to get noticed by the big players—until Mayor [[Cricket Granger]] caught wind. Instead of a death sentence, it turned into the deal of Marco’s life. With Granger as silent partner, Marco could scale up, spreading Luxyn across [[Gutter Row]] and beyond, laundering slugs into legitimate fronts. When Granger joined forces with Brile in [[Charspire]], Marco adapted again, managing supply lines between mines and streets with the kind of precision that made even the Loyalist Guards look clumsy. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Cautious, coldly logical, and slow to trust. Marco is patient and deliberate, rarely showing anger or excitement. He speaks little but always listens—calculating the angles before making any move. He treats loyalty like gold and betrayal like a death sentence. **Vices:** Cigars, expensive liquor, and the illusion of control. Marco doesn’t touch his own product but spends big to look the part. His real addiction is power and the quiet thrill of beating the odds. **Abilities:** Master manipulator, sharp negotiator, and ruthless tactician. He’s an expert at staying invisible—never leaves a trail, never loses his temper. Runs a tight crew and inspires absolute loyalty or total fear. **Secrets:** Marco still hides money and a false identity, just in case he needs to disappear. He keeps a list of everyone who’s ever crossed him. He knows about Granger’s secret dealings with Brile before anyone else did—and quietly keeps leverage on both men. **Beliefs:** He believes family comes first, no matter the cost. The world is a cruel place, and only the smart, careful, and loyal survive. Trust is a weapon, and hope is a weakness. ## Role In Disgraceland Marco Murray is the true face behind [[Gutter Row]]’s drug trade and the [[Murray Boys]]’ growing empire. He operates in the shadows, never flaunting his power but pulling strings that reach from the darkest alleys to the mayors’ offices. No one moves Luxyn in [[Gutter Row]] or [[Charspire]] without his blessing—and everyone knows it.

NOTE TITLE: [[Mark Jeffrey]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"journal","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_mark.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Steeltown]]","territory":"[[Steeltown]]","district":"[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]","faction":"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","role":"Vice-President of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","03 - The Devil In The Row","06 - Showdown In Gage Park"],"tags":["character","protagonist","main","steeltown","wrecking_crew","el-santo","chapter06"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 10:41:33"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: journal NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_mark.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Steeltown]]" territory: "[[Steeltown]]" district: "[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]" faction: "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" role: "Vice-President of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 03 - The Devil In The Row - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - protagonist - main - steeltown - wrecking_crew - el-santo - chapter06 --- # MARK JEFFREY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[mark.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Vice President of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Alias/Nickname:** East Mountain Mauler **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Strategic, charming, grounded , funny **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 30 **Height:** 6'1" **Weight:** 210 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 18th of Hollowtide, 2156 **Occupation:** Vice President of a motorcycle gang **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Known Associates:** [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Katie Kowalski]], [[Joe Ameen]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“You better pray to El Santo.”

If [[Jimmy Douglass]] is the soul of the Wrecking Crew, **Mark Jeffrey** is its brain — the tactician with a cigarette in his teeth and a smirk that means trouble. While Jimmy charges through the fire, Mark calculates the exits. Together, they’re unstoppable. Raised in the industrial grind of Steeltown, Mark grew up watching his brother fight to protect their people. But while Jimmy inherited their father’s brawler spirit, Mark leaned into the long game. He studies people, studies maps, and makes sure the Crew doesn’t rush into a fight it can’t finish. But don’t mistake planning for cowardice — Mark’s fists speak fluent rebellion, and his knuckles know the Duke’s loyalists by name. He’s got a crooked smile, a scar near his collarbone, and a laugh that defuses tension faster than any weapon. His tactical brilliance keeps the Crew on course — but it’s his sense of humor and loyalty that keep them from falling apart. Mark may never seek the spotlight, but without him, the whole movement would collapse under its own fire. He’s the anchor behind Jimmy’s spark — and the one who’ll keep Disgraceland standing once the smoke clears. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Clever, calm, and always in control — Mark’s the Crew’s most stable hand, equally quick with a plan or a joke. **Vices:** Chain-smoker, deep thinker. Covers his fears with sarcasm and secondhand smoke. **Abilities:** Master strategist, intuitive mediator, and gifted with people — he diffuses fights, predicts enemy moves, and plans logistics like a general. **Secrets:** A hidden notebook under his mattress contains his blueprint for rebuilding Disgraceland after the Duke. No one’s seen it. Not even Jimmy. **Beliefs:** Revolutions are only worth fighting if you’ve got something better to build when the dust settles. Mark’s here to win the future, not just the war. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Mark Jeffrey** is the Wrecking Crew’s mind — Vice President, peacemaker, tactician. He keeps Jimmy alive, the Crew together, and the resistance one step ahead.

“What’s mine is mine. And what’s yours... is mine too, if I want it.”

The farmland of [[Threshton]] was supposed to be the breadbasket of United Tribucia—rolling crops, fat cattle, and grain enough to feed a thousand. Instead, it's a graveyard of hunger, and at the top of the food chain sits Mayor [[Marla Rusk]], bloated and smug, gnawing on roasted drumsticks while her people scrape mold off potato skins. Rusk wasn’t elected. Hell, she wasn’t even picked. She offered herself up to [[The Duke]] as a loyal pair of eyes and ears—specifically aimed at the [[Rancher Collective]]. She promised to keep them in line, expose secret trades, and sniff out disloyalty like a truffle pig. In return, she demanded two things: immunity from oversight, and the right to “reclaim” any food she found. And oh, did she find food. Rusk hoards it all—grain, meat, fresh fruit, pickled goods, root cellars stacked to the rafters in the mayor’s estate while the rest of [[Threshton]] suffers under her rule. Her slaves, the largest number in all of DISGRACELAND, are forced to work her private farms with nothing but thin broth and beatings for fuel. Anyone who questions her gets shackled or disappears into the cornfields. She rules with greed and gossip. No one trusts her, not even The Duke’s other mayors. But she doesn’t need trust. She’s useful. She watches the ranchers—especially [[Turner Anderson]] and [[Freddy Blanchard]], who she resents deeply. She keeps a ledger of what goes in and out of every farm, tracking everything like a bloated tax hawk. If someone’s feeding citizens under the table, Rusk finds out. Her mansion, the Gullet House, is a grotesque palace of overindulgence. Roasting pits run day and night. Servants fan her while she eats. Pigs are fattened, then killed for entertainment. She throws Feast Nights where Loyalist guests watch slaves fight for scraps while Rusk laughs with a turkey leg in each hand. But the land remembers. And so do the people. And if hunger doesn’t kill her, rage might. ## Personality **Temperament:** Boastful, petty, and dangerously paranoid. Quick to punish, quicker to indulge. **Vices:** Gluttony, greed, voyeurism. Addicted to power and full plates. **Abilities:** Obsessive recordkeeping, cruel manipulation, political blackmail. She knows what everyone eats and who fed them. **Secrets:** Keeps secret trade records on every rancher, including past betrayals by [[Soria Langston-Clay]]. May have poisoned a Rancher Collective member years ago to earn her spot. **Beliefs:** Hunger is control. Everything can be owned. Generosity is treason. ## Role in Disgraceland [[Marla Rusk]] rules [[Threshton]] with a stomach full of stolen grain and an ego too fat to fail. Her value to The Duke lies in her ability to track every seed and slaughter—no matter how small. But her reign isn’t built to last. If the people ever rise, she’ll be the first to fall. ## Appearances

“I’m not trying to win. I’m just trying to make sure someone tells the truth after the fire.”

Marlon Lambert grew up in **Threshton**, raised by a father who printed grain receipts and a mother who ran messages for the Rancher Collective. He learned to read on old ration slips and grew up knowing that what people _write down_ matters more than what they say. He moved to [[CHARSPIRE]] to work for the _Tribucia Tribute_, where he quickly made a name for himself digging into agricultural corruption and Loyalist zoning scandals. Then **[[Rachel Gold]]** showed up — and the bar moved. She wrote fire. He wrote fact. She was headline ink. He was page three. Instead of resenting her, he fell for her. Not instantly, not with flowers — but with long nights watching her retype whole paragraphs, yelling at the press chief, storming out of the archive room muttering about “cover-ups and cowards.” He’s still in love. But he stays quiet. He’s also become a regular at **The Hollow House**, where **Shana** feeds him breadcrumbs and occasionally lets him sleep in the back room when someone’s chasing him for asking the wrong questions. Marlon isn’t trying to be the best. He’s just trying to make sure **someone remembers the truth** when Rachel’s gone. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Reserved, thoughtful, slightly awkward. He doesn’t interrupt. He listens. Always scribbling in his notepad like he’s transcribing your soul. The kind of guy who knows exactly what’s going on — and pretends he doesn’t until it’s too late for you. **Vices:** Cigarettes. Whiskey. [[Rachel Gold]]. He visits the **[[Hollow House]]** weekly — sometimes for a drink, sometimes for a tip, sometimes just to see **[[Shana]]** smirk when he asks the wrong questions. **Abilities:** Investigative journalist with deep connections in [[Threshton]], [[Gutter Row]], and [[Ashmoor]]. Can blend into a room and make people forget he’s there — until his article drops. Keeps a coded shorthand that only he understands. **Secrets:** Has written drafts of love letters to Rachel that he never sends. Keeps a personal journal separate from his reporting — filled with observations about Rachel, Shana, and the growing unrest. Fears the day Rachel disappears chasing a story, because he won’t survive it **Beliefs:** The story matters more than the byline. Rachel deserves to be protected — even if she’d never ask for it ## Role In Disraceland Marlon Lambert is **Disgraceland’s second-best journalist** — and he knows it. Working in the same newsroom as **[[Rachel Gold]]**, he’s talented, respected, and entirely overlooked… which makes him **very dangerous** in his own way. He’s a quiet operator. He asks the right questions, earns the right trust, and knows how to disappear until the headline drops. He’s also hopelessly in love with Rachel — and has been for years. She doesn’t know. And if she does, she’s too focused on the story to care. So Marlon does what he always does: lights a smoke, follows the lead, and keeps the flame buried under copy edits. ## Appearances

“You’ve got Morris now. And as long as I’m with you… everything’s going to be just fine.”

Morris Gable is the face you see when the rest of Disgraceland goes dark. Five nights a week, at the stroke of midnight, he welcomes the weary, the desperate, and the damned to _Night Time with Morris Gable_ — a talk show turned tranquilizer, beamed into every home by government mandate. With his perfectly sculpted hair and voice smooth as melted wax, Morris offers calm in the chaos. He never stumbles, never sweats, and never speaks a word that hasn’t been rehearsed. His past is a carefully airbrushed mystery. Official records suggest he was once a radio performer in the Capital Crescent, though no recordings survive. Others claim he worked as a magician, a failed actor, or even a Ministry interrogator with a knack for persuasion. What’s known is that when The Duke’s Loyalists began expanding media control, Morris was already waiting — a volunteer eager to become the voice of the new age. Morris now lives in a heavily guarded estate in **South-East Gravenwild**, one of the few clean and comfortable corners of **Charspire**. The studio itself is a concrete tower of humming wires and static screens deep in **Gravenwild proper**, cloaked in smoke and steel. From there, he broadcasts manufactured joy, one chuckle at a time, under the glowing banner of Clay Millwrights. No one knows what he believes. Maybe he believes nothing. Or maybe he believes too much. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Charming, composed, unfailingly polite. He never loses his cool — not on screen, not in public, not even alone. His calm feels practiced, like a man who’s buried his nerves so deep they forgot how to shake. **Vices:** Vanity. He’s obsessed with his appearance, his image, his legacy. Drinks alone most nights. Keeps a hidden stash of preserved cosmetics and vintage cologne. Whispers his own name into the mirror when he’s sure no one’s listening. **Abilities:** Master of tone, pacing, and presence — hypnotic speech. Can read any cue card like it was carved from his soul. Knows how to pivot, deflect, and redirect any question. Allegedly has a photographic memory. **Secrets:** He keeps a box under his bed with recordings of himself trying to tell the truth. He’s never aired them. **Beliefs:** Morris doesn’t believe in The Duke. He believes in _order_. In _calm_. In keeping the screaming down to a dull murmur. He believes the truth is a poison and that people want to be lied to — kindly, nightly, beautifully. ## Role In Disgraceland Morris Gable is the midnight voice of state-sponsored comfort — a propaganda host designed to keep the people soothed, distracted, and loyal. He is loved by many, trusted by most, and truly known by no one. ## Appearances

**Base of Operations:** Nightclub in Vileby, Gutter Row  
**Leaders:** [[Marco Murray]] (boss), [[Francis Murray]] (enforcer), [[Rosa Murray]] (treasurer), [[Nico Murray]] (junior member)  
**Allies:** Mayor [[Gorren Brile]] (Charspire), Mayor [[Cricket Granger]] (Gutter Row)  
**Main Activities:** Drug distribution, extortion

---

## Overview

The Murray Boys are the most feared crime family in [[Gutter Row]] and [[Charspire]], their influence growing every year. Built from nothing by [[Marco Murray]], the crew started with petty hustles and small-time rackets. Marco kept a low profile, never letting the [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] cops catch a whiff of his real business.

As Marco’s [[Luxyn]] operation grew, he brought his brother Francis on board. Together, they built the Murray Boys into the go-to organization for anyone needing muscle, drugs, or a debt collected. When Mayor Cricket Granger found out about Marco’s Luxyn trade, he offered protection—so long as the Murray Boys moved product for him. Later, a similar deal was struck with Mayor Brile in Charspire, giving the Murrays control of Luxyn’s supply chain from mine to market.

Rosa Murray, Marco’s wife, manages the family’s finances and keeps the books so clean even [[The Duke]]’s men have trouble finding dirt. Their son, Nico, is just starting to make a name for himself—mostly causing headaches for the rest of the crew.

---

## Structure

- **Marco Murray (Boss):** Founder and brains of the operation. Handles major deals, alliances, and keeps the peace between Gutter Row and Charspire.
- **Francis Murray (Enforcer):** Marco’s loyal brother. Acts as the muscle—settling scores, collecting debts, and making sure nobody crosses the Murray Boys twice.
- **Rosa Murray (Treasurer):** Marco’s wife and the crew’s accountant. Keeps the money flowing, bribes paid, and the authorities distracted.
- **Nico Murray (Junior):** Marco and Rosa’s son. Spoiled, cocky, and trying to prove himself in the family business.

---

## Activities

- **Selling & Distributing Luxyn:** The Murray Boys control most of the Luxyn trade in Gutter Row and Charspire, supplying for Mayor Brile and Mayor Granger.
- **Extorting Local Businesses:** Shopkeepers and merchants pay for “protection.” Those who don’t quickly regret it.
- **Nightclub HQ:** They operate out of a nightclub in Vileby—a front for their operations and a hub for business, deals, and muscle.

---

## Reputation

Feared and respected in equal measure. The Murray Boys are known for being ruthless with enemies, loyal to their own, and always getting paid. Their network stretches through Gutter Row’s worst alleys and Charspire’s darkest corners. No one sells Luxyn or runs a racket on their turf without their say-so.

---

“Relax. You really think anything bad could happen to a Murray?”

Nico Murray grew up wanting for nothing, the only child of [[Marco Murray|Marco]] and [[Rosa Murray|Rosa]]. With two powerful parents and a taste for the high life, Nico has never known the struggle that shaped his family. He was sent to the best schools, always had the best clothes, and never missed a party worth being seen at. Spoiled by luxury and cushioned from real danger, Nico’s world is flashy—filled with expensive watches, fast rides, and the kind of trouble you can usually buy your way out of. Cocky, charming, and quick with a joke, Nico has always thought of himself as untouchable—a prince of Disgraceland’s underworld, even if he’s just started learning what that actually means. Recently, though, cracks have started to show in his golden world. Nico’s parents are slowly letting him in on the family business. He likes the taste of power, but he still treats it like a game—more interested in the thrill and attention than the danger. He boasts about things he barely understands, flirts with anyone who’ll listen, and imagines himself as the future king—even as the real wolves circle closer than he realizes. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Brash, overconfident, and witty. He’s quick to charm and quicker to show off, but deep down he’s still just a kid, a little in over his head. **Vices:** Fast cars, women, gambling, and living above his means. Nico loves being the center of attention, even when it gets him in trouble. **Abilities:** Naturally charismatic, street-smart (to a point), and good at talking himself out of trouble. He can be clever and resourceful when he has to be, but hasn’t faced any real consequences—yet. **Secrets:** Nico’s started to notice the danger his parents face, and sometimes wishes he could walk away. He keeps a stash of cash and an old revolver hidden in his room—just in case. He’s already made promises to a rival gang, thinking he can play both sides. **Beliefs:** He thinks he’s invincible, believes he’s destined for greatness, and has a soft spot for his mother, though he hides it under bravado. ## Role In Disgraceland Nico is the cocky heir apparent of the [[Murray Boys]], strutting through [[Gutter Row]] and [[Charspire]] like he owns the place—protected by his last name, but dangerously unaware of how quickly fortunes change in Disgraceland.

> — [[Morris Gable]]

## 🕰 Overview
*Night Time with Morris Gable* is the flagship late-night broadcast of [[TTV Studios]], aimed at soothing the nerves of a fractured nation while subtly reinforcing loyalty to the regime. Airing five nights a week across all of [[DISGRACELAND]], it delivers charm, distraction, and just enough optimism to keep people passive.

The show is not mandatory, but it might as well be. CRT sets gifted by [[The Duke]] ensure everyone has access. In many homes, Morris is the only voice still speaking when the world goes quiet.

---

## 📋 Format
### 🗣 Opening Monologue
Delivered from his desk with a glowing microphone and practiced smile. Warm, vaguely hopeful, always safe. Opens every night with:  
*“If the world’s still turnin’ — then I’ll still be talkin’. Welcome to Night Time, friends.”*

### ✨ Bright Spots
Footage of regime achievements across the territories. New rail lines, ration increases, community events — all curated, staged, or exaggerated for effect.

### 🎤 Guest Appearances
Carefully vetted guests — factory workers, local “heroes,” regime-approved performers — share cheerful stories that reinforce the illusion of progress and unity.

### 🎸 Live Music by *The Wanderers*
Every episode features a live musical performance by [[The Wanderers]], a beloved Disgraceland band. Their presence has boosted the show’s popularity across even the more rebellious territories.  
Morris personally recruited them, recognizing their influence. They rarely speak on air, but always close with a subtle nod to the camera.

### 🌒 Final Thoughts
Morris ends the show with a quiet monologue and a reassuring smile, sending viewers to sleep with soft words and measured calm.

---

## 📺 Cultural Impact
- **Charspire & Gutter Row:** The show is embraced as soothing late-night comfort.
- **Steeltown & Threshton:** Viewed with skepticism or irony, but still widely watched.
- Children mimic Morris’s voice. Fan art and black-market merchandise exist.
- Some claim hearing Morris’s voice helps them sleep. Others say it’s the only reason they haven’t screamed in years.

---

## 🏢 TTV Studios & Broadcast Details
Filmed live from **[[TTV Studios]]** in the heart of industrial **Gravenwild**. The building is one of the last fully functional towers from the pre-Tetra era, retrofitted with massive signal boosters and armed [[Redforce]] patrols.

The studio set is bright on screen but surrounded by soot-streaked scaffolding and smoke beyond the cameras. Power is often inconsistent, but the signal rarely fails.

---

## 🧠 Trivia
- Morris wears the same style of burgundy suit every night — he owns over 40 identical versions.
- [[The Wanderers]] are rumored to slip hidden anti-Duke messages into their instrumentals.
- A leaked memo once described the show as *“the regime’s velvet rope — not to bind, just to lull.”*
- [[The Duke]] has never appeared on the program.

## Biography

> “Words are just bullets with better aim, baby. And I don’t miss.”


**Tren Knight**, better known on the streets as **“Ninepack,”** is the slick-talking, sharp-dressing broker of [[The Third Row]] and the blood kin of [[Samson Knight]] — his little cousin, but nobody calls him that if they like their teeth.

With the looks of a prophet and the tongue of a hustler, Baby Nine was never built for the alleys or the blade. But he could sell heat to Charspire and talk a Loyalist guard into handing over their badge. From the time he was twelve, he was running side hustles, love notes, and dirty credits through the pipes of [[Vileby]], always one move ahead of his enemies and two steps behind the girls.

While [[Jailface]] cleans up messes, Baby Nine *prevents* them — or makes sure they turn a profit when they happen. He organizes the tribute flow, fences high-value goods, manages outside syndicate communications, and smooths tensions between rival crews with charm, smoke, and veiled threats. His connection to Mr. Knight gets him access, but his silver tongue keeps him indispensable.

He’s a poet when drunk, a savage when crossed, and a legend in bed — if his rhymes are to be believed.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Charismatic, fast-talking, smooth under pressure. Loves attention, but rarely loses control.

**Vices:** 
Women, wordplay, and private stashes of imported liquor. Keeps a book of poems he’s never shown anyone.

**Abilities:** 
Deal-making, double-speak, blackmail, negotiation. Can read a mark in seconds and flip them in minutes.

**Secrets:** 
Ninepack is rumored to be running quiet talks with a Threshton contact, despite Knight’s warnings. Whether it’s treason or business... only he knows.

**Beliefs:** 
Everything can be negotiated. Everyone wants something — your job is to find out what and charge double.

## Role in Disgraceland
Ninepack is the velvet tongue of The Third Row — a street poet with hustler instincts who makes sure the market never stops spinning, and no deal ever closes without a cut for Mr. Knight.

"The land remembers. And so do I."

Nita Blackbird was born into a resilient Indigenous community along the remnants of the Sinner's Sea, a people who held on to their traditions even as the world crumbled around them. She was taught to read the land, track game, and endure the harsh realities of a fractured world. Her family believed that survival wasn’t just about strength — it was about remembering who they were. That belief shattered the day the Duke’s enforcers came. They razed her village, claiming it was harboring rebels. Nita’s parents were killed in the slaughter, and her younger brother was dragged away in chains. Left for dead, Nita vowed to one day find him or at least make those responsible pay. For years, she wandered the desolate roads of Disgraceland, surviving through her skills and the whispers of the land. Her fierce reputation eventually caught the attention of the Unseen Widows. Veerah, the enigmatic leader, offered Nita a place among them — not just as a warrior, but as a symbol of retribution. The Widows moved like shadows, assassinating those who served the Duke and liberating those who suffered under his rule. Nita quickly became one of Veerah’s most trusted operatives. Her ruthless efficiency in the field, combined with her quiet compassion for the innocent, earned her respect within the ranks. Despite her loyalty, however, doubt lingers. While Veerah is revered as a prophet, Nita remains skeptical of her visions. The certainty with which Veerah commands the Widows unnerves her. Nita follows orders, but she watches — questioning whether the ends truly justify the means. Her gold bird emblem, stitched over her heart, serves as a reminder of her family and the freedom she fights for. Every mission she undertakes is another step toward avenging the past and preventing others from suffering the same fate. But Nita knows that one day, her loyalty to the Widows and her personal quest for justice may collide. The question is — when that day comes, which path will she choose? --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Nita is stoic, grounded, and fiercely intuitive. She speaks with purpose, rarely wastes breath, and moves through the world like she’s always listening for something most people can’t hear. She is protective, introspective, and commands respect with quiet authority. **Vices:** Obsessively carves notches into her gear — one for every life taken in her pursuit of justice. Refuses to stay in one place for too long. Prone to disappearing for days at a time to "clear her head." **Abilities:** Master tracker and wilderness scout. Exceptional with bows, blades, and snares. Reads terrain and movement like second nature. Knows when she’s being watched. Can move silently for miles. Deeply tuned to her surroundings. **Secrets:** She still believes her brother may be alive — and has followed rumors of him to places even the Widows avoid. Keeps a small carved animal figure from her childhood hidden in her satchel. **Beliefs:** Believes in justice more than vengeance, but often confuses the two. Skeptical of Veerah’s divine gift — she follows her out of loyalty and shared purpose, not blind faith. ## Role In Disgraceland Nita serves as the Unseen Widows' top scout, hunter, and survivalist. When a mission demands traversing dangerous terrain, uncovering hidden camps, or striking from the wilderness, Nita is sent. Her ability to stalk a target unseen across miles of broken country has earned her a ghostlike reputation. Veerah trusts her instincts, even if their beliefs don’t align. Among the Widows, Nita is both a warrior and a guardian — a symbol that there’s still honor in the fight. But her soul is divided, caught between duty to the Widows and a personal promise to a family she may never see again.

# NOCHE DE LUCHA

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ Backburn Show
> ![[ancientnl.png|450]]  

## Overview
**Noche de Lucha (“Night of the Fight”) is a one night, 16 person single elimination tournament that takes place every four years.** 
**Open to All:**   Traditionally reserved for faithful of [[El Santo]], the tournament is now open to all, regardless of faith, in recognition of the world’s upheaval and the need for unity. Even an Ember Saint won the last Noche de Lucha. An event talked about in every corner of Disgraceland.
 **Selection:**  The Senior Enmascarados—the highest council of the faith—select 16 fighters based on merit, reputation, and sometimes, rumor or legend or popular support.
**The Arena:**  Held in the Arena Mascarada in [[STEELTOWN#East Mountain|East Mountain]], [[Steeltown]].
**The Celebration:**  Noche de Lucha is a festival as much as a tournament—food, music, street games, and weeks of communal joy and rivalry.
**The Prize:**  The winner is crowned Grand Luchador, head of the faith and symbol of the era’s spirit for the next four years.
**Enduring Tradition:**  War, bombs, famine—nothing has stopped Noche de Lucha. It is the one promise the world has kept.

## ANCIENT ORIGINS

Since time immemorial, every four years on the 15th–20th of [[Calendar|Rainsun]], Noche de Lucha has been held.

- **Sacred Combat:** The earliest Nights took place at the center of ancient villages, on stone platforms beneath torchlight. Masked warriors fought not for sport, but to resolve disputes, seek the blessing of their gods, or determine leaders.
- **The Masked Champion:** Legends tell of a figure known only as **[[El Santo]]**, the first to don a sacred mask and win the Night—not through brute strength, but through heart, cunning, and mercy.
- **The Eternal Ring:** These battles happened in rings drawn in dirt, carved in stone, or built from woven ropes—always as a circle, representing eternity and unity.
- **Rituals & Myths:** Every Noche began with offerings, music, and storytelling. Winners were believed to carry the favor of the divine, and sometimes, to become living saints.

## EVOLUTION

The tradition endured. As civilizations rose and fell, the Night was passed down through generations, its true origins lost but its rituals surviving.  
Later cultures reshaped it—sometimes as gladiator games, sometimes as wrestling, sometimes as rebellion against tyrants.  
But always:  
- Masks, to honor the unknown gods and spirits  
- A ring, to contain the struggle  
- The winner’s right to challenge fate and change their life

## LEGACY IN DISGRACELAND

In the world of Disgraceland, **Noche de Lucha** is the oldest surviving ritual. It is the **heartbeat of the Faith of El Santo** and the unbroken thread connecting the present to a forgotten age.

Even after the fall, the bombs, and the end of empires, the Night remains.  
Each four-year cycle is not just a contest—but a reenactment of a myth older than memory.

## CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE

**Noche de Lucha** is:
- The living memory of ancient peoples
- Proof that unity, struggle, and hope endure
- A bridge between mortals and the divine

“I am proof that death is an obstacle, not an end. Soon, Disgraceland will understand the cost of true immortality.”

Long ago, during the chaos of the dark years, Ora Razchek was just another brilliant scientist trying to save his own skin. Working in secret, he developed a radical, invasive AI—one designed to replace failing brain tissue, rewrite memory, and eventually take over the entire mind. He called it the “Continuum Protocol.” He tested it on himself, right before the world fell apart. The experiment _killed_ him… but he got back up. The human part of Ora Razchek died on that table, but what woke up was something else—a hybrid consciousness, a cold, calculating mix of Ora’s memories, instincts, and an ever-adapting artificial mind. He has taken the young [[Hella]] under his wing. **Now, Ora cannot die—** at least, not as long as his brain (and its implanted AI) remains intact. He doesn’t age. He doesn’t sleep. He barely feels pain. And as his humanity slips further away, all that remains is the drive for power, and a sick curiosity: _How many others can he remake in his image?_ ### **His Mission:** - He “perfected” himself, but now he wants to claim dominion over Disgraceland. No more hiding in the shadows. - He’s building an army of AI-brain monsters, all ultimately controlled by his own will—a network of living weapons, each one a reflection of his own immortal experiment. - When the time is right, he’ll unleash his “children” to wipe out the city’s leaders, topple the Duke, and take his seat as the true ruler—a god among insects. ### **Unbeknownst to all:** - **Nobody knows Razchek is already dead.** To the world, he’s just a weird, reclusive old man in goggles. - His army waits below, perfectly still until the signal comes—a dark, silent hive beneath the city. - Only one thing can kill Ora Razchek: destroying the AI core in his brain. Anything less, he survives—rebooting, rebuilding, learning from every failure. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Detached. Inhumanly calm. Observes more than he speaks — if he speaks at all. He carries the unsettling serenity of someone who already knows how and when you’ll die. **Vices:** Obsession with immortality, disregard for human life, compulsive need to “improve” humanity. **Abilities:** Superhuman intellect, inhuman patience, neural network control over all his creations, can transfer some of his consciousness to other AI brains if needed. **Secrets:** He’s already dead. If his brain is destroyed, the entire army loses connection—instant, chaotic failure. **Beliefs:** Death is a sickness, and he is the cure. Humanity is a species that must evolve or perish, and he alone can drive that evolution. ## Role In Disgraceland While every other bastard’s fighting over scraps, Ora Razchek is quietly getting ready to turn the entire world upside down. The scariest part? Nobody suspects a thing. Not yet.

  - ### **Part 1**: 
    Shana, the owner of Hollow House takes a break from managing her girls and steps out back for a cigarette in the night air. Two clearly drunk loyalist guards appear acting like assholes and ask her for a smoke and start harrassing Shana, but Shana is cool and confident and does what she can to try and calm things. NOTE TITLE: [[Owen McCready]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_owen.png","religion":"None","status":"Alive","location":"[[CHARSPIRE]]","territory":"[[CHARSPIRE]]","district":"[[CHARSPIRE#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]]","faction":"None","role":"[[TTV Studios]] Station Manager","chapters":["07 - The Spotlight Lies"],"tags":["character","individual","neutral","stillborn-star","chapter07"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/06 19:56:22"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_owen.png religion: None status: Alive location: "[[CHARSPIRE]]" territory: "[[CHARSPIRE]]" district: "[[CHARSPIRE#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]]" faction: None role: "[[TTV Studios]] Station Manager" chapters: - 07 - The Spotlight Lies tags: - character - individual - neutral - stillborn-star - chapter07 --- # OWEN 'SWITCH' McCREADY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[owen.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Station Manager of [[TTV Studios]] **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** Gravenwild, [[CHARSPIRE]] **Public Reputation:** None **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 51 **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 224 lbs. **Date of Birth:** August 6th, 2135 **Occupation:** Station Manager **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** **Known Associates:** [[Morris Gable]] **Faith:** None **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I don’t care who’s running the show, long as I get paid and nobody screws with my tower. You want the truth? Don’t look for it on TV.”

Owen “Switch” McCready is the reluctant lifeblood of [[TTV Studios]], the last broadcast engineer in a world that barely remembers television. Fifty-eight but looks older, he’s wiry, stoop-shouldered, with permanent bags under his eyes and nicotine-stained fingers. His voice is hoarse, his wit sharper than the broken glass around the [[CHARSPIRE#Gravenwild|Gravenwild]] streets. He was running illegal radio, hiding from every government and corporation until [[The Duke]]’s people found him and gave him an offer he couldn’t refuse: fix the tower, run the shows, and keep his head down. Switch is seen as a necessary evil by the regime and an enigma to the citizens — a guy who seems to exist in the walls, always lurking behind cables or vanishing into the static. He’s never at ease except when buried in tangled wires or soldering something by flashlight. Most folks have no idea if he’s loyal, broken, or just too tired to care. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Blunt, antisocial, and unflappable under pressure. Switch is not mean, but he’s got no patience for small talk or bullshit. Prefers silence to company, except for a late-night drink with one of the crew who actually knows which end of a soldering iron gets hot. If you waste his time, he’ll let you know. If you show up to help, he’ll grumble but let you stay. **Vices:** Bourbon, hand-rolled cigarettes, and scavenged painkillers. Sleeps in the equipment room more nights than not, bottle in hand. His biggest vice, though, is isolation: Switch avoids people, feelings, and especially hope, burying himself in work and routine. **Abilities:** A natural with anything electrical or mechanical, from broadcast towers to shortwave radios and analog security cams. Can fix almost anything with spare wire, scrap metal, and tape. Has an uncanny knack for reading a situation — he can smell trouble before it happens, and knows how to keep a low profile when the wrong people are sniffing around. **Secrets:** Keeps a private shortwave set tuned to “forbidden” frequencies — sometimes intercepts rebel transmissions or pirate music, never says a word. He secretly recorded The Duke’s first address at TTV, stashing the original tape in a hidden box “for insurance.” Once helped a resistance runner sneak out by faking a signal blackout. Most dangerous secret: he’s got enough dirt on the Loyalist Guards to ruin several careers, but no desire to be a hero. **Beliefs:** Trusts machines more than people, and believes survival means staying invisible. Cynical about politics; sees The Duke as “just another bastard in charge.” Deep down, though, Switch believes in freedom of information — but he’s convinced trying to fight the system outright just gets you killed. ## Role In Disgraceland Switch is the only reason the signal reaches every home, bar, and bunker in Tribucia. He keeps TTV running, not out of loyalty, but because nobody else can. Both The Duke’s men and the general public leave him alone — he’s too useful to threaten, too strange to befriend. ## Appearances

# 🏴 [[Poundball]]

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ POUNDBALL
> ![[pound.png|450]]  

**Poundball** is a brutal, fast-paced sport played throughout Disgraceland in abandoned lots, broken parking decks, and dusty fields. It’s a game of speed, force, and survival — where glory is earned through blood and bruises. Banned in [[Ashmoor]] but beloved everywhere else, Poundball is more than a game — it’s a warzone with rules.

---

## 🧱 Basic Rules

- **Teams of 6:**
  - **3 Runners** – Only players allowed to carry or pass the Poundball.
  - **2 Pounders** – Defense. Smash and stop opposing runners by any means.
  - **1 Anchor** – A grounded goalie. Cannot leave the goal zone.

- **The Ball:**
  A 25-pound leather-wrapped sand-and-scrap core called the *Poundball*.

- **Field:**
  Played on any wide-open space. Each end has a marked **scoring zone** — sometimes spray-painted, sometimes built from junk.

- **Scoring:**
  A runner scores by:
  - Crossing into the scoring zone while holding the ball (3 points), or
  - Underhand-lobbing it into the "zone", usually a trashcan, from outside (1 point).

- **Turnovers:**
  If a runner is tackled and drops the ball before scoring or passing, possession flips to the other team after three hits if the Runner still holds the ball.

- **Passing:**
  Lateral or underhand only. No overhand forward throws.

- **Winning:**
  First team to 13 points or the most points in 45 minutes.

---

## 🚫 Fouls & Penalties

- **Illegal moves:** Eye-gouging, biting, groin shots.
- **Grifter Drops:** Faking a drop to bait a hit. Results in a **Grime Stop**.
- **Scrap Box:** Players penalized for dirty play serve 3 minutes in a caged side zone.

---

## 🥊 Positions & Strategy

| Role       | Description                        |
|------------|------------------------------------|
| **Runner** | Agile, strategic, good hands       |
| **Pounder**| Massive, mean, relentless hitters  |
| **Anchor** | Stationary juggernaut, goal guard  |

**Tactics:**
- **"Bleeding the Field"** – Luring defenders to one side for a clean run.
- **"Gravel Grind"** – A low crawl burst to sneak past defenders.
- **"Fleshing the Anchor"** – Forcing the goalie to commit so another runner can score.

---

## 🎭 Poundball Attire

Players wear scavenged, makeshift gear for protection and intimidation:

- **Runners:**
  - Stripped-down outfits for speed.
  - Gloves, elbow wraps, light pads.
  - Often shirtless or in cut tanks.

- **Pounders:**
  - **Makeshift shoulder pads** fashioned from metal scraps, car seat foam, or layered rubber.
  - Reinforced boots, padded forearms, chain wraps.

- **Anchors:**
  - Heavy torso padding.
  - **Leather helmets**, some with horn-like additions or personal paintjobs.
  - Thick gloves for bone-breaking tackles.

Many paint their faces or bodies with ash, rust, or blood before matches. Team symbols are often carved or stitched into their gear.

---

## 🔥 Notable Teams

- **[[Steeltown Wreckers]]** – Tough, brawling veterans. Never back down.
- **[[Threshton Cattle Dogs]]** – Fast, deceptive, and full of dirty tricks.
- **[[Gutter Row Shockrats]]** – Street kids turned legends. Aggressive and wild.
- **[[Charspire Heavy Bolts]]** – Built like mining rigs. Known for crushing hits.
- **[[Ashmoor Gildsmen]]** – Rich-sponsored killers. Well-trained and ruthless.
- **[[Coffin Island Lockjaws]]** – Inmates. Silent. Scary. Undefeated in brawls.

---

## 🏆 Poundball Culture

Poundball is more than entertainment — it’s a release. A way for citizens to forget about Loyalists, rations, or chains. Betting is rampant. Fans chant in the stands made of shipping crates, and riots often break out when a ref call goes wrong.

Kids play it with bricks and trashballs in alleys. Adults die playing it for glory. Legends are born in the dust and blood of the Poundball pit.

---

> “You don’t *win* Poundball. You *survive it longer than the other bastard.*”

NOTE TITLE: [[Prophet Veerah]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_veerah.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Prophet, Head of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","protagonist","widow","prophet","main","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:44"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_veerah.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: Prophet, Head of the [[Unseen Widows]] chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - protagonist - widow - prophet - main - mirella - chapter5 --- # PROPHET VEERAH > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[veerah.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Prophet and Head of the [[Unseen Widows]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Prophet **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Unknown **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** Widowed **Age:** Unknown **Height:** 5'10" **Weight:** 133 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Prophet cult leader **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Riley Thorne]] [[Len Vyne]] [[Nita Blackbird]] **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“The stars don’t scream. They whisper. And if you’re foolish enough to ignore them… they burn.”

Veerah was once no different from the countless forgotten souls of Disgraceland — another survivor scraping by in a world that had long since abandoned hope. But everything changed the night the visions began. Dreams of fragmented moments, distant faces, and twisted landscapes plagued her sleep. At first, she thought them the fevered remnants of hunger and exhaustion. But when those dreams started to unfold in reality — each detail as precise as she had seen — Veerah knew she had been touched by something far beyond comprehension. She called it a gift, though whether it was a blessing or a curse remains uncertain. In a world shattered by war and ruin, certainty is a rare commodity. Yet Veerah’s followers see her as a prophet, a vessel for divine truth. To them, her dreams are the whispered will of a higher power. The Unseen Widows formed around her, not merely as warriors but as devoted disciples. They believe every word that passes Veerah’s lips, seeing her as a guiding light in the perpetual darkness of Disgraceland. But Veerah is no mere oracle. Beneath the gilded tiara that crowns her golden hair is a mind sharpened by hardship. Before the Widows, she was a ghost, moving through the shadows, mastering the art of silent death. She learned the value of patience — the perfect kill is never rushed. Every flicker of light, every shifting shadow, became her allies. Now, she passes these lessons to her sisters, transforming them into assassins that strike without warning. They wear their veils and black garb like armor, their beauty a weapon as sharp as any blade. Veerah teaches them to use the desires of others to their advantage, understanding that seduction is as deadly as steel. Despite her growing legend, there are whispers of doubt that even Veerah cannot silence. Each vision takes its toll, leaving her exhausted and frayed. She claims to hear the voice of a higher being, but in the stillness of the night, she sometimes wonders if the voice is merely her own. The Widows know nothing of her uncertainty — to them, she is infallible. Yet the burden of prophecy weighs heavy. Every life taken by her word, every drop of blood spilled in her name, carves a deeper wound within her soul. Still, Veerah remains resolute. The Duke’s tyranny cannot go unanswered, and Disgraceland’s suffering will not endure forever. Whether her path is righteous or not, she will follow her visions until the end. And when the time comes, the Widows will be ready — their hands steady, their blades sharp, and their faith unwavering. For to defy Veerah is to defy fate itself. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Veerah is poised and enigmatic, radiating an eerie calm even in chaos. She’s introspective, deliberate, and unshakably confident in public — yet harbors private doubts she shares with no one. Her voice is soft, her words carry weight, and her silence says even more. > [!infobox] > > ![[veerah preach.png|260]] **Vices:** Keeps her pain to herself, refusing rest or comfort. Addicted to control — not power, but control. Occasionally indulges in rare, potent opiates to silence the visions **Abilities:** Vivid, often traumatic visions of the future; always accurate. Trained in silent movement, blade work, and psychological warfare. Inspires unwavering loyalty and obedience in her followers **Secrets:** She is no longer sure if the voice in her dreams is divine… or her own madness **Beliefs:** Her visions are sacred truths, whether from a god, a force, or something else ## Role In Disgraceland Veerah is the leader and prophet of the **Unseen Widows**, a cult-like faction of all-female assassins operating from the Drownlands. Feared, worshipped, and untouchable, she influences events from the shadows, shaping Disgraceland’s future one death at a time. Whether messiah or madwoman, she stands as a symbol of vengeance, destiny, and quiet terror.

“You don’t scare me. I’ve been threatened by better men, and they all ended up in my footnotes.”

**Rachel Gold** was born in a pressroom — ink on her hands before she could write. Her parents ran an underground news flyer during the early years of the Loyalist consolidation, smuggling stories across borders and burning presses before raids. When the Tetra bomb fell, her father disappeared and her mother went silent. Rachel never stopped chasing the story. Now, she writes for the **[[Tribucia Tribute]]**, the last printed paper in Disgraceland. Most reporters just rewrite Loyalist briefings or publish puff pieces about grain yields. Not Rachel. She digs. She exposes. She names names. Her coverage of **[[Gorren Brile|Mayor Brile]]’s torture camps**, **[[Sgt. Rottwyler]]’s black market raids**, and **slave trafficking in [[Gutter Row]]** made her both a hero and a target. Her column, _Gold’s Truth_, runs front page more days than not. And every time it does, someone in power loses sleep. Her editors constantly warn her to **stay away from The Duke**, and so far, she has — _publicly_. But there’s a folder buried in her filing cabinet. A thick one. With red string and ink stains. And one day, that story’s going to break. And when it does… Disgraceland won’t be ready for it. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Quick-witted, relentless, and unapologetically direct. She's got no patience for bullshit, small talk, or weak coffee. She’ll listen to your story — but only if you get to the point. **Vices:** Caffeine, long nights, confrontation. Smokes only when she’s about to publish something risky. Keeps a loaded recorder in her boot and a pair of brass knuckles in her desk drawer — just in case. **Abilities:** Master investigator — knows how to bribe, charm, or blackmail the truth out of anyone. Carries an old, beat-up press badge that’s saved her life more than once. Can type a full article in one sitting, no edits needed. **Secrets:** Keeps a hidden file on The Duke — dozens of leads, names, and clues no one’s allowed to see. Has an informant inside The Silo, though even she doesn’t know their real name. **Beliefs:** The truth matters — even if no one believes it ## Role In Disgraceland Rachel Gold is Disgraceland’s **last real reporter** — a fast-talking, hard-punching journalist who digs where she shouldn’t and prints what no one else will. She’s the kind of woman who asks the dangerous questions, writes the answers in bold, and _signs her name at the bottom_. Her exposés have rattled mayors, exposed corruption, and nearly got her killed more than once. She’s beloved by the public, hated by the powerful, and barely tolerated by her own editors. ## Appearances

NOTE TITLE: [[Raina & Risa]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_randr.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","twins","assassins","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:48"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_randr.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Widow of the [[Unseen Widows]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - twins - assassins - mirella - chapter5 --- # RAINA & RISA > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[randr.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Twin Blades of the Widows **Alias/Nickname:** The Sisters, The Split Curse **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Feared; spoken of like urban legends **Gender:** Female (identical twins) **Spouse:** None **Age:** Early 20s **Height:** 5'5" **Weight:** 118 lbs. each **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Twin assassins **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], [[Riley Thorne]], [[Nita Blackbird]], each other **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“You can’t kill what moves in two places at once.”

Raina and Risa were born into the unforgiving wastes of Disgraceland, twin daughters of a wandering trader and a mother who died before their third birthday. From their earliest days, the sisters were inseparable, bound by the unspoken understanding that survival meant staying together. Their father led a nomadic life, navigating the scorched remnants of the old world, bartering stolen scraps and scavenged goods. It wasn’t a life of comfort, but it was a life. That life ended the day their caravan crossed paths with the Duke’s enforcers. Accused of trading contraband and withholding supplies, their father was executed without trial. The twins were dragged away, separated, and sold into servitude. For years, they endured lives of torment — Raina forced into hard labor, Risa into the twisted entertainment of the Duke’s wealthy allies. But even apart, the sisters’ bond never broke. They clung to the hope of finding one another, whispering silent promises beneath the stars. When the time came, they made good on those promises. Raina escaped first, slaughtering a guard with a jagged scrap of metal. Risa’s liberation followed soon after, her captors falling to the ruthless precision of a stolen dagger. Reunited and stained with the blood of their tormentors, the sisters fled into the night. They were no longer victims — they were vengeance made flesh. It was Veerah who found them next, drawn by the shadows they left in their wake. The Unseen Widows offered them sanctuary and purpose. Raina, fierce and unrelenting, became a master of close-quarters combat, wielding her blades with ruthless efficiency. Risa, calculating and precise, embraced the art of silent death, her throwing stars finding their mark without fail. Together, they are a force of nature — twin specters feared even among the Duke’s most hardened enforcers. Though bound by their loyalty to the Widows, the sisters remain wary of Veerah’s unwavering belief in her visions. Unlike some of their sisters, Raina and Risa do not follow blindly. They follow each other. The world has taken everything from them, but as long as they stand side by side, the sisters of the Unseen Widows will never be broken. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Raina is raw fire — quick to strike, blunt, and driven by instinct. Risa is the cooling shadow — calm, clever, and dangerously observant. Together, they form a perfect balance of chaos and precision. They speak in unison when they wish to intimidate, but often communicate without words at all. **Vices:** They don't sleep unless the other is watching. Both suffer from fragmented nightmares, often reliving their separate captivities. Raina breaks things when angry. Risa journals in code no one else understands. **Abilities:** Raina is a brutal melee fighter — excels in confined combat, knife work, and disarming enemies with speed and strength. Risa specializes in ranged precision, poisons, and stealth infiltration. Together, they perform tandem attacks that overwhelm opponents before they understand what’s happening. **Secrets:** Each keeps scars the other has never asked about. Risa knows one of her captors still lives, and she hasn’t told Raina. Raina sometimes wonders if they'd survive being separated again — and dreads the answer. **Beliefs:** They believe in each other before anything else. Their faith in Mirella is quiet, ritualistic, and mostly tied to Veerah's influence — but they follow the Widow creed as long as it aligns with their bond. ## Role In Disgraceland Raina and Risa are among the most feared Widows in the field. Their synchronized tactics make them nearly impossible to counter — one distracts, the other kills. They are often deployed for missions requiring shock value, disruption, and psychological warfare. Their presence alone is enough to cause panic among Loyalist ranks. Though they outwardly serve Veerah, their true allegiance has always been to each other. To lose one would be to lose both — and if that ever happens, Disgraceland may tremble.

History of the Rancher Collective
>

“Our mission is survival.”

Long before [[The Duke]] cemented his rule with rations and rifle barrels, [[Threshton]] was just dust, starvation, and wild cattle. After the [[Tetra Bomb]], most of the area fell silent — fields went fallow, families scattered, and the old supply chains turned to rust. What remained was fought over, stolen, or hoarded by those with the might to defend it. But in the ruins of that scorched earth, after decades had healed what time could of the land, a man named [[Harp Langston]] planted a seed — literally and otherwise. He built [[Threshton#Red Night Ranch|Red Night Ranch]] with scarred hands and the kind of fury only true survival breeds. While others traded bullets for bread, Harp raised cattle and coaxed wheat out of poisoned soil. His methods were brutal, his land cursed with sweat and bone, but somehow, it worked. He fed himself, then a few neighbors, then word started spreading: “There’s food in [[Threshton]].” Soon, other ranches sprouted like weeds around Red Night — desperate men trying to mimic Harp’s stubborn miracle. A few succeeded. Most failed. But the ones who made it? Harp brought them to his table. Not out of charity. Out of strategy. “We got two choices,” he’d said, leaning over a cracked map and a bottle of rotgut whiskey. “Fight each other ‘til we all starve… or link arms and deal from strength.” Thus, the [[Rancher Collective]] was born — five ranches banding together, agreeing to share resources, protect their convoys, and negotiate food distribution as one voice. And it worked. [[The Duke]], still consolidating power in [[Ashmoor]], needed a reliable food source — and the Collective had it. So a deal was struck: 30% for the ranchers. 70% for the Duke. Harsh, but better than bullets. Over time, ranches rose and fell, and with them, membership shifted. Only Harp remained constant — the scarred sentinel of Red Night Ranch. Others came and went. Turner Anderson, now the largest landowner in Threshton, brought size and steady leadership. Freddy Blanchard brought heart and muscle. Beau DuNoir brought silver-tongued deals and backroom charm. And then, like a bad smell in a locked room, came Danny Dandelion, who conned his way into Snake Kiss Ranch and a seat at the table. The Collective operates under simple but ironclad rules: - Majority vote rules. Always. - No one acts alone in major trade matters. - All members must contribute to the food output. - And every meeting ends with a shot of whiskey — no matter how heated the vote. They are not friends. They are not brothers. They are a working alliance, forged by fire and held together by the brittle string of necessity. Without them, Disgraceland starves. With them, it teeters on the edge of rebellion. And everyone knows — the day the [[Rancher Collective]] falls apart… the whole damn region goes with it.

NOTE TITLE: [[Raynar Ventura]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_raynar.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Ashmoor]]","territory":"[[Ashmoor]]","district":"[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]","faction":"[[Loyalist Guard]]","role":"Associate to [[The Duke]]","chapters":["02 - Ghosts On The Waves","04 - Glowing Darkness"],"tags":["character","loyalist","military","ashmoor","antagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:00:01"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_raynar.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Ashmoor]]" territory: "[[Ashmoor]]" district: "[[ASHMOOR#The Silo|The Silo]]" faction: "[[Loyalist Guard]]" role: "Associate to [[The Duke]]" chapters: - 02 - Ghosts On The Waves - 04 - Glowing Darkness tags: - character - loyalist - military - ashmoor - antagonist - stillborn-star --- # RAYNAR VENTURA > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[raynar.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Associate to The Duke **Alias/Nickname:** The Snake in the Grass **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Slimy **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 51 **Height:** 5'11" **Weight:** 158 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Associate **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I don’t need a weapon. I need a whisper. One well-placed truth does more damage than any bullet ever could.”

No one remembers where Raynar Ventura came from — and those who claim to are probably lying. Some say he was once a street magician in the ashes of Old Chicago. Others swear he was a bureaucrat before the bomb, cataloguing death tolls and hoarding water credits. What is known is that Raynar thrives in power vacuums. And Disgraceland is one big vacuum waiting to be filled. Raynar has no official rank. No uniform. No title beyond the vague and terrifying: “[[The Duke]]’s Listener.” But everyone knows who he is — the man in black with the smirk, the notebook, and the voice that never rises above a whisper. He walks freely between every region in [[DISGRACELAND]]. [[Territories/Steeltown]], [[GUTTER ROW]], even the edges of [[The Drownlands]] — always smiling, always listening. He’ll trade sugar with farmers in [[Threshton]], drink rotgut with pirates on [[Rustwater Bay]], and promise favors he has no intention of fulfilling. Because Raynar’s greatest weapon is information, and his loyalty belongs only to the man who pays him best — currently, that’s The Duke. But not even [[The Duke]] trusts him. Not really. Raynar has hundreds of informants, from desperate children to well-placed guards, all paid in Slugs, secrets, or future promises. He refers to them as “his little ears.” Some whisper for him out of fear, others out of greed. But no one ever meets Raynar twice the same way. Sometimes he's pleasant. Sometimes chilling. Always writing something in that black notebook, which no one's ever seen him part with. He’s in his late forties, slim and sharp, dressed in black like he's in permanent mourning for a world that never loved him back. His mustache is pencil-thin, his hair tighter than his smile. Some think he's a coward. Others think he’s untouchable. The truth is somewhere in between — because Raynar has survived this long by never being anywhere long enough to get shot. Colt despises him. Rottwyler has threatened him openly. [[Emily Burton]] can’t stand his stare. And yet… none of them dare cross him, because Raynar knows something on everyone. And when the walls begin to crumble, Raynar Ventura won’t be crushed beneath them. He’ll already be halfway to the next regime. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, sly, and unfazed — Raynar is never rattled, always watching, and speaks in a tone that makes even confessions sound polite. **Vices:** Manipulation for pleasure. He doesn’t just gather secrets — he _plays_ them, pitting people against each other like it’s a private game of dominoes. **Abilities:** Master manipulator, expert in surveillance, persuasion, and social camouflage. He can blend into any crowd, extract truths with a smile, and disappear before the fallout lands. **Secrets:** Hidden in the spine of his infamous black notebook is a single, yellowed photograph — a woman and child no one has ever seen, names scratched out. He never looks at it, but he always knows it’s there. **Beliefs:** Nothing lasts but leverage. Raynar doesn’t believe in sides, only in survival — and survival belongs to those who know _everything_ before it matters. ## Role In Disgraceland **Raynar Ventura** is Disgraceland’s whisper broker — a ghost in black who walks between factions, gathering power through silence and ink. He doesn’t rule, command, or fight… but when the dust clears, he’ll be the one holding the receipts.

# Overview of Religions in Disgraceland:



### **[[Church of the Ember Saint]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** This is the **wealthiest and most widespread faith** in Disgraceland. It reveres the **Ember Saint**, a legendary figure who braved fire to save hundreds during the Burning of Prattia, an ancient city. Followers believe that **suffering is a forge**, through which the faithful emerge stronger, and that fire purifies without destroying. **Service to others is sacred**, while hoarding wealth or power is considered heresy.
- **Practices & Traditions:** They follow the **Ember Book** of parables and conduct **Rites of Passing** where the dead are cremated and a single ember is given to the family. Monthly, they light communal fires on **Ember Day** for storytelling and sharing food, and hold a **Saint’s March** with lanterns on the anniversary of the Great Fire.
- **Symbols:** The **Burning Halo** (a golden ring of flame) and the **Unburned Hand** (a palm surrounded by stylized fire).
- **Structure:** Before the Water Wards they were led by the **High Flame (Pontiff)**, chosen from the **Council of Embers** (senior clergy), with **Redrobes** serving as priests/priestesses, and **Lay Faithful** as everyday followers. Today it's an unorganized religion.
- **Influence:** Their cathedrals, even if ruined, remain **symbols of hope**. Ember celebrations unite people, including non-believers. Figures like [[Bobby Cutman]], [[Dusty Dillon]], and the Murray family members (Marco, Rosa, Francis, Nico) are listed as followers.
- **Relationships:** They are **bitter rivals** with the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] and **somewhat opposed** to the [[Faith of Mirella]] due to differing elemental outlooks (fire vs. earth). They have **strong mutual respect** with the Faith of [[El Santo]].

### **[[Faith of Mirella]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** This is an **ancient, secretive, and feared** faith tied to swamps, bogs, and shadowed waters. Followers believe the world itself recoiled from mankind's violence, and the sleeping goddess **Mirella (the Sleeping Mother)** waits for women to reclaim what was lost. **Men are considered dangerous, expendable, or cursed** by birth. The faith emphasizes **prophecy, visions, and blood rites**, believing Mirella’s dreams shape fate and her will is revealed through them.
- **Practices & Traditions:** Initiates wear **black veils** as a symbol of mourning, secrecy, and solidarity. They conduct **Dream Rites** involving herbs, chanting, and bloodletting, and perform an **Offering** on each new moon by letting blood fall into the swamp. The dead are returned to the earth in **unmarked graves** near water or roots.
- **Symbols:** The **Gold Bird** (a stylized golden bird on a black background) and **Tangled Roots** (marked in chalk or blood).
- **Structure:** Led by a **Prophet (currently [[Prophet Veerah|Veerah]])**, who is believed to channel Mirella’s will. Elite followers are the **Unseen Widows** (assassins, spies, ritual law keepers), with **Sisters** as ordinary faithful. Men are rarely trusted and never included in inner circles.
- **Influence:** Their influence spreads quietly, often among the desperate and wronged. **The Drownlands** is their largest and most sacred sanctuary. Even [[The Duke]]’s men avoid crossing the Widows. [[Prophet Veerah]] had a vision of "creatures of metal and flesh" that she interprets as a war Mirella wants the Widows to stop.
- **Relationships:** They **distrust** the Word of the Stillborn Star. They are **openly opposed** to the [[Church of the Ember Saint]]. They mostly **ignore** [[El Santo]]'s followers.

### **Faith of [[El Santo]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** More than a religion, it's the **pulse of Disgraceland’s working class, fighters, and survivors**. It honors grit, resilience, and justice earned with blood. **El Santo**, the Masked Saint, is believed to battle darkness in the underworld, with his spirit rising in every act of courage. **Justice is personal**, found in action, loyalty, and honor, rather than corrupt law. **Pain, bruises, scars, and broken bones are sacred marks** of survival.
- **Practices & Traditions:** Every follower owns a **mask**. After fights, combatants participate in the **Brotherhood of Bruises** to share drinks and bless wounds. They hold **Vigil Matches** where a champion fights for truth, and an annual **Day of the Last Bell** for remembrance and sparring. The **Noche de Lucha** tournament, held every four years, is the heart of their culture.
- **Symbols:** The **Mask** (white, silver, or gold) and **Bruised Knuckles**.
- **Structure:** The spiritual head is the **[[Grand Mascara]]**, with the **Grand Luchador** ([[Noche de Lucha]] champion) as a spiritual icon. The **Senior Enmascarados** are a secretive council who remain powerful figures in the religion.
- **Influence:** This faith is the **"glue" in [[Steeltown]]** and a beacon across Disgraceland, with even rivals showing up for Noche de Lucha. All training grounds and gyms are considered sacred. Many members of the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] follow this faith.
- **Relationships:** They are sometimes rivals, sometimes allies with the [[Word of the Stillborn Star]], and have **strong mutual respect** with the [[Church of the Ember Saint]]. They have little direct overlap with the Faith of Mirella.
