(cont'd) ### **[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]**
- **Core Beliefs:** This is the **oldest organized religion** in Disgraceland, dating back to ancient times. It revolves around **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star]]**, an ancient dead sun that slumbers beyond mortal sight. Believers see all things in cycles destined to fade and restart when Galliah awakens. **Silence is holy**, and truth is found in what is _not_ said. They believe in a **Great Reset** where Galliah will "ignite" and burn everything to ash to start a new cycle.
- **Practices & Traditions:** They observe the **Silence Hour** (meditation at dusk) and swear **Ash Oaths** over cold ashes. On the first new moon, they hold a **Star Vigil**, and adherents often take a second name with an "-ah" or "-en" suffix after the Rite of Stillness.
- **Symbols:** The **Unlit Star** (a black circle with a faint lavender halo) and **Chains of Renewal** (interlocking rings).
- **Structure:** Led by the **First Stillborn** (living prophet), who channels Galliah’s will and appoints **Speakers** (local religious heads).
- **Influence:** The **Disgraceland calendar was originally structured by Stillborn priests**, and many laws about contracts, death, and inheritance stem from their traditions. Many high-ranking Loyalists and figures associated with [[The Duke]], such as [[Emily Burton]], [[General Colt]], Mayor [[Gorren Brile]], [[Jacoban Clay]], [[Morris Gable]], [[Raynar Ventura]], [[Sgt. Rottwyler]], [[Soria Langston-Clay]], [[Tyren Will]], and [[Warren Scottyard]], are followers.
- **Relationships:** They are **bitter rivals** with the [[Church of the Ember Saint]]. They have **little direct conflict** with the [[Faith of Mirella]]. They view [[El Santo]]'s faith as a regional offshoot or heresy.

It's clear that while some religions are more common among the ruling class (Word of the Stillborn Star), others resonate more with the working class and those in rebellion (Faith of El Santo, Church of the Ember Saint).

NOTE TITLE: [[Riley Thorne]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"quest","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_riley.png","religion":"[[Faith of Mirella]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[The Drownlands]]","territory":"[[The Drownlands]]","faction":"[[Unseen Widows]]","role":"Protector of [[Prophet Veerah]]","chapters":["05 - Sight Unseen"],"tags":["character","widow","stealth","assassin","mirella","chapter5"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 14:02:53"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: quest NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_riley.png religion: "[[Faith of Mirella]]" status: Alive location: "[[The Drownlands]]" territory: "[[The Drownlands]]" faction: "[[Unseen Widows]]" role: "Protector of [[Prophet Veerah]]" chapters: - 05 - Sight Unseen tags: - character - widow - stealth - assassin - mirella - chapter5 --- # RILEY THORNE > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[riley.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Widow Blade **Alias/Nickname:** Ghost Knife **Home Location:** [[The Drownlands]] **Public Reputation:** Known in whispers only **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** None **Age:** Approx. mid-20s **Height:** 5'6" **Weight:** 120 lbs. **Date of Birth:** Unknown **Occupation:** Stealth operative, assassin **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Unseen Widows]] **Known Associates:** [[Prophet Veerah]], other Widows **Faith:** [[Faith of Mirella]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

"Some people were born to fight. I was born to disappear."

Riley Thorne’s life was marked by loss before she could fully understand it. Born to a scavenger mother in the decaying wastelands of Disgraceland, she spent her earliest years rummaging through the bones of the old world. Her mother, fierce and resourceful, did her best to shield Riley from the brutal reality of the Duke’s rule. But no one could stay hidden forever. When Riley was just ten, her mother was captured and publicly executed by the Duke’s enforcers for stealing from one of the regime’s supply convoys. The image of her mother’s lifeless body swinging from the gallows burned into Riley’s memory, igniting a hatred that never cooled. Alone and afraid, Riley learned to survive by vanishing into the shadows. The ruins of the past became her refuge — broken concrete towers and rusted steel skeletons offering concealment. She scavenged scraps of food and salvaged discarded tools, slowly honing her skills. Over the years, whispers of rebellion reached her ears. Small pockets of resistance, desperate to overthrow the Duke, began to stir. By her late teens, Riley had aligned herself with one such group, using her stealth and cunning to sabotage supply lines and strike fear into the regime. But her actions earned her powerful enemies. During a high-stakes assassination attempt on one of the Duke’s top commanders, Riley was captured and left for dead, her body battered and broken. Yet death did not claim her. It was Veerah, enigmatic leader of the Unseen Widows, who found Riley on the brink of her end. Under Veerah’s care, Riley recovered. The Widows offered her something she hadn't known since her mother’s death — a family. With them, she became a weapon of silent vengeance. Her skill with daggers and short blades grew unmatched, and her ability to move unseen became legendary. Though she serves the Widows with loyalty, a lingering doubt remains. While Veerah’s visions guide the faction’s every step, Riley cannot shake the unease that comes with blind faith. She remains stoic and guarded, her heart still burdened by the weight of the past. Despite the blood she has spilled, there is still a spark of compassion within her. Riley fiercely protects her sisters in the Widows, seeing reflections of herself in the broken women Veerah has gathered. But as tensions rise in Disgraceland and the Duke’s hold tightens, Riley finds herself at a crossroads. Vengeance once defined her, but now she questions whether there is more to fight for. The path forward is uncertain, but one truth remains — Riley Thorne is not done surviving. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Riley is cold on the outside, simmering beneath with quiet intensity. She speaks little, listens much, and watches always. Distrustful by nature, she trusts only those who've bled beside her. Her loyalty, once earned, is absolute — but rarely given. **Vices:** Sleeplessness. Nightmares keep her awake, and when they don’t, she refuses rest out of guilt. She sharpens her blades obsessively, a ritual of control. Distrusts comfort. **Abilities:** Elite stealth operative. Master of knives and short blades. Can vanish in plain sight. Deep intuition for traps, movement, and enemy intent. Skilled in sabotage and infiltration. **Secrets:** Doesn’t fully believe in Veerah’s visions — and sometimes thinks about leaving. Still keeps a piece of her mother’s scarf hidden in her gear. **Beliefs:** Faith in Mirella, but more as metaphor than god. Believes in survival. In sisterhood. In making the powerful bleed. ## Role In Disgraceland Riley Thorne serves as one of the Widows' deadliest field agents — their silent blade, sent when the mission calls for precision, patience, and vanishing without a trace. She does not preach. She does not lead. She kills. And yet her actions hold weight among the Widows, especially the younger ones who look to her as proof that survival and strength are possible after tragedy. Where Veerah brings faith, Riley brings grit. Where Veerah inspires awe, Riley inspires caution. She is the shadow to the Prophet’s light — unseen, but always there.

“I don’t need to shout. The pavement hears me just fine.”

**Rodney Blythe** doesn’t talk much. He doesn’t need to. His silence speaks volumes, and his fists do the rest. Built like a slab of steel and just as unyielding, Rodney is the wall you want between your people and the storm. Once a prisoner in the Duke’s forced labor camps, Rodney spent years beneath rubble and ash, hauling wreckage from bombed-out ruins. When a collapse left him buried alive, he clawed his way out. That moment — his rebirth — made him harder than any iron he ever lifted. The Crew found him broken but breathing. [[Abel May Jr.]] saw a survivor, not a stranger, and vouched for him. Since then, Rodney has never wavered. His word is rare, but his loyalty is absolute. As Road Captain, he’s the one who gets them home. He leads convoys through danger, enforces discipline, and settles disputes with his bare hands. If Jimmy is the spirit, and Mark is the voice, Rodney is the spine. Without him, the Crew would buckle under its own weight. He’s not without ghosts — and he never speaks of the past. But in quiet moments, a bent dog tag hidden in his vest says everything he won’t. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Steady, focused, and silent — Rodney listens first, acts second, and regrets nothing. **Vices:** Carries his guilt like weight on his back — never complains, never lets it go. **Abilities:** Route strategist, convoy lead, close-combat specialist — Rodney plans like a general and hits like a truck. **Secrets:** A dog tag hidden in his vest once belonged to someone who didn’t make it out. He checks it before every ride. **Beliefs:** Strength is protection, not power. Loyalty is a language. And the road is sacred — you never abandon the ride, or the riders. ## Role In Disgraceland **Rodney Blythe** is the Wrecking Crew’s steel spine — the Road Captain who guides the charge, clears the path, and brings the warriors home.

NOTE TITLE: [[Rosa Murray]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_rosa.png","religion":"[[Church of the Ember Saint]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","territory":"[[GUTTER ROW]]","district":"[[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]","faction":"[[Murray Boys]]","role":"[[Marco Murray]]'s Wife, [[Jimmy Douglass]]'s ex","chapters":["04 - Glowing Darkness"],"tags":["character","antagonist","murray","chapter04"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 13:54:18"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_rosa.png religion: "[[Church of the Ember Saint]]" status: Alive location: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" territory: "[[GUTTER ROW]]" district: "[[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]" faction: "[[Murray Boys]]" role: "[[Marco Murray]]'s Wife, [[Jimmy Douglass]]'s ex" chapters: - 04 - Glowing Darkness tags: - character - antagonist - murray - chapter04 --- # ROSA MURRAY > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[rosa.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Treasurer in the [[Murray Boys]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Enforcer **Home Location:** Vileby, [[Gutter Row]] **Public Reputation:** Cougar **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** [[Marco Murray]] **Age:** 39 **Height:** 5'7" **Weight:** 131 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 19th of Greensun, 2141 **Occupation:** Treasurer for the Murray Boys **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Murray Boys]] **Known Associates:** [[Marco Murray]], [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Gorren Brile]], [[Cricket Granger]], [[Jacoban Clay]], [[Soria Langston-Clay]] **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Men start fires. Women decide who gets burned.”

Rosa grew up on the tough streets of [[Steeltown]], the daughter of a steelworker and a mother who ruled the house with iron discipline. She learned to hold her own early—fighting with boys, taking dares, and running wild with her neighborhood crew. [[Jimmy Douglass]] was one of those kids—her first crush, her first fistfight, maybe even her first real heartbreak. When her family moved to [[Charspire]] at sixteen so her father could work the mines, Rosa had to start over. Charspire was meaner, colder, but Rosa was tougher. She waited tables, hustled, and quickly learned the rules of survival. That’s when she met [[Marco Murray]]—older, sharp, protective, and with a loneliness that matched her own. They married within a year. Sixteen years later, Rosa isn’t just Marco’s wife—she’s his most trusted partner and the backbone of the [[Murray Boys]]. She handles the books, smooths over deals, keeps the officials happy, and makes sure nobody in the crew gets sloppy. She knows where every slug is hidden and isn’t afraid to put someone in their place—politely, or not. Rosa is fiercely loyal to Marco, but there’s still a little corner of her heart reserved for memories of [[Jimmy Douglass]]. Old letters, faded photos, and silent “what ifs” she’ll never speak aloud. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Confident, poised, and unflappable. Rosa has nerves of steel and a razor-sharp tongue when needed. She’s warm and protective with her family, but icy and formidable when the business calls for it. **Vices:** Red wine, classic soul records, and the thrill of keeping secrets. She loves expensive shoes and occasionally bets big at the tables—she always bets on herself. **Abilities:** Expert with numbers, master at reading people, and has an instinct for danger. Rosa can bluff her way through any situation, and nobody’s ever caught her in a lie. **Secrets:** She keeps an old photograph of her and [[Jimmy Douglass]] tucked away. Sometimes she discreetly tips Jimmy off if it won’t put Marco at risk. She’s also stashing money on the side—just in case she ever needs a quick exit. **Beliefs:** Family comes first. Loyalty is earned, every single day. Never let anyone see you bleed. ## Role In Disgraceland Rosa Murray is the [[Murray Boys]]’ silent power—everyone who matters knows she’s the one who keeps the operation smooth, the books clean, and the local politicians loyal. She’s the calm in the storm and the last word in any crisis.

The only newspaper in circulation in Disgraceland. role: Owner of the [[Tribucia Tribute]] chapters: - tags: - character - individual - protagonist - news - ember-saint --- # ROYCE SINCAYD > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[royce.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Owner & Editor of the [[Tribucia Tribute]] **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** Dog City, [[CHARSPIRE]] **Public Reputation:** Well-liked **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** **Age:** 60 **Height:** 5'9" **Weight:** 154 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 23rd of Frostsun, 2126 **Occupation:** Owner of the [[Tribucia Tribute]] **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** **Known Associates:** **Faith:** [[Church of the Ember Saint]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“Sometimes survival means knowing when to hit 'delete' instead of 'print.'”

Once a firebrand of post-war journalism, **Royce Sincayd** founded the *[[Tribucia Tribute]]* with nothing but a broken printing press, a pocket full of ink cartridges, and a vision: truth above all. In the early years after the Long Winter, he was revered as a voice of resistance and integrity — exposing corruption, giving voice to the starving, and holding fledgling regional powers accountable. But time wears on even the sharpest ideals. Decades of veiled threats, missing colleagues, and slow, suffocating pressure from [[The Duke]] chipped away at Royce’s resolve. These days, he still calls the shots in the newsroom, but everyone knows the *Tribute* won't publish anything directly negative about The Duke. He tells himself it’s survival. That it’s better to bend than break. He walks the halls of his paper with an old man’s limp and a heavy conscience, watching as younger, hungrier reporters like [[Rachel Gold]] test the boundaries he no longer has the strength to push. The presses still roll. But what they print isn’t always the truth anymore — just the truth he’s allowed to tell. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Measured, weary, calculating. Royce used to speak in fire; now he speaks in sighs. **Vices:** Cheap cigars, self-pity, and willful ignorance when it suits him. **Abilities:** Master editor and political survivor. Knows how to shape a story — or bury it. **Secrets:** Keeps a locked drawer of unpublished exposés, including a damning file on [[Jacoban Clay]] and internal TTV memos. He may have been directly warned by [[The Duke]] years ago — and caved. **Beliefs:** Still believes in truth, deep down. But believes more in staying alive to print another day. ## Role In Disgraceland A once-proud truth-teller turned compromised gatekeeper of the press. His silence props up The Duke as much as his old words once challenged him. ## Appearances

History of the Rustwater Raiders
>

“Stormborn. Steel-fed. No graves on water.”

The [[Rustwater Raiders]] are Disgraceland’s most infamous aquatic marauders, their black sails a harbinger of violence and smoke. Born from betrayal and bound by blood, they sail where no one else dares, feeding on fear and salt. Captain [[Lyla Bonetooth]] forged the Raiders from chaos. Her mutiny aboard a government patrol ship lit the first fire — when she seized the vessel and rechristened it [[The Black Marauder]], the era of the Raiders began. What followed was a campaign of calculated terror: raiding settlements, destroying convoys, and rewriting the rules of power in the bay. Beside her sails the stone-faced [[Blacktide Cray]], a man said to have drowned once and clawed his way back. And behind the captain’s smile is [[Silas Vayne]], the crew’s voice in foreign waters and their dagger in the dark. [[Zadie Adeyemi]] and [[Darius Adeyemi]], siblings with secrets, fuel the Raiders' dominance through invention, sabotage, and strategy. [[Salt-Eye Marlow]] — once a killer-for-hire, now a killer-by-oath — ensures discipline through violence. Their reach spans far past the deck of the Marauder. They rule invisible harbors and hidden ports, unmarked on any map but whispered of in terror. No fortress is safe, no merchant unwatched. Even the [[The Duke]] treads lightly when the Raiders loom. Their code is brutal: freedom at all costs, and loyalty unto death. Mutiny is met with blades. Weakness is thrown to the sea. But loyalty? Loyalty is treasure — and Captain Bonetooth rewards it with spoils and survival. The Raiders live without chains. No kings. No borders. Just the wind, the blade, and the endless blue. And still they sail — through mist and myth, leaving legends in their wake. ---

## Biography

> “I don’t need to raise my voice. The room already belongs to me.”

**Sable Marris** grew up on the _rich edge of ruin_ — the daughter of a failed merchant who taught her two things before skipping town: how to count money, and how to count men. She learned to fend for herself early, moving through [[Vileby]]’s backdoor lounges and dust-shack casinos with poise and heat, using words as weapons and silk as armor. But she was never just chasing a man — she was chasing a throne.

Then came **Samson Knight**. She didn’t beg for his attention. She caught it. And held it. What started as mutual amusement turned to something more dangerous: trust.

Sable is the one woman who can speak plainly to Mr. Knight without drawing fire. She doesn’t walk behind him — she walks beside him, dressed to kill and twice as sharp. While the world sees her as a trophy of his empire, those who know better realize: she helps shape it.

Behind the scenes, Sable acts as a silent advisor, an event planner, and a social manipulator. She knows how to read power structures like blueprints. She knows who to bribe, who to blackmail, and when to disappear. She doesn’t pull the trigger, but she picks the target.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Graceful, deliberate, and iron-willed. Never loud, always heard.

**Vices:** 
Jewelry, red wine, slow jazz, and perfectly timed revenge.

**Abilities:** 
Influence, information gathering, manipulation. Knows how to break men using words alone.

**Secrets:** 
Keeps detailed records on every deal Knight has ever made — and a backup copy hidden outside the city.

**Beliefs:** 
Power is more beautiful when it’s quiet. Comfort is earned. And no man rules alone.

## Role in Disgraceland
Sable Marris is the unspoken empress of Samson Knight’s world — the velvet whisper behind his iron presence, helping him rule Gutter Row with subtlety, glamour, and cold precision.

“I see clearer than the ones who build thrones. I see what waits behind the mirror. And brother… it’s already moving.”

No one knows where **Salem Quinn** was born, and he doesn't offer the story. Some say he was once a scholar in the Old Capitol, a physician-psychic hybrid whose insight was so precise it bordered on supernatural. Others claim he emerged from the Ash Dunes after the Tetra Bomb fell, eyes burned shut by divine wrath. What is known is this: he walks north, alone, wearing the same blood-red suit and carrying a gold-handled cane that never strikes a pebble wrong. His eyes are pale, milked-over, but unscarred. He is blind — completely — yet he never stumbles. Salem’s visions began long before the world was cracked open. He saw fire in the skies as a boy. Saw fields drown, people vanish, and cities become bones. He didn’t understand them then. He tried to ignore them. Tried to live small, quiet. But the visions didn’t stop — they sharpened. Became louder. Now they come in fits, in dreams, in static whispers between heartbeats. Sometimes they leave him convulsing. Sometimes just weeping. He keeps walking anyway. He has no faction, no banners, no weapons. And yet wherever he goes, people move aside. Even gang lords and smugglers hush their tongues when he passes. In every town between **Gutter Row** and **Ashmoor**, someone always recognizes him. They call him _The Blind Seer_, or _The Walking Warning_. Children bring him water. Elders beg him for insight. He answers rarely, and only in riddles. But Quinn isn’t wandering. He’s on a mission — one only he seems to fully understand. His goal is singular: gain an audience with **[[The Duke of Disgraceland]]**. To stand before the tyrant in his Silo throne and deliver the words that burn behind his blind eyes. Whether the message is salvation or damnation, even Quinn isn’t sure. But he knows this: if the Duke ignores it, something worse than war is coming. Some say Salem has met **[[Veerah]]**, the prophet of the Unseen Widows, and that the two shared a vision that nearly broke them both. Others whisper that Salem already knows how Disgraceland ends — he’s just giving the world a chance to prove him wrong. --- ## Personality > [!infobox] > > ![[sqq.png|300]] **Temperament:** Quiet. Unshakably calm. His words come slow, each one measured like they cost something. He doesn’t argue. He just speaks — and lets the silence do the rest. **Vices:** None apparent. He neither eats in public nor asks for shelter. Some swear he walks barefoot through snow and glass. Others say he weeps blood when no one is watching. Truth is, nobody’s sure where he sleeps… or if he sleeps at all. **Abilities:** Blind, yet walks without assistance — even through minefields and ruins. Receives visions in dreams or seizures — often apocalyptic, symbolic, or maddeningly cryptic. Can sense a person’s emotional state through voice and posture alone. **Secrets:** Has seen visions of the Tetra bomb before it fell. Shares a psychic resonance with [[Veerah]] — though neither one fully understands it. - His blindness may not be natural. Rumors suggest it was _taken_ from him — as payment. **Beliefs:** Disgraceland’s time is nearly up ## Role In Disgraceland **Salem Quinn** is a prophet out of time — a man blind to the world, yet cursed to see too much. He travels slowly but purposefully, walking from the rot of [[GUTTER ROW]] toward the tyranny of [[Ashmoor]], seeking one thing: an audience with [[The Duke]]. His message is unknown, but the look on his face suggests it’s already too late. ## Appearances

“They all scream the same in the end. Some just take longer to get there.”

Salt-Eye Marlow is what happens when survival forgets to bring a conscience. Bald, hulking, and half-blind, he walks the Black Marauder like a ghost who never learned how to die. His milky eye gave him the name — the stories gave him the fear. He once served another crew. That crew no longer exists. After a failed stand against Lyla Bonetooth’s Raiders, Marlow knelt in the blood of his comrades and offered to switch sides. Lyla said yes… but only after he slit their throats himself. He did it with a smile. Now, Salt-Eye is the Raiders’ mad dog — the one they keep leashed until a message needs sending or a body needs breaking. He laughs through executions, jokes mid-interrogation, and collects trophies from those he’s put down — teeth, fingers, tags. Nobody knows what the trophies mean. Maybe not even him. He’s loyal to Lyla, but not because of belief. Because she lets him _be_. And in a world that chews up outcasts like him, that’s the closest thing he’s got to religion. Even Silas Vayne keeps a wary eye on him. Because while Salt-Eye might be a dog… nobody knows who he’ll bite next. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Unstable, gleefully violent, and always grinning. Marlow is the kind of man who whistles while flaying someone. **Vices:** Betrayal, sadism, chaos. He lives for the breaking point — yours, not his. **Abilities:** Master of close-quarters brutality and bloodletting. Pain doesn’t deter him — it feeds him. He tracks wounded targets by scent and finishes them slow. **Secrets:** Keeps trophies from kills and whispers to them. Rumors say he’s making a list — or maybe it’s a prayer. Or a tally. No one wants to ask. **Beliefs:** Life has no rules. Codes are chains. Survival is the only gospel — and Lyla Bonetooth is the first person to ever give him freedom instead of a cage. ## Role In Disgraceland **Salt-Eye Marlow** is the Raiders’ nightmare unleashed — the one you send to prove a point. He’s not trusted. He’s not liked. But when you need to paint a deck red, he’s the brush.

## Biography

> “If you step into my market, you play by my math. You don’t like the numbers? Don’t come back.”


**Samson Knight**, known across Gutter Row as **Mr. Knight**, is the commanding leader of [[Third Row]] — the dominant street gang that controls the heart of the [[Three Nail Market]] in [[Vileby]]. A towering, broad-shouldered Black man with a clipped beard and eyes that don’t blink when they should, Samson carries the aura of someone who’s seen the worst and decided to become worse.

Born in a crumbling tenement on Row Three sometime in the 2150s, Samson was raised amid violence, ration lines, and betrayal. His mother worked market tables, his father disappeared during the Charspire riots, and by thirteen Samson was already known as a quiet enforcer who didn’t need to yell to make you fold. He climbed the ranks of the gang as muscle, but when the founders fell — Eddie to a back-alley bullet and Shad to the chaos of the [[Blackshift Massacre]] — he didn’t grieve. He moved.

In the fractured years that followed, when The Third Row splintered into infighting and ruin, Samson played a long game. He killed who he had to. Paid who he couldn’t. And whispered unity until it became law. By 2178, there was no one left to challenge him — not in the gang, not in the market.

Today, Mr. Knight runs the Three Nail Market like a quiet king. He doesn’t yell, doesn’t flinch, and doesn’t forget. He counts slugs by the firelight in the backrooms of bloodstained buildings, surrounded by killers who owe him their lives — or fear losing them.

## Personality

**Temperament:** 
Calm, calculating, immovable; speaks slowly but hits fast. Keeps control through presence, not theatrics.

**Vices:** 
Money, memory, and power — and maybe a taste for control that goes deeper than business.

**Abilities:** 
Expert at organization, intimidation, and maintaining order through layered fear. Brilliant strategist with unmatched street knowledge of Gutter Row.

**Secrets:** 
Keeps a black-bound book of names — debts owed, promises broken, and things that can't be forgiven. Some say it includes [[The Duke of Disgraceland]].

**Beliefs:** 
Loyalty is earned in blood. Money is the only true voice in Disgraceland. The past is a weapon — sharpen it.

## Role in Disgraceland
Samson Knight is the silent king of the streets, holding together the underworld economy of Gutter Row while ensuring the Three Nail Market stays open, profitable, and absolutely his.

@ [-300~250] Yayoi Period

“Every scream's got its own note, you just gotta listen close. Some of 'em? Real pretty.”

**[[Scumbag]]** is an open wound walking. Nobody knows his real name, and nobody asks. He’s one of Gutter Row’s most feared creatures — a man so utterly depraved that even the hardened slavers of Three Nail Market cross the street when they see him. He’s not a crime boss, not even a proper gang member. He’s a wildcard, a freak, and a sadist. He walks with a swagger soaked in blood and shit, because nobody’s ever put him down for good. He’s raped, murdered, mutilated, and laughed through it all. Cops? He mocks them. The market bosses? He spits in their stalls. Loyalist Guard? He disappears into the grime like a cockroach when they come sniffing, then reappears days later like nothing happened. Some say he cuts deals. Others say he knows things. But the truth is simpler: the city’s rotted, and it lets its worst creatures live so long as they cause the right kind of chaos. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Wildly unstable. He swings from eerie calm to maniacal frenzy in seconds. He talks to himself, to objects, to shadows. Everything’s a joke to him — especially pain. He loves to toy with people psychologically before unleashing violence. **Vices:** All of them. He indulges in sadism, rape, mutilation, torture, arson, cannibalism, and drug abuse — particularly Luxyn. He also collects “trophies” from his victims: fingers, eyeballs, tongues. Keeps them in his coat pockets like candy. **Abilities:** Extremely agile and fast in close quarters. Masters unpredictability — throws off even seasoned fighters. Savvy with hiding, blending in, and escaping. Pain tolerance is off the charts, almost inhuman **Secrets:** He’s killed multiple Loyalist officers, but their deaths were covered up to avoid panic. **Beliefs:** He believes the world ended after the Tetra bomb, and everything now is a twisted afterlife. There is no right or wrong, just _performance._ People are meat with makeup. Pain is the only truth. He thinks [[The Grim Man]] is a bedtime story, a joke — but a _funny one._ ## Role In Disgraceland **[[Scumbag]]** is the unpunished evil that everyone endures. He haunts Gutter Row as a symbol of the regime’s failure — or complicity. His existence dares someone, anyone, to rise up and stop him. But no one has. Yet. ## Appearances > - [[Hymn From A Dead Girl]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Selena Matissao]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":"journal","NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_selena.png","religion":"[[El Santo]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Steeltown]]","territory":"[[Steeltown]]","district":"[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]","faction":"[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","role":"Woman of Mayhem for the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]","chapters":["01 - Main Event Shadows","06 - Showdown In Gage Park"],"tags":["character","protagonist","steeltown","wrecking_crew","el-santo","chapter06"],"created":"2025/05/05 19:34:07","modified":"2025/06/03 10:43:20"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: journal NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_selena.png religion: "[[El Santo]]" status: Alive location: "[[Steeltown]]" territory: "[[Steeltown]]" district: "[[Steeltown#Gage Park|Gage Park]]" faction: "[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" role: "Woman of Mayhem for the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]" chapters: - 01 - Main Event Shadows - 06 - Showdown In Gage Park tags: - character - protagonist - steeltown - wrecking_crew - el-santo - chapter06 --- # SELENA MATISSAO > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[selena.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Woman of Mayhem **Alias/Nickname:** The Phoenix **Home Location:** [[Steeltown]] **Public Reputation:** Feared, admired, elusive **Gender:** Female **Spouse:** Widowed **Age:** 26 **Height:** 5'8" **Weight:** 137 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Scout, Tracker, Raider **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] **Known Associates:** [[Jimmy Douglass]], [[Mark Jeffrey]], [[Rodney Blythe]] **Faith:** [[El Santo]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“They call me The Phoenix like I’m gonna rise from the shadow in the night. But I don’t hide. I walk in the open, so they remember exactly who’s chasing them.”

**Selena Matissao** is not a ghost. She’s the firestorm that comes after the ghosts have fled. Once a wife, now a warrior, she carries her pain like a blade — sharp, precise, and always ready to strike. She lost her husband, Michael, to one of the Duke’s purges. His death was meant as a warning. Instead, it ignited a legend. Selena rose from the ashes of her old life and carved a new path — one soaked in vengeance and marked by justice. She joined the Wrecking Crew not as a victim, but as a predator. They call her _The Phoenix_ because she never stops rising. No matter how much blood she spills, no matter how broken the land becomes, Selena burns forward — fierce, focused, and impossible to stop. She moves through the wilderness like wind through reeds. Her tracking skills are unmatched. Her ability to survive off the grid makes her the Crew’s most valuable scout and assassin. Where others lose the trail, Selena finds it. Though she rarely speaks of it, her bond with [[Mark Jeffrey]] runs deep. There's heat beneath their banter — a tenderness they both fear, yet quietly crave. He grounds her. She sharpens him. Neither knows what comes next, but both understand they won’t face it alone. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Calm, lethal, and calculated — Selena rarely wastes words, and when she acts, it’s with unflinching precision. **Vices:** Obsession with revenge — she pushes herself to the brink chasing ghosts she’s not sure she can ever exorcise. **Abilities:** Master tracker, survivalist, silent killer — she disappears into the wastelands and reemerges with intel, plans… or blood. **Secrets:** Buried beneath a root-tangled tree outside Steeltown is a box holding her wedding ring. She still checks it monthly — not to retrieve it, just to know it’s there. **Beliefs:** Hope must be fought for. Grief must be forged into something sharp. And the land will only heal when its tormentors are gone. --- ## Role In Disgraceland **Selena Matissao** is the silent flame of the Wrecking Crew — a myth made real, a blade made from grief. She doesn’t chase glory. She chases reckoning. > [!rustwater]- Surprise > ![[selenaass.png|600]]

ROTTWYLER > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[rott.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Sargeant of the [[Loyalist Guard]] **Alias/Nickname:** The Dog Faced Gremlin **Home Location:** [[ASHMOOR]] **Public Reputation:** Brutal Military Man **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 41 **Height:** 6'4" **Weight:** 258 lbs. **Date of Birth:** **Occupation:** Sargeant of the Loyalist Guard **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** [[Loyalist Guard]] **Known Associates:** [[The Duke]], [[General Colt]] **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“FINGERS OFF!”

If [[The Duke]] is the mind of Disgraceland, Sgt. Rottwyler is the teeth. A mountain of a man with arms like tree trunks and a chest built for knocking down doors, Rottwyler is the absolute authority over the [[Loyalist Guard]] — the elite, brutal enforcers who maintain the Duke’s grip on the region. He speaks rarely, growls often, and listens never. His every word sounds like it’s been chewed up with gravel. He is feared more than The Duke himself, and that’s just how he likes it. Rottwyler was once a mercenary in the Carbine Wastes before the [[Tetra Bomb]] erased most of his former employers. When the smoke cleared, he rode east with nothing but a pack of ammo, a wounded dog, and a pocket full of Slugs. The Duke found him bloodied, half-starved, and still swinging. Instead of killing him, he offered him rank. Rottwyler never forgot that. His loyalty is absolute. So much so that, in a twisted public ceremony years ago, Rottwyler severed his own left pinky finger as a demonstration of obedience and lifelong service. Now, it’s tradition — every Loyalist must cut off their own pinky to join the Guard. Some faint. Some scream. Rottwyler just watches, cigar clenched between his teeth, eyes cold and unmoved. That cigar? It’s never gone. No one’s ever seen him without it — even when torturing prisoners or training recruits. It's said he lights it with the ashes of traitors. His breath smells like blood, tobacco, and disdain. Rottwyler has no family. No past. His body is all scar tissue and routine. Wake. Train. Patrol. Punish. Sleep. He lifts weights in the courtyard of The Silo every dawn, shirtless, while Loyalists stand in formation around him like statues. Dissent is weakness. Mercy is treason. The Duke is law. But not everyone believes he's unshakable. [[Emily Burton]] once said, in a whisper behind a locked door, “Even dogs break when they’re beaten enough.” --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Unflinching and sadistic — Rottwyler doesn’t speak unless it’s to bark an order, and he enjoys watching fear bloom in a man’s eyes more than he enjoys victory. **Vices:** Pain — giving it, not feeling it. He trains harder than any recruit, punishes weakness without hesitation, and carries an unholy satisfaction in the breaking of bones and spirits. **Abilities:** Near-superhuman strength and pain tolerance; master of close-quarters combat and battlefield tactics. His presence alone can quell riots, and his brutality keeps the Loyalist Guard sharp and afraid. **Secrets:** Beneath his bedframe, wrapped in oilcloth and sealed with wax, is the collar of the dog he rode east with — long dead, buried in Ashmoor's soil. He digs it up every year on the same night, sits with it, and says nothing for hours. **Beliefs:** The chain of command is sacred. The Duke saved his life, and loyalty to him is the only code that matters. Emotion is for corpses. _“Obey, or be buried.”_ ## Role In Disgraceland Sgt. Rottwyler is the iron fist of The Duke’s regime — commander of the Loyalist Guard and enforcer of obedience through sheer terror. Where The Duke speaks of order, Rottwyler ensures it, one broken jaw at a time.

“You’d be surprised how much truth slips out when the lights are low and the drinks are cold.”

A decade ago, **Shana** stepped into **[[GUTTER ROW]]** with nothing but a cracked mirror compact, a bullet scar on her thigh, and the quiet resolve of a woman who'd survived too many men with too many promises. No one knows where she came from. Some say she danced for Loyalists in [[Ashmoor]]. Others whisper she slit a governor’s throat with her garter clasp and never looked back. What’s known is this: she found a rotting tenement at the edge of the Red Light District and turned it into **[[Hollow House]]** — a burlesque lounge, a pleasure den, a confessional in disguise. No neon. No stage lights. Just velvet curtains, bruised perfume, and a firm house code: _her girls come first._ She started with three women — all discarded, wounded, or in hiding. She gave them food, safety, and a cut that didn’t reek of exploitation. Word spread. Quickly. One by one, other women came — runaways, rebels, ex-slaves, ex-killers — and each found more than survival under Shana’s roof. They found **power**. She never advertised. She didn’t need to. **Her name moved through the filth like fire** — the madame who didn’t sell her girls, didn’t let them get hurt, and didn’t care who you were if you broke her rules. Now The [[Hollow House]] is legend. Men come for pleasure. Women come for shelter. Everyone leaves with fewer secrets. And while Gutter Row eats most who try to rise, **Shana thrives**. She’s more than a business owner. She’s **a quiet queen** in a district of rats — red curls, top hat, and eyes that see through silk and lies. She’s got dirt on half the mayors in Disgraceland, and they all know better than to come knocking uninvited. They say The Hollow House is named for what’s left of the people who leave it. But those who stay? They don’t feel hollow. They feel **safe**. And in Gutter Row, that’s a miracle. --- ## Personality > [!infobox] > > ![[shanabeau.png|260]] **Temperament:** Warm smile, sharp mind. She’s velvet on the surface, razors underneath. Knows when to flirt, when to intimidate, and when to vanish. Plays the fool sometimes — just long enough to see who’s stupid enough to believe it. **Vices:** Smokes rare roseleaf tobacco. Has a taste for secrets, good wine, and expensive perfume. Occasionally disappears for days without telling anyone. Always returns sharper than when she left. **Abilities:** Master manipulator, listener, and reader of people. Keeps hidden ledgers tracking debts, favors, lies — not for blackmail, but for survival. Has dirt on _every mayor, gang captain, and Loyalist officer_ who’s stepped into her lounge. Knows what’s coming before it hits the streets. **Secrets:** Has an arrangement with one of the Rustwater Raiders — reason unknown. Keeps a locked room in the back of the lounge. No one enters but her. **Beliefs:** Men think they run the world. They don’t even run their own hands. ## Role In Disgraceland Shana is the flame at the center of the Red Light District — the woman everyone underestimates until it’s too late. She owns and runs the most notorious, tightly controlled burlesque lounge in Gutter Row — a place where bodies dance and lips loosen. She’s not a spy, but she knows **everything**. And that’s why she’s still breathing.

“I’ve slit more throats with a whisper than most men do with steel.”

Silas Vayne is the whisper behind the waves, the man who can make a threat sound like a promise and a death sentence feel like a business deal. Smooth Silas, they call him — not just for his voice, but for how he glides through chaos like a shadow with a smirk. Born to a pair of South American traders who danced the line between legal commerce and smuggling, Silas grew up bartering his way through ports before he ever swung a blade. By the time the Tetra bomb brought fire to the sky, he already knew that survival wasn’t about strength — it was about charm, leverage, and knowing who to betray at the right time. The collapse brought him north, where calmer waters held sharper sharks. He met Lyla Bonetooth aboard the future _Black Marauder_, recognizing a fellow predator with eyes on the helm. When the mutiny came, it was Silas who whispered discontent into the ears of the weak and fearful, making sure their knives were ready before Lyla ever gave the signal. He didn’t just back the rebellion — he orchestrated half of it from the shadows. Now, as her right hand, Silas Vayne is the crew’s voice in foreign ports and backroom deals. Where Lyla enforces order through dread, Silas ensures respect is paid with interest. He smooths over the messes, cuts the final throats, and keeps the crew in line with grins that slice like razors. Silas is a vision of calculated chaos — tattoos sprawled across his chest and arms, waves and serpents winding around a ship caught in a storm. He wears a red bandana slicked with sea sweat and a spiked leather coat that creaks with menace. The man is a contradiction: warm and venomous, inviting and dangerous. He is loyal to Lyla, for now. But ambition roils just beneath the surface. He’s running cons on everyone — even her. Because Silas doesn’t serve forever. He builds empires from whispers, and one day soon, he might just crown himself king of the tide. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Charming, slippery, and unreadable. Silas turns tension into opportunity and never says more than he must. If he's smiling, you're already playing his game. > [!infobox] > > ![[rsl.png|260]] **Vices:** He’s addicted to secrets and the thrill of the con. Lies spill from him easier than breath. He skims from every deal, flirts with betrayal, and gambles with more than gold. **Abilities:** An unmatched manipulator. Whether charming a room or dismantling a mutiny with one whisper, Silas moves unseen until it’s too late. He fights with precision but prefers never to draw steel — words, to him, are sharper. **Secrets:** He’s trading secrets behind Lyla’s back — with Loyalist defectors, rogue Raiders, even old Wreckers. There’s a long con at play, and only Silas knows where it ends. **Beliefs:** Control. It doesn’t matter who commands the ship, so long as Silas is the one steering its fate from behind the curtain. ## Role In Disgraceland **Silas Vayne** is the voice of the _Black Marauder_, the smirk behind the steel. While others fight and bleed, he’s the one shaking hands, signing deals, and deciding who gets to drown. Without him, the Raiders lose their edge.

#  Sliver

> "Luck’s a lie. In *Sliver*, you either *bleed for your win* or you lose with style." — [[Ninepack]]

## 🩸 Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ game of sliver
> ![[sliver.png|450]]

**Sliver** is a rogue-deckbuilder card game born in the underbelly of [[Gutter Row]] and [[Steeltown]]. Inspired by old-world poker but twisted by post-collapse desperation, it's part strategy, part madness.

Some say the game was first played with bones and blood in the [[Three Nail Market]]

---

## 🕹 How to Play

### 🎯 Objective
Build hands to score **Influence** each round. First to **100 Influence** wins. In outlaw variants, the winner takes all—coin, secrets, or lives.

### 👥 Players
2–4 players (standard); up to 6 in high-stakes variants.

### 🃏 Deck Composition

#### Standard Deck (64 cards):
- Suits:
  - **Bones** (Spades)
  - **Ashes** (Clubs)
  - **Blood** (Hearts)
  - **Coin** (Diamonds)
- Ranks: 1–10 per suit
- 4 "Wild" Sliver-backed cards (draw from **Sliver Deck**)

#### Sliver Deck (20 cards):
Unique power cards that warp reality and strategy. Drawn through combos or faction effects.

#### Modifier Deck (30 cards):
Cards that grant permanent or round-limited buffs/debuffs. Includes:
- **Scar Cards** (persistent effects)
- **Rust Cards** (negative mutations)
- **Favor Cards** (faction or character boosts)
- **Dust Cards** (instant plays, volatile)

---

## 🔄 Game Loop

1. **Draw Phase**
   - Each player draws **7 base cards**.
   - If a card or effect allows, draw from the **Sliver Deck** or **Modifier Deck**.

2. **Build Hands**
   - Players arrange their 7 cards into a single **poker-style hand**.
   - Traditional hands apply (Pair, Three-of-a-Kind, Straight, Flush, etc.).
   - Some Sliver or Modifier cards allow players to split into **multiple hands**.

3. **Play Phase**
   - Play up to 2 Sliver or Modifier cards before revealing.
   - Cards may enhance hand strength, add multipliers, or sabotage others.

4. **Reveal Phase**
   - Players reveal hands simultaneously.
   - Hands are scored based on tier + any effects.
   - Highest hand wins the **Influence Pool** for the round.
   - Second-highest earns **1 Influence**, others get nothing.

5. **Burn Phase**
   - All played cards go to discard except Scar and Rust (they persist).
   - Draw back to 7. Repeat.

---

## 🧠 Hand Scoring Example

| Hand Type        | Influence Gain | Notes                                |
|------------------|----------------|--------------------------------------|
| Pair             | +2             | Basic combo                          |
| Two Pair         | +4             | Common early-game score              |
| Three-of-a-Kind  | +6             | Moderate score, combo friendly       |
| Straight         | +8             | Sequential, hard to block            |
| Flush            | +10            | Same suit                            |
| Full House       | +13            | Rare, strong                         |
| Four-of-a-Kind   | +16            | Unlocks special Sliver draw          |
| Straight Flush   | +20            | May trigger **Vision** effects       |
| Bone Royal (10-9-8-7-6, Bones) | +30 | Legendary, rare as sin              |

---

## 💀 Sliver Cards (Drawn Separately)

| Name                        | Effect                                                                 |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **[[The Grim Man]]**        | Destroy lowest scoring card on all other players' hands                |
| **[[Dusty Dillon]]'s Echo** | If you make a Straight, score 1.5x and draw one Modifier next round    |
| **Gable’s Signal**          | Cancel one opponent’s Modifier this round                             |
| **Widow’s Mercy**           | If you lose this round, deal 3 damage to a chosen player’s deck        |
| **Steeltown Switch**        | Swap hands (at random) with one player before reveal                   |
| **Double Duke**             | Your hand score is doubled, but you draw 1 less card next round        |

---

## ☠ Modifier Cards

### Scar Cards (Persistent)

| Name           | Effect                                                            |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Burnt Nerve    | Lowest scoring hand is doubled each round                        |
| Hollow Crown   | Start each game with one Sliver draw                             |
| Bone Tattoo    | Flushes of Bones grant +4 extra Influence                        |

### Rust Cards (Negative)

| Name         | Effect                                                      |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Brittle Deck | Max hand size is reduced by 1                              |
| Flickering Eye | You must reveal your hand early each round               |
| Cracked Memory | You cannot use the same Modifier more than once per game |

---

## 🔥 Culture & Setting

- **Backburn rules** apply in underground games. All modifiers allowed. Real-world stakes often replace Influence.
- Winners may demand weapons, favors, secrets, or blood.
- Famous tables:
  - **The Red Table** in [[GUTTER ROW#Vileby|Vileby]]

## **“SNAKE EYES IN THRESHTON”**  
##### _A B-Side from the End Times_

> At the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]], tensions simmer as the [[Rancher Collective]] grapples with oppressive demands from [[The Duke]] ahead of the extravagant [[Ashmoor Festival]]. When the smooth-talking [[Danny Dandelion]] hints at secret dealings and hidden advantages, longtime skeptic [[Beau DuNoir]] grows suspicious and turns to his uneasy rival, the steadfast [[Turner Anderson]]. Over a game of [[Sliver]]—equal parts strategy and subtext—the two forge a reluctant pact, determined to uncover the truth and protect their own, even if it means confronting betrayal from within.

The sun was bleeding out behind the [[Threshton]] bluffs, and the yard outside the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] buzzed with low murmurs, hoofbeats, and the occasional barked order. Wagons creaked under the weight of bundled feed and crates nailed shut with rusted iron. The air smelled of churned dust, old sweat, and the copper tang of coming tension as the Collective headed for home.

[[Beau DuNoir]] loitered near the water trough, one boot resting on a fence rail, his fingers shuffling a weatherworn deck of [[Sliver]] cards with idle precision. He watched the ebb and flow of ranch hands like a man studying currents before wading in.

From the stable’s shadow, [[Danny Dandelion]] emerged, jacket slung loose over one shoulder, a silver tooth winking when he smiled. [[Beau DuNoir]] straightened.

"Evenin', [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said casually, not looking up from the cards. "Care to cut in for a hand?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] slowed, his gait relaxed, the picture of disinterest. "Temptin'. Real temptin'. But I’ve got irons in the fire. Things that need seein’ to."

"Strange how a man gets busiest right after a meeting," Beau mused, letting the cards flutter between his hands.

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’s grin sharpened just slightly. "You know how it is. Some of us run leaner ops. Gotta stay nimble. Weather’s been rough out east. Lost a chicken coop roof to a dust devil the other day—spun it clean into the neighbor’s well. Damnedest thing."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] smirked. "That so? Heard the only whirlwind you wrestle with is a bottle of rye and a girl named Lottie."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ chuckled. "She broke up with me, said I was too mysterious. Can you believe that?"

"Heartbreaking," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said dryly. "And how’s the ranch otherwise?"

"Oh, flourishing," [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ said, arms wide. "Had a calf born with two heads last week. Named ‘em both Duke."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] barked a laugh, sharp and brief. "You should put that on your labels. Might get you a promotion."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ winked. "Maybe I’ll bring ‘em both to the festival. Let ‘em do tricks."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] eyes [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]], "How you feelin' about the Festival anyway, [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] finished loading up his carriage and turned back to [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]], wiping his hands. "You know how it is, one way or another The Duke is gonna get what he wants. I don't get why Turner and Freddy are so damn adamant on fighting back against the Loyalists every chance they get. We'd all be living easier if those two would drop their self-ritousness and come back down to Tribucia, [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. But I've learned in my years wandering this shit-hole, these things kinda work out as they should, you know?"

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] kept his eyes glued to [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]. "And somehow that always ends up with you on top, eh [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]]? Now you wouldn't be heading off all quick to tell nobody of what was discussed here in a [[Rancher Collective|Collective]] meeting, would you?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’'s smile didn't falter, but his eyes cooled a shade. "[[Beau DuNoir|Mr. DuNoir]], I am shocked and appauled." [[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] said with feigned insult. "I got some old ladies ranch I gotta whip back up into shape, [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. This shit takes time you know? We’re all trying to stay ahead, right? I know you fellas don't like me, but I'm trying here!"

"Sure," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said slowly, slipping a card from the deck and flipping it in a lazy arc. The Jack of Knives landed face-up on the fence rail. "Stayin’ ahead."

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]]’ tipped his hat. "Seeya in [[Ashmoor]], [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. Don’t spend all your luck in one place."

He mounted his horse with the smooth grace of a man who never rushed unless it served a purpose. Beau and Danny held their gaze a little longer than necessary. Within moments, he was a dust-trail heading east.

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] watched until the figure disappeared behind the hills. Then he pocketed the deck, face unreadable. He pulled out a slim pack and removed a cigarette, before turning back toward the ranch house, his boots echoing a silent resolve.

The sunset has given way to a full moon over [[Threshton]], and the wind had quieted into long, sighing breezes that rustled through the dry grass. The lights inside the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] burned low, a scatter of amber behind dusty windows.

[[Turner Anderson]] was just finishing a ledger note when the knock came—three short raps, one deliberate pause, and a fourth. Cautious but curious, he opened the door to find [[Beau DuNoir]] standing there, cigarette stub tucked behind his ear, hat in hand.

"[[Turner Anderson|Turner]]."

"[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]."

"Didn’t figure you’d be asleep yet."

"Wasn’t. Come on in."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] handed [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] a drink half-full and they settled across from each other at the old, wooden kitchen table, a squat candle guttering between them. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] set a chipped sliver board between them without a word, and Beau dealt the opening hands. The pieces clinked gently like old bones.

Silence reigned for the first few rounds. The game was a language of its own: folds and calls, strategic retreats, and calculated risks. [[Sliver]] wasn't poker—it was poker's feral cousin, dragged through blood and ash and rebuilt with bones and desperation. Cards from the Modifier Deck flickered into play—[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] dropped a Favor Card early, boosting his next hand, while Turner held back, calculating. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]]’s brow furrowed as [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] slid a double bluff into play, pairing a low Flush with a bluff of having drawn from the [[Sliver]] Deck.

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[b2.png|300]]

"Heard [[the Black Marauder|The Marauder]] was headed in [[Steeltown]]'s direction." [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said, finally. Breaking the awkwardness.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] looked up from his cards at that. "You don't say? Don't think [[Jimmy Douglass|Douglass]] and his crew aren't going to like that too much. [[Rustwater Raiders|Raiders]] been pushing their luck anyway. It was just a matter of time until they crashed head on with the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]], I suppose."

[[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] studied his own cards "I suppose so."

"You didn’t come here give me news on the pirates though, did you [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]?" [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] finally said, voice flat and taking a long swig from his glass.

"No," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] agreed, eyes fixed on the board. "Had a talk with [[Danny Dandelion|Dandy]] after the meeting. He’s got tells—little things he don’t realize he’s sayin’."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] eyed him. "He always had a big mouth."

"This was different. He was in a real hurry to get back. Talking about us needin' to get in-line with [[The Duke]], stop acting all rightous. Acted like it was nothin’, but he clammed up right after."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] leaned back, gaze sharpening. "You think he’s sellin’ us out?"

"Think he’s trying to climb out of our circle and into a more gilded one," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said. "And he’s got the charm and the lies to pull it off if we ain’t careful."

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] moved a chip, testing [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]. "Why bring this to me? You and me, we ain't been exactly cordial."

"‘Cause we both know a snake when we see one," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] said, voice low. "And I figure we’d both rather keep one eye open than end up bleedin’ on some [[Ashmoor]] stage while [[Danny Dandelion|Danny fuckin' Dandelion]] reaps the applause. And [[Turner Anderson|Turner]], whether you like it or not, the rules of the [[Rancher Collective|Collective]] make us all partners. It's in all of our interests to keep the snakes out.

The candle flickered as [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] studied him. Finally, he nodded once, slowly.

"We watch him. We keep our ears open at the festival. And if he steps wrong—"

"Then we step first," [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] finished, his tone like steel drawn in the dark.

They played in silence for a while longer. The chips clacked, cards slid across the wood like whispered secrets. A Rust Card came into [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]]'s hand—bad luck embodied—but he held onto it, letting its presence color his next move. The game was less about winning now, more about understanding. A ranch hand delivered dinner to the two men who broke bread together for the first time. When it ended, the candle had burned nearly to its base.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] stood and walked [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] to the door He extended a hand. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] stood and walked [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] to the door He extended a hand. Beau took it. took it.

"This don’t make us friends," [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] said.

"Didn’t say it did."

Outside, the wind picked up again [[Beau DuNoir|Beau]] looked up at the starry night at the [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] and sighed.

The [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] sat squat and wide beneath a bruised violet sky, its silhouette jagged as rusted tin against the daylight. Inside the longhouse, a flickering line of oil lamps cast drunken shadows across weathered wood, scar-marked walls, and a dozen faces worn raw by sun, grit, and years of compromise.

[[Turner Anderson]] leaned forward in his high-backed chair at the head of the table, a silver-buttoned relic once belonging to some long-dead cattle baron. His voice was low and deliberate, scraping through the room like a whetstone on bone. "We start now. Don’t matter who’s late. If you ain’t here, you’re part of the problem."

Boots scuffed against floorboards as the [[Rancher Collective]] shifted, their collective presence bristling with unease. Old grudges and fresh suspicions hung in the air, thicker than the dust that lined their boots.

[[Turner Anderson|Turner]] broke the silence first. "Alright, first. Ranch status. I'll go first. [[Threshton#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]] is smooth and steady out. Calves are strong, fences held through the last windstorm. Could be worse."

"Clockwork," [[Harp Langston]] grunted. "Always is, long as folks keep their heads and hands busy."

[[Freddy Blanchard]] stepped in with a nod. "Operating like a machine. No hiccups—yet. But this [[Ashmoor]] push could gum up the works."

[[Beau DuNoir]] leaned back, arms crossed. "Brought in twenty more heads last week, hoping to grease the gears a little. Economy’s lagging like a drunk mule."

[[Danny Dandelion]] adjusted his hat and offered a grin. "Just getting warmed up. Promised myself I’d jump right in—soon as I ride back tomorrow."

A few smirks curled around the table, but no one laughed. The air was too thick for that. The Duke’s shadow stretched far.

"[[Ashmoor Festival]]," Turner continued, pausing to spit into the iron bucket near his feet. "Duke says we double our stock for the parade drive. Wants horses and bone oxen dressed up like court dancers. Wants fireworks. Wants songbirds in gilded cages. Wants what he always wants—more."

A chorus of grunts and muttered curses followed. [[Harp Langston]], lean as a rake, too old for this shit and twice as bitter, slapped his calloused hand on the table. "It ain’t a festival, it’s a bleed-out. We send him our best, and he struts it through [[Ashmoor]] like he birthed it himself. We get what? A pin and a pat?"

[[Danny Dandelion]] lounged sideways in his chair, eyes half-lidded under a wide-brimmed hat dipped low. "Nobody said anything about a pin. Duke’s demands are steep, sure," he said, voice smooth as creamed corn. "But they always are. We get by. We always get by."

[[Harp Langston|Harp]] snorted. "That so? You got a secret herd hid out in the canyons, Dandy?"

[[Danny Dandelion|Danny]] gave a lazy shrug, lips quirking. "No secrets here. Just better bookkeeping."

Across from him, [[Beau DuNoir]] rolled a sliver chip between his fingers, the tin clink barely audible. "Maybe [[The Duke]] wants songbirds 'cause he ain’t got ears for the truth," he drawled. "Or maybe he just likes cages."

A ripple of nervous laughter broke the tension, fleeting as prairie smoke. [[Turner Anderson|Turner]] let it hang a moment before nodding once. "That’s enough. We meet his quota. For now. But we ain’t gonna dance harder just 'cause [[The Duke]] changed the tune. We keep eyes open. We talk if things start smellin' wrong."

One by one, the ranchers pulled flasks or small bottles from their coats. Tradition dictated the close—iron, fire, and whiskey. They drank in solemn ritual, each sip a pact written in burn and silence.

Outside, the wind howled low through the mesquite, and somewhere in the far setting sun, a coyote laughed.

“Loyalty is a matter of leverage. Nothing more.”

The only daughter of Threshton's oldest and most revered rancher, [[Harp Langston]], Soria was raised amid grit, cattle, and the stubborn code of rancher pride. But she was never interested in crops or community. She wanted influence — power wrapped in silk, not soil. Years ago, when whispers of rebellion stirred in the fields and ranchers began secretly feeding starving citizens, Soria made a choice. One night, she slipped away and told a group of Loyalist Guards exactly who was involved. It was betrayal. Of blood and home. And it paid off. [[The Duke]], ever hungry for loyalty and leverage, brought her to [[The Silo]]. Soria’s sharp tongue and sharper mind caught his eye. She became his scribe, organizing his affairs, drafting his decrees. Some say she seduced him. Others say she simply outmaneuvered every other vulture in the room. When [[Ashmoor]]’s previous mayor drowned in his own bath under “peculiar circumstances,” The Duke didn’t hesitate. He appointed Soria as mayor — elegant, merciless, and loyal only to herself. She now presides over the wealthiest, most reconstructed part of [[United Tribucia]], where she hosts opulent galas while the rest of the land starves. Her citizens loathe her. The Duke trusts her. And her father — if he's still alive — likely wishes he had strangled her in the crib. ## Personality **Temperament:** Charming, cunning, and quietly venomous. Always composed — never shows anger, only disapproval. **Vices:** Control, vanity, and the thrill of betrayal. Seduction is both a tool and a weapon. **Abilities:** Political maneuvering, manipulation, and flawless rhetoric. She can dismantle a room without raising her voice — or lifting a finger. **Secrets:** Maintains a secret ledger of every bribe, betrayal, and favor owed inside The Silo — including dirt on The Duke himself. She’s preparing for something bigger. **Beliefs:** Power is beauty. Loyalty is transactional. Weakness is a sin. Everyone is replaceable — even blood. ## Role in Disgraceland [[Soria Langston-Clay]] is the ruthless architect of Ashmoor’s political machine. Though she owes her rise to The Duke, her ambitions stretch beyond mere servitude. She embodies everything her father despised — a traitor cloaked in velvet. Her enemies call her poison in perfume. Her allies know better than to call her anything at all. ## Appearances

# State of Tribucia

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎The Silo, Ashmoor
> ![[state.png|400]]  

# 📡 [[State of Tribucia]]
> “*Your land. My vision. Our duty.*” — *[[The Duke]]*

## 🗓 Schedule
- **Every [[CALENDAR|Alphaday]]** at **20:00hrs**  
- **Broadcast live from** [[The Silo]] on **[[TTV Studios]]**  
- **Mandatory viewing** across [[TRIBUCIA MAP]], though enforcement is unofficial and widely ignored outside of [[Ashmoor]].

---

## 🎙 Overview
The **State of Tribucia** is a weekly broadcast led by **[[The Duke]]**, designed to **project authority, maintain illusionary order, and reinforce loyalty** across the fractured zones of Disgraceland. Though framed as a patriotic update, each address is carefully crafted propaganda — blending truth with distortion, veiled threats with hollow optimism.

Each episode opens with a militaristic version of the *Hymn of Unity*, followed by a wide shot of **[[The Duke]]** standing beneath a giant eagle-and-scythe emblem in a cold metal chamber deep inside [[The Silo]]. He speaks alone — no advisors, no questions, just the voice of a ruler to his subjects.

The broadcasts vary in length from **20 minutes to an hour**, depending on current events, [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew|Wrecking Crew]] movements, political unrest, or how much ego-stroking **[[The Duke]]** needs that week.

---

## 🗝 Purpose
- Reaffirm **The Duke’s control and divine right** to rule.  
- Announce **policies**, **fuel quotas**, **slave relocations**, or **raids**.  
- Issue **warnings**, call out **traitors**, or deliver personal messages to mayors like [[Soria Langston-Clay]] or [[Gorran Brile]].  
- Respond to incidents (e.g., rebel attacks, blackouts, shortages) with **blame-shifting** and **ominous rhetoric**.

---

## 🗣 Tone & Delivery
**[[The Duke]]** speaks with calm theatrical flair — part dictator, part televangelist. His voice is confident, sonorous, and condescending, often addressing viewers as “*my children*” or “*my debtors in paradise-to-be*.”

He often ends each address with a ritualistic phrase:  
> *“May the fires of unity burn ever upward. May your loyalty be as constant as my gaze.”*

---

## 📺 Reception & Impact
- In **[[Ashmoor]]**, residents typically watch out of fear or ambition.  
- In **[[Steeltown]]**, many **refuse to watch**, though some relay summaries via pirate radio.  
- **[[Gutter Row]]** treats it as a drinking game.  
- In **[[The Drownlands]]**, it is considered an ill omen to even speak during the broadcast.  
- **[[Threshton]] ranchers** often *intentionally work late* to miss it, calling it "**the Bull’s Sermon**."  
- **[[Charspire]] factories** pipe it in through loudspeakers, though most workers wear earplugs.

---

## 🧠 Notable Lore Hooks
- [[Rachel Gold]] once tried to fact-check a broadcast. She was *"reassigned to cultural desk duties."*  
- The phrase **“Two Harvests, One Hope”** was first coined in a 2179 address — later used to justify doubling [[Threshton]] grain quotas.  
- A malfunction in 2183 caused [[The Duke]]’s face to **freeze mid-grin** for 11 minutes — the clip was later turned into a banned [[Steeltown]] sticker.

History of the Steeltown Wrecking Crew
>

“Pray to El Santo, the Wrecking Crew is coming.”

The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] wasn’t born from ambition — it was born from grief. Long before [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland claimed his iron throne, [[Steeltown]] was a place of industry and resilience. Steel mills once roared, their fires lighting the sky as men like [[Darrell Douglass]] worked tirelessly to provide for their families. The people of Steeltown didn’t have much, but they had each other — a bond forged in sweat and smoke. But when the [[Tetra bomb]] fell and the water wars erupted, everything changed. The mills shut down, and the city crumbled. Fuel became scarce, and clean water even scarcer. The Duke, sensing opportunity, seized control of what little remained, imposing brutal taxes and using his enforcers to crush any resistance. When the people of Steeltown dared to stand up, the Duke made an example of them. Among those victims was Darrell Douglass, a man who refused to bow. He led a strike against the Duke’s fuel rationing, calling for fair treatment. His courage inspired others, but the Duke had no tolerance for defiance. Darrell was beaten and left to die in the streets — a message to anyone who dared to challenge the regime. But the Duke underestimated the spirit of Steeltown. Darrell’s sons, Jimmy and [[Mark Jeffrey]], didn’t weep. They didn’t beg. They rose. Fueled by anger and the need for justice, Jimmy vowed to tear down the system that took their father. He gathered a handful of like-minded souls — fighters, mechanics, survivors — and together they formed the Steeltown Wrecking Crew. At first, they were nothing more than a band of rebels on patched-together bikes, striking back where they could and vanishing before the Duke’s forces could respond. But word spread. Stories of the Crew's defiance reached every corner of Disgraceland. People whispered of the brothers in black, of roaring engines and fires in the night. For the forgotten, the Wrecking Crew became a symbol of resistance. Jimmy, with his relentless fire, led the charge. Mark, ever the tactician, made sure they stayed one step ahead. They struck supply chains, liberated prisoners, and rerouted stolen resources to the people. And as their legend grew, so did their numbers. The Steeltown Wrecking Crew welcomed outcasts and survivors — anyone willing to fight for something greater. Among the first to join was [[Abel May Jr.]], a towering force who had been left for dead by the Duke’s men. Jimmy and Mark saved his life, and from that day, Abel swore to stand by them. He became the Crew’s enforcer, a wall of muscle and loyalty. Then came [[Joe Ameen]], the mechanical genius who kept the Crew’s bikes and rigs running. Joe hated the Duke’s control over the fuel supply, and his skills became invaluable in their war. The Crew rode faster and hit harder with Joe’s ingenuity fueling their machines. [[Katie Kowalski]] was another pillar of the Crew. A self-taught doctor, she grew up alongside Mark and Joe. When the violence of the wasteland left its mark, it was Katie’s steady hands that patched the wounds. Her kindness tempered the Crew’s brutality, a reminder that not all battles are fought with steel. Even as the Crew grew, their bonds remained unbreakable. Every patch earned was a promise — to fight, to protect, and to stand together. The Crew wasn’t just a rebellion. It was family. But the Duke wasn’t blind. As the Wrecking Crew’s reputation spread, so did the Duke’s wrath. He sent his enforcers to burn their hideouts, slaughter their allies, and sow fear wherever the Crew’s name was spoken. Brady and Brody May, twisted remnants of the Duke’s experiments, were unleashed as his monstrous enforcers. The fact that they were Abel’s own cousins made the betrayal even more bitter. Yet, no matter how much blood the Duke spilled, the Crew endured. Jimmy’s calls for full rebellion grew louder. He believed the people of Disgraceland were ready to rise. But Mark, ever the cautious one, knew the price of war. Tension simmered between the brothers, though their love for each other kept it from boiling over. In the face of hardship, the Crew’s spirit only strengthened. [[Selena Matissao]] joined the fight, a fierce warrior who had lost her husband to the Duke’s cruelty. Known as The Phoenix in the streets, she brought her tracking skills and ruthless efficiency to the Crew’s cause. When [[Lincoln Jones]] arrived, his quick thinking and fierce loyalty earned him a place among them — as well as the role of the Crew’s most celebrated cook. Now, the Steeltown Wrecking Crew is more than a rebellion. They are a symbol of what Disgraceland could be — free from tyranny, united by the bonds of survival. They still ride the twisted highways, their engines roaring defiance against the Duke’s rule. For Jimmy, the war is far from over. He dreams of the day the Duke falls, of a world where children no longer grow up in fear. Mark watches the horizon, knowing the hardest battles are yet to come. Abel, Joe, Katie, Selena, Lincoln, and every patched-in member stand ready — because to wear the Steeltown Wrecking Crew patch means to fight for something worth dying for. And so, they ride. ---
