Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎STEELTOWN > ![[s5t.png|400]] Steeltown is a rustbucket miracle. A defiant patchwork of soot-streaked buildings and stubborn souls holding tight to dignity with oil-stained hands. Once the fire-belching pride of pre-Tetra industry, this was where steel was born and rails were fed across the continent. Now? It's a smoldering husk of its former self… and still somehow, impossibly, alive. The chimneys still cough black smoke like dying lungs. Oil drums burn on every corner just to beat back the frost, and market stalls burst out between rusted scaffolds and slag piles like weeds through concrete. What little industry survives does so through spit, weld, and willpower, jury-rigged machines, local scrapworks, and makeshift furnaces that forge just enough parts, just enough weapons, just enough hope to keep the fires lit. It's a town that shouldn't work anymore. But it does. Districts like [[STEELTOWN#Mohawk Valley|Mohawk Valley]] and [[STEELTOWN#Cannon|Cannon]] house most of the laborers, rough-and-tumble families living stacked in old brick tenements or boxcar shanties. [[STEELTOWN#Gage Park|Gage Park]] is where the kids play and the river cuts through. [[STEELTOWN#Barton|Barton]] is home to the Mayor and other more affluent citizens of [[Steeltown]]. [[STEELTOWN#The Hammer|The Hammer]] is where the hard fishermen make their living. The southern most point of [[Steeltown]], bordering the Sinner's Sea. Officially, **[[BLUEFORCE]]** patrols these streets — [[The Duke]]’s sanctioned peacekeepers, dressed in crisp blue uniforms and stiff regulation. But the people call them **Blue Shirts**, mostly with a sneer, and they don’t hold the reins here. Not really. The real law is written in exhaust fumes and tire tracks by the **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**, a biker gang turned protectorate. Their clubhouse flies the colors over an old foundry, and their presence alone keeps most slavers, thieves, and Loyalist enforcers from pushing too hard. There’s a balance here, but it’s a bloody one. **Mayor [[Ellis Westmount]]**, a former union-buster from [[Ashmoor]], rules like a boot on the throat, pushing The Duke’s taxes, cracking down on trade. But the [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] doesn't take orders from city hall. Not really. They raid Loyalist convoys when the shipments get too fat, free slaves smuggled in from **Charspire**, and sometimes, if the mood's right, torch a Blue Shirt patrol car just to remind everyone who really owns these streets. Steeltown’s people live hard, die young, and laugh anyway. They drink strong, love rough, and wear their scars like medals. They’re not waiting for liberation. They _are_ liberation, a quiet resistance of grease-stained hands and midnight deals. And if rebellion ever truly sparks across Disgraceland, it won’t begin in a palace or a chapel. It’ll start here. In [[STEELTOWN#Gage Park|Gage Park]]. With steel, smoke, and a war cry carried on the wind. ---

Districts

#### Gage Park Closest to the poisoned banks of the Rustwater River, Gage Park is where [[Steeltown]] breathes in the smoke and spits back grit. Cranes creak above rusted docks, unloading shipments by day and bodies by night. The [[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]] keep their clubhouse here, casting a long shadow over the bay. South of Gage Park, the Rustwater Bay churns with sludge and secrets, a dark vein feeding the territory's lifeblood. --- #### Barton They call Barton the crown of Steeltown, but that crown’s cracked and copper green. It’s where Mayor [[Ellis Westmount]] lives behind reinforced glass, and the streetlamps actually work. The folk here aren't rich by [[Ashmoor]] standards, but they’ve got roofs, clean shirts, and enough distance from the riots to sleep easy. Barton pretends the rest of Steeltown doesn’t exist, and most days, it succeeds. --- #### Mohawk Valley The beating, bleeding heart of Steeltown. Mohawk Valley is a labyrinth of flame-belching stacks, collapsing row houses, and workers who haven’t taken a full breath in years. It’s the biggest district, packed with families who eat steel dust and shit rust. You don’t move to Mohawk. You survive it. Factory whistles mark the hours, and fists mark everything else. --- #### Cannon Up near Knuckles Lake, Cannon sprawls like a bad idea that never stopped growing. Steelworkers who couldn’t squeeze into [[STEELTOWN#Mohawk Valley|Mohawk Valley]] built shacks between half-finished homes and forgotten projects. Cannon’s a maze of contradictions, where kids play ball beside men with lung burns, and every decent street's got a burned-out twin. It’s loud, proud, and on the edge of boiling over. --- #### The Hammer Way down south, where [[Steeltown]] kisses the sea, lies The Hammer. Don’t let the pretty beaches fool you—this place works. Fishermen drag nets at dawn, while smugglers move food from [[Threshton]] under tarps and half-truths. The Hammer’s where meals are made, fish are gutted, and sea-worn families cling to the only honest trade left. It smells like salt, diesel, and fried eel. --- #### East Mountain Rising above the smoke and grind, East Mountain is forested, quiet, and strange. A far cry from the steel districts below, this is sacred land to followers of the [[El Santo]] faith. At its peak sits the Cathedral of [[the Grand Mascara]], white-stone and gold, visible for miles on a clear day. Pilgrims hike wooded trails while old-timers claim to see spirits in the trees. You don’t go to East Mountain to make noise. You go to listen. ---

# SWILLPOTS

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ SWILLPOT in CHARSPIRE
> ![[swill.png|450]]

# 🥃 Swillpots of Disgraceland

Swillpots are the lifeblood of the broken people of Disgraceland — rough, loud, chaotic watering holes where drinks flow, fists fly, and secrets slip like spilled liquor on a crooked counter. While technically unsanctioned, they’ve become so culturally ingrained that even [[The Duke]] dares not outlaw them, despite his well-known hatred for alcohol. He’s called it “the rust in the gears of rebuilding,” but even his most Loyalist advisors know that banning swill would spark instant riots.

### 📜 History

The first Swillpot was nothing more than a hole-in-the-wall lean-to near the original strip mine in [[Charspire]], almost 50 years ago. Miners needed somewhere to forget how close they were to death every day, and a one-eyed ex-barkeep named [[Renny Slub]] gave them that place. His original shack, **The First Spill**, still stands — though it’s mostly a museum piece now, kept up by locals out of spite and pride.

From there, Swillpots spread across Tribucia, becoming a sacred refuge for the overworked, the outcast, the outlaw, and the brokenhearted.

---

## 🧃 Standard Fare

**Popular Drinks:**
- Lager
- Ale
- Whiskey
- Rum
- Wine

Most Swillpots also serve greasy food: meats, stews, thick breads, or salt-fried root vegetables. The rare ones offer fancier mixed drinks or imports — but expect to pay heavy in **slugs**.

---

## 🍻 Notable Swillpots by Region

### **STEELTOWN – The Furnace Gullet**
A loud, sweat-soaked pit of hammered steel and busted stools. Locals say fights here settle quicker than court disputes. Always hot inside, no matter the season. Home turf for a few off-duty Wrecking Crew bruisers.

### **ASHMOOR – The Amber Touch**
A 'high-class' Swillpot by Disgraceland standards. Velvet seats, expensive wines, and waitstaff that’ll rob you blind with a smile. Frequented by minor bureaucrats, spies, and smugglers in nice coats.

### **GUTTER ROW – The Slick Room**
Run out of the bottom floor of a collapsing tenement in Vileby. Walls drip from busted pipes, and rats are considered regulars. Nobody knows who actually owns it, but everyone pays the same: don’t cause trouble, or you disappear.

### **CHARSPIRE – The Spill House**
The original. Old, blackened stone walls with rusted beams overhead. Hasn’t cleaned its tankards in years. RedForce guards have an unspoken rule to leave it alone — even they need to forget sometimes.

### **THRESHTON – The Broken Bale**
A rancher-run hideaway where cowboys drink their fill and trade secrets over sour mash and molasses bread. Anyone badmouthing the [[Rancher Collective]] gets their boots nailed to the porch.

---

## 🧨 Notes

- The Duke would outlaw alcohol entirely if he believed he could get away with it.
- Instead, he taxes it heavily in Ashmoor, ignores it in Steeltown, and pretends it doesn't exist in Gutter Row.
- Despite his hatred, it’s common knowledge that some of his most loyal guards drink off-duty.

“I don’t need to see the fire. I trust the man holding the match.”

Tate Faulkner used to wear a badge. Worked checkpoint patrol near the [[Ashmoor]] perimeter during the early days of the Loyalist unification. He was known for two things: following orders _exactly_, and hitting harder than a horse kick. But everything changed the day he encountered [[Salem Quinn]]. Salem was just a blind man in a red suit then — quiet, strange, bleeding from the nose. But when Salem spoke, Tate listened. The things the old man described hadn’t happened yet… but within six months, every detail came true. A raid. A bridge collapse. The death of Tate’s entire unit. All except him. After that, Tate left his post and found the Seer. He never went back. No orders. No explanation. Just started walking beside him, watching his back, clearing the way. Over time, Tate became more than a bodyguard — he became **Salem’s interpreter**, organizer, translator, protector. He writes down every vision, studies patterns, checks dates, and warns locals when he can. Tate doesn’t believe in fate. But he believes in **[[Salem Quinn]]**. And if whatever’s coming is as bad as Salem says it is… Tate plans to meet it head-on — clipboard in hand, teeth bared. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Grim. Efficient. Intimidating. Speaks in short, clear bursts like he’s giving field orders. Rarely jokes, but has a dry, savage wit when cornered. Has no patience for nonsense, cruelty, or poetry. **Vices:** Caffeine. Precision. Control. May enjoy violence more than he admits. Refuses to read fiction. **Abilities:** Expert in hand-to-hand combat and crowd control. - Memorizes every detail — routes, rations, names, faces. Shoots to wound unless Salem says otherwise. Keeps detailed notes of Salem’s visions and interpretations. **Secrets:** Was once a Loyalist security officer… until he saw one of Salem’s visions come true. Keeps a tattered photo of a young girl in his pocket — never talks about her. Once broke a man’s spine for insulting Salem in front of children **Beliefs:** The Seer sees. His job is to make sure he **gets to where he needs to be.**. ## Role In Disgraceland Tate Faulkner is the rock that follows the storm. He’s not a mystic. He doesn’t see visions. But he **believes** in Salem Quinn with a conviction that’s downright terrifying. While Salem moves through Disgraceland as a whisper, Tate is the **crack of thunder** right behind him — clipboard in one hand, sidearm in the other. He handles the world so Salem doesn’t have to. ## Appearances

# [[Tetra Bomb]]

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[tbomb.png|cover hmed]]

> [!warning]+ Classification: EXTINCTION-LEVEL DEVICE  
> **Code Name:** TETRA  
> **Type:** Multi-element fusion warhead  
> **Era:** Final Phase of the [[Water Wars]]  
> **Blast Radius:** Unmeasured – total ecosystem-level detonation  
> **Casualties:** Estimated 7.2 billion (direct and chain-reaction effects)  
> **Known Surviving Cities:** Zero

> *"It wasn't built to save anyone. It was built to end the argument."*  
> – Unknown scientist, post-incident interview

## ☣️ Design & Composition

The **Tetra Bomb** was the result of a last-ditch black project from the Unified Continental Defense Pact during the height of the **[[Water Wars]]** — a conflict already choking the planet’s final resources.

The bomb’s name refers to its four core components:

1. **Helionite Plasma** – A synthetic isotope that destabilized upon impact with moisture  
2. **Black Crysilin Dust** – A nano-powder that fed on electrical currents and atmospheric pressure  
3. **Red Virex** – A biochemical ignition gel that reacted violently with oxygenated blood  
4. **Human Nervous Tissue** – Taken from dying test subjects. No explanation ever declassified.

The fourth element was added late. It worked.

---

## 💀 Deployment

The bomb was **not tested**. No simulation was conclusive. The scientists and strategists that signed off on its use assumed a localized continental sterilization effect — a final scare tactic.

What happened instead was **a cascade of chain reactions** across the stratosphere. Weather patterns collapsed. Power grids melted. Any nearby biome — human, animal, or machine — stopped functioning.

And then, silence.

---

## 🌎 Aftermath

Surprisingly… nature survived.

| Element             | Status After Detonation |
|---------------------|-------------------------|
| **Fresh Water**     | Largely unaffected      |
| **Plant Life**      | Regrew within months    |
| **Human Civilization** | Functionally erased |
| **Digital Infrastructure** | Obliterated |
| **Nuclear Fallout** | None – Tetra had no uranium, no fusion ring. |

The only immediate result:  
**One long, endless winter.**  
Cold enough to kill the desperate. Quiet enough to bury the loud.  
A thousand unmarked graves frozen in the open.

---

## 🧬 Legacy

- Tetra was only detonated once.  
- The schematics were **never recovered**.  
- The name “Tetra” is now used in **curses, prayers, and warnings**.  
- Some say remnants of the fourth element — the **nervous tissue core** — are still out there, buried beneath Dead Waters.  
- Others claim the **Reckoning Coil** is its second birth.

---

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎A SWAMP IN THE DROWNLANDS > ![[drown.png|400]] A place older than the fall. The Drownlands slither in the lowlands east of Ashmoor, a haunted quilt of drowned trees, rotted boardwalks, and fog that never lifts. Some call it a swamp, but that word doesn't do it justice. It's a breathing thing — a tangled forest of gnarled cypress and ash, their roots strangled in black water, their limbs hung with funeral moss. The air smells of wet bark, fungal rot, and something sweet underneath, like the perfume of something long dead still clinging to its bones. Sunlight barely filters through the canopy here. Instead, the world is lit in pale greens and grays, reflections of half-light on slick water. Frogs croak like old engines. Insects hum in strange rhythms. Every so often, you might hear the slap of something large slipping beneath the surface — and if you're smart, you don't go looking. The Unseen Widows rule these parts. Women clad in black, silent and swift, they watch from the shadows, veiled faces peeking between the moss. Most folks believe they’re witches, or ghosts, or both. But the Widows follow one woman only — **Veerah**, their Prophet. They say she sees the future in her sleep. They say her dreams come true. They say no man who walks into the heart of the Drownlands returns unchanged… if he returns at all. People steer clear, and for good reason. The land doesn’t welcome strangers. Paths vanish. Trees move. Your voice doesn’t echo here, it sinks. The Drownlands aren’t just a place. They’re a warning. And they remember you.

“Obey, and endure.”

His real name is long forgotten — or buried by design. To the people of Disgraceland, he is simply The Duke. A title taken, not earned. He wasn’t elected, appointed, or asked — he declared himself savior in the aftermath of the end of the world. And in a way, he was. Then again, so is a parasite to a corpse. Before the [[Tetra Bomb]], he had been a high-ranking officer in a private military firm during the final stages of the [[Water Wars]]. Brutal, efficient, and ideologically obsessed with order, he led sieges on fractured city-states and quelled rebellions under the banner of peace. He never blinked at atrocity. His uniform today — a patched-together bastardization of old-world military regalia — is stitched from the flags of defeated enemies, the epaulettes torn from bodies, medals self-assigned. When the [[Tetra Bomb]] dropped and the world fell silent, The Duke didn’t grieve. He saw opportunity. He took to the woods north of [[WATER#Faded Lake|Faded Lake]] and claimed an old estate once belonging to some long-dead tech mogul. There, he began The Rebuild — a militarized compound that eventually became [[Ashmoor]], with [[The Silo]] at its heart. The Silo is both symbol and weapon: a towering, welded-together grain hoard that feeds the loyal and starves the rest. The Duke believes that civilization failed because it became too soft. He teaches that the weak destroyed the world, and only by obedience, order, and iron-willed leadership can it be saved. His broadcasts are required viewing across Disgraceland — sermons of fear disguised as hope, always ending with his chilling motto: “Obey, and endure.” But behind his cold precision lies cruelty. He kidnapped [[Emily Burton]], a child at the time, years ago — the daughter of a dissenting scientist who disappeared soon after. She is now the Duke’s “First Lady”, a forced role inside his mansion-prison. He cannot bear children. He does not touch her. Yet he parades her as a symbol of dominance. The perfect wife. The perfect silence. But not forever. He hosts his weekly address, the [[State of Tribucia]] live every Alphaday on the [[TTV Studios|TTV Network]]. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Controlled and theatrical — he speaks like a preacher but rules like a butcher. He never yells, only issues decrees with unnerving calm and expects the world to obey. > [!infobox] > > ![[prop.png|260]] **Vices:** Delusions of legacy. He feeds on adoration, even if he has to manufacture it. Parades, statues, broadcasts — all scripted to reinforce the fantasy that he _saved_ the world, not conquered its corpse. **Abilities:** Tactical genius in psychological warfare and population control. A master propagandist who builds loyalty through fear, scarcity, and ritual. He can spot dissent in a crowd by a blink. **Secrets:** Deep beneath The Silo, he keeps a sealed chamber filled with relics of the old world — possibly tech, possibly something far darker — and he visits it alone, sometimes for hours, emerging shaken but silent. **Beliefs:** The strong must rule or all is lost. Emotion is rot. Freedom is a myth. The world didn’t end because of violence — it ended because men stopped _obeying._ His gospel: _“Obey, and endure.”_ ## Role In Disgraceland Self-declared ruler of United Tribucia. Created the militarized territory of **Ashmoor** around an old estate, now known as **The Silo**. Commands the **Loyalist Guard**, controls food distribution, and uses propaganda to keep control. Directly responsible for multiple atrocities across the land, all committed under the guise of “the greater good.” Hosts daily propaganda announcements across all of United Tribucia every night at 18:00 hrs. Mandatory viewing.

## Summary
The **Grand Mascara** is the supreme spiritual leader of the [[El Santo]] faith, a secretive and powerful figure chosen by the High Council, known as the [[Senior Enmascarados]], upon the death of the previous leader. His true identity is unknown to the public. He is both revered and feared.

## Appearance
- Wears flowing white and silver ceremonial robes with golden accents
- Always masked in a traditional silver luchador mask
- Draped in a dark silver cape
- Carries an amulet engraved with the sacred mask symbol of El Santo

## Known Traits
- Never removes his mask in public
- Charismatic, solemn, and unwavering
- Commands respect across all of [[DISGRACELAND]]
- Speaks with deliberate conviction
- Treats the mask as sacred — to remove it is to surrender the faith

## Beliefs and Teachings
- "To wear the mask is to carry the burden of the people."
- Preaches **strength in the face of oppression**
- Encourages followers to help the less fortunate and defend the weak
- Believes the mask makes all equal — rich, poor, noble, or slave

## Succession
- The Grand Mascara is chosen only upon death
- Selection process handled in secret by the [[Senior Enmascarados]]
- The chosen one disappears from public life and is reborn as **Mascara**

## Current Status
- The 157th Grand Mascara
- Believed to have been appointed shortly after the Long Winter
- Seen occasionally at major temples or during sacred rites
- Suspected to have political influence beyond the church

## Notes
- Rumors circulate that he was once a champion luchador before taking the vows
- Some say he speaks to the Mask of Santo itself
- The phrase **“The Mask Endures”** is often associated with his rule

"If you hear the chain, it’s too late." — overheard in the tunnels beneath Gutter Row

The boy had no name by the time the fire took everything. The [[Loyalist Guard]] stormed through [[Steeltown]] Sector 9 just before dawn, enforcing a tax no one could pay and silencing mouths that asked why. His father tried to fight — with a rusted hammer and bad knees. His mother screamed as they were dragged into the street. His little sister never made it out of the crawlspace. He hid under the porch, face pressed to ash, listening to the house burn. Listening to the boots. The silence. The laughter. When it was over, he climbed into the wreckage and found his sister’s doll, blackened but still intact. He didn’t cry. There was no time for grief in Disgraceland. The next week was snow and blood and starvation. He wandered south — limping, fevered — until the city changed around him. Until the buildings sagged lower, and the smoke smelled different, more alive. Until people stopped looking him in the eye. That’s when he crossed into [[Gutter Row]]. [[Gutter Row]] didn’t offer sanctuary. Just indifference. He slept in the sewers beneath the [[Three Nail Market]], where black market traders sold flesh and fungus in equal measure. He learned the alleys. Learned the language. Watched how a man could get stabbed, stripped, and forgotten in under a minute — and how no one would say a thing. He spoke to no one. He simply watched. Waited. Collected every scream, every kick, every whisper behind the slave cages and drug dens. And then, one night, a chain went missing from a slaughterhouse. A spike followed, torn from the center of a disassembled meat press. The next night, a slaver known for collecting children turned up outside the Glassneedle Bar, hanging from a pipe, his tongue nailed to his chest with a spike driven through his ribs. The doll — the same scorched doll — was tied to his belt. That’s when the tapping began. You hear it before you see him. Tap. Tap. Tap. The end of the chain dragging over stone. A signal. A warning. A countdown. He moves like smoke — slow until it’s too late. Appearing in doorways, behind dumpsters, beneath subway grates. Some say he walks through walls. Others say he becomes the wall. He never speaks. Never. But the blood tells stories. He kills without hesitation — rapists, slavers, gang enforcers, crooked guards. Always the worst. Always the ones who thought the Row had forgotten them. The people of Gutter Row don’t call him a hero. They just say, “The Grim Man walks.” He’s their shadow. Their reckoning. Their nightmare that protects them from worse. The Loyalists claim he’s an urban legend, a scare tactic, propaganda. But they still don’t patrol Gutter Row at night. Not alone. And though his chain was born in the blood of the Row, his ghost walks far. They say he’s been seen in Threshton, in the fields behind the Red Night Ranch. In the smoke stacks of Charspire. Even once — once — outside the gates of The Silo. The Grim Man doesn’t care where you sin. Only that you did.** --- ## Personality > [!infobox] > > ![[grimbrile.png|260]] **Temperament:** Silent. Calculated. Unforgiving. He does not react — he decides. There is no negotiation, no rage, no mercy. He doesn’t kill in anger — he kills like it’s a ritual. **Vices:** None known. Doesn't drink, smoke, or speak. May not even sleep. If pain is a vice, he carries it like armor. **Abilities:** Stealth bordering on supernatural — moves without sound when he chooses. Master of improvised weapons, particularly chain-and-spike. Expert in urban terrain: alleys, sewers, rooftops. Possibly impervious to fear, intimidation, or pain. **Secrets:** May have once trained under the Unseen Widows, or simply survived them. Knows underground paths others don’t — possibly even access routes into The Silo **Beliefs:** Justice is dead; only reckoning remains. The system cannot be fixed — it must be punished ## Role In Disgraceland The Grim Man is the walking judgment of Disgraceland — a myth made flesh. His presence weaves through every region like a whispered warning. He doesn't lead. He doesn't follow. He _hunts_. No one is safe from him, and no one is innocent enough to summon him. But when he appears, the guilty know exactly why.

# [[The Silo]]


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎The Silo, Ashmoor
> ![[silo.png|500]]  

## Overview
**[[The Silo]]** is the towering, marble-and-steel heart of [[Ashmoor]] — a brutalist palace-turned-government fortress that serves as the official residence and command center of [[The Duke]] of Disgraceland. Rising from the highest point in the city like a monument to dominion, it casts a long shadow over the rebuilt districts below.

Once an abandoned military weapons facility from the Water Wars, The Silo was repurposed by [[The Duke]] during his rise in 2144. It is both a symbol of order and a shrine to his narcissism, wrapped in banners, statues, and surveillance.

---

## Description
- **Architecture**: Cold, brutalist structure reinforced with blastproof plating and reinforced glass. Marble columns line the entrance, stained from rain and smoke. Twin Loyalist banners hang from the central tower.
- **Interior**: Lavish, polished floors contrast with bare steel walls. Giant screens line every corridor, looping messages of "unity through strength." Secret passageways and panic rooms are built into the walls. Most who work here know only fragments of its layout.
- **Security**: Operated by [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]] and elite [[Loyalist Guard]], with surveillance drones in constant rotation. Unauthorized entry is a death sentence.

---

## Key Areas
- **The Throne Room**: Where [[The Duke]] delivers speeches and performs his weekly *[[State of Tribucia]]* broadcasts. It features a golden throne forged from melted artillery.
- **The Chapel of Continuity**: A strange, candlelit room filled with relics from the pre-Tetra era — propaganda photos, tattered flags, and the original blueprints of [[TRIBUCIA MAP]].
- **The Glass Office**: [[Soria Langston-Clay]]'s elevated, fully transparent work chamber. She can see everyone. They cannot see her.
- **The Underlevels**: Heavily restricted subfloors rumored to house interrogation cells, vaults of pre-war tech, and black project labs. Only a few living people know its full contents.

---

## Lore & Significance
- **Foundation**: Converted in 2144 by [[The Duke]] after uniting the [[Ashmoor]] factions. Became a seat of power by 2150.
- **Public Perception**: Seen as both sacred and terrifying. Citizens of [[Ashmoor]] call it "The Eye." Rumors say it broadcasts sonic signals at night.
- **Propaganda Hub**: He hosts his weekly address, the  [[State of Tribucia]] live every [[CALENDAR|Alphaday]] on the [[TTV Studios|TTV Network]].

---

## Notable Events
- **2157**: The assassination attempt by the Ashmoor Scholars — ended in the mass public execution of 43 citizens on the Silo’s steps.
- **2169**: [[Soria Langston-Clay]] appointed Mayor of Ashmoor from within The Silo after a "gas leak" killed the previous mayor.
- **2182**: Alleged quake under The Silo revealed a sealed chamber. Access denied. [[Salem Quinn]] called it "a voice buried in the steel."

---

## Secrets & Theories
- **Silo Core**: Conspiracy theorists claim the entire building is powered by a pre-Tetra AI core known as “Motherglass.”
- **Ghost Broadcasts**: Late-night static often cuts across other channels with snippets of [[The Duke]] speaking... when he isn’t on air.
- **Unseen Access**: Some believe the [[Unseen Widows]] infiltrated the Silo once. Only [[Veerah]] would know if that’s true.

---

## Quote
> “This isn’t a building, it’s a mirror. And it shows us all just how small we are.”  
> — [[Royce Sincayd]], in an unpublished editorial draft

## 🎤 Overview  
**The Wanderers** are a post-collapse rock group formed in the streets of Charspire, now known across [[DISGRACELAND]] as the nightly house band on *Night Time with Morris Gable*. While the regime promotes them as “a symbol of restored culture,” many citizens — especially the young and restless — feel something deeper pulsing beneath the music.

Led by [[Jaden Kade]], a wiry frontman with a scorched voice and rebel heart, The Wanderers walk a dangerous line between performance and resistance. Their lyrics ride the edge of censorship, and every show feels like a gamble — how much truth can be hidden in a song before someone notices?

---

## 🎶 Style & Themes  
Their sound is a fusion of post-industrial blues, rustrock, and stripped-down synthwave.  
- Instruments are salvaged, wired by hand, often shorting out mid-performance.  
- Lyrics often reference roads, fire, static, chains, and lost memory — metaphors for rebellion, surveillance, and grief.

**Notable Songs:**  
- *“Last Light Left”* — Believed to be about the failed uprising in [[Steeltown]]  
- *“Cracked Signal”* — Features a reversed vocal loop that some claim is a coded message  
- *“Rustwater Hymn”* — Banned from public radio three weeks after debut  
- *“King of Glass”* — Thought to be a veiled insult toward [[The Duke]]  
- *“Deadman Waltz”* — A fan favorite known to stir emotion in live crowds

---

## 🎤 Relationship with Morris Gable  
Their inclusion on *Night Time with Morris Gable* is widely seen as strategic — both for the regime, which uses their popularity to retain viewer interest, and for Jaden Kade, who uses the airtime to echo unrest through rhythm.

**Publicly:**  
- Morris praises them weekly as “the soul of the nation.”  
- The band appears polite and cooperative — but never speaks much during interviews.

**Privately:**  
- Jaden Kade despises Morris but respects the opportunity.  
- It’s a cold truce: ratings in exchange for silence.

---

## 🔥 Rebellion Rumors  
- Multiple resistance cells have reportedly used The Wanderers’ lyrics as code phrases.  
- Bootlegged live recordings circulate in outlaw zones.  
- It’s believed the band helps fund small acts of sabotage using their TTV stipend.  
- Some fans claim to have received blank tapes from the group containing anti-regime broadcasts when played backward.

---

## 🧠 Trivia  
- The band refuses to play pre-Duke cover songs — all material is original.  
- Their instruments have names: Jaden’s guitar is “**Crowtooth**,” Silas’s snare is “**July**

# 📍 Three Nail Market — Vileby, Gutter Row


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait
> ![[tnm.png|500]]  

## Overview

The **Three Nail Market** is the blackened heart of commerce in [[Gutter Row#Vileby|Vileby]], a festering urban sprawl within [[Gutter Row]]. Named after the three rusted nails still embedded in the wall of the first slave-post in the region, the market operates as a brutal bazaar of flesh, chemicals, and desperation. It's a place where danger is the currency, and survival is the only reward.

---

## Structure

### 🔹 The Top Layer – *"The Facade"*
- A chaotic mix of legitimate and not-so-legitimate vendors.
- Stalls sell scavenged tech, canned goods, reworked clothing, and "imported" wares.
- Some stores are fronts for brothels, gambling rings, or backroom clinics.
- Lanterns of specific colors above doorways serve as coded signals — red for sex, green for meds, blue for weapons.

### 🔸 The Mid Layer – *"The Run"*
- Reached through alleys, basements, or coded stairwells.
- Location of most drug deals, Luxyn exchanges, illegal surgeries, and smuggling transactions.
- Slave pens are wheeled in and out under cover of tarps.
- Frequented by gangs, mercs, and rogue surgeons.

### ⚫ The Deep Layer – *"The Roots"*
- Hidden tunnels and ruins beneath the city used during the Water Wars.
- Secretive auction halls, holding cells, execution rooms, and biochemical labs.
- Ghostly quiet, except when it’s not — screams are common and ignored.
- Whispers of blood rites, body modification dens, and worse.

---

## Notable Elements

- **[[Luxyn]] Trade**  
  A rare and potent hallucinogenic stimulant, Luxyn is difficult to manufacture.  
  - Main suppliers:  
    - **The [[Murray Boys]]** – a local crime family with blood-soaked hands.  
    - **[[Lash Hawkins]]** – a gutsy young street dealer with a growing rep.  
  - Both do their selling in Three Nail Market, often guarded and always watched.

- **Slave Auctions**  
  Weekly events held in the mid and deep layers. Children, workers, and “custom orders” available. Desperate men and women can "sell themselves" into slavery. This system is often abused.

- **Flesh Parlors**  
  Gruesome medical dens where "doctors" perform on the desperate.

- **Merc Boards**  
  Physical message boards listing contracts: hits, deliveries, abductions, or organ bounties.

---

## Power & Protection

- **The Nail Lords** *(Details TBD)*  
  A shadow council of market overlords who maintain order, enforce the rules, and extract tribute.

- **Mayor: [[Cricket Granger]]**  
  Corrupt and cunning. Publicly dismisses the market, privately benefits from it.

- **Official Force: [[Loyalist Guard#Blackforce|Blackforce]]**  
  Gutter Row's designated security unit. Known for brutality but rarely step foot inside Three Nail.

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎THRESHTON > ![[df.png|400]] Threshton is the dusty breadbasket of Disgraceland — a land of cracked soil, stubborn cattle, and long grudges. Stretching wide across the southern edge of the map, it’s where the grain grows, the livestock breeds, and the backbones break. The region feeds the rest of United [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]], but barely feeds itself. Every harvest is taxed by [[The Duke]]'s regime, skimmed off by crooked ledgers and escorted out by [[Loyalist Guard#**Amberforce**|Amberforce]], the brown-shirted enforcers who watch the silos closer than they watch the streets. At the heart of Threshton is the [[Rancher Collective]] — a loose and uneasy alliance of ranch owners who were once competitors, now forced to work together under pressure. Their ranches are sprawling compounds with weather-beaten fences and names that sound like threats: [[THRESHTON#Double Cross Ranch|Double Cross Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Bonebreak Ranch|Bonebreak Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Snake Kiss Ranch|Snake Kiss Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Red Night Ranch|Red Night Ranch]], [[THRESHTON#Hangman's Ranch|Hangman’s Ranch]]. They meet under candlelight and spit into the same whiskey bottle when the deals are done. Officially, they only trade with the Duke. Unofficially, a good portion of their grain and meat finds its way into the hands of the hungry in [[Steeltown]] and [[Gutter Row]]. The region’s largest settlement is Farmington — not much more than a loose web of barns, bunkhouses, and crop mills, but it’s where the deals are struck and the rumors fly. Out here, the land is everything, and trust is rare. Outsiders aren't welcomed without purpose. Even the [[Loyalist Guard#**Amberforce**|Amberforce]] treads lightly. Threshton’s mayor, [[Marla Rusk]], is a wiry, sun-wrinkled woman who’s survived more droughts and shootouts than most men in Disgraceland. She’s not part of the Collective, but she knows how to play them against each other when she needs to. The Duke appointed her to keep the food flowing and the workers in line — but whether she truly answers to him, or to the people of Threshton, is an open question. She smiles like a rattlesnake. Keeps a shotgun in the room during every meeting. And no one — not even the ranchers — wants to be alone with her for too long.

Districts

#### Double Cross Ranch Westernmost and best run, **Double Cross Ranch** is [[Turner Anderson]]'s empire of dirt and precision. The docks hum with activity day and night, moving food across Tribucia like lifeblood through veins. Anderson’s operation is smooth, strict, and respected. Workers here know their roles, the land stays clean, and the books are balanced. If something fails, it gets fixed. If someone fails, they’re gone. --- #### Red Night Ranch [[Harp Langston]]'s legacy is carved into the soil of **Red Night Ranch**, the oldest in Tribucia. It’s where the first post-bomb harvest grew, a turning point etched into every Tribucian textbook — but here, it's religion. Named for the crimson sky the night Harp and his wife staked their claim, the ranch is sacred to some, mythic to others. The land remembers, and Harp walks it like a man guarding memory with a shotgun. --- #### Hangman's Ranch Won in a game of [[Sliver]] and managed like a tavern with cattle, **Hangman’s Ranch** belongs to [[Beau DuNoir]]. It hugs the border of Steeltown’s [[Steeltown#West Mountain|West Mountain]], and if the ranch itself runs well, that’s thanks to the actual ranchers. Beau's often too busy drinking, gambling, or charming someone he shouldn't. Parties at Hangman’s are legendary. So are the debts. But the cattle still come fat and the grain gets weighed — somehow. --- #### Bonebreak Ranch If you hear a whip crack in Threshton, it’s probably coming from **Bonebreak Ranch**. [[Freddy Blanchard]] runs it hard, runs it clean, and works the land like he's still proving something. It’s the most productive of the ranches, known across Disgraceland for its meat — thick, red, and tough like the men who raise it. Blanchard doesn’t smile much. His ranch speaks for him. --- #### Snake Kiss Ranch The runt of the land. **Snake Kiss Ranch** used to be a thriving estate until [[Danny Dandelion]] talked the elderly widow Greta Harp into signing it over. Since then, the place has slipped into disrepair, with fences falling and workers walking. Danny talks big, dresses louder, and pretends he’s one of the boys. He isn’t. The other ranchers know it. Snake Kiss is a joke — and Danny’s the punchline nobody laughs at. --- #### Split Rest Far north, where Threshton touches the Wildlands and Gravebay, sits **Split Rest** — a trading outpost turned district. Supplies, tools, weapons, smokes — it’s all here, alongside the mayor’s home and a few dusty bars that stay open too late. The winds from the bay carry secrets, and locals say the Wildlands howl at night. Split Rest is where civilization ends and something stranger begins. ---

# [[Transportation in Disgraceland]]

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Specific Vehicles
> **[[Steeltown Wrecking Crew]]**: Every member rides a functioning motorcycle — mostly retrofitted cruisers or choppers. Their loud engines are a warning and a promise.
> **Sgt. Rottwyler**: Drives a reinforced military Hummer painted bone-white, covered in decals and Loyalist Guard iconography.
> **[[The Duke]]**: Travels in a fully restored white limousine — old-world luxury, spotless, custom-armored. It’s said he has never once driven it himself.
> **Mayors**: Each appointed mayor is provided a standard black sedan and a full-time government driver. The vehicles are symbolic of power, even if they require regular patchwork repairs.
> There are official buses that travel into [[Charspire]] each day for work.
> 
>> [!rustwater] Transportation
>> ![[car.png|400]]

## Overview

Transportation in Disgraceland is a brutal mix of scarcity, improvisation, and control. With fuel tightly rationed and roads barely maintained, only the powerful ride in comfort — while the rest walk, limp, or saddle up.

---

## Fuel Economy

All known fuel reserves and refining operations are controlled by [[The Duke]], with refining centralized in [[Charspire]] under the iron grip of Mayor [[Gorren Brile]]

Fuel is distributed exclusively through state-run depots in each major territory, sold at severe markups. This keeps everyday citizens dependent, while also rewarding loyalty and punishing dissent.

Smuggling fuel is punishable by death — and still happens daily.

---

## Common Transportation Methods

- **Walking**: The most common way to get around. Simple. Free. Slow. Dangerous.
- **Pack Animals**: Horses, mules, and even oxen are making a slow return. Ranchers in [[Threshton]] have started quietly breeding stock again. Carts, carriages, and sleds are now a common sight in rural regions.
- **Scavenged Bikes & Carts**: Children, merchants, and drifters often use homemade wheelbarrow carts or two-wheeled junkbikes made from scrap.
- **Automobiles**: Rare. Frankenstein rigs built from old-world parts and scrap. Think Mad Max — armored panels, engine smoke, and heavy welds. Loud. Unpredictable. Respected.

---

## Notable Vehicles



---

## Road Conditions

Most highways are fractured, overgrown, or outright collapsed. Bridges are rare and fiercely protected. Those that remain are either toll-controlled or watched by [[Loyalist Guard]].

Travel outside safe zones is extremely risky — requiring guards, fuel, water, and luck.

---

## Black Market Travel

If you know the right people, you can:

- Rent a hidden fuel stash.
- Buy a seat on a roaming trader’s armored bus.
- Hire a stealth wagon convoy to smuggle you through enemy regions.

Just don’t ask questions. And always pay in advance.

# TRASHFLICKS

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ TRASHFLICK
> ![[trash.png|450]]

> "Luck’s a lie. In *Sliver*, you either *bleed for your win* or you lose with style." — [[Ninepack]]

## 🩸 Overview

Trashflicks are low-budget, underground films passed around Disgraceland on scavenged tapes, discs, or crude cartridges. Screened on battered CRTs in basements, alley clubs, or projected onto ruined walls, Trashflicks are the desperate artform of a starving culture. Content ranges wildly — from salvaged pre-Tetra movies, to outlaw documentaries, raunchy comedies, staged propaganda parodies, and even whispered rumors of snuff or prophetic reels.

---

# 🎞️ Trashflick Genres

> _“The Duke’s afraid of guns in the streets, but not half as afraid as he is of a tape in the right hands.”_

Trashflicks are the chaotic, street-level soul of Disgraceland cinema. Shot, edited, and distributed by desperate hands using salvaged tech, they reflect the raw emotional nerve of a society struggling to breathe.

---

#### 🕰️ Pre-Fall Relics

**Description:**  
Ultra-rare original pre-Tetra cassettes — action movies, romantic dramas, cartoons, even sitcoms — usually warped, static-laced, or dubbed over.

**Value:**  
Extremely scarce. Most believe only **[[The Duke]]**, **[[Jacoban Clay]]**, and a few elite collectors possess intact originals.

**Popular With:**  
Wealthy traders, rebel archivists, artists hunting for forgotten truth.

**Subculture:**  
“**Tape Purists**” believe the soul of the old world lives on in its flicks.

---

#### 📽️ Disgraceland Docs

**Description:**  
Raw handheld footage and stitched-together edits exposing corruption, starvation, rebel activity, secret experiments, and executions. Sometimes staged, sometimes all too real.

**Notable Flicks:**  
- *Grain Chain* — exposes famine tactics in **[[Threshton]]**  
- *White Tiger* — rumored footage of a beast in **[[The Drownlands]]**  
- *Red Tape* — alleges **[[The Duke]]** uses doubles  

**Popular With:**  
Steeltown crews, underground educators, Widows, and rebel youth.

**Danger Level:**  
High. Possession is a crime punishable by imprisonment or worse.

---

#### 🎭 Blacktown Comedies

**Description:**  
Crude sketch reels, sarcastic puppet shows, or street acts captured during **[[Backburn]]** gatherings. Some are brilliant. Some are borderline nonsense.

**Subgenres:**  
- *Ha Ha Holes* — joke reels mocking regions or public figures  
- *Ratstick & Friends* — a filthy puppet show parodying Loyalist propaganda

**Popular With:**  
Everyone who needs to laugh to keep from crying — especially in **[[Gutter Row]]**.

**Slang:**  
**“Bloopers”** — prank reels or slapstick failures turned viral.

---

#### 🔥 Loverunners (Sextapes)

**Description:**  
The best-selling Trashflicks. Shot in secret, passed around under fake names. Sometimes consensual, sometimes questionable, always watched.

**Why They’re Big:**  
In a world starved of intimacy and driven by paranoia, voyeurism becomes currency.

**Notable Rumors:**  
- *The Widow’s Mouth* — said to feature a disguised Unseen Widow  
- *Ashmoor After Dark* — suspected Loyalist bait series  

**Trade Lore:**  
A seller in **[[Charspire]]** allegedly produced over 200 tapes under 17 pseudonyms before vanishing.

---

## 🦆 Duke-Flips & Propaganda Spools

**Description:**  
Two opposing categories — one mocking, the other glorifying **[[The Duke]]**.

- **Duke-Flips:** Overdubbed, cut-up broadcasts turned into satire or horror.  
- **Propaganda Spools:** Clean, well-produced Loyalist reels glamorizing regime victories.

**Secret Culture:**  
Some flicks are **“True Forks”** — tapes spliced to contain both a propaganda reel *and* its mockery, depending on how they're played.

**Suspected Creators:**  
Rumors point to the **Blueforce Media Division** for the propaganda, and rogue editors from **[[Ha Ha Hole]]** or the **[[Tribucia Tribute]]** for the flips.

---

## ⚙️ The Charspire Machines

**Origin:**  
A seller named **Harrel Kint** in East Gravenwild began repairing old cassette players and handheld recorders in 2175, selling them from a junk stall.

**The Decline:**  
By 2181, Kint had vanished. Official reports cite a “licensing issue.” His workshop burned one week later.

**Legacy:**  
Kint’s refurbished devices, now called **“Kint Boxes”**, are valuable collector’s items. Some say they contain hidden features or preloaded banned flicks.

---

(cont'd) ## 🔟 Top 10 Most In-Demand Trashflicks in Disgraceland

These are the flicks people lie, steal, and bleed for. Some are traded like holy relics. Others are whispered about like cursed myths. Most are illegal. All are unforgettable.

---

### 1. 🎥 *Ashmoor After Dark*  
**Genre:** Loverunner / Suspected Propaganda  
**Rumors:** Said to be produced by Loyalists as bait. Features a masked man resembling **[[The Duke]]** in multiple graphic scenes. Some swear it's real. Others claim it's a test.  
**Status:** Extremely dangerous. Possession can result in disappearance.

---

### 2. 🎥 *Grain Chain*  
**Genre:** Docu-tape  
**Summary:** Documents famine enforcement in **[[Threshton]]**, including Loyalist dumping sites, corrupt crop seizures, and interviews with starving families. Credited with sparking three food riots.  
**Status:** High-priority contraband. Blueforce raids any known screening site.

---

### 3. 🎥 *The Widow’s Mask*  
**Genre:** Loverunner / Hoax Flick  
**Rumors:** A heavily stylized tape featuring a veiled woman in black performing ritualistic dances and whispering cryptic lines. Promoted as a “Widow reveal,” but almost certainly staged.  
**Truth:** No verified connection to the **[[Unseen Widows]]**. Likely a tasteless imitation or Loyalist psy-op.  
**Status:** Controversial, widely condemned in **[[The Drownlands]]**, but still sold under the table.

---

### 4. 🎥 *The Feral Tape*  
**Genre:** Found Footage / Horror  
**Summary:** Footage from a destroyed Redforce outpost. Flashes of something inhuman. Ends with a whisper over static: *“We’re not dead. We’re waiting.”*  
**Status:** Dozens of bootlegs exist. No one knows who shot it.

---

### 5. 🎥 *Duke’s Doodles*  
**Genre:** Parody  
**Summary:** A surreal animated satire of **[[The Duke]]** as a deranged children’s show host, co-starring a talking goose and haunted sink. Borderline genius.  
**Status:** Spread mostly via Ha Ha Hole patrons. Creators remain anonymous.

---

### 6. 🎥 *The Nine-Hour Kiss*  
**Genre:** Loverunner  
**Summary:** A continuous shot of two lovers in hiding — possibly ex-Wrecking Crew. Shows intimacy, desperation, and confession. Not pornographic — emotional, raw, and real.  
**Status:** Treasured and worn thin. Original tape believed lost.

---

### 7. 🎥 *Static Eden*  
**Genre:** Art Film / Prophetic Vision  
**Summary:** A disturbing montage of decaying cities, broken statues, biomech corpses, and stormlight flickers — all set to a droning hum.  
**Rumors:** Some believe it's based on a real dream. Others call it a hoax.  
**Status:** Treated with reverence by some cult circles. Illegal in Ashmoor.

---

### 8. 🎥 *Stitched Up*  
**Genre:** Docu-tape / Horror  
**Summary:** Smuggled footage allegedly from **[[Ora Razchek]]'s** mansion. Shows flickering images of reanimated bodies, mechanical organs, and stitched skin.  
**Status:** “Too fake to be true” — unless you’ve seen one of his monsters.

---

### 9. 🎥 *Red Velvet Goldmine*  
**Genre:** Loverunner  
**Rumors:** Shot in a high-rise suite in **[[Ashmoor]]**. The masked woman resembles a high-ranking official. Some say **[[Soria Langston-Clay]]**, though it's never confirmed.  
**Status:** Blacklisted by name. Copies fetch entire livestock trades.

---

### 10. 🎥 *The Day the Sky Forgot*  
**Genre:** Spoken Word / Documentary  
**Summary:** A former steelworker narrates his life before, during, and after the Tetra Bomb, over footage of the cratered ruins. Beautiful and heartbreaking.  
**Status:** Played quietly in backrooms. Always gets passed on.

---

> _“You can burn books. You can hang preachers. But a flick? That shit crawls.”_  
> — **[[Reel Rat Jules]]**, legendary tape-runner


---

> _“Every tape tells a truth. Doesn’t matter if it’s a lie.”_ — **[[Reel Rat Jules]]**, black market legend



## 🎬 Glossary & Slang

- **Tape Purist** – someone who believes pre-Fall cinema holds historical truth
- **Reel Rat** – slang for Trashflick traders and bootleggers
- **Tape Burn** – the distortion caused by overwriting old tapes (also slang for watching too much in one sitting)
- **Static Run** – a long night of flicks watched through haze and fuzz
- **Veed** – short for "viewer", usually used mockingly
- **True Fork** – a tape spliced to contain both propaganda and parody

---

Let me know if you want a **Trashflick Hall of Fame** with famous tapes and who starred in them — or even a **Reel Rat** NPC page for a black market tape lord.

# Tribucia Tribute

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[paper.png|300]]

## Overview  
The *Tribucia Tribute* is the largest and most widely read newspaper in [[TRIBUCIA MAP|Disgraceland]]. Though not officially mandatory, it’s printed overnight and delivered to homes and businesses every morning — making it a daily presence in nearly every region.

Originally founded as a beacon of free journalism, the paper has since become a tool of subtle propaganda under the watchful eye of [[The Duke]]. Direct criticism of the regime is forbidden, though occasional subversive truths still slip through — especially when reported by the paper’s most famous journalist.

---

## Ownership  
The paper is owned by [[Royce Sincayd]], a once-principled journalist turned political opportunist. Royce started the *Tribucia Tribute* out of a genuine love for storytelling, public truth, and accountability. Over time, he succumbed to political pressure and now cooperates directly with Loyalist Forces to ensure all Duke-facing articles are filtered or adjusted to maintain “order.”

Royce is not hated by the public — but nobody really trusts him either.

---

## Key Staff  

- **[[Rachel Gold]]** — The paper’s uncontested star reporter. She’s known across Tribucia as a folk hero. Brilliant, fearless, and relentless in her pursuit of truth. Her stories always find the beating heart of a crisis, even if she has to dig it out with her bare hands.  
  Despite the risk, [[Royce Sincayd]] is often forced to run her stories front and center, knowing the public demands it. Rachel constantly tests the paper’s boundaries and frequently butts heads with Royce over censorship.

- **[[Marlon Lambert]]** — A capable, methodical journalist who lives in [[Rachel Gold]]’s shadow. Marlon lacks her charisma but is quietly respected. He often cleans up after her, does follow-ups on her investigations, and keeps her safe when things get risky. He won’t say it, but he’s protective of her — maybe too much.

---

## Recent Controversy  
A recent front-page piece by [[Rachel Gold]] broke down the new fuel tax imposed by [[The Duke]], detailing how it disproportionately hurts working citizens while funneling wealth into Ashmoor. Though the article never directly attacked The Duke, the numbers spoke for themselves.  

The fallout was immediate: protests, ration hoarding, and quiet investigations into Rachel’s past sources. [[Royce Sincayd]] nearly fired her, but public backlash forced him to keep her in place — for now.

---

## Public Reputation  
The *Tribucia Tribute* is both trusted and distrusted. Most people read it because there’s no real alternative. But many know to read between the lines, especially in [[Rachel Gold]]’s stories.  

Her byline signals something worth reading.  
Royce’s editorials usually signal something worth ignoring.  
Nobody talks about Marlon’s stories — but everybody reads them.

---

## Possible Future Threads  
- An underground press begins circulating, inspired by [[Rachel Gold]]’s bravery.  
- [[Royce Sincayd]] receives a direct order from [[The Duke]] to muzzle her permanently.  
- [[Marlon Lambert]] begins investigating Rachel’s enemies... without telling her.

# TTV Evening News

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎TTV EVENING NEWS
> ![[en.png|400]]  

> “United we stand, informed we thrive.”  
> — Warren Scottyard, opening line to every broadcast

## Overview  
The **TTV Evening News** is the primary nightly news broadcast aired across all of United Tribucia, streaming directly into every home via the mandatory CRT television sets issued by The Duke. Airing five nights a week at **18:00 sharp**, the program recaps daily events across the six major regions, delivers weather updates, and highlights notable achievements of Loyalist programs.

While the show claims impartiality, it's heavily censored and curated by the **Tribucian Communication Bureau**, ensuring all content either supports Loyalist rule or tactfully avoids criticizing it. Citizens see the show as either a dependable news source or subtle propaganda, depending on who you ask — and where you live.

The broadcast originates from **Studio 3B at TTV Headquarters in Gravenwild, Charspire**, the same complex where [[Night Time with Morris Gable]] is filmed.

---

## 🧑‍💼 Anchors

### [[Warren Scottyard]]
**Role:** Lead Anchor  
**Background:** Once a decorated field journalist during the reconstruction years, [[Warren Scottyard]] earned his reputation covering The Duke’s rise in Ashmoor. With a deep, authoritative voice and icy composure, Warren is both respected and distrusted depending on who's watching. He's seen as the "face of facts" by Loyalists and the "voice of polished lies" by skeptics.  
**Style:** Calm, unwavering, textbook Loyalist professional. Tends to pause dramatically before stating statistics or issuing official statements.

> “The Duke reminds us tonight — stability is not free. It is earned.”

---

### [[Layla Hawk]]
**Role:** Co-Anchor & Field Correspondent  
**Background:** A younger, sharper contrast to Warren, [[Layla Hawk]] was handpicked from a pool of regional broadcasters in Threshton for her charisma and on-camera presence. Rumors suggest she’s the niece of a former Loyalist commander, but nothing's confirmed. Layla covers softer segments, like weather, daily spotlights, and public health alerts, but occasionally handles field reports in more dangerous regions like Gutter Row or Steeltown.  
**Style:** Relatable, conversational, often smirking beneath the surface. A few viewers suspect she’s not quite as Loyalist-aligned as she lets on.

> “Sun’s rising early in Threshton tomorrow — but not as early as the ranchers hope. Grain quotas remain unmet for the fourth week running.”

---

## 🎥 Segments

- **The State Rundown:** Quick summaries from each region. Loyalist-approved only.  
- **Weather from the Watchtower:** Regional weather provided via airship telemetry and ground scouts.  
- **Public Safety Alerts:** Official bulletins from the Guard Forces. Often vague or cryptic.  
- **Faces of Tribucia:** Human-interest pieces focused on "model citizens" and Loyalist success stories.  
- **Field Reports:** Pre-recorded dispatches from reporters embedded across the regions.

---

## 🕯️ Cultural Impact

The TTV Evening News remains required viewing for many Loyalist families and a tolerated background noise in poorer households where it doubles as a light source. In black markets and backrooms, recordings are often edited into parody broadcasts known as "False Flags" — spliced with unflattering cuts, subversive commentary, or ghosted transmissions that include forbidden footage.

Layla Hawk has a secret following in Steeltown zines, where her smirks and unscripted side comments are interpreted as signs of quiet resistance.

---

# TTV Studios


> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Hollow House
> ![[ttv.png|500]] 

> “Broadcasting Unity to All of Disgraceland — Like It or Not.”

## Details
**Location:** Gravenwild, [[Charspire]]  
**Type:** Post-apocalyptic Broadcast Station  
**Owner:** [[The Duke]] (through loyalist proxies)  
**Station Manager:** [[Owen McCready]] (see below)

---

### Overview

TTV Studios is the only functioning television and radio station in Disgraceland. Housed in a crumbling, retrofitted broadcast building topped by a patched-together transmission tower, it’s become the lone source of “official” news, propaganda, and nightly entertainment for the people of Tribucia. The original tower dates back to pre-Tetra times; the current crew scrounged, rewired, and extended it until the signal finally reached every region again.

**TTV** (“Tribucia TeleVision”) schedule:

| Program           | Date                              | Time              |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| [[TTV Evening News]]  | Every Weeknight                        | 18:00hrs       |
| [[Night Time with Morris Gable]]      | Every Weeknight          | 23:00hrs    |
| [[WLL Fight Night]]      | Weekly Every Restday   | 22:00hrs         |
| [[The Duke]]'s [[State Of Tribucia]] Address    | Weekly Every Alphaday| 20:00hrs           |

The building is a hodgepodge of old tech, scavenged gear, jury-rigged generators, and blacked-out windows. On-air sets are painted to look more impressive on screen than in person — think flickering stage lights, patched curtains, and “live” audiences comprised mostly of the same few extras in different hats.

---

### Staff & Security

- **Manager:** [[Owen McCready]] — A burned-out, deeply private old technician, brought in by The Duke’s people for his uncanny knack for keeping ancient tech alive. Just wants to clock out, drink himself to sleep, and avoid getting dragged into the region’s politics.
- **Security:** A mix of bored Loyalist Guards and failed actors doubling as “security” on camera.
- **Production Crew:** Whoever can still operate a camera, solder a wire, or read a script.

---

### Station Manager: [[Owen McCready]]

**Bio:**  
Gruff, hunched, maybe late 50s, always in a sweat-stained broadcast cap, haunted eyes. Used to run pirate radio back in the Water Wars. Knows how to get a picture up on a broken screen with nothing but a coat hanger and a prayer. Trusts nobody, drinks nightly, and keeps a sawed-off shotgun hidden behind the filing cabinet “just in case.” Hates The Duke, but hates the alternative (unpaid work, or worse) more.

> “I just keep the lights on. What you do in front of the cameras is your problem.”

---

### Lore Notes

- **The tower** is visible from anywhere in Gravenwild — tall, ugly, patched with sheet metal and wire, always buzzing with static and the occasional power arc.
- Most citizens tune in, even if they don’t admit it. Half for news, half for a laugh at how desperate the government is to control the story.
- Occasional “signal interruptions” happen when someone sabotages the lines or when storms hit, but Switch usually gets it running again.

---

“A man’s worth ain’t counted in coin or cattle. It’s in how many mouths he’s fed and how many devils he’s held off ‘til the sun comes up.”

Turner Anderson was born under a copper sky in the scorched outskirts of [[Threshton]], back when the region was still choking on dust and lawlessness in the immediate fallout of the [[Tetra Bomb]]. His father was one of the first to settle after the skies cleared, carving a patch of land out of the dead soil and coaxing life from it with blood and fire. Turner grew up with blisters on his hands and a rifle slung across his back — by age thirteen, he’d already buried two rustlers and a mother lost to the cough. The [[Double-Cross Ranch]] became legend during the first wave of post-bomb settlements. Named after the cattle brand his father carved from scrap iron — two crude Xs overlapping — the ranch stood for resilience and survival. Turner led efforts to irrigate the fields using a jerry-rigged network of salvaged piping and old-world farm tech. He was the first to successfully grow wheat in Tetra-scorched soil and the first to trade cattle beyond Threshton’s borders. But it was never just about survival for Turner — it was about pride. Dignity. Feeding people who’d never known anything but hunger. As the [[Rancher Collective]] formed to organize the increasingly fragile supply lines, Turner naturally stepped into a leadership role. The other four ranchers — each tough in their own right — respected his steady hand, his iron-bound code, and his willingness to ride into danger to protect a shipment of grain or a rusted-out water pump. Some say the first meeting of the Collective was settled over whiskey and blood in Turner’s barn, after he challenged a land baron to a knife duel to stop a water hoarding scheme. Turner won — didn’t kill the man, but left him without his trigger finger. He’s seen the Duke’s claws tighten around Threshton year after year — tariffs, fuel rations, guards posted at silo checkpoints. He understands the deal: the Duke supplies power, fuel, and some semblance of order in exchange for the region’s food. But Turner knows damn well that it’s extortion dressed up as stability. Still, breaking from [[The Duke]] would mean starvation for half the map. That conflict lives in his eyes — every time he signs off on a shipment destined for [[Ashmoor]]. He wears black like mourning cloth. Lost his only son in a skirmish near [[GUTTER ROW]] — a fight over food the boy never should’ve been in. That grief made Turner harder, quieter. Now he rides alone most days, inspecting the herds, keeping the young ranch hands in line, making sure no one skims from the weight scales. Some say if there ever is a rebellion in Threshton, it won’t start with the loud mouths or the gun hawks. It’ll start when Turner Anderson stops sending crates of grain to Ashmoor. And when that happens, the whole damn food chain might come crashing down. --- ## Personality > [!infobox] > > ![[duke3.png|260]] **Temperament:** Stoic and principled. Turner speaks little, listens deeply, and weighs every decision like it could break a man. He is the calm in the storm — until pushed too far. **Vices:** Whiskey before sunup. Long, lonely rides. The need to fix everything himself. **Abilities:** Master survivalist and rancher; pioneered post-Tetra agriculture in Threshton. Skilled marksman and knife fighter; once ended a land dispute with a blade, not a bullet. - Natural leader; commands respect without ever asking for it. **Secrets:** Has met privately with **Freddy Blanchard** more than once to discuss what happens _after_ the Duke falls. **Beliefs:** Justice is non-negotiable. The Duke is a disease, and Disgraceland won’t heal until he’s ripped out root and stem. Jimmy believes in the people — and that they’re worth every scar. ## Role In Disgraceland Turner Anderson is the heart and backbone of Threshton. A living symbol of what the land used to be — and what it still could become. He holds the food supply chain together by sheer will and grit, walking the razor’s edge between obedience to the Duke and quiet rebellion. If Turner ever tips the scales, Disgraceland won’t be able to ignore it. ## Appearances > - [[Snake Eyes In Threshton]]

NOTE TITLE: [[Tyren Will]] METADATA:{"obsidianUIMode":"preview","NoteIcon":null,"NoteStatus":"New","thumbnail":"zz_media/th_tw.png","religion":"[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]","status":"Alive","location":"[[Gutter Row]]","faction":"None","role":"Owner of the [[Ha Ha Hole]]","chapters":[null],"tags":["character","individual","protagonist","stillborn-star"],"created":"2025/05/28 11:19:41","modified":"2025/06/03 11:03:44"} NOTE BLOCK CONTENT: --- obsidianUIMode: preview NoteIcon: NoteStatus: New thumbnail: zz_media/th_tw.png religion: "[[Word of the Stillborn Star]]" status: Alive location: "[[Gutter Row]]" faction: None role: "Owner of the [[Ha Ha Hole]]" chapters: - tags: - character - individual - protagonist - stillborn-star --- # TYREN WILL > [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Character Portrait > ![[tyren.png|400]] ## Overview **Titles:** Owner of the [[Ha Ha Hole]] **Alias/Nickname:** **Home Location:** [[Gutter Row]] **Public Reputation:** Eccentric, Beloved **Gender:** Male **Spouse:** None **Age:** 67 **Height:** 5'8" **Weight:** 152 lbs. **Date of Birth:** 28th of Greensun, 2119 **Occupation:** Prison Warden **Status:** Alive **Affiliation:** None **Known Associates:** **Faith:** [[Word of the Stillborn Star]] **Appearances:** ```dataview list from "DISGRACELAND" where contains(this.chapters, file.name) sort file.name asc ``` --- ## Biography >

“I’ve been kissed by kings and slapped by cowards, but nobody ever left this club without feeling something. That’s power, darling, and it scares the hell outta tyrants.”

[[Tyren Will]] is the legendary founder and master of ceremonies at the infamous [[Ha Ha Hole]] comedy club in Savage Hill, [[Gutter Row]]. A towering, slender man with wild white hair and a knack for showmanship, he’s a local hero and cultural icon, often described as the heart of Gutter Row’s spirit. He opened the club back in the 2140s as a defiant beacon of free expression when laughter itself had become rare. Now almost 70 years old, [[Tyren Will]] remains as sharp as ever, always perched at the bar in his signature robe with a cigarette burning between his fingers, watching the next generation of comics take the stage. He refuses to leave the club even during violent crackdowns in Gutter Row. His presence is a statement. His laughter — shrill and contagious — still commands the room. Though [[The Duke]] despises him and what the club represents, he dares not move against Tyren or the [[Ha Ha Hole]]. To do so would risk open revolt in the district. Despite persistent rumors about his sexuality, Tyren brushes off questions with a sly grin, often quipping that his “one true love is the punchline.” Whether he’s a relic from a forgotten era or the soul of Gutter Row made flesh depends on who you ask — but no one denies his impact. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Playful but unshakably principled. Tyren is theatrical, sharp-tongued, and endlessly curious, with an almost mystical calm beneath his flamboyant surface. He’s kind to underdogs, merciless to bigots, and impossible to intimidate. **Vices:** Chain-smokes unfiltered cigarettes. Addicted to performance — can’t stand silence. Has a habit of goading Loyalist officials just to see how far he can push them **Abilities:** Masterful orator and crowd manipulator. Encyclopedic memory of jokes, stories, and underground history. Has deep connections to black market information networks (disguised as comedy bookings) **Secrets:** Once had a clandestine romantic relationship with a Loyalist officer who later disappeared **Beliefs:** Comedy is the last weapon of the free. ## Role In Disgraceland [[Tyren Will]] serves as the living pulse of rebellion in Gutter Row. Through the Ha Ha Hole, he nurtures subversive thought disguised as entertainment. He is proof that resistance doesn’t always come with a gun — sometimes it walks on stage in a robe and goggles and tells a dirty joke. ## Appearances

History of the Unseen Widows
>

“Veerah will lead us all to the everlasting light.”

The Unseen Widows are a shadow that lingers over Disgraceland — silent, patient, and deadly. They are not a mere faction or band of raiders; they are a force born from sorrow and vengeance. Composed solely of women who have endured the worst of the world’s cruelty, the Widows move unseen through the ruins, striking without mercy and disappearing before the blood dries. Their name is both a warning and a promise. Many who cross them will not live to see their assassins. The Widows trace their origin to Veerah, a self-proclaimed prophet who rose from the ashes of despair. After her vivid dreams of the future began to come true, she was declared a living oracle by those desperate to believe in something greater. But the Widows were not built on faith alone. Many of the women who now call her leader were once victims of the Duke’s brutality — slaves, prisoners, and survivors of unimaginable torment. When they had no one else, Veerah offered them purpose. In her name, they found strength. Operating under a strict code of silence and loyalty, the Unseen Widows are masters of assassination, espionage, and psychological warfare. Veerah teaches them the art of moving without sound, of vanishing into shadows, and of striking down their enemies before they are even aware of the threat. Each Widow wears black, their faces partially veiled to mask their identities. Only Veerah remains unveiled, her golden hair and striking presence a symbol of the divine force they believe guides them. A gold bird emblem — the mark of the Widows — gleams on the chest of every member, a symbol of rebirth from the ashes of their past. But it is not only steel that makes the Widows formidable. Veerah instructs her followers to use their femininity as a weapon. Beauty, charm, and seduction are as deadly as any blade in a world where desire blinds even the most powerful. The Widows infiltrate, manipulate, and dismantle their enemies from within, leaving ruin in their wake. While most of the women are trained assassins, others specialize in gathering intelligence, sowing fear, and undermining the Duke’s strongholds. Their devotion to Veerah is absolute. Many see her as a living conduit of divine will, believing that her visions are proof of a higher power’s guidance. Dissent is rare, but those who question her prophecies are met with suspicion. Even the most trusted Widows, like Riley Thorne, Raina, and Risa, carry unspoken doubts about the true nature of Veerah’s visions — but to speak them aloud would risk exile or worse. While their methods are brutal, the Widows justify their violence as necessary in their fight against the Duke’s tyranny. But the longer they operate from the shadows, the more the line between justice and vengeance blurs. For now, they remain a whispered legend, feared by the powerful and revered by the oppressed. In Disgraceland, mothers tell their children that the Widows only come for the wicked. But in truth, the Widows come for anyone standing in their way.

## **“VISIONS IN THE NIGHT”**  
##### _A B-Side from the End Times_

> In the crumbling cathedral ruins of [[GUTTER ROW]], the blind prophet [[Salem Quinn]] delivers a sermon of hope to his followers amidst the rising dread of Disgraceland’s unraveling. That night, Salem is seized by a terrifying vision of a future ruled by human-machine hybrids, sacred spaces defiled, and trust betrayed. Shaken to his core, he confides in his loyal companion [[Tate Faulkner]], revealing a horrifying glimpse of Tate's own potential corruption. But in the quiet of dawn, faith triumphs over fear. Salem chooses trust, affirms his belief in Tate’s goodness, and declares their next destination with unwavering resolve: an audience with [[The Duke]].

Dawn stretched slowly over the crumbling spires of the cathedral, painting the sky in dull rose and ash-grey. The courtyard stones, still slick with last night’s rain, steamed faintly in the growing light. Birds did not sing. There were no birds here. Only the faint wheeze of the wind through shattered stained glass, and the slow, measured breath of a man alone with something too vast to voice.

[[Salem Quinn]] sat cross-legged on the cold stone, his cane laid beside him like a relic. His milky eyes were closed. His face was tense—not with fear, but with incomprehension, like a man trying to remember a dream that was never his. The vision had lodged itself deep within him like a shard of alien metal. Nothing he knew—no dogma, no mythos, no history—contained what he had seen. No book in the [[Faith of Mirella]], no parable in the [[Church Of The Ember Saint]] or symbol in the [[Word Of The Stillborn Star]], spoke of beasts made of machine-thought and corrupted divinity.

And yet, he knew. With marrow-deep certainty, he knew it was prophecy. A warning not of what might be—but what would be.

Footsteps approached—soft, cautious. [[Tate Faulkner]] emerged from the archway with a ration flask in hand, eyes shadowed from sleep not taken.

"You're up early," he said, kneeling slowly beside him.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] didn’t open his eyes. “Sleep is a kind thing. It avoided me.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] gently helped him to his feet and eased him onto the worn bench beneath the rusted courtyard bell. He placed the flask into Salem’s hands.

“Here. Drink. It’s yesterday’s draw, but it’s clean.”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] took a small sip, then rested the flask on his knee. For a long moment, he said nothing.

Then—quietly, as if speaking aloud made it real—he began to speak.

“I saw the end of flesh,” he said. “And the birth of something... else. Something vast and vile. Cities melted into lines of light. People erased and rewritten as code. And you, [[Tate Faulkner|Tate]]—”

He turned toward the man, though his eyes didn’t move. “You were one of them. Your arm... was no longer yours. It burned this place to ash.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] froze.

The silence stretched.

Then slowly, carefully, he sat beside his prophet and set his jaw. “Then I swear to you now—I will never lift hand nor harm against you. Or this temple. I don't care what future some dream-vision says. That ain't me. It won't be.”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] smiled, faint and warm. He reached out, fingers brushing [[Tate Faulkner|Tate]]’s cheek.

“I know,” he said. “You’re a good man, [[Tate Faulkner]]. You carry weight with conscience. That is rare. I trust you more than the visions that haunt me.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] looked away, nodded once.

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] helped [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] to his feet and handed him his ruby red sunglasses.

“Now,” [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] said, “we prepare the carriage.”

[[Tate Faulkner|Tate]] blinked. “For what?”

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]]’s face turned toward the rising sun.

“We’re going to see [[The Duke]].”

Dinner was quiet. The clink of tin cutlery echoed lightly in the high, ruined arches of the side chamber, where rain patted steadily against the broken glass above. [[Tate Faulkner]] had warmed root stew over a cracked brazier, the scent of pepper and bone marrow wafting in the cold. [[Salem Quinn]] ate little, but murmured thanks all the same. He moved like a man wading through thought, each bite a mechanical ritual.

When the bowls were cleaned and the fire doused, Tate took Salem by the arm and helped him down the corridor. The prophet’s quarters were simple: a cot, a writing desk, and a tiny shrine of twine and melted wax beside a weathered book..

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] touched the shrine briefly with two fingers, bowing his head.

"Grant me stillness between the static," he whispered.

He sat at the desk, fumbled for his pen and scribbled a few jagged lines into his journal—notes written not for remembrance, but warning. He stood slowly and sighed. He made his way to the cot to lay down fully clothed, arms at his sides, and close his pale, unblinking eyes.

Almost immediately the room collapsed inward.

Sound vanished.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] stood, no longer in stone and shadow, but in a cold, synthetic void that pulsed like a machine’s heartbeat. The air crackled with binary static. Flesh and steel twisted together in obscene harmony.

Seraphic beings emerged—towers of chrome and bone, their wings jagged with circuitry. Their mouths opened wide, screaming in reverse tongues that scraped the soul raw.

Beneath him, cities unraveled into wireframe grids. Human faces pixelated, data-washed, then rewritten—erased of identity, recoded into conduits. Their expressions flickered with corrupted memory, like half-finished prayers infected with malware.

A metallic serpent slithered across a horizon of ash, swallowing cathedrals whole and vomiting out spires of living circuitry. A massive clock tower loomed, its hands spinning backwards, each tick a shriek of unspeakable names.

And there—

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]] saw his own temple.

Flames licking up the columns, the stained glass shattered inward. And in the center: [[Tate Faulkner]]—no longer a man, but a machine mockery, his arm deformed into something brutal and unnatural, torching the altar with calculated malice.

Then came [[The Duke]], seated on a throne of code and fire, his eyes hollow and burning with binary light. Crowned in a halo of zeros, he watched the world burn.

And then the beasts came—

Waves of hybrid abominations, half-man, half-machine, screaming from the code, tearing through cities and flesh alike. No gods. No heroes. Only algorithmic hunger and ruin.

[[Salem Quinn|Salem]]’s body writhed in the cot. His back arched. His mouth opened in a mechanical howl—discordant, echoing like a machine’s dying breath.

When his eyes snapped open, they wept blood.

His fingertips were scorched black. The scent of ozone and burning flesh filled the small room.

He gasped and panted for air as [[Tate Faulkner]] burst into the room and to Salem's side.

"It's coming. Oh no, it's coming."
