The light filtered in through the shattered rose window, casting fractured beams of color onto the stone floor of the old cathedral ruins in [[GUTTER ROW#Nailstooth|Nailstooth]]. Dust floated in the golden shafts like ghost motes, stirring as sandalwood incense curled upward in slow, reverent spirals. The broken pews and vine-choked altars bore the memory of another age, but today, they thrummed softly with new voices—chanting, low and rhythmic, echoing in the throat of the old house of worship.

[[Salem Quinn]] moved through the corridor with unearthly precision, the heels of his worn boots clicking a slow tempo on the marble tiles. His blind eyes, milk-pale and unmoving, gave no hint of recognition, yet he turned at the exact moment an acolyte bowed, his hand brushing theirs like he had seen them all his life. Beside him, always a half-step behind, padded [[Tate Faulkner]], silent save for the faint creak of worn leather and the occasional whisper of breath as he kept watch.

“Faith is a muscle,” [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] murmured, voice like brushed velvet, "and in times like these, it must be exercised or it will atrophy."

He paused before a woman veiled in grief, her hands knotted like twine in her lap, and crouched. His fingers found hers gently, reverently. "He did not die without meaning," he said, and the way her breath caught said he’d struck the wound true. "He was born of storm and buried in stillness. But you carry his name now—and in that, his purpose is still alive."

She wept then, quietly. He rose.

A few steps more, and a child was lifted to him—no more than a few days old, wrapped in threadbare linen. Thunder growled outside as rain pattered against the high, broken glass. He touched the child’s forehead, his other hand on the father’s shoulder.

"She is a storm-child," [[Salem Quinn|Salem]] whispered. "Born into thunder so she may never fear it. May her cry always shake the unjust."

By the time he reached the dais, the room had fallen into hush. A thousand eyes watched him as he stood before the cracked podium, his fingers tracing the ruined carvings like braille.

He did not raise his voice. He did not need to.

"We are not the first to suffer. And we will not be the last. The world does not end just because it groans. It groans, yes—but like a ship bearing weight across deep waters. Like bones realigning themselves beneath skin. Like a woman birthing a child in the dead of night. And just like that, the sun will rise again.

I know many of you feel the weight of these times. The streets of [[GUTTER ROW]] sag beneath sorrow and smog. Out in [[Ashmoor]], the [[Ashmoor Festival|festival]] banners fly, promising wine and fire and distraction—but behind them? Fear. Tension like a match held to powder. Even the Final Reckoning draws near. [[Bobby Cutman]] against [[Bastian Redd]]—two men smashing toward each other like gods of violence, and still, we cheer. We wager. We pretend their fight will settle something greater.

But listen to me now: strength is not in spectacle. It is in standing up when you wish only to fall. It is in kindness when cruelty is easier. It is in the mother who feeds her child from an empty cupboard. In the elder who still lights a candle for a god no one else believes in.

I have seen what waits behind tomorrow. And it is cruel. It is cold. But it is not empty. If you stand upright—if you endure—then the sun will rise. Perhaps not for you. Perhaps not for me. But for someone. And that is enough.

This place is broken, yes. But so are bones before they heal stronger. So are swords before they’re sharpened. Do not fear the fracture. Embrace the forging. This is our hour in the fire. And we will emerge shaped anew.

So hold your neighbor. Feed the orphan. Speak truth, even when your voice shakes. And when you wake, wake with purpose.

May you go with your head held high."

And with that, he was gone—his cane never striking wrong, even once.

"Truth is like a fine suit. It’s not about what fits — it’s about what sells."

[[Warren Scottyard]] is the dashing, immaculately-groomed anchor of the _TTV Evening News_, the state-approved nightly broadcast in United Tribucia. With his rich, velvety voice and perfect hairline, he brings calm to the chaos with every segment, summarizing war, disaster, and civil unrest with an easy charisma that leaves viewers oddly reassured. He was personally handpicked by [[The Duke]] after a private audition in The Silo — a meeting shrouded in speculation, but one that sealed Warren’s rise as the most trusted voice in the nation. Since then, he’s become a nightly presence in every home, even in the poorest districts where static-riddled broadcasts are the only source of light. Born in the ashes of post-Tetra Ashmoor to an affluent family of land surveyors and property speculators, Warren rose through the ranks of TTV faster than most, thanks in part to his social circle. He’s a familiar face at high-society galas, private club dinners, and those strange elite functions where the wine flows endlessly and nothing is ever spoken of afterward. He resides in a pristine estate in **Diamond Valley**, rubbing shoulders with the ruling class. Despite his comfort and elite status, the public oddly still likes him — or maybe they’re just hypnotized by that voice. Warren is close with [[Morris Gable]], and the two men are often seen together at exclusive functions or caught whispering just before air. He also shares a business-minded camaraderie with [[Jacoban Clay]], occasionally hosting “special interest” segments that just so happen to feature Clay Industries or Loyalist initiatives in a glowing light. ## Personality **Temperament:** Smooth, diplomatic, and unfailingly composed. Warren rarely loses his cool and has mastered the art of being both likable and untouchable. He knows how to make someone feel seen while revealing nothing about himself. **Vices:** Fine scotch, vanity, and a quiet but enduring addiction to influence. He collects rare books, not to read them, but to impress the kind of guests who would notice. **Abilities:** Expert orator with hypnotic tone and perfect timing. Political survivalist — always knows the safest stance. Deep connections in TTV, Ashmoor politics, and the elite power web. **Secrets:** He once broadcast a heavily edited report that led to a militia being wiped out in Threshton. He knew it would happen. He keeps a burner radio tuned to the pirate frequency of [[The Blackwire]], claiming it’s “for awareness.” He’s heard messages that rattled him. Occasionally slips messages into broadcasts — invisible to the masses, but encoded for someone. **Beliefs:** Warren believes in control, in order, in the power of image. He doesn’t care who rules, so long as the lights stay on and the cameras stay rolling. Public emotion is something to be managed, like weather or traffic. ## Role In Disgraceland The perfectly-groomed public face of Loyalist truth and civility. He soothes the citizens, comforts the regime, and keeps the blood off the news desk.

# [[The Water Wars]]

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Global Conflict
> **Conflict Name:** The Water Wars  
> **Duration:** 2109 – 2121  
> **Catalyst:** Privatization of global freshwater supplies  
> **Final Event:** Detonation of the [[Tetra Bomb]]  
> **Casualties:** Estimated 5.6 billion lives (direct and secondary effects)
> 
>> [!rustwater] Water Wars
>> ![[w.png|400]]

> *"They didn’t fight for territory. They fought for the last cup of clean water."*  
> – Recovered transmission, Year 2109

## 🌊 Background

The planet was already dying.  
The oceans were poisoned, the skies were cracked, and the aquifers had run dry.

In the final decades of civilization, most remaining freshwater sources were sold off under what was known as the **Global Hydration Accord** — a desperate treaty that handed control of water to corporate conglomerates in exchange for infrastructure repair.

The people revolted. The governments panicked.  
The corporations fortified.  
And war began.

---

## 🏴 Phase One: The Corporate Front

Private security forces armed with bleeding-edge tech enforced strict water zones. The world was carved into zones of control.

- **The North Reach**: First major flashpoint. Riots led to the collapse of three citystates.  
- **The Coil Rim**: Tech hubs where AI combat drones were first deployed.  
- **Flood Zones**: Heavily bombed river territories. Access denied to civilians.  
- **The Salt Wastes**: Deserts soaked in blood and broken desalination rigs.

---

## 🤖 Phase Two: The Machine Years

| Technology             | Role in the War |
|------------------------|-----------------|
| **Combat Drones**      | Controlled key rivers and dam zones  
| **Skimmer Raiders**    | Stole mobile reserves mid-transit  
| **Neural Infantry**    | Failed attempt at mind-linked soldiers  
| **Orbital Pulse Cannons** | Used to vaporize contested reservoirs

Most of this tech died with the cities that built them.

---

## 🧍 Phase Three: The Return to Blood

By 2118, the machines were gone — broken, turned rogue, or unpowered.  
And the world returned to the old ways.  
Boots. Guns. Trenches. Mass graves.

Water shipments were hijacked by the gallon. Whole battalions slaughtered to take a single well. And in the end, everyone was thirsty.

---

## 💥 Final Phase: The Tetra Ignition

When the **[[Tetra Bomb]]** was deployed across the **Midcontinent Line**, nothing survived.

Not the corporations.  
Not the governments.  
Not the war.

The world froze.  
And then it waited to be reborn.

---

## 📅 Major Events Timeline

| Year | Event Title | Description |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| **2109** | **Global Hydration Accord** | Governments privatize all freshwater to survive infrastructure collapse. |
| **2111** | **The Severance Riots** | Dozens of megacities fall to internal unrest after water bans. |
| **2113** | **Corporate Armies Mobilize** | Security forces backed by hydro-conglomerates take control of rivers, dams, lakes. |
| **2114** | **Battle for the North Reach** | First massive conflict. Water convoys intercepted. Dams destroyed. |
| **2115** | **Orbital Strikes on the Coil Rim** | Entire tech cities erased to stop rebel AI control. |
| **2116** | **Neural Infantry Collapse** | Linked soldiers begin disappearing or going berserk. Project abandoned. |
| **2118** | **The Low-Tech Turn** | Countries resort to infantry, tanks, and desperation warfare. |
| **2121** | **Tetra Ignition** | The [[Tetra Bomb]] is dropped. The war ends. So does civilization.

---

## 🔗 Legacy

- No government has ever reformed.
- Fresh water remains the rarest commodity in [[DISGRACELAND]].
- Children are taught to fear thirst before fire.
- No one speaks of the Accord anymore — only the aftermath.

---

Overview

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎CHARSPIRE > ![[chars.png|400]] Water is both a source of survival and sorrow in Disgraceland. What little remains is poisoned, patrolled, or pulsing with death. These are the major bodies of water that shape the land, carve borders, and drown hope.

Bodies of Water


#### Sinners' Sea - South-West edge of Tribucia - If the [[WATER#The Dead Waters|The Dead Waters]] are cold and silent, the **Sinner’s Sea** is loud, lawless, and cursed by name. This roiling western ocean crashes against the black cliffs of [[Steeltown#The Hammer|The Hammer]] and seeps into [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] and the shanty wharfs of [[GUTTER ROW#The Docks|The Docks]]. Its waves smell like salt and rust, and its tides carry in wreckage, bones, and broken cargo from lands no longer listed on maps. Old sailors swear the sea shifts. That islands once charted vanish overnight, and strange lights flicker beneath the waves. It’s said that the worst criminals — the ones even [[The Duke]] won’t keep — are exiled into its current. No records, no trials, just pushed into the surf and forgotten. Despite the danger, this sea is not empty. Smugglers, pirates, and ghost-traders sail its chop. Some say they dock on hidden coves along the western cliffs. Others claim there’s a floating market far out past where compasses spin, where you can buy anything — if you’re willing to pay in memory or blood. - They call it the **Sinner’s Sea** because only the damned survive it. --- #### Rustwater Bay - Between [[Steeltown]] and [[Gutter Row]] - A polluted bay of orange-brown runoff from the broken mills and machine-yards of [[Steeltown]]. Thick with sludge and sharp with rust stink, the bay is technically navigable — but good luck finding a boat that’ll survive more than an hour. Gulls feed on ironfish here, and even the pirates give it a wide berth. --- #### Rustwater River - Runs inland from [[WATER#Rustwater Bay|Rustwater Bay]] - The toxic artery that cuts through [[Steeltown]] and spills into the gutters of [[Gutter Row]]. Locals sometimes use it for travel, and desperate scavengers paddle homemade rafts down it. Children born near it often have breathing issues. Some swear the river “talks” at night — whispering curses or laughter beneath the current. --- #### Grave Bay - Dead center of [[Tribucia Map|Tribucia]] - A stagnant inland sea that once connected various trade routes. Now it sits thick and unmoving — a brackish grave for lost ferries, traitors, and political prisoners. The name isn’t poetic. Bodies float here, face-down or face-up, bloated and forgotten. On calm nights, people say the surface glows faintly red. Nobody knows why. --- #### The Dead Waters - The eastern coast of Tribucia. - The **Dead Waters** stretch endlessly east of [[Charspire]] and [[Gutter Row]], swallowing the coastlines of Burnt Coast, Broken Bones Bay, and the jagged Four Tombs Islands. It is the last known ocean in this ruined world — vast, lifeless, and unnavigable by ordinary means. No merchant ships cross it. No trade lanes exist. It’s said that even the storms avoid this water. The salt here tastes bitter, wrong. Fog banks roll in without warning, and massive skeletal fish sometimes wash up on the jagged shorelines, long dead and unidentifiable. The [[Unseen Widows]] believe the sea remembers the end of the old world — that it’s where the gods once drowned themselves after the [[Tetra Bomb]]. [[The Duke]] has declared it off-limits to all but official Loyalist craft, though even they rarely venture far from the coast. - Many say it’s not the sea that’s dead — it’s everything that enters it. --- #### Faded Lake - Far north, bordering [[Threshton]], [[The Drownlands]] & [[Ashmoor]] - A frigid inland lake shrouded in pale mist most of the year. Its waters are dark, and nothing reflects on its surface. [[Coffin Island]] Prison sits like a broken tooth in the center. Rumor claims the bottom of the lake is littered with chains, bones, and drowned inmates — and that the lake itself “remembers.” Some locals refer to it as _The Eye That Never Shuts._ --- #### Broken Bones Bay Named for what it gives, not what it takes. Broken Bones Bay is a jagged stretch of beach and black water, where rusted ship remains rot beside sun-bleached shanties. Kids fish with wire. Old folks drink sea-moonshine and stare out past the surf, muttering about shapes that move under the water. It’s a place for the unwanted, the forgotten, and those too stubborn to die inland. You don’t vacation here. You vanish here. ---

# 🜨 Word of the Stillborn Star

> [!NOTE|clean no-i right]+ ‎Church of El Santo
> ![[ss.png|400]]  

> **"The silence between the stars is not emptiness. It is Galliah, watching, waiting, and remembering us all."**


**Word of the Stillborn Star** is the oldest organized religion in the world of Disgraceland. Its roots stretch back to the age of ancient cities and lost empires—when astronomers gazed up and wrote of a silent, failed sun named **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**.  The faith is cold, patient, and relentless. Believers see all things as cycles, destined to fade and restart when **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** finally awakens. Rituals are stark and quiet. Theirs is a god that speaks only through absence.

## Core Beliefs

- **Galliah, the Stillborn Star:**  
  A celestial body that never ignited—trapped between birth and death. **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** is both god and warning, a promise that everything ends and begins again.
- **The Echo of Silence:**  
  Silence is holy. The world is full of lies and noise, but truth is found in what is *not* said. Temples and homes of the faithful are austere and eerily quiet.
- **The Great Reset:**  
  One day, when corruption overtakes the world, **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]** will “ignite,” burning everything to ash and starting the cycle anew.
- **Prophecy of Return:**  
  When omens align, the First Stillborn (the living prophet) will lead the faithful to “witness the Dawnless Light”—the sign of Galliah’s return.

---

## History

- **Founded by Mesh'den:**  
  Once a lonely astronomer-priest, Mesh'den claimed to hear **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s voice in the silence. His followers, called **Stillborns**, swept through ancient cities and unified warring tribes with their chilling faith.
- **First Religion of the Old World:**  
  For centuries, it was the dominant faith. Many early texts, city laws, and holidays are rooted in Stillborn doctrine.
- **Decline and Survival:**  
  Overtaken in influence by the Ember Church and others, Stillborns are now a minority, but remain respected (and sometimes feared) for their age and mystery.

---

## Practices & Traditions

- **The Silence Hour:**  
  At dusk, followers meditate in silence, facing the eastern sky.
- **Ash Oath:**  
  Vows are sworn over cold ashes—a reminder that all things fade.
- **Star Vigil:**  
  On the first new moon of each year, all Stillborns gather for a night-long silent vigil, watching the sky for Galliah’s sign.
- **Names of the Faithful:**  
  Most adherents take a second name in old tongue (“-ah” or “-en” suffix) after completing the Rite of Stillness.

---

## Symbols

- **The Unlit Star:**  
  A black circle with a faint lavender halo—**[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s mark.
- **Chains of Renewal:**  
  Interlocking rings, symbolizing endless cycles.

---

## Structure

- **First Stillborn:**  
  The living prophet, said to channel **[[Galliah, the Stillborn Star|Galliah]]**’s will. The First Stillborn leads all major rites and appoints regional Speakers.
- **Speakers:**  
  Local religious heads, guardians of doctrine and silent keepers of the faith.
- **Lay Stillborns:**  
  Everyday followers; expected to maintain silence, charity, and ritual observance.

---

## Influence

- **Law & Time:**  
  The Disgraceland calendar was originally structured by Stillborn priests. Many laws about contracts, death, and inheritance come from their traditions.
- **Temples:**  
  Ancient, spartan buildings—many now ruined or repurposed by newer faiths.

---

## Holy Days

- **Day of Quiet (last day of the year):**  
  All work stops at dusk. The world is meant to fall silent—no music, no fire, no words—until dawn.
- **Vigil of Ashes (midyear):**  
  The faithful gather, burn old regrets and tokens, and let the ashes scatter at sunrise.

---

## Famous Quotes

- "We are the dust that dreams of fire."
- "When Galliah wakes, so too shall the world sleep."
- "Truth lives where sound dies."

---

## Notable Figures

- **Mesh'den:**  
  Founder and “First Stillborn.”  
- **Current First Stillborn:**  
  (Name open for your input—can flesh out if you want.)

---

## Relationship With Other Faiths

- **Church of the Ember Saint:**  
  Bitter rivals in the old world—Ember preaches action, Stillborns preach patience.
- **Faith of Mirella:**  
  Little direct conflict; both are considered “old faiths.”  
- **El Santo:**  
  Not directly opposed—Stillborns view El Santo as a regional offshoot or heresy.

---

> *“All things end in silence, but Galliah’s silence is never empty.”*

---

# World Lucha Libre

> [!column] Information
>> [!rustwater] Description:
> In Disgraceland, **Lucha Libre** is king.  
> It’s not choreographed wrestling—it’s brutal, high-stakes MMA, the truest test of will and skill. The sport kept its ancient name from the legendary [[Noche de Lucha]], but here, the fights are real.  
> Spectacle is everything: dramatic entrances, wild personalities, and fierce rivalries light up every show. But in the cage, nothing is fake—victory and pain are both earned.
> 
>> [!rustwater] World Lucha Libre
>> ![[wll1.png|250]]

> **"No script, no mercy—just blood, grit, and glory."**

## History

> [!infobox]
>
> ![[wll.png|260]]

- **Origins:**  
  Lucha Libre grew from the old [[Noche de Lucha]] tournaments—an ancient tradition of combat, now evolved into a spectator sport for a broken world.
- **Golden Age:**  
  Before the [[Tetra Bomb]], the **WLL (World Lucha Libre)** was a global phenomenon. Champions toured the world, and the best fighters became household names.
- **The Fall:**  
  After the [[Tetra Bomb]], the sport vanished. Only small, dangerous underground matches survived in the chaos.
- **Revival:**  
  In the last 15 years, as Disgraceland clawed back to stability, a wealthy industrialist (a bitter rival to [[Jacoban Clay]]) resurrected the WLL—building a new arena in [[Gutter Row]] and sparing no expense on belts, hype, and spectacle.  
  Anyone with fists, dreams, or something to prove can enter—win, and you might become a legend.

---

## Culture & Masks

- **Masks:**  
  In modern Lucha Libre, masks are *not* required. The mask remains a sacred symbol for the clergy and the most faithful of [[El Santo]], but the sport itself is about the fighter’s reputation, skill, and swagger.
- **The Show:**  
  Theatrics, promos, and hype are a must. Fighters adopt bold personas, enter the arena like legends, and stir the crowd before a punch is even thrown.
- **The Fights:**  
  All-out MMA—no scripts, no predetermined winners, no mercy.  
  Fighters are judged by toughness, technique, and the ability to thrill a crowd.

---

## The Modern WLL

- **Arena:**  
  The new WLL arena in [[Gutter Row]] is part fortress, part theater—a beacon of light (and vice) in the chaos.
- **Fighter Recruitment:**  
  Open call. The desperate, the daring, and the washed-up all get a shot. The best rise fast; the weak go home broken or worse.
- **Titles:**  
  Real belts, real champions. Winning one means respect, money, and all the trouble that comes with fame in Disgraceland.
- **Promoters:**  
  The WLL’s owner is a kingmaker—pitting would-be legends against each other and using the league to grow his own influence.
- **Entertainment:**  
  Beyond the fights, every show is an event: music, fireworks, dancing, wild costumes. It’s part bloodsport, part circus, all survival.

---

## Impact on Society

- **Unity & Escape:**  
  For a few hours, faith, faction, and class mean nothing. People come together to watch the fights, forget their troubles, and gamble their last coins.
- **Fame & Fortune:**  
  Fighters can become folk heroes—or cautionary tales.  
  Some win riches, others disappear after a brutal loss.
- **Rivalries:**  
  The WLL is a pressure valve for Disgraceland. Old grudges and street feuds often play out in the cage, with the crowd roaring for blood.

---

## Famous Champions (Examples)

- **“The Sand Viper”** – undefeated, merciless, beloved by the crowd, but feared in the locker room.
- **Freya “The Iron Widow”** – former Unseen Widow who shocked the world with her fighting spirit.
- **Marcus “Steeljaw” Torres** – a Steeltown legend known for never tapping out.

---

## Notable Moments

- **The Arena Riot (Year 2182):**  
  When a match ended in a disputed stoppage, fans stormed the cage. The promoter doubled security after.
- **The First Open Challenge:**  
  The owner’s “anyone can fight” policy led to a month where a farmer, a priest, and a disgraced Loyalist all stepped into the ring—none won, but the city still talks about it.

---

## Connections to Faith

- **El Santo’s Influence:**  
  The faith’s values—endurance, honor, and justice—live on in the sport’s code, even if most fighters now go unmasked.
- **Noche de Lucha:**  
  Once every four years, the line between faith and sport blurs as champions from the WLL are invited to compete in the greatest tournament of all.

---

“If you’re playing the game right, they’ll never see the knife till it’s buried in their ribs.”

Zadie Adeyemi doesn’t need to shout. When she speaks, the room listens — not out of fear, but because it knows she’s already done the math on how to burn it down. The Black Marauder runs on iron, blood, and fire… and Zadie keeps it all balanced. Born in the rust-riddled ruins of Disgraceland’s eastern edge, she survived on wit, weaponry, and weaponized charm. Now she’s Quartermaster of the Raiders — the one who tracks every bullet, blade, and bottle aboard the ship, and ensures every raid ends with profit, not excuses. She’s Lyla’s shadow strategist, a storm in a silk coat, and the one crewmembers fear disappointing more than the Captain herself. Zadie’s got eyes on every angle. When she negotiates, you don’t realize you’ve lost until she’s already two ports away. And behind that leather-bound journal she always carries? Blueprints. Names. Vengeance. Maybe even futures she’s yet to cash in. Her loyalty to Lyla Bonetooth is firm. For now. But make no mistake — Zadie is nobody’s pawn. If the tides shift, she’ll already be standing where the water breaks. The only person who gets past her armor is her brother, **Darius**. She doesn’t speak softly to him — she commands him the same as anyone else. But the bond between them is deep and ancient. She’s his calm. He’s her chaos. --- ## Personality **Temperament:** Commanding, poised, and calculating. Zadie doesn’t raise her voice — she silences others with presence alone. **Vices:** Control. She craves leverage and influence the way others crave comfort. Secrets are her currency, and power is her drug of choice. **Abilities:** Master of logistics, tactics, and psychological warfare. Zadie can plot a raid, flip a mutiny, or collapse an enemy faction without raising her blade — though she’s deadly with it too. **Secrets:** Her journal is rumored to contain blackmail, backup plans, hit lists — even post-Lyla contingencies. Nobody knows how deep it goes. **Beliefs:** Survival is earned. Loyalty is negotiable. And power belongs to the one willing to play the long game. ## Role In Disgraceland **Zadie Adeyemi** is the spine of the Black Marauder. While others shout, bleed, or threaten — she plans. She executes. And she wins. She’s not the next in line… she’s the one building the throne.
